Summary
- Introduce programmatic defaults and easier resetting/loading for main table column preferences.

What I changed
- ColumnPreferences
  - Added a private default constructor that creates a hard-coded default column layout (types, keys and widths).
  - Added ColumnPreferences.getDefault() factory method.
  - Added setAll(...) to copy columns and column sort order from another ColumnPreferences instance.

- MainTablePreferences
  - Added a private default constructor and MainTablePreferences.getDefault().
  - Added setAll(...) to copy all preference fields from another MainTablePreferences instance.

- JabRefGuiPreferences
  - Removed the old hard-coded COLUMN_NAMES and COLUMN_WIDTHS default strings from the defaults map and replaced usage with programmatic defaults.
  - When clearing/importing preferences, main table preferences and column preferences are now reset via the new getDefault() objects.
  - Refactored retrieval logic: getMainTablePreferences() and getMainTableColumnPreferences() now delegate to new helper methods that load from the backing store but fall back to the provided defaults if no stored settings exist.
  - Added helper methods getMainTablePreferencesFromBackingStore(...) and getMainTableColumnPreferencesFromBackingStore(...) to centralize reading from the backing store with sensible defaults.

Behavioral impact
- The main table columns now have a single source of truth for defaults in code (ColumnPreferences.getDefault()). If a user has no stored column settings in the preferences, the app will use these programmatic defaults.
- The new setAll(...) methods allow other parts of the code to replace preference objects atomically while preserving JavaFX observable lists/properties usage.

Misc
- Minor whitespace cleanup.

This change simplifies preference defaults management, makes defaults easier to maintain in-code, and ensures clear fallback behavior when stored preferences are absent.

text:
Major refactor and feature addition for scripts/syncLang.py

Summary
- Add argparse-based CLI with subcommands: markdown, status, update and print (missing/obsolete/duplicates).
- Introduce a main() entry point and replace previous ad-hoc argv handling.
- Add optional PathFinder (pathlib-based) to locate repository structure when running under Python 3; guarded by try/except to preserve Python 2.7 compatibility.

Refactor and renames
- Keys.duplicates() renamed to Keys.find_duplicates().
- Several helper functions renamed for clarity: __read_file_as_lines -> __read_lines_from_file, __check_properties -> __compare_properties, update() -> update_properties(), status_create_markdown() now accepts markdown_file parameter.
- New static helper Keys.format_key_and_value() and SyncLang.__print_keys() to centralize formatting/printing.
- Replace manual missing-key loop with a set-difference implementation in __missing_keys (now static).
- Improved file-path handling: main localization file constants and helpers to determine main file for comparisons.

Behavioral improvements
- New extended_logging flag (formerly extended) and set_extended_logging_enabled() method; extended output printing is centralized and consistent.
- New methods to print missing/obsolete/duplicate keys per file or for all files: print_missing_keys*, print_obsolete_keys*, print_duplicate_keys*.
- status and update operations now use the refactored compare/update flows and use the new Keys API consistently.
- Markdown output now writes to a configurable filename parameter and logging is updated.

CLI usage examples
- python ./scripts/syncLang.py markdown
- python ./scripts/syncLang.py status -e
- python ./scripts/syncLang.py update --extended
- python ./scripts/syncLang.py print missing
- python ./scripts/syncLang.py print duplicates -f JabRef_fr.properties

Misc
- Encoding-safe file read/write behavior remains (UTF-8 with codecs).
- Logging messages improved and extended prints now use __print_keys for nicer output.

Notes
- PathFinder requires Python 3.4+ (pathlib). The import is optional and falls back silently if unavailable, keeping compatibility with older Python/Jython runtimes.

Summary:

- Introduces a new text field for files that are automatically detected by JabRef and displayed in the General tab of the entry editor.
- Changes the icon used for automatically linked files from BRIEFCASE_CHECK to LINK_PLUS (more intuitive "link with plus" symbol).

Why:

Automatically detected files were shown without an editable text field, which made the UI less consistent and less friendly for users who want to inspect or edit the detected file path. The icon BRIEFCASE_CHECK was also misleading; LINK_PLUS better communicates an automatically discovered link that can be added.

What changed:

- Added a text field for automatically detected files listed in the entry editor's General tab so users can view/edit the path directly.
- Replaced the BRIEFCASE_CHECK icon with LINK_PLUS for automatically linked files.
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to describe the user-facing change.

Screenshots:

- Before (file not linked / file linked): see PR screenshots.
- After (file not linked / file linked): see PR screenshots.

Testing:

- Manually tested the feature in a running JabRef instance.
- No automated tests were added for this UI change.

Documentation:

- The user documentation currently refers to the icon as a "suitcase". If this change is accepted, the docs should be updated to describe it as a link with a plus sign. We did not create a documentation PR to avoid creating an issue prematurely.

text:
Add AtomicFileOutputStream: atomic, safe file replacement with temporary file and backup

- Introduces AtomicFileOutputStream, a FilterOutputStream that writes to a temporary file (".tmp") and atomically replaces the target file on close.
- Workflow: write to temp -> create backup of original file (".sav") -> move temp to target using ATOMIC_MOVE + REPLACE_EXISTING -> optionally delete backup.
- Preserves POSIX file permissions when available (reads permissions from original and restores them on the new file).
- Attempts to lock the temporary file via FileOutputStream channel to avoid concurrent writes; handles OverlappingFileLockException and the JDK-8167023 network-drive issue (logs a warning and continues without a lock).
- Ensures data is flushed and fd.sync() is called before closing; robust error handling: on write/flush/move errors the temporary file is deleted and the backup is preserved when appropriate.
- Provides abort() to cancel the write and remove temporary and backup files, and getBackup() to access the backup path.
- Constructor accepting Path/temporary Path/OutputStream is package-private to facilitate testing; the public constructor uses a FileOutputStream (since Files.newOutputStream does not allow file locking).

This implementation reduces risk of partial writes and data loss, improves cross-instance safety, and keeps behavior consistent across POSIX/non-POSIX file systems.

Add WordKeywordGroup implementation and unit tests for keyword parsing and explicit group behavior

- Add WordKeywordGroup: a KeywordGroup implementation that matches entries when a given field contains specified word(s). Supports configurable keyword separator, case sensitivity, and a mode to only split words at the separator. Implements GroupEntryChanger to add/remove the search expression from entries.
- Add KeywordListTest: unit tests for KeywordList parsing and formatting. Tests cover empty input, single/multiple keywords, different delimiters, whitespace handling, duplicate elimination, bracketed keywords, and getAsString producing a delimiter + space format.
- Add ExplicitGroupTest: unit tests for ExplicitGroup add/remove/contains behavior. Verifies adding groups updates the groups field correctly, duplicate additions are ignored, removal does not alter fields where the group name appears only as part of another word/token, and matching handles whitespace, slashes and bracketed group names properly.

Add searchable Preferences dialog with label highlighting

What I changed
- Introduced a search box in the Preferences dialog and hooked it up to a new PreferencesSearchHandler.
- Implemented PreferencesSearchHandler to filter the list of preference tabs and highlight matching Labeled controls inside tabs.
- Added CSS rules (PreferencesDialog.css) to style the side menu, preference pane container and the search highlight pseudo-class (:search-highlight).
- Wired the search handler into PreferencesDialog so the ListView of tabs is filtered live and matches in both tab names and label texts.

Files modified/added
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preferences/PreferencesDialog.java
  - Added search TextField and integrated PreferencesSearchHandler
  - Bound the filtered list to the tabs ListView
  - Kept import/export/reset/show preferences functionality intact
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preferences/PreferencesSearchHandler.java
  - New handler that: builds a map of PrefsTab -> Labeled nodes, filters tabs by query (case-insensitive), and applies a PseudoClass for highlighting matches
  - Clears highlights when the query is empty
  - Note: currently traverses direct children of a tab builder (only one level)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preferences/PreferencesDialog.css
  - Added styling including -fx-background-color for highlight: -jr-light-red and other layout styles

Behavior/Details
- Search is case-insensitive and matches against tab names and the text of Labeled nodes inside each tab.
- Matching labeled controls are highlighted by toggling a pseudo-class (search-highlight); the color is defined in the CSS.
- When the search box is cleared, highlights are removed and the full tab list is restored.

Notes / Future improvements
- PreferencesSearchHandler currently only inspects direct children of a tab builder (one level). If deeper traversal is needed, the node traversal can be made recursive to catch nested labeled nodes.
- There is a small TODO/FIXME in PreferencesDialog.initalize() (typo: initalize) left as-is; consider modeling the dialog with FXML in a follow-up.

Summary

- Add a preferences migration to handle Windows registry patch / downgrade related preference changes and to keep preference storage compatible across versions.
- Update the JabRef preferences API to reflect renamed/removed preference keys and to provide correct defaults for migrated settings.
- Include a .reg patch file (JabRef-downgrade-regpatch.reg) to assist users who need to revert Windows registry changes made by newer versions.
- Add unit tests to validate the new migration behavior and ensure no regressions when migrating old preference data.

Why this change

- Prevents issues caused by leftover or renamed preference keys when upgrading or downgrading JabRef.
- Improves stability and user experience during version transitions by automatically migrating or cleaning up problematic preference entries.
- Adds tests to ensure the migration remains reliable over time.

Fixes #7633 — improve handling of curly braces in titles when searching arXiv.

Problem
- The ArXiv fetcher previously removed all curly braces from titles when building queries and when comparing titles, which could change intended LaTeX formatting or alter words that should remain braced.

What this change does
- Introduces two helper methods in StringUtil:
  - removeAllBraces(String): utility to strip all braces (added for completeness).
  - removeBracesAroundCapitalizedWords(String): repeatedly removes only braces around capitalized words (e.g., "{Word}" or "{{Word}}" -> "Word").
- Uses removeBracesAroundCapitalizedWords in ArXiv.fetcher when constructing the search query and when comparing the entry title to the returned arXiv title, so queries match titles that contain braces around capitalized words without stripping other braces unnecessarily.
- Adds unit tests (ArXivTest) to cover matching by title with and without curly braces to prevent regression.
- Consolidated JUnit imports in tests.

Why
- This preserves braces used for LaTeX formatting while allowing the fetcher to match common cases where authors braced capitalized words in titles, improving full-text discovery on arXiv for entries whose titles contain such braces.

Tests
- New tests verify that findFullText succeeds for a paper whose title is provided with and without curly braces around capitalized words.

Notes
- No user-facing behavior changes besides improved arXiv matching; CHANGELOG update not included.

Summary
- Improve BibTeX import robustness by adding character-set detection and fallback handling when declared encodings are wrong or files lack a BOM.

What I changed
- Added ICU4J library (lib/icu4j.jar and lib/icu4j-src.jar) and wired it into the build (build.gradle).
- Implemented encoding-detection/fallback logic in the BibTeX importer (src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fileformat/BibtexImporter.java) and adjusted importer infrastructure (src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/Importer.java) as needed to support the new behavior.
- Added unit tests that cover edge cases around file encodings:
  - UTF-16BE with BOM
  - UTF-16BE without BOM
  - Files that declare UTF-8 but are actually encoded in Windows-1252 (decoding fails; fallback detection used)
  Tests: src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fileformat/BibtexImporterTest.java and the corresponding test resources in src/test/resources/...
- Updated documentation and metadata: external-libraries.md and CHANGELOG.md to reflect the new dependency and the import improvements.

Why
- Real-world BibTeX files sometimes either lack a BOM or declare the wrong encoding. Previously this could lead to failed decoding or incorrect import results. Using ICU4J charset detection as a fallback makes importing more reliable and resilient to such files.

Notes / Impact
- Adds ICU4J as a bundled dependency which increases distribution size slightly but improves encoding detection significantly.
- Behavior is backwards compatible: existing well-encoded files fall back to the original logic; only problematic files gain improved handling.
- Unit tests were added to lock in the improved behavior.

Summary:
Ensure renaming of FileEntry objects during cleanup runs on the JavaFX Application Thread to avoid illegal off-thread field modifications.

text:
Introduce Lucene-based search infrastructure and tests

This PR implements a full-text search system for the library using Lucene and wires it into the application model. Main additions and highlights:

- DatabaseSearcher: New facade to perform searches against a BibDatabaseContext using a SearchQuery. It validates queries, delegates to LuceneManager, converts matched entry ids back to BibEntry objects in library order and purges empty entries.

- LuceneManager: Central manager that holds indexers and a searcher. It:
  - Initializes BibFieldsIndexer (in-memory) and a linked-files indexer (DefaultLinkedFilesIndexer or ReadOnlyLinkedFilesIndexer fallback on IO error).
  - Registers a preferences listener to toggle linked file indexing.
  - Starts background indexing tasks at startup and exposes methods to add/remove/update/rebuild/close indexes.
  - Provides blockLinkedFileIndexer() to temporarily disable linked-file indexing and a search(SearchQuery) helper that populates SearchQuery results.
  - Posts indexing lifecycle events (IndexStartedEvent, IndexAddedOrUpdatedEvent, IndexRemovedEvent, IndexClosedEvent) to the database.

- Indexer implementations:
  - BibFieldsIndexer: An in-memory index for entry fields (uses ByteBuffersDirectory). Indexes entry id, type and all searchable fields (except groups) to a default field.
  - DefaultLinkedFilesIndexer: Filesystem-backed index for PDF fulltext using FSDirectory. Reads PDF pages, tracks modification times, removes stale files, optimizes on close, and deletes temporary unsaved index directories.
  - ReadOnlyLinkedFilesIndexer: Read-only wrapper using an existing index directory when only read access is available.
  - LuceneIndexer: Interface shared by indexers.

- Tests:
  - DatabaseSearcherTest: Unit tests for searching simple entry fields and handling invalid queries.
  - DatabaseSearcherWithBibFilesTest: Parameterized tests using sample .bib files to verify title-casing search and fulltext searches on attached PDF files. Uses a CurrentThreadTaskExecutor and temporary index directories.

- Other details and robustness:
  - Uses BackgroundTask + TaskExecutor for all indexing operations, and HeadlessExecutorService for closing indexes.
  - Graceful fallback to read-only linked-files indexing when initialization IO errors occur.
  - Proper resource cleanup via close/closeAndWait methods and listener removal on close.
  - Ensures correct handling of unsaved libraries by creating unique unsaved index directories.

This change adds search/fulltext capability for both bibliographic fields and attached PDF files, integrates preference-driven behavior, and includes tests validating the implemented behavior.

If a file is changed externally, JabRef is doing a 3-way merge between the last saved value vs current value in JabRef vs new value in file.
The way this is done is by first comparing the last saved file with the current (changed) file, and then trying to find additional/other changes in the currently open database. This is really complex and I believe there is some subtle bug in the logic leading to #5257.

With this PR, the change scanner is changed to a to simple 2-way merge between the current value in JabRef vs new value in file. This is way simpler and I hope this PR fixes #5257.
In a few edge cases, the 2-way merge has a small disadvantage. For example, consider the following steps:
- User A opens file
- User A changes field `Author` to `User A` and adds field `Title` with value `new`
- User B opens file
- User B changes field `Author` to `User B`
- User B saves file

At this point, User A gets a message that the file changed with the following changes:
- field `Author` changed from `User A` to `User B`
- field `Title` was removed

The 3-way merge could detect that `Title` was newly added, and thus could automatically reapply this change.  This is no longer possible with the simple 2-way merge.

This pull request refactors the `IndexingTaskManager` and `PdfIndexer` classes to improve the efficiency and readability of the full-text search indexing process. The changes include:

- **IndexingTaskManager**:
  - Switched from using a `LinkedList` to a `ConcurrentLinkedQueue` for better concurrency support.
  - Simplified the task queue management and progress updates.
  - Added a locking mechanism to ensure thread-safe operations.
  - Updated the `createIndex` method to use a simpler approach without directly interacting with the database.
  - Added methods to handle individual tasks for adding and removing entries from the index.

- **PdfIndexer**:
  - Removed the direct dependency on the `BibDatabase` and simplified the `createIndex` method.
  - Updated the test cases to reflect the new method signatures.

- **Localization**:
  - Added new localization strings for better user feedback during the indexing process.

These changes should result in a more robust and maintainable indexing system.

- Implemented view/controller logic:

  - GeneralPropertiesView: added FXML fields for the new controls, listeners that update the glyph and tooltip based on whether the current path is absolute, and handlers that call the ViewModel to toggle paths.
  - GeneralPropertiesViewModel: added togglePath(StringProperty) to convert between absolute and relative paths (using the library path as base) and refactored directory browse handlers to use setDirectory(...) which chooses relative vs absolute when storing selected paths. Also renamed librarySpecificDirectoryPropertyProperty() -> librarySpecificDirectoryProperty().
- IconTheme: added two new icons ABSOLUTE_PATH and RELATIVE_PATH.
- Localization: added English tooltip strings for switching to absolute/relative path.
- CHANGELOG: documented the new toggle button and change to path display (show relative path w.r.t. library path in Library Properties).

Introduce MetaData model class to manage JabRef database metadata and notify listeners about changes.

Key responsibilities and features:
- Store various metadata properties: save order config, save actions (field formatter cleanups), default and per-entry-type BibTeX key patterns, grouping tree, encoding, database mode, protection flag, default and per-user file directories (including LaTeX dirs), and content selectors.
- Provide getters/setters for all metadata with validation (Objects.requireNonNull where appropriate) and optional wrappers for nullable fields.
- Post change events via an internal EventBus: posts MetaDataChangedEvent and GroupUpdatedEvent. Supports registering/unregistering listeners and temporarily disabling event propagation to avoid event loops (setEncoding with ChangePropagation).
- Manage unknown metadata entries and expose unmodifiable maps for user/LaTeX file directories and unknown metadata to preserve encapsulation.
- Implement equals and hashCode based on relevant fields to enable comparison of MetaData instances.

This class centralizes metadata handling and change notification for the application, enabling consistent updates and listeners for metadata modifications.

  - Chat history view and prompt component wired up via FXML (AiChatComponent.fxml).

  - Provides retry, cancel and prompt-history functionality (reversed user messages used for prompt suggestions).
  - Clear and helper methods (delete last message, update prompt history, update notifications per entry).

Summary:
Improve the full-text lookup flow to support progress reporting when searching multiple entries online and to properly download and attach the found PDFs to their corresponding entries.

What changed:
- FindFullTextAction:
  - Replaced BackgroundTask.wrap(...) with a JavaFX Task<Map<Optional<URL>, BibEntry>> so a progress dialog can be shown while looking up full texts for multiple selected entries.
  - Progress is updated for each entry looked up and a progress dialog is displayed via DialogService.
  - When a URL is found, the download is started into the chosen target directory and, once finished, the downloaded file is converted into a LinkedFile and attached to the BibEntry (instead of linking the remote URL directly).
  - Handles malformed URLs and notifies the user appropriately.

- LinkedFileViewModel:
  - Extracted the download preparation logic into a new method prepareDownloadTask(Path targetDirectory, URLDownload urlDownload) that returns a BackgroundTask<Path>.
  - The existing download() behavior remains unchanged but now delegates to prepareDownloadTask internally. prepareDownloadTask is reused by FindFullTextAction so a custom onSuccess action can be provided (to add the downloaded file to the entry).

Other notable details:
- URLDownload is used to determine file type and to perform the actual network download.
- Downloads are executed on the existing Globals.TASK_EXECUTOR to keep work off the FX thread.
- Duplicate linking is avoided: if the entry already contains the same LinkedFile it is not downloaded again and the user is informed.

Files modified:
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/externalfiles/FindFullTextAction.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/LinkedFileViewModel.java

Motivation:
- Provide user feedback when performing full-text lookups across multiple entries.
- Ensure found PDFs are downloaded into the library file directory and attached to the entry (improves usability compared to simply linking the remote URL).

Notes / TODOs:
- The change keeps the existing single-file download behavior intact for the entry editor.
- Tests and changelog entry were not included in this PR (see issue checklist).

Fix: make file path relative when creating entry from PDF

What changed
- When creating an entry from a PDF file, the stored file path is now made relative to the repository/project root rather than kept as an absolute path.

Why
- Absolute file paths caused portability problems (entries broke when the project was moved or cloned into a different location). Storing relative paths makes entries resilient to repository relocation and easier to share.

Implementation notes
- The entry creation logic now computes a relative path (using the repo/project base as the reference) and normalizes separators.
- If the PDF file is outside the repository root, the code falls back to storing the original path (preserving behavior in that edge case).
- Added/updated unit tests to cover the new behavior, including cross-platform path normalization.

Impact
- Backwards compatible: existing entries are unchanged; new entries created from PDFs will use relative paths.
- No changes to external APIs or data formats beyond the path value stored for new entries.

Add and improve Key Bindings preferences UI and backing view model

This PR implements and refines the Keyboard Shortcuts (Key Bindings) preferences tab and its view model, together with unit tests to validate behavior. Main changes:

- UI (KeyBindingsTab)
  - Added search box with flashing background styling to indicate invalid search, and integrated a search icon.
  - Populates presets menu from available KeyBindingPreset implementations and wires menu actions to load presets.
  - Uses a TreeTableView to display key binding categories and individual bindings; columns show action name, current shortcut and clickable icons for reset/clear actions.
  - Consumes key events on the table and delegates binding changes to the ViewModel to allow setting new shortcuts via keyboard input.
  - Added helper actions: Reset bindings, Expand All, Collapse All.

- ViewModel (KeyBindingsTabViewModel)
  - Reads key bindings from a KeyBindingRepository and builds KeyBindingViewModel hierarchy by category.
  - Implements filtering logic (search) across binding localization, category and key combination.
  - Handles setting new bindings from KeyEvent objects, including special keys (F1, etc.) and key combinations with modifiers.
  - Persists changes to GuiPreferences.keyBindingRepository and accumulates a restart warning when bindings are changed.
  - Adds user confirmation dialog for resetting all key bindings and a method to load presets.
  - Registers available presets (BashKeyBindingPreset, NewEntryBindingPreset) by default.

- Tests
  - Added and updated unit tests to cover:
    - Validation that invalid key events are not saved.
    - Handling and saving of special keys (function keys).
    - Category items are ignored when assigning bindings.
    - New bindings are stored in the repository and persisted to preferences.
    - Reset-to-default behaviors and nuances around repository state after resets.
  - Some tests include OS/CI assumptions (assumeFalse or DisabledOnCIServer) where appropriate.

Why this change
- Provides a full-featured, discoverable UI for users to search, change, reset, and load presets for keyboard shortcuts.
- Ensures keybinding changes are validated and persisted correctly.
- Adds tests to prevent regressions around keyboard input handling and preference persistence.

Notes for reviewers
- The search/filter behavior expands categories when a search is active; collapsing/expanding all is handled by helper methods.
- Resetting all bindings shows a confirmation dialog via DialogService.
- The view model writes changes to the preferences repository; this will trigger the restart warning returned by getRestartWarnings().

- jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preferences/keybindings/KeyBindingsTab.java
- jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preferences/keybindings/KeyBindingsTabViewModel.java
- jabgui/src/test/java/org/jabref/gui/keyboard/KeyBindingsTabModelTest.java
- jabgui/src/test/java/org/jabref/gui/preferences/keybindings/KeyBindingViewModelTest.java

This PR focuses on functionality and test coverage; follow-up PRs may refine UI styling and additional presets as needed.

Summary

This PR fixes selection of custom export formats with uppercase file extensions for the "Copy -> Export to Clipboard" action (fixes #6285) and refactors ExportToClipboardAction to improve dependency injection, robustness and error handling.

Changes

- CHANGELOG.md: Added entry documenting the fix for uppercase file extensions when exporting to clipboard.

- ExportToClipboardAction
  - Injects ExporterFactory, ClipBoardManager and TaskExecutor instead of accessing Globals directly.
  - Replaced string-based extension filtering with FileType-based filtering using a SUPPORTED_FILETYPES set of StandardFileType values. This prevents issues with case and multi-extension matching.
  - Uses exporterFactory to obtain exporters and filters by exporter.getFileType() instead of comparing raw extensions.
  - Improves background task error handling: logs the exception and shows an error dialog via DialogService on failure (instead of silently swallowing). Uses the injected TaskExecutor to run tasks.
  - Uses injected ClipBoardManager to set clipboard content.
  - Removed an unnecessary exception rethrow and simplified cleanup logic.

- JabRefFrame and RightClickMenu
  - Updated call sites to pass Globals.exportFactory, Globals.clipboardManager and Globals.TASK_EXECUTOR into ExportToClipboardAction constructors.

- TemplateExporter
  - Uses StandardFileType.fromExtensions(...) to construct FileType instances, enabling correct lookup of known file types.

- StandardFileType
  - Added fromExtensions(...) which will return an existing StandardFileType if any of the given extensions match, otherwise an UnknownFileType is created.
  - Added/normalized extensions (HTML includes both "html" and "htm") and clarified that extensions should be lowercase without dots.

- UnknownFileType
  - New class to represent non-standard/unknown file types; normalizes extensions (removes dot, converts to lowercase) and implements equals/hashCode.

- CopyCitationAction
  - Added missing @Override annotation on execute().

Why

Previously exporter selection compared raw extension strings which failed when custom export formats used uppercase extensions or different normalization. The switch to FileType-aware matching combined with normalization in UnknownFileType resolves those issues. Injecting dependencies (ExporterFactory, ClipBoardManager, TaskExecutor) improves testability and reduces reliance on globals. Error handling during export is now surfaced to the user and logged.

Impact

- Fixes #6285 (custom exports with uppercase file extension could not be selected for export-to-clipboard).
- No behavior changes expected for existing exporters except more robust matching and user-visible errors on failures.
- Call sites were updated to pass new dependencies.

Summary

This PR improves Bibtex key generation for title-related patterns by updating BibtexKeyPatternUtil to handle the [title] and [camel] patterns in accordance with the documentation (http://help.jabref.org/en/BibtexKeyPatterns). It addresses behavior reported in issues #2604 and #2589 and builds on earlier work in #2597.

What I changed

- Added cases for the [title] and [camel] key pattern tokens in BibtexKeyPatternUtil.
- Reworked the approach for camel-case conversion: the previous attempt using CaseFormat.LOWER_CAMEL.to(...).replaceAll(...) fails when the title is not already in lowerCamel form. The new handling avoids relying on that assumption and normalizes titles more reliably.
- Updated several tests and added new tests to reflect the documented behavior of title/camel patterns.

Why

The existing implementation produced incorrect keys for many titles because it assumed a specific input case for CaseFormat conversions. The changes aim to make key generation conform to the documented patterns and handle real-world title inputs more robustly.

- Tests: new tests added and some existing tests updated to match documentation-driven expectations.
- Manual testing: features manually tested in a running JabRef build.
- Known issues: there are still failing tests that I need to investigate and fix before this is ready to merge.

EntryEditor: refactor and feature improvements

- Register SpecialFieldUpdateListener for the edited entry so special-field updates (e.g. ranking/quality) propagate to the editor UI.
- Reworked tab construction to better support BibLaTeX: primary/secondary optional fields, deprecated aliases and an optional “Deprecated fields” tab. Other/required/general tabs are handled consistently and custom tab fields from preferences are respected.
- Improved source panel handling:
  - Use a monospaced JTextArea with highlighting and proper focus/key bindings.
  - Robust parsing/storage of edited BibTeX source. Parsing errors now show a clear dialog with options to edit or revert and prevent closing until fixed.
  - getSourceString now uses the LatexFieldFormatter and BibEntryWriter to produce the source representation.
- Add support for a rich set of extra field components via getExtra(): date/time picker, external resource controls, journal abbreviation toggles, content selectors, DOI/Eprint/ISBN helpers, owner setting, yes/no toggles, month picker, gender/editor-type/pagination/type controls and a crossref helper.
- Ensure file list editor instance is tracked when created by any tab so AutoLinkAction can call autoSetLinks() reliably.
- Key and field storage behavior:
  - Centralized StoreFieldAction handles changes to cite keys, regular fields and the source pane; validates and formats fields using LatexFieldFormatter and enforces legal BibTeX key rules.
  - GenerateKeyAction respects preferences (avoid overwriting key / warn before overwriting), generates keys using BibtexKeyPatternUtil and records undo information.
  - Timestamp update logic is integrated into field/key changes and recorded as undoable edits when enabled in preferences.
- Keyboard and UI polish:
  - Consistent key bindings for moving panels, storing fields, help and save actions are set on text components and the toolbar.
  - Type label is rendered vertically and supports right-click to change entry type.
  - Navigation actions (next/previous entry) ensure selection and visibility in the main table.
- Miscellaneous:
  - Improved focus handling so the main table selection follows the entry being edited.
  - Various logging and error handling improvements (debug logs on parse/format errors).

These changes improve BibLaTeX compatibility, robustness of source editing and user experience when editing entries, changing types and working with special fields and file links.

Summary: Add support for recognizing and handling ISBNs and arXiv IDs in the websearch feature.

What this does:
- Detects ISBNs and arXiv identifiers entered into the websearch box (accepts common formats and both prefixed forms like "ISBN:978..." / "arXiv:xxxx.xxxxx" and plain inputs).
- Validates and normalizes detected identifiers.
- Routes identifier queries to the appropriate metadata lookup (bibliographic lookup for ISBN, arXiv metadata for arXiv IDs) and surfaces the returned metadata and direct links in search results.
- Falls back to the existing generic websearch behavior for non-matching inputs.

Why: Many users want to quickly find bibliographic records or paper pages by entering an ISBN or arXiv ID directly. This change streamlines that workflow and returns richer, more relevant results for these identifier-based queries.

Notes on implementation:
- Detection uses regex-based heuristics and validation for ISBN-10/13 and arXiv ID formats.
- Lookups are performed via the configured metadata services; errors fall back to normal websearch and are logged.
- Existing UI/search result formats are reused; identifier results include metadata summary and a link to the source record.

Tests & docs:
- Unit tests added for detection, normalization, and lookup handling of ISBN and arXiv inputs.
- Integration tests verify search flow and fallback behavior.
- Documentation updated to mention supported identifier formats in the websearch help.

Compatibility: Backwards-compatible; no changes to existing websearch behavior for non-identifier queries.

Closes #14237

Summary

This PR fixes an issue where keyboard shortcuts in Preferences → Keyboard shortcuts could not be edited or persisted. Global application shortcuts were consuming KeyEvent instances before the shortcut editor received them, so pressing keys did not update the selected binding and changes were not saved.

What I changed

- Ensure the TreeTableView in KeyBindingsTab receives key presses by adding a KeyEvent filter that consumes the event and forwards it to the ViewModel (KeyBindingsTabViewModel#setNewBindingForCurrent). The existing setOnKeyPressed remains in place.
- Fix persistence of edited shortcuts by syncing the in-memory UI KeyBindingRepository into GuiPreferences in storeSettings(): clear the preferences repository and copy the current bindings so changes actually get saved.
- Updated and added unit tests to reflect and verify the new behavior, including a test that verifies storeSettings writes the edited binding into the preferences repository. Some tests are annotated to be disabled on CI where they are known to be flaky.
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to note the fix.

Files changed

- jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preferences/keybindings/KeyBindingsTab.java
- jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preferences/keybindings/KeyBindingsTabViewModel.java
- jabgui/src/test/java/org/jabref/gui/keyboard/KeyBindingsTabModelTest.java
- jabgui/src/test/java/org/jabref/gui/preferences/keybindings/KeyBindingViewModelTest.java
- CHANGELOG.md

Why this fixes the bug

Global shortcut handling prevented the Preferences keyboard editor from receiving key events. By installing an event filter directly on the key bindings table, we prevent the global shortcuts from intercepting the event and forward it to the ViewModel, so the selected binding updates immediately. Persisting changes by copying the repository contents into GuiPreferences ensures edits are saved and survive restart.

Testing notes / Steps to reproduce

1. Open JabRef → Preferences → Keyboard shortcuts.
2. Select any shortcut entry (e.g., “Close library”).
3. Press a new key combination (e.g., Ctrl+Shift+L).
4. Click Save and restart JabRef.
5. Verify the new shortcut appears in the list and works in the application (e.g., Ctrl+Shift+L closes the library).

Additional

- Added/updated JUnit tests to cover editing and persistence of keybindings.
- CHANGELOG updated to mention the fix.

Linux desktop integration improvements

- Implement robust file and folder opening on Linux: openFile now prefers a user-configured application (from ExternalFileTypes) and falls back to Desktop.getDesktop().open, with xdg-open as a final fallback.

- Correct handling of non-BMP code points in UnicodeToLatexFormatter: use appendCodePoint(...) and skip the next index when encountering a non-BMP code point so high/low surrogates are not treated as separate characters.
- Add a mapping for U+1D716 (mathematical italic epsilon) in HTMLUnicodeConversionMaps so it converts to $\epsilon$.
- Add a unit test (formatHighCodepointUnicodeCharacter) to cover high codepoint conversion and update CHANGELOG.md.

Fixes #7387.

This pull request introduces backward compatibility for JabRef 4.3.1 users who may want to revert from version 5.0. It includes changes to the `PreferencesMigrations` class to ensure that preferences set in version 5.0 can be used in older versions of JabRef. Summary

- jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/frame/JabRefFrame.java: Pass a supplier to OpenConsoleAction that queries getCurrentLibraryTab() at invocation time and returns the active tab's BibDatabaseContext (null-safe). Why
- Previously the Open Console action used the BibDatabaseContext of the tab that was used to build the context menu, which could be different from the currently active tab when the global shortcut was used. This change fixes that discrepancy so the terminal opens in the active library directory.

Related
- Closes #14130

Testing
- Manually tested in a running JabRef instance. A screen recording demonstrating the behavior is included in the PR description.

Notes
- The supplier returns null when no library tab is active; the action is null-safe as before.

This pull request introduces a series of enhancements and bug fixes to the JabRef project, specifically focusing on the `.jbang` scripts and various core functionalities. The changes include:

1. **Enhanced PR Checkout Script**:
   - Improved the script to handle both pull request numbers and branch names.
   - Added support for checking out the main branch if the PR is already merged.
   - Enhanced error handling and logging for better user feedback.

2. **JabRef Code Cloning Script**:
   - Added a new script to clone the JabRef repository, supporting both default and custom target directories.
   - Ensured the script checks if the target directory already exists to avoid unnecessary operations.

3. **JabKit Launcher**:
   - Updated dependencies and runtime options for better compatibility and performance.
   - Added support for multiple repositories and dependency sources.

4. **BibTeX Languageserver Launcher**:
   - Enhanced the launcher script with updated dependencies and runtime configurations.
   - Improved logging and error handling for better diagnostics.

5. **BibTeX Server Launcher**:
   - Updated the launcher script to include new dependencies and runtime options.
   - Added support for multiple repositories and improved logging.

6. **AI Summarization Task**:
   - Introduced a new background task for generating summaries of BibTeX entries using AI models.
   - Added support for summarizing multiple documents and combining summaries.
   - Improved error handling and progress tracking.

7. **BibTeX Functionality Enhancements**:
   - Added new built-in functions for BibTeX processing, including string manipulation and conditional execution.
   - Improved the handling of edge cases and enhanced error messages.

8. **Citation Key Generation**:
   - Enhanced the citation key generator to support custom patterns and regular expressions.
   - Added functionality to append letters to keys to ensure uniqueness.

9. **File Handling Improvements**:
   - Improved the handling of linked files, including moving files to default directories and renaming them.
   - Added support for copying and moving files with or without renaming.

10. **PDF Content Importer**:
    - Enhanced the PDF content importer to better parse and extract bibliographic information from PDF files.
    - Added support for detecting and extracting titles by font size and position.

11. **INSPIRE Bibtex Filter Reader**:
    - Fixed the filter reader to handle special cases and improve the parsing of BibTeX entries from INSPIRE.

12. **Name Formatter**:
    - Added a new layout formatter for flexible name formatting using BibTeX `name.format$` methods.
    - Provided examples and documentation for easier configuration.

13. **URL Download**:
    - Enhanced the URL download class to handle redirects, cookies, and MIME type detection.
    - Improved error handling and logging for better reliability and user experience.

These changes collectively enhance the usability, performance, and robustness of JabRef, making it a more powerful tool for managing bibliographic references.

To address this, the SSL verification bypass has been centralized and moved to the start of the application in `JabRefMain`. Summary

Closes #12634

This PR fixes threading issues in the AbbreviateAction class by ensuring all UI updates run on the JavaFX Application Thread. Previously, some UI mutations were performed from background threads which could trigger exceptions such as IllegalStateException and IndexOutOfBoundsException. The problematic updates are now wrapped to execute on the JavaFX thread (e.g., via Platform.runLater), preventing these race conditions.

What I changed

- Moved UI update code in AbbreviateAction to the JavaFX thread.
- Kept behavior unchanged aside from ensuring thread-safety.

Why

Updating the UI from background threads causes intermittent exceptions and unstable behavior. Running UI updates on the JavaFX thread resolves these issues.

Testing

- Manual testing performed; no exceptions observed.
- Reference: StackOverflow discussion used as guidance.

Notes

- No automated tests were added for this change.
- This PR is focused on thread-safety; no user-visible behavior changes are expected.

Add centralized dependency rules and version constraints for the build platform

This PR introduces a Gradle build logic file that defines dependency conflict resolution, module mappings and extra Java module information, and it updates the versions platform with many dependency constraints.

Key changes:
- Add org.jabref.gradle.base.dependency-rules.gradle.kts
  - Configure gradlex plugins: extra-java-module-info, jvm-dependency-conflict-resolution and java-module-dependencies
  - Enable consistent resolution against the :versions platform
  - Patch JVM dependency variants for org.openjfx JavaFX modules to map platform-specific jar variants (linux, mac, win, aarch64, etc.)
  - Define a number of module-specific patches: removing or adding transitive dependencies, adding API dependencies, merging jars and workarounds (e.g. WireMock, Guava, Kotlin stdlib, jeuclid, log4j-to-slf4j)
  - Configure extraJavaModuleInfo to provide explicit module names, exports, requires, uses, patchRealModule/preserveExisting and other module metadata for many third-party libraries (JavaFX, OkHttp, WireMock, TestFX, Jersey, HK2, JNA, PDFBox, etc.)
  - Set extraJavaModuleInfo failOnAutomaticModules = true and skipLocalJars = true to be strict about automatic modules

- Update versions/build.gradle.kts
  - Add a java-platform project to centralize versions
  - Define version constants (javafx, lucene, pdfbox)
  - Add BOMs and platform registrations (ai.djl BOM, dev.langchain4j BOM, enforcedPlatform for embedded-postgres-binaries)
  - Add a large set of dependency constraints (api) for libraries used across the project (JavaFX modules, DJL/langchain4j modules, WireMock shims, Guava, OkHttp/Okio, PDFBox, Lucene, JUnit/Testing libs, Jersey/HK2, many others)

Why:
- Centralizes version management and platform-enforced dependency resolution
- Provides explicit Java module metadata for non-modular or automatic-module dependencies so builds with the Java module system are more reliable
- Adds platform-aware handling for native JavaFX artifacts to avoid resolution conflicts
- Applies targeted workarounds for known upstream issues (e.g. WireMock) and trims unneeded compile-only transitive deps

No source code logic changes are included — this is build infrastructure and dependency/version management only.

text:
Add Citation Relations tab duplicate detection and import functionality

This PR implements the Citation Relations UI and logic improvements:

- Add a new record CitationRelationItem to hold fetched BibEntry, optional local entry and a boolean flag indicating whether the entry already exists in the current database.
- Implement CitationRelationsTab UI and behavior:
  - Use asynchronous BackgroundTask fetching (citing / cited-by) via BibEntryRelationsRepository and TaskExecutor, with cancel/refresh controls and ProgressIndicator.
  - Display results in a styled CheckListView showing each fetched entry with actions: open URL/DOI, select/add entry, or jump to local entry when a duplicate is detected.
  - Integrate duplicate detection using DuplicateCheck to mark entries already present in the database and show them with a distinct style (duplicate-entry) and a “jump to entry in library” action.
  - Support selecting multiple fetched entries with checkboxes/toggle buttons and an Import button that imports the checked entries into the library and updates the citing/cited fields accordingly via CitationsRelationsTabViewModel.
  - Provide appropriate placeholders/messages when DOI is missing, when no results are found, or when errors occur, and notify the user on abort/success.
  - Improve list cell behavior (no selection model, toggling on click for non-local items) and visual styling via ViewModelListCellFactory.

- Add CSS styling for fetched/duplicate rows and other related UI elements in Base.css (e.g. .duplicate-entry) to visually distinguish duplicates and fetched items.

Additional notes:
- Background tasks for citing and cited-by searches can be canceled/ refreshed independently.
- Error handling shows notifications and provides a restart search button.

This implements the duplicate-checker and import workflow for citation relations (see CHANGELOG entry).

Summary

This PR reworks the BibTeX String Editor dialog to improve UI consistency and behavior. It introduces a redesigned FXML layout with icon buttons, an actions column for deletion, improved table editing behavior, and a new item model for strings. Validation visualization has been refactored to use pseudo-classes and tooltips instead of ControlsFxVisualizer. Several utility classes were updated to support these changes.

What changed

- UI / FXML
  - Replaced the old dialog layout with a new HBox/VBox layout that shows the string table and a vertical toolbar with icon buttons for Help and Add.
  - Added a dedicated actions column (delete icon) in the table.
  - Renamed FXML controls (tblStrings -> stringsList, colLabel -> labelColumn, colContent -> contentColumn, added actionsColumn and addStringButton).

- View (BibtexStringEditorDialogView)
  - Uses the new table columns and icon buttons, binds the table to the viewModel's list property and sets up cell factories.
  - Replaced ControlsFxVisualizer usage with per-cell pseudo-class handling and tooltips.
  - Handles duplicate label detection on label edit; shows an error and restores the old label when a duplicate is entered.
  - When adding a new string, the new row is opened for editing automatically.
  - Uses IconTheme for icons and ValueTableCellFactory for the delete action cell.

- ViewModel (BibtexStringEditorDialogViewModel)
  - Replaced the old BibtexStringViewModel list with a ListProperty<BibtexStringEditorItemModel>.
  - Adds logic to create unique default labels for new strings ("NewString", "NewString1", ...).
  - save() now writes the current list back to the BibDatabase.
  - Exposes labelAlreadyExists(...) and stringsListProperty() for the view to use.

- Item model (BibtexStringEditorItemModel)
  - Renamed from BibtexStringViewModel and adapted validators to the new class name.

- Utilities
  - ViewModelTextFieldTableCellVisualizationFactory: replaced the ControlsFxVisualizer-based approach with a pseudo-class + tooltip approach, added careful handling to find the lazily created TextField inside TextFieldTableCell (small "hack" to support possible HBox graphics), ensures focus/select on startEdit, manages subscriptions to avoid leaks.
  - ViewModelListCellFactory: improved subscription handling and pseudo-class management for validation.

- CSS and localization
  - Moved the .list-cell:invalid/.table-cell:invalid rule to Base.css for consistency and removed the duplicate entry from EntryEditor.css.
  - Updated English localization keys: changed the "Remove selected Strings" translation to "Remove string %0" and removed the old duplicate key.

Notes & rationale

- The TextField inside a TextFieldTableCell is created lazily and is a private member; Node.lookup() couldn't reliably find it early enough. To reliably focus/select the text field when editing starts we inspect the TableCell graphic and handle both the case where the cell graphic is the TextField directly or wrapped inside an HBox. This is admittedly a small hack to work around JavaFX internals but keeps behavior responsive for edit actions.

- Validation visualization was simplified to use pseudo-classes ("invalid") + tooltips and explicit bindings. This avoids the direct dependency on ControlsFxVisualizer in the dialog and keeps the styling consistent (via Base.css).

- The commit removes the old selection-based remove API in favor of an explicit per-row remove action (click delete icon) and a removeString(item) method in the view model.

Known issues / follow-ups

- Table cell validation and certain table-cell related behaviors are still not perfect; this PR is a step toward consistency but additional follow-ups will be needed to fully stabilize validation visuals and edit commit behavior.
- I reworked the commit-on-focus-lost behavior but reverted the change temporarily due to deeper issues with the cell factory — follow-up fixes will be required.

Testing & review notes

- Manual testing required: open the String Editor, add new strings, edit labels and contents, try duplicate labels (should show an error and revert), remove strings using the delete icon, and save.
- Check that invalid cells are styled via the invalid pseudo-class and that tooltips show validation messages.

Related

- Follow-up to #5737. Thanks to @tobiasdiez for the pointer that helped get past the node lookup issues.

Add a new Scite tab to the entry editor

This PR introduces a dedicated "Scite" tab in the entry editor to surface Scite-related information for bibliography entries. Changes include:

- UI: Updated EntryEditorTab.fxml to include the Scite tab in the entry editor layout.
- Implementation: Added SciteTab.java which implements the Scite tab's UI logic and any necessary interactions with the entry editor.
- Integration: EntryEditor.java updated to create/attach the Scite tab alongside existing editor tabs.
- Localization: Added new strings to JabRef_en.properties for the Scite tab labels/messages.
- Tests: Added SciteTabTest.java with unit tests covering the new tab's behavior.
- Changelog: Documented the addition in CHANGELOG.md.

This change adds the UI and basic wiring for the Scite feature; network/error handling and further behavior are covered by the included tests and implementation in SciteTab. The PR is focused on integrating the new tab into the entry editor and providing localization and tests.

Refactor and harden RIS importer parsing

- Cleaned up and centralized parsing logic in RisImporter to make the code easier to follow and maintain.
- Improved robustness against malformed or non-standard RIS files by adding defensive null checks and trimming/unescaping of parsed values.
- Better handling of multi-valued fields (e.g. multiple authors / contributors) so repeated RIS tags are merged into the corresponding BibEntry fields correctly.
- Improved mapping for common fields (DOI, URL, year/date) to reduce incorrect or missing metadata after import.
- Preserve unknown/unsupported tags while improving logging to aid debugging of problematic input files.

These changes reduce runtime errors when importing imperfect RIS files and improve the quality of imported entries. The refactor also lays groundwork for adding more tag mappings and unit tests in follow-up work.

Summary

This PR unifies several equals implementations across the codebase following the discussion in #1631. The intention is to reduce stylistic differences and make the equals logic more consistent, while keeping behavior unchanged.

What I changed

- Harmonized equals implementations in a number of classes, notably ProxyPreferences and FieldChange.
- Applied the same approach where possible to classes implementing Formatter, reconciling cases where equals/hashCode were using defaultEquals/defaultHashCode and cases where they were not.

Notes and caveats

- The style is not exactly identical everywhere, but the core ideas are applied consistently.
- Some of these equals methods look like they were auto-generated; we may want to standardize code generation instead of hand-editing.
- No behavioral changes are intended — this is a refactor to improve consistency.

Follow-ups

- Decide on a canonical equals/hashCode generation strategy (manual, Lombok, IDE generation, or a utility) and apply it project-wide.
- Decide how Formatter implementations should handle defaultEquals/defaultHashCode and make that consistent.
- Consider adding unit tests to lock in equals/hashCode semantics where needed.

Related issue: #1631

text: This PR addresses the performance and memory issues associated with the context menus in the editor by implementing lazy initialization. By using the `Supplier` interface, the context menus are only instantiated when the user right-clicks on a field, significantly reducing the initial memory footprint and improving performance. The changes result in a near-zero impact on both memory and performance when users do not interact with the context menus. Closes #12233

Summary

Adds an optional Markdown rendering toggle to the AI Summary panel so users can view the AI-generated summary as formatted Markdown (rendered HTML) or as raw Markdown text.

What I changed

- Added a "Markdown" CheckBox to org/jabref/gui/ai/components/summary/SummaryShowingComponent.fxml displayed below the AI Summary.
- Implemented toggle handling in org/jabref/gui/ai/components/summary/SummaryShowingComponent.java. When the checkbox is checked the TextArea is hidden and a WebView is shown with rendered HTML; when unchecked the raw TextArea is shown.
- Wrapped the existing TextArea in a StackPane to manage layering and visibility cleanly.
- Implemented the WebView programmatically and lazily (initialized only when needed) to avoid failures in localization-related tests (findMissingLocalizationKeys / findObsoleteLocalizationKeys).
- Used the existing org/jabref/logic/layout/format/MarkdownFormatter.java to convert raw Markdown to HTML for rendering.

Why

Some users prefer to read a formatted summary instead of raw Markdown. This toggle gives users control over the presentation without changing the underlying summary text.

Usage notes

- Toggle the "Markdown" checkbox to switch between raw and rendered views.
- To copy formatted content from the WebView: click inside the WebView, press Ctrl/Cmd + A to select all, then Ctrl/Cmd + C to copy.

- Markdown checkbox unchecked: (raw Markdown view)

Testing & checklist

- Change described in CHANGELOG.md for user-facing change.
- Manually tested in running JabRef.
- Screenshots included in PR description.
- WebView implemented lazily to avoid test interference.

Notes

- No additional Markdown formatting library was introduced; existing MarkdownFormatter is reused.
- WebView creation is programmatic to avoid FXML-related localization test issues.

Summary
Introduce observable preferences for Language and FileHistory. This change makes those preference values reactive: other parts of the app can subscribe to updates and react immediately when language or file history preferences change.

What I changed
- Added an observable preferences layer (API to subscribe/unsubscribe and to get/set values).
- Exposed observable properties for:
  - Language preference
  - FileHistory preference
- Wired preference setters to persistence so changes are saved to storage immediately.
- Updated relevant components to consume the observable preferences instead of reading values once at startup.
- Added unit tests covering change notifications and persistence integration.
- Documentation: brief usage notes for subscribing to changes and an example for language switching.

Why
Making Language and FileHistory preferences observable simplifies keeping UI and services in sync with user preference changes without manual wiring or polling. It also centralizes preference-related side effects (e.g., saving to disk) in one place.

Notes for reviewers / Testing
- Verify subscribing to language changes triggers updates in UI immediately (e.g., language switch controls and localized strings reflect change without reload).
- Verify file history updates notify subscribers when the preference changes and persisted value matches the last change.
- Check tests added under the preferences test suite.
- No breaking changes expected; fallback/default values remain unchanged.

Summary
- Purge legacy field-saving customizations from preferences, GUI and writer/formatter logic as decided in issue #116.
- Simplify BibEntryWriter: remove multiple write styles and user-configurable field-order/spacing/wrapping options; always write required fields first (unsorted), then remaining fields, with indentation based on the longest field name in the entry.
- Simplify LatexFieldFormatter: remove wrap-field behavior and related preference handling.
- Remove GUI elements related to these options from the File preferences tab.
- Make saving less intrusive: only entries changed during a session are reformatted on save (no mandatory reformat of the entire database).

What changed (high level)
- CHANGELOG.md: document removal of field saving options and new save/format behavior.
- JabRefPreferences.java: remove constants and default values for WRITEFIELD_* and INCLUDE_EMPTY_FIELDS preferences.
- BibEntryWriter.java:
  - Remove caching and logic for different write styles (sorted, unsorted, user-defined).
  - Always use the single simplified write strategy (required fields first, remaining fields second).
  - Stop honoring include-empty-fields preference; empty fields are not written.
  - Compute indentation per entry (longest field name) and write the equal sign as part of the field display string.
  - Only reserialize entries that have been modified in the session.
- LatexFieldFormatter.java: remove wrap-field related member and behavior; always format field content via the parser without additional wrapping.
- FileTab.java: remove checkboxes, radio buttons and text fields for field-saving options (include-empty-fields, same-column/spacing, wrap field line, field order controls); update UI accordingly.
- BibEntryWriterTest.java: update tests to reflect new formatting (equal signs placement and entry-level indentation), ensure BibTeX mode is set in tests, and add a new test for adding a field with longer name to verify indentation.

Behavioral notes / migration
- Preferences related to WRITEFIELD_ADDSPACES, WRITEFIELD_SORTSTYLE, WRITEFIELD_USERDEFINEDORDER, WRITEFIELD_WRAPFIELD and INCLUDE_EMPTY_FIELDS have been removed. Existing saved values for these keys will no longer be used.
- Field names are written in lower case and the output now appends ' = ' after the field name; alignment is computed per-entry instead of across the whole database.
- Only entries that were modified during the session will be reformatted on save.

- Added a test (addFieldWithLongerLength) to verify correct per-entry indentation after adding a longer field name.

Summary

- Introduce a FileHistory model and integrate a Recent Libraries menu into the UI.

What I changed

1. New model: FileHistory
   - Added src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/util/io/FileHistory.java
   - FileHistory extends ModifiableObservableListBase<Path> and stores the recent file list with a fixed capacity (HISTORY_SIZE = 8).
   - Provides convenience methods: newFile(Path) (adds-to-top / move-to-top), removeItem(Path), remove/get/size semantics and a static factory FileHistory.of(List<Path>). This makes recent-file data observable for JavaFX UIs.

2. UI: Recent libraries menu
   - Added src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/menus/FileHistoryMenu.java
   - Displays the FileHistory content as a Menu in the File menu.
   - Handles opening files via OpenDatabaseAction and shows an error dialog if a file doesn’t exist (removes it from history in that case).
   - Supports quick access by typed numeric keys (e.g. pressing 1..8 will open the corresponding recent library). To support filenames with underscores, mnemonic parsing is disabled for menu items.
   - Menu is disabled when there are no recent files and is updated when newFile() is called.

3. Integration with preferences and GUI
   - GuiPreferences now holds a FileHistory instance (GuiPreferences constructor / getGuiPreferences()).
   - JabRefPreferences persists recent databases using the existing RECENT_DATABASES key and converts to/from FileHistory via FileHistory.of(...) and storeFileHistory(...) so previous persistence remains compatible.
   - JabRefFrame now creates and uses a FileHistoryMenu, and supports opening recent libraries via key typing when the menu is shown.

4. Tests
   - Added unit tests for FileHistory: src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/util/io/FileHistoryTest.java
   - Tests verify insertion order, move-to-top behavior, removal, size, isEmpty and get(index).

Behavioral notes

- Maximum history size is 8. When adding beyond that, older entries are dropped.
- When a recent file is missing, the user is shown an error dialog and the file is removed from the history.
- FileHistory is observable and integrated with GuiPreferences so UI components can listen to changes and update automatically.

Why this is useful

- Centralizes recent-files handling in a small observable model class and integrates it cleanly with preferences and the UI.
- Enables keyboard access to recent libraries and improves robustness when files have been moved or deleted.
- Adds tests to ensure correct ordering and behavior of the recent-files list.

Summary

- Add secure storage for sensitive credentials using the OS native credential store (java-keyring).
- Add an option to persist the proxy password between sessions and stop storing proxy passwords in clear text.
- Migrate custom fetcher API keys into the OS keyring and load/store them from there.

What changed

- New dependency: com.github.javakeyring:java-keyring:1.0.2 and module requirement (requires java.keyring).
- Preferences & security
  - Proxy password persistence support added (ProxyPreferences.persistPassword).
  - Proxy password is now stored encrypted in the OS keyring when persist is enabled.
  - Fetcher API keys are migrated to the keyring and are read/written encrypted from/to the keyring.
  - Added migrations to move existing fetcher API keys into the keyring at startup (PreferencesMigrations.moveApiKeysToKeyring).
  - JabRefPreferences: new logic to read/write/delete proxy password and fetcher keys using Keyring; clearing preferences now also removes stored fetcher keys from the keyring.

- UI changes
  - Network preferences: added a new checkbox "Persist password between sessions" and bound to the new preference.
  - JabRef startup: if proxy authentication is required and persistence is enabled, proxy will be registered during startup without prompting; otherwise a password dialog is shown.
  - L10n: new entry for the persist-password checkbox label.

- Fixes
  - Fix security issue where proxy password could be stored in clear text. Proxy passwords and custom API keys are now encrypted and stored in the OS keyring.
  - CHANGELOG updated to document the new options and the security fix wording.

- Tests
  - Updated/added unit tests to cover ProxyPreferences changes and the migration to keyring (PreferencesMigrationsTest uses mocked Keyring).

Files touched (high level)
- build.gradle, module-info.java: add java-keyring dependency and module requirement.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preferences/network/*: add UI checkbox and ViewModel wiring for persisting proxy password.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/net/ProxyPreferences.java: add persistPassword property and related methods.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/preferences/JabRefPreferences.java: keyring integration for proxy & fetcher keys, migration helpers, and clearing keyring entries.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/migrations/PreferencesMigrations.java: migration to move fetcher API keys into keyring.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/JabRefGUI.java: startup flow updated to honor persisted proxy passwords.
- src/test/java/*: update and add tests for proxy preferences and migration behavior.
- CHANGELOG.md and l10n resources: document new feature and update wording for the proxy password fix.

Notes and considerations

- When users enable "Persist password between sessions", passwords and API keys will be stored in the OS credential store. If the keyring is unavailable or access fails, JabRef logs a warning and falls back to not using persisted credentials.
- Existing fetcher API keys from preferences will be migrated to the keyring on startup; the legacy keys entry is deleted after a successful migration.
- If a user disables persist for proxy password, the stored proxy credential is removed from the keyring.

This change improves security by removing clear-text storage of credentials and integrates with the OS-provided credential store for better credential handling.

This PR adds support utilities for GUI logging and task execution, and enhances the application exception type:

- Add JabRefException improvements
  - New localizedMessage field and constructors that accept a localized message.
  - getLocalizedMessage() overridden to return the localized message if present, otherwise falls back to getMessage() and logs a debug message.

- Add GuiAppender (Log4j2 plugin)
  - A custom Log4j2 appender that forwards LogEvent objects to the GUI log archive (LogMessages).
  - Ensures a default PatternLayout is used when none is provided and logs an error when the appender name is missing.
  - Appending is performed on the JavaFX application thread via DefaultTaskExecutor.runInJavaFXThread to keep UI updates thread-safe.

- Add DefaultTaskExecutor implementation
  - Utilities to run jobs on the JavaFX thread:
    - runInJavaFXThread(Callable<V>) uses a FutureTask + Platform.runLater and waits for the result, logging Interrupted/Execution exceptions and returning null on failure.
    - runInJavaFXThread(Runnable) posts a Runnable to the JavaFX thread.
  - Implements TaskExecutor.execute(BackgroundTask<V>) by running tasks in a new thread and wrapping them in a JavaFX Task to wire onRunning, onSuccess and onException handlers back to the provided callbacks.
  - Converts non-Exception Throwables into Exception instances when invoking the exception handler.

text:
Fix Linux terminal "working directory" argument handling (#9953)

Summary
- Fix incorrect construction of the "working directory" argument for Linux terminal emulators so opening a terminal uses the intended directory.
- Addresses issue #9953 where terminals opened in the default directory (e.g. home) instead of the selected path.

What changed
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/desktop/os/Linux.java
  - gnome-terminal: pass the flag and path as two separate arguments ["--working-directory", <path>] so ProcessBuilder receives the option and its value correctly.
  - xfce4-terminal: use the single-argument form required by this emulator ["--working-directory=<path>"] (concatenate the path to the flag value).
  - konsole: pass the flag and path as two separate arguments ["--workdir", <path>].
- CHANGELOG.md
  - Add an entry describing the fix in user-facing terms.

Why
- The previous argument formats were malformed for two of the three supported emulators (gnome-terminal and konsole), which caused the working-directory option to be ignored when launching the terminal via ProcessBuilder. xfce4-terminal specifically requires the "--working-directory=<dir>" single-argument format, so it must be provided as one string.

Tests and validation
- No new unit tests were added because asserting which OS command and runtime behavior a spawned terminal uses is brittle and would require substantial refactoring of existing tests. Manual testing was performed to confirm the terminal opens in the selected directory for the supported emulators.

Files changed
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/desktop/os/Linux.java
- CHANGELOG.md

Notes
- This is a targeted fix that corrects argument formatting for common Linux terminal emulators. If more terminal emulators are added in the future, their required argument formats should be confirmed and handled accordingly.

Summary:
Delete the one-time download link immediately after a successful download to prevent reuse and improve security.

What this PR does:
- Updates the download endpoint to invalidate/remove the link once the file has been served.
- Ensures deletion is performed transactionally to avoid race conditions when multiple requests arrive.
- Adds/updates tests (unit and integration) to cover successful deletion, concurrent access, and expected error handling when a link no longer exists.
- Updates the client behavior to show a clear message when a link has expired or been used.
- Adds/updates documentation for the download API to note that links are single-use.

Why:
One-time download links should be unusable after they have been used. This change prevents accidental or malicious reuse of links and aligns behavior with the intended security model.

Testing / How to verify:
1. Create/generate a download link.
2. Use the link to download the file — verify the file is delivered as expected.
3. Attempt to use the same link again — verify the endpoint returns the expected error (404/410) and the UI shows a clear message indicating the link is no longer available.
4. Run automated tests included in this PR to validate deletion behavior and concurrency safeguards.

Notes:
- If any database schema changes were required to track link state, those migrations are included.
- No breaking API changes: callers just need to handle the possibility of a link being immediately unavailable after a prior download.

text: This pull request enhances the DOI parser to handle special characters more effectively. Specifically, it addresses issues where certain characters like backslashes, curly brackets, square brackets, backticks, pipes, and carets were causing problems in parsing DOIs correctly. The changes include updating the regular expression used to clean the DOI string to remove these special characters. text:
Summary

This PR fixes a startup problem that could occur when JabRef is started with files to open. The root cause was that the FileUpdateMonitor instance was not stored on startup, which led to null references later when opening files. Additionally, this PR enables Java assert statements when running the application via Gradle to make the added sanity checks effective during development.

Problem

- fileUpdateMonitor was created in JabRefGUI.initialize() but not assigned to the instance field, resulting in null dereferences when other components expect it to be available (e.g. opening files at startup).
- Assert checks in several places could be useful to catch incorrect initialization, but assertions were not enabled when running via Gradle.

Changes

- jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/JabRefGUI.java
  - Assigns the created DefaultFileUpdateMonitor to this.fileUpdateMonitor so the monitor is available to other components.

- jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/LibraryTab.java
  - Adds assertions that fileUpdateMonitor is non-null when a database path is present (constructor and resetChangeMonitor) to catch incorrect initialization early.

- jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/importer/actions/OpenDatabaseAction.java
  - Adds assertions that fileUpdateMonitor is non-null before opening files and before creating background tasks that rely on it.

- jabgui/build.gradle.kts
  - Enables Java assertions for the Gradle "run" task (enableAssertions = true) so the added assert statements are evaluated during development runs.

Effect

- Prevents startup failures when opening files by ensuring the FileUpdateMonitor is properly initialized and available.
- Improves developer diagnostics by enabling assert checks in Gradle runs.

Related

- Follow-up to #13012

Testing

- Manually tested running JabRef and opening databases at startup; the issue is resolved.

- [x] I own the copyright and license under MIT
- [/] CHANGELOG updated if applicable
- [/] Tests added if applicable
- [x] Manually tested changed features in running JabRef

Notes

- Assertions are enabled only for the Gradle "run" task; production/packaged builds are unaffected unless assertions are explicitly enabled.

text:
Fixes #7420 — Prevent citation keys from being unintentionally overwritten on import

Summary
- Change: When preference 'Citation key patterns' → 'Overwrite existing keys' is unchecked, CitationKeyGenerator.generateKey() will only overwrite the entry's citationKey if it is blank. If the entry already has a non-blank citationKey it will be preserved. When the preference is checked, behavior is unchanged (existing keys are overwritten).

Why
- Previously imports could overwrite existing citation keys even when users had disabled the 'Overwrite existing keys' preference. This restores the expected behaviour and prevents accidental changes to manually-set keys.

What I changed
- Updated CitationKeyGenerator.generateKey() to respect the overwrite preference by only generating a key for blank citationKey values when overwrite is disabled.
- Added unit tests covering the new behavior.
- Manually tested the changed features in a running JabRef instance.

Notes
- Tests were added and manual testing performed (see checklist in PR body).
- No changelog entry added yet — happy to add one if desired or to update documentation if reviewers think it's necessary.

Please review and let me know if the behavior should be adjusted (for example, different semantics for certain import paths).

text:
Add support for pushing citations to Texmaker

Summary
- Implements SourceForge feature requests #318 and #582: allow users to push selected citations from JabRef directly into Texmaker.

What changed
- Added a new PushToTexmaker implementation (src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/external/PushToTexmaker.java) that invokes Texmaker with an insert command and the citation keys.
- Registered the new application so it appears in the list of push targets (PushToApplicationButton.java) and added its settings button to the External preferences tab (ExternalTab.java). The grid layout in the External tab was expanded to accommodate the new button.
- Added preference keys (JabRefPreferences.java): TEXMAKER_PATH and CITE_COMMAND_TEXMAKER, with sensible defaults for Windows and non-Windows installations, and the default cite command matching existing push integrations.
- Persisted settings from the PushToTexmaker settings panel into the global preferences.
- Included a Texmaker icon and entries in the icon properties (src/main/resources/images/crystal_16/texmaker.png and Icons.properties).
- Updated CHANGELOG to announce the new feature.

Behavior and UI
- Users can configure the path to the Texmaker executable and the cite command via the PushToTexmaker settings panel (Browse button included).
- When pushing entries, JabRef will call the configured Texmaker executable with the insert command to insert the formatted citation keys into the active Texmaker document. The operation reports errors to the UI if the path is not defined or the executable cannot be called.

Files touched
- Added: src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/external/PushToTexmaker.java
- Modified: JabRefPreferences.java, PushToApplicationButton.java, ExternalTab.java, CHANGELOG, src/main/resources/images/crystal_16/Icons.properties
- Added icon: src/main/resources/images/crystal_16/texmaker.png

Testing notes
- Configure Texmaker path in the External preferences for Texmaker.
- Select one or more entries in a library, use the Push to Texmaker action, and verify Texmaker receives the citation insert (and that JabRef reports errors if the path is missing or the call fails).

This change integrates Texmaker as a target for the existing push-to-application framework and follows the same preferences/setting patterns used by other editors in JabRef.
