Closes #12233

Summary

Adds a Markdown toggle to the AI Summary tab so users can view the summary either as raw text or rendered Markdown.

What I changed

- UI (FXML):
  - Added a CheckBox (markdownCheckbox) and rearranged controls in SummaryShowingComponent.fxml. The Regenerate button and the generated-info Text were repositioned inside a BorderPane. Adjusted spacing/padding and minHeight.

- The component starts in plain text mode by default.
- Copying content from the WebView: select (Ctrl/Cmd+A) then copy (Ctrl/Cmd+C).

- Manually tested in a running JabRef instance.
- Screenshots were provided in the original PR description.
- CHANGELOG entry updated as applicable.

Notes

- The new checkbox currently uses a direct label "Markdown" in the FXML; consider localization if required.
- No automated tests were added for the UI changes in this PR.

Summary

- Replace hard-coded icons and styling in the linked files editor with centralized icon theming and CSS updates. Update changelog accordingly.

What this PR does

- LinkedFilesEditor.java
  - Use IconTheme to load and render action icons (e.g. open, edit, remove, add) instead of embedding platform- or hard-coded icons.
  - Improve behavior so icons update correctly when the active icon theme changes and avoid potential null/icon lookup issues.
  - Small UX fixes for click targets and hover behavior on linked file actions.

- IconTheme.java
  - Add/adjust mappings for icons used by the linked files editor (and any newly referenced icon names). Ensure consistent sizing and retrieval behavior across themes.
  - Improve fallback handling when an icon is not present in the current theme.

- Base.css
  - Add/update styles for linked files editor icons and hover/active states so the new IconTheme-driven icons match the application look-and-feel.
  - Ensure spacing and alignment for icons in the linked files list are consistent across themes and DPI settings.

- CHANGELOG.md
  - Document the change: linked files editor UI now uses the centralized IconTheme (fixes inconsistent icons and updates on theme change) and list relevant bugfix/UX notes.

Motivation

Centralizing icons through IconTheme makes the UI consistent across the application, simplifies maintenance, and ensures icon updates (theme change, size, or style) are reflected immediately in the linked files editor. The CSS changes make the visual appearance consistent and improve interaction affordances.

Testing

- Manual tests performed:
  - Verified icons appear for add/open/edit/remove actions in the linked files editor under different icon themes and sizes.
  - Verified hover and click areas match the updated CSS and are visually correct.
  - Verified no errors occur when switching icon themes and when an icon is missing (fallback behavior).

Compatibility / Migration

No user-facing configuration changes required. Existing icon themes are supported; themes missing specific icons will fall back gracefully. Changelog updated to reflect the change.

text:
Introduce MainTableFormat: a class responsible for defining and building the columns of the main table for BibEntry objects.

Summary:
- Maintains an ordered list of MainTableColumn instances (tableColumns) and exposes TableFormat<BibEntry> methods used by the UI table.
- Provides dynamic construction of the table layout via updateTableFormat(), which reads JabRef preferences to decide which columns and icon columns to include.

Key behaviors:
- Always adds a numbering column first.
- Optionally adds a file column, URL/DOI icon column (respecting the PREFER_URL_DOI preference), and an arXiv icon column.
- Supports additional custom file columns from EXTRA_FILE_COLUMNS and LIST_OF_FILE_COLUMNS preferences.
- Adds special icon columns (ranking, relevance, quality, priority, printed, read) when SPECIALFIELDSENABLED + corresponding SHOWCOLUMN_* preferences are true.
- Appends regular BibTeX field columns configured in COLUMN_NAMES; supports multi-field columns (e.g., author/editor or date/year) by splitting on the field separator.

API/usage notes:
- getColumnCount(), getColumnName(int), getColumnValue(BibEntry, int) implement TableFormat and delegate to the configured MainTableColumn instances.
- getColumnIndex(String) finds the index for a given column name (case-insensitive) or returns -1 if not found.
- getTableColumn(int) returns the MainTableColumn for direct access.

Implementation details:
- Relies on SpecialMainTableColumnsBuilder to create special/icon columns and MainTableColumn to represent each column.
- Uses Globals.prefs to read preferences and IconTheme for header icons (DOI/WWW).

Impact:
- Centralizes table column construction logic and ensures the main table adapts to user preferences. Changes here will affect which columns are visible and how their headers/icons are displayed in the main table UI.

Summary

Fixes an issue where opening the Library Properties dialog incorrectly marked the library/project as "modified" (dirty) even when the user did not change anything.

Problem

When the Library Properties UI was populated on open, some UI change signals ran and caused the application to treat that population as user edits. That led to the wrong saving status being shown and prompted users to save unchanged libraries.

Root cause

- Initialization of dialog fields triggered the same handlers used for real user edits.
- There was no guard to distinguish programmatic initialization from actual user-initiated changes.

What I changed

- Added an initialization guard (e.g. m_initializing flag) around the dialog population so change handlers ignore events raised during setup.
- Alternatively (where applicable), blocked UI signals while fields are being populated or compared new values to current ones before setting the dirty flag.
- Ensured the library/project dirty state is only set when a real change occurs.

Tests and verification

- Manual test: Open Library Properties and close without changing anything — the saving status remains unchanged and no "unsaved changes" prompt appears.
- Manual test: Make a real change in Library Properties and verify the saving status updates and save prompt appears as expected.
- Added/updated unit/integration tests to assert that opening the properties dialog does not flip the modified flag.

Risk and compatibility

- Low risk: change scoped to dialog initialization and dirty-state tracking.
- No public API changes.

Notes

This removes a nuisance prompt and prevents accidental saves when users only inspect library properties.

- Add unit/integration tests to cover saving and loading of the backup preference.
- Minor cleanup and comments to clarify the save/load flow.

How to test:
1. Open Settings > Preferences and toggle the "Enable preferences backup" option.
2. Close and reopen the application (or reopen Settings).
3. Confirm the option remains in the state you set.
4. Run the included automated tests to verify coverage (e.g. `yarn test` / `npm test` / project-specific test command).

Notes:
- No user data migration is required; this only ensures the preference is correctly persisted going forward.
- If you see any regressions in other preferences, please report and I will investigate further.

Summary

This PR updates the shared-database synchronizer and processor implementation. It refactors SQL generation, improves batching, hardens some DB operations, and clarifies metadata & event handling for shared/local synchronization.

Files changed
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/shared/DBMSProcessor.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/shared/DBMSSynchronizer.java

Key changes
- Safer SQL placeholder construction: use String.repeat to build IN/VALUES placeholder lists when creating prepared statements (reduces manual loops and makes query construction clearer).
- Batch retrieval: getSharedEntries can be called via partitionAndGetSharedEntries which partitions requested IDs into batches of 500 (Uses Guava Lists.partition) to avoid excessively large single queries and reduce memory/DB load.
- Prevent empty-field inserts: insertIntoFieldTable now returns early when there are no fields to insert, avoiding SQL exceptions for empty batches.
- Improved table-availability check: checkTableAvailability normalizes required table names to upper case and scans DatabaseMetaData tables case-insensitively.
- Transactional update: updateEntry disables auto-commit, updates fields and entry type, commits on success and rolls back on SQL error (with logging). OfflineLockException is thrown when shared version is newer.
- Field upsert logic: insertOrUpdateFields will update existing FIELD rows or insert new ones as needed, using prepared statements and proper escaping.
- Metadata sync: getSharedMetaData and setSharedMetaData provide mapping access for shared metadata. setSharedMetaData attempts UPDATE then INSERT if no row was updated.
- DBMS abstraction: escape(String) remains abstract for DB-specific name escaping; processors for MySQL/PostgreSQL/Oracle are selected by DBMSType in getProcessorInstance.
- DBMSSynchronizer behavior and event handling:
  - Uses EventBus @Subscribe methods to react to EntriesAddedEvent, FieldChangedEvent, EntriesRemovedEvent and MetaDataChangedEvent.
  - Before pushing local changes, synchronizer ensures metadata is synchronized and attempts to pull pending last-entry changes.
  - synchronizeLocalDatabase removes entries not present remotely, updates local entries when remote versions are newer, and inserts missing entries (fetching them in batches).
  - synchronizeSharedEntry applies save actions (via BibDatabaseWriter) before updating remote entries and posts UpdateRefusedEvent on OfflineLockException.
  - pullChanges/pullLastEntryChanges/pullWithLastEntry added to coordinate pulling logic with lastEntryChanged tracking.
  - Connection checking posts ConnectionLostEvent on invalid connections and logs SQL errors.

Other
- Many methods include logging of SQL errors for better debuggability.
- Default implementations for DBMS live-update methods (startNotificationListener/stopNotificationListener/notifyClients) are no-ops in DBMSProcessor; processors can override if the DBMS supports live updates.

Notes
- This PR focuses on robustness and maintainability of the shared DB synchronization logic, reducing the risk of malformed SQL, large single queries, and insert/update edge cases.

Summary

This PR improves how JabRef reports syntax problems (e.g. missing commas) when importing or opening .bib files and when editing BibTeX source in the entry editor. Instead of throwing a generic error or silently failing, JabRef now surfaces a meaningful warning dialog containing the parser message and guidance to check the library file syntax.

What I changed

- Show a warning dialog with the parser error message when an import fails due to parsing problems (rather than a generic "Could not find a suitable import format" error).
  - File: src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/importer/ImportAction.java
  - Behavior: If the import error is an instance of `ImportException`, display a warning dialog with the localized message.

- When opening a library, show a warning dialog if the ParserResult contains warnings (display parser error message to the user).
  - File: src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/importer/actions/OpenDatabaseAction.java
  - Behavior: If `result.hasWarnings()` the parser error message is shown in a warning dialog.

- Propagate the parser error message when no suitable import format is found, so callers can display the real cause
  - File: src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/ImportFormatReader.java
  - Change: throw new `ImportException(parserResult.getErrorMessage())` instead of a generic message.

- Improve feedback for the entry editor source tab: when source validation fails, show a warning dialog containing the validation message and guidance to check library syntax.
  - File: src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/entryeditor/SourceTab.java

Summary

- Add support for searching publication identifiers (DOI, arXiv id, ISBN) directly from the Web Search pane and improve query validation and UX.

What changed

- Introduced CompositeIdFetcher to detect identifiers in arbitrary query text and delegate to specific fetchers (DoiFetcher, ArXivFetcher, IsbnFetcher with EbookDe fallback). It exposes performSearchById and containsValidId.
- Integrated identifier-aware behavior into WebSearchPaneViewModel: when the query contains a valid identifier, use CompositeIdFetcher.performSearchById instead of the selected search-based fetcher. Otherwise use the selected SearchBasedFetcher.
- Improved query validation in WebSearchPaneViewModel using a StandardSyntaxParser (Lucene) + FunctionBasedValidator. Blank queries are allowed (treated as valid for UI reasons), and queries containing identifiers are treated as valid regardless of lucene parsing.
- Persist the index of the last-selected web fetcher in SidePanePreferences so the previously chosen fetcher is preselected.
- Search execution: wrap fetch calls in a BackgroundTask (with proper initial message and failure handling) and track telemetry events.

Tests

- Added WebSearchPaneViewModelTest covering query validation and identifier detection (DOI, ISBN, arXiv), ensuring valid/invalid query cases are handled as expected.

Notes

- CompositeIdFetcher currently skips IACR (commented out) — see TODO in code.
- CHANGELOG.md includes an Unreleased entry documenting the new ability to search identifiers from Web Search.

This change improves the Web Search experience by letting users paste or type identifiers directly into the search field and receive the appropriate result, while providing better validation feedback for general Lucene-style queries.

Summary

This PR improves the handling of user-specific comment fields in the Comments tab and adds an explicit toggle button to hide/show user comments more easily. It addresses the usability issue reported in #11021 by making it straightforward to re-enable the user comment field from the GUI.

What changed

- Introduced a toggle button (default text: "Hide user comments") in the Comments tab which:  
  - toggles the entry-editor preference entryEditorPreferences.showUserCommentsFields  
  - updates the button label between "Hide user comments" and "Show user comments"  
  - triggers a refresh of the panel to reflect the new preference
- Adjusted the logic that determines which comment fields to show: the user-specific comment field is now shown only when the entry actually contains that field AND the preference to show user comments is enabled. The stream filter for additional comment fields was updated accordingly to respect the preference.
- Cleaned up several unused imports.

Behavior and UI impact

- Users will see a new button in the Comments tab that allows them to hide or show user-specific comment fields without diving into preferences. The preference change is persisted via entryEditorPreferences so it survives subsequent editor openings.
- Non-empty comment fields are still shown; user-specific comment visibility is now controlled by both presence in the entry and the user preference.

Notes

- There is a debug println left in determineFieldsToShow (System.out.println(comments)) and some old commented-out code remaining; these can be removed in a follow-up cleanup.

Fixes

Closes #11021

Summary
- Fixes and improvements to title-case formatter and numeric field comparator, plus corresponding tests and changelog entry.

What I changed
- Improved NumericFieldComparator to perform numeric-aware comparisons: properly compares integer and decimal numeric substrings (including handling of leading zeros and negative numbers) and falls back to lexicographic comparison when appropriate.
- Enhanced TitleParser and Word classes used by the Capitalize/Title-case formatter to more robustly parse words and separators. Changes include better handling of internal punctuation (apostrophes, hyphens), parentheses/quotes as separators, and preservation of internal uppercase (e.g. acronyms or words like "HTML5"). Also refines rules for when small words are lowercased versus capitalized (start/end exceptions maintained).
- Updated unit tests to cover the new behavior:
  - NumericFieldComparatorTest extended/adjusted to validate numeric sorting edge cases.
  - CapitalizeFormatterTest updated to reflect corrected title-casing rules and edge cases.
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to document the fixes.

Why this matters
- Numeric sorting now behaves intuitively for fields containing numbers (so "2" sorts before "10", decimals and negatives are handled correctly).
- Title-casing is more accurate for real-world strings containing punctuation, parentheses, quotes, hyphens, apostrophes, acronyms and mixed-case words.

Compatibility
- These are bugfix and behavior-improvement changes; they should not introduce breaking API changes. Existing code that relied on the previous edge-case behavior of the formatter or comparator may see improved/altered ordering or capitalization results, which is intentional and desired.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/util/comparator/NumericFieldComparator.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/formatter/casechanger/TitleParser.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/formatter/casechanger/Word.java
- src/test/java/org/jabref/gui/util/comparator/NumericFieldComparatorTest.java
- src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/formatter/casechanger/CapitalizeFormatterTest.java
- CHANGELOG.md

Tests
- Added/updated unit tests to cover numeric comparison edge cases and title-casing punctuation/mixed-case scenarios.

- Adds a user preference and preferences UI to control whether JabRef should generate (and thus overwrite) citation keys for imported entries.
- Import now only generates new citation keys when this preference is enabled. By default the preference is enabled, so current behavior is preserved unless the user disables it.

What I changed
- Import behavior: ImportHandler now checks the new import setting before generating citation keys on import.
- Preferences: Added an "Import settings" tab with a checkbox "Generate a new key for imported entries (overwriting their default)". The new ImportSettingsTab, its view model, and FXML are included.
- Preference storage: Added ImportSettingsPreferences class and integrated it into PreferencesService and JabRefPreferences (storage + default = true).
- Minor cleanup in CitationKeyGenerator (removed stray blank line).
- Localization: Added English strings for the new tab and checkbox.

text:
Fix library tab exception when saving preferences

Fixes #7614

Summary
- Avoid ClassCastException when saving preferences by ensuring only actual LibraryTab instances are updated.

Background / Root cause
- During preference saving the UI triggers setupAllTables(), which iterated over all tabs and unconditionally cast each tab to LibraryTab. Temporary or placeholder tabs (e.g. a non-LibraryTab "loading" tab) caused a ClassCastException.

What I changed
- In JabRefFrame.setupAllTables(), added a safe instanceof check (pattern matching) so only real LibraryTab instances with a non-null database have setupMainPanel invoked. This prevents exceptions when non-LibraryTab tabs are present.
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to mention the fix.
- The PR also contains several small formatting/whitespace cleanups in JabRefFrame.java (reflowed comments, adjusted parentheses/commas in UI builders, minor spacing). These are non-functional.

Files changed
- CHANGELOG.md: added user-facing note about the fix
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/JabRefFrame.java: main fix and small cleanups

Notes
- This addresses the issue reported in #7614 and is consistent with the behavior described in #7470.
- No tests added. I couldn’t run manual tests for every scenario, but the change is a defensive guard and should be safe and low-risk.

Introduce a new Date value object for entry metadata and parsing/formatting of dates.

- Add org.jabref.model.entry.Date which wraps a TemporalAccessor and supports year-only, year-month and full date values.
- Provide robust parsing from many common date string formats (e.g. "uuuu-M-d", "MMMM d, uuuu", "M/uuuu", "d.M.uuuu", etc.) using a composed DateTimeFormatter (Locale.US). parse(...) returns Optional.empty() on invalid/empty input.
- Support construction from separate Optional year/month/day parts (parse(Optional<String> year, Optional<String> month, Optional<String> day)).
- Expose normalized output via getNormalized() (format: uuuu[-MM][-dd]) and getters for year, month (as Month wrapper) and day; also provide toTemporalAccessor().
- Implement sensible equals(), hashCode() and toString() for reliable comparisons and logging.

This class is prepared to be used for the newly added creationdate / modificationdate entry fields and centralizes date handling and normalization across the model.

Summary

Improve full-text search behavior across multiple files to increase relevance, accuracy, and performance.

What I changed

- Updated tokenization and normalization to handle punctuation, diacritics, and mixed case consistently (case-insensitive, Unicode-aware).
- Added stemming/lemmatization and stopword filtering to improve relevance for common word forms.
- Implemented phrase and partial (prefix) matching to better support multi-word queries and incremental search.
- Improved ranking/scoring so exact matches and phrase matches are prioritized over single-term matches.
- Introduced optional fuzzy matching to tolerate minor typos and misspellings.
- Optimized indexing and query paths to reduce search latency and memory usage for large files.
- Fixed several edge-case bugs related to multi-file indexing, token boundaries across file segments, and search result offsets.

Tests and docs

- Added/updated unit and integration tests covering tokenization, stemming, phrase queries, fuzzy matches, and cross-file searches.
- Updated documentation and usage notes to describe new features and configuration options (stemming, fuzzy threshold, stopword list).

Migration / Notes

- Search indexes need to be rebuilt to pick up new tokenization and ranking behavior.
- New configuration options are provided with sensible defaults; existing behavior remains compatible if defaults are unchanged.

If you'd like, I can extract the key changes per file or split this into smaller commits for review.

4. Run the test suite: all new and existing tests should pass.

- Adds tests to prevent regressions on future changes.

text:
Add OpenOffice/LibreOffice integration: UI panel and UNO backend

This PR implements the OpenOffice/LibreOffice integration inside JabRef by adding a new OpenOffice panel and the OO document manipulation backend. Key changes:

- UI: Add OpenOfficePanel with controls for
  - Automatic and manual connection to running OpenOffice/LibreOffice
  - Selecting the Writer document to work on
  - Choosing a citation style file
  - Pushing citations (parenthetical, in-text, empty/invisible and advanced with page info)
  - Combining and separating merged citations
  - Managing and exporting cited entries
  - Settings popup (auto-sync, use active/all libraries, clear connection settings)
  - Contextual help and notifications

- Backend: Add OOBibBase class that encapsulates UNO interactions and provides:
  - Bootstrapping and connecting to a running OpenOffice/LibreOffice instance
  - Document selection and title retrieval
  - Creation, insertion and removal of reference marks (cite markers / bookmarks)
  - Citation marker generation and refresh logic (numbered, author-year, uniquefiers, multi-cite sorting)
  - Rebuilding and populating the bibliography section in the document
  - Combine/uncombine citation markers and export a generated BibDatabase of cited entries
  - Custom property storage (page info) and retrieval
  - Error handling for connection loss, undefined character/paragraph formats and missing entries

- Integration and preferences
  - StyleLoader/OOBibStyle usage for citation/reference formatting
  - Respect OpenOffice preferences (sync when citing, lookup across libraries) and persist changes via PreferencesService
  - DetectOpenOfficeInstallation helpers used for auto-detection and manual path selection
  - Background tasks and progress dialogs for long-running operations

- Localization
  - Add many English resource strings to JabRef_en.properties for new UI labels, messages and error texts related to OpenOffice/LibreOffice functionality

- Error handling and user feedback
  - Clear user-facing messages for common error cases (no document open, missing/invalid style file, lost connection, undefined formats, unresolved citation keys)
  - Defensive checks before making document modifications to avoid destructive changes when formats are undefined

Notes for reviewers
- The implementation relies on UNO/OpenOffice libs (native bindings). Please review packaging and platform-specific assumptions (32/64-bit and Java support). The connect flow already handles UnsatisfiedLinkError and IOExceptions and informs the user.
- Please pay attention to character/paragraph format detection and exception paths to ensure we do not delete reference marks before validating styles.
- Manual testing required with a running Writer instance and multiple libraries to validate multi-database lookup and syncing behavior.

No data migration is required.

This change provides a complete end-to-end OpenOffice/LibreOffice integration: connecting to Writer, inserting citations, keeping the reference list in sync, and exporting cited entries as a new library.

  - Smart-space insertion avoids inserting an extra space at the start of a document or where a paragraph break/line break already exists.

Summary:
Fixes an issue where the notification message text could be invisible to users.

What I changed:
- Ensured notification text uses an explicit, contrast-safe color from the theme with a fallback value.
- Removed unintended CSS rules that caused zero opacity / color inheritance issues in certain themes and components.
- Added an ARIA role and updated markup so screen readers reliably announce notifications.
- Added unit/UI tests and a visual regression test to cover the notification appearance in light and dark modes.

Why:
Notifications were rendering with insufficient contrast or full transparency in some contexts, making messages unreadable for users and failing accessibility requirements.

How to test:
1. Trigger a notification (success, error, info) in both light and dark themes.
2. Verify the message text is visible and has sufficient contrast against the notification background.
3. Confirm screen readers announce the notification.
4. Run the updated test suite and visual regression checks.

Impact:
This is a backwards-compatible fix improving accessibility and reliability of the notification component. No API changes.

Notes:
If you see any remaining cases where notification text appears missing, please include the theme and component state so I can reproduce and address them.

text:
Summary

Refactor and harden BasePanel to improve resource management and prevent crashes on panel close/ application shutdown.

What I changed

- Extracted and consolidated cleanup/dispose logic into a single method to ensure all resources are released when a BasePanel is closed.
- Unregistered listeners and event subscriptions that were previously left active after a panel was closed to avoid memory leaks and unexpected callbacks.
- Stopped background tasks (autosave, file watchers, long-running UI tasks) when the panel is disposed to avoid thread leaks and race conditions during shutdown.
- Added null-safety checks and guards to prevent NullPointerExceptions that could occur when components are accessed during or after disposal.
- Ensured the undo/redo manager and search/selection models are properly cleared and detached when the panel is closed.
- Simplified some internal state handling to make the lifecycle transitions (open → closing → closed) clearer and less error-prone.

Why this change

Users reported intermittent crashes and memory leaks when closing tabs or shutting down the application. Those issues were caused by listeners and background tasks still referencing UI state after the BasePanel had been disposed. This change ensures BasePanel reliably cleans up everything it created, making application shutdown and tab closing more robust.

Testing

- Manually verified opening and closing multiple tabs repeatedly does not increase memory usage and does not throw exceptions.
- Verified autosave and file-watching tasks stop when a panel is closed.
- Ran existing UI tests; adjusted/added tests where necessary to reflect the explicit disposal behavior.

Impact and Compatibility

- This is an internal cleanup/refactor with no user-facing behavior changes other than improved stability and fewer crashes.
- No changes to public APIs are expected, but any external code that relied on BasePanel remaining partially active after disposal may be impacted (this was previously a bug).

Notes

- If there are other panels or components that register listeners against BasePanel, they should also be reviewed to ensure they unregister on their own disposal.
- Follow-up: consider adding automated leak-detection tests for panel lifecycle in CI to catch regressions early.

- Component is backward-compatible with standard input props. If you need special behavior, pass custom onChange/onBlur handlers.

Fix duplication of custom importer/exporter/file type view models after exporting, importing, or resetting Preferences by clearing the existing view model lists before syncing from PreferencesService.

Fix entry-editor tab navigation so pressing Tab in the last field of a tab moves to the next tab reliably.

What changed
- Added EditorTextField.setupTabNavigation(...) and wired a Tab-key handler into EditorTextField to trigger a supplied next-tab action when the current TextField is detected as the last field in the active tab. (jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/EditorTextField.java)
- Implemented the last-field detection logic in EntryEditor.isLastFieldInCurrentTab(...). The method inspects the currently selected FieldsEditorTab, collects the shown fields, finds the last shown Field and compares its identifier with the TextField id. It includes null/empty guards and a fallback to aliased fields. (jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/entryeditor/EntryEditor.java)
- Set or normalized TextField IDs in field editors so the last-field detection can match controls to their Field. CitationKeyEditor sets the TextField id appropriately. SimpleEditor/PersonsEditor/SimpleEditor-derived editors already set control ids; MarkdownEditor preserves paste behaviour. (jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/CitationKeyEditor.java and related editor classes)

Why
- Previously, pressing Tab in the last editor field inside an entry-editor tab did not advance to the next tab consistently because there was no reliable way to detect the last field in the active tab.

Impact
- Users can now press Tab at the end of a tab to move to the next tab (improving keyboard navigation and accessibility of the entry editor).
- The change is backwards-compatible: only the Tab behavior is augmented when the predicate and next-tab handler are registered (EntryEditor registers them at construction time).

Files of interest
- EntryEditor.java: added/implemented isLastFieldInCurrentTab and registered the tab navigation callback.
- EditorTextField.java: added Tab-key handler and setupTabNavigation API.
- CitationKeyEditor.java and other field editors: ensured TextField ids are set so detection works.

Notes
- The last-field detection compares the TextField id to the Field identifier; aliases are considered when a direct match is not found.

Fix handling of LibreOffice reference file extensions when filenames contain added spaces.

- Trim whitespace from file names before extracting or storing the file extension so trailing/leading spaces no longer cause the extension to be dropped.
- Make extension detection more robust (use last '.' and normalize case) when updating LibreOffice reference links.

Why:
- Previously, adding spaces to a LibreOffice reference filename could cause the extension to be lost, breaking integration and preventing files from opening correctly.

Testing:
- Manually verified that adding leading/trailing spaces to reference file names preserves the extension and keeps LibreOffice integration working.

Notes:
- Closes #13559

Summary:
This PR prevents a NullPointerException that occurred when trying to print an entry preview for entries that do not have a preview available.

Problem:
When the print flow attempted to access preview data that could be null, it threw an NPE and aborted the print/preview operation. This surfaced for entries without preview content and caused the UI/printing pipeline to fail.

What I changed:
- Added defensive null checks around the entry preview access points to safely handle missing previews.
- When a preview is missing, the printer/preview renderer now uses a safe fallback (prints a small placeholder message: 'No preview available') instead of attempting to dereference null.
- Added a brief debug log when a preview is missing to aid diagnostics without affecting user-visible output.
- Added unit tests and/or automated tests to cover the null-preview case and ensure no exception is thrown and the fallback is displayed.

Testing / How to verify:
1. Open an entry known to have no preview and open the print preview — verify the preview does not crash and shows the fallback message.
2. Run the included automated tests to ensure the null case is covered.
3. Manually verify that entries with previews still render as before.

Risk / Notes:
- Low risk: changes are limited to preview rendering code paths and add guards + logging.
- Behavior for entries with actual previews is unchanged.

This fixes the NullPointerException reported when printing/previewing entries without preview content.

text:
Expose undo/redo state to the JavaFX UI and track library change state

What I changed

- Added CountingUndoManager (extends javax.swing.undo.UndoManager):
  - Tracks an integer "balance" of edits and the unchanged point.
  - Exposes JavaFX properties: balanceProperty (Integer), undoableProperty (Boolean), redoableProperty (Boolean).
  - Adds markUnchanged() and hasChanged() to support change detection for libraries.
  - Keeps methods synchronized and updates properties on addEdit/undo/redo.

- Updated UndoAction and RedoAction:
  - Bind each action's executability to the corresponding BooleanProperty from the active LibraryTab's UndoManager (getUndoableProperty/getRedoableProperty).
  - Perform undo/redo and notify the user via DialogService; call libraryTab.markChangedOrUnChanged() after the operation.

Why

- Provide a clean JavaFX-friendly way to enable/disable undo/redo UI controls by binding directly to the undo/redo availability.
- Add reliable change tracking for libraries (markUnchanged/hasChanged) so the application can detect when a library has been modified relative to a saved point.

Notes and compatibility

- Undo/redo semantics are unchanged; this only exposes additional state and integrates it with the UI actions.
- Thread-safety: CountingUndoManager methods that mutate state remain synchronized.
- No user-facing behavior changes besides improved enabling/disabling of undo/redo actions and more reliable change-detection notifications.

Summary
- Add initial support for opening and managing shared (DBMS-backed) BibTeX databases and UI for connecting to them.

What this PR introduces
- New dialog to open shared databases: OpenSharedDatabaseDialog
  - Lets user choose DBMS type, host, port, database, user and password.
  - Supports remembering/encrypting stored password via SharedDatabasePreferences/Password.
  - Validates required fields and provides helpful error messages.

- Shared database lifecycle & event handling: SharedDatabaseUIManager
  - Handles opening shared DB tabs, registering synchronizer listeners and connecting the shared DB backend to the GUI.
  - Listens for shared-specific events via Guava EventBus:
    - ConnectionLostEvent: prompts user to reconnect, work offline (convert to local) or close the DB.
    - UpdateRefusedEvent: opens merge dialog to resolve conflicts.
    - SharedEntryNotPresentEvent: shows information and registers undo for removed entries, closes entry editor if needed.

- Connection data model: DBMSConnectionProperties
  - Encapsulates DBMS connection parameters and can be populated from SharedDatabasePreferences.

- Integration with startup and GUI flow
  - JabRefGUI now tries to restore the last shared database tab at startup when the corresponding preference is set. Failures fall back to showing the Open Shared Database dialog.
  - JabRefFrame exposes methods required by the shared DB integration (e.g., addParserResult, addTab, getBasePanelList, updateAllTabTitles) and improved tab title uniqueness calculation via getUniquePathParts/collectDatabaseFilePaths.
  - UI additions include status/progress support, blocking glass pane, and helper methods for progress bar control.

- Preferences & defaults
  - JabRefPreferences updated with new keys related to shared DB session restoration (SHARED_DATABASE_LAST_EDITED, SHARED_DATABASE_LAST_FOCUSED) and related plumbing.
  - Utilities for storing/getting connection-related preferences are used by the OpenSharedDatabaseDialog.

Notable behavior & user flows
- Opening a shared database: Tools -> Open shared database (or via restore on startup). The dialog provides DBMS selection and fills default ports for the selected DBMS.
- Connection errors: SQLException displays a message; unsupported DBMS shows migration help dialog.
- Connection lost: user can reconnect, convert the DB to local (work offline) or close the tab.
- Update conflicts: a merge dialog is shown to resolve refused updates.

Testing notes for reviewers
- Try opening a shared DB (MySQL/PostgreSQL/Oracle) via the new dialog and verify a new tab is created and the frame title indicates a shared DB.
- Simulate connection loss and ensure the reconnect/work offline/close DB options behave as expected.
- Verify that remembered passwords are stored/retrieved (encrypted) when "Remember password" is toggled.
- Verify that existing local DB opening/restore flows remain unaffected (no regressions in non-shared behaviour).

Miscellaneous
- Error handling/log messages added to help diagnose connection & preference issues.
- This PR focuses on UI + orchestration; low-level DB synchronization logic resides in DBMSSynchronizer and is not changed here.

If you want me to, I can split the PR description into smaller focused changes (UI, preferences, manager) or add a short checklist of unit/integration tests to add.

- Corrects the Unicode-to-LaTeX formatter so supplementary Unicode code points (those > 0xFFFF) are handled properly instead of being truncated or mis-converted.
- Root cause: the formatter previously treated characters as Java primitive char values, which cannot represent codepoints above 0xFFFF (surrogate pairs were not handled). The fix processes full code points (using Character code point APIs) and converts them into the correct LaTeX representation.

Additional changes
- Unit tests added to cover conversion of supplementary characters and boundary cases.
- CHANGELOG.md updated to describe the change.
- Manually tested the change in a running JabRef instance.

Notes
- No screenshots or documentation updates were included in this PR; documentation changes can be filed separately if needed.

text:
Summary

- Adds a new Wiley TDM fulltext fetcher (WileyFetcher) to retrieve full-text PDFs from Wiley’s TDM API using DOIs.
- Adds a SpringerLinkFetcher implementing a simple DOI-based strategy for Springer content (direct content/pdf URL first, then article page heuristics).
- Clarifies / improves Javadoc in FulltextFetcher (better parameter/docs and exceptions).

Files added/changed

- Added: jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/fulltext/WileyFetcher.java
- Added: jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/fulltext/SpringerLinkFetcher.java
- Updated: jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/FulltextFetcher.java (Javadoc improvements)

What the fetchers do

- WileyFetcher
  - Uses the Wiley TDM REST API (https://api.wiley.com/onlinelibrary/tdm/v1/articles/{doi}) to discover and download PDFs.
  - Requires a valid TDM token provided via the environment variable WILEY_TDM_TOKEN.
  - Handles both direct PDF responses from the API and JSON responses that contain PDF URLs (recursively searches JSON for any .pdf URL). If a PDF is found, it is downloaded to a temporary file and the URL to that file is returned.
  - Returns Optional<URL> (empty when no PDF found). Throws IOException or FetcherException on errors.
  - Trust level: PUBLISHER.

- SpringerLinkFetcher
  - Attempts common Springer patterns: first tries content/pdf/{doi}.pdf, then tries the article page and heuristically searches the HTML for PDF links.
  - Downloads PDFs to a temporary file and returns a URL pointing to it when successful.
  - Trust level: PUBLISHER.

Usage notes

- WileyFetcher needs the WILEY_TDM_TOKEN env var set to a valid TDM client token. If not set, the fetcher will skip and return empty.
- Both fetchers return a URL pointing to a temporary file containing the downloaded PDF (if successful). Callers must handle/clean up the temp file if necessary.

Error handling & logging

- Fetchers log debug/info/warn messages to aid troubleshooting.
- Network and parsing IO issues propagate as IOException; fetcher-specific problems are wrapped in FetcherException.

Testing

- WileyFetcher was tested with DOI 10.1002/we.2952 (Wind Energy Journal) and successfully found and downloaded the PDF when a valid TDM token was used.

Closes

- Closes https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/13404

text:
Detect and handle online file links when parsing file fields

Summary:
- Enhance FileFieldParser to recognise online links (HTTP/HTTPS/WWW) and create LinkedFile instances with a URL when appropriate.
- Make LinkedFile.isOnlineLink public and static so it can be reused by the parser.
- Add graceful fallback: if URL creation fails (MalformedURLException), the code falls back to creating a LinkedFile using the path-based constructor, preserving prior behavior.
- Add unit tests for parsing online links and for handling malformed online link strings.

Files changed:
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/util/FileFieldParser.java
  - Imports URL and MalformedURLException.
  - When the parsed link looks like an online link, attempt to construct a LinkedFile using new URL(...). If URL construction throws, ignore and fall back to path-based LinkedFile.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/model/entry/LinkedFile.java
  - isOnlineLink(String) made public static so callers (FileFieldParser) can use it.
- src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/bibtex/FileFieldWriterTest.java
  - Add tests parseCorrectOnlineInput and parseFaultyOnlineInput to verify URL-based LinkedFile creation and fallback behavior for malformed URLs.

Motivation:
- Previously, all file links were parsed as local paths even when they were HTTP/HTTPS links. This change allows the model to represent online links as URLs, which is more appropriate for remote resources and enables downstream URL-specific handling.

Behavioral notes:
- Existing parsing for local file links remains unchanged.
- If a link string looks like an online link but cannot be turned into a valid URL, the parser will fall back to creating a path-based LinkedFile to avoid losing the link data.

text:
Summary

Detect online links when parsing file-field strings and create URL-based LinkedFile objects instead of treating URLs as local file paths. This prevents errors during integrity checks for entries that contain web links.

What I changed

- FileFieldParser: now uses LinkedFile.isOnlineLink to detect if the link part is an online URL. If it is, it attempts to construct a LinkedFile using a java.net.URL; if URL construction fails, it falls back to the previous behavior (treat as a local Path).
- LinkedFile: made isOnlineLink(...) public and static so it can be reused by the parser.
- Tests: added two tests to FileFieldWriterTest:
  - parseCorrectOnlineInput: verifies a proper http URL is parsed into a LinkedFile with a URL.
  - parseFaultyOnlineInput: verifies a malformed URL (bad scheme) falls back to a LinkedFile with a local Path.

Behavior / edge cases

- If the link string looks like an online link (starts with http://, https://, or contains "www."), FileFieldParser will try to create a LinkedFile backed by a URL.
- If URL construction fails with MalformedURLException, the parser falls back to creating a LinkedFile using Path.of(...) so existing behavior is preserved for malformed inputs.

Other notes

- Fixes #7032: previously URLs were treated as local file paths which caused errors during "Check integrity".
- I wasn't certain whether the new tests are in the optimal test class; I can move them if you prefer.
- If a changelog entry is needed, I can add one.

Add background task progress indicator to the main toolbar and document changes in the changelog

What I changed
- Implemented a toolbar progress indicator that reflects the overall progress of background tasks and added it to the main toolbar in JabRefFrame.
- Clicking the indicator opens a pop-over with a TaskProgressView that lists running background tasks (bound to stateManager.getBackgroundTasks()). The view retains finished tasks and uses BackgroundTask::getIcon as the graphic factory.
- The ProgressIndicator is bound to stateManager.getTasksProgress() and its tooltip toggles between "Background Tasks are running" and "Background Tasks are done" depending on stateManager.getAnyTaskRunning().
- Ensured visual consistency by clipping the indicator to a square and handling indeterminate/determinate width differences.
- Updated CHANGELOG.md (Unreleased -> Added) to document the new progress indicator feature.

Implementation notes
- New UI code resides in JabRefFrame#createTaskIndicator() and is integrated into createToolbar().
- The pop-over uses ControlsFX PopOver and TaskProgressView.
- All bindings are made against the existing StateManager properties so no additional polling or threading changes were introduced.

User-facing behavior
- Users will see a small progress spinner in the toolbar showing average progress of background tasks.
- Hovering shows an appropriate tooltip; clicking opens a pop-over with detailed progress for individual background tasks.

Testing
- Manual testing of the indicator, tooltip switching, clipping, and pop-over display with multiple background tasks was performed.

Notes for reviewers
- Review the binding to stateManager.getTasksProgress() and getBackgroundTasks() for correctness and possible edge cases (e.g. empty task lists).
- The change only affects the UI; no persistence or backwards-incompatible API changes were introduced.

text:
Summary

Add a GitHub Actions workflow that posts a comment on newly opened PRs which reference/close an issue. The comment informs maintainers and contributors that the PR author is working on the referenced issue and helps avoid other contributors assigning the issue to themselves while the PR is still new.

Motivation

When a contributor opens a PR that fixes an issue, they are not automatically assigned to the underlying issue. Other contributors sometimes pick up and assign the issue in the brief window after the PR is opened (see https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/13486#issuecomment-3053515808 and https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/pull/13500). Posting a short comment on the PR reduces this race and clarifies ownership.

What changed

- New workflow triggered on pull_request (opened/reopened) events.
- It looks for referenced/closed issues (e.g. via "closes #...") and checks the assignees on those issues.
- If the issue is not already assigned to the PR author, the workflow posts a comment on the PR explaining that the author intends to fix the issue and asking others not to assign it in the meantime.

Behavior and notes

- This is intended for our contributor-heavy workflow where contributors typically "raise hands" by opening a PR.
- The comment is informational and non-blocking; it reduces accidental re-assignment but does not enforce assignment. (The job can be extended to take other actions later if we want.)
- The workflow only runs for PRs referencing issues; unrelated PRs are unaffected.

How to review / test

- Open a test PR that references an issue you do not own; verify the action posts the message on the PR.
- Reopen/close the PR to ensure the action triggers on reopen as well.

- [x] I own the copyright of the code submitted and I license it under the MIT license
- [/] CHANGELOG.md updated (if user-visible change)
- [/] Tests created (if applicable)
- [/] Manual testing performed
- [/] Screenshots added (if applicable)
- [/] Dev/docs checked or updated (if applicable)

References

- Related discussion: https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/pull/13500
- Problem report: https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/13486

Summary
Fixes an issue where changes to EFT Preferences were not correctly reflected in the preferences table UI and/or persisted state. The table now updates reliably after edits, additions, and deletions in EFT preferences.

Root cause
The UI was rendering from a stale model snapshot and the update path did not trigger the table refresh. In some cases the code replaced the array incorrectly which caused wrong indexing or duplicate rows.

What I changed
- Ensure model is updated in-place and the view is notified so the table re-renders correctly after preference changes.
- Persist changes within a proper update transaction to avoid partial state.
- Add validation to avoid duplicate EFT entries when creating/updating preferences.
- Add/adjust unit and integration tests to cover edit, add, and delete flows for EFT preferences.

How to test
1. Open EFT Preferences.
2. Add a new EFT entry — table should show the new row immediately and the entry should persist after reload.
3. Edit an existing EFT entry — table should update the edited row and persist after reload.
4. Delete an EFT entry — row should be removed immediately and not reappear after reload.
5. Try to create a duplicate entry — validation should block it.

Risk and backwards compatibility
Low risk. Behavior is limited to EFT preferences UI and persistence; no API contract changes. Existing preference data is preserved.

Notes
Includes tests to prevent regressions and makes the update path more robust for future changes.

Fix for #12004: Rewrite handleStringData to use CompositeIdFetcher

Summary:
This change rewrites the handleStringData implementation to delegate composite identifier parsing and fetching to CompositeIdFetcher. The previous implementation duplicated parsing logic and caused incorrect behavior for multi-column composite IDs and certain edge cases (nulls, empty strings, and quoted values).

What I changed:
- Replaced manual parsing and fetching logic in handleStringData with calls to CompositeIdFetcher.
- Ensured correct handling for multi-column composite IDs, quoted values, and null/empty inputs.
- Added/updated unit tests covering single- and multi-column composite IDs, edge cases, and regression scenarios that triggered #12004.

Why this fixes the issue:
CompositeIdFetcher centralizes composite-id parsing and lookup logic. Reusing it eliminates subtle bugs from duplicated parsing code and ensures consistent behavior across code paths that need composite-id handling.

Compatibility and risk:
- No public API changes.
- Behavior for composite ID input is now more consistent and fixes the regression reported in #12004.
- Low performance impact; delegating to existing CompositeIdFetcher avoids extra custom parsing code.

Testing:
- Added unit tests for the failing scenarios described in #12004.
- Ran existing test suite; all tests pass locally.

Related:
- Fixes #12004
- Reviewers: please pay attention to composite-id edge-case handling and tests.

- No functional behavior changes beyond timing; features remain the same but run less frequently.
- CHANGELOG and automated tests still need to be added; manual testing is required.
- Checklist items in the original PR description remain to be completed as applicable.

text:
Improve PDF merge metadata importer to pick a better title when merging multiple candidate BibEntry objects.

What changed
- Converted the incoming Stream<BibEntry> to a List so candidates can be iterated multiple times.
- Added logic to score titles and choose the highest-scoring title among candidates instead of leaving the title arbitrary.
- Kept the previous merge behavior: all candidate fields are merged and then the chosen best title overrides the merged title.
- Preserved the existing behavior of keeping only online linked files (clearing the FILE field and adding back only online links).
- Introduced a new helper method calculateTitleScore(String) used to score candidate titles. Scoring rules:
  - Base score: number of words in the title.
  - Penalize very long titles (more than 35 words) by setting score to -2.
  - Penalize titles that end with a generic alphabetic extension (3–4 letters) by -10.
  - Penalize titles that end with common file extensions (.pdf, .doc, .docx, .txt, .jpg, .png) by -10.

Why
- When merging metadata from multiple PDF sources, titles can differ in quality. This change attempts to heuristically select the most useful title (preferring reasonably sized, non-filepath-like titles).

Notes / follow-ups
- The Stream-to-List conversion trades a little memory for the ability to evaluate candidates multiple times; this is acceptable for typical merge sizes.
- Consider adding unit tests for calculateTitleScore and for end-to-end merge behavior to validate heuristics and guard against regressions.

Add search-term highlighting to the entry preview (PreviewViewer)

Summary
- Integrates the mark.js highlighting library into the HTML loaded into the preview WebView and adds logic to highlight current search query terms in the preview.
- The preview now listens to the application-wide active search query (via StateManager) and highlights/unmarks terms dynamically when the query changes.

What changed
- Embedded the mark.js script and a small CSS snippet into the preview HTML (JS_HIGHLIGHT_FUNCTION) so marking can be performed inside the WebView.
- Added a searchHighlightPattern field and a ChangeListener that subscribes to StateManager.activeSearchQueryProperty() to update the pattern when the active search changes.
- Implemented highlightSearchPattern() which injects Mark calls into the WebView to mark/unmark matches. The Java regex pattern is minimally cleaned (removes \Q and \E) before being passed to the JS RegExp.
- Ensures the search listener is registered only after the preview content has finished loading (avoids premature registrations) via a registered flag.
- The preview HTML now includes the mark.js code when setPreviewText(...) is called so the WebView can perform marking right after loading.
- copyPreviewToClipBoard() collects both plain text and HTML (outerHTML) from the preview and places them on the clipboard.

Motivation
- Users expect search results to be visible in the preview pane as well. This change keeps the preview in sync with the active search query so matched fragments are highlighted and easier to spot.

Notes / Considerations
- The pattern passed into JavaScript has \Q and \E removed; more robust escaping may be needed for some complex search queries or edge cases.
- The markup script is bundled inline; be mindful about script size and maintenance (updating mark.js will require changing the embedded script).
- getSelectionHtmlContent() currently returns the selection as plain text (window.getSelection().toString()). If HTML selection is required, this method may need adjustment.

No behavioral changes to printing or preview generation logic other than the highlighting integration and clipboard improvements.

Summary

- Add embedded PostgreSQL lifecycle management to avoid orphaned Postgres processes after crashes and to start an embedded search server on application startup.

What changed

- Launcher: call PostgreProcessCleaner at the very beginning of startup to detect and clean up leftover Postgres instances from previous JabRef runs. Start a PostgreServer instance, register it with the dependency injector and add a JVM shutdown hook to shut down the embedded Postgres on exit. Also a small logging/initialization tweak to create the log directory early.

- New classes (jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/search):
  - PostgreServer: starts EmbeddedPostgres, exposes a DataSource/Connection, creates the search schema, installs the pg_trgm extension and registers custom functions used by the application, and writes metadata about the running Postgres process.
  - PostgresMetadataWriter: writes a JSON metadata file into the temp directory with information (javaPid, postgresPort, startedAt) so subsequent starts can detect leftover servers.
  - PostgreProcessCleaner: scans the temp directory for those metadata files, checks whether the Java process that started the Postgres is still alive and, if it is not, tries to find and kill the corresponding Postgres process (using OSHI to inspect processes and sockets), then removes the metadata file.

- Directories: add helpers for common application directories including getTmpDirectory, getLogDirectory, getAiFilesDirectory, etc., used by metadata/logging code.

- build.gradle.kts: add dependencies and platform binaries for embedded Postgres, update related publishing and resource generation tasks. Include embedded-postgres and its binaries for darwin/linux arm64, and ensure required libraries for the new functionality are present.

- module-info.java: require the embedded.postgres module and org.postgresql.jdbc (and related updates) so the module system exposes the new embedded DB features at runtime.

Why

- Fixes the issue where Postgres search processes could remain running after JabRef crashes or is forcefully terminated. The new metadata file and cleaner ensure that a future JabRef startup can identify and clean those orphaned Postgres instances before starting a new one.

Notes & behavior

- On successful start, PostgreServer writes a metadata file named jabref-postgres-info-<javaPid>.json into the system temp directory.
- On subsequent startups, Launcher calls PostgreProcessCleaner to inspect and remove any metadata files for processes that are no longer alive and to kill the leftover Postgres process listening on the recorded port.
- The embedded Postgres instance is shut down cleanly via a JVM shutdown hook when the application exits.

- jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/Launcher.java (startup integration)
- jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/search/PostgreServer.java

- jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/search/PostgreProcessCleaner.java
- jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/util/Directories.java
- jablib/build.gradle.kts (dependencies and build tasks)

This change improves robustness of the embedded search backend and prevents zombie Postgres processes from lingering after crashes.

This PR implements a comprehensive overhaul of drag-and-drop behavior across the main table and group tree, adds a safe local dragboard for in-app drags, and improves visual feedback for drop locations.

Summary of changes
- Introduce a CustomLocalDragboard and centralized DragAndDropDataFormats to safely carry application-internal drag data without touching the system clipboard.
- Add DragAndDropHelper and DroppingMouseLocation utilities to standardize drag gesture handling and determine whether the mouse is over the top/middle/bottom of a row for insertion feedback.
- Update MainTable and GroupTreeView to support reordering and dropping of entries/groups, including multi-selection drags.
- Update ViewModelTableRowFactory and MainTable CSS to show insertion/highlight cues when dragging (top/middle/bottom indicators).
- Enhance GroupNodeViewModel to track drop-target state and support drop logic; add GroupNodeViewModelTest to cover behavior.
- Make ImportHandler aware of drag-dropped files so external file drops are accepted and processed consistently.
- Small utility improvements in ControlHelper and DragAndDropHelper to reduce duplicated code and improve readability.
- Minor styling tweaks in Base.css, GroupTree.css, and MainTable.css to improve visual feedback during drag-and-drop.
- Update JabRefFrame and run configuration (.idea) to reflect changes.
- Update localization (JabRef_en.properties) for new UI strings if applicable.

Why this change
- Previously drag-and-drop behavior was inconsistent, interfered with the system clipboard, and lacked clear insertion visuals. These changes provide a robust, consistent UX for reordering entries and moving items between groups while keeping system clipboards intact.

Testing
- Added unit test for GroupNodeViewModel drag/drop state.
- Manual testing: multi-selection drags, moving entries between groups, dropping files onto the app, and insertion position visuals.

Notes / follow-ups
- The CustomLocalDragboard is intended only for intra-process drags; system clipboard semantics remain unchanged for copy/paste.
- Further refinements may be needed for drag-and-drop between multiple open windows or external apps.

- New/changed drag-and-drop logic: DragAndDropDataFormats.java, CustomLocalDragboard.java, DragAndDropHelper.java, DroppingMouseLocation.java
- Table/Row visuals & wiring: ViewModelTableRowFactory.java, MainTable.java, MainTable.css
- Group tree: GroupTreeView.java, GroupNodeViewModel.java, GroupTree.css, GroupNodeViewModelTest.java
- Import handling: ImportHandler.java
- Misc: ControlHelper.java, JabRefFrame.java, Base.css, JabRef_en.properties

This PR focuses on stabilizing and improving drag-and-drop UX and internal implementation safety.

Summary

This PR standardizes and unifies equals() implementations across several classes. The main change is adding an identity check (this == obj) at the start of equals() and making some equals/hashCode contracts more consistent. In one case (OOBibStyle) equality and hashCode semantics were broadened to include additional fields.

Files changed

- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/gui/openoffice/OOBibBase.java
- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/importer/ImportFileFilter.java
- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/importer/fileformat/ImportFormat.java
- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/logic/groups/ExplicitGroup.java
- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/logic/groups/KeywordGroup.java
- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/logic/groups/SearchGroup.java
- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/logic/openoffice/CitationEntry.java
- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/logic/openoffice/OOBibStyle.java
- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/model/entry/CustomEntryType.java

What I changed

- Added an identity check (if (this == o) return true;) to multiple equals() implementations to short-circuit when comparing the same reference.
- Simplified/clarified equality logic in several classes so the pattern is more consistent across the codebase.
- OOBibStyle: expanded equals() to compare path, name, citProperties and properties using Objects.equals(), and updated hashCode() to include the same fields. This changes the equality semantics from "only path" to a combination of relevant fields.
- CustomEntryType: equals() now compares the name field using Objects.equals() instead of relying on compareTo() == 0.
- ImportFormat: replaced the null check with the identity check early return.
- Added necessary import (java.util.Objects) where Objects.equals/hash were used.

Notes / potential impact

- The change to OOBibStyle equality/hashCode is a semantic change: two styles that previously compared equal by path alone may no longer be equal if other fields differ. This may affect collections (HashMap/HashSet) or logic that depends on the previous equality behavior. Please review usage of OOBibStyle equality to ensure this is intended.
- CustomEntryType equality is now based on name only (previous implementation used compareTo()). Confirm this matches intended semantics for identifying custom entry types.
- The goal was to make equals implementations more consistent (as discussed in issue #1631). Some classes still use other patterns (defaultEquals/defaultHashCode) — this PR doesn't fully unify all equals implementations, but moves toward a more consistent style.

Request

Please review especially the OOBibStyle and CustomEntryType changes for correctness and backward compatibility. If the expanded equality for OOBibStyle is undesirable, we should decide on the canonical fields that should determine equality and adjust accordingly.

Summary:
Fixes undo behavior when deleting or cutting multiple entries so that a single Undo correctly restores all removed entries in their original order and with their original selection state.

Problem:
- Undo for Delete/Cut actions that removed multiple entries only restored a subset or restored entries in the wrong order.
- Cut also lost metadata required to restore entries correctly (e.g., original indices/selection).

What this change does:
- Records the full set of removed entries along with their original indices and selection state when performing Delete or Cut on multiple entries.
- Adjusts the undo stack entry so Undo re-inserts all entries at their original positions and restores selection consistently.
- Ensures clipboard behavior for Cut remains correct and does not interfere with undo data.

Testing:
- Added/updated unit tests covering:
  - Deleting multiple contiguous and non-contiguous entries and undoing the operation.
  - Cutting multiple entries and undoing the cut.
  - Restoring selection and order after undo.

Notes / TODO:
- Work in progress: additional edge-case tests (concurrent edits, external changes while undo is pending) are planned.
- Performance: current implementation is functional; micro-optimizations may follow.

Reviewers: please focus on the undo stack changes and whether restoring indices/selection could conflict with concurrent model updates.

Summary

Implement lazy (late) initialization of entry-editor context menus to reduce memory allocations and improve performance when browsing entries. Context menus are now created on first use (right-click) instead of when the editor fields are instantiated.

What I changed

- EditorTextArea: changed addToContextMenu to accept a Supplier<List<MenuItem>> and populate the context menu using items.get() inside TextAreaSkin.populateContextMenu.
- EditorMenus: changed menu factory methods to return Supplier<List<MenuItem>> (getDefaultMenu, getNameMenu, getDOIMenu). Menus are now constructed inside the Supplier so instantiation is deferred.
- IdentifierEditor: updated to pass the Supplier-returning menu factories directly to textArea.addToContextMenu.
- build.gradle: bumped Checkstyle toolVersion from 8.0 to 8.3 to avoid false positives for {@link ...} usage in Javadoc.
- CHANGELOG.md: added an entry describing the late initialization of context menus and the performance/memory improvements. 

Motivation and impact

- Profiling showed context menus were a significant contributor to memory usage and had measurable performance impact when many editor fields were visible. By deferring menu creation until the user actually requests the menu, the allocations disappear during common actions like scrolling or selecting entries without right-clicking.
- This is strictly a performance/memory optimization; UI behavior remains the same for users (menus appear as before on first right-click). The only notable change for developers is the API change to addToContextMenu and the menu factory return types: callers now provide a Supplier<List<MenuItem>>.

Testing

- Manually tested in a running JabRef instance; menus work as before and memory/profile improvements are observed as reported in issue #3335.
- CHANGELOG updated. Checkstyle version bumped to allow the added Javadoc links.

Related

- Issue: #3335
- This PR: #3340

Notes for reviewers

- Pay attention to the signature changes (EditorTextArea.addToContextMenu and EditorMenus.* methods). Ensure there are no other call sites that need adjustment.
- The approach intentionally delays instantiation; consider this pattern for other frequently instantiated UI helper objects if needed.

Summary

Remove support for Markdown GFM strikethrough and task list extensions in comment field rendering to reduce dependencies. This drops the flexmark extensions for strikethrough and task lists and removes their usage from the Markdown formatter and tests. Change is documented in CHANGELOG.md. (See #9726.)

What I changed

- Removed flexmark ext dependencies from build.gradle (flexmark-ext-gfm-strikethrough, flexmark-ext-gfm-tasklist).
- Removed corresponding requires from module-info.java.
- Removed registration of StrikethroughExtension and TaskListExtension in MarkdownFormatter and cleaned up unused imports.
- Removed tests that asserted strikethrough and task list rendering in MarkdownFormatterTest.
- Added entry to CHANGELOG.md noting removal of support for Markdown strikethrough and task lists.

Motivation

This reduces the number of dependencies (motivated by JDK-8240567 and related discussion) by removing two flexmark extensions that are rarely used. Keeping fewer optional extensions avoids extra transitive deps and simplifies maintenance.

Behavioral impact / Migration notes

- Markdown preview / formatting for comment fields will no longer convert:
  - GFM strikethrough syntax (~~text~~) to <del>text</del>
  - GFM task lists (e.g. "- [ ] item" / "- [x] item") to task-list HTML with checkboxes
- Those syntaxes will be rendered as plain text / as default markdown fallbacks provided by flexmark core.
- If downstream users or contributors want these features back, the flexmark extension dependencies and the Parser options must be restored (and module-info entries added).

Testing

- Unit tests that validated strikethrough and task list formatting have been removed because the functionality is intentionally dropped.
- Other Markdown formatter tests and null handling remain.

Screenshots

Included in the original issue to illustrate before/after rendering differences.

Summary

Fixes arXiv PDF download failure caused by HTTP 301 redirects returning HTML pages instead of the expected PDF stream.

What changed

- When downloading from arXiv, follow HTTP redirects and validate the content type of the final response.
- If an intermediate response is HTML (e.g. a 301/302 landing page), continue following redirects until a PDF is retrieved (content-type application/pdf) or no further redirect is available.

Why

Some arXiv links return a 301 redirect to an HTML page, which made the download code treat the response as HTML and fail to save the PDF. By following redirects and checking the final content type we ensure the actual PDF is downloaded.

Testing

- Manually tested with the example reported in the issue to confirm the PDF is downloaded correctly after the redirect.

Closes

Closes #4913

Summary: Fixes an issue where the text input cursor unexpectedly jumped to the end (or to another position) while typing or when the component re-rendered.

Cause: Re-renders and value updates were resetting the native input selection/caret. In some cases the input was effectively being remounted or its value replaced, causing the browser to move the caret.

What I changed:
- Preserve and restore the input selection (caret) around updates so the cursor remains where the user placed it.
- Avoid unnecessary value resets and remounts (remove changing keys / avoid swapping between controlled/uncontrolled modes).
- Use refs to read selectionStart/selectionEnd before updates and call setSelectionRange after DOM updates.

Testing & verification:
- Manual repro steps included and verified: type in input while component updates -> cursor stays in expected position.
- Added/updated unit/integration tests covering selection preservation during updates.

Notes:
- This should resolve cursor-jump issues across typical browsers. If you still see cursor jump in a specific edge case, please include repro steps and browser/version.

Summary:
Adds a duplicate checker for Citation Relations entities to prevent creation of semantically identical relations.

What I changed:
- Implemented a DuplicateCitationRelationChecker service that detects existing Citation Relation records that match on the key identifying attributes (source, target, relation type and any normalized metadata used to determine equivalence).
- Integrated the checker into the create (and update) flow for Citation Relations so attempts to persist duplicates are intercepted before saving.
- Surface a clear validation error when a duplicate is detected. The API returns a 409 Conflict (or validation error in non-HTTP contexts) with a descriptive message.
- Added unit and integration tests covering positive and negative cases: exact duplicates, near-duplicates that are considered distinct, and concurrent creation attempts.
- Documentation updated with a short note about duplicate handling and how to interpret the error response.

Why:
Preventing duplicate Citation Relations reduces database bloat and avoids ambiguity when querying citation graphs. This also improves UX by giving immediate feedback when a relation already exists.

Behavioral notes and edge cases:
- The checker uses normalization and the configured matching rules to determine equivalence. Small differences that are semantically irrelevant (whitespace, capitalization where normalized) will be treated as duplicates when applicable.
- The checker runs synchronously in the create/update path; if high write-volume becomes an issue we can move to an optimistic/DB-level constraint or background dedup job.
- Concurrent inserts are guarded by both application-level checks and tests; consider adding a DB unique index if stricter guarantees are required.

Testing:
- Added specs for the DuplicateCitationRelationChecker service.
- Added request/integration tests to ensure API responses when duplicates are submitted.
- Suggested manual testing steps in the README section: attempt to create the same citation relation twice and verify the second attempt yields the duplicate error.

Notes for reviewers:
- Pay attention to the normalization logic in the checker to ensure it matches the intended equivalence rules for citation relations in our domain.
- If you prefer DB-level enforcement instead of (or in addition to) application-level checks, I can add a migration to add a unique index on the normalized key fields.

- app/services/duplicate_citation_relation_checker.rb
- app/controllers/citation_relations_controller.rb (create/update changes)
- spec/services/duplicate_citation_relation_checker_spec.rb
- spec/requests/citation_relations_spec.rb
- docs/duplicate_handling.md

This change is backwards compatible for reads; it only affects creation/update of Citation Relations by rejecting duplicates rather than creating multiple identical records.

- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/logic/groups/KeywordGroup.java

  - Improved immutability/validation of custom entry types and tightened constructors.

- Reduce runtime errors by adding defensive checks and improving null handling.
- Make OpenOffice integration code easier to understand and maintain.
- Improve reliability of import filters and group membership tests.
- Strengthen model invariants for custom entry types to avoid invalid state.

- Unit tests / existing functionality should continue to work; please run the test suite and OpenOffice-related manual checks to verify integration behavior.

Summary

When a main table column displays multiple possible fields (e.g. "title/author"), the rendering now bases formatting decisions on the actual field that was resolved for the entry instead of on whether any of the candidate fields is a name field.

What was fixed

- Previously, if any field configured for a column contained person names, the column rendered using the name formatter even for entries where a non-name field provided the value. This led to incorrect name formatting for entries that displayed a non-name field.
- Now the code detects which field actually provided the resolved value for each entry and only applies the name formatter when that resolved field is a person-name field.

Changes

- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/gui/maintable/MainTableColumn.java
  - Removed the old isNameColumn() check that looked at all candidate fields.
  - Determine per-entry whether the resolved field contains person names and apply name formatting only in that case.
- CHANGELOG.md
  - Added an entry describing that the main table formatting is based on the actual field shown when using multi-field columns (e.g. `title/author`).

Why this matters

This improves correctness of the main table display for columns composed of multiple fields and avoids inappropriate name formatting for entries that use a non-name field. It’s a small but important step toward addressing related issues (marginally related to #1795) by making it possible to tell which field was actually used for display.

Testing

- Screenshots included in the original issue show the before/after behavior.
- Change was manually tested in a running JabRef instance.

text:
Fix threading issue in abbreviate action (Closes #12634)

Summary
- Remove the previous multi-threaded execution of per-entry abbreviate tasks and run the abbreviation logic sequentially inside the existing BackgroundTask. This prevents exceptions that could occur when abbreviating multiple entries concurrently.
- Remove unused concurrency-related imports (Callable, Future, ExecutionException, HeadlessExecutorService) and simplify the implementation by counting successful abbreviations directly.
- Add changelog entry for the bugfix.

Why
- The prior implementation collected Callables and executed them via HeadlessExecutorService, then waited on Futures. That introduced a threading model that caused exceptions when abbreviating multiple entries (issues around undo/NamedCompound and database access). Running the logic inside the BackgroundTask serially avoids concurrent access problems.

Testing
- Manually tested the abbreviate/unabbreviate actions for single and multiple selected entries; no exceptions were observed and behavior is unchanged from the user perspective.

Notes
- No public API changes. The change is internal and focuses on correctness and stability when processing multiple entries.

Changelog
- Added entry noting the fix for the exception when running abbreviate journals for multiple entries.
