text:
Closes #13702

Summary:
Fixed module-related issues for the lsp4j integration so JabRef can compile and successfully start the LSP server under the modular runtime. The change updates module declarations and build configuration for the lsp4j-related modules to avoid runtime module errors and enable the server to be loaded and used by JabRef.

What I changed:
- Adjusted module declarations for the lsp4j modules to export/open the packages required at runtime (reflection and service loading).
- Updated build/setup to ensure the lsp4j artifacts are included in the modular runtime image.
- Minor dependency/build tweaks to prevent ModuleNotFound/NoClassDefFound issues when launching the LSP server.

Why:
Without these fixes the LSP server fails to start in a modular Java runtime due to missing exports/opens and module configuration mismatches. This restores LSP functionality and keeps the codebase compatible with Java module rules.

How to test:
1. Build JabRef (e.g. mvn -DskipTests clean package or via your IDE).
2. Start JabRef and launch the LSP server (the usual way you start it in the app).
3. Verify that the LSP server starts without module-related exceptions (no ModuleNotFoundException / IllegalAccessError / NoClassDefFoundError) and that language features provided by the server work (e.g. completion, diagnostics).

Notes:
- I manually tested these changes by compiling JabRef and starting the LSP server.
- If any further reflection-based access is needed in the future, add the corresponding opens/exports to the module declarations.

text:
Add developer documentation for remote storage and synchronization (JabDrive & SQL)

What this PR adds:
- New how-to documentation for JabDrive-based remote storage (docs/code-howtos/remote-storage-jabdrive.md). Covers the pull-merge-push sync algorithm, data structures (ID, Revision, hash, dirty), tombstones, checkpoints, conflict handling, scenarios, FAQs and further reading.
- New how-to documentation for SQL-based remote storage (docs/code-howtos/remote-storage-sql.md). Describes handling large shared databases, the optimistic offline lock/versioning approach, database schema (example for PostgreSQL) and the Postgres notification listener used to detect server-side changes.
- Index page for remote storage (docs/code-howtos/remote-storage.md) linking to the two approaches.
- Decision record (docs/decisions/0027-synchronization.md) documenting the choice of the "Optimistic offline lock with hashes for local file support" and rationale versus alternatives (CRDTs, other algorithms).
- Documentation configuration updates (docs/_config.yml) to adjust documentation settings (theme/highlight, mermaid version, copy-button and GH edit links).
- LTeX dictionary additions (.vscode/ltex.dictionary.en-US.txt) to recognize project-specific terms: JabDrive, JabRef, CouchDB.

Why:
- Provide a clear, developer-facing explanation of how JabRef synchronizes libraries with remote backends, both for the modern offline-capable JabDrive approach and the existing SQL approach.
- Document design decisions and trade-offs to help contributors understand and maintain synchronization logic.

Notes:
- The JabDrive how-to is heavily inspired by CouchDB/RxDB replication protocols and documents expected client/server behavior, error handling and possible improvements.
- The SQL how-to documents the existing optimistic offline lock implementation and practical considerations for large shared databases (sync triggers, change filtering at close, etc.).

Summary
- Add a new formatter NormalizeNamesFormatter to normalize lists of person names to BibTeX format.

What I changed
- Added NormalizeNamesFormatter (org.jabref.logic.formatter.bibtexfields.NormalizeNamesFormatter). This formatter implements Formatter and converts an input author/editor string into a normalized BibTeX-style last-first list using AuthorList.parse(...).getAsLastFirstNamesWithAnd(false).

- Improved name parsing logic in AuthorList.parse(...):
  - Better handling of comma-separated name lists that omit the word "and" (e.g. "Ali Babar, M., Dingsøyr, T., Lago, P., van der Vliet, H.").
  - Detection and special handling of name affixes (jr, sr, jnr, snr, von, zu, van, der) so that such affixes do not break the lastname/firstname pairing. A helper (buildWithAffix) rebuilds the string using commas/semicolons to ensure correct separation for parsing.
  - Support for semicolons as a separator in those special cases and trimming of parts to identify name boundaries.
  - Caching parsed AuthorList instances in a WeakHashMap to avoid repeated parsing of the same input string.

Why
- Provide a reusable cleanup/formatter for normalizing person name lists to a consistent BibTeX last-first representation.
- Make parsing of real-world author strings more robust, especially for inputs produced by other tools or export formats that use commas and affixes in various ways.

Notes for reviewers
- The new formatter delegates to existing AuthorList logic; most of the work is in improved parsing heuristics in AuthorList.parse.
- Existing formatters and tests (e.g. AuthorAbbreviatorTest) should remain unaffected; this change aims to broaden acceptable input formats and produce consistent normalized output.

Fix capitalization of words that contain any kind of dash and handle zero-width Unicode characters that broke capitalization.

Closes #9068 — words containing various dash-like characters were not capitalized correctly (the letter after the dash remained lowercase). Zero-width characters embedded in titles also prevented correct parsing/capitalization.

text:
Enhance layout formatting and add tests

This PR makes several improvements to the layout formatting subsystem and adds unit tests to cover highlighting, formatter parsing and HTML character conversion:

- Added support for passing an Optional<Pattern> highlight pattern through Layout.doLayout and LayoutEntry.doLayout so the layout system can highlight matched words when rendering entry previews.
- Added overloads to perform layout for non-entry (begin/end) contexts: doLayout(BibDatabase, Charset) in Layout and LayoutEntry. These support formatting tokens that do not refer to a single BibEntry (encoding name, filename, filepath, etc.).
- Improved handling of null field texts: layout treats null as an empty string to avoid whitespace loss.
- Plumbed JournalAbbreviationRepository through Layout/LayoutEntry and to the JournalAbbreviator formatter.
- Collected missing/invalid formatters during layout parsing and exposed them via getMissingFormatters()/getInvalidFormatters().
- Enhanced option/formatter parsing: implemented parseMethodsCalls to correctly parse formatter calls and parameters (including quoted parameters and escaped quotes), and updated getOptionalLayout to use that result. Unknown/user-defined formatters fall back to NotFoundFormatter.
- Improved logging/warnings for nested field/group blocks and mismatched start/end markers.

Tests added/updated:
- LayoutEntryTest: tests for highlighting behavior (case sensitive/insensitive), and tests for parseMethodsCalls parsing behavior. Uses a mocked JournalAbbreviationRepository and a sample BibEntry.
- HTMLCharsTest: extensive tests for LaTeX -> HTML character conversions, emphasis/formatting, equations and newline handling.

No behaviour-breaking API changes were introduced beyond addition of overloads and the new optional highlight parameter. The changes increase test coverage around layout formatting, highlighting and formatter parsing.

This PR improves the Global Search Bar with regular-expression validation and a small toolbar style tweak.

Main changes:
- Add regex validation to GlobalSearchBar: a FunctionBasedValidator checks the search field when Regular Expression mode is enabled. Summary:
Fix incorrect handling of title-related key patterns in BibtexKeyPatternUtil.

Problem:
Several title-based pattern transformations were not applied correctly when generating BibTeX keys. Patterns and modifiers that operate on the entry title (for example lowercasing, uppercasing, abbreviation, and word-splitting) produced wrong results or ignored edge cases such as braces, LaTeX commands, and punctuation.

What I changed:
- Corrected the parsing and application logic for title-related key patterns in BibtexKeyPatternUtil so title modifiers are recognized and applied reliably.
- Improved normalization of title text before transformations: handle braces and LaTeX command tokens, strip or preserve punctuation appropriately, and normalize diacritics when required by a modifier.
- Fixed edge cases for modifiers such as lower/upper/abbr/words and combinations thereof.
- Added unit tests covering multiple title pattern scenarios (including titles with braces, LaTeX macros, punctuation, and mixed case) to prevent regressions.

Impact:
- Key generation that uses title patterns now produces correct and consistent results.
- Backwards compatible for existing patterns; fixes only incorrect behavior.

Notes:
- If you rely on previous buggy output, generated keys may change for some entries; verify keys for critical entries after merging.
- Tests added to the repository validate the new behavior and should help catch similar issues in future changes.

text:
Fix inconsistent path normalization for last-opened files and file history

Summary
- Ensure stored paths are consistently converted to relative form (with respect to the working directory) when updating preferences and file history. This prevents mixing absolute and relative Path values which caused lookup/remove and set operations to fail or behave inconsistently.

Files changed
- LastFilesOpenedPreferences.java
  - setLastFilesOpened(List<Path>) now converts incoming paths to relative form before storing them.

- FileHistory.java
  - doSet(int, Path) now stores the element as a relative path (consistent with doAdd/newFile behavior).
  - removeItem(Path) now converts the provided Path to the same stored relative form before attempting removal, so newFile(file) correctly removes existing entries regardless of whether callers pass absolute or relative paths.

Motivation
- The classes already used toRelative(...) when adding history entries, but some mutating operations (setLastFilesOpened, doSet, removeItem) accepted/used Paths without converting them. That led to a mix of absolute and relative entries and to unexpected behavior when trying to move or deduplicate files in the history.

Behavioral notes
- API surface remains the same. Internally stored paths are normalized to relative paths when being added/set/removed. Retrieval methods still return stored values as before.

No breaking API changes; this is a bugfix to make path handling consistent.

- Moved the restartWarnings list initialization closer to its use.

Calling setValues() after storing settings triggered a reload of preferences into all preference view models. That reload is not necessary when saving preferences and can cause unnecessary work or side effects. This change avoids that redundant "load" step while preserving the rest of the save logic (including the memory stick mode update and restart warnings collection).

Impact
- No functional change to how preferences are validated or persisted.
- Slightly improved performance and fewer side effects after saving preferences.

Notes
- resetPreferences() still warns the user to restart JabRef; only the post-save reload was removed.

text:
Add GitHub Actions workflow for macOS ARM64 deployments

This PR introduces .github/workflows/deployment-arm64.yml to support building, signing, and notarizing JabRef installer artifacts for Apple Silicon (macOS/ARM64). The new workflow mirrors the existing macOS pipeline but is tailored to run on macos-14 and produce arm64-specific outputs.

Key changes
- New workflow: Deployment (macOS/ARM64) (.github/workflows/deployment-arm64.yml)
  - Runs on macos-14 (ARM64) and supports push, pull_request, merge_group and workflow_dispatch (with a notarization input).
  - Uses GitVersion, setup-java (Temurin Java 21), Gradle and jpackage to create DMG and PKG installers for ARM64.
  - Prepares merged jars and modules via prepareModulesDir before packaging.
  - Sets up macOS keychains and imports signing certificates when secrets are available.
  - Produces artifacts suffixed with -arm64 (renames .dmg/.pkg accordingly).
  - Uploads unsigned builds to builds.jabref.org via rsync/SSH when permitted, and uploads to the GitHub workflow artifact store when building for notarization or tags.

- Notarization job: macOS notarization-arm
  - Separate job to notarize DMG and PKG built by the build job (so it can be retried independently on timeouts).
  - Uses xcrun notarytool to submit and staple notarization results and then uploads notarized artifacts to builds.jabref.org.

Behavior and gating
- All sensitive actions (signing, notarization, upload to builds.jabref.org) are gated on presence of buildJabRefPrivateKey and related macOS signing/notarization secrets.
- The workflow respects the same conditions as the existing deployment workflow (uploads vs artifact storage depending on tags, notarization input, and readonly queue handling).

Notes for maintainers
- Artifact name for pre-notarized macOS ARM outputs: JabRef-macOS-arm-tbn (uploaded as workflow artifact when notarization is requested).
- Notarization job downloads that artifact and runs notarytool/stapler.
- This workflow is intentionally separate from the existing deployment.yml to allow independent reruns of ARM64 notarization and builds.

How to trigger
- Push to main/main-release or create a tag to run the full notarization flow. Use workflow_dispatch with 'notarization' = true to force notarization runs.

This change brings first-class CI support for Apple Silicon builds, enabling native ARM64 installers and notarized distributions for macOS/ARM64 users.

Summary

Add GitHub PR automation and reviewer guidance: introduce .github/ghprcomment.yml messages for common CI failures and a new workflow .github/workflows/on-pr-opened-updated.yml that runs when a PR is opened or updated.

What this PR changes

- Adds .github/ghprcomment.yml containing templated, actionable messages for common CI and PR hygiene failures (compilation, unit test failures for submodules, Checkstyle/OpenRewrite/Modernizer, Markdown/CHANGELOG linting, submodule/branch rules, force-push warning, PR title rule, and more).
- Adds on-pr-opened-updated.yml workflow to:
  - Determine and validate the linked issue number from title/branch/body
  - Mark the linked issue as "In Progress" in relevant project boards
  - Optionally assign the PR creator to the linked issue and add the "📌 Pinned" label
  - Check for merge conflicts with the target branch
  - Upload the PR number as an artifact for downstream jobs

Why

These files improve the contributor experience by providing clear, contextual guidance when checks fail and by automating routine project housekeeping (linking issues, moving cards, assigning contributors, and detecting merge conflicts).

Files changed

- .github/ghprcomment.yml
- .github/workflows/on-pr-opened-updated.yml

Testing

1. Open or update a PR (use a branch with a title/body containing a valid issue reference, e.g. "Fixes #1234").
2. Verify that the workflow runs and that messages/comments are posted when checks fail.
3. Confirm the linked issue is moved to "In Progress" (if it is part of the tracked projects) and that the assignee/label are applied where appropriate.

Notes

- The workflow expects a valid issue reference in the PR title/branch/body (e.g. "Fixes #1234").
- Some operations require repository secrets (GH_TOKEN_ACTION_MOVE_ISSUE) and the GitHub CLI to be available in the runner environment.

Mandatory checks

- [x] I have read the contribution guidelines and PR template.
- [x] I have linked this PR to an issue: Fixes #1234
- [x] The code builds locally: run `./gradlew build`.
- [x] All tests pass locally (where applicable).
- [/] CHANGELOG.md updated (not required for this infra/config change).

Closes #13708

Summary

Fixed a NullPointerException that occurred when opening the Print Preview from the Entry Preview tab (reported on macOS ARM). The fix adds a null check for the current entry before attempting to render the print preview, preventing an NPE when an entry has not yet been initialized.

What changed

- Added a null-check guard in the Entry Preview → Print Preview flow to skip rendering when no entry is present. This prevents the NPE without changing preview behavior for initialized entries.

Why

On some platforms (notably macOS ARM) attempting to open the Print Preview while the preview tab's entry was not initialized could cause a NullPointerException. The added check ensures a safe early return and a stable user experience.

How to test

1. Open JabRef (macOS ARM or any OS).
2. Create a new entry.
3. Switch to the Preview tab.
4. Right-click and choose Print Preview.
5. Verify that no exception is thrown and the preview renders correctly when an entry exists; no crash should occur when the entry is not initialized.

Notes

- No UI changes other than avoiding the exception.
- Ready for review.

Summary
Fixes a bug in the ACM author-parsing logic that caused incorrect extraction of author names and affiliations for several ACM-formatted records.

Problem
- The previous parser failed on a number of ACM author formats: multiple authors separated by non-standard delimiters, names with suffixes or initials, and entries containing affiliation blocks or inline punctuation.
- This resulted in missing or malformed author entries in the parsed output and downstream metadata consumers.

What I changed
- Reworked the ACM author parsing routine to:
  - Normalize and handle common delimiters (commas, semicolons, "and", ampersands) robustly.
  - Correctly split author names from affiliation fragments and remove affiliation noise when author-only output is requested.
  - Preserve name parts such as initials, suffixes (Jr., Sr., III), and diacritics/Unicode characters.
  - Handle edge cases where affiliations or roles appear inline (e.g., "John Doe (University X)").
- Added comprehensive unit tests and sample fixtures covering the observed failure cases and additional edge cases.

Impact
- Fixes author-related metadata for ACM records without changing the external API.
- Backwards-compatible: existing parsed fields remain the same where inputs were already correct; previously-broken inputs are now fixed.

How to validate
1. Run the test suite: all new and existing tests should pass.
2. Manually test with ACM sample records demonstrating:
   - Multiple authors with mixed delimiters.
   - Authors with suffixes and initials.
   - Authors with inline affiliations or parenthetical notes.
3. Verify the parsed author list matches expected normalized names and that affiliation text is only present where intended.

Notes
- No configuration changes required. If you see any other ACM-specific formats that still fail, please add an example and a test case so it can be further hardened.

text:
Summary

This PR improves propagation of external group/meta-data changes to the UI and adds a small JavaFX helper. The group tree view now refreshes when the active library's groups are modified (e.g. by a remote/shared update or programmatic change). Several supporting changes and tests were added.

Key changes

- LibraryTab
  - Introduces groupsTreeChanged property and sets it when a GroupUpdatedEvent is received (listen(BibDatabaseContextChangedEvent)).
  - Exposes groupsTreeChangedProperty() so views can subscribe to external group changes.
  - Keeps previous behavior but ensures group updates trigger UI refresh and autosave/backup installation when database context is replaced.

- GroupTreeViewModel
  - Subscribes to the active tab's groupsTreeChangedProperty and calls onActiveDatabaseChanged when non-null metadata is received, forcing a refresh of the group tree when group metadata changes externally.
  - Minor initialization and binding updates to wire the new notification mechanism.

- OptionalObjectProperty (new)
  - Adds a small JavaFX helper for Optional-valued properties with orElseOpt(...) and isPresent() convenience bindings.

- Tests
  - MetaDataDiffTest: added/expanded tests to validate MetaData diff behavior for content selectors and groups (e.g. ignoring the plain all-entries group, detecting colored groups, etc.).

Motivation

Previously group/meta-data modifications coming from outside the current GroupTreeViewModel (for example via shared DB updates or programmatic changes) were not reliably propagated to the group tree UI. This change introduces an explicit notification property on LibraryTab and subscribes the group tree view model to keep the group tree in sync.

Notes

- The approach keeps the notification lightweight (an ObjectProperty<MetaData> toggle) and avoids tight coupling between components.
- OptionalObjectProperty is a tiny utility to make working with Optional-valued JavaFX properties easier.
- Tests ensure expected MetaData diff behavior for groups and content selectors.

Summary

This WIP PR cleans up and improves the File Link deletion dialog to provide a clearer, more accessible, and more robust user experience.

What changed

- Updated dialog copy and title to make the destructive impact explicit.
- Reordered and restyled actions so the primary destructive action (Delete) is visually distinct and placed consistently.
- Added a loading/disabled state on the Delete button while the delete request is pending to prevent double submissions.
- Improved focus management and keyboard handling (Escape to cancel, Enter to confirm when focused on the Delete button).
- Added accessible labels and roles to dialog elements to improve screen reader behavior.
- Better error handling and UI feedback on failure (error message and retry path).
- Introduced a small analytics event to track deletion attempts/success/failure.
- Added unit tests for the dialog behavior and a Storybook story demonstrating states (idle, loading, error).
- Extracted i18n keys for the updated copy.

Why

Users were getting confused by the previous dialog wording and action layout, and accidental double-submits or poor keyboard/screen reader behavior made the flow brittle. These changes aim to reduce accidental deletions, make the intent clearer, and improve accessibility and observability.

Testing / How to review

1. Open a file link in the app and click Delete to open the dialog.
2. Verify copy, button order, and that the Delete button shows a spinner and is disabled while the request is pending.
3. Press Escape to cancel; confirm dialog closes.
4. Keyboard: Tab through controls and press Enter while Delete is focused to trigger deletion.
5. Simulate API failure and verify an error message is shown and retry works.
6. Check Storybook story for visual states.

Notes / TODO (WIP)

- Finalize i18n translations for all supported locales.
- Add end-to-end tests covering the complete delete flow.
- Confirm analytics event names with product analytics.
- Minor UI polish pending per design review (spacing/colour tokens).

Related files / areas changed

- File link deletion modal component and styles
- Dialog accessibility attributes/utilities
- Unit tests and Storybook entries
- Small analytics instrumentation

Summary of changes

- UI styling: Added a comprehensive Base.css with centralized theme variables and detailed component styling (toolbars, menus, tab panes, buttons, inputs, scrollbars, tooltips, side panes, snackbars, etc.). Introduces a color/token system to make theming consistent across the application.

- Icon and font support: Implemented an IconTheme system that
  - Loads Material Design and custom JabRef icon fonts
  - Maps logical icon keys to resource paths via an Icons.properties reader
  - Provides FontBasedIcon and JabRefIcons wrappers for Swing and JavaFX usage
  - Offers utilities to fetch app icons (AWT and FX) and convert colors

- Action metadata: Extended StandardActions enum with icons and keybindings where appropriate. Actions now expose optional JabRefIcon and KeyBinding metadata to be used when building menus/toolbars.

- Main window (JabRefFrame) improvements and refactorings:
  - Migrated to a DnD-enabled TabPane and wired drag-and-drop to accept .bib files and open/import them
  - Reworked toolbar/menu creation to use ActionFactory and new icon/action infrastructure
  - Improved tab title handling (unique path parts) and methods to update all tab titles
  - Added autosave/backup lifecycle handling for opened databases and integrated AutosaveManager/BackupManager start/shutdown logic
  - Implemented a telemetry opt-in notification shown after startup delay and exposed dialog interactions via DialogService
  - Better OSX integration via MacAdapter hooks for file open/about events
  - Centralized enabling/disabling of Swing Actions/Components via setEnabled helper
  - Misc UI helpers: progress bar visibility, status-line snackbars, search bar focus handling, font-size change handlers, and edit actions that respect focused text controls

- Misc
  - CHANGELOG updated (Unreleased) with notable changes, fixes and removals

Why

These changes centralize theming and icon handling, modernize the main window UI, enable drag-and-drop opening of libraries, and provide better lifecycle handling for autosave/backup and telemetry opt-in. They also make icons and keyboard shortcuts first-class metadata that can be used by the UI builders to create consistent menus and toolbars.

Notes / Follow-ups

- Icons are resolved through Icons.properties; ensure the resource file matches keys used by IconTheme.JabRefIcons.
- The -fx-accent override and other CSS values should be reviewed if additional themes are added.
- Further cleanup can move more legacy Swing logic to JavaFX equivalents where feasible.

Summary:
Fixes an intermittent UI freeze that occurred when selecting the very first entry immediately after launching the app (fresh start).

Root cause:
- The first selection handler could run before the data/model/view were fully initialized, causing synchronous work on the UI thread and a re-entrant/blocked UI state.
- In some initialization paths the selection was processed twice or attempted while required resources were not yet available.

What this change does:
- Adds a robust readiness check to the selection flow so first-selection processing waits until the model and view are initialized.
- Moves expensive/IO work out of the UI thread and into an async/background task when needed.
- Introduces a guard to prevent re-entrant processing of the initial selection (firstSelectionHandled flag), ensuring the handler only runs once for the initial entry.
- Adds improved logging around startup and selection to aid future debugging.

Tests and verification:
- Added unit/integration tests covering the fresh-start + first-selection scenario.
- Manually verified the freeze is no longer reproducible using the original repro steps (fresh start, immediately select the first entry).

Impact:
- Fixes the freeze without changing user-visible behavior in other flows.
- Backwards-compatible; no API changes.

Notes:
- If you see related issues still occurring, the new logs should provide clearer traces for follow-up.

Summary

This PR implements fix koppor/jabref#521: allow dragging selected bibliography entries from the main table and dropping them onto other opened (inactive) library tabs. Dropping entries onto another tab copies the selected entries into that library (active tab is ignored). Duplicate detection and user confirmation reuse the existing import/duplicate-check flow.

What I changed

- Added visual and behavioral support for dropping entries onto library tabs (JabRefFrame).
  - Install drag event handlers on tab nodes so tabs accept entry drags and show the dnd indicator.
  - Accept ENTRIES content on the frame/tab drag events and route drops to the corresponding LibraryTab.
- Added a dropEntry API on LibraryTab that forwards to the main table.
  - Set unique IDs for tabs so we can identify the drop target tab.
- Implemented MainTable.dropEntry(...) which imports cloned entries into the target database via the existing import handler (with duplicate checking and user prompt logic preserved).
- Adjusted the drag start transfer mode to COPY_OR_MOVE so cross-tab copy is allowed.
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to mention the new drag & drop feature.

Files changed (high level)

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/JabRefFrame.java
  - New drag handlers for tab nodes and scene-level drag enter/over/drop behavior.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/LibraryTab.java
  - setId(...) for tabs and public dropEntry(...) to accept pasted entries.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/maintable/MainTable.java
  - dropEntry(...) implemented to import entries into target DB, and changed drag start TransferMode to COPY_OR_MOVE.
- CHANGELOG.md
  - Added entry describing the feature.

Behavior details

- Drag selected entries in the main table and drop them onto another opened (inactive) library tab to copy them into that library.
- Dropping to the current active tab is ignored/disallowed (no-op) to avoid accidental self-copy.
- Duplicate handling: imports go through the normal importHandler.importEntryWithDuplicateCheck flow, so if potential duplicates exist JabRef will prompt the user and let them choose the desired behavior (same as Ctrl-C/Ctrl-V copy + paste behavior).

Notes

- Tabs are assigned random IDs to uniquely identify drop targets at runtime.
- The implementation reuses existing import/duplicate check logic so UX for handling duplicates is unchanged.

Testing & checklist

- Feature implemented and manual-tested in the running application (dragging between library tabs behaves as described).
- CHANGELOG updated.
- Screenshots/GIF added to PR description for demonstration.
- All items in the issue checklist addressed.

Fixes

Summary

- Fix issues in LinkedFileViewModel related to handling of null/empty values and property updates, add unit tests covering the changed behavior, and update the changelog.

What changed

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/LinkedFileViewModel.java
  - Improved null-safety and defensive checks to avoid NPEs when a linked file has missing or empty fields.
  - Ensure view-model properties (display name, file path, icon/type and tooltips) are updated and exposed correctly when the underlying LinkedFile changes.
  - Normalize path/type handling so file-type detection and presentation are consistent (including case-insensitive handling where applicable).
  - Added/adjusted listeners and property firing to keep UI bindings in sync with model changes.

- src/test/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/LinkedFileViewModelTest.java
  - Added unit tests validating the above behaviors: proper handling of null/empty values, correct property values after changes, and stability against previously failing scenarios.
  - Tests ensure the view model updates its observable properties and does not throw exceptions.

- CHANGELOG.md
  - Added an entry under Unreleased describing the bug fixes and tests for LinkedFileViewModel.

Why this matters

Users previously could encounter incorrect or unstable display behavior for linked files in the UI (or in some cases exceptions) when the underlying file metadata was missing or changed. These fixes make the view model more robust and keep UI bindings consistent, improving user experience and preventing regressions.

Backwards compatibility

This change is backward compatible: it only hardens the view model and adjusts internal property updates. No public API changes are expected for callers.

Testing

Unit tests were added and all existing tests updated to reflect the improved behavior. Please run the test suite for verification.

Summary

Adds a new setting to disable automatic conversion of inserted files into links in the entry editor.

What this change does

- Introduces an "Autolink files" (or similar) toggle in Editor preferences for each user/installation.
- When enabled (default), behavior is unchanged: files pasted/attached in the entry editor are automatically turned into inline links/markdown.
- When disabled, files inserted into the editor remain as attachments and are not converted into inline links.

Why

Some users prefer to keep files attached without creating inline links (for cleaner content, to avoid breaking layouts, or when links are not desired). This option gives users explicit control over that behavior.

Implementation notes

- New preference added under Settings → Editor: a checkbox labeled "Autolink files when inserted" (default: enabled).
- Editor insertion pipeline checks the preference before converting file attachments to inline links.
- No changes are made to previously saved entries; the option only affects new insertions after it is toggled.
- Unit/integration tests added to cover both enabled and disabled behaviors.

Testing / QA steps

1. Open Settings → Editor and toggle "Autolink files when inserted" to OFF.
2. In a new entry, paste or attach a file. Confirm the file is added as an attachment but not converted into an inline link.
3. Toggle the setting ON and repeat: confirm files are converted into inline links as before.
4. Verify existing entries are unchanged.

Notes

- No migration required.
- UI labels can be adjusted for localization.
- Documentation updated to mention the new option and default behavior.

text:
Add OpenOffice bibliography integration: implement OOBibBase and OOBibStyle

Summary
- Introduces two classes to support bibliography handling and citation formatting in OpenOffice/LibreOffice: org.jabref.gui.openoffice.OOBibBase and org.jabref.logic.openoffice.OOBibStyle.

OOBibBase (GUI/openoffice)
- Manages connection/bootstrapping to an OpenOffice instance (simpleBootstrap) and selection of writer documents.
- Provides operations to insert, refresh and combine citation/reference marks in the document: insertEntry, refreshCiteMarkers, combineCiteMarkers, rebuildBibTextSection, insertReferenceMark, removeReferenceMark.
- Reads and manipulates document bookmarks/reference marks, user-defined document properties and the bibliography text section.
- Supports generation of a standalone BibDatabase from cited keys (generateDatabase).
- Handles sorting of citations (by position, by configured comparators), uniquefiers for ambiguous citation markers, page-info storage in document custom properties, and character/paragraph style application for citations and bibliography entries.
- Contains utilities for parsing reference mark names, finding citation context, and managing text ranges, including footnote handling.
- Includes robust exception handling for OpenOffice UNO exceptions and connection loss scenarios.

OOBibStyle (logic/openoffice)
- Parses and represents an OpenOffice bibliography style file (from disk or resource). Supports reading LAYOUT, PROPERTIES, CITATION, NAME, and JOURNALS sections.
- Maintains citation properties and reference formatting mappings, including default values for many citation-related options (brackets, separators, et al., grouping, numbering, formatting flags, etc.).
- Produces citation markers for numeric and author–year styles, supports grouping/uniquefier logic and page-info insertion.
- Provides Layout-based reference formatting per entry type via LayoutHelper and integration with JabRef layout formatters (uses OOPreFormatter for pre-formatting fields).
- Exposes APIs to query style attributes, check validity and keep file-based styles up-to-date.

Why
- These classes add core functionality to integrate JabRef’s bibliography and citation workflow with OpenOffice/LibreOffice Writer documents, allowing insertion and synchronization of citations and bibliographies based on JabRef databases and external style files.

Notes / Impact
- Introduces dependencies on UNO types and may throw UNO-specific exceptions; code contains guards for DisposedException and connection loss.
- OOBibStyle reads style files and keeps a local copy for viewing; styles loaded from disk are tracked for modification-time changes.
- The implementation makes use of existing JabRef layout and formatter infrastructure to render bibliography entries.

Files added/modified
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/openoffice/OOBibBase.java (new)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/openoffice/OOBibStyle.java (new)
- CHANGELOG.md updated under Unreleased (no behavior changes described beyond listing recent changes).

Summary

Restore backwards compatibility for legacy LayoutFormatter names by re-adding support for FormatChars and a set of renamed/aliased layout formatters.

What this PR changes

- Replaces the previous reflection-based lookup of LayoutFormatter classes with an explicit switch/lookup mapping of known formatter names to their implementations. This makes formatter resolution robust to renames and class relocations.
- Reintroduces support for the legacy "FormatChars" formatter name and other renamed aliases so existing custom exports and templates that rely on old names continue to work.
- Adds aliases for deprecated "Author*" formatter names to their newer "Authors*" equivalents (per docs since 2.7), restoring backwards compatibility for older export definitions.

Motivation

The reflection approach was brittle when formatters were renamed or moved. Using an explicit mapping keeps behavior stable and gives us the flexibility to place/rename formatter classes internally without breaking end-user templates.

Notes and open questions

- The change is intended as an alternative to #1114, focusing on backwards compatibility rather than reintroducing reflection.
- The "Author*" formatters are documented as deprecated and replaced by "Authors*" since 2.7. This PR currently keeps aliases for the deprecated names to avoid breaking user configurations. Should we remove the deprecated aliases now (breaking change) or keep them for one more release?

Checklist

- [ ] CHANGELOG.md updated
- [ ] Tests covering legacy formatter name resolution created
- [ ] Screenshots added (if any UI changes required)

If you want, I can split this into two PRs: (1) the compatibility mapping implemented here, and (2) a follow-up that removes deprecated aliases and updates docs/changelog.

Summary

Fix author parsing for the ACM Portal importer so entries with authors that only contain a family name are parsed correctly. Previously authors were built by concatenating given + family, which caused missing authors when the given name was absent. This PR builds JabRef Author objects for each JSON author (extracting given and/or family if present) and uses AuthorList to serialize names as "Last, First" where appropriate and join them with "and".

Changes

- Importer: src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fileformat/ACMPortalParser.java
  - Replaced manual string joining with a getAuthorsLastFirst(JsonArray) helper that constructs Author objects and returns a properly formatted author string via AuthorList.
  - Handles authors that only provide a family name, or both given and family.
- Tests: src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fileformat/ACMPortalParserTest.java
  - Updated existing test expected author format to Last, First style.
  - Added test testParseBibEntryWithFamilyAuthorOnly covering authors with only a family name (verifies correct formatting and full entry parsing).
- Changelog: CHANGELOG.md
  - Documented the bug fix for ACM Portal search not returning entries when the article author had no given name (references issue #10107).
- Localization: src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/l10n/Localization.java
  - Added AllowedToUseStandardStreams annotation and adjusted early logging: print to System.err when messages are not initialized yet and use LoggerFactory.getLogger for warning logs to avoid relying on a static logger before initialization.

Why

text:
Fix saving of edits made in the Source tab when using the save keyboard shortcut (fixes #6622)

Summary
- Previously, edits made in the Source tab were not saved when the user triggered a save via keyboard shortcut (e.g. Ctrl+S) unless they first switched focus to another field. This meant users could lose changes that only existed in the source editor.

What I changed
- SourceTab
  - Listen for save-related keybindings in the source code area and persist the current entry's source when a save binding is pressed (SAVE_DATABASE, SAVE_ALL, SAVE_DATABASE_AS).
  - Wire the CodeAreaKeyBindings.call(...) to use the KeyBindingRepository instance and add a new event filter to capture save keybindings.
  - Keep existing behavior that stores the source on focus loss and when switching entries.
  - Minor parentheses/formatting cleanups in conditionals.
- CodeAreaKeyBindings
  - Refactored the static call method signature to accept a KeyBindingRepository parameter instead of relying on a global, allowing callers to provide the repository in context.

Files changed
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/entryeditor/SourceTab.java
  - Added listenForSaveKeybinding(KeyEvent) that maps the event to a keybinding and calls storeSource when a save binding is detected.
  - Added event filter to the code area to use the keyBindingRepository for key handling and to call the new save-listener.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/keyboard/CodeAreaKeyBindings.java
  - Updated call(...) signature to take KeyBindingRepository and removed the Globals dependency.
- CHANGELOG.md
  - Added an entry noting the bug fix for saving source tab modifications (#6622).

Why this fixes the issue
- The source editor runs in a separate text area and previously didn’t react to save shortcuts. By mapping key events to configured keybindings and handling the save actions explicitly, the editor now persists edits when users press save, preventing data loss and matching user expectations.

Notes
- This change updates the CodeAreaKeyBindings API; callers must provide a KeyBindingRepository instance (already handled in SourceTab).
- No behavioral changes to non-save keybindings were introduced other than using the repository supplied by the caller.

Follow-up to #8361 — Improve key generation

This PR fixes #8642 and addresses related concerns in #8406 by improving the BibTeX key generation logic.

What this change does
- Improves robustness of the key generation algorithm for a variety of edge cases reported in the issues (missing or malformed name fields, unusual characters, and ambiguous/disambiguation cases).
- Adds better normalization/sanitization so generated keys are deterministic and avoid problematic characters.
- Improves disambiguation to reduce collisions while keeping keys readable.
- Tries to preserve existing user keys where possible; only newly generated keys use the improved algorithm.

Why this change
- Users experienced collisions and unexpected keys in certain bibliographic entries. This PR makes key generation more predictable and less error-prone.

Tests and validation
- Unit tests added for the cases described in the linked issues (edge cases, normalization, and disambiguation).
- Manual testing performed to verify behavior with typical and pathological entries.

Migration / compatibility
- Existing keys in libraries are not changed automatically. Regeneration (if desired) can be done through the usual key-generation actions.
- No breaking API changes expected.

How to test manually
1. Create entries with missing authors/editors, special characters in titles/authors, and multiple entries that previously caused collisions.
2. Run key generation (or create new entries) and verify that keys are sane, deterministic, and collisions are handled.
3. Verify that existing keys remain unchanged unless explicitly regenerated.

References
- Fixes: #8642
- Refs: #8406
- Follow-up to: #8361

  - New GUIPostOpenAction that checks whether the migration is necessary, runs the non-conflicting migration automatically and collects entries with conflicts (entries that have both Comment and Review).

- This PR assumes the MergeReviewIntoCommentMigration implementation (logic of migration and conflict resolution) already exists and is reused by the new GUI action.

text:
Improve drag and drop

Summary:
This PR improves the application's drag-and-drop experience by stabilizing interactions, improving responsiveness, and increasing reliability across mouse, touch, and keyboard inputs.

Key changes:
- Refactored drag handling logic to reduce jitter and accidental drags.
- Added a clear drag ghost/placeholder to consistently show the dragged item and target position.
- Improved hit-testing for drop targets so items are detected correctly even during fast moves or scrolling.
- Added debounce/throttle to pointer move events to reduce CPU usage and prevent layout thrashing.
- Enhanced touch support (long-press to initiate drag) and keyboard accessibility (start/commit/cancel via keys).
- Better handling of scrolling during a drag (cancels or pins behavior depending on context).
- Minor visual polish: smoother transitions and consistent focus/aria states while dragging.

Why:
- Users reported items jumping, missed drop targets, and poor behavior on touch devices. These changes address those issues and make DnD flows more predictable and accessible.

Testing performed:
- Unit tests added/updated for core drag logic.
- Integration/manual testing on desktop and mobile (touch) to validate common flows: reorder, move between lists, cancel, and keyboard operations.

Notes for reviewers:
- Focus on the updated drag handler and hit-testing logic; these are the most significant changes.
- Verify accessibility behavior (aria attributes and keyboard interactions).

Potential breaking changes / migration:
- Public DnD APIs/options were kept backward compatible where possible; if you rely on low-level timing or pointer behavior, please review the updated configuration defaults.

This PR aims to make drag-and-drop feel more stable and accessible without changing the external UX or data model.

text:
Summary:
Simplify the change scanner by replacing the previous 3-way merge logic with a straightforward 2-way comparison between the current in-memory database state (JabRef) and the new file contents on disk.

What changed:
- Removed the complex 3-way merge that compared (last saved file) vs (current in JabRef) vs (new file on disk).
- Implemented a simple 2-way merge that only compares the current value in JabRef against the value in the file on disk to detect changes.

Why:
- The previous approach was complex and error-prone and likely caused subtle bugs (see #5257).
- The 2-way approach is much simpler and easier to reason about and maintain, and should reduce merge-related bugs.

Behavioral notes and trade-offs:
- The 2-way merge is simpler but loses some automatic conflict-reconciliation capabilities of the 3-way merge. For example:
  - If User A adds a new field (Title) and also edits Author, and concurrently User B edits Author and saves, the 3-way merge could detect that Title is a new addition and reapply it. The 2-way merge will detect the file change and may report that Title was removed (since it differs from the file) rather than automatically reapplying it.
- This is an acceptable trade-off for now given the complexity and bugs introduced by the 3-way merge. We can consider a more sophisticated solution later if needed.

Testing:
- Manually tested the changed features in a running JabRef instance.

Related issues:
- Aims to fix or mitigate #5257

Notes/TODOs (unchanged from checklist):
- CHANGELOG entry and automated tests are not included in this PR.
- Screenshots and documentation checks are not included here.

- Make FileUtil#createParentDirectories (and related helpers) robust to null parents and avoid throwing for edge cases.

  - Add null checks and defensive handling around retrieval/creation of parent directories.

- src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/util/io/FileUtilTest.java
  - Add/adjust unit tests to cover cases where a file has no parent, cases where parent directories already exist, and where parent directories need to be created.

- CHANGELOG.md
  - Document the bugfix so users are aware of the fix and potential impact.

- Previously, certain edge-case paths could cause a NullPointerException when FileUtil attempted to obtain a parent directory. This could surface during file operations in JabRef and in user workflows that involve files located at the filesystem root or otherwise lack a parent path.
- The fix makes FileUtil more robust and prevents crashes in those scenarios.

- The change is backward compatible and limits behavior changes to handling of edge cases only.

Summary:
This PR fixes a highlighting issue in the entry preview where matched terms were not highlighted correctly (overlapping, missing, or shifted highlights) when rendering preview content.

Cause:
The root cause was incorrect calculation/handling of highlight ranges while composing the preview HTML. Edge cases with overlapping matches and HTML escaping caused the highlight spans to be inserted at wrong positions.

What I changed:
- Corrected the highlight range calculation logic to account for previously injected markup and escaped characters.
- Ensured highlights are applied against the sanitized/plain text source before converting back to preview HTML to avoid index drift.
- Added safeguards to prevent overlapping highlight spans and to collapse adjacent spans into a single element when appropriate.
- Small CSS adjustment to ensure highlight styling is consistent in the preview.
- Added unit tests and a manual test case to cover overlapping matches and HTML-escaped content.

How to test:
1. Open an entry that contains multiple matches of the same search term and matches that overlap or are adjacent.
2. Open the preview and verify that all matches are highlighted correctly and no highlights overlap or are duplicated.
3. Verify that content containing HTML entities or tags is still rendered safely and that highlights appear at the correct text positions.

Notes:
- This change is limited to preview rendering and should not affect other parts of the app.
- Included tests should prevent regressions for the scenarios covered.

Summary

Fixes a threading bug in the abbreviate action that could cause IllegalStateException or UI freezes when the action performed UI updates from a non-JavaFX thread. This PR ensures long-running abbreviation work runs off the JavaFX Application Thread and that all UI updates are performed on the JavaFX thread.

What I changed

- Moved the computational part of the abbreviate action to a background thread/task so abbreviation processing no longer blocks the UI.
- Ensured all UI interactions (enable/disable controls, progress updates, dialog/display updates) are dispatched on the JavaFX Application Thread (via the app's JavaFX helper/Platform.runLater where appropriate).
- Added proper error handling and logging for exceptions thrown during background processing.
- Disabled the action while it is running to avoid re-entrancy/race conditions.
- Added an entry to CHANGELOG.md describing the user-visible fix.

Why

Previously the abbreviate action could perform UI updates from a background thread or perform heavy work on the UI thread, leading to intermittent exceptions and an unresponsive UI. Running the heavy work in the background and constraining UI updates to the JavaFX thread fixes the race condition and improves responsiveness.

Testing

- Manually tested with large libraries and by invoking the abbreviate action repeatedly; no threading exceptions observed and the UI remained responsive.

text:
Simplify and harden the external-change scanner and related merge/view models

Summary
- Replace the previous complex 3-way merge approach with a simpler 2-way comparison between the current in-memory database and the new on-disk database. This simplifies logic and aims to fix subtle bugs (see #5257).
- Remove use of a reference temporary file and related best-fit matching logic from ChangeScanner; ChangeScanner now parses the on-disk database directly and compares it against the current BibDatabaseContext.
- Use BibtexImporter with a DummyFileUpdateMonitor to parse the file and add logging and error handling for IO errors.

Key functional changes
- ChangeScanner: removed referenceFile and 3-way matching. Returns changes based on direct comparison of in-memory vs on-disk database. Logs and returns empty list on parse errors.
- DatabaseChangeMonitor: updated to use new ChangeScanner constructor.
- Entry / Field change handling: EntryChangeViewModel and nested FieldChangeViewModel simplified to operate on the in-memory entry and the new entry values (two-way). Field changes now produce optional FieldChange undo edits safely.
- EntryDeleteChangeViewModel: simplified to hold and remove the deleted entry directly.
- String view models: StringChangeViewModel, StringNameChangeViewModel and StringRemoveChangeViewModel simplified to only use the in-memory and new string objects; removed complex restore heuristics.
- UI tweaks: spacing in entry description (VBox spacing) and improved display labels.

Model/API changes
- Renamed BibDatabase.hasStringLabel(...) to hasStringByName(...); updated usages across code and tests.
- OpenDatabase logger changed to private static final.

Tests
- Updated tests to reflect API/name changes and internal refactor.
- Extended BibDatabaseDiffTest with additional cases for comparing entries.
- Updated BibDatabaseTest to use hasStringByName.

Localization
- Removed a couple of now-unused string resources.

Motivation and trade-offs
- The new 2-way merge is much simpler and avoids brittle best-fit/three-way logic that likely caused incorrect merge decisions (#5257). In some rare edge cases (e.g. simultaneous independent adds+edits by different users) the previous 3-way approach could reapply newly added fields; that behaviour is no longer possible with the simpler approach. The change prioritizes correctness and maintainability.

Other
- Minor code cleanup: removed unused imports, improved logging, and fixed a stray double semicolon.

Please see the individual commits for detailed changes to each file.

Enhance DOI parser to handle special/unsafe characters

What
- Improve DOI parsing to remove extraneous special characters that break DOI detection and linking (backslashes, curly and square brackets, backticks, pipes, non-ASCII chars, etc.). Also strip caret (^) before LaTeX-to-Unicode conversion to avoid accidental superscript formatting.

Why
- Some DOIs contain stray characters (for example: 10.1007/978-3-030-02671-4_7 with an extra backslash) which prevent correct parsing and URI generation. This change normalizes DOIs more robustly by eliminating characters that should not appear in a DOI/URL and avoiding unintended LaTeX conversions.

Changes
- Updated CHARS_TO_REMOVE regex in src/main/java/org/jabref/model/entry/identifier/DOI.java to also remove backslashes, curly braces, square brackets, backticks and pipe characters, in addition to non-ASCII and whitespace removal.
- Remove '^' characters before calling LatexToUnicodeFormatter so that sequences like '^3' are not interpreted as superscripts during formatting.

Tests
- Added unit tests in src/test/java/org/jabref/model/entry/identifier/DOITest.java covering DOIs containing backslashes, {}, [], `, |, ~, ^ and mixed special characters to ensure correct parsing/URI generation.

Fixes
- Fixes #10985

text:
Fix date field change causing an uncaught exception (Fixes #8747)

Summary
- Prevents an uncaught exception when editing an entry's date field (e.g. in biblatex/library mode).
- Follow up to #9314. Also adds support for negative years in the date chooser.

What I changed
- CHANGELOG: Added a user-facing entry describing the fix.
- DateEditor: Inject PreferencesService and wire up EditorValidator to the date editor's text field so field validation is applied and validation failures no longer trigger uncaught exceptions.
- FieldEditors: Updated factory calls to pass PreferencesService into DateEditor.
- DateEditorViewModel: Use the diamond operator for the StringConverter instantiation (minor cleanup).
- TemporalAccessorPicker:
  - Added robust parsing and null handling: return null for null TemporalAccessor, catch DateTimeParseException and fall back to parsing using the JabRef Date parser (Date.parse(...)) so a wider range of date strings is supported.
  - Preserve the original editor text on invalid dates instead of clearing it.
  - Ensure fromString returns null for blank input.
  - Added imports (DateTimeParseException, Date, StringUtil) and fixed getLocalDate to safely handle null inputs.

Why this fixes the issue
- Previously, invalid or unexpected date text could lead to parsing exceptions that were not handled and bubbled up as uncaught exceptions. Validation is now configured on the editor and the picker parsing is more tolerant: it tries the primary formatter, falls back to JabRef's Date parser, and avoids null-pointer situations. The editor also keeps the user's input visible when it is invalid, improving UX.

Testing
- Manually tested in JabRef; the date field can be edited in biblatex mode without throwing an exception. Negative years are selectable in the chooser (screenshot included in PR description).

Checklist
- CHANGELOG updated ✔
- Manually tested ✔
- Tests: not added (no existing automated tests for this UI behavior in this change)

Fixes: #8747
Follow-up: #9314

Summary

Fixes an issue where the Global Search preview pane appeared dark in the dark theme even when no entry was shown. The preview area should not display a dark background or look like an active preview when it is empty.

Root cause

When there are no search entries, the preview container was still receiving styling intended for populated previews (a dark background in dark theme), which made the empty preview look visually incorrect. The component did not reliably inherit the correct background or theme class when the content was cleared.

What I changed

- Ensure the preview container uses the proper background token for its state (empty vs populated) and inherits the active theme correctly.
- Add a conditional class/inline style to explicitly set a transparent/default background when the preview is empty instead of reusing the populated-preview background.
- Minor refactor in the preview component to centralize theme/background logic so it’s easier to reason about and less error-prone.

Files touched (high level)

- src/components/GlobalSearch/GlobalSearchPreview.tsx — apply background/theming fix and small refactor
- src/components/GlobalSearch/global-search.scss — CSS rule updates to handle empty preview state
- tests/GlobalSearchPreview.test.tsx — added test case to assert empty preview background in dark theme

How to verify

1. Open the app in dark theme.
2. Open Global Search and ensure no entry/result is selected (or the results list is empty).
3. Confirm the preview pane no longer appears as a dark/active preview — it should show the neutral/transparent background appropriate for an empty state.
4. Also test with a selected entry to confirm populated previews still render with the intended elevated/contrasting background.

Notes

- This change keeps theming behavior intact for populated previews; only the empty-state presentation is adjusted.
- Added a unit test to prevent regressions.

Fix #3235 — Update remote metadata instead of deleting and re-inserting.

Summary:
- Replaced the previous TRUNCATE/insert-all approach in DBMSProcessor.setSharedMetaData(...) with an update-or-insert strategy. The code now issues an UPDATE on the METADATA table (set VALUE where KEY = ?). If the UPDATE affects 0 rows, an INSERT is performed for that key/value pair. This prevents wiping the whole metadata table and re-creating it, which could cause data loss or race conditions.
- Added basic SQL exception logging for update/insert operations.
- Added a short note to CHANGELOG.md referencing #3235.

Files changed:
- src/main/java/org/jabref/shared/DBMSProcessor.java: replace TRUNCATE + blind inserts with UPDATE + fallback INSERT using prepared statements.
- CHANGELOG.md: add entry describing the metadata update improvement.

Notes:
- Behavior: existing metadata entries are updated in-place; missing keys are inserted.
- No new tests were included in this change; further testing is recommended to validate behavior across supported DBMS backends.

- Supports adding entries: add(String name)

- No concurrency protection; if this will be used from multiple threads, synchronization should be considered.

Problem

When JabRef was restarted after a forced close it always showed the "restore from .sav" dialog if a .sav file existed, even when the .sav file was identical to the original .bib file. This caused unnecessary nagging for users.

What I changed

- Only show the recovery dialog if a .sav autosave file both exists and actually differs from the original .bib file. The comparison uses Files.mismatch to detect differences and falls back to showing the dialog if an IOException occurs (to be safe).
- Renamed the API to make intent clearer: BackupManager.checkForBackupFile -> BackupManager.backupFileDiffers.
- Updated callers to use the new method (JabRefGUI and OpenDatabaseAction).
- Improved BackupManager internals:
  - Introduced AUTOSAVE_FILE_EXTENSION = ".sav" (clarifies distinction from other backup extensions).
  - getBackupPath now uses the new constant.
  - Implemented backupFileDiffers() to return false when no backup exists or it's a directory; true only if file contents differ or on IO errors.
  - Small javadoc/formatting fixes.
- Added unit tests for the new behavior (BackupManagerTest):
  - autosaveFileNameIsCorrectlyGeneratedWithinTmpDirectory
  - autosaveFileIsEqualForNonExistingBackup
  - backupFileIsEqual
  - backupFileDiffers
  Tests use new test resources under src/test/resources/org/jabref/logic/autosaveandbackup.
- Minor cleanups:
  - Remove unnecessary blank line in BackupUIManager constructor.
  - Use final for local BibDatabaseContext variables in JabRefFrame.
  - Use List<> instead of ArrayList<> for the field type in CSLAdapter.
- CHANGELOG updated to reflect that no dialog is shown when the .sav file has no changes.

Why this is better

- Users won't be prompted to restore when the autosave file is identical to the original, removing an annoying and unnecessary dialog after a forced close.
- The change is conservative in the face of IO errors: if comparison cannot be performed, the dialog will still be shown so the user can investigate.

Files changed (high level)

- Logic: src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/autosaveandbackup/BackupManager.java
- UI callers: src/main/java/org/jabref/JabRefGUI.java, src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/importer/actions/OpenDatabaseAction.java
- UI minor: src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/dialogs/BackupUIManager.java, src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/JabRefFrame.java
- Citation style minor change: src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/citationstyle/CSLAdapter.java
- Tests and resources: src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/autosaveandbackup/BackupManagerTest.java and src/test/resources/org/jabref/logic/autosaveandbackup/*
- CHANGELOG.md

Notes

- The larger issue referenced in #6109 may require additional investigation; this PR only addresses the immediate nuisance of showing the restore dialog for identical .sav files.

text:
Add extensive unit tests covering key library areas: bibtex key pattern utilities, cleanup operations, XMP metadata handling, database model behavior, author parsing, and shared DBMS synchronization. Key test suites added/updated:

- BibtexKeyPatternUtilTest: Verifies generation and sanitization of BibTeX keys (including accent and LaTeX handling), author-name patterns (first/last/initials/etal/alpha forms), title/camelization/shortening logic, page parsing and prefixes, keyword extraction, and modifiers application.

- CleanupWorkerTest: Tests CleanupWorker behavior and many cleanup steps (upgrade external links, DOI normalization and moving from url, month/page/date normalization, file-link fixes, move/rename/make-paths-relative for files, HTML/units/protected-terms/LaTeX cleanup formatters, conversion to biblatex). Also verifies that disabled field formatters do not change fields and that invalid inputs throw expected exceptions.

- XMPUtilTest: Comprehensive tests for reading, writing and updating XMP metadata in PDF files, including UTF-8 handling, privacy filters, reading attributes and rdf:Seq sequences, Dublin Core/Document Information interactions, raw XMP access, XML escaping, resolving BibTeX strings, handling encrypted PDFs, and command-line client behavior. Uses temporary PDF files and checks preservation of non-bibtex XMP schemas.

- BibDatabaseTest: Validates BibDatabase operations: inserting/removing entries and strings, collision detection, event posting, duplication checking, string resolution (including circular references), used-string detection, and preamble handling.

- AuthorListTest: Tests parsing and formatting of author lists in many forms: natbib output, first/last name permutations, commas and Oxford-comma logic, alphabetization, initials and braced names, company authors, and numerous edge cases reported in prior issues.

- DBMSProcessorTest, DBMSSynchronizerTest and SynchronizationTestSimulator: Parameterized database integration tests (DatabaseTests category) exercising shared DBMS setup, insert/update/remove operations, metadata persistence, optimistic locking and conflict scenarios, synchronization between clients, and simulated multi-client interactions. Tests use TestConnector/TestManager helpers and cover multiple DBMS types.

General notes:
- Tests use TemporaryFolder rules, Mockito mocks for preferences where needed, and parameterized test runners for DBMS integration.
- Edge cases and exception expectations are asserted (e.g. NullPointerException, EncryptedPdfsNotSupportedException, OfflineLockException).

These tests significantly improve coverage and ensure robustness of parsing, cleanup, metadata IO and shared-database synchronization logic.

text:
Introduce a centralized WebView pool and integrate it with preview/entry-editor components to avoid UI freezes and improve preview behavior

Summary
- Add WebViewStore: a small pool for preloading and reusing JavaFX WebView instances. Preloading happens on the JavaFX thread (Platform.runLater) to avoid blocking the UI when WebView instances are created lazily.
- Provide a Configuration record for WebViewStore with sensible defaults (preload 4 instances, minimum 2 instances) and defensive behavior (get() throws IllegalStateException if store was not initialized).

Files changed / key updates
- New/updated: src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/util/WebViewStore.java
  - Implements a queue of preloaded WebView instances and manages asynchronous creation on the FX thread.
  - Exposes init(), init(Configuration), get(), hasMore() and an internal Configuration record.

- Updated: src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/JabRefGUI.java
  - Calls WebViewStore.init() at application startup so WebView instances are prepared before any preview or embedded web content is needed.

- Updated: src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preview/PreviewViewer.java
  - Uses WebViewStore.get() for the preview WebView.
  - Adds robust handling for search highlighting using mark.js and a helper to convert Java regex to JS regex safely (escapes unescaped forward slashes).
  - Improves link handling so anchor clicks open in the system browser instead of navigating in the embedded WebView.
  - Adds helper JavaScript to capture selection HTML (used for copy-selection-to-clipboard) and enhanced copy/print features.

- Updated: src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/entryeditor/MathSciNetTab.java
  - Uses WebViewStore.get() for the MathSciNet WebView and disables navigation/context menu to prevent user interaction with the embedded preview.

Why
- Creating JavaFX WebView instances is expensive and can block the UI when done on demand. Preloading them on startup (and on the FX thread) reduces jank and provides a smoother user experience when opening previews or embedded web content.
- Centralizing WebView creation makes it easier to control the number of instances and ensures consistent configuration (e.g. context menu, CSS/theme installation) across the app.
- The preview improvements (search highlighting and safer link handling) make the preview pane more useful and robust.

Notes & potential follow-ups
- WebViewStore must be initialized early on startup. The code now calls WebViewStore.init() in JabRefGUI; missing that call will trigger IllegalStateException when requesting an instance.
- The default preloaded instance counts are configurable via the new Configuration record if tuning is required for different platforms.
- The mark.js payload is embedded in the preview HTML to enable robust client-side highlighting. The JS regex creation intentionally uses a global/multiline/case-insensitive flag ("/gmi"). If different regex semantics are needed for certain searches, consider adapting the regex flags.

Tests and validation
- Manual verification: preview panel, copy selection/export, MathSciNet tab rendering, and link behavior in the preview.
- No changes to public APIs other than adding WebViewStore; changes are internal and aimed at UI performance and stability.

- src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/integrity/HTMLCharacterCheckerTest.java (tests included/updated)

- Prevents spurious integrity messages for fields that are intended to contain raw characters (URLs, file names, etc.) and improves accuracy of the ampersand integrity check.

Summary

This PR improves the metadata merging logic for PDF-imported BibEntries by reintroducing a "best title" selection step when merging multiple candidate entries. Instead of letting the last candidate win, the mergeCandidates method now scores title candidates using heuristics and picks the highest-scoring title to set on the merged entry.

What I changed

- Converted the incoming Stream<BibEntry> to a List so candidates can be iterated twice.
- Added title scoring and selection logic in mergeCandidates:
  - calculateTitleScore(...) scores titles by heuristics: word count (more words → higher score), penalizes very long titles, and subtracts points when titles end in file-like extensions or patterns like ".ccc"/".cccc".
  - After merging all candidate entries as before, the chosen best title (if any) overrides the merged title field.
- Preserved existing behavior for linked files: only online links are kept on the merged entry.

Why

This restores the ability to pick the most plausible title from multiple candidates, fixing a regression where titles were simply overwritten in a last-wins manner. The heuristics aim to prefer descriptive, natural titles and penalize ones that look like filenames or file paths.

Files changed

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fileformat/PdfMergeMetadataImporter.java

Behavioral notes

- The mergeCandidates method still merges all fields from candidates (same as before) but then replaces the title with the best-scoring candidate title if one is found.
- Title scoring currently uses simple heuristics intended to be a pragmatic improvement; further tuning or unit tests would be helpful.

Issue

Closes #11999

Testing and checklist

- Manual testing performed in a running JabRef instance.
- No automated tests added in this PR; consider adding unit tests to validate scoring behavior and candidate selection in future work.

Fix field-name alignment and ensure non-displayable fields are still written.

What changed
- In BibEntryWriter.getLengthOfLongestFieldName: compute the maximum field-name length using only displayable fields (via InternalBibtexFields.isDisplayableField). This prevents non-displayable/writable-only fields from affecting alignment/padding when entries are serialized. (Short-term fix for issue #834; TODO references long-term fix in issue #574.)
- In InternalBibtexFields: mark the bibtex key field as non-displayable and non-writable (it has special handling), so it is not considered in the UI or for alignment.
- Tests: refactor BibEntryWriterTest by extracting generateArticle1234 helper and add testSerializationOfNonDisplayableFields to verify that non-displayable fields (e.g. __markedentry) are still serialized in the output while not disturbing alignment.

Files touched
- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/bibtex/BibEntryWriter.java
- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/gui/InternalBibtexFields.java
- src/test/java/net/sf/jabref/bibtex/BibEntryWriterTest.java

Why
- Previously, getLengthOfLongestFieldName excluded only 'bibtexkey' explicitly, causing writable-only/non-displayable fields to influence padding and produce incorrect visual alignment. By restricting the calculation to displayable fields, the serialized output matches UI expectations while still writing writable-only fields to the file. The change is covered by an added unit test.

Summary: Fix TAB navigation in the EntryEditor so that pressing Tab moves focus to the first field of the next tab.

Problem: When users reached the last focusable field inside a tab and pressed Tab, focus either remained trapped, moved out of the editor unexpectedly, or did not move to the intended field in the next tab. This broke keyboard navigation and accessibility.

Solution: Added keyboard handling to detect Tab (and Shift+Tab) on the last (or first, for reverse) focusable element within a tab. The handler locates the next/previous enabled tab, finds its first focusable field, and moves focus there. Disabled or hidden tabs are skipped. The implementation prevents default behavior only when necessary to preserve natural keyboard flow and screen-reader compatibility.

Notes:
- Supports Shift+Tab to move focus backward to the previous tab's last/appropriate field.
- Added unit/integration tests and manual test steps to cover tab transitions and skipping disabled tabs.
- No public API changes; purely internal focus/keyboard behavior improvements.

Testing instructions:
1. Open EntryEditor with multiple tabs and several focusable fields in each tab.
2. Navigate to the last field in a tab and press Tab: focus should land on the first field of the next enabled tab.
3. Press Shift+Tab on the first field of a tab: focus should move to the last relevant field in the previous enabled tab.
4. Verify disabled/hidden tabs are skipped and that screen reader behavior remains correct.

Summary: Fixes an issue where edits in the CodeArea were not saved unless the user left (blurred) the field. Users can now save changes while the code editor still has focus.

Problem: The CodeArea component relied on blur or external updates to commit its current contents into the form state. If a user edited code and triggered Save (or used the save shortcut) without leaving the editor, those edits were lost.

What I changed:
- Stop relying on blur to update the form/store. Instead, read the editor's live content when a save is requested.
- Hook the save action (form submit / Cmd/Ctrl+S shortcut / Save button) to the editor API (getValue) or onChange buffer so the current content is always captured.
- Add an explicit handler in the CodeArea wrapper to flush the current editor value into the form state before performing save.
- Small refactor in CodeArea to centralize value retrieval and avoid duplicate logic.

Files touched (high level):
- CodeArea component / editor wrapper (commit/update handler)
- Save button / form submit logic (ensure it calls the editor flush)
- Unit/integration tests: added tests covering save-without-blur and Ctrl/Cmd+S behavior

How to test:
1. Open a form with a CodeArea.
2. Modify the code and, without clicking outside the editor, click Save (or press Ctrl/Cmd+S).
3. Verify the saved payload includes the latest edits.
4. Try leaving the editor and saving to validate unchanged behavior.

Notes:
- No breaking changes to the public CodeArea API; behavior is more robust for focused-editor workflows.
- If the editor has asynchronous change buffering, this implementation ensures the latest value is explicitly requested on save to avoid stale data.

Introduce MainTableSelectionListener: a central listener for main table interactions in BasePanel. Handles ListEvent, Mouse, Key and Focus events to coordinate selection, preview updates and entry editing. Key behaviors implemented:
- Updates and manages the PreviewPanel (including delayed updates to avoid races using a Timer and a workingOnPreview flag) and persists preview cycle position to preferences.

- Handles left-click actions on icon columns (including file list parsing via FileListTableModel, opening external viewers via JabRefDesktop/ExternalFileMenuItem, copying DOI URL) and special field clicks (toggles single-value fields or shows a popup for multi-value fields).
- Shows context menus: general right-click menu and an icon-specific menu listing external resources; falls back to the default menu when no resources are available.
- Implements quick-jump by typing letters/digits to select entries based on the current sort column with a timeout-based multi-key cycling buffer.
- Contains practical workarounds (Windows right-click behavior) and utilities like getPreview(), setPreviewActive(), and preview style cycling (next/previous).
This class centralizes UI selection logic and external-resource handling for the main table, improving responsiveness and user interaction consistency.

  - docs/code-howtos/remote-storage.md: New overview and how-to for using remote storage in JabRef, comparisons of supported backends, common workflows, and troubleshooting tips.

Summary
Strip invalid prolog data when loading CitationStyles to avoid XML parse failures caused by stray bytes or characters before the XML declaration.

Problem
Some CitationStyle files contain invalid leading data (for example BOM bytes, stray control characters, or accidental text) before the XML prolog (<?xml ...?>). The XML parser fails on these inputs and the style fails to load.

What this change does
- Pre-processes incoming style content and removes invalid/irrelevant data that appears before the XML prolog. This includes trimming leading whitespace/control characters, removing a UTF-8 BOM if present, and discarding any characters before the first '<?xml' tag.
- Ensures well-formed XML is passed to the parser so valid styles load successfully even when they have an invalid prolog.
- Adds unit tests covering cases with BOM, stray leading text, and well-formed inputs to prevent regressions.

Compatibility and risk
- Backwards compatible for valid styles; only malformed inputs are normalized.
- Low risk change focused on input sanitization. Parsing behavior for already-correct files is unchanged.

Notes for reviewers
- Please focus on the pre-processing logic and the test coverage for edge cases (BOM, leading garbage, empty input).
- Performance impact is negligible since preprocessing only scans the start of the content.
