text:
Introduce WebViewStore to preload and reuse JavaFX WebView instances to avoid UI freezes when creating WebView objects

- Add new org.jabref.logic.util.WebViewStore
  - Maintains a queue of preloaded WebView instances and lazy-creates new ones when needed
  - Provides init() overloads (default Configuration(4,2) and custom Configuration) and get() to obtain a WebView
  - Preloads instances on the JavaFX thread via Platform.runLater
  - Throws IllegalStateException if get() is called before init()

- Initialize the store at application startup
  - Call WebViewStore.init() from JabRefGUI to ensure WebViews are preloaded early

- Use the store instead of constructing WebView directly
  - Replace new WebView() with WebViewStore.get() in MathSciNetTab and PreviewViewer to reuse preloaded instances and reduce UI lag

- Changelog
  - Add entry noting the fix for app lag when selecting an entry after a fresh start (#8446)

- Small cleanup
  - Removed an extra blank line in JabRefMain

Rationale: constructing JavaFX WebView instances on demand can cause noticeable UI freezes. Preloading and reusing WebView instances reduces perceived lag and improves responsiveness when showing previews or embedded web content.

text:
Add preference tab view models for managing custom exporters, custom importers and external file types

This PR introduces three new view-model classes used by the Preferences UI to manage user-configurable exporters, importers and external file types:

- CustomExporterTabViewModel
  - Binds a list of ExporterViewModel instances for the UI and a selected-exporters list for selection handling.
  - Loads custom exporters from PreferencesService (setValues) and persists them back (storeSettings).
  - Provides add/modify/remove operations for exporters using CreateModifyExporterDialogView via DialogService (dialog result is validated and added/updated in the list).

- CustomImporterTabViewModel
  - Binds a list of ImporterViewModel instances and a selected-importers list for UI selection.
  - Loads custom importers from preferences and persists them back to ImporterPreferences.
  - Adds importers from files or archives: supports selecting .class files, .jar and .zip archives and allows picking a class inside an archive.
  - Converts file paths into class names (pathToClass) when adding non-archive class files.
  - Handles errors during archive opening and importer instantiation, logging and showing user-friendly error dialogs.
  - Provides removal of selected importers.

Summary

- Improve and harden HTTP downloading and ISBN fetchers. Make network fetches more robust, handle edge cases and HTTP response handling more explicitly, and update tests accordingly.

What changed

- URLDownload
  - Hardened HTTP handling: improved handling of HTTP status codes and redirects, added sensible timeouts and headers, and fixed issues around response reading/encoding so fetchers receive correct content.
  - Ensures clearer error propagation when downloads fail.

- IsbnFetcher
  - Adjusted orchestration/error handling so empty or failed network responses are handled gracefully.
  - Improved logging and null-safety when combining results from multiple fetchers.

- IsbnViaOttoBibFetcher
  - Switched to the improved URLDownload behavior, fixed parsing/encoding issues, and made the fetcher resilient to unexpected HTML responses or missing fields.

- Tests
  - Updated/extended tests (WebFetchersTest, IsbnViaChimboriFetcherTest, IsbnViaEbookDeFetcherTest, IsbnViaOttoBibFetcherTest) to reflect the new download behavior, proper error handling, and to mock/verify the corrected HTTP response handling.

Why this change

- Previously some fetchers could receive malformed or partially-read responses, mishandle redirects or non-OK HTTP responses, and cause brittle behavior or test failures. Centralizing and improving HTTP handling in URLDownload and making fetchers resilient fixes multiple intermittent issues and makes behavior predictable.

Notes

- No API changes intended for external callers beyond improved robustness and clearer errors for failing downloads.
- Tests were adjusted to reflect the corrected behavior and to ensure continued stability of web fetchers.

[ #5428](https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/5428) - Issue this PR solves

Gradle was warning about deprecated feature usage. Logs show jacoco append to be the feature that is deprecated.From my understandind the propery is currently ignored.

Removed the Jacoco append property from build.gradle and builds don't throw any deprecation warnings anymore.

The append property in Jacoco is meant to write to the same coverage file. But as mentioned in this [issue](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/issues/5269) setting it to true broke the build caching capability. So starting Gradle 5.0 a breaking change was introduced where they did away with the append property. The default behavior was set to behave as if append is initially false to enable build caching and then append is set to true before passing to the jacoco agent.
This meant that multiple tasks could not use the same coverage file but Jacoco merge is a feature that let's you achieve the same functionality. The gradle for the project does use Jacoco Merge to merge the various .exec file results, so removing the append property should not break coverage.

Implement full text lookup and robust linked file handling

This change adds a FindFullTextAction to look up and download full text PDFs for selected BibEntry objects and complements it with the LinkedFileViewModel functionality that manages linked file operations and downloads.

Key points:
- FindFullTextAction
  - Uses FulltextFetchers to search for full text URLs for all selected entries in a background Task.
  - Prompts the user for confirmation when operating on many entries (threshold WARNING_LIMIT).
  - Resolves the target file directory from JabRef preferences and shows an error if no directory is configured.
  - Avoids duplicate links and downloads found files into the configured directory using LinkedFileViewModel.prepareDownloadTask and URLDownload.
  - Notifies the user on success, failure or when no full text is found.
  - Uses concurrent structures and the global task executor to run background work without blocking the UI.

- LinkedFileViewModel
  - Provides UI-facing operations for linked files including open, openFolder, rename (with conflict handling), moveToDefaultDirectory, moveToDefaultDirectoryAndRename, delete (with user prompt), edit, and writeXMPMetadata.
  - Implements downloading of online links: prepares and executes download tasks, binds download progress to UI properties, and updates the linked file entry once download completes.
  - Infers file type from MIME type or URL extension to set suggested file type and name prior to download.
  - Exposes observable properties for download progress, ongoing state, and whether the file was automatically found.
  - Uses LinkedFileHandler, FilePreferences, XmpPreferences, DialogService, and TaskExecutor for file operations, XMP writing, and user interaction.

Error handling and UX:
- All network and IO operations are executed in background tasks and report errors via dialogService.
- Provides clear user feedback: progress dialogs during lookup, notifications on completion, and error dialogs for missing directories, invalid URLs, permission issues, or download failures.

This work integrates full text discovery with the existing linked file infrastructure and improves safety and user feedback when downloading and managing external files.

Refactor SpecialFieldValue to improve clarity and robustness

Summary
- Clean up and modernize the SpecialFieldValue implementation.
- Introduce clearer mapping between the internal representation and a user-facing display name, and provide a stable parsing/lookup API.

What changed
- Encapsulated value-related metadata in the enum (display name / serialization name) to ensure a single source of truth for each special-field value.
- Added a static lookup method (fromString / parse) to resolve a string to the corresponding enum value in a null-safe and case-insensitive manner.
- Overrode toString()/getDisplayName() to return appropriate presentation strings and made serialization names explicit to avoid ambiguity when persisting values.
- Improved null-safety and input validation (using Objects.requireNonNull / defensive checks) to reduce potential NPEs and parsing errors.
- Cleaned up imports and added JavaDoc/comments to clarify behavior and intended usage of the API.

Backward compatibility
- The enum still represents the same conceptual set of special-field values; public API additions are additive (parsing and accessor helpers). Existing callers should continue to work, and will benefit from a more predictable mapping and parsing behavior.

Why this helps
- Reduces spread of string literals for special-field values across the codebase.
- Makes it easier to serialize/deserialize special field values reliably and to present human-readable names in the UI.
- Simplifies future maintenance and additions of new special field values.

Notes
- No functional changes to other modules were made in this commit; callers can opt to use the new parse/getDisplayName helpers to simplify their code.

Closes #13015

Summary

Reformats the BibTeX shown in the Import dialog's "Show BibTeX source" preview to JabRef's canonical style. The incoming BibTeX string is parsed into a BibEntry and rendered with BibEntryWriter (reformat=true). If parsing fails, the raw string is shown unchanged. This makes the preview readable and consistent with JabRef formatting guidelines.

Implementation details

- Parse the incoming BibTeX string into a BibEntry.
- Render the entry using BibEntryWriter with reformat=true.
- Fall back to displaying the original string if parsing fails.

Why

Imported BibTeX shown in the preview could be unformatted or inconsistent. Reformatting in the preview improves readability and gives users a representation that matches how JabRef stores and writes entries.

How to test

1. Open JabRef and create a new library.
2. In Firefox (with the JabRef plugin installed), go to a page with importable references (example: https://learning.oreilly.com/library/view/infrastructure-as-code/9781098150341/).
3. Click the plugin's "Import references..." button and open the resulting popup.
4. Select "Show BibTeX source" and inspect the preview.
5. Compare to previous behavior: the BibTeX should now be reformatted (see Before/After screenshots attached in this PR).

Before/After

- Before: unformatted, hard-to-read BibTeX in preview.
- After: Canonically formatted BibTeX matching JabRef's writer style (more readable and consistent).

Notes

- If the parser cannot interpret the incoming string, the raw string is displayed unchanged to avoid data loss.
- Unit tests were not added for this UI change [/] (not applicable).

- Change has been described in CHANGELOG.md for users.
- Developer and user documentation were checked; issues were created/updated where needed.

text:
Add Import Entries dialog and backing view model to support interactive import of parsed BibTeX entries

This change introduces a new import inspection dialog (ImportEntriesDialog.fxml + ImportEntriesDialog.java) and its view model (ImportEntriesViewModel.java) to present parsed entries to the user and perform the actual import. Key features:

- Interactive selection: parsed entries are displayed in a CheckListView with per-entry add-toggle buttons and quick actions (Select all new entries, Select all entries, Unselect all).
- Show BibTeX source: an optional, collapsible BibTeX source panel (CodeArea) is shown when the user enables "Show BibTeX source".
- Import target: a combobox lets the user choose which open library to import into (labelled "Library to import into").
- Download linked online files: a checkbox to download linked online files on import; this preference is remembered.
- Duplicate detection: asynchronous checks for duplicates; a duplicate button is displayed for entries that appear to be duplicates and opens the duplicate resolver to handle them.
- Entry preview: each list cell shows type icon, title, year/journal, authors and an optional summary (abstract) using a compact layout.
- Counters & disabling: total/selected counters update live and the Import button is disabled when no entries are selected.
- Import behavior: ImportEntriesViewModel collects parser results (BackgroundTask), handles duplicate warnings (with opt-out preference), builds ImportHandler to import entries, merges strings/metadata into the target database and optionally downloads linked online files using LinkedFileViewModel.
- Misc: better UX for single-item imports (auto-select new entries when only one entry parsed), and a few styling/border tweaks for the BibTeX source area.

Files added/modified:
- src/main/resources/org/jabref/gui/importer/ImportEntriesDialog.fxml: dialog layout
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/importer/ImportEntriesDialog.java: dialog controller
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/importer/ImportEntriesViewModel.java: view model handling parsing result, duplicate checks and import logic
- src/main/resources/l10n/JabRef_en.properties: added/used localization keys (e.g., Select all new entries, Library to import into, Show BibTeX source, Download linked online files, Total items found:, Selected items:)

Why:
- Provide users with a clear, interactive way to review parsed entries before importing (including viewing raw BibTeX), resolve duplicates and choose the destination library, improving import reliability and transparency.

text:
Fix and harden author name parsing in AuthorListParser

Summary:
- Improve tokenization and normalization of author names to handle a wide range of edge cases encountered in BibTeX-style name fields.
- Treat semicolon (;) as an author separator (equivalent to "and").
- Improve detection of token casing (upper/lower) including special handling for TeX-escaped commands and Han script characters to avoid incorrect "von"/"last name" detection.
- Add/adjust TeX special command names handling to better detect case for tokens starting with TeX commands (TEX_NAMES).
- Correct handling of hyphenated names and name parts when determining von/last/first/junior parts.
- Properly handle comma-separated name lists with affixes (jr, sr, jnr, snr, von, zu, van, der) so that names like "Ali Babar, M., Dingsøyr, T., ..." are parsed correctly and names with junior/senior affixes are preserved.

Why:

Fix exception when saving name formatters (fixes #9120)

Summary
- This PR fixes an exception that occurred when saving name formatters. The underlying issue was that the lists passed into NameFormatterPreferences were not created as modifiable ObservableArrayList instances, which could lead to errors when the UI attempted to modify or observe them.

What I changed
- In NameFormatterPreferences, create the internal lists with FXCollections.observableArrayList(...) instead of FXCollections.observableList(...). This ensures the lists are modifiable and properly observable by JavaFX.
- Added a short changelog entry: "We fixed an issue where name formatter could not be saved. [#9120]".

Why this fixes the issue
- observableArrayList produces an ObservableList implementation that supports modification and listener notifications as expected by the UI code. Using observableList with an external list could result in an unsupported or non-observable backing list, which triggered the exception when saving.

Tests and verification
- Unit tests were added where applicable.
- Manually tested the changed feature in a running JabRef build to confirm that name formatters can now be saved without exceptions.
- Screenshots for the UI change were included in the PR description where relevant.

Other notes
- Developer and user documentation were checked and updated if necessary.

Fixes: #9120

Introduce JabRefFrame: main application frame and tabbed library container

- Add JabRefFrame which composes the main UI (menu + toolbar, tabbed libraries, side pane, main table and entry editor) and implements LibraryTabContainer and UiMessageHandler.

- Layout and lifecycle: initialize layout, drag-and-drop (FrameDndHandler), file history menu, welcome tab creation, adding/removing library tabs and tab context menus.
- Key bindings: wire many global shortcuts (focus table/groups, next/previous library, search, open global search dialog, create new entries for common types, navigation back/forward, close database) using the preferences key binding repository.
- State bindings: connect tab selection, active database, search synchronization, auto-completer and window title to StateManager; bind canGoBack/canGoForward properties.
- Tab actions and commands: create contextual menu items for library properties, open database folder, open console, and close/close others/close all libraries; add OpenDatabaseFolder action that opens the library folder and selects the .bib file in the OS file explorer.
- Focus and UI polish: ensure focus behavior when switching tabs and when showing the entry editor; provide refresh and open-last-edited functionality.

Implement main application window (JabRefFrame) and update changelog

This PR introduces the main UI class JabRefFrame and documents notable changes in the changelog. The JabRefFrame implements the primary window and wiring for the application, and includes the following highlights:

- Main window layout
  - Creates top menu bar and toolbar with grouped actions (new/open/save, edit, undo/redo, search, entry operations, push-to-app, cleanup, etc.).
  - Integrates a SidePane and TabPane for multiple library tabs and keeps the side pane size persisted.
  - Binds window title to the currently selected library tab.

- Tab and library lifecycle management
  - Add/close/remove library tabs with proper cleanup hooks, autosave/backup startup and shutdown.
  - FileHistory menu and actions to open recent libraries.
  - Robust quit/close workflow asking for confirmation when background tasks are running, libraries are modified, or empty entries exist.
  - Handles shared database conversion/cleanup when closing shared DBs.

- Drag & Drop
  - Adds drag-and-drop support for .bib files onto the tabbed pane, including a visual drop indicator tab.

- Key bindings and focus handling
  - Global keybinding initialization with mappings for navigation, search, and quick new-entry actions.
  - Focus owner tracking and per-tab focus management to ensure clipboard/cut/paste operations act on the correct database.

- Background tasks and telemetry
  - Progress indicator in the toolbar showing background tasks; clicking opens a popover with a TaskProgressView listing tasks.
  - One-minute delayed telemetry opt-in prompt (if enabled in preferences) that asks the user to share anonymous usage statistics.

- Import & entry workflows
  - New Entry From ID button opens a PopOver-driven GenerateEntryFromIdDialog.
  - Import of ParserResult: either open a new tab or import entries into the current tab using ImportEntriesDialog.
  - Import cleanup step applied to parsed entries before presenting import dialog.

- Menus & commands
  - Constructs the full application menu (File, Edit, Library, Quality, Lookup, Tools, View, Options, Help) and registers actions across modules.
  - Dynamically builds Lookup identifier submenu from available IdFetchers.

- Miscellaneous
  - Uses EasyBind and ControlsFX PopOver for UI bindings and popovers.
  - Integrates Undo/Redo event handling hooks and registers an UndoRedoEventManager.
  - Provides helper actions for opening database folders, copying linked files, rebuilding fulltext indices, and more.

Add JSTOR fetcher (search + fulltext)

This PR introduces a new fetcher for jstor.org and integrates it into the existing fetcher registry.

Key changes
- Add JstorFetcher implementing SearchBasedParserFetcher and FulltextFetcher (src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/JstorFetcher.java).
  - Builds search and complex query URLs for JSTOR search endpoints.
  - Parses JSTOR search results using Jsoup, collects citation IDs and downloads BibTeX via the /citation/text endpoint, and parses entries with BibtexParser.
  - Implements findFullText(BibEntry) by parsing the article page and extracting a PDF link from elements with the data-doi attribute.
  - Marks trust level as META_SEARCH.
- Register JstorFetcher in WebFetchers (src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/WebFetchers.java):
  - Included in getSearchBasedFetchers and getFullTextFetchers so JSTOR participates in search-based and fulltext fetching flows.
- Add unit tests for the JSTOR fetcher (src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/JstorFetcherTest.java):
  - Tests searching by title and fetching PDF URL for a known record.
  - Disables year-only searches (JSTOR does not support searches based only on year).

Notes
- The fetcher depends on ImportFormatPreferences for BibTeX parsing.
- The parser downloads citation text for each result item and aggregates BibTeX before parsing.
- findFullText currently requires the entry to contain a URL and expects a single element with data-doi on the article page.

Related
- Implements feature to search JSTOR referenced in the changelog/unreleased: "We added a new fetcher to enable users to search jstor.org" [#6627].

text:
Add comprehensive unit tests and robustness improvements for BibTeX key generation

This PR strengthens and documents the behaviour of the BibTeX key generation utilities and fixes several edge-cases discovered while adding tests.

What this PR does

- Adds extensive unit tests covering many aspects of BibTeX key generation (src/test/java/...):
  - BibtexKeyPatternUtilTest: tests for diacritics/accents, institution detection and abbreviation, many author-format patterns (auth, authors, authIniN, authAuthEa, authEtAl, authshort, nAuthors, oneAuthorPlusIni, etc.), title formatting/casing (camel, title_case, capitalize, sentence_case), page parsing (first/last page), keyword handling, and checkLegalKey behaviour with and without enforcement.
  - MakeLabelWithDatabaseTest: tests for key generation when considering an existing database (duplicates handling, always-add-letter preference, regex replacements, modifiers such as :lower/:upper/:abbr and alternate text when fields are empty).

- Improves BibtexKeyPatternUtil implementation to handle more real-world corner cases:
  - Robust diacritic handling (unifyDiacritics / removeDiacritics) and institution key generation (generateInstitutionKey) to produce sensible, shorter keys for institutional names and umlaut handling.
  - parseFieldMarker now correctly parses field markers with escaped characters and parenthesised modifiers (e.g. default text like [author:(No Author Provided)] and modifiers containing parentheses or escaped colons).
  - applyModifiers now supports:
    - abbreviation modifier (abbr) which builds initials from words correctly,
    - integration with Formatters via Formatters.getFormatterForModifier(modifier) so case changers and other formatters are applied,
    - alternate-text modifiers in parentheses which are used when the generated label is empty.
  - checkLegalKey respects the enforce flag and removes only illegal/special characters accordingly, and returns null for null input.
  - getAddition implements base-26 letter suffix generation (a..z, aa..az, ...) used for duplicate resolution.
  - Helper methods for title formatting: formatTitle, getTitleWordsWithSpaces, camelizeTitle, camelizeSignificantWordsInTitle, removeSmallWords, and related helpers produce the expected title-based key parts.
  - makeLabel overload accepting BibDatabaseContext to fetch the pattern from metadata.

Why

- The newly added tests revealed subtle issues in parsing and formatting (diacritics, escaped modifiers, empty-field defaults, and duplicated-key suffix logic). Fixing these improves the reliability of generated citation keys in many locales and complex entry contents.

Notes

- No public API breaking changes: the fixes are internal to the key generation logic. An additional convenience overload for makeLabel(BibDatabaseContext, ...) was added to obtain the pattern from database metadata, simplifying callers that operate at the database context level.
- Tests cover many legacy and corner cases to avoid regressions in future refactorings.

This PR aims to make cite-key generation more robust and well-tested across a wide range of inputs and user preferences.

Summary of changes

- Add SearchTextField helper: extracted creation of a JavaFX clearable TextField (ControlsFX) with localized prompt text to SearchTextField.create(). This centralizes the TextField creation and keeps prompt/localization logic in one place.

- Improve GlobalSearchBar integration with JavaFX and icons:
  - Use the JavaFX TextField inside a JFXPanel (CustomJFXPanel) and wire it into the UI through a Scene. Subscribe to text changes via EasyBind to trigger searches.
  - Wire up search controls and behavior: global search toggle (with shortcut), regex and case-sensitive toggles, search mode button cycling and persistence to SearchPreferences, and auto-complete hookup.
  - Implement search lifecycle: performSearch, performGlobalSearch, endSearch, clearSearch, validation of SearchResultFrame, and SearchQuery creation/validation.
  - Display search results count and status using pseudo-class changes for no-results / results-found, update toolbar icon for grammar-based searches, and show a rich Tooltip (JavaFX) containing a TextFlow description.
  - Provide an "open current results" button that either opens global results or shows local findings in a SearchResultFrame.
  - Add SearchKeyAdapter to prevent arrow keys from moving focus out of the field and to consume clipboard/selection keybindings so they don't propagate to the main frame.

- IconTheme improvements and usage:
  - Use a JabRefIcon enum that wraps MaterialDesignIcon glyphs and optionally colors, and exposes convenience methods to obtain FontBasedIcon (small/large), graphics for JavaFX, and underlying icon metadata.

  - Provide utilities to load image icons for both Swing (ImageIcon) and JavaFX (Image), read icon mappings from an Icons.properties file, and expose a getLogoSet() for app icons.

Summary:
Improves the key generation logic to produce more reliable, collision-resistant keys while keeping the public API backwards-compatible.

What changed:
- Reworked the core key generation algorithm to use a stronger entropy mix (cryptographically secure RNG + timestamp + monotonic counter) to reduce collisions and predictability.
- Moved key generation into a dedicated utility module and simplified the public-facing helper functions.
- Added input validation and clearer error messages when key parameters are invalid or out of range.
- Added unit tests, edge-case tests, and basic benchmarks to validate uniqueness, performance, and correctness.

Why this change:
- Existing keys had a small but measurable collision/predictability risk in high-concurrency scenarios. The new approach reduces that risk while maintaining compact key sizes.
- Centralizing the logic improves maintainability and makes future enhancements (namespacing, versioning) easier to add.

Compatibility & migration:
- No breaking changes to the public API; existing consumers should continue to work as before.
- If you relied on previous key formats for external systems, verify compatibility — the new keys preserve length and character set in most cases but may differ in internal composition.

Tests & performance:
- New unit tests and benchmarks added. Tests assert uniqueness under concurrency and validate format correctness.
- Benchmarks show improved reliability; performance remains comparable to or better than the previous implementation.

Notes for reviewers:
- Focus review on the crypto usage and concurrency handling in the new utility module.
- Pay attention to the added tests for edge cases and race conditions.

Add zbMATH importer/fetcher

- Introduces a new ZbMATH fetcher (org.jabref.logic.importer.fetcher.ZbMATH) that can search zbmath.org and fetch entries by zbMATH identifier. The fetcher:
  - Builds queries against https://zbmath.org/bibtexoutput/ for both searches and id lookups (uses an: prefix for identifier lookups).
  - Requests up to 200 results for queries and 1 result for id lookups.
  - Calls URLDownload.bypassSSLVerification() (mirrors existing behavior in other fetchers).
  - Parses results using the BibtexParser and performs post-cleanup steps (moves msc2010 -> keywords, fjournal -> journal, removes braces from journal and title).
  - Contains a TODO/comment about possibly using the zbMATH citation matcher for entry-based lookups.

- Registers ZbMATH in WebFetchers so it is available as a search-based, id-based and entry-based fetcher (and included in id fetchers where applicable).

- Adds unit tests (src/test/java/.../ZbMATHTest.java) that verify search by query and search by id return the expected BibEntry.

- Updates CHANGELOG (Unreleased) to announce the ability to add a new entry via its zbMATH ID.

Notes / follow-ups:
- The fetcher currently bypasses SSL verification using URLDownload.bypassSSLVerification(); consider reviewing this for security implications.
- The citation-matching endpoint is mentioned as a potential enhancement for entry-based matching (left as TODO).

text:
Summary of changes

This PR implements and enhances several core components across the application, including application startup behavior, linked-file handling, multiple fetchers for external services, and version utilities. Key updates by file:

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/JabRefMain.java
  - Improved startup initialization flow: installs fallback exception handler, initializes preferences and runs preference migrations.
  - Configures proxy settings and authentication when required.
  - Starts background tasks and applies preferences (import/export formats, protected terms, newline override).
  - Adds routine to clear out-of-date full-text search indices by deleting directories older than the current index.
  - Handles multiple application instances via the remote server client/server logic.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/LinkedFileViewModel.java
  - Full implementation of linked-file view model features and UI interactions:
    - Properties for download progress, download ongoing state, automatically-found flag and offline-PDF flag.
    - Validation to check if a linked file exists (online links are exempt).
    - Opening files and folders, including resolution via file preferences and informative error dialogs.
    - Renaming with conflict checks and user confirmation, moving files to the default directory, and combined move+rename operations.
    - Deletion flow with dialog offering to remove from entry or delete from disk.
    - Downloading online linked files: SSL handshake checking, inferring file type from MIME/URL, preparing download tasks that preserve SSL settings, duplicate-file checks and automatic adding of downloaded file to the entry.
    - Writing metadata (XMP) to PDFs and embedding BibTeX entries.
    - Parsing PDF metadata using multiple importers and showing a merge dialog.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/IEEE.java
  - Implements IEEE fetcher supporting both full-text lookup and paged search parsing.
  - Parses IEEE API JSON responses into BibEntry objects (authors, abstract, DOI, pages, keywords, identifiers, PDF URL, etc.).
  - Tries to detect IEEE PDF URLs via URL/DOI heuristics and by parsing HTML frames when required.
  - Builds API queries for search with support for filtering by journal and year range and respects pagination.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/MrDLibFetcher.java
  - Adds Mr. DLib recommendations fetcher (Entry-based fetcher).
  - Uses URIBuilder to construct Mr. DLib requests with partner/app id and app version.
  - Respects user preferences for sending language, OS and timezone information.
  - Parses XML responses using MrDLibImporter and surfaces meaningful fallback messages on errors.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/ZbMATH.java
  - Adds ZbMATH fetcher for searching and identifier-based lookups against zbmath.org.
  - Implements citation matching: builds parameterized requests from entry fields (title, journal, authors, year, pagination, volume, issue) and retrieves zbMATH identifiers.
  - Requests bibtex output for found identifiers and uses BibtexParser to parse results.
  - Performs post-cleanup on fetched entries (move/format fields, remove braces).

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/util/Version.java
  - Utility to parse version strings (supports major/minor/patch/stage/dev and strips CI suffixes).
  - Fetches available releases from GitHub and converts them to Version objects.
  - Implements comparison logic (isNewerThan, shouldBeUpdatedTo) including development stage stability handling.
  - Provides helper to build changelog URL for a specific version and implements DevelopmentStage enum.

Notes
- The PR focuses on robust handling of external resources (downloads, remote servers, fetcher APIs) and safe startup/cleanup procedures.
- Error handling and user feedback (dialogs, notifications) are included wherever file/network operations can fail.

If you want, I can split this PR into smaller focused changes (e.g. LinkedFile edits, each fetcher, version util, startup cleanup) to make review easier.

Summary:
- Display the total number of citations for each entry in the UI and expose that value in the API.

What I changed:
- Backend: added computation of total citations for an entry and included it in the entry payload as "totalCitations".
  - For performance, this is returned from a counter cache when available, otherwise calculated with an aggregate COUNT query.
  - Added a migration to add a citations_count field (counter cache) and a backfill script to populate existing counts.
- Frontend: shows the total citation count on the entry details view (near title/metadata) as a small badge/label. Handles zero and null values gracefully and uses localized wording for singular/plural where appropriate.
- Tests: added unit tests for the backend field and API response, plus integration/UI tests to assert the count is rendered correctly and updates on refresh.

Files / areas touched (high-level):
- Backend entry model/serializer/controller: include totalCitations in API output, migration/backfill script
- Frontend entry-details component/template and styles: display badge/label for total citations
- Tests: model/api tests, frontend snapshot/integration tests

How to review / test manually:
1. Run the migration and backfill (if prompted).
2. Start the server and open an entry detail page. Verify a "Total citations: N" badge appears next to the entry title or metadata.
3. Create or remove a citation for the entry and refresh the page; verify the count updates accordingly (or that an incremental update happens if real-time update behavior exists).
4. Call the entry API (e.g., GET /entries/:id) and confirm the response includes "totalCitations" with the expected numeric value.

Notes:
- The change is backward-compatible: existing API clients will still receive previous fields and can ignore the added "totalCitations" property if not needed.
- The counter cache migration and backfill are included to avoid expensive COUNT queries on high-traffic endpoints. If you prefer not to run the migration immediately, the code will fall back to computing counts on the fly.
- No breaking UI or API changes expected.

If reviewers want, I can separate the migration/backfill into a follow-up PR to reduce risk during deployment.

- Update site config (docs/_config.yml) to enable Mermaid (version 9.4.3) and the copy-code button.
- Add editor dictionary entries (.vscode/ltex.dictionary.en-US.txt) for JabDrive, JabRef, and CouchDB to improve spellchecking.

This PR is purely documentation/configuration focused and does not change application logic.

text:
Summary

Fixes issue #2811: the BibTeX key generator failed to use crossref information when generating keys for entries that reference other entries (via crossref). As a result, fields such as author/editor, year, or title pulled from the referenced entry were ignored and produced incorrect or incomplete keys.

What I changed

- Updated the BibTeX key generation logic to resolve crossref references and consult the referenced entry when required fields are missing from the child entry.
- Implemented safe traversal of crossref chains (uses referenced fields only when original entry lacks them), with cycle detection and a sensible depth limit to avoid infinite loops.
- Added unit tests covering:
  - Direct crossref usage (child uses parent's year/author/editor)
  - Transitive crossrefs (A -> B -> C)
  - Cyclic crossref detection and fallback behavior
  - Cases where child entry already has fields (no override)
- Minor documentation/comments describing the new behavior and rationale.

Why this fixes the issue

Previously the generator only inspected the entry itself; for entries that rely on crossref to inherit metadata from a parent (common for proceedings, inproceedings, etc.), the generator could not produce the expected key because required fields were missing. By resolving and merging crossref metadata when needed, the generator now produces consistent keys that match users' expectations and BibTeX inheritance semantics.

Compatibility and performance

- Behaviour is backward compatible for entries that already contain the required fields; no changes to existing keys in those cases.
- Performance impact is negligible for normal bibliographies; the implementation limits traversal depth and detects cycles to avoid expensive resolution.

Notes

- Tests included to prevent regressions.
- If desired, we can make the traversal depth configurable in a follow-up.

- Consider enabling additional SpotBugs detectors or integrating with IDEs for developer feedback.

text:
Fix title-related key patterns to match documentation and expected behavior

What I changed
- Implemented proper handling for title-related key patterns in BibtexKeyPatternUtil:
  - Added support for [title] (camelize significant words) and [camel] (capitalize and concatenate all words).
  - Introduced helper methods: formatTitle (removes LaTeX commands, hyphens and normalizes whitespace), camelizeTitle/getCamelizedTitle, camelizeSignificantWordsInTitle, removeSmallWords and a refactored getTitleWordsWithSpaces using Scanner/StringJoiner.
  - Updated applyModifiers to return these title variants where appropriate, and adjusted veryshorttitle handling to remove small words first.
- Minor cleanup: small parenthesis style change in a condition and added imports for Scanner and StringJoiner.

Why
- The previous implementation did not produce title-derived keys consistent with the documentation (help.jabref.org/en/BibtexKeyPatterns) and expectations reported in issues #2604 and #2589. The prior approach using CaseFormat required the title to already be in lower-camel form, which is not generally true. The new implementation parses and normalizes the title, handles small words correctly and provides the documented behaviors for [title] and [camel].

Tests & changelog
- Updated and added unit tests to reflect the corrected behavior (BibtexKeyPatternUtilTest and MakeLabelWithDatabaseTest).
  - Adjusted several expected key outputs to the new behavior and added tests for the new [camel] and [title] behaviors.
- Updated CHANGELOG.md with the fix entry.

Notes
- The changes aim to align key-generation with the documented patterns. Some cite-key expectations changed accordingly (tests updated to match).
- This supersedes attempts that relied on CaseFormat for camel-casing, offering more robust handling for typical BibTeX titles (including LaTeX formatting removal and hyphen handling).

text:
Fixes #8446 — Prevent UI freeze on first entry selection after fresh start

Summary
- The freeze occurring when selecting an entry for the first time (caused by constructing a JavaFX WebView for the preview panel) has been fixed by preloading WebView instances on the JavaFX thread.

What I changed
- Added a new utility: org.jabref.logic.util.WebViewStore
  - Preloads WebView instances on the FX thread using Platform.runLater to avoid blocking the UI during first use
  - Provides WebViewStore.get() to obtain a preloaded instance (and falls back to creating one if needed)
  - Dynamic refill: when the available instances drop below a configured minimum, additional instances are scheduled to be created
  - Default configuration preloads 4 instances and keeps a minimum of 2 (configurable via WebViewStore.init(Configuration))
  - Throws IllegalStateException if get() is called before initialization
- Initialize the store at application startup: call WebViewStore.init() in JabRefGUI
- Replace direct new WebView() calls with WebViewStore.get() in:
  - PreviewViewer
  - MathSciNetTab
- Update CHANGELOG.md with a user-facing note about the fix
- Minor whitespace cleanup in JabRefMain

Why this fixes the issue
- Constructing a WebView for the first time triggers costly initialization that caused a 3–4 second freeze when selecting the first entry. By preloading WebView instances asynchronously at startup, the expensive initialization happens off the critical first-selection path and the preview/editor can immediately obtain a ready WebView.

Notes for maintainers
- WebViewStore.init() must be called at application startup before components call WebViewStore.get().
- The default config is conservative (4 preload, 2 minimum) but can be tuned if needed.
- I evaluated a proxy-based approach (building PreviewViewer via CompletableFuture + Platform.runLater) but it was more complex and risked changing behavior, so I chose the preloading approach instead.

Testing
- Manually tested in running JabRef; selecting the first entry after a fresh start no longer causes the freeze (video included in the original issue/PR).

text:
Add CitationStyle utility to load and discover CSL styles

Summary
- Introduces org.jabref.logic.citationstyle.CitationStyle, a representation for Citation Style (CSL) files containing filepath, title and raw source.
- Provides methods to load styles from classpath resources or external files, parse title from CSL XML and discover bundled styles when running from a JAR.

Details
- createCitationStyleFromFile(String): loads a CSL file from the classpath (resource) or from the filesystem. Uses CSLUtils.readURLToString for resources and Files.readAllBytes for external files.
- createCitationStyleFromSource(String, String): parses the CSL XML to extract the <title> under <info> and constructs a CitationStyle. Parsing errors are logged and result in null.
- stripInvalidProlog(String): guards against invalid prolog / leading bytes before the first '<' (helps when files contain unexpected characters or BOM).
- discoverCitationStyles(): enumerates entries in the running JAR and loads files ending with .csl (skips entries under "dependent"). Logs a helpful error and returns an empty list if not running from a JAR or on failure.
- isCitationStyleFile(String): checks filename against configured citation style extensions (uses FileExtensions.CITATION_STYLE).
- getDefault(): convenience to load the default style (/ieee.csl).
- equals() and hashCode() overridden to compare CitationStyle instances by their source content.

Logging & error handling
- Parsing, IO and URI errors are logged via commons-logging. createCitationStyleFromFile returns null on failure so callers should handle null results.

Why
- Centralizes CSL style handling and makes it easy to read styles both bundled inside the application jar and provided as external files.
- Makes title extraction robust against malformed prologs and provides discovery for packaged CSL styles.

Notes for reviewers / testing
- Test loading built-in style using CitationStyle.getDefault().
- Test loading external .csl file path and a classpath resource (e.g., "/ieee.csl").
- Verify discoverCitationStyles() returns a list when running from the assembled JAR and logs a clear message when running from source.
- Check behavior when giving malformed XML or files with leading BOM/bytes — parsing error should be logged and method should return null.

Introduce robust handling for column preference variable name changes and restore backward compatibility for pre-5.0 preferences.

What changed
- JabRefPreferences: Renamed the COLUMN_* constants to the new mainTableColumn* names (mainTableColumnNames, mainTableColumnWidths, mainTableColumnSortTypes, mainTableColumnSortOrder) and added a comment explaining the rename to support backward compatibility with pre-5.0 releases.

- PreferencesMigrations:
  - Reordered migration calls in runMigrations so that changeColumnVariableNamesFor51 runs before upgradeColumnPreferences and restoreVariablesForBackwardCompatibility runs after upgradeColumnPreferences. This ensures correct copying/conversion of old preference keys and maintains backward compatibility.
  - Added changeColumnVariableNamesFor51(JabRefPreferences): copies values from the old hardcoded keys (e.g. "columnNames", "columnWidths", "columnSortTypes", "columnSortOrder") into the new JabRefPreferences keys if present and the new keys are empty.
  - Added restoreVariablesForBackwardCompatibility(JabRefPreferences):
    - Detects field:... and special:... prefixed columns from the new mainTableColumnNames and restores legacy plain names into the old key names ("columnNames", "columnWidths", "columnSortTypes", "columnSortOrder"). It also creates sensible default widths (100) and clears sort settings for compatibility.
    - Ensures MAIN_FONT_SIZE is stored as an integer: if the preference is stored as a double string (e.g. "11.2"), it rounds and writes it back as an int to handle older versions that expect an int.
  - Minor import addition (Collections) and explanatory comments about hardcoded variable names.

- Tests (PreferencesMigrationsTest):
  - Added tests for changeColumnVariableNamesFor51 to ensure old keys are copied into the new keys.
  - Added a test to ensure upgradeColumnPreferences does not write back incompatible old keys unexpectedly.
  - Added a test for restoreVariablesForBackwardCompatibility to verify extraction of plain field names from "field:"/"special:" entries, setting default widths, clearing sort settings, and converting font size from a double string to an int.

Why
- Earlier releases (pre-5.0) used different column variable names and formats. Newer versions changed both the variable names and formats, which caused incompatibilities when users downgraded or when older versions read newer preferences. These changes ensure:
  - Existing old preferences are copied into the new keys so newer code can read them.
  - Newer preference formats that include prefixes (field:/special:) are converted back to plain legacy formats so older JabRef versions can create and use preferences correctly.
  - MAIN_FONT_SIZE is consistently stored as an integer to avoid type issues.

This PR is focused on making the preferences migration path safe and reversible so users can update/downgrade without losing or corrupting preference data.

Summary

Improve the user friendliness of automatically detected file links in the entry editor by making the accept/link action more prominent, changing the icon to a more intuitive symbol, and visually de-emphasizing files that are only auto-detected until the user accepts them. This addresses user feedback and fixes #3607.

What I changed

- UI behavior
  - Move the accept (auto-link) button to the far left of each file row so the action is easier to find.
  - Use a link-plus icon for automatically found files instead of the suitcase/briefcase icon (BRIEFCASE_CHECK -> LINK_PLUS), which better communicates "add/link this file".
  - Render automatically found file names with lowered opacity (70%) until the file is accepted, making it clear they are not yet linked.
  - Ensure the accept button is only visible/managed when the file is automatically found so layout does not leave gaps.

- Implementation details
  - Added a CSS pseudo-class for the faded appearance and updated Base.css with a .file-row-text:opacity rule to set the 70% opacity.
  - Bind the pseudo-class state to the LinkedFileViewModel.isAutomaticallyFoundProperty() using EasyBind so the text fades in/out automatically.
  - Reordered the HBox children so the accept button appears before the file info, and bound the button's managedProperty() to the same isAutomaticallyFoundProperty() to avoid empty spacing when not shown.
  - Replaced the automatic-file icon constant in IconTheme to use LINK_PLUS.
  - Updated CHANGELOG.md to describe the user-facing change.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/LinkedFilesEditor.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/icon/IconTheme.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/Base.css
- CHANGELOG.md

Notes
- Manually tested in a running JabRef instance. Screenshots are included in the PR description to show before/after states.
- Documentation (docs.jabref.org) still references the old suitcase icon; this should be updated to describe the new link-with-plus icon if the change is accepted.

Fixes
- Fixes #3607

Replace eager/null-initialized context menu fields with late initialization to simplify lifecycle management and eliminate unnecessary null checks.

What I changed

- Converted context menu-related variables from nullable types (or early initialization) to lateinit properties and/or lazy initialization where appropriate.
- Moved context menu construction code into lifecycle-appropriate callbacks (e.g., onCreateContextMenu / when first accessed) so menus are created only when needed.
- Removed redundant null checks and Elvis operators around those menu variables.
- Updated related call sites to assume non-nullability after initialization.

Why

- Prevents initialization-order and nullability issues during component lifecycle transitions.
- Improves readability by removing noise from defensive null handling.
- Ensures menus are created at the appropriate time, avoiding wasted work and potential NPEs when accessing them before initialization.

- Manually verified context menus open and close correctly across typical lifecycle flows (creation, rotation, background/foreground).
- Verified no crashes from accessing menu properties before creation.
- Adjusted/added unit/instrumentation tests where applicable to reflect non-null properties.

Notes / Considerations

- Lateinit properties must not be accessed before initialization; ensure creation path is executed (e.g., during onCreateContextMenu or first access).
- If any code paths rely on menus being present very early, move initialization accordingly or keep a guarded path.

Files touched (high level)

- Context menu related classes and activities/fragments (variables and initialization moved/updated).

- CHANGELOG.md: documented the UI change.

Why:
- Improves discoverability and clarity for automatically detected files by making the linking action more visible and providing a clear visual state for files that are not yet linked.

Add UI controls and behavior to hide AI and related-tabs and improve AI privacy notices

Summary
- Add buttons to hide AI-related tabs and Mr. DLib related-articles tab from the privacy dialogs so users can opt out of seeing those tabs.
- Enhance the AI privacy notice UI to list AI providers with links to their privacy policies and to display information about the DJL embedding model download size.
- Wire up actions to open provider/privacy links in the system browser and to toggle the corresponding preferences (requiring restart to take effect).

What changed
- UI
  - src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/ai/components/privacynotice/PrivacyNoticeComponent.fxml
    - New layout: adds provider/privacy hyperlinks, embedding model text, and buttons: “I agree” and “Hide 'AI tabs'”.
  - src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preferences/entryeditor/EntryEditorTab.fxml
    - Added checkboxes for showing AI tabs and the Related Articles tab and an accept-recommendations checkbox bound to Related Articles toggle.

- Behavior / Logic
  - src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/ai/components/privacynotice/PrivacyNoticeComponent.java
    - Populates AI provider privacy hyperlinks in a GridPane and binds wrapping widths.
    - onIAgreeButtonClick enables AI via AiPreferences and invokes the provided callback.
    - hideAITabs() disables the AI Summary and AI Chat tabs in EntryEditorPreferences and shows a restart warning.
    - openBrowser() uses NativeDesktop with error handling (DialogService + logging).
  - src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/entryeditor/RelatedArticlesTab.java
    - Privacy dialog for Mr. DLib now includes a “Hide 'Related articles' tab” button which sets the preference to hide the tab and prompts for restart. The existing “I Agree” action updates MrDlib preferences as before.

- Localization / Strings
  - src/main/resources/l10n/JabRef_en.properties
    - Add many AI and Mr. DLib related strings (privacy notice, embedding model text, UI labels like “Hide 'AI tabs'”, “I agree”, “Show tab 'AI Chat'”, “Show tab 'AI Summary'”, “Hide 'Related articles' tab”, etc.).

Other
- CHANGELOG.md updated to mention the new button in Privacy notice and Mr. DLib privacy settings for hiding related tabs.

Notes
- Hiding tabs updates preferences but requires a restart for changes to take effect; users are warned accordingly.
- Provider privacy policy links open via NativeDesktop and errors are surfaced via the DialogService.

Files modified (high level)
- PrivacyNoticeComponent.fxml, PrivacyNoticeComponent.java
- RelatedArticlesTab.java
- EntryEditorTab.fxml
- JabRef_en.properties
- CHANGELOG.md

This change improves privacy control and discoverability of AI/privacy information and provides a straightforward way for users to hide AI and recommendation UI elements if they prefer not to use them.

text: This is a refactored version of the JabRefPreferences class, which provides a centralized way to manage preferences for the JabRef application. The class includes various methods for getting and setting preferences, including language, citation key patterns, external applications, and more. The preferences are stored in a hierarchical structure, with each preference having a unique key and value. Summary
- Fixes a bug where external group metadata changes were not merged into the database when applying metadata changes. This addresses issue #8873.

What I changed
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/bibtex/comparator/GroupDiff.java
  - Corrected the order of arguments passed to the GroupDiff constructor in compare(...). The original and new group roots were swapped, which caused later logic to treat external changes as if they were the original state.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/collab/MetaDataChangeViewModel.java
  - When applying metadata changes, restore the groups root to the original value because group changes are handled separately by GroupChangeViewModel. This prevents inconsistencies when metadata and group changes are applied together.
  - Added a clarifying comment.

- src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/bibtex/comparator/GroupDiffTest.java
  - Updated the expected GroupDiff construction to match the corrected argument order.

- CHANGELOG.md
  - Added an entry noting the fix for external group metadata changes not being merged.

Why this fixes the problem
- The compare(...) method previously returned a GroupDiff with swapped original/new roots, so downstream code misinterpreted which tree was the original and which was the new version. Correcting the order ensures merge/apply logic sees the proper original vs. new group roots. Additionally, ensuring MetaDataChangeViewModel leaves group handling to GroupChangeViewModel avoids inconsistent state when both metadata and group diffs exist.

Tests
- Updated GroupDiffTest to reflect the corrected parameter order. Existing tests cover the corrected behavior.

Add preview pane with search highlighting to Global Search results

- Integrate PreviewViewer into GlobalSearchResultDialog to display a rendered preview of the selected search result. The preview is created with the library-specific PreviewLayout from preferences and updated when the selection changes.
- Wire selection listener so the preview shows the currently selected entry and falls back to the previous entry when selection is cleared.
- Remove SpecialFieldColumn from the search results table to simplify the table view for the dialog.
- Implement search-term highlighting inside PreviewViewer using mark.js: convert Java SearchQuery patterns to JavaScript regular expressions (escaping forward slashes) and call mark.js methods to highlight / unhighlight matches in the WebView content.
- Ensure links in the preview open in the system browser (JabRefDesktop.openBrowser) instead of navigating inside the WebView, and avoid page-whiteout with a default preview body when no entry/layout is set.
- Add copy/selection helpers to export plain text and HTML from the preview to the clipboard and keep them functional for global search previews.
- Keep theming support by applying ThemeManager CSS to the WebView and make the dialog’s Keep-on-Top toggle reflect the view model state with appropriate icons.

This improves the Global Search UX by showing a live, themed preview of selected entries with highlighted search terms and copyable content.

Summary

Fixes a bug in the import pipeline where custom entry types that contained duplicate fields (by name or id) were imported incorrectly — fields could be lost, merged incorrectly, or the import could fail.

Root cause

The import logic deduplicated fields using the wrong key and did not consistently map source field IDs/UUIDs to new or existing field IDs in the target system. That caused collisions when the imported entry type contained fields that shared labels or IDs with each other or with existing fields in the target.

What I changed

- Import now uses stable field UUID mapping rather than relying on field labels for deduplication.
- When a conflict is detected, the importer will generate new UUIDs for genuinely new fields and update all internal references to those fields so entries keep correct links.
- Duplicate fields in the source are preserved when intended (rather than being silently merged) and are disambiguated safely when necessary.
- Added defensive checks and clearer logging for field conflicts during import.

Tests

- Added unit tests covering: duplicate field names, duplicate field UUIDs in the import payload, and collisions with existing fields in the target project.
- Added integration tests that verify entries referencing those fields maintain correct links post-import.

Compatibility and migration notes

- No database schema changes required.
- Backwards-compatible behavior for existing imports; this change only affects the import path.

Impact

- Fixes import failures and data loss when importing custom entry types with duplicate fields.
- Low-risk change limited to import logic, but recommend running imports on staging first for critical projects.

Release note

Fixed import of custom entry types so duplicate fields are handled correctly and no longer lost or merged incorrectly.

text: This pull request addresses the issue of incorrect glyph icon colors in the Search Bar when using Dark Mode. The changes ensure that the icons are now clearly visible and consistent with the dark theme. Fix Export to Clipboard selection for custom exporters with uppercase file extensions

Problem:
- Custom export formats that declared their file extension in uppercase (e.g. ".HTML") were not selectable via "Copy... -> Export to Clipboard". The comparison between exporter file types and the supported file type set was case-sensitive and the FileType equality implementation mutated internal lists, which could lead to incorrect mismatches or runtime issues.

What I changed:
- Normalized and made FileType equality comparisons robust and case-insensitive by ensuring extension strings are handled in lowercase and by avoiding in-place mutation when comparing extension lists (UnknownFileType.equals now compares copies/sorted lists rather than sorting the originals).
- Ensured the exporter filtering used by ExportToClipboardAction correctly recognizes custom exporter file types regardless of case so they show up in the exporter choice dialog.

Files touched / key points:
- logic/util/UnknownFileType.java: fixed equals() to perform non-mutating, case-insensitive comparison of extensions.
- (Related) logic/util/StandardFileType.java: existing file type enums are lowercase; comparisons now work reliably against UnknownFileType.
- gui/exporter/ExportToClipboardAction.java and gui/maintable/RightClickMenu.java: use the exporter selection/filtering flow that now correctly identifies matching exporters.

Result:
- Custom exporters with uppercase or mixed-case file extensions are now correctly listed and selectable in "Copy... -> Export to Clipboard" (fixes #6285). No user-facing behavior changed otherwise; this is a correctness/stability fix.

text:
Add StateManager to centralize GUI state and connect GlobalSearchBar to application state

Summary of changes
- New StateManager class
  - Centralizes GUI state: active database, active groups, selected entries, selected groups per database, active search query, and a per-database search result-size map.
  - Provides properties and helper methods to get/set the active search query, selected entries/groups, clear selections, and fetch entries in the current database.
  - Binds activeGroups to the selectedGroups entry for the currently active database.
  - Ensures safe defaults and uses OptionalObjectProperty for optional state values.

- GlobalSearchBar updates and integration
  - Integrates GlobalSearchBar with StateManager: the search field is bound bidirectionally to stateManager.activeSearchQueryProperty(). Changes in the UI update the central state and vice versa.
  - When a search is performed, the search query is pushed into StateManager via setSearchQuery(); clearing the field clears the active search via clearSearchQuery().
  - Subscribes to stateManager.activeSearchQueryProperty() to update the visible result count using stateManager.getSearchResultSize().
  - Keeps existing behavior for invalid regex and invalid search queries; shows appropriate messages and pseudo-class styling.
  - Retains and extends autocompletion support: reflection helper to access the AutoCompletionBinding popup and a custom popup skin that adds a toolbar (regular expression toggle, case sensitivity toggle, and search mode button) to the suggestion popup.
  - Adds UI niceties: delayed search execution (SEARCH_DELAY), animated expand/contract of the search field on focus, validation visualization for regex, and tooltip/hint management.

Why
- Centralizing GUI-related state in StateManager simplifies sharing state between different UI components and avoids scattering stateful logic throughout the codebase.
- Connecting GlobalSearchBar to StateManager allows consistent handling of search state and search result counts across the application.

Notes
- The new StateManager is designed to be used by other GUI components in future changes (e.g., panels, main table) to read/write shared UI state (active database/groups/search).

Summary

This PR restores backward compatibility for users who want to downgrade from JabRef 5.x back to JabRef 4.3.1 (or other pre-5.0 releases). It adds migration logic to preserve and convert column preference variables, restores older variable names and values so older JabRef versions can read them, and includes a Windows registry patch that helps users revert preferences after trying newer versions.

What I changed

- Add migration steps and utilities
  - Introduced changeColumnVariableNamesFor51(JabRefPreferences) which copies pre-5.1 preference keys (hardcoded names) into the new preference keys when appropriate.
  - Introduced restoreVariablesForBackwardCompatibility(JabRefPreferences) which:
    - Converts 5.0+/5.1-style column names (field:... and special:...) back into plain field names and writes them to the old keys (columnNames, columnWidths, columnSortTypes, columnSortOrder) so older JabRef versions can read a familiar format.
    - Supplies default widths (100) for restored columns and clears column sort types/order so older versions will regenerate reasonable defaults.
    - Fixes a font-size backward-compatibility issue by coercing font size values previously stored as doubles into an integer preference key.
  - Adjusted runMigrations ordering so that variable name changes and backward-compatibility restores are executed in the correct sequence.

- Preferences key changes
  - JabRefPreferences had the column-related constant names changed to the new mainTableColumn* names (mainTableColumnNames, mainTableColumnWidths, mainTableColumnSortTypes, mainTableColumnSortOrder). The code now uses these constants and handles copying/restore to the old names for backward compatibility.

- Tests
  - Added unit tests in PreferencesMigrationsTest for:
    - changeColumnVariableNamesFor51 behavior
    - restoreVariablesForBackwardCompatibility behavior (including font-size coercion and default width filling)
    - Ensuring upgradeColumnPreferences does not overwrite older compatibility variables inappropriately

- Misc
  - Included JabRef-downgrade-regpatch.reg to help Windows users revert registry-stored preferences when downgrading.

Files touched (high level)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/migrations/PreferencesMigrations.java: added migration methods and reordered migration calls
- src/main/java/org/jabref/preferences/JabRefPreferences.java: renamed column-related preference constants and documented the reason
- src/test/java/org/jabref/migrations/PreferencesMigrationsTest.java: added tests for the new migration behavior
- JabRef-downgrade-regpatch.reg: registry patch to assist Windows downgrades

Why this is needed

JabRef 5.0 changed the format and names of main table column preferences, making it impossible for users to go back to older JabRef versions without losing or corrupting their column configuration. This PR provides a migration path so users who try newer versions can safely return to JabRef 4.3.1 (or other pre-5.0 releases) and keep working with sensible preferences.

Related issues
- fixes #5933
- fixes #6234
- refs #4579

Notes and remaining questions

- The PR contains a Windows registry patch (JabRef-downgrade-regpatch.reg). We should decide how to distribute or include this in installers (question from OP).
- Testers: It would be helpful if someone with Java 8 and JabRef 4.3.1 could verify the full downgrade process (including applying the regpatch and running an older installer).

- [x] Tests added
- [x] Manually tested changed features
- [ ] CHANGELOG updated (if applicable)

Summary

This PR implements a new "ottobib" fetcher to retrieve bibliographic metadata from the Ottobib service. The fetcher is registered with the existing fetcher registry and can be used the same way as other fetchers (e.g., CrossRef, GoogleBooks).

What I changed

- Added a new fetcher module: fetchers/ottobib.py
  - Performs HTTP requests to Ottobib with configurable timeout and retry policy.
  - Parses Ottobib responses and maps fields into the projects standard bibliographic entry format (title, authors, publisher, year, ISBN, etc.).
  - Handles common error cases and returns normalized error messages when Ottobib is unreachable or returns unexpected content.
- Registered the ottobib fetcher in the global fetcher registry so it can be invoked by name.
- Added unit tests for the ottobib fetcher:
  - Tests for successful fetch and parsing from sample Ottobib output.
  - Tests for timeouts, bad responses, and retry logic.
  - Uses recorded fixtures/mocked HTTP responses to keep tests deterministic.
- Documentation updates:
  - Added usage notes to the fetchers section describing how to enable/use the ottobib fetcher and available configuration options (timeout, retries, user-agent).
- Minor: added utility helpers for safe HTML parsing and basic caching (in-memory TTL) that help the ottobib fetcher and that other fetchers can reuse.

Why this change

Ottobib provides a convenient way to look up bibliographic metadata by ISBN. Adding this fetcher increases the number of sources available for automated metadata resolution, improving coverage for certain publishers and older books.

Behavior and configuration

- Default behavior: attempt a single fetch with a short timeout, fall back gracefully on failure.
- Configurable settings: timeout (seconds), number of retries, cache TTL, and user-agent override.
- Errors from Ottobib are returned in the fetchers standard error format so callers can make consistent decisions about retries or fallbacks.

Tests

- New tests added under tests/fetchers/test_ottobib.py covering success and failure cases.
- CI: tests pass locally and on CI with mocked HTTP responses.

Backward compatibility / Migration

- Non-breaking: the new fetcher is additive and does not change existing fetchers or the default registry behavior unless explicitly enabled/used.

Notes / Follow-ups

- Consider adding a scraping-avoidance delay or shared rate-limiting across fetchers if usage increases to avoid overloading Ottobib.
- If Ottobib offers or introduces an API, consider switching from HTML parsing to the API for more robust parsing.

If you want, I can split the fetcher and helper utilities into separate PRs or add an integration test calling the live Ottobib service (currently mocked).

Extend RIS importer: add support for many additional RIS tags and improve mappings

What changed
- RIS importer (RisImporter.java): extended recognition and mapping of many RIS tags to JabRef fields:
  - Journal/title tags: T2, J2, JA mapped to journal if missing; JO, J1, JF override journal
  - Author/editor variants: A2, A3, A4 now treated as authors when appropriate; ED handled as editor; AU and A1 still supported
  - Number field: also map AN, C7, M1 to number
  - Address: include PP as address
  - URL: accept L2 and LK as URL in addition to UR
  - Year/date: accept Y2 in addition to Y1, PY, DA and extract year
  - DOI: recognize M3 and DO and add via addDoi
  - Event title, note, short title, eprint/pubmed, translator: map C3, N1/RN, ST, C2 (with eprinttype=pubmed), TA
  - Unmapped/aux fields saved into nonstandard BibTeX fields: AV->archive_location, CN/VO->call-number, DB->archive, NV->number-of-volumes, OP->original-title, RI->reviewed-title, RP->status, SE->section
  - ID still mapped to refid
- Normalization and post-processing:

  - Month parsing and setMonth usage preserved
- Minor refactor: rename local BibEntry variable from b to entry for clarity

- Updated test parameter list to include the new test

Why
- To broaden RIS import coverage and correctly handle more varieties of RIS tag names used in exported files from different tools and providers, improving import fidelity and reducing manual fixes after import.

text:
Add localization QA tools: JUnit tests and a sync script

What I changed
- Added scripts/syncLang.py — a helper script to check, update and produce a markdown status of localization (.properties) files under src/main/resources/l10n. Supports commands: status, update and markdown, with an optional -e/--extended flag. The script fixes unambiguous duplicates, removes obsolete keys, adds missing keys and sorts files when running update, and writes status.md for markdown.
- Added src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/l10n/LocalizationConsistencyTest.java — comprehensive JUnit tests to ensure localization quality:
  - allFilesMustBeInLanguages: verifies .properties files match Languages.LANGUAGES
  - ensureNoDuplicates: detects duplicate keys inside property bundles
  - keyValueShouldBeEqualForEnglishPropertiesMenu / Messages: asserts English files use key=key conventions (Menu removes &)
  - languageKeysShouldNotBeQuotedInFiles: ensures code does not use quoted language keys
  - findMissingLocalizationKeys / findMissingMenuLocalizationKeys: reports keys used in code but missing in English property files
  - findObsoleteLocalizationKeys / findObsoleteMenuLocalizationKeys: finds keys in English files that are no longer used
  - localizationParameterMustIncludeAString: enforces localization parameter usage includes a String literal when required
  - Embedded DuplicationDetectionProperties helper to detect duplicate keys when loading properties

Why
- Improve localization maintenance by automatically checking consistency, spotting duplicates, missing or obsolete entries and by providing a tool to sync translations with the English source.

How to use / test
- Generate a status markdown: python ./scripts/syncLang.py markdown
- Check status on console: python ./scripts/syncLang.py status [-e|--extended]
- Update translation files automatically (fixing unambiguous issues): python ./scripts/syncLang.py update [-e|--extended]
- Run the test suite: ./gradlew test (or ./gradlew check)

Notes
- This PR does not change application behavior; it adds tests and tooling for localization quality.
- CHANGELOG.md was not modified in this PR.

text:
Preferences UI & backend: Add import/export/show/reset functionality and preference utilities

Summary
- Add Import, Export, Show and Reset buttons to the Preferences dialog (PreferencesDialog).
- Implement import/export flows (file chooser, error handling, user notifications) and a confirmation reset that clears preferences and shared-database preferences.
- Add helper actions to persist and apply changes immediately (storeAllSettings, updateAfterPreferenceChanges).
- Add several convenience methods and utilities to JabRefPreferences: exportPreferences, importPreferences, getPreferences (returns Map), getObject helper, putStringList/getStringList (with escaping), color utilities, and other getters/setters to better manipulate preferences programmatically.

Details
- PreferencesDialog
  - Adds UI buttons for Import preferences, Export preferences, Show preferences (opens PreferencesFilterDialog), and Reset preferences.
  - Implements the import action with a file dialog that accepts XML, imports into Preferences via JabRefPreferences.importPreferences, prompts user to restart, and updates the runtime preferences state.
  - Implements the export action which first stores current settings and then saves preferences to a chosen XML file using JabRefPreferences.exportPreferences; stores the last export path.
  - Implements Reset preferences action which asks for confirmation, clears the stored Preferences node and SharedDatabasePreferences, notifies the user to restart, and updates the runtime state.
  - Adds storeAllSettings() to validate and persist all preference tabs, flush preferences, and refresh UI (table renderers, entry editor colors, group icons, etc.).
  - Adds updateAfterPreferenceChanges() to reinitialize export formats and entry-editor tab list after changes.

- JabRefPreferences
  - Implements exportPreferences(String) and importPreferences(String) wrappers using java.util.prefs API to read/write preferences subtree as XML with proper exception translation to JabRefException.
  - Adds getPreferences() returning a Map<String,Object> of all stored preferences (attempts appropriate type conversions via getObject()).
  - Adds putStringList/getStringList utilities that store/parse lists with escaping of the delimiter (‘;’) and related helper methods (convertListToString, getNextUnit).
  - Adds color helpers (getColor, getDefaultColor, putColor) and RGB parsing helper.
  - Other small helpers: getCustomTabFieldNames(), getUser(), overwritePreferences (for testing), getWrappedUsername(), etc.

Why
- Provide users with a safe and convenient way to import/export their preferences (useful for migrations, backups, portable setups and memory-stick mode).
- Allow users to inspect preferences via a filter dialog and to reset to default configuration if needed.
- Improve programmatic access to preference data for runtime reinitialization and testing.

Behavior & Compatibility
- Importing preferences requires restart for some changes to take effect; users are warned.
- Resetting preferences clears both user prefs and shared-database preferences (after confirmation). Users are warned to restart.
- Export writes the Java Preferences subtree to an XML file compatible with the java.util.prefs export/import utilities.

Testing & Notes
- Error conditions (I/O, invalid preferences XML, backing store exceptions) are logged and shown to the user via dialogs.
- After storing preferences via the dialog, UI components are updated immediately (renderers, entry editor colors, tables, group selector) to reflect most changes without restart when possible.
- Provided overwritePreferences is intended ONLY FOR TESTING (keeps singleton controllable in tests).

Summary:
This PR renames the AI provider label to indicate API compatibility and updates UI messages to reflect the selected model when generating summaries. It ensures that users running local or API-compatible LLMs can clearly select and see the provider/model used during processing and in the AI chat.

What I changed:
- Renamed the provider option in Preferences → AI to the API-compatible label (OpenAPI / API-compatible provider) so it’s clear that non-OpenAI endpoints can be used.
- Updated the processing UI message shown while generating an AI summary to reference the model selected by the user (so the progress/processing page now shows which model is generating the summary).
- Updated the AI Chat footer/credit text to indicate the chat is powered by an OpenAPI / API-compatible provider when that option is selected.
- Added a brief CHANGELOG entry describing the visible change.

Why:
Users running local LLMs (e.g. LM Studio, llama.cpp) or other API-compatible endpoints need a clear provider label and feedback in the UI which model is being used. These changes make configuration and runtime feedback clearer and avoid implying only OpenAI is supported.

How to test:
1. Open Preferences → AI
2. Select the provider labeled OpenAPI / API-compatible
3. Enable expert settings
4. Run a local LLM or API-compatible endpoint (LM Studio, llama.cpp, etc.) and enter the corresponding URL in the preferences
5. Import a PDF and open the Summary tab; while the summary is being generated, verify the processing message shows the model you selected
6. Open AI Chat and verify the bottom/footer indicates it is powered by the OpenAPI / API-compatible provider

Notes:
- Closes https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/13585
- Screenshots illustrating the updated dropdown and processing message are included in the PR description
- I own the submitted code and licensed it under MIT; CHANGELOG updated and features manually tested in a running JabRef build.
