Summary:

Add recording of user search history so recent searches are stored, retrievable, and manageable.

What this change does:

- Records each search query along with metadata (timestamp, user ID/session ID, search scope) when a search is executed.
- Persists search entries in the database (new SearchHistory table/model) with an index on user and timestamp for fast lookup.
- Exposes endpoints to fetch recent searches and to clear/delete individual or all history entries.
- Adds frontend UI components: a dropdown/list of recent searches on the search input, with options to re-run or remove entries and a button to clear all.
- Adds configuration for history retention and an opt-out user preference.
- Includes unit and integration tests for backend storage, API endpoints, and frontend behavior.

Why:

- Improves user experience by allowing quick access to prior searches and reducing repeated typing.
- Enables smarter UX features (e.g., autocomplete from history) in future iterations.

Implementation notes:

- Database: new SearchHistory model with columns: id, user_id (nullable for anonymous), session_id, query_text, scope, created_at. Migration included.
- Backend: search execution path now calls a SearchHistoryService to validate and persist entries. New API routes: GET /api/search/history, DELETE /api/search/history/:id, DELETE /api/search/history (clear all).
- Frontend: search input component enhanced to request recent searches on focus, render list, support re-run and delete actions, and respect user preference for history recording.
- Security & privacy: history recording is disabled by default for anonymous sessions and can be disabled by users in settings. Stored queries are treated as user data and follow existing retention/purge policies. Queries are not sent to third parties.

Testing & QA:

- New unit tests for service and model validations.
- Integration tests for API endpoints (authentication, authorization, pagination).
- E2E tests covering UI interactions: saving a search, showing history, re-running a search, deleting entries, and toggling opt-out.
- Manual QA steps included in the PR checklist: create searches, verify persistence, test clear/delete, verify opt-out behavior, and confirm retention policy enforcement.

Migration & rollout:

- Includes a schema migration to add the SearchHistory table.
- Backfill not required.
- Feature can be toggled via config flag for staged rollout.

Notes:

- Follow-up work: autocomplete from history, server-side deduplication, and analytics aggregation for anonymized trends.

Summary:
Adds restoration functionality for the shared database so snapshots/backups can be applied to a shared DB instance in a safe, auditable, and repeatable way.

What this PR does:
- Introduces a new RestoreService that orchestrates validating, preparing, and applying a backup snapshot to the shared database.
- Adds an API endpoint (POST /api/shared-db/restore) and CLI command (shared-db restore) to trigger restores.
- Integrates restore mechanics with existing backup storage to fetch and verify snapshots before applying.
- Ensures restores run inside a transactional workflow with locking to avoid concurrent writes and includes pre- and post-restore checks.
- Adds permission checks and audit logging for all restore operations.
- Adds unit and integration tests to cover success, validation failures, partial-restore rollbacks, and permission enforcement.

Implementation notes:
- Restore operations validate snapshot integrity and schema compatibility before making changes.
- The restore flow supports a dry-run mode and an optional force flag to bypass non-critical validations.
- Extensive logging and progress reporting are included to help debug long-running restores.

Migration / configuration:
- No destructive schema changes planned; ensure backup storage credentials/config are available in the environment.
- New config values: SHARED_DB_RESTORE_ENABLED (feature toggle), BACKUP_STORAGE_* (already in config, verify access).

Testing & validation:
- Run unit tests: ./gradlew test (or equivalent).
- Run integration tests for restore paths; exercise the API endpoint or CLI against a staging snapshot.
- Recommended to perform a test restore to a staging instance before enabling in production.

Backward compatibility & rollout:
- Feature is behind a toggle; default is disabled to avoid accidental restores.
- Non-breaking to existing backup usage; enables controlled restoration for shared DB.

Notes:
- Please review the permission model and audit entries; I added tests but a security review is recommended before enabling in production.
- Example API payload and CLI usage are documented in the updated README.

text:
Re-add FormatChars support and restore backward-compatible formatter name mapping

Summary
- Restore support for legacy formatter names (including the old "FormatChars") by replacing the previous reflection-based formatter lookup with an explicit name -> formatter mapping.
- Make a few related cleanups and small refactorings in LayoutEntry construction and formatter parsing.

What I changed
- LayoutEntry
  - Replaced the dynamic reflection-based factory with getLayoutFormatterByName(name) that returns the appropriate LayoutFormatter instance for known names. This adds explicit mappings for many formatter names and several backward-compatible aliases (e.g. "FormatChars" -> LatexToUnicodeFormatter, "HTMLToLatexFormatter" and "HtmlToLatex", "UnicodeToLatexFormatter" and "UnicodeToLatex").
  - getOptionalLayout is now an instance method that uses the LayoutEntry instance (and repository) directly rather than a static method that required passing the repository.
  - Fixed some local-variable initialization and scoping (blockEntries, LayoutEntry le -> now created inline with groupType), and removed an unnecessary commented marker.
  - Added a number of imports for formatters and pre-formatters used in the new mapping.

- Globals
  - Removed FILETYPE_PREFS_EXT constant (previously "_dir").

- GUIGlobals
  - Removed PE_HEIGHT constant (value 2).

Why this was done
- The repository previously renamed/relocated a number of LayoutFormatter classes which broke backward compatibility for exporter configurations that used legacy formatter names (notably FormatChars). The old approach used reflection and a class-name based lookup. By using a switch-based mapping we can provide aliases and support legacy names while also being more flexible about package/class name changes.

Notes & follow-ups
- This PR is intended as an alternative to #1114 to restore backwards compatibility for renamed layout formatters.
- The change reintroduces compatibility for many legacy formatter names; behavior for recognized names should be unchanged.
- There are a number of legacy "Author*" formatters. According to documentation they are deprecated in favor of the unified "Authors" formatter. Should we remove the deprecated Author* formatters now? (left as a question in the issue.)

TODO (left open in the issue)
- Update CHANGELOG.md describing this change
- Add tests covering the legacy-name mappings
- Add screenshots if any UI changes are introduced (none in this PR)

Summary
Fix the logic that enables and disables the Undo and Redo toolbar buttons and menu items so they accurately reflect the current document’s undo/redo state.

Problem
- Undo/Redo toolbar buttons and the corresponding menu items could become out of sync with the document history (e.g., buttons remained enabled when there was no history or stayed disabled after an undoable action).
- Menu items and toolbar buttons used different update paths, causing inconsistent UI state when switching documents or when the active document’s history changed.

What this change does
- Centralizes the enable/disable logic for Undo and Redo so the toolbar buttons and menu items are updated from the same source of truth.
- Ensures the UI listens to the active document’s history/stack change notifications and updates enablement immediately on: performing undo/redo, new edits, clearing history, switching the active document, opening, and closing documents.
- Only the active document controls the global Undo/Redo UI state; switching documents refreshes the state from the newly active document.
- Preserves existing keyboard shortcut behavior and command routing.

Tests and verification
- Added unit/integration checks (where applicable) to exercise enabling/disabling on history changes and document switches.
- Manually verified scenarios: performing edits, undoing to empty history, redoing after undo, switching between documents with different history states, closing the active document.

Notes
- No public API changes. This is a UX/bugfix only.
- Should reduce confusion and prevent cases where toolbar/menu actions are offered when they would do nothing.

This PR contains a collection of small but important cleanups and enhancements across several modules: 

Key changes
- importer: ImportFileFilter
  - Improved filter description construction using StringJoiner.
  - Implemented equals() and hashCode() for correct comparisons and use in collections.

- importer.fileformat: ImportFormat
  - Added convenient reader helpers (getUTF8Reader, getUTF16Reader, getReader) that accept Path and Charset and return BufferedReader.
  - Added importDatabase(Path, Charset) overload which sets encoding and file on the ParserResult.
  - Implemented robust equals(), hashCode(), toString() and getId() normalization.
  - General API improvements for safer I/O handling (try-with-resources).

- logic/groups: KeywordGroup, ExplicitGroup, SearchGroup
  - Improved parsing/fromString implementations and serialization logic for groups.
  - KeywordGroup: robust handling of regex compilation, add/remove support, case-sensitive and separator-aware removal of keywords, and clearer toString formatting.
  - ExplicitGroup: added legacy entry key handling for backwards compatibility, deepCopy, equals() and stable toString serialization that writes legacy keys in deterministic (sorted) order.
  - SearchGroup: parsing and toString kept consistent; added equals() and contains() delegation to SearchQuery.
  - Several equals()/deepCopy() fixes and better logging on unexpected errors.

- logic/openoffice: CitationEntry, OOBibStyle, OOBibBase
  - CitationEntry: encapsulates citation reference mark data; tracks original page-info and supports detection of page-info changes; implements Comparable, equals(), and hashCode().
  - OOBibStyle: extensive parsing and representation for OpenOffice bibliography styles. Improvements include safe reading of style files, handling of properties/citation settings, utility methods for citation formatting, and use of LayoutFormatterPreferences when parsing layouts.
  - OOBibBase: No functional API changes, but contains many utilities used by OpenOffice integration (reference mark handling, bibliography rebuilding, citation insertion and formatting).

- model/entry: CustomEntryType
  - parse() now returns Optional<CustomEntryType> with robust validation of the serialized format.
  - Added utility getters, asString serialization and consistent capitalization.

Why
- These changes improve robustness, correctness (equals/hashCode), and usability of import and grouping code paths.
- The new reader helpers and import overload make it easier to work with different file encodings and avoid resource leaks.
- Group classes now serialize and deserialize consistently and handle legacy data more gracefully.

No behavioral breaking changes are expected; mostly internal improvements and API additions to simplify future work and testing.

Summary

Fixes a bug in the entry editor where pressing TAB while editing a text field did not correctly switch the editing focus to the next field. After this change, TAB (and Shift+TAB) commit the current edit, move focus to the next/previous editable field, and start editing that field immediately.

Root cause

The editor did not properly commit or stop the current cell editor before changing focus, and it did not initialize the new editor when focus was moved via the Tab key. As a result the UI either kept editing the old field, lost the edit, or failed to place the caret in the newly focused field.

What I changed

- Handle Tab and Shift+Tab key events in the entry editor flow so the current text field is committed/stopped before moving focus.
- Ensure the next/previous field receives focus and that a new text editor is started for that field with the caret placed appropriately.
- Update internal editing state bookkeeping so the active edited field index remains correct after switching.

Tests and verification

- Added tests (and/or manual verification steps) to ensure Tab/Shift+Tab: commit current edit, move focus, and begin editing the target field.
- Manually tested common scenarios: first/last field wrapping, fields with validators, and undo/redo after switching.

Compatibility

No public API changes. Behavior change is limited to the entry editor UI and fixes a regression in user input handling.

text:
This pull request improves the change scanner in JabRef by simplifying the merging process from a 3-way merge to a 2-way merge. The previous 3-way merge compared the last saved file, the current value in JabRef, and the new value in the file, which was complex and potentially error-prone. The 2-way merge now only compares the current value in JabRef with the new value in the file, making the logic simpler and more reliable. This change aims to fix issue #5257, which likely resulted from the complexity of the 3-way merge logic.

However, this simplification might have a minor disadvantage in certain edge cases. For example, if two users modify the same entry in different ways and one user adds a new field, the 2-way merge will not be able to automatically reapply the addition of the new field when the file is updated. Despite this, the overall improvement in reliability and simplicity is expected to outweigh this limitation.

The changes include updates to the `ChangeScanner`, `DatabaseChangeMonitor`, and various `ChangeViewModel` classes to reflect the new 2-way merge logic. Additionally, the `BibDatabase` class and related tests have been updated to ensure consistency and correctness.

Summary

- Store proxy passwords and custom API keys securely in the OS native credential store instead of storing them in clear text in preferences.
- Add java-keyring (com.github.javakeyring:java-keyring:1.0.2) dependency and module export (java.keyring) to access the native credential store.

What changed

- UI
  - Network preferences: replaced session-only info label with a "Persist password between sessions" checkbox so users can opt-in to store proxy password across sessions.

- Preferences & behavior
  - ProxyPreferences gained a persistPassword property and related getters/setters. The Network preferences view binds to that property.
  - JabRefPreferences now reads/writes proxy password from/to the OS keyring when persistPassword is enabled. When disabled, stored credentials are removed from the keyring.
  - When starting JabRef, if proxy auth is enabled and persistPassword is set with a non-empty password in the keyring, JabRef will register the proxy automatically. If no persisted password is available the password dialog will be shown.
  - Custom web fetcher API keys are migrated to and read from the OS keyring. A migration helper moves existing in-pref keys into the keyring (encrypted via existing Password helper).
  - If the keyring is unavailable or access fails, JabRef logs warnings and falls back to defaults (no stored password).

- Migrations
  - Added PreferencesMigrations.moveApiKeysToKeyring to migrate fetcher API keys from preferences into the OS credential store.

- Tests
  - Updated/added unit tests to cover the ProxyPreferences changes and the migration logic (PreferencesMigrationsTest and ProxyTest).
  - Tests mock Keyring to verify keys are written during migration.

- Other
  - Updated CHANGELOG.md to describe the feature and the fix that previously stored clear text passwords.
  - Added localization string for the new persist-password checkbox.
  - Module descriptor updated to require java.keyring.

Notes for reviewers / users

- This is opt-in for proxy passwords: users must check "Persist password between sessions" to save a proxy password in the OS credential store.
- Stored API keys and proxy passwords are encrypted (using the existing Password helper with internal preferences) before being put into the keyring.
- If the OS keyring cannot be accessed or an error occurs, JabRef continues to run but will not be able to persist/retrieve the secure credentials; appropriate warnings are logged.

Fixes / related issues

- Fixes clear-text proxy password storage issue (#8055)
- Implements storing API keys in OS credential store (follow-up to #9652)
- Closes related melting-pot issue: JabRef/jabref-issue-melting-pot#106
- Depends on: #10004

Files touched (high level)
- build.gradle, module-info.java (keyring dependency)
- GUI: NetworkTab.fxml, NetworkTab.java, NetworkTabViewModel.java, JabRefGUI.java
- Preferences & migration: JabRefPreferences.java, ProxyPreferences.java, PreferencesMigrations.java
- Tests: ProxyTest.java, PreferencesMigrationsTest.java
- CHANGELOG.md and localization updates

Manual testing

- Changes have been manually tested in a running JabRef instance (enter proxy config, toggle persistence, check connection, and verify proxy registration).

text:
Add unified "Send" actions and external programs preferences

Summary
- Introduces a new "Send" menu (Tools -> Send) with two actions: "As Email" and "To Kindle".
- Adds corresponding context menu entries in the main table right-click menu.
- Implements email-sending actions that use the mailto: mechanism and optionally open folders for attachments (to support mail clients like Microsoft Outlook that don’t accept attachments via mailto).
- Extends preferences to configure email-related settings (email subject, Kindle email, and the option to automatically open folders of attached files) and wires these to the External Programs preference tab with validation.

Details
- New/changed UI
  - Tools menu: new Send submenu containing "As Email" and "To Kindle" (JabRefFrame#createSendSubMenu).
  - Right-click menu: added Send submenu for entries (RightClickMenu#createSendSubMenu).
  - Preferences: External programs tab (ExternalTab.fxml / ExternalTab.java / ExternalTabViewModel.java) now exposes:
    - Subject for sending references
    - Kindle email address
    - "Automatically open folders of attached files" checkbox
  - Validation added for custom terminal / file browser fields in the External tab.

- New action classes
  - SendAsEMailAction (abstract): common logic to build mailto: URI, collect attachments from selected entries, and call Desktop.mail. Runs inside a BackgroundTask and reports success/failure via the DialogService.
  - SendAsStandardEmailAction: fills the email body with the selected entries serialized as BibTeX (uses BibEntryWriter/BibWriter).
  - SendAsKindleEmailAction: sends attachments to the configured Kindle email; action is only enabled when entries are selected and have linked files.

- Preferences integration
  - ExternalApplicationsPreferences: stores emailSubject, kindleEmail and the auto-open-folder preference.
  - JabRefPreferences: loads/saves these external application preferences and exposes them to the rest of the application.

- Miscellaneous
  - StandardActions enum extended with SEND, SEND_AS_EMAIL and SEND_TO_KINDLE entries.
  - Proper logging and user-friendly notifications for success/failure cases; Outlook limitation (attachments via mailto unsupported) is mitigated by opening the containing folders when configured.

Files touched (high level)
- GUI: JabRefFrame.java, RightClickMenu.java, ExternalTab.fxml, ExternalTab.java, ExternalTabViewModel.java
- Actions: SendAsEMailAction.java, SendAsStandardEmailAction.java, SendAsKindleEmailAction.java
- Preferences & models: ExternalApplicationsPreferences.java, JabRefPreferences.java
- Enums/resources: StandardActions.java, localization strings updated (JabRef_en.properties)

Behavioral notes & testing
- "As Email": opens the system mail client with subject/body populated. The body contains the BibTeX representation of the selected entries.
- "To Kindle": targets the configured Kindle email, opens folders of attached files if the preference is enabled. The menu item is only enabled when selected entries have linked files.
- If Desktop.mail() is not supported or no active database/selection exists, the action will notify the user of the error.
- Test by selecting one or more entries, using Tools -> Send -> As Email and Send -> To Kindle, and verifying the mail client behavior. Also confirm the External Programs preferences persist and validation works.

Why
- Provides an integrated, consistent way to send selected bibliography entries by email and to Kindle from both the Tools menu and the entry context menu, while offering user-configurable preferences and handling common mail client limitations.

text:
Summary

When a bibliographic entry referenced from a file was removed, the code sometimes threw a NullPointerException (complaining about an empty database) caused by an UnknownBibTexEntry path. This PR replaces that behavior by throwing a BibEntryNotFound exception instead, which clearly reports the problematic reference mark.

What changed

- Throw BibEntryNotFound when a reference points to an entry that is no longer present.
- Ensure the exception message contains the problematic reference mark so users/developers can identify the missing entry.

Why

Previously the removal of an entry could produce a confusing NPE. The new behavior is explicit and informative: callers receive a BibEntryNotFound and can present a meaningful error to users or handle the missing reference programmatically.

Related

Fixes #4932

- Added JavaDoc/comments for public methods to make intended behavior clearer.
- Removed some unused code and tightened visibility of internal helpers.

- Pay attention to the thread-handling code paths and owner window resolution.
- Run UI/manual tests that open various dialogs (confirmation, input, file choosers, error dialogs) to ensure behavior is unchanged from the user perspective.

Adds an automated monthly check for external links to prevent and detect broken links in the repository.

What this change does:
- Adds a GitHub Actions workflow (e.g. .github/workflows/check-external-links.yml) that runs once a month and scans the site/docs for external links.
- Uses a link-checking action/tool to crawl configured pages, validate external URLs, and fail or report when broken links are found.
- Creates an actionable report (comment or issue) when broken links are discovered so they can be triaged and fixed.
- Documents the new check in the repository (README/CONTRIBUTING) and provides notes on how to run it manually or adjust schedule.

Why:
- Regular, automated checks help catch and fix broken external links before they affect users and reduce manual maintenance overhead.

Schedule and behavior:
- Runs monthly (configurable cron schedule on the workflow) against the default branch.
- Can be triggered manually (workflow_dispatch) for ad-hoc runs.
- Workflow behavior (fail vs report) is configurable in the workflow file.

Testing:
- Workflow was validated with a dry run and sample link-check on a branch; the reporting mechanism was tested by creating a simulated broken link.

Notes:
- You can adjust the cron schedule, change the link-checking tool, or modify reporting (create issue vs fail CI) via the workflow file.
- If you want different frequency or additional pages to scan, update the workflow inputs or config file accordingly.

Fix importing of custom entry types with duplicate fields

Closes #11127

What I changed
- Avoid throwing an exception when duplicate fields are encountered while building custom entry types. Instead, the builder now logs a warning and marks the entry type as having warnings.
- When parsing custom entry type definitions (MetaDataParser), skip (do not import) any custom entry type that produced warnings (i.e., had duplicate fields). A warning is logged with the offending comment.
- Added a small API change to BibEntryTypeBuilder: hasWarnings() to allow callers to detect problematic builds.
- Updated tests: two tests that previously expected IllegalArgumentException are disabled because the builder no longer throws; duplicates are now logged and the importer ignores the faulty type.
- CHANGELOG entry added describing the bug fix.

Why
- An exception during parsing of custom entry types with duplicate fields prevented opening existing libraries that contained such types. This was introduced by a previous change that did not migrate or tolerate duplicate fields. Skipping problematic custom types and logging a warning allows JabRef to open libraries instead of failing.

Files changed
- src/main/java/org/jabref/model/entry/BibEntryTypeBuilder.java: log duplicate-field occurrences, record warnings instead of throwing, add hasWarnings().
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/util/MetaDataParser.java: skip custom entry types that have warnings and log the original definition.
- src/test/java/org/jabref/model/entry/BibEntryTypeBuilderTest.java: disabled two tests that expected exceptions when duplicates occur (behavior changed to logging).
- CHANGELOG.md: note about the fix.

Testing
- Manually tested opening libraries with custom entry types containing duplicate fields; JabRef no longer throws and opens the library, while logging the problematic custom type. Unit tests adjusted/disabled where appropriate.

Upgrade project to use MADR 4.0.0.

What this PR does

- Bumps MADR to version 4.0.0 (templates, docs generator and any dependency entries updated).

MADR 4.0.0 contains format and tooling improvements that make ADRs easier to write and consume. This aligns our ADRs with the latest MADR conventions and ensures compatibility with the latest tooling.

- Inspect the updated ADR template and a couple of migrated ADRs to confirm metadata and content were preserved correctly.

This PR changes the mouse button that triggers the OpenUrlAction for the linked identifier column in the main table from left-click (PRIMARY) to right-click (SECONDARY). As a result, a right-click on the identifier cell now opens the popup list of identifiers (URL, DOI, etc.) allowing the user to select which identifier to open, rather than immediately attempting to open a link on left-click.

- Previously a primary (left) click executed the OpenUrlAction immediately, preventing the user from selecting between multiple identifiers.
- Switching to secondary (right) click brings up the identifier popup list so the user can choose which link to open.

Changes

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/maintable/columns/LinkedIdentifierColumn.java
  - Replaced MouseButton.PRIMARY with MouseButton.SECONDARY in the onMouseClicked event handler so right-click triggers OpenUrlAction.

Fixes

- fixes #8758
- fixes #8802

Testing / How to verify

1. Start JabRef and open the main table with entries that have multiple identifiers (e.g. DOI and URL).
2. Right-click (secondary click) on the identifier cell of an entry.
3. Confirm that the identifier popup list appears and you can select a DOI, URL, etc., and that the hyperlink action is available.
4. Left-click (primary) no longer immediately opens the link.

Notes

- This is a minimal change (single-line update) to the mouse button check and does not modify the OpenUrlAction behavior itself.
- Screenshot (from issue): the identifier popup list appears as expected.

text:
Summary

Add timestamp checks for .bak backup files used by BackupManager to avoid unnecessary conflict dialogs when the .bib file has been modified by external tooling (git, cloud sync, manual edits). If the .bak file is older than the .bib file, the check now considers timestamps before prompting the user about differences.

Problem

Previously, when a .bak file differed from the .bib file but had an older timestamp, BackupManager still showed a dialog asking how to resolve the difference. This leads to spurious dialogs in normal workflows where the main file was updated outside JabRef (e.g. git merges, cloud sync) and the backup is legitimately older.

What this PR changes

- Adds timestamp comparison logic for .bak files so BackupManager will not show a conflict dialog when the .bak is older than the corresponding .bib file and differences are expected due to external updates.
- Keeps existing behavior for genuine conflicts where timestamps indicate the .bak should be treated as the authoritative version.
- Includes unit tests covering the new timestamp-based behavior.

Why this fixes the issue

By respecting file modification times we avoid false-positive conflict dialogs caused by external modifications. This makes the backup/restore flow less disruptive for users who use version control or cloud sync.

Related

- Follow-up to: #9054
- Fixes: koppor/jabref#597

- [ ] Screenshots added (not applicable)
- [ ] Documentation checked/updated if needed

This change is limited to BackupManager's decision logic and unit tests. No UI changes were introduced beyond the adjusted prompt behavior based on timestamps.

- Adds an ADR and supporting documentation describing the chosen synchronization approach for remote databases: an "Optimistic offline lock" augmented with hashes and client-side dirty flags to support offline-first workflows and external edits.

Files added/changed (high level)

- docs/decisions/0027-synchronization.md: new ADR explaining context, considered options (optimistic offline lock, CRDTs), decision outcome and rationale.

Why

- Capture and standardize the synchronization strategy and implementation guidance for both the modern offline-first JabDrive approach and the existing SQL synchronization approach.
- Provide a reference ADR that records the decision, trade-offs and links to implementation docs so future contributors can follow the design rationale.
- Improve documentation tooling (mermaid + copy button) and local spellchecking for repo-specific terms.

Notes

- The JabDrive how-to documents a pull-merge-push cycle (inspired by CouchDB/RxDB) suitable for an offline-capable server/client setup and describes client metadata, tombstones, checkpoints and conflict handling.
- The SQL how-to documents the established optimistic-offline-lock approach currently used for PostgreSQL/MySQL and references the DB notification/listener implementation.

Closes

- Closes https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/7618

- No code changes beyond docs; tests / runtime verification not applicable here.

text:
This PR introduces first-class support for BibLaTeX language identifiers (langid) throughout the model and UI, plus related unit tests and small integration updates.

Highlights
- Add Langid enum (model):
  - Enumerates language identifiers with human-readable names and their BibLaTeX/langid string values.
  - Provides parsing and lookup helpers (parse, getByLangid) and a getJabRefFormat() helper for writing BibTeX-format strings.
- UI: LanguageEditorViewModel (option editor):
  - New OptionEditor view model to edit the LANGUAGEID field in the entry editor.
  - Implements a StringConverter to convert between user input and Langid, supports both langid strings (e.g. "bulgarian") and human-readable names (e.g. "Basque").
  - Provides the full list of Langid values for selection and a display conversion returning the human-readable name.
- Integration:
  - FieldEditors now creates an OptionEditor backed by LanguageEditorViewModel for fields with FieldProperty.LANGUAGE (so StandardField.LANGUAGEID is edited via the new control).
  - FieldFactory considers LANGUAGEID among non-text fields (getNotTextFields) so it receives correct handling where needed.
  - BibEntry: convenience setter setLangid(Langid) added to store language identifiers on entries.
- Tests:
  - LangidTest: extensive parameterized tests for parsing and lookup (by name and by langid), including invalid inputs.
  - LanguageEditorViewModelTest: verifies getItems(), conversion to/from strings (including human readable names), and handling of null/blank inputs.

Notes
- Conversions: the editor's StringConverter.toString returns the langid string (lower-case identifier) while convertToDisplayText returns the human-readable name shown in UI lists.
- The new code maintains backward compatibility: existing behavior for other fields is unaffected.

This change provides robust, tested support for the biblatex langid field in both the data model and the entry editor UI.

- No breaking changes to existing fetchers or the public fetcher API.
- Basic retry and error handling are implemented; consider adding caching or rate-limit handling if heavy usage is expected.

Batch retrieval for large shared libraries

What changed:
- Added DBMSProcessor.partitionAndGetSharedEntries(List<Integer>) which partitions the list of shared IDs into 500-element batches using com.google.common.collect.Lists.partition and aggregates results by calling getSharedEntries for each batch.
- Replaced the direct call to getSharedEntries(...) with partitionAndGetSharedEntries(...) in DBMSSynchronizer.synchronizeLocalDatabase so inserting many shared entries is done in batches.
- Added the corresponding import and Javadoc for the new method.
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to include a fix for a large shared database library content not being shown (issue #8788).

Why:
- Prevents problems (oversized queries / performance issues) when querying a very large number of shared IDs at once by splitting the work into manageable batches of 500.

Notes:
- Behavior is preserved for ordinary use; only the retrieval is performed in batched calls for large ID lists.

This pull request introduces several enhancements and fixes for the JabRef application, specifically focusing on the OpenOffice integration and citation management. Key changes include:

- **Enhancements:**
  - Added a new option to change the timezone parameter when connecting to a shared database.
  - Updated the URL field formatting to trim leading and trailing whitespace.
  - Added a new cleanup operation that detects and moves arXiv identifiers to the `eprint` field.
  - Added a "Move file to file directory and rename file" option for simultaneously moving and renaming document files.
  - Improved the reliability of the MathSciNet fetcher.
  - Added a new keyboard shortcut to close the entry editor with `Ctrl + E`.
  - Added an option to choose the theme (dark or light) in the preferences dialog.
  - Optimized the code responsible for connecting to an external database, leading to significant performance improvements.
  - Added the ability to execute default actions in dialogs using `Ctrl + Enter`.
  - Grouped and reordered the main menu items for better organization.

- **Bug Fixes:**
  - Fixed an issue where the application crashed due to insufficient inotify instances.
  - Resolved an issue where custom exports could not be selected in the 'Export (selected) entries' dialog.
  - Fixed an issue where the group tree was not updated correctly after an entry was changed.
  - Corrected the sorting of composite author names.
  - Fixed an issue where commands followed by a hyphen did not work.
  - Resolved an issue where the custom file column was sorted incorrectly.
  - Fixed an issue where the context menu on the main table selected the wrong entry.
  - Resolved an issue where the first field in the entry editor was not focused when adding a new entry.
  - Fixed an issue where the menu on Mac OS was not displayed correctly.
  - Improved the parsing of author names with abbreviated infixes.
  - Fixed an issue where the month was not shown in the preview.
  - Resolved an issue where the RIS import would overwrite the article date with the accessed date.
  - Fixed an issue where a null pointer exception was thrown when a referenced entry in an Open/Libre Office document was no longer present in the library.

These changes aim to improve the overall stability, performance, and user experience of JabRef, particularly in its OpenOffice integration and citation management features.

Summary:
Add functionality to the main table to show a popup list of available identifiers for a record (URL, DOI, ISBN, etc.) and allow the user to select one and open it directly from the popup.

What this change does:
- Displays an identifier popup when the identifier cell (or an indicator) in the maintable is clicked or focused.
- Lists all available identifiers for the selected entry (URL, DOI, ISBN, handle, etc.), showing a readable label for each item.
- Lets the user click an identifier to open it in a new tab/window using the appropriate scheme (http(s) for URLs, DOI resolver, etc.).
- Supports keyboard navigation inside the popup and ESC to close.

User-facing behavior:
- Clicking the identifier area opens the popup instead of immediately opening a default identifier.
- The popup shows each identifier with a label and optionally an icon or domain to help choose.
- Selecting an identifier opens it in a new tab; the popup closes automatically.
- If only one identifier is present, behavior is unchanged except the popup gives explicit confirmation/choice.

Implementation notes:
- Added a popup component bound to maintable rows; the component receives the record identifiers and renders a selectable list.
- Implemented identifier normalization and resolution logic (e.g. prepend DOI resolver when needed, ensure valid URL schemes).
- Ensured safe target opening (window.open with rel="noopener noreferrer" where appropriate).
- Added keyboard handling (Arrow keys, Enter, Escape) for accessibility.
- Minor UI/UX styles added to position and theme the popup consistently with the maintable.

Files changed (high-level):
- maintable component: hookup to show popup, pass identifiers
- identifier-popup component: new component for rendering list/handling selection
- utils/identifier-helpers: normalization and URL-building for DOI/ISBN/etc.
- styles: CSS for popup positioning and keyboard focus states
- tests: unit tests for identifier resolution and popup open/close behavior

Testing:
- Unit tests for identifier normalization and resolver mapping.
- Integration tests to verify popup opens on click, keyboard navigation works, and selected identifier opens expected URL.
- Manual QA: tested records with multiple identifiers, single identifier, and malformed entries.

Compatibility & notes:
- Default opening behavior preserved when underlying identifier list is empty.
- No breaking changes to existing APIs.
- Consider adding telemetry/analytics later to track which identifier types are most used.

This PR improves discoverability and control over which identifier is used when opening record links directly from the maintable.

Summary

Add a small launcher used by the Snap build to ensure python extension modules are importable when the app runs in the confined snap environment.

Problem

When packaged as a snap the application failed to import compiled python extensions because the runtime import paths and environment differ from a normal system install. That caused crashes at startup or when extension-backed features were accessed.

What this change does

- Introduces a launcher script that prepares the environment (adjusts PYTHONPATH and other necessary env vars) and then execs the real application binary/python entrypoint.
- Updates the snap packaging to use the new launcher as the snap command (so the fix only applies inside the snap).

Why this fixes it

The launcher ensures the app sees its bundled site-packages and native extension modules in the snap sandbox, restoring the correct import behavior without changing application code.

Testing / How to verify

1. Build the snap locally (snapcraft). 2. Install the resulting snap and run the app. 3. Confirm that previously failing imports of extension modules now succeed and the related features work.

Compatibility

This change only affects the snap launcher path; it does not alter normal system installs or application code paths.

Notes

Include reviewers familiar with snap packaging if additional adjustments to snapcraft.yaml are required.

Remove field-saving customization and simplify BibTeX serialization

Summary
- Remove legacy field-saving options (field ordering, wrapping, include-empty-fields and related UI) and simplify how BibTeX entries are serialized.
- Only reformat entries that were changed during the current session; unchanged entries are emitted verbatim using their parsed serialization.
- Always write fields in a deterministic order: required fields first, then remaining fields. The user-configurable sorting modes (alphabetic, unsorted, user-defined) were removed.
- Change field formatting: the equal sign ("=") is appended to the field name and alignment/indentation is computed per-entry (based on the longest field name within the entry) instead of using a global alignment across the database or relying on preferences.
- Remove field-wrapping behavior controlled by preferences; LatexFieldFormatter no longer attempts configurable wrapping.
- Update tests and changelog to reflect the new behavior and expectations.

What changed (high level)
- JabRefPreferences: removed constants and default settings for WRITEFIELD_ADDSPACES, WRITEFIELD_SORTSTYLE, WRITEFIELD_USERDEFINEDORDER, WRITEFIELD_WRAPFIELD and INCLUDE_EMPTY_FIELDS. Defaults and persistence for these options are taken out.
- BibEntryWriter: large simplification and cleanup:
  - Always use the same writing strategy (required fields first, then remaining fields).
  - Do not reformat unchanged entries; write parsed serialization if the entry was not modified.
  - Compute indentation per entry via the longest field name, and incorporate " = " into the field display name. The old global max length and user preferences-based spacing/wrapping are removed.
  - Remove user-defined order and other obsolete branches.
- LatexFieldFormatter: removed configurable field wrapping code paths and related preference reads; formatting always uses the parser.format(content, fieldName) behavior.
- FileTab (preferences UI): removed controls related to include-empty-fields, same-column spacing, user-defined field order, wrap-field-line and associated radio controls and handling. store/set methods no longer read or write those preferences.
- Tests: updated expected serialization strings to match new formatting rules and behavior (per-entry indentation, equals placement). Added a new test (addFieldWithLongerLength) that ensures indentation is recalculated when a longer field is added to an entry. Also ensure tests set BIBLATEX_MODE appropriately.
- CHANGELOG: document removal of field-saving options, reformat-on-change behavior, and the new '=' placement and per-entry indentation.

Migration / compatibility notes
- Existing preference keys related to legacy field-saving options are removed. Any persisted values for those keys will be ignored.
- Existing databases will not be reformatted on save unless individual entries have been modified in the session; unchanged entries are preserved as-is.

Summary

This PR significantly improves the performance and memory usage of the journal abbreviation loading and repository logic (partial fix for #2966). Loading/parsing of the built-in journal lists is now much faster (previously ~10s, now almost instantaneous) and much less memory-hungry.

What changed

- Major refactor of JournalAbbreviationRepository
  - Replaced multiple maps and a SortedSet with a single HashSet to store abbreviations (initial capacity ~16k). This reduces memory consumption significantly (roughly 1/10th of the previous footprint for these structures).
  - Replaced lower-case key map lookups with case-insensitive comparisons (equalsIgnoreCase) performed while streaming the HashSet. This avoids repeated string lowercasing and object churn.
  - Simplified API implementations using stream + map/filter and Optional.
  - Removed ordering guarantee (SortedSet) — repository now stores a set of unique abbreviations.

- AbbreviationParser
  - Changed internal storage from LinkedList to HashSet (initial capacity ~5k) and removed explicit duplicate checks because HashSet enforces uniqueness. This reduces parsing time and duplication overhead.
  - Other small cleanups.

- FileUpdateMonitor
  - Removed duplicated getTempFile implementation and moved a synchronized getTempFile() helper to the class top. Return type clarified to java.nio.file.Path.

Tests

- Updated tests relying on deterministic ordering. Two tests were adjusted/removed because the repository no longer preserves a sorted order:
  - ManageJournalAbbreviationsViewModelTest: updated expected file contents order.
  - JournalAbbreviationRepositoryTest: removed tests that depended on sorting behavior and a test that asserted a particular next-abbreviation behavior tied to ordering.

text:
Fix UTF BOM parsing

What/Why:
- Fixes a bug where BibTeX files that start with a UTF BOM caused detection of the encoding header to fail. The code previously checked line.startsWith("%"), which returned false when BOM bytes precede the percent sign. Java returns the BOM characters in the read String, so the percent sign could be at a non-zero index.
- The importer now searches for the first '%' in the trimmed line (skipping any leading BOM chars) and uses the substring from that position. This ensures comment/header lines are recognized even when a BOM is present.

Changes:
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fileformat/BibtexImporter.java
  - Use indexOf('%') and substring(percentPos + 1) to correctly locate the header comment after potential BOM characters.

- src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fileformat/BibtexImporterTest.java
  - Expanded and reworked tests to cover UTF-8 and UTF-16BE files with and without explicit headers. Added parameterized test encodingExplicitlySuppliedCorrectlyDetermined to assert whether encoding is detected as explicitly supplied in metadata.
  - Adjusted existing tests to assert correct parsing of Umlaut characters across these encodings.

- CHANGELOG.md
  - Updated changelog entries (formatting and added a note about the encoding header/BOM fix).

Impact:
- Fixes parsing of .bib files that contain a BOM at the beginning and ensures the encoding header is respected. This resolves issue #9926.

Tests:
- Added/updated unit tests to assert correct character parsing and that encodingExplicitlySupplied is set correctly for files with/without encoding headers for UTF-8 and UTF-16BE.

Summary

This PR upgrades OkHttp from 4.12.0 to 5.0.0 and adjusts the Gradle module mappings to match the renamed artifacts introduced in OkHttp 5.

What changed

- versions/build.gradle.kts: bumped com.squareup.okhttp3:okhttp from 4.12.0 to 5.0.0.
- build-logic/src/main/kotlin/org.jabref.gradle.base.dependency-rules.gradle.kts: updated module names to use okhttp-jvm and okhttp-jvm-sse and map them to the existing module names (okhttp3 and okhttp3.sse).

Why

OkHttp 5 is a major release with renamed artifacts for JVM-specific modules. Bumping to 5.0.0 keeps dependencies up to date, brings new fixes/improvements, and requires updating our dependency-module mappings so Java module info is applied correctly.

Notes and compatibility

- The module mapping change ensures extraJavaModuleInfo continues to recognize the OkHttp artifacts (now okhttp-jvm and okhttp-jvm-sse).
- Verify any code that referenced OkHttp internals if there were breaking API changes between 4.x and 5.x. This PR only updates dependency versions and module mappings; source changes were not necessary in this repository.

Testing steps

1. Clean and build the project: ./gradlew clean build
2. Run unit and integration tests: ./gradlew test
3. Start JabRef and exercise functionality that uses HTTP networking (e.g., fetching metadata, DOI lookups, web-based importers) to ensure no runtime regressions.
4. Verify module information resolution in runtime images if you use Java modules or jlink.

Related

Closes https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/13509

Checklist

- [x] Dependency bumped
- [x] Gradle module mappings updated
- [x] Built and smoke-tested JabRef locally

This PR adds macOS signing, notarization and custom DMG packaging to the CI pipeline, includes mac-specific resources and helper scripts, and applies a jpackage signing workaround.

Key changes:
- GitHub Actions workflow (.github/workflows/deployment.yml):
  - Added OS X signing secrets to env and new macOS-specific steps to import code signing certificates into a keychain, resign the app, build DMG/pkg, notarize with Apple (polling for status), staple notarization, and verify signatures (spctl / codesign).
  - Use joschi/setup-jdk for mac (Java 15 ea) and actions/setup-java for other OSes; updated java-version usage.
  - Added OSX-specific steps guarded by matrix.os checks and separated JDK setup for mac vs linux/windows.
  - Restore gradle cache step retained; renamed/adjusted shell types for later steps (powershell for renaming on Windows).
  - Set deploy job strategy fail-fast: false.

text:
Fix saving on network drive under macOS

Summary:
- Prevents an exception when saving a library located on a network share (e.g. SMB) on macOS by making file-lock acquisition tolerant of the JDK bug that throws an IOException.

What changed:
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/exporter/AtomicFileOutputStream.java: temporaryFileLock is no longer final and is obtained with tryLock() inside a try/catch. If acquiring the lock throws an IOException (workaround for https://bugs.openjdk.org/browse/JDK-8167023) we log a warning and continue without a lock instead of failing.
- CHANGELOG.md: Added an entry describing the fix for saving on network shares under macOS.

Why:
- On some network drives (tested with a Windows SMB share from macOS) FileChannel.lock() can throw an IOException due to a known JDK bug, which made saving fail. Using tryLock() and catching the exception prevents the save operation from erroring out.

Notes and limitations:
- If the lock cannot be acquired we continue without a file lock, so concurrent writes from other JabRef instances are not prevented. This is a pragmatic workaround to restore functionality for network drives.

Fixes #10452.

Adds support for exporting bibliographies to CSL-compatible YAML and fixes blank-line handling in template-based exporters.

What's included

- New YAML exporter:
  - Adds built-in layout templates (src/main/resources/resource/layout/yaml.layout, yaml.begin.layout, yaml.end.layout) to produce CSL YAML output.
  - Registers a new "CSL YAML" TemplateExporter in ExporterFactory.
  - Adds StandardFileType.YAML so YAML is treated as a standard file type.
  - Includes unit tests (YamlExporterTest) covering empty exports and expected YAML output for entries.

- Blank-line behaviour improvements:
  - Introduces BlankLineBehaviour enum to control how blank lines are handled by TemplateExporter (KEEP_BLANKS, DELETE_BLANKS).
  - Fixes the previous deleteBlankLines behavior by wiring the new enum through TemplateExporter constructors and using it during export.
  - Enables DELETE_BLANKS for the RIS exporter so extra blank lines are removed for RIS output.

- New layout formatter:
  - Adds CSLType (LayoutFormatter) and registers it in LayoutEntry to map JabRef entry types to CSL types used in the YAML layout.

- Minor implementation notes:
  - TemplateExporter now splits layout output on newline sequences and writes lines conditionally when DELETE_BLANKS is set (uses OS.NEWLINE).
  - Small code cleanup and Javadoc formatting.

- Documentation / changelog:
  - CHANGELOG.md updated to mention YAML export support and a fix for the RIS exporter adding extra blank lines.

Related issue: #6974

Tests: New unit tests in src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/exporter/YamlExporterTest.java. Manual testing was performed in running JabRef.

text:
Add DOI identifier handling with comprehensive parsing, normalization and tests

This change introduces the org.jabref.model.entry.identifier.DOI class which provides robust handling for Digital Object Identifiers (DOIs) and Short DOIs. Key capabilities:
- Accepts and normalizes a wide range of DOI representations: plain DOI, short DOI, DOI/urn prefixes (doi:, urn:, urn:doi:), and many URL forms (doi.org, dx.doi.org, doi.acm.org, doi.ieeecomputersociety.org, etc.).
- Decodes HTTP/HTTPS DOI URLs (including percent-encoded path segments) to extract the underlying DOI.
- Recognizes shortcut short DOIs like doi.org/abcd and converts them to the internal 10/... form.
- Finds DOIs and short DOIs inside arbitrary text (findInText).
- Provides helpers: parse (returns Optional), isValid, getExternalURI (constructs encoded resolver URI), getURIAsASCIIString, getDefaultField (StandardField.DOI), getNormalized, toString.
- Correctly handles encoding of reserved characters when constructing URIs and logs on unexpected URI encoding errors.
- Implements case-insensitive equality and consistent hashCode using Locale.ENGLISH lowercasing.

Also adds DOITest with extensive parameterized tests and unit tests covering:
- Parsing and normalization of many DOI/short DOI formats, whitespace handling, URL/URN variants, and domain variants.
- Encoding/decoding behavior for reserved characters (% " # space ?).
- findInText scenarios (including edge cases and rejection of non-DOI text).
- Validation and error cases that should throw IllegalArgumentException.
- Equality behavior and isShortDoi checks.

These additions provide a well-tested and flexible DOI representation for use throughout the codebase.

Opening the Library Properties dialog caused the metadata saveActions to be written into the .bib/.sav comment block and triggered a change event, resulting in the UI showing the library as changed (wrong saving status) even when the user made no edits.

- Prevents spurious change events and the creation of the jabref-meta saveActions comment when merely opening or displaying Library Properties.

- Updated tests and fixtures to reflect the new default behavior.
- Updated documentation to mention the new default and how to enable sync explicitly.

- Existing installations that relied on automatic sync will not have specialfields copied to keywords after this change. To restore previous behavior, enable the new configuration flag in your settings.
- No automatic data changes are performed by this PR.

- Unit tests updated to assert no default sync occurs.
- Manual test: create/update records with specialfields and confirm keywords are unchanged unless sync setting is enabled.

- Check that the new configuration flag is clearly named and documented.
- Verify there are no remaining code paths that bypass the setting.
- Confirm tests cover both enabled and disabled states.

- This implements the requested dropdown to change the reference library during AUX import so users can pick which open library should be used as the reference when resolving citation keys.
- The change is backwards-compatible and scoped to the AUX import workflow (no other UI changes).

Add RFC fetcher (RfcFetcher) to retrieve bibliographic entries from the IETF datatracker

- Implement RfcFetcher which builds the correct datatracker URL for a given identifier and returns a BibTeX parser. The fetcher:
  - Adds an "rfc" prefix for numeric RFC identifiers when missing (e.g. "1945" -> "rfc1945").
  - Does not add the "rfc" prefix for draft identifiers (identifiers starting with "draft").
  - Constructs URLs of the form https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/<identifier>/bibtex/ and uses BibtexParser to parse results.
- Provide help page mapping (FETCHER_RFC) and ensure parser uses DummyFileUpdateMonitor.
- Add comprehensive unit tests (RfcFetcherTest) covering:
  - Name retrieval (getName)
  - Successful lookups for drafts and RFCs (with and without RFC prefix)
  - Edge cases for empty, invalid, or non-existing identifiers
  - Validation of parsed BibEntry content for the draft and RFC examples
- Update changelog (Unreleased) to list the RFC/Draft related fix.

This adds support for fetching RFCs and IETF drafts from datatracker.ietf.org and includes tests to ensure correct identifier handling and parsing behavior.

This PR updates the application changelog and implements a large set of improvements and UI features in the main application window (JabRefFrame).

CHANGELOG
- Add many Unreleased entries documenting added, changed, fixed and removed items (highlights: new preference for unwanted characters in BibTeX key generation; ShortScience search support; entry editor tooltips; basic markdown in custom previews; duplicate DOI integrity check; option to download fulltext files while importing; and many performance and UI fixes).

JabRefFrame (main window)
- Add and wire up the primary main window UI class with menus, toolbar and side pane management.
- Toolbar
  - Add new task/progress indicator in the toolbar that binds to the state manager's task progress and shows a PopOver task list when clicked.
  - Integrate main toolbar actions (new/open/save, edit actions, undo/redo, new-entry shortcuts, push-to-application, generate cite keys, cleanup, social links etc.).
- Menus
  - Build full application menu bar (File, Edit, Library, Quality, Lookup, View, Tools, Options, Help) with action factory integration and dynamic menus (e.g. lookup id fetchers and view items).
- Drag and drop
  - Implement drag-and-drop support for opening .bib files with a visual temporary tab indicator.
- Key bindings
  - Add global keyboard event filter for mapped KeyBinding actions (focus table, next/previous library, search, create new entries of common types).
- Background tasks & telemetry
  - Add progress indicator with tooltip state changes and a PopOver to display running background tasks.
  - Show telemetry opt-in prompt (delayed) if the user has not yet been asked; persist answer.
  - On quit: wait for background tasks, show dialog to allow quitting while tasks run.
- Tabs & panels
  - Tab management: addTab/removeTab/updateAllTabTitles, unique path part handling for disambiguating tabs, tooltips with absolute paths, tab close handlers.
  - Bind active database to selected tab; ensure correct focus, selected entries and search query propagation when switching tabs.
  - Autosave and backup integration on opening/closing tabs (start/shutdown) when appropriate.
- File/history management
  - File history menu integration and tearDown logic to store last opened files and last focused tab.
- Import/drag handling
  - Add import inspection dialog for imported entries and logic to open ParserResult in existing or new tabs.
- Utilities & small helpers
  - Helper methods for detecting file/url/doi in selected entries and other UI utility methods.
  - Improved behavior for divider position persistence and side pane visibility.
- Quit/close behavior
  - Confirm-save dialog when quitting/closing modified local libraries; convert and close shared databases properly; shutdown autosave/backup managers; wait for save-finished dialog.

Other
- Add Undo/Redo event listener glue (UndoRedoEventManager) to hook into undo manager events and update UI accordingly.

Overall this PR brings a comprehensive implementation and polishing of the main application frame, menu and toolbar, integrates background task visualization and telemetry prompts, improves drag-and-drop and tab handling, and documents many changes in the changelog.

Fix for #8788 — Show contents of large shared database libraries

What I changed
- Fixed an issue where the content of a large shared database library was not shown (Fixes #8788).
- Added a new method partitionAndGetSharedEntries(List<Integer>) in DBMSProcessor that partitions the list of shared IDs into batches of 500 and queries each batch separately, then aggregates the results.
- Replaced the direct call to getSharedEntries(...) with partitionAndGetSharedEntries(...) in DBMSSynchronizer so large ID lists are handled in chunks.
- Added an import for com.google.common.collect.Lists and updated CHANGELOG.md with a short user-facing note.

Why
- Very large lists of shared IDs could cause the single database query to fail or not return content (e.g., due to DB / SQL limits on IN-lists). Partitioning into smaller batches avoids building oversized queries and ensures entries are fetched reliably.

Files changed
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/shared/DBMSProcessor.java: new partitionAndGetSharedEntries method
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/shared/DBMSSynchronizer.java: use partitionAndGetSharedEntries when inserting entries
- CHANGELOG.md: added entry describing the fix

Notes for reviewers
- The partition size is 500 (chosen as a safe default). This can be tuned if needed.
- Manual testing was performed with large shared libraries to verify entries are now shown correctly.

Fixes: https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/8788

Summary:
Add detection of online links (e.g. http://, https://, ftp://) to FileFieldParser so that file fields containing URLs are recognized and handled appropriately.

What this does:
- Detects when a file field value is an online link instead of a local path.
- Parses and canonicalizes URL values and marks them as remote/online files in the parsed output.
- Preserves existing behavior for local file paths and other non-URL values.

Why:
Some consumers provide file references as URLs. Previously FileFieldParser only recognized local paths, causing remote links to be treated incorrectly. This change enables correct parsing and downstream handling of online file references.

Implementation notes:
- Detection is based on a URL check for common schemes (http, https, ftp). The parser falls back to existing logic for non-URL values.
- No breaking changes to the parser API; behavior for local files remains unchanged.

Tests and docs:
- Adds unit tests covering detection of various URL formats and ensures existing tests for local paths still pass.
- Updates documentation to mention support for online-link detection.

Compatibility and migration:
- Backward compatible. No migration required. Downstream code that needs to differentiate remote vs local files should check the parser output flag/property added for remote links.

Summary:
Adds a small snap launcher to avoid launching a second JabRef instance when invoked from the browser extension / native messaging host. This fixes CLI parsing errors seen when the extension calls JabRef and resolves importing issues in the snap distribution.

What I changed:
- Added snap/local/JabRef-launcher: a shell script that calls the runtime java binary and starts the module org.jabref/org.jabref.JabRefLauncher.
- Updated snap/snapcraft.yaml to add a jabref-launcher part (dump plugin) that installs the script as bin/JabRef and to remove the original bin/JabRef produced by the jabref part during the build.

Why:
The browser extension / native messaging host sometimes invoked the packaged JabRef in a way that caused the main launcher to spawn another instance and to mis-parse CLI options, producing errors and preventing imports. Providing a dedicated launcher that directly invokes the JabRef module inside the snap runtime avoids spawning a second instance and removes those errors.

Related issues:
Fixes #5537
Fixes JabRef/JabRef-Browser-Extension#165

Testing:
- Manually tested running JabRef from the snap and verified the extension import flow no longer produces the CLI parsing errors (as reported in the linked discussion).

Notes:
- No changelog or automated tests were added in this PR. Manual testing was performed as required.

Behavioral notes / testing:
- Fetching an entry by DOI/ISBN/other ID now runs in background; dialogs for client/server errors are shown as before but without blocking the UI.
- If no entry is found, the user is prompted to either add an entry manually or return to the dialog.
- Focus is restored to the ID input after the fetch completes.

- Render the "keywords" field as interactive tags in the entry editor.

- Adds a new tag-based UI for keywords using a TagsField (FXML + controller).
  - New FXML: src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/KeywordsEditor.fxml
  - New editor component: src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/KeywordsEditor.java

- Adapts FieldEditors factory to use the new KeywordsEditor constructor: src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/FieldEditors.java
- Updates CHANGELOG.md to mention the new Keywords field behavior.

Behavior and implementation details:
- Keywords are displayed as tags with a removable icon; clicking the icon removes the tag.
- Tags provide a context menu with Copy, Cut and Delete actions. Copy/Cut copy the tag text to the clipboard and show a small notification; Cut also removes the tag.
- Autocompletion and suggestions are supported via the existing SuggestionProvider; suggestions are converted to Keyword objects and the typed request is included at the top if missing.
- The TagsField is configured with a converter, matcher (case-insensitive startsWith), comparator (alphabetical), and new-item producer.
- The view model binds the tag list bidirectionally to the underlying entry text using the user-configured keyword separator; parsing/serialization is done in KeywordsEditorViewModel.
- KeywordList.serialize(...) is used to turn a List<Keyword> into the keyword field string using the configured delimiter.

Developer notes / compatibility:
- The KeywordsEditor constructor signature changed: it now relies on injection of services (PreferencesService, DialogService, UndoManager, ClipBoardManager, KeyBindingRepository) and takes (Field, SuggestionProvider<?>, FieldCheckers). Call sites that directly instantiate KeywordsEditor should be updated accordingly; the FieldEditors factory has already been updated.
- New classes use ViewLoader and DI (@Inject) to load FXML and obtain services.

Files of interest:
- Added: KeywordsEditor.fxml, KeywordsEditor.java, KeywordsEditorViewModel.java
- Modified: FieldEditors.java, KeywordList.java, CHANGELOG.md

This change improves usability for keyword editing by offering a modern tag-based UI with full autocompletion and convenient per-tag actions.

Summary

Fix NullPointerException in the Medline importer when the Journal ISSN is missing. This prevents the Medline fetcher from crashing on articles where the <ISSN> element is absent and allows the remaining metadata to be imported normally.

What I changed

- Added a null check for journal.getISSN() before calling issn.getContent() in MedlineImporter.addArticleInformation().
  - Previously: putIfValueNotNull(fields, FieldName.ISSN, issn.getContent());
  - Now: if (issn != null) { putIfValueNotNull(...); }

- Added test resources that reproduce the case of a PubMed/Medline article without an ISSN:
  - src/test/resources/.../MedlineImporterTestArticleNoISSN.xml (sample PubMedArticle without ISSN)
  - src/test/resources/.../MedlineImporterTestArticleNoISSN.bib (expected BibTeX output)

Why

Calling getContent() on a null ISSN caused an NPE when importing certain Medline articles. This change makes the importer robust against missing ISSN entries and fixes issue #2110.

Summary
- Resolve issue where BibTeX author fields like {Hans-Joachim Habermann, Frank Leymann} were not parsed correctly by AuthorListParser.
- Add a heuristic to handle the special case of exactly two authors provided as a single comma-separated value so they are converted to the canonical "Last, First AND Last, First" form.

Context / Example
- Input (from ebook.de):
  @book{9783110702125,
    Author = {Hans-Joachim Habermann, Frank Leymann},
    ...
  }
- Before: parser failed to split and normalize this into two "Last, First" authors.
- After: converted to: {Habermann, Hans-Joachim AND Leymann, Frank}

What I changed
- Implemented a new heuristic in AuthorListParser#parse that detects the two-author comma case and splits/normalizes authors correctly.
- Added unit tests covering this case and several related edge cases to ensure correct behavior.
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to describe the fix for end users.

- Manual testing in a running JabRef is still pending.

Related
- Fixes/addresses: #8652 (reported conversion from ebook.de)
- Main file changed: src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/AuthorListParser.java
- Tests added under corresponding test package.

I modified the mergeCanditates method to merge the "best" title candidate. This consisted of also adding a helper method to this process, calculateTitleScore. This method scores titles based on a variety of heuristics, such as file path endings, ending with .(chars), and the number of words contained with a title. 

mergeCanditates method effectively merges all candidates, and then overrides the previously merged title with the chosen best title.

This pull request aims to enhance the performance of the journal abbreviation loader, repository, and parser within JabRef. The primary improvements include switching from `LinkedList` to `HashSet` for storing abbreviations, which significantly reduces memory usage and speeds up the lookup process. Additionally, the use of `equalsIgnoreCase` instead of converting strings to lowercase before comparison further optimizes performance. These changes reduce the initial load time from approximately 10 seconds to almost instantaneous. text:
Add support for tooltips on custom dialog buttons and improve linked-file rename/move UX

Summary
- Introduces a new DialogService API to show custom dialogs with tooltips for individual ButtonTypes and implements it in JabRefDialogService.
- Updates LinkedFileViewModel to use this new dialog capability when handling file-name conflicts during rename operations and to provide a clearer, safer rename/move workflow.
- Adds improved conflict resolution behavior (Replace / Keep both / Provide alternative / Cancel) with a suggested non-conflicting filename and appropriate error handling.
- Adds/updates related localization strings.

Details
1) DialogService/JabRefDialogService
- New API: DialogService.showCustomButtonDialogWithTooltipsAndWait(Alert.AlertType, String, String, Map<ButtonType,String>, ButtonType...) — allows attaching tooltips to dialog buttons to provide extra context without cluttering the dialog content.
- JabRefDialogService implements the new API. The implementation creates a dialog, sets the content, attaches the provided ButtonTypes and wires the tooltips to the corresponding buttons using Platform.runLater (ensuring the buttons exist in the scene graph).
- Utility: shortenDialogMessage helper added to JabRefDialogService (keeps long messages within a size limit when needed).

2) LinkedFileViewModel
- Rename flow reworked to better detect conflicts and offer clearer choices to the user when a target filename already exists:
  - Uses LinkedFileHandler.findExistingFile(...) to check for an existing file.
  - If a conflict exists, computes a non-overwriting suggested filename via FileNameUniqueness.getNonOverWritingFileName and shows a confirmation dialog with options: Replace, Keep both (shows tooltip with suggested filename), Provide alternative file name, Cancel.
  - Uses the new DialogService method with tooltips to attach the suggested-file-name tooltip to the Keep both option.
  - Handles actions accordingly: overwrite, keep both (rename to suggested non-conflicting name), ask for alternative, or cancel.
  - Attempts the rename via linkedFileHandler.renameToName(targetFileName, overwriteFile) and shows a localized error dialog if an IOException occurs (e.g. file locked).
- Also small defensive behavior changes: remote links are not renamed/moved, and missing files produce an explicit "File not found" error dialog.

3) Localization
- Added strings used in the new dialogs/options (e.g., "Provide alternative file name", messages shown in the file-exists dialog and rename/move error messages) in JabRef_en.properties.

Why
- It improves the UX when renaming or moving linked files by giving users clearer choices and contextual hints (via tooltips), and prevents accidental overwrites by offering a suggested non-conflicting name.

Files changed
- jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/DialogService.java — new method signature added to interface.
- jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/JabRefDialogService.java — implementation of the new dialog method, plus utility and dialog adjustments.
- jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/LinkedFileViewModel.java — improved rename/move logic and use of the new dialog method.
- jablib/src/main/resources/l10n/JabRef_en.properties — new/updated localization strings for UI texts added.

Backward compatibility
- DialogService gained a new method; all implementations must implement it. This PR provides the corresponding implementation in JabRefDialogService.

User-visible behavior
- When renaming a linked file that conflicts with an existing file, the user now sees a clearer dialog with choices and a tooltip showing the suggested filename for the "Keep both" option. Errors such as locked files or missing files are reported with helpful, localized messages.

Summary

- Fixes issue #7016: Toggle of special fields did not work for entries that were sorted. The problem was caused by the selected-entries list being modified by the sort strategy during iteration, which prevented the toggle from being applied correctly (and previously caused a ConcurrentModificationException).

What I changed

- specialfields/SpecialFieldAction.java: Make a defensive copy of the selected entries (new ArrayList<>(bes)) and iterate over that copy when applying field changes. This prevents sorting or other modifications of the original list from affecting the operation.
- Base.css: Add .icon-button:disabled { -fx-opacity: 0.4; } to fix opacity of disabled icon-buttons (issue #7195).
- CHANGELOG.md: Add entries for the above fixes.

Why

- Iterating and modifying a list that is backed by a sorted or observable collection can change the list order during the loop and lead to unexpected behavior or exceptions. Using a copy isolates the update operation from any reordering performed by the UI or sort strategy.

Notes

- Manual testing of the toggle action on sorted entries was performed and the issue is resolved.
- No automated tests were added in this patch.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/Base.css
- CHANGELOG.md

Summary of changes

This PR introduces support and preferences handling for Special Fields and wires related UI/actions throughout the application, along with several supporting improvements and refactorings.

Key additions
- New SpecialFieldsPreferences class (gui.specialfields) encapsulating the special-fields-related settings and a convenience isKeywordSyncEnabled() helper.
- New view-models and actions for special fields:
  - SpecialFieldViewModel, SpecialFieldValueViewModel: provide UI-friendly representations and actions for special-field values.
  - SpecialFieldAction: command to set/toggle special fields on selected entries, with undo support and localized status messages.
- Preferences API extended to expose special-field preferences in PreferencesService and JabRefPreferences, including storing/loading and UI bindings.
- Table preferences (TableTabViewModel) now respect special-field related toggles (insert/remove special-field columns) and persist settings.
- Menus and right-click context menus now include special-field menu items when special fields are enabled.
- ManageKeywordsViewModel integrates with special-field synchronization: keyword changes trigger SpecialFieldsUtils synchronization when enabled.

Other changes and improvements
- ParserResult: added toOpenTab flag and related helpers to control whether parsed results should be merged into the current tab or open a new one.
- MainTable and MainTable-related classes: improved drag-and-drop handling (including local dragboard handling), keyboard-driven jump-to search, selection behavior, and integration of import/link actions via ImportHandler.
- RightClickMenu: centralizes copy/export/citation options, and wires preview/citation styles into copy submenu.
- JabRefPreferences: added special-fields-related preference keys and methods to store/retrieve SpecialFieldsPreferences; many preference getters/setters and caching logic improved/used by UI.

Behavioral notes
- When special fields are enabled, new columns are available for display in the main table and the appropriate menu entries appear in Edit and entry context menus.
- If "auto-sync special fields to keywords" is enabled, keyword edits performed via Manage Keywords will synchronize special fields automatically.
- Special-field operations are undoable and update the entry editor/main UI consistently.

Files touched (non-exhaustive)
- gui/specialfields: SpecialFieldAction, SpecialFieldViewModel, SpecialFieldValueViewModel, SpecialFieldsPreferences
- gui/preferences: TableTabViewModel
- gui/edit: ManageKeywordsViewModel
- gui/maintable: MainTable, RightClickMenu
- gui: JabRefFrame, ParserResult
- preferences: JabRefPreferences, PreferencesService

text:
Add BibEntryWriter to serialize BibEntry objects and tests to verify formatting and behavior

This change introduces BibEntryWriter, responsible for serializing BibEntry instances to BibTeX/BibLaTeX text. Key behaviors implemented:

- Preserve original serialization for entries that were not modified (no changes and reformat=false).
- Provide writeWithoutPrependedNewlines for cases where prepended newlines should be omitted.
- Serialize entries with the header @Type{key, ...} and a special handling for the cite key field.
- Write fields in the following order: required fields, optional fields (without duplication), then remaining fields in alphabetical order.
- Respect InternalBibtexFields flags when deciding which remaining fields to include: when writing normally only writeable fields are included; when determining display-related lengths, only displayable fields are considered (quick fix for issue #834).
- Compute alignment/indentation based on the longest displayable field name so the " = " column lines up across fields.
- Lowercase field names in output (biblatex-style) and use field-specific formatting via LatexFieldFormatter.
- Skip empty fields (unless they should be included) and throw a descriptive IOException when field formatting fails.

Tests added/updated in BibEntryWriterTest cover:

- Basic serialization and spacing expectations for article entries.
- Serialization including non-displayable but writeable fields (e.g. __markedentry).
- Round-trip parsing and writing, including preserving/stripping of leading/trailing newlines.
- Behavior when entries are modified (must reformat output and lowercase fields).
- Special syntax handling for the month field (#mar#) and alignment updates when a longer field (howpublished) is added.
