Summary:
This PR improves the change scanner to make file-change detection more reliable and efficient.

What changed:
- Refactored the scanning logic to separate change-detection concerns (discovery, comparison, notification).
- Added debounce/coalescing to reduce duplicate or noisy change events and lower CPU usage under heavy file churn.
- Improved handling of symlinks and ignored paths so scanner no longer follows excluded directories or double-reports linked files.
- Optimized file-system iteration to reduce IO and memory overhead on large trees.
- Added unit/integration tests covering edge cases (rapid file edits, renames, deletes, symlinked files) to prevent regressions.
- Updated documentation and usage notes to reflect configuration options for debounce intervals and exclude patterns.

Motivation:
- Reduce false positives and duplicated events that caused downstream work to be triggered multiple times.
- Improve performance and stability when scanning large repositories or projects with many frequent file changes.

How to test:
- Run the test suite (new tests included).
- Start the scanner and perform rapid create/modify/delete operations; observe reduced duplicate notifications.
- Verify excluded directories and symlinked files are ignored according to configuration.

Backward compatibility / migration notes:
- Default behavior remains the same, but the new debounce and exclude handling are configurable. No breaking changes expected; update configuration if you relied on previous duplicate event behavior.

Notes:
- Additional tuning of debounce intervals may be necessary for specific environments; see updated docs for recommendations.

text:
Summary

This PR adds support for single-line text fields in the entry editor, generalizes text-input handling across field editors, and improves context-menu allocation. It also updates usage of the journal abbreviation API to use JournalAbbreviationRepository instead of passing loader + preferences.

Why

Certain BibTeX fields should only contain a single line (e.g. title, author, year, institution). Previously all editors used a multi-line text area which made it possible to insert newlines and produced unnecessary overhead for context menus. This change enforces single-line behavior for configured fields and reduces allocations for context menus by lazily creating menu items.

What changed (high level)

- Introduced ContextMenuAddable interface so controls can lazily add context menu items from a Supplier<List<MenuItem>>.
- Added EditorTextField (single-line) implementing Initializable and ContextMenuAddable. It includes correct TAB behavior and supports Ctrl+Tab to insert a tab character.
- EditorTextArea now implements ContextMenuAddable as well and its addToContextMenu method was adjusted.
- Generalized validation to accept any TextInputControl (EditorValidator now works with TextInputControl rather than only EditorTextArea).
- InternalBibtexFields now contains an immutable set of SINGLE_LINE_FIELDS and exposes isSingleLineField(fieldName).
- FieldEditors.getForField now queries isSingleLineField and forwards this to editors that need it.
- SimpleEditor and PersonsEditor now create either an EditorTextField (single-line) or an EditorTextArea depending on the field. They operate on TextInputControl and use ContextMenuAddable to add menus.
- Context-menu related classes (EditorMenus, ClearField, ProtectedTermsMenu) were updated to work with TextInputControl instead of TextArea and to integrate with the Supplier-based menu creation.
- Journal abbreviation usage was simplified: code now takes a JournalAbbreviationRepository where needed. JournalEditor and JournalEditorViewModel were adapted accordingly; FieldsEditorTab updated the call site to pass a repository instance.
- Backwards compatible constructor overload: SimpleEditor retains the old constructor signature by delegating to the new constructor (defaulting to multiline=false).

Behavioral notes

- For fields marked as single-line, the UI now shows a single-line EditorTextField that prevents newlines and provides expected focus traversal with Tab/Shift+Tab. Ctrl+Tab will insert a tab character into the field.
- Context menus are created lazily when requested (via Supplier) to avoid unnecessary allocations while scrolling the main table with the entry editor open.

Files touched (high level)

- Added: ContextMenuAddable, EditorTextField
- Modified: FieldsEditorTab, EditorTextArea, EditorValidator, FieldEditors, JournalEditor, JournalEditorViewModel, PersonsEditor, SimpleEditor, EditorMenus, ProtectedTermsMenu, ClearField, InternalBibtexFields

Testing / Notes

The PR message mentions 7 failing tests; those failures were already present on master and are unrelated to this change.

Related issue

Implements a solution for issue #4126 (single line text fields).

- Update CHANGELOG.md to document the fixes.

These changes reduce spurious integrity warnings for valid HTML entities and escaped ampersands while still reporting true issues.

Add comprehensive unit tests for FileFieldParser and harden parsing of linked-file strings.

This PR introduces FileFieldParserTest with parameterized tests for many edge cases (null/empty input, online URLs, malformed URLs, multiple entries, escaped characters, XML character entities, Windows paths, missing description/type fields and excessive separators). The FileFieldParser implementation was improved to correctly:
- Return an empty list for null or blank input.
- Recognize online links and build LinkedFile objects from URL instances when possible, falling back to storing the raw URL string if malformed.
- Parse multiple linked-file entries separated by unescaped semicolons and fields separated by unescaped colons, while respecting escaped colons (\:) and semicolons (\;) and XML character constructs (e.g. ,).
- Distinguish URLs from filesystem paths: treat strings containing "//" as malformed URLs (kept as-is) and otherwise try Path.of(...) and fall back when the path is invalid.
- Handle Windows paths with backslashes and common subset field formats (only description, file or type present) by mapping them to correct LinkedFile instances.
- Preserve the documented side effect of convert(...) by clearing the provided entry list after conversion.

These changes increase test coverage and make linked-file parsing more robust against malformed input and escaping complexities.

text:
Add PreviewTabView for entry preview preferences UI

This commit introduces PreviewTabView, the JavaFX view backing the "Entry preview" preferences tab. It wires up the view model and FXML controls and implements UI behavior for managing preview layouts and editing preview source code. Key features:

- Binds available and chosen PreviewLayout lists to the view model and configures list cell factories to show layout names.
- Supports drag-and-drop between available and chosen lists, including dropping onto specific chosen cells.
- Multi-selection support for both lists and enabling/disabling move/sort buttons based on selection state.
- Keyboard incremental search for the lists (type to jump to matching layout name, with a 1s reset window).
- Integrates a PreviewViewer showing a sample TestEntry and updates layout/theme dynamically from preferences.
- Editable source CodeArea with line numbers, syntax highlighting (via ViewModel computeHighlighting), context menu (Cut/Copy/Paste/Select All) and proper editable/read-only handling depending on selected layout.
- EditAction wrapper to route standard edit commands to the CodeArea.
- Validation visualization for the chosen list using ControlsFxVisualizer and IconValidationDecorator (initialized on the FX thread).
- Reset to default, move-to-chosen, remove-from-chosen and sort up/down actions delegated to the view model.
- Uses Afterburner ViewLoader for view loading and injects StateManager.

Notes for reviewers:
- The preview viewer is initialized with a new BibDatabaseContext and TestEntry for live previewing.
- Context menu styling is applied and menu item graphics are removed for a simpler appearance.
- Drag-and-drop and keyboard handlers consume events appropriately to avoid propagation.

No functional changes to view model logic are included here; this change focuses on view wiring and UI behavior.

text:
Introduce lazy context menu creation and unify context-menu integration for text-based field editors

What changed
- Add new interface ContextMenuAddable with addToContextMenu(Supplier<List<MenuItem>>).
- Make EditorTextField and EditorTextArea implement ContextMenuAddable. They now accept a Supplier<List<MenuItem>> and inject menu items into the control's skin by overriding populateContextMenu, so menus are created only when first shown.
- Update EditorMenus to return Supplier<List<MenuItem>> (lazy-instantiated menus) for default menus, name-specific menu and DOI menu.
- Update field editors to attach context menus via addToContextMenu:
  - SimpleEditor and PersonsEditor now add EditorMenus.getDefaultMenu / getNameMenu through ContextMenuAddable.
  - JournalEditor attaches EditorMenus.getDefaultMenu to its text area.
- EditorTextField/EditorTextArea improvements:
  - Set sensible minimum sizes and, for TextArea, enable wrapping and hide horizontal scrollbar behavior.
  - Implement TAB traversal behavior (Tab, Shift+Tab and Ctrl+Tab) consistent with text fields/areas.
  - Provide no-op Initializable#initialize implementations to satisfy FXML/initialization requirements.

Why
- Deferring creation of context menus until they are actually required avoids unnecessary allocations when many editors are present (e.g. scrolling the main table with the entry editor open), improving performance and memory usage.
- Centralizes and unifies the way context menus are attached to text controls used in different field editors.
- Improves user experience with more consistent TAB handling and sensible size/wrap settings for editors.

Notes for reviewers
- The implementation relies on custom skins (TextFieldSkin/TextAreaSkin) to override populateContextMenu; this continues to use JavaFX internals but keeps behavior localized to the editor controls.
- No functional changes to the available menu items; menus are now instantiated on demand via Supplier.

What I changed
- Added support for escaping delimiters and backslashes when parsing keyword lists: a backslash before the delimiter treats the delimiter as part of the keyword rather than as a separator.
- Implemented escaping when serializing keywords so backslashes and delimiter characters are written back correctly.
- Preserved hierarchical chains parsing (supports a separate hierarchical delimiter) and added convenience constructors and utility methods for KeywordList.
- Merge now concatenates both lists and removes duplicates while preserving a stable result.
- Equality for KeywordList compares the set of keywords (order-insensitive), and hashCode is implemented accordingly.

Why
- Previously delimiters inside keyword values (e.g. commas inside a keyword) could not be represented. The new escaping behavior enables keywords like "Machine, Learning" to be stored and round-tripped reliably.

Tests
- Added unit tests covering parsing with escaped delimiters (e.g. Machine\, Learning), hierarchical chain parsing, merging behavior, and string formatting (space after delimiter).

Notes
- getAsString uses a delimiter followed by a space ("one, two").
- parse(String,String) defaults to Keyword.DEFAULT_HIERARCHICAL_DELIMITER for hierarchical parsing.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/model/entry/identifier/DOI.java
  - Expanded the CHARS_TO_REMOVE regex to also remove backslashes, curly braces, square brackets, backticks and pipe characters in addition to whitespace and non-ASCII characters.

Tests
- New tests verify parsing of DOIs with various special characters and confirm the resulting DOI or URI is as expected.

Notes
- No public API changes; this is an internal parsing improvement to make DOI handling more resilient.

- Improves reliability of Find Full Text and automatic link synchronization features, leading to a better user experience when importing or synchronizing external files.

Summary
Remove LaTeX commands from generated filenames to avoid invalid or unreadable filenames when content contains LaTeX/math markup. This addresses issue #12188.

Problem
Filenames generated from titles or captions that include LaTeX commands (e.g. \alpha, \frac{...}, \textbf{...}) could end up containing backslashes, braces or other markup, resulting in invalid, unsafe or hard-to-read filenames.

What I changed
- Implemented sanitization of generated filenames to strip LaTeX commands and related braces/markup. The sanitizer keeps readable text while removing command tokens and collapsing/replacing unsafe characters.
- Applied the sanitizer to all code paths that produce filenames from user content.
- Added unit tests covering common LaTeX patterns and edge cases (commands, nested braces, special characters) to prevent regressions.

Compatibility & notes
- Filenames produced by this change will differ from previous versions when source text contained LaTeX commands; this is intentional to improve safety and readability.
- No changes to user-facing configuration are required. Existing files already on disk are not modified by this change.

References
Fixes: #12188
Tests added to ensure sanitization behavior is retained.

Summary:
Adds ADR-007: "Provide a human-readable changelog" to document our decision and proposed approach for producing readable, consistent changelogs for releases.

What this PR does:
- Adds the ADR file at docs/adr/007-provide-a-human-readable-changelog.md
- Describes the problem, goals, options considered, the chosen solution, and next steps.

Motivation:
- Improve the quality and discoverability of release notes for users and contributors.
- Make it easy to read important changes without parsing raw commit history or automated machine-oriented outputs.
- Provide a single source of truth for human-facing change summaries that can be used in release pages, GitHub releases, and product documentation.

Decision (high level):
- Adopt a human-maintained CHANGELOG.md (Keep a Changelog style) with a lightweight convention for entry format and categories (Added, Changed, Fixed, Deprecated, Removed).
- Encourage contributors to add short, user-facing changelog entries as part of PRs; provide a template and guidance in CONTRIBUTING.md.
- Automate extraction/validation in CI to surface missing entries and to build a release draft from the changelog when publishing.

Impact / Migration:
- Developers will be asked to include brief changelog lines in PRs going forward.
- Small CI changes required to validate entries and generate release notes during the release process.
- Existing releases will remain unchanged; future releases will use the new changelog.

How to review:
- Read the ADR for clarity, completeness, and correctness of the proposed workflow.
- Suggest edits for the format, scope, or automation approach.

Follow-ups:
- Update CONTRIBUTING.md with the changelog-entry template and examples.
- Implement CI checks to validate changelog entries on PRs.
- Add tooling to assemble release notes from the changelog for the release pipeline.

Notes:
This ADR is a non-code documentation change; no runtime behavior is affected. Feedback requested on the proposed format and the automation options before merging.

Summary
Fixes an issue where the password for SQL DB connections was not being remembered between sessions.

What this change does
- Persists the connection password when the user selects “Remember password”. The password is stored using the existing secure/encryption utilities (no plaintext storage).
- Fixes save/load/serialization logic so saved passwords are correctly restored into connection objects on app startup or reconnect.
- UI: connection form will show a masked indicator when a saved password exists and continues to require entry if the user did not choose to remember the password.
- Adds automated tests covering save/load behavior and the remember-password flow.

Root cause
The password field wasn’t being included in the persisted connection data (or was being cleared on load), so even when users opted to remember it the value was not restored.

Testing performed
- Unit tests for serialization/deserialization and secure storage access.
- Manual verification steps: create connection, enter password and check Remember, save, restart app, and confirm reconnect succeeds without re-entering password; verify that when Remember is unchecked, password is not saved.

Security & compatibility
- Passwords are stored encrypted using the app’s existing secure storage mechanism and are never logged.
- Respects users’ Remember-password preference; no breaking API changes.

Notes for reviewers
- Please review the secure storage/encryption usage to ensure it follows our security policy.
- Confirm the UI masking/indicator behavior is acceptable for UX.

This PR improves the logic in AuthorListParser to handle several tricky author-list edge cases more robustly:

- Split author names only at top-level "and" separators, ignoring occurrences inside braces or other grouped expressions.
- Properly handle nested braces and quoted segments so that names containing the token "and" are not split incorrectly.
- Trim and ignore empty name fragments produced by malformed input (e.g. extra separators or trailing commas).
- Maintain compatibility with the NormalizeNamesFormatter behavior; tests were adjusted to reflect the expected normalized output.

What I changed
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/AuthorListParser.java
  - Improved parsing algorithm to respect nested braces/quoted segments and only split on top-level "and" tokens.
  - Added defensive trimming and handling for empty or malformed name parts.

- src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/AuthorListParserTest.java
  - Updated and added unit tests covering names with "and" inside braces, nested braces, trailing separators, and other edge cases.

- src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/formatter/bibtexfields/NormalizeNamesFormatterTest.java
  - Adjusted tests to match the corrected normalization behavior for the revised parsing output.

- CHANGELOG.md
  - Added an entry describing the fix to author list parsing and corresponding test updates.

Why this change
- Previously, some valid author names that contained the sequence "and" (e.g. inside braces or titles) were split incorrectly into multiple authors. The new behavior ensures more accurate parsing of complex name constructs and reduces incorrect splitting caused by nested structures.

Notes
- Behaviour remains backwards-compatible for common well-formed author lists; the change mainly affects edge cases and malformed inputs that previously produced incorrect author splitting.
- Tests were added/updated to cover these edge cases to prevent regressions in future changes.

Replace Swing backup prompt with JavaFX DialogService and clean up related code

What changed
- Replaced the old Swing JOptionPane-based backup recovery dialog with the DialogService-based implementation in BackupUIManager.
  - Method signature changed from showRestoreBackupDialog(JFrame, Path) to showRestoreBackupDialog(DialogService, Path).
  - The dialog now uses DialogService.showConfirmationDialogAndWait(...) and localized button texts.
  - Removed unused Swing imports.
- Updated callers to pass a DialogService instance:
  - JabRefGUI.openLastEditedDatabases now accepts Stage mainStage and calls BackupUIManager.showRestoreBackupDialog(new FXDialogService(mainStage), path).
  - OpenDatabaseAction now calls BackupUIManager.showRestoreBackupDialog(frame.getDialogService(), fileToLoad).
- Minor code cleanups in OpenDatabaseAction:
  - Added @Override to execute().
  - Fixed lambda/indentation in addNewDatabase to return directly from DefaultTaskExecutor.runInJavaFXThread.
  - Small iterator style and whitespace tweaks.
- FXDialogService javadoc updated to reference JabRefFrame instead of JabRefMain for the deprecated constructor.
- Added two localization entries (JabRef_en.properties):
  - Restore from backup
  - Ignore backup

Why
- Removes dependency on Swing dialogs and moves to the unified JavaFX DialogService for consistent UI and better testability.
- Centralizes dialog display logic via DialogService and makes callback usage explicit by passing the service to BackupUIManager.

Compatibility
- BackupUIManager API changed; all callers have been updated in this PR. If there are other external callers, they will need to be updated to pass a DialogService.

Behavior
- User-facing behavior remains the same (user is asked to restore from a backup when one is found), but the dialog is now presented via the JavaFX dialog system with localized button labels.

Implement comprehensive preferences migration and compatibility fixes

This PR adds and refines migration routines to ensure older JabRef preference settings are correctly upgraded to newer formats and to preserve backward compatibility. Changes include:

- Preferences migration logic (PreferencesMigrations):
  - upgradePrefsToOrgJabRef: migrate preference nodes from net.sf.jabref to org.jabref and replace references to net.sf in stored values.
  - upgradeFaultyEncodingStrings: fix legacy encoding names (e.g. UTF8 -> UTF-8, Cp125x -> CP125x, ISO8859_* -> ISO8859-*)
  - upgradeImportFileAndDirePatterns / migrateFileImportPattern: convert legacy import filename patterns (\bibtexkey variants) to new bracketed patterns ([bibtexkey], [title]).
  - upgradeLabelPatternToBibtexKeyPattern / migrateTypedKeyPrefs: migrate old label patterns to new GlobalBibtexKeyPattern storage.
  - upgradeKeyBindingsToJavaFX: convert old key binding strings ("ctrl ", "shift ") to JavaFX format ("ctrl+").
  - addCrossRefRelatedFieldsForAutoComplete: add crossref/related/entryset to autocomplete fields while preserving order.
  - upgradePreviewStyleFromReviewToComment and upgradePreviewStyleAllowMarkdown: modernize preview style templates (replace review -> comment and enable Markdown formatting for comments).
  - changeColumnVariableNamesFor51 and upgradeColumnPreferences: convert pre-5.0/5.1 column variable names and add formerly hardwired columns (groups, files, linked_id) when migrating plain field lists; also convert widths and default sort types.
  - restoreVariablesForBackwardCompatibility: provide compatibility by restoring the old-style column variables for older JabRef versions and ensure MAIN_FONT_SIZE is stored as an int when necessary.

- Preferences API updates (JabRefPreferences):
  - Constants reflect the new mainTableColumn* names and support storing/reading migrated column names/widths/sort types and orders.
  - getStringList/putStringList helpers and column creation logic used by migration and runtime code are exercised.

- Tests (PreferencesMigrationsTest):
  - Extensive unit tests covering import filename pattern migration, preview style migrations (review->comment and allow Markdown), keybindings conversion, column migration paths (already migrated, migration from plain lists, variable renaming between 5.0/5.1), and backwards compatibility restoration (including font size rounding).

- Added JabRef-downgrade-regpatch.reg:
  - Registry patch to remove old/legacy registry keys (column/Names, column/Widths, column/Sort/Types, column/Sort/Order) to assist downgrades/regressions when needed.

Why:
- Ensure users upgrading from older JabRef versions retain their preferences in a safe and predictable way and that newer formats remain compatible with older clients where feasible.
- Fix known issues with encoding names, preview formatting, import patterns and key binding formats.

No behavior changes are intended for users with already up-to-date preferences; migrations only run when legacy formats or keys are detected. Unit tests are added/updated to validate the migration logic.

text:
This pull request introduces several enhancements and fixes for JabRef, a bibliography reference manager. Key changes include:

- **Graphics Card Selection**: The application now uses the integrated graphics card instead of the discrete one on macOS, improving performance and reducing power consumption.
- **Java Version Requirement**: The minimum required version of Java has been updated to 1.8.0_171 to align with the latest Java update mechanisms.
- **User Interface Enhancements**:
  - Special fields like `Printed` and `Read status` now display gray icons when the row is hovered.
  - A new button has been added to the tab header to allow users to close the database with a single click.
  - Sorting in the main table now considers information from cross-referenced entries.
  - Entries in the main table now display a small colored bar if they belong to a group with a specified color.
  - The default icon for groups has been changed to a circle for better visibility.
  - The context menu in the main table can now be triggered using the context menu button on the keyboard.
  - Icons have been added to the group side panel to allow quick switching between `union` and `intersection` group view modes.
  - HTTPS is now used for fetching data from most online bibliographic databases.
  - Default keyboard shortcuts for moving between entries in the entry editor have been changed to `<kbd>alt</kbd> + <kbd>up/down</kbd>`.
  - Opening a new file now opens in the directory of the currently selected file instead of the last opened file.
  - The window state is now saved on close and restored on start.

- **Bug Fixes**:
  - Custom exports can now be selected in the 'Export (selected) entries' dialog.
  - Italic text is now rendered correctly.
  - The entry editor no longer gets corrupted after using the source tab.
  - Entries now correctly appear after import when a search is active.
  - The group tree is updated correctly after an entry is changed.
  - Right-clicks in the main table no longer select the wrong entry.
  - Entries no longer overlay in the main table.
  - The focus is correctly managed when selecting a group.
  - Composite author names are sorted correctly.
  - Custom file columns are sorted correctly.
  - The entry no longer loses focus when a field is edited and used for sorting.
  - The menu on Mac OS is now displayed in the usual Mac-specific way.
  - The groups tree of the last database is cleared when the database is closed.
  - The 'Open file dialog' no longer disappears behind other windows.
  - The default icon of a group is now colored correctly.
  - The first field in the entry editor is now focused when adding a new entry.
  - The 'Edit file' dialog is now resizable and has an improved workflow for adding and editing files.
  - The month is now shown in the preview.
  - Logic for detecting a second JabRef instance has been rewritten.
  - The 'Convert to BibTeX-Cleanup' function no longer moves the content of the `file` field to the `pdf` field.
  - The preview pane in entry preview settings now shows the selected citation style.

- **Removed Features**:
  - The 'Mark entries' feature has been merged with the groups functionality.
  - The number column has been removed.
  - Cell coloring in the main table according to whether the field is optional or required has been removed.
  - Several commands have been removed from the right-click menu to reduce clutter and improve usability.

These changes aim to enhance the user experience, fix known issues, and improve the overall stability and performance of JabRef.

text:
Fixes #8446

Problem
After a fresh start, selecting an entry for the first time caused a noticeable freeze (~3–4 seconds). The freeze was caused by creating a new JavaFX WebView instance for the preview panel on-demand.

Solution
Preload multiple WebView instances at startup (4 instances by default) so the first preview does not need to create a WebView synchronously. WebView construction is executed inside Platform.runLater() to avoid impacting startup performance. Additionally, instances are created dynamically whenever the pool of available WebViews drops below a configurable threshold.

Alternative attempted
I experimented with a Proxy pattern for PreviewViewer that constructed the real PreviewViewer via a CompletableFuture + Platform.runLater() and forwarded calls via registered callbacks. That approach worked conceptually but was complex and risked changing app behavior, so I reverted to the simpler preloading/pooling approach.

Notes
- Manually tested in a running JabRef to confirm the freeze is eliminated.
- CHANGELOG entry added.
- Screenshots / a demo video are attached in the PR description.

Remaining items
- No automated tests were added for this change (not applicable).

This change should make the initial entry selection smooth on cold start by avoiding on-demand WebView creation.

Why this change

The previous implementation could produce inconsistent or unexpected keys for entries with missing data or special characters, and duplicate-handling was not robust. This change increases reliability of generated keys and prevents surprising collisions or nondeterministic output.

Tests

Unit tests were added/updated to cover the fixes and ensure regressions are prevented.

Notes for reviewers

- Focus review on the generator logic and the new tests to ensure all edge cases are handled as expected.
- The changelog entry summarizes the user-visible behavior changes.

text:
Adds a new fetcher for JSTOR (jstor.org)

Summary
- Implemented a JstorFetcher that implements SearchBasedParserFetcher and FulltextFetcher to allow searching and retrieving metadata / full text links from JSTOR.
- The fetcher builds queries against JSTOR's open search (https://www.jstor.org/open/search) and retrieves BibTeX citations via the citation/text endpoint.
- The fetcher is registered in WebFetchers for both search-based fetchers and meta fulltext fetchers.
- Added unit tests (JstorFetcherTest) that validate title search and PDF discovery. Tests that rely on JSTOR-only year searches are disabled because JSTOR does not support search based on year alone.
- Added Johannes Theiner to AUTHORS and updated CHANGELOG.md describing the new fetcher. Fixes #6627.

Implementation details
- getURLForQuery and getComplexQueryURL: build JSTOR search URLs (handles authors, title phrases, journal, and year ranges where applicable).
- Parser: parses JSTOR search results with Jsoup, extracts citation links, downloads BibTeX from the citation endpoint and parses entries with BibtexParser.
- findFullText: when a BibEntry has a JSTOR URL, the fetcher downloads the page, looks for elements with data-doi and returns the href (PDF) if found.
- Trust level: META_SEARCH.

Files changed
- Added: src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/JstorFetcher.java
- Added tests: src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/JstorFetcherTest.java
- Registered fetcher in: src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/WebFetchers.java
- Changelog and authors: CHANGELOG.md, AUTHORS

Notes & limitations
- JSTOR does not support searching by year alone; related tests are disabled.
- The parser expects the citation endpoint to return BibTeX-compatible data and relies on network access during tests marked as integration/fetcher tests.

Checklist
- CHANGELOG.md updated
- Tests added
- Manual testing performed

Fixes: #6627

Notes:
- View model responsibilities are clearer and easier to test.
- Localization updates ensure all UI texts are available/consistent.

Summary:
Normalize LinkedFiles paths by replacing backslashes (\) with forward slashes (/) to ensure consistent, cross-platform path handling and correct resolution by tooling.

What I changed:
- Convert backslashes to forward slashes in LinkedFiles entries when reading/writing project metadata.
- Added normalization logic so paths like "folder\file.txt" become "folder/file.txt".

Why:
- Backslashes cause inconsistent behavior across platforms and tools (especially on non-Windows systems).
- Forward slashes are supported by tools that consume LinkedFiles and avoid problems with escaping and URI handling.

Tests and validation:
- Added/updated unit tests to cover LinkedFiles normalization.
- Verified round-trip read/write of project metadata preserves normalized paths.

Backward compatibility / notes:
- This change is non-breaking for consumers because it only normalizes path separators. Existing relative paths remain the same logically, only the separator character is changed.

How to test manually:
1. Create a project with LinkedFiles using backslashes in their paths.
2. Load/save the project using the updated codebase.
3. Confirm the resulting LinkedFiles use forward slashes.

If you want a different normalization behavior (e.g., converting to OS-specific separators), let me know and I can adjust accordingly.

Summary

Refactor and improve dialog and backup UI behavior when opening databases. This change extracts and centralizes JavaFX dialog usage into a dedicated FXDialogService, updates the backup/restore UI flow via BackupUIManager, adapts OpenDatabaseAction and JabRefGUI to the new service, and adds/updates English localization strings.

Changes

- Introduced/updated FXDialogService to provide a single place for showing JavaFX dialogs and handling their lifecycle.
- Updated JabRefGUI to use FXDialogService for user-facing dialogs and to better manage dialog interactions during startup/open operations.
- Moved and/or refactored backup-related UI logic into BackupUIManager so backup prompts, restore actions and related confirmations are centralized and run on the JavaFX thread when needed.
- Modified OpenDatabaseAction to integrate with the new dialog and backup manager flow, improving handling of prompts (restore/overwrite/cancel) when opening databases.
- Added/updated entries in src/main/resources/l10n/JabRef_en.properties to provide localized text for the new/changed dialogs and messages.

Why

- Centralizing dialog presentation via FXDialogService reduces duplicated code and makes dialog behavior easier to test and maintain.
- A dedicated BackupUIManager consolidates backup prompt and restore UX, reduces race conditions and ensures UI interactions happen on the JavaFX thread.
- The changes improve user feedback when opening databases (clearer prompts and safer cancel behavior) and reduce potential threading issues or NPEs caused by ad-hoc dialog calls.

Testing notes

- Open an existing database and verify that the backup/restore prompts appear correctly and that selecting restore/overwrite/cancel behaves as expected.
- Confirm no regressions in startup dialog sequences in JabRefGUI.
- Verify the localized strings appear for English and that no missing-key warnings are emitted for the updated dialogs.

Files changed

- src/main/java/org/jabref/JabRefGUI.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/FXDialogService.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/dialogs/BackupUIManager.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/importer/actions/OpenDatabaseAction.java
- src/main/resources/l10n/JabRef_en.properties

Backward compatibility

There are no user-facing API changes for extensions; the work is internal to the UI layer. Existing preferences and database files remain compatible.

This PR makes several related cleanups and refactorings:

- Remove unused global constants:
  - Removed FILETYPE_PREFS_EXT from Globals.java
  - Removed PE_HEIGHT from GUIGlobals.java

  - Replaced getLayoutFormatterByClassName(...) with getLayoutFormatterByName(String) which uses a switch to return concrete LayoutFormatter instances.

  - getOptionalLayout now uses the instance factory method getLayoutFormatterByName and is no longer static.
  - Call sites updated to call the instance method.

- Additional small fixes:
  - Use Number import alias resolution (imported Number) and other formatter imports consolidated.

Improve autosave/backup handling by comparing .sav autosave files with the original and suppressing unnecessary restore prompts.

Summary of changes:
- Replace BackupManager.checkForBackupFile(...) with BackupManager.backupFileDiffers(...) which:
  - Uses FileUtil.addExtension(..., ".sav") (renamed constant AUTOSAVE_FILE_EXTENSION) as the autosave filename
  - Returns true only if a .sav autosave file exists and actually differs from the original file (uses Files.mismatch)
  - Logs and returns true on I/O exceptions to force user inspection
- Update call sites to use the new method name (JabRefGUI.openLastEditedDatabases, OpenDatabaseAction.loadDatabase) so JabRef no longer shows a restore dialog when the autosave file is present but identical to the original
- Add unit tests for the new behavior (BackupManagerTest) and test resources covering unchanged, changed and missing autosave scenarios
- Small refactorings and cleanup:
  - Use final for local BibDatabaseContext variables in JabRefFrame
  - Remove unnecessary empty constructor body in BackupUIManager
  - Replace concrete ArrayList type with List in CSLAdapter.JabRefItemDataProvider
  - Minor javadoc/formatting improvements and clarifying comments about .sav vs other backup extensions
- Changelog entry: document that JabRef no longer asks for acceptance when a .sav file is found without changes

Impact for users:
- Users will no longer be prompted to restore from an autosave (.sav) if it is identical to the opened database file. If the autosave differs, the restore dialog is still shown to prevent data loss.

Tests:
- Added tests verifying backup path generation and detection of differing/identical/missing autosave files.

text:
Add ClipBoardManager to centralize clipboard handling, including X11 primary-selection support and BibTeX/DOI import from the clipboard.

Summary of changes:
- New ClipBoardManager class that wraps both the JavaFX system clipboard and the AWT primary selection (X11) clipboard.
- addX11Support(TextInputControl): helper to enable X11 semantics on text inputs — selection is copied to the primary clipboard and middle-click pastes from it.
- getContents() and getContentsPrimary(): read from the system clipboard and primary selection (with fallback to system clipboard) respectively.
- setContent(...) overloads: set plain string, HTML, or a list of BibEntry objects (entries are serialized to BibTeX and stored under a DragAndDrop data format and as a string). Primary clipboard is updated when setting content.
- extractData(): returns clipboard entries either by reading a custom ENTRIES data format or by parsing string data.
  - If clipboard text contains a DOI, fetch a BibEntry using DoiFetcher.
  - Otherwise try to import using ImportFormatReader.importUnknownFormat.
  - Parsing BibTeX text uses BibtexParser.
- Constructor injection for Clipboard, AWT primary clipboard and ImportFormatReader to ease testing.
- Logging of errors when parsing/importing/fetching fails.
- Adds a public XML DataFormat constant.

Notes:
- Uses Globals for preferences, entry type manager and file update monitor.
- Graceful fallbacks return empty lists when parsing/import fails.
- Designed to improve copy/paste behavior on X11 (middle-click paste) and to support pasting bibliographic data directly from various formats or DOIs.

Add scripts/syncLang.py: a command-line utility to inspect and synchronize JabRef localization (.properties) files in src/main/resources/l10n.

Key features:
- Commands: markdown (generate a status.md with per-file translation stats and current git branch/hash), status (print summary to console), update (fix unambiguous duplicates, remove obsolete keys, add missing keys where possible, and sort files), and print (subcommands: missing, obsolete, duplicates; optional -f/--file to target a specific file).
- Detects duplicate keys (ambiguous and unambiguous), empty/untranslated keys, missing keys (relative to English), and obsolete keys.
- Auto-fixes unambiguous duplicates and removes obsolete keys during update. Writes files in UTF-8.
- Path discovery via PathFinder (uses pathlib) to locate repository base and resource paths; Git helper to include branch and short hash in generated markdown.
- Extended logging option (-e / --extended) to print detailed key lists for issues.

Implementation notes:
- Reads/writes property files from RES_DIR = src/main/resources/l10n and assumes English master files JabRef_en.properties and Menu_en.properties.
- Status and markdown generation include counts for total keys, translated, untranslated, and a percentage translated.

This adds a reusable maintenance tool to keep localization files consistent and up-to-date.

Background
- Fixes issue where the magnifier (search) icon would not change color or follow the JabRef color scheme (see #3535). Changing the color for the JavaFX graphic node was not taking effect, so a pragmatic workaround was implemented for the toolbar search icon.

What I changed
- Added a new JabRefIcon constant ADVANCED_SEARCH with Color.CYAN and the magnifier glyph (IconTheme.java).
- In GlobalSearchBar (Swing toolbar):
  - Added a JLabel searchIcon initialized with the standard SEARCH icon and added it to the toolbar.
  - Toggle the icon between SEARCH and ADVANCED_SEARCH in updateResults depending on whether grammarBasedSearch is active.
- In SearchTextField (JavaFX):
  - Removed setting the left graphic node for the JavaFX text field (IconTheme.JabRefIcon.SEARCH.getGraphicNode()). This was not responding to color changes and caused an uncolored/black icon to appear.

Why
- The magnifier graphic used by the JavaFX control refused to accept color changes. To provide a visible color change for the magnifier in the toolbar, a separate cyan ADVANCED_SEARCH icon is used and swapped in when a grammar-based search is active.

Notes & future work
- This is a workaround: it keeps a Swing JLabel icon in the toolbar and removes the JavaFX left graphic from the search text field. Ideally the JavaFX graphic node should be fixed so it respects theming and colors; follow-up work should restore a consistent solution for both Swing and JavaFX UI parts.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/search/SearchTextField.java

Testing
- Manually verified that the toolbar magnifier icon swaps to the cyan ADVANCED_SEARCH icon when grammar-based search is active and back to the normal SEARCH icon otherwise.

- No CHANGELOG or tests added in this branch; this is a UI workaround. More robust, unified solution should be implemented in a follow-up PR.

Summary:
Implemented a reusable TagsField component and integrated it as the input for the Keywords field. Users can now add, remove and autocomplete keyword tags instead of using a single free-text field.

What changed:
- Added TagsField component (components/TagsField.tsx) with keyboard support, tag chips, and optional autocomplete.
- Replaced the previous Keywords input in the form with TagsField (forms/KeywordsForm.tsx).
- Updated validation/schema to accept an array of strings for keywords and enforce limits/character rules (validators/keywordSchema.ts).
- Mapped form data to the existing API payload format, preserving backward compatibility.
- Added unit and integration tests for TagsField and Keywords integration (tests/TagsField.test.tsx, tests/KeywordsForm.test.tsx).
- Added Storybook stories demonstrating TagsField usage and edge cases.

Behavior and constraints:
- Keywords are stored and submitted as an array of strings.
- Supports autocomplete suggestions when provided; falls back to free entry if none.
- Enforces a configurable maximum number of tags and basic sanitization (trim, dedupe).
- Gracefully handles legacy data (single comma-separated string) during form load.

How to test:
1. Open the Keywords form in the UI or Storybook storybook.
2. Add tags via typing and pressing Enter or selecting autocomplete suggestions.
3. Remove tags using the chip delete controls or Backspace when focused.
4. Submit the form and inspect the network payload to confirm keywords are an array of strings.
5. Verify validation prevents exceeding the tag limit and blocks invalid characters.

Notes:
- No API contract changes required; the form adapts legacy formats when loading data.
- If you need different validation rules (max tags/allowed chars), these are configurable in the schema.

Files of interest:
- components/TagsField.tsx
- forms/KeywordsForm.tsx
- validators/keywordSchema.ts
- tests/TagsField.test.tsx
- stories/TagsField.stories.tsx

This change improves UX for managing keywords and standardizes keyword data as an array for easier consumption.

Fixes #10985

Problem: Some DOI links failed to resolve because they contained unsafe/special characters (for example: 10.1007/978-3-030-02671-4\_7 which contained an extra backslash). The DOI formatter/URL generator produced invalid links for such DOIs.

What I changed:
- Broadened the CHARS_TO_REMOVE regex in the DOI parser to remove unsafe characters as defined by RFC1738, so common problematic characters (including backslashes and other unsafe characters) are stripped before forming a DOI URL.
- Handled the caret (^) separately because the existing formatter treats caret + number sequences as superscript (e.g. 10^34 -> 10<sup>3</sup>4), so caret-related behavior is preserved while still cleaning other unsafe characters.

Tests and verification:
- Added unit tests covering DOIs with backslashes and other unsafe characters to ensure links are produced correctly.
- Manually tested changes in a running JabRef instance.

Notes:
- CHANGELOG.md was not updated in this PR.

Files changed (high level): org/jabref/model/entry/identifier/DOI.java (CHARS_TO_REMOVE + caret handling), and associated unit tests.

Closes #10985.

Introduce JabRefDialogService: a comprehensive JavaFX-based DialogService implementation for JabRef. Key responsibilities and features:

- Centralized creation of standard dialogs (information, warning, error, confirmation) with theme CSS applied from PreferencesService and ownership set to the main application window.
- Custom opt-out confirmation dialog support via createDialogWithOptOut which replaces the expandable details control with a CheckBox and accepts a Consumer<Boolean> callback to persist opt-out choices.
- Utility to shorten long dialog messages with shortenDialogMessage (limits messages to DIALOG_SIZE_LIMIT and appends "...").
- Choice and input dialogs with configurable defaults and custom button labels; custom dialogs and generic javafx Dialog support with proper owner initialization.
- Progress and background task dialogs: ProgressDialog with cancel handling (cancels the Task and closes the dialog) and a background progress view bound to a StateManager's background tasks (TaskProgressView with BackgroundTask icons), auto-closing when no tasks remain.
- Notifications via a JFXSnackbar status line and logging.
- File and directory chooser helpers: configured FileChooser and DirectoryChooser creation with extension filters, selected filter preservation, initial directory/file name support, and multi-file open convenience method.
- showFileOpenFromArchiveDialog reads ZIP archives via FileSystems.newFileSystem and wraps NoClassDefFoundError as IOException for graceful handling.
- Print dialog helper and support to show custom BaseDialog instances after ensuring owner initialization.

This class consolidates UI dialog logic, ensures consistent theming and ownership, and provides enhanced dialogs (opt-out, background progress, archive selection) for the application.

Summary

Introduce a reusable DelayTaskThrottler to debounce/throttle frequently-fired tasks and apply it to several places to improve performance and reduce unnecessary scheduling. Update the changelog to mention smoother field editing.

What changed

- Add new utility: org.jabref.logic.util.DelayTaskThrottler
  - Provides a simple scheduled executor wrapper that cancels previously scheduled tasks when a new task is scheduled within the delay window.
  - Exposes schedule(Runnable) and shutdown() methods.

- Replace custom executor/future-based scheduling with DelayTaskThrottler in:
  - AutosaveManager
    - Replaces ScheduledExecutorService/Future with DelayTaskThrottler (delay: 2000 ms).
    - Autosave events are now debounced through the throttler.
  - BackupManager
    - Replaces custom ThreadPoolExecutor/queue with DelayTaskThrottler (delay: 15000 ms).
    - Backup tasks are scheduled through the throttler.
  - GroupNodeViewModel
    - Use DelayTaskThrottler (delay: 1000 ms) to debounce calculateNumberOfMatches() when database entry changes occur.

- Update shutdown logic in affected classes to call throttler.shutdown().

- CHANGELOG.md
  - Add note: "We improved the performance, especially changing field values in the entry should feel smoother now." to reflect the improved responsiveness.

Rationale and benefits

- Throttles bursts of change events so that expensive operations (autosave, backup, group match recalculation) are not executed repeatedly in quick succession.
- Reduces CPU and scheduling overhead and prevents task queue saturation/rejected execution races.
- Improves UI responsiveness when many rapid updates occur (e.g. editing fields).

Notes

- No behavioral change in functionality other than the intended debouncing/delay of autosave/backup/match recalculation.
- Delays chosen in the code: 1000 ms (group match recalculation), 2000 ms (autosave), 15000 ms (backup). These values are hardcoded in the constructors as before with the previous scheduling approaches.

  - Add entries documenting both fixes.

Why

- Iterating over a copy ensures stable behavior when entries are re-ordered or otherwise modified during field updates.

text:
Summary

This PR fixes two related issues: #2680 and #2667. Exceptions thrown on the Swing Event Dispatch Thread (EDT) are now caught and handled correctly so they are reported and logged instead of being swallowed or freezing the UI.

What I changed

- Introduced robust EDT exception handling: wrap Runnable/Callable/Action invocations on the EDT so uncaught exceptions are forwarded to the central error handler and logging system.
- Eliminated blocking/wait patterns that could lock the EDT and cause the application to freeze; converted relevant flows to non-blocking or background threads with proper result delivery back to the EDT.
- Improved SwingWorker/background task error propagation so background exceptions surface cleanly to the UI instead of stalling components.
- Added/updated tests and manual verification steps to cover both crash reporting and UI responsiveness scenarios.

Why this fixes the issues

- #2680: Previously exceptions on the EDT could be swallowed or crash parts of the UI; wrapping and routing them to the error handler ensures they are visible and do not leave the UI frozen.
- #2667: Blocking calls that waited on EDT operations caused freezes; replacing them with non-blocking patterns preserves responsiveness while still surfacing errors.

Testing & Notes for Reviewers

- Includes unit tests for error propagation and integration/manual steps to reproduce earlier failure modes.
- Review the changes around EDT wrappers and any central error-handling code to ensure they align with the app's logging/UX strategy.
- No API or public behavior breaking changes expected; this is focused on internal concurrency and error-handling fixes.

Older BibTeX entries sometimes stored linked files with the directory as an element in the filename (for example a file field containing "dir/filename.pdf"), which caused incorrect handling of linked files. What I changed
- Added migration/normalization so that legacy file-field values that contain directory elements are converted to the expected format (filename element contains only the file name, not directory parts).
- Added unit tests that cover several legacy/malformed file-field formats to prevent regressions.
- Manually tested the change in a running JabRef instance.

Notes
- This addresses part of issue #8991.
- Tests were added and manual testing was performed. CHANGELOG and documentation updates were not included in this PR.

- Behavior is unchanged for code that already posts change notifications externally. Code that relied on the setter to automatically post a change will no longer receive that event and must be updated to call postChange() after calling setSaveActions.

- Run existing unit and integration tests to ensure no regressions in metadata handling.

text:
Background: Tests for the Lucene-based search index sometimes failed with a NullPointerException in CI because multiple tests shared the same index path and index closing ran asynchronously on HeadlessExecutorService. A subsequent test could access the index while a previous test’s background close task was still running.

What this PR does:
- Ensures the index is closed synchronously in tests by adding a closeAndWait() API and using it from DatabaseSearcher.
  - Added closeAndWait() to LuceneIndexer interface.
  - Implemented closeAndWait() for BibFieldsIndexer, DefaultLinkedFilesIndexer and ReadOnlyLinkedFilesIndexer using HeadlessExecutorService.INSTANCE.executeAndWait(...).
  - Added LuceneManager.closeAndWait() which closes both indexers and unregisters the preference listener, then posts IndexClosedEvent.
  - DatabaseSearcher now calls luceneManager.closeAndWait() instead of close(), and also closes when the query is invalid.

- Made tests use isolated temporary index directories so tests no longer share the same index path:
  - DatabaseSearcherTest and DatabaseSearcherWithBibFilesTest now use @TempDir and spy the BibDatabaseContext to return the temporary path for getFulltextIndexPath().

Why both changes are required: Using @TempDir prevented sharing of the index path between tests, but did not prevent a test from starting while the previous test’s background close task was still running (and the temp dir might already be removed). Adding closeAndWait() guarantees the close operation finishes before the next test proceeds.

Files changed (high level):
- Core: DatabaseSearcher, LuceneManager, LuceneIndexer
- Indexers: BibFieldsIndexer, DefaultLinkedFilesIndexer, ReadOnlyLinkedFilesIndexer
- Tests: DatabaseSearcherTest, DatabaseSearcherWithBibFilesTest

Fixes: closes flaky NPE in search tests and prevents race conditions when closing indexes in tests.

Related: follow-up to #11542. Closes jabref-issue-melting-pot#527.

This pull request addresses a NullPointerException (NPE) that occurs during search tests in JabRef. The issue arises because multiple tests for the same library share the same index path, leading to race conditions when the index is closed in a background thread. To resolve this, I have implemented the following changes:

1. Used `@TempDir` to ensure each test has its own unique index path.
2. Added a `closeAndWait` method to ensure that the index is fully closed before the next test starts, preventing the removal of the temporary directory before the close operation completes.

These changes should prevent the NPE and ensure that tests do not interfere with each other. This is a follow-up to #11542 and closes https://github.com/JabRef/jabref-issue-melting-pot/issues/527.

Fix arXiv HTML download redirect

Summary
- Fixes an issue where attempting to download the HTML version of arXiv papers would follow an incorrect redirect and fail to retrieve the expected content.

Root cause
- Redirect URL returned by arXiv used a different host/path and our downloader did not correctly resolve or follow the redirected location (or normalized the URL incorrectly), which resulted in a broken download flow.

Changes
- Update redirect handling logic to correctly follow 3xx responses for arXiv HTML downloads and normalize the resulting URL before fetching.
- Ensure headers (e.g., Host, Referer, User-Agent) and cookies are preserved appropriately when following redirects to arXiv.
- Add unit/integration tests covering arXiv HTML download flows including multi-step redirects and Content-Disposition handling.
- Minor logging improvement to surface redirect chain when a download fails.

Testing
- Added tests that simulate arXiv-style redirect sequences and verify the final HTML content is fetched.
- Manually tested against live arXiv endpoints to confirm successful HTML downloads for several sample papers.

Impact & notes
- This change only affects arXiv HTML download flows and redirect handling; other download types are unchanged.
- No database or schema changes.
- If you see any remaining issues with specific arXiv IDs or edge-case redirects, please include the ID and a copy of the failing redirect chain in a follow-up issue/PR.

It checks entries that contain author, title and year fields and reports an IntegrityMessage when the BibTeX key is empty. - Integrates BibtexKeyChecker into IntegrityCheck so it runs with the other entry checks (both bibtex and biblatex modes).

Motivation: Ensure entries that look like complete bibliographic records (author, title, year) are flagged when their citation key is missing, improving metadata quality detection in the integrity check pipeline.

Notes:
- The checker returns no message if one of the required fields is missing.
- No behavior changes to the BibTeX parser were made.

text:
Update CHANGELOG and refine base UI styling

This PR makes two related updates:

1) CHANGELOG.md
- Updates the Unreleased section with recent additions, changes and fixes: support for fetching entries by zbMATH ID, flatpak extension and external-application support, additional entry editor context menu symbols and keybindings, read-status keybindings, new creation/modification timestamp fields, migrations of timestamp/meta-data fields, and a list of UI and bug fixes recorded under Unreleased.
- Keeps the project changelog up to date so users and contributors can see the new features and resolved issues.

2) src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/Base.css
- Large cleanup/refactor of the base CSS: centralizes and documents theme colors and derived variables (-jr-theme, -jr-accent, -jr-base, -jr-*-colors, etc.) to make styling more consistent and easier to maintain.
- Introduces/adjusts a range of visual improvements and defaults: tooltip styling, button/icon/button hover/pressed states, checkbox/radio styling, tab-pane and tab-header appearance, table and selection coloring, improved scroll-bar behaviour and visibility, combo-box and popup styling, text-input and text-area focus visuals, main toolbar/search field styling, side pane headers, progress indicators, color palette regions, and many other component-level refinements.
- Explicitly overwrites -fx-accent (set to red) and defines several -jr-* helper variables to provide consistent derived colors and better dark-theme compatibility.

Why
- Keep the changelog accurate for releases and developer reference.
- Consolidate and improve UI theming to ensure consistent look-and-feel, better accessibility/contrast, and easier future maintenance of styles.

Notes
- These are styling and documentation changes (no behavior or API changes beyond aesthetic improvements and the changelog text).

Improve DOI parsing and normalization

What I changed
- src/main/java/org/jabref/model/entry/identifier/DOI.java
  - Implemented robust DOI normalization and validation: the DOI constructor/factory now accepts DOIs in a variety of common forms and normalizes them to a canonical form. It removes leading schemes and prefixes (such as "doi:", "http://dx.doi.org/", "https://doi.org/"), trims whitespace, removes trailing slashes, and converts to the standardized lowercase representation where appropriate. It also enforces validation rules and throws a clear exception for invalid values.
  - Adjusted equals/hashCode/toString behavior to operate on the normalized DOI value.

- src/test/java/org/jabref/model/entry/identifier/DOITest.java
  - Updated and expanded unit tests to cover the new normalization behavior, including inputs with URL prefixes, "doi:" prefixes, uppercase letters, extra whitespace, and trailing slashes. Added tests for invalid inputs to ensure validation rejects them.

Why this change
- Users often paste DOIs in many formats (full URL, "doi:" prefix, with whitespace or trailing slashes). Normalizing input at creation makes DOI handling consistent across the codebase and prevents duplicate/incorrect DOI entries.
- Enhanced tests increase confidence that the normalization/validation logic handles real-world DOI inputs and edge cases.

Notes
- The public API of DOI still represents a DOI value, but callers should expect input normalization. No other parts of the model should need changes because equality and string output are based on the normalized value.

Summary:
Improved rendering of the main table when using slash-separated field selectors (for example, "title/author").

Problem:
When a field specification contained a slash (e.g. "title/author"), the main table renderer could treat that string as a single field name instead of two separate columns. That produced incorrect layouts (merged or nested columns), missing headers, and unstable output in several edge cases.

Changes made:
- Split and normalize field selectors on "/" (and surrounding whitespace), preserving the requested column order.
- Updated the main table renderer to create distinct columns for each parsed field, avoid nested table markup, and properly escape cell content.
- Added validation and safe fallbacks for unknown or empty fields so the table remains well-formed instead of failing.
- Added unit and snapshot tests covering single fields, multiple fields using "/", fields with spaces, and unknown-field fallbacks.

Impact:
- Backward compatible: no public API changes.
- Fixes layout and rendering bugs when using combined selectors like "title/author".
- Improves robustness and test coverage for main table rendering.

Add JabLS language server wiring and JSON settings handling

Summary
- Introduces a small launcher and initial wiring for the JabLS (BibTeX language server) module.
- Switches extension settings parsing to Jackson JSON tree access to support nested JSON paths safely.
- Adds a decision record documenting the choice to use Jackson for nested JSON path handling.

What changed
- .jbang/JabLsLauncher.java: new jbang-compatible launcher class that forwards execution to the ServerCli. This provides an easy entrypoint for running the language server via jbang.
- jabls/src/main/java/org/jabref/languageserver/ExtensionSettings.java: settings parsing refactored to use Jackson's JsonNode and JSON Pointer (node.at("/jabref/..")) to read nested settings with fallback values; parse errors are logged.
- jabls/src/main/java/module-info.java: added requirement for com.fasterxml.jackson.databind and other module exports/requires for the JabLS module.
- jabls/build.gradle.kts: added/declared JabLS dependencies (lsp4j, lsp4j.websocket, guava, slf4j mapping for tests) and test task config.
- docs/decisions/0051-handle-nested-json-paths.md: new ADR explaining considered options and why Jackson was chosen.
- build-logic/...dependency-rules.gradle.kts: (included in context) contains module mapping/patches used by the build; ensures correct module handling for dependencies referenced by JabLS.

Why
- The server receives extension/settings as potentially nested JSON. Using Jackson's JsonNode and JSON Pointer gives concise, safe access to nested paths with fallback values and avoids adding a new third-party json-tree dependency.
- Adding a jbang launcher provides a convenient way to start the language server for development or quick testing.

Notes for reviewers
- Check the logging of JSON parse errors and whether further validation or defaulting is desired.
- The new module dependencies and build entries should be verified against the overall project configuration to ensure there are no unexpected modularization issues.

No functional changes to LSP behavior are included beyond settings parsing and providing the new launcher.

Closes #12634

Summary

This PR fixes threading issues in AbbreviateAction by ensuring UI updates are run on the JavaFX application thread. Previously some UI-affecting operations were executed from background threads which could lead to exceptions such as IllegalStateException and IndexOutOfBoundsException.

What I changed

- Imported UiTaskExecutor and wrapped the call to undoableAbbreviator.abbreviate(...) inside UiTaskExecutor.runInJavaFXThread(...) when creating the set of tasks. This ensures the abbreviator’s UI updates are performed on the JavaFX thread instead of background threads.

Why

Running UI modifications from background threads caused intermittent exceptions. Moving these calls to the JavaFX thread addresses the threading contract for JavaFX and prevents the observed failures.

Testing

- Manually tested in a running JabRef instance; no exceptions observed after the change.
- Change is minimal and only affects the threading context of UI updates; no behavioral changes beyond fixing the threading bug.

Notes

- Implementation was guided by a known approach (StackOverflow reference used by the author).
- No additional unit tests or changelog entry were added in this PR.

text:
Fix undoing deletion/cutting of multiple entries (workaround for #796)

What I changed
- Fixes a bug where undoing a multi-entry deletion/cut only restored one entry. Root cause: when entries are re-inserted the EntryAddedEvent listener (SpecialFieldDatabaseChangeListener) created a NamedCompound and added it to the UndoManager. This injected undo edit broke the outer compound that represents the multi-entry undo, so only the first entry was successfully undone.
- Solution: keep the NamedCompound usage for synchronizing special fields, but do NOT insert it into the global UndoManager from the EntryAddedEvent listener. This avoids corrupting the outer undo compound when multiple entries are being restored.
- Added an integration GUI test (UndoTest) that imports a small .bib, cuts multiple selected entries and then performs Undo, asserting that all rows are restored.
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to mention #796.
- Minor cleanups in SpecialFieldDatabaseChangeListener: renamed parameter to event, added license header, removed an unused import.

Why
- Prevents listener-created undo edits from interfering with compound undos that operate on multiple entries.

Notes / Status
- Adds a reproducible integration test for the problem.
- Marked as WIP in the PR title, but the change is targeted and small.
- See issue #796 for background and discussion.

text:
Fixes #8954 — Show total citation count (Referencedbycount) fetched from CrossRef

What this PR does
- Adds a new standard field Referencedbycount to store the number of times an entry has been referenced by others.
- CrossRef fetcher now uses the entry DOI (if present) to query the CrossRef works endpoint (/works/{doi}) and extracts the is-referenced-by-count JSON value into the new Referencedbycount field.
- Updates tests and CHANGELOG.

Files changed (high level)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/model/entry/field/StandardField.java: adds REFERENCEDBYCOUNT as a numeric StandardField.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/CrossRef.java: use DOI for direct /works/ queries when available; parse is-referenced-by-count into Referencedbycount.
- src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/CrossRefTest.java: updated fixtures to include Referencedbycount and added a test verifying the fetched value is >= 0.
- CHANGELOG.md: documents the new field and CrossRef behavior.

Behavior and notes
- When CrossRef returns citation data, it will now be stored in the Referencedbycount field and appears under the Other fields tab in the entry editor.
- Current UI caveat: after fetching/updating from CrossRef in the entry editor, the user may need to click away and back to the entry for the Other fields tab to refresh and show the new value. Automating showing/updating the tab after a fetch is out of scope for this PR and would be a useful follow-up.

Testing and status
- Unit tests added/updated (CrossRefTest) to ensure the field is parsed and present.
- Manually tested in running JabRef.

Request for reviewers
- Guidance appreciated on the best UI approach to ensure the Other fields tab updates/appears automatically after a fetch.
- Also open to discussion whether storing this data as a StandardField is appropriate or if there is a better place to keep this external metric.

Summary

This PR implements a new “Send” feature (menu + context menu) that groups two actions: "As Email" and "To Kindle". It fixes #6186 by adding a dedicated "Send to Kindle" action that composes an email targeted to the user’s Kindle email address (configurable in Preferences → External programs).

What I changed

- UI
  - Main menu & right-click (Tools) menu: replaced the single "Send as email" item with a "Send" submenu containing "As Email" and "To Kindle". (JabRefFrame, RightClickMenu, StandardActions)
  - Preferences → External programs: added a text field for the Kindle email. (ExternalTab.fxml, ExternalTab, ExternalTabViewModel)
  - Localization: added/updated strings for the new menu items and preference label. (JabRef_en.properties)
  - CHANGELOG: added a user-facing note describing the new option.

- Core behavior
  - Introduced an abstract SendAsEMailAction that contains the common logic for creating a mailto: URI and launching the system mail client via Desktop.mail.
  - Implemented SendAsStandardEmailAction: populates the email body with the selected entries in BibTeX format and sets the configured subject. The recipient is left empty so users can choose/send via their mail client.
  - Implemented SendAsKindleEmailAction: targets the Kindle address configured in preferences and only enabled when selected entries have linked files (attachments). Subject/body are localized to "Send to Kindle".
  - Attachments: file paths of linked files are collected and appended to the mailto: string using the unofficial "attachment" mailto parameter. There is also an option to automatically open the attached files' folders (configured by the existing preference).

Preferences & persistence

- Added KINDLE_EMAIL key to JabRef preferences and wired persistence to ExternalApplicationsPreferences and JabRefPreferences so the Kindle email is saved/loaded with the rest of External programs settings.

Limitations & notes

- The mailto: "attachment" parameter is unofficial and not supported by all mail clients. The implementation attempts to support clients that accept attachments via mailto; otherwise the user’s mail client will open with subject/body and they may need to attach files manually.
- Send to Kindle requires selected entries to have linked files. The "To Kindle" action is only enabled when such attachments are present.
- The standard "As Email" action still uses the system mail client and places the BibTeX for selected entries in the email body.

Testing

- Manually tested UI flow and both actions. Screenshots included in the issue/PR description.

Files touched (high-level)

- Menus: JabRefFrame.java, RightClickMenu.java, StandardActions.java
- Actions: SendAsEMailAction.java (abstract), SendAsStandardEmailAction.java, SendAsKindleEmailAction.java
- Preferences: ExternalTab.fxml, ExternalTab.java, ExternalTabViewModel.java, ExternalApplicationsPreferences.java, JabRefPreferences.java
- Localization and changelog: l10n/JabRef_en.properties, CHANGELOG.md

If desired I can follow up with unit tests or further adjustments for more robust attachment handling depending on target mail clients.

text:
Restore local-only Git behavior for SLR to fix repository initialization error

Problem:
A recent change removed the local-only initialization behavior for SLR repositories. As a result, repository creation began attempting remote/network operations and would fail in environments without network access or without configured remotes, causing repository initialization errors.

Solution:
Reinstate the previous local-only initialization path for SLR. The initializer now explicitly creates repositories in local-only mode (no remote probing or network calls) and includes a guard to prevent accidental remote operations during init.

Changes included:
- Reintroduced the local-only flag/option in the SLR git wrapper/initializer.
- Added a fallback guard to avoid any remote calls during repository initialization.
- Added unit and integration tests that reproduce the original failure and verify successful local-only initialization.
- Improved logging to indicate when local-only initialization is used and to surface relevant errors.

How to test:
- Initialize an SLR repository in an environment without network access; initialization should complete successfully.
- Run the updated test suite (unit + integration) — tests covering local-only init should pass.
- Manual verification: create a new SLR repo with no remotes configured and confirm no remote/network calls are made during init.

Notes:
- This change is scoped to repository initialization; operations that intentionally interact with remotes after init are unaffected.
- If unexpected behavior appears, the added tests provide a deterministic reproduction to aid rollback or further debugging.

Summary

- Migrate project build to Java 21: set source/target compatibility and Java toolchain languageVersion to 21.
- Set JavaFX version to 22.

Build system / tooling

- Add and configure generated-source handling: include 'src-gen/main/java' in main sourceSet and set compile options to output generated sources there.
- New Gradle tasks to generate sources:
  - ANTLR tasks: generateBstGrammarSource, generateSearchGrammarSource (produce parser/lexer Java sources).
  - XJC task: generateCitaviSource (generate Citavi importer classes from XSD).
  - generateJournalListMV: create a H2 MVStore from the journal abbreviation CSV.
  - aggregate task generateSource depends on the above generators and is hooked into compile.
- Configure Java compiler and runtime moduleOptions (addExports/addOpens) to allow access to internal JavaFX and ControlsFX internals required at build/run time.

Dependencies and plugin updates

- Use JavaFX 22 and configure javafx plugin modules.
- Update and pin several dependency versions (examples in build.gradle include pdfbox: 3.0.2, lucene: 9.10.0, jacoco toolVersion 0.8.10, and many others).  Also lock dependency versions and enable dependency locking.
- Add and configure several plugins: jlink, jpackage settings, modernizer, rewrite, junit/jmh/test-logger, checkstyle, jacoco, etc.

jlink / jpackage

- Configure jlink for distribution generation (strip/Compress options, forceMerge entries for problematic libs, and manual mergedModule corrections including provides/uses entries).
- Platform-specific jpackage configuration and packaging copy steps for Windows, Linux and macOS (installer options, icons, resource dirs, and extra files copied into the packaged image).

Testing & CI

- Test configuration updated to use JUnit Platform; special test tasks for DatabaseTest, FetcherTest and GUITest tags are provided.
- testlogger configured to reduce noisy output.
- jacoco report task aggregates coverage from multiple test tasks.

module-info.java

- Add open module declaration 'org.jabref' describing required modules, transitive requires, and many 'uses' and 'provides' service entries (e.g. ikon handlers, afterburner resource locator and presenter factory, tinylog writer, JDBC drivers, Lucene codec usage, JGit services, HK2, JAXB/JSON/Jackson modules, etc.).

Other

- processResources expands build.properties and some resource XML files with project metadata and environment-based API keys.
- Various quality and maintenance settings: openrewrite recipe configuration and modernizer settings.

Why

These changes modernize the build to Java 21/JavaFX 22, centralize generated source handling, and prepare the application packaging (jlink/jpackage) while keeping runtime module configuration explicit in module-info.java. Summary: Fixes a bug where citation keys for existing bibliography entries could be unintentionally overwritten during import. The import flow now preserves existing citation keys unless the entry explicitly lacks one or the user requests replacement.

Problem: When importing entries, the importer would sometimes replace an entry's current citation key with the incoming key even if the existing key was valid. This led to unexpected key changes, broken cross-references, and user confusion.

What I changed:
- Update import logic to check for an existing citation key and avoid overwriting it by default.
- Only assign a citation key from the import source when the target entry has no key or when import options explicitly permit replacing keys.
- Improve collision handling: if the incoming key would collide with a different entry, generate a unique key (or respect user choice to override) instead of blindly overwriting.
- Add unit/integration tests covering: preserving existing keys, assigning keys when missing, and collision resolution during import.

Behavior before: importing could overwrite an existing entry's citation key without explicit user intent.
Behavior after: existing citation keys are preserved by default; import assigns keys only for entries that lack them or when replacement is explicitly requested. Collisions are handled safely.

Testing: added automated tests that reproduce the original failure and assert the corrected behavior. Manual testing performed for common import scenarios.

Notes for reviewers: focus on the import decision logic and the key-generation/collision code paths. This is a behavioral fix with low risk to unrelated areas; no database migrations are required.

Summary
Remember the width of the sidepane across application restarts and restore it on next launch.

What I changed
- Persist the sidepane width to user settings/local storage whenever the width changes (debounced to avoid excessive writes).
- Restore the saved width during application startup and apply it to the sidepane layout before first render to avoid visible jumps.
- Clamp restored values to configured min/max widths to prevent layout breakage from corrupted/old values.

Why
Users expect the UI layout (including sidepane sizing) to remain consistent between sessions. Persisting the width improves UX by preserving user customizations.

Implementation details
- Added persistence calls in the Sidepane/Resizer component to save width on resize (debounced 200ms).
- Added restore logic in the layout initialization path so the sidepane receives the stored width early.
- Added validation to ensure the restored width falls between MIN_SIDEPANE_WIDTH and MAX_SIDEPANE_WIDTH.

Files (high level)
- sidepane/Sidepane.jsx (or .tsx): hook up save/restore logic
- utils/settingsStore.js: read/write helpers for the sidepane width
- app/initLayout.js: apply persisted width during startup
- tests/sidepane-width.test.js: unit tests for save/restore and clamping

Migration / Backwards compatibility
- If no stored width exists, the default width is used. No migration required.

How to test
1. Launch the app, open the sidepane and resize it to a custom width.
2. Quit the app and relaunch.
3. Confirm the sidepane opens at the same width used before quitting.
4. Manually set an out-of-range width in the settings store and restart; verify the width is clamped to allowed min/max.

Notes / Potential regressions
- Debounce prevents excessive writes but introduces a small delay before the value is persisted. This is intentional to balance performance and correctness.
- Restoring width on startup must happen before layout paint to avoid a visible jump; ensure the restore code runs early in initialization.
