text:
Fix intermittent NullPointerException in search tests caused by a race when closing Lucene indexes.

Problem
- Tests for the same library shared the same index path. The index was closed in a background thread which sometimes ran after a subsequent test started, resulting in an NPE (example CI failure linked in the issue).
- Tests use org.jabref.gui.util.CurrentThreadTaskExecutor to run background tasks sequentially, but index closing used org.jabref.logic.util.HeadlessExecutorService#INSTANCE which allowed the race.

What I changed
- Use @TempDir for the index path so tests get isolated temporary indexes.
- Add a closeAndWait helper that schedules the index close and waits until the close task finishes. This ensures the closing completes before the next test (or before the temp dir is removed).

Why this fixes the issue
- @TempDir alone didn’t fully resolve the flakiness because the temp directory could be deleted before the asynchronous close finished. By waiting for the close task to complete, we eliminate the race between test teardown and the background close execution.

Notes
- Follow-up to #11542.
- Closes https://github.com/JabRef/jabref-issue-melting-pot/issues/527.

This change reduces intermittent test failures (NPE) by making index closing deterministic in tests.

Summary

Re-enable X11 primary-selection clipboard support for TextInputControl while avoiding a JDK bug that caused StringIndexOutOfBoundsException when cutting/deleting text.

What I changed

- Added import javafx.application.Platform.
- Replaced the previous selectedTextProperty listener with an InvalidationListener that runs the selection read on the JavaFX application thread via Platform.runLater:
  - This reads the selection using input.getSelectedText() inside Platform.runLater and copies it to the X11 primary clipboard (primary.setContents(...)) only when non-empty.
- Kept existing middle-click paste behavior (inserting primary selection at caret).

Why

Listening directly to selectedTextProperty can trigger a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException when cutting/deleting text due to a JDK bug (JDK-8176270). Running the selection read inside Platform.runLater and using an InvalidationListener works around that issue while restoring the previously-removed X11 primary-selection support.

References

- Fixes #5708
- JDK bug: https://bugs.openjdk.java.net/browse/JDK-8176270

Notes for reviewers

- This reintroduces X11 primary-selection behavior that had been disabled because of the exception. If there are concerns about X11 compatibility or a cleaner workaround that avoids adding any listener to selectedTextProperty, please advise.
- Manual testing: selection -> cut/copy and middle-click paste scenarios on X11 have been considered; please validate on target platforms.

- Add a mechanism to notify when groups metadata changes in a LibraryTab and react to that in the GroupTreeViewModel so group-tree updates can be propagated across tabs.
- Refactor GroupTreeNodeViewModel into a Java record and update all usages accordingly.
- Update various undo/redo helper classes to use the record accessor API.
- Add a test to ensure MetaDataDiff detects differences when group color is present.

Details
- LibraryTab
  - Introduced an ObjectProperty<MetaData> groupsTreeChanged to publish group tree changes.
  - When a BibDatabaseContextChangedEvent is a GroupUpdatedEvent, groupsTreeChanged is fired (set to null then to the new MetaData to ensure change listeners fire).
  - Exposed groupsTreeChangedProperty() for consumers to observe.

- GroupTreeViewModel
  - Subscribes to the active tab's groupsTreeChanged property and calls onActiveDatabaseChanged when a metadata change is observed, forcing a refresh of the group view.
  - Replaced the old refresh() invocations with initRefreshListener() which initializes the listener/refresh behaviour. (Note: a debug print "Simulate database changed" is present.)

- GroupTreeNodeViewModel
  - Converted class into a record: GroupTreeNodeViewModel(GroupTreeNode node).
  - Updated all methods to use the record accessor or field and modernized code (switch expression, Optional.isPresent(), etc.).
  - Some visibility tweaks (e.g., printInItalics now private).

- Undoable* classes
  - Updated UndoableAddOrRemoveGroup, UndoableModifySubtree, and UndoableMoveGroup to use the new record accessor node() (instead of getNode()).

- Tests
  - Added MetaDataDiffTest.metadataWithColoredGroupsShowsDiff to verify that metadata differences are detected when group color is different/added.

- Misc
  - Small import / formatting adjustments in OptionalObjectProperty and other files.

Notes / TODOs
- There is a System.out.println("Simulate database changed") left in GroupTreeViewModel — likely a leftover debug statement and should be removed.

- LibraryTab currently sets groupsTreeChanged to null then to the new MetaData to force the change notification; this approach works but may be revisited for a cleaner notification pattern.

Fix auto-update of the External File Types table in Preferences by introducing a dedicated row view-model and adapting the tab & edit dialog to work with it. This makes table updates reactive and fixes problems with editing/adding/removing external file types. Fixes #5902.

What I changed

- Introduced ExternalFileTypeItemViewModel that wraps ExternalFileType for use as table rows (icon, name, extension, mimetype, application, conversion helper).

Previously the table used ExternalFileType objects directly and updates (edits/adds/removes) did not reflect reliably in the UI. Wrapping rows in a dedicated view-model with proper JavaFX properties and using ValueTableCellFactory ensures the TableView reacts to changes and renders correctly.

text: This pull request addresses an issue where LaTeX commands, such as \mkbibquote{...}, were not being removed from generated filenames when using the [fulltitle] pattern. The fix involves adding a call to `RemoveLatexCommandsFormatter.format()` before cleaning the filename with `FileNameCleaner.cleanFileName()`. text:
Add CSL YAML export support and related plumbing

This change introduces a new export format for YAML (CSL-compatible) and the supporting infrastructure:

- Implemented a new TemplateExporter registration for "CSL YAML" in ExporterFactory (id: "yaml"). The exporter is configured to remove blank lines (BlankLineBehaviour.DELETE_BLANKS) so generated YAML does not contain empty lines between fields.
- Added BlankLineBehaviour enum to control how TemplateExporter handles blank lines (KEEP_BLANKS / DELETE_BLANKS) and updated TemplateExporter to respect this option when writing entry layouts.
- Added YAML layout resources: yaml.begin.layout, yaml.layout and yaml.end.layout under resource/layout to define the YAML output structure.
- Added a CSLType LayoutFormatter (org.jabref.logic.layout.format.CSLType) to map JabRef entry types to CSL type strings used in the YAML output (e.g. Article -> article, Book -> book, etc.). Registered CSLType in LayoutEntry so it can be used from layouts via \format[CSLType]{...}.
- Extended StandardFileType with a YAML entry and ensured TemplateExporter can be created with a YAML FileType.
- Added unit tests (YamlExporterTest) covering empty-export behavior and verifying the generated YAML content for Article and Misc entries.

Notes:
- The TemplateExporter now supports an explicit blank-line behaviour parameter to better control exporters that require compact output (used by RIS and YAML).
- Existing export mechanism and layout-based exporters are reused; no new heavyweight exporters were introduced.

This implements the feature "support for exporting to YAML" and includes tests to validate the output format.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5037600/28175332-3b59e1da-67f4-11e7-9560-f2a504205c0a.png)
Main boost came from using `equalsIgnoreCase` instead of using `equals(text.toLowerCase())` and changing `LinkedList` to `HashSet` as we don't care about the ordering.

text:
Add DOI identifier class with comprehensive parsing, normalization, URI handling and tests

This PR introduces the org.jabref.model.entry.identifier.DOI class which implements the Identifier interface and provides robust handling of Digital Object Identifiers (DOIs) and Short DOIs. Key behaviors and APIs added:

- Parsing and construction
  - Accepts multiple DOI schemes: plain DOIs, URN (urn:doi:...), DOI prefixes (doi:), and HTTP/HTTPS DOI URLs (doi.org, dx.doi.org, domain variants like doi.acm.org, doi.ieeecomputersociety.org, etc.).
  - Supports Short DOIs (10/xxxx) and DOI shortcuts such as doi.org/abcd (converted internally to 10/abcd).
  - Cleans and normalizes input using URL-decoding, LatexToUnicodeFormatter, removal of whitespace, backslashes, brackets, pipes, non-ASCII characters, and special handling for leading/trailing underscores.
  - Throws IllegalArgumentException for invalid inputs; parse(String) returns Optional<DOI> to safely attempt parsing.

- Validation and detection
  - static isValid(String) to quickly check DOI validity.
  - static findInText(String) to locate DOIs/short DOIs inside arbitrary text using multiple regex patterns.

- URI handling
  - getExternalURI() and getExternalURIWithCustomBase(String) to produce encoded resolver URIs (default https://doi.org/). getExternalURIFromBase(URI) used internally.
  - getURIAsASCIIString() to return ASCII-encoded URI string.
  - Correctly encodes reserved characters per DOI handbook (e.g. % -> %25, space -> %20, etc.).

- Equality and hashing
  - DOIs are case-insensitive: equals() compares case-insensitively and hashCode() uses lowercase (Locale.ENGLISH).

- Tests
  - Comprehensive DOITest covering: valid DOIs and short DOIs, whitespace and non-ASCII cleanup, backslashes/braces/pipes/`/[]/^ removal, URL decoding and encoding behaviour, findInText cases, rejection of invalid or embedded DOIs and unusual URLs, and correct detection of short DOIs via isShortDoi().

Notes
- A TODO comment remains in getExternalURI(): dependency injection should be used to respect user preferences for custom resolvers.

This change adds a robust DOI model suitable for matching, normalizing and creating resolver URIs for bibliographic entries, and is backed by an extensive test suite validating a wide range of edge cases.

  - Accepts multiple DOI schemes: plain DOIs, URN (urn:doi:...), DOI prefixes (doi:), and HTTP/HTTPS DOI URLs (doi.org, dx.doi.org, domain variants like doi.acm.org, doi.ieeecomputersociety.org, etc.).
  - Supports Short DOIs (10/xxxx) and DOI shortcuts such as doi.org/abcd (converted internally to 10/abcd).
  - Cleans and normalizes input using URL-decoding, LatexToUnicodeFormatter, removal of whitespace, backslashes, brackets, pipes, non-ASCII characters, and special handling for leading/trailing underscores.
  - Throws IllegalArgumentException for invalid inputs; parse(String) returns Optional<DOI> to safely attempt parsing.

- Validation and detection
  - static isValid(String) to quickly check DOI validity.
  - static findInText(String) to locate DOIs/short DOIs inside arbitrary text using multiple regex patterns.

- URI handling
  - getExternalURI() and getExternalURIWithCustomBase(String) to produce encoded resolver URIs (default https://doi.org/). getExternalURIFromBase(URI) used internally.
  - getURIAsASCIIString() to return ASCII-encoded URI string.
  - Correctly encodes reserved characters per DOI handbook (e.g. % -> %25, space -> %20, etc.).

text:
Improvements to the ArXiv fetcher and string utilities; new/updated tests

This PR makes several changes to improve arXiv search reliability and parsing, and adds/updates tests to cover those cases:

- ArXiv fetcher (src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/ArXiv.java):
  - Construct title search queries after removing braces around capitalized words to avoid arXiv API mismatches for titles that use braced capitalization (e.g. {Human}).
  - Normalize and correct line breaks for title and abstract text returned by the API.
  - Improve API error handling: when the HTTP response code is 400, parse the error stream to provide a more informative FetcherException.
  - Keep accent-stripping for queries to work around arXiv API issues with accented characters.

- String utilities (src/main/java/org/jabref/model/strings/StringUtil.java):
  - Added/extended methods to remove braces around capitalized words (and related helper patterns) so that titles like "Machine versus {Human} {Attention}..." are handled correctly when building queries.
  - General string normalization utilities used by the fetcher are consolidated/used.

- Tests (src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/ArXivTest.java):
  - Extensive tests added/updated to verify behavior for:
    - Finding full text by DOI, EPRINT (with/without prefix and version), and by title.
    - Handling of titles with acute accents and titles using braced capitalized words.
    - Identifier lookup (old-style ids, http/https/trimmed URLs, malformed ids) and trust level.
    - Phrase, boolean AND and paged searches.

These changes make the arXiv integration more robust for real-world titles (accents, braced capitalization), provide better error messages from the API, and improve test coverage for edge cases.

Why
- This implements issue #7575 by generalizing the previous DOI-only handling (follow-up to PR #9969) so users can paste an ISBN or arXiv identifier (or include them in surrounding text) into Web Search and get an ID-based lookup.

Notes
- Existing DOI behavior is preserved; imports/refactoring cleaned up accordingly.
- Unit tests added to cover the new detection logic.

Fixes
- Fixes #7575

Summary

This PR ensures that the file link is removed from an entry after the linked file has been downloaded. This prevents stale or broken links from remaining in the database after the file has been downloaded and potentially moved or removed.

What I changed

- Remove the reference to the file/link from the entry once the download completes successfully.

Why

- Fixes the behavior reported in #6588 where downloaded files left behind invalid or unwanted links in the entry.
- Keeps the library cleaner and avoids confusion from dead links.

How to test manually

1. Start JabRef and open an entry that contains a file link to a downloadable resource.
2. Trigger the download for that file.
3. After the download finishes, verify that the file link has been removed from the entry.

Fixes

- Fixes #6588

Summary
- Fix false "metadata changed" notifications when saving unchanged libraries by improving equality and hashing in metadata- and cleanup-related classes.

What changed
- Implemented consistent equals/hashCode/toString methods and minor fixes:
  - FieldFormatterCleanup: fixed equals implementation (correct parameter name and logic).
  - FieldFormatterCleanups: added hashCode, equals and toString implementations.
  - ContentSelector: added toString and minor equals formatting change.
  - MetaData: updated hashCode to include additional fields (laTexFileDirectory, contentSelectors, etc.) and added toString.
- Updated CHANGELOG to mention the bug fix.

Why
- The app reported that metadata had changed on save even when nothing relevant changed. By providing correct equals/hashCode logic for metadata- and cleanup-related objects, comparisons no longer report spurious differences and thus avoid triggering the misleading notification.

Related
- Fixes #9159

Summary

This PR implements several keyword editor improvements requested in #10984: improved paste behavior, double-click editing, drag-and-drop reordering, and optional alphabetical ordering when adding keywords.

What changed

- Paste behavior: When pasting text into the keywords editor, if the pasted content can be parsed into keywords it is added immediately (no need to press Enter). Multi-keyword clipboard contents are parsed using KeywordList.parse() with the current keyword separator.
- Double-click on a tag: Double-clicking a keyword removes it from the tag list and enters edit mode with the keyword text in the editor so it can be modified.
- Drag & drop reordering: Tags can be reordered via drag and drop. The implementation uses JavaFX dragboard events and a temporary draggedKeyword to move items within the TagsField.
- Alphabetic ordering: If the current keyword list is already alphabetically ordered (or has been set to sorted by this editor), newly added keywords are inserted into the correct alphabetical position. Otherwise new keywords are appended at the end.

Files changed

- CHANGELOG.md: Added a user-facing changelog entry describing the new keyword editor features.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/KeywordsEditor.java: Implemented the behaviors above (clipboard paste handling keyed to the paste keybinding, double-click to edit, drag/drop handlers, and sorted insertion logic). Added a small internal flag (isSortedTagsField) and draggedKeyword state to manage ordering behavior and DnD.

Implementation notes

- Paste handling uses KeyBindingRepository (instantiated via Injector) to detect the paste key combination and the ClipBoardManager to read clipboard text.
- Pasted text is parsed into a KeywordList and each keyword is added to the TagsField.
- Drag & drop relies on string content in the dragboard and moves the dragged Keyword within the tags list.
- The editor still synchronizes the TagsField tags with the view model via bidirectional binding.

Closes

- Closes #10984

Checks

- CHANGELOG entry added
- Manually tested UI behavior
- Screenshots provided in the original issue/PR description

Fix and harden backup management logic

This PR updates BackupManager and its unit tests to improve reliability and correctness of file backups.

Key changes
- Ensure backup directory is created before attempting to write backups.
- Create backups atomically: write to a temporary file and move it into place to avoid leaving partially written files.
- Use timestamped backup filenames and enforce the configured maximum number of backups by deleting the oldest backups when the limit is exceeded.
- Improve error handling and logging for I/O operations to avoid silent failures.
- Clean up temporary files on failure to prevent leftover artifacts.

Tests
- BackupManagerTest was added/updated to validate:
  - Backup creation works and produces a timestamped copy.
  - The maximum number of backups is respected (oldest backups removed).
  - Behavior when the original file does not exist or I/O errors occur.

Why this change
- Previously backups could be left in a corrupted state if a write was interrupted, and backup rotation was not consistently enforced. These changes make the backup process more robust and predictable, reducing the chance of data loss.

No public API changes are introduced; this is an internal robustness improvement for autosave and backup behavior.

Summary

- Make import/reader behavior more robust when the declared file encoding is incorrect: undecodable characters are now replaced instead of causing decoding failures or being dropped. This is implemented by using a CharsetDecoder with CodingErrorAction.REPLACE when reading BibTeX files.

What changed

- Import/decoding
  - BibtexImporter: use a CharsetDecoder with onMalformedInput(REPLACE) and read files via an InputStreamReader + BufferedReader so unreadable bytes are replaced rather than failing. MetaData encoding is still preserved.
  - Importer.getCharset: adjust charset-detection logic (special-case ASCII detection) and simplify handling for detected charsets.
  - getReader(InputStream) signature no longer declares IOException and uses the detected Charset for InputStreamReader.
  - Note: currently no user-visible warning is issued when replacements happen; this is noted in code and in CHANGELOG.

- Tests and fixtures
  - Added tests for UTF-16 (BE) handling and for the case where a file is encoded in Windows-1252 but declares UTF-8; verifies that unreadable characters are replaced (expected replacement character in parsed result).
  - Added test resource encoding-windows-1252-but-utf-8-declared--decoding-fails.bib.

- Dependencies and packaging
  - Bumped JavaFX to 18.0.1 and updated related openjfx module coordinates.
  - Upgraded many third-party libraries (highlights): Jackson -> 2.13.3, H2 mvstore -> 2.1.214, Apache Tika -> 2.4.1, BouncyCastle -> bcprov-jdk18on 1.71, Lucene -> 9.2.0, JGit -> 6.2.0, Flowless -> 0.6.10, jsoup -> 1.15.1, LibreOffice -> 7.3.4, mariadb -> 2.7.6, postgresql -> 42.4.0, scala-library -> 2.13.8, commons-codec -> 1.15, unirest -> 3.13.10, and others listed in external-libraries.md.
  - Removed direct dependency on com.ibm.icu:icu4j-charset and added a note in external-libraries.md about our fork of ICU (https://github.com/JabRef/icu) and the upstream PR.

- CHANGELOG
  - Added an entry explaining that characters that cannot be decoded with the specified encoding are replaced (and how to find such characters using Integrity Check).

Notes for reviewers

- The decoding change intentionally replaces malformed input rather than failing. This avoids import errors when file encoding declarations are wrong, but it may silently alter data (replacement characters). Currently no UI warning is shown — the change log mentions this and users can use the Integrity Check to find such characters.
- Please pay attention to dependency bumps for native packaging and runtime compatibility (JavaFX module version bump and upgraded native libs).

- Prevent saving an invalid main file directory in Preferences -> File and show an error dialog if the configured path does not exist or is not a directory.
- Show an error dialog when downloading an external file fails due to an invalid/unwritable target directory (instead of failing silently).

Background:
Many users paste file paths into the main file directory field instead of using the file chooser, which could leave an invalid path in preferences. What I changed
- Updated src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fileformat/RisImporter.java (addDoi).
- Added an else branch that validates DOI-like input using a regular expression (adapted from Wikidata P356) and stores it when it matches.

Why
- Previously only values starting with the literal "doi:" were normalized and stored as the DOI field. Plain DOI strings (e.g. 10.1000/xyz123) were ignored. This change ensures valid DOI strings without the prefix are recognized and imported.

Notes
- Regex used: 10\.[0-9]{4,}(?:\.[0-9]+)*/(?:(?!["&'])\S)+ (based on Wikidata P356).
- Manually tested in a running JabRef instance.
- No automated tests or changelog entry included in this PR.

Closes #6530.

text:
Summary

Adds a small utility program that generates a LaTeX table of all characters handled by the converter and fixes a number of incorrect character mappings.

What it does

- Adds a character-generator program that prints, for each entry: the number, the character as Unicode (using \symbol{nnn}), the resulting LaTeX symbol and the LaTeX code used.
- Includes example output (CharGen5.pdf) to verify mappings visually.
- Corrects several character mappings in the converter so the LaTeX output is more accurate.

Notes and caveats

- Using \usepackage[utf8]{inputenc} only worked reliably for accented characters in my tests. Printing raw Unicode characters in the .tex file worked inconsistently depending on LaTeX engine and fonts.
- Display of some symbols depends on chosen LaTeX packages and fonts; additional packages or font changes may allow more symbols to render correctly.
- This work is related to #1761 but does not fully include that issue’s changes.

Testing & Documentation

- Manually tested the changed features in a running JabRef instance.
- Documentation impact noted; an issue was created for the outdated help page at help.jabref.org.

Notes for reviewers

- See attached CharGen5.pdf for example output and to review mappings.
- Consider further improvements by adding fonts/packages to the generated LaTeX or switching to a Unicode-capable engine to improve direct Unicode rendering.

Summary

- Add a friendly PR-hygiene comment and enforce an assignment check when a PR is opened/updated.
- Make the assignment step tolerant for normal issues but strict for issues labeled with a "good*" label.

What changed

1) .github/ghprcomment.yml
- Added a new comment template (jobName: "Ensure that contributor is assigned (fails if not commented on issue)") that will be posted on PRs reminding contributors to assign themselves to the linked issue and pointing them to CONTRIBUTING.md. The message is friendly and explains the expected workflow.

2) .github/workflows/on-pr-opened-updated.yml
- The ensure_assignment job now only runs for PRs coming from a different repository (i.e. external contributors / forks): if: github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name != 'JabRef/jabref'. This avoids interfering with internal branches.
- The job retrieves issue labels and looks for labels starting with "good". If such a label exists, SILENT=false (the assignment update will fail loudly if it cannot add the assignee). If no "good*" label is found, SILENT=true which makes the assignee update tolerant (patch will not cause the job to fail if the GH API call cannot add the assignee).
- The GH API call to update issue assignees is wrapped so that failures are ignored when SILENT=true.

Why

- Problem: a contributor can open a PR immediately after creating it and before the author (or project members) can mark/assign the issue. That allows other contributors to grab the issue in the short window, causing confusion (observed in #13486).
- Solution: post a brief instruction on the PR to remind people to assign themselves and try to automatically add the PR author as assignee. To avoid breaking the workflow for normal issues, the job is silent unless the issue is explicitly marked with a "good*" label (good-first/second/...). For labeled beginner-friendly issues we keep strict behavior so we avoid unassigned beginner issues.

Notes

- This change focuses on PRs from forks (external contributors) to minimize impact on internal workflows.
- The change is intentionally conservative: only issues with a "good*" label will produce a hard failure if the assignment cannot be made.

Related

- Trigger: https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/pull/13500
- Incident example: https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/13486#issuecomment-3053515808

Checklist

- Added comment template and adjusted workflow behavior to reduce assignment races and to encourage contributors to follow CONTRIBUTING.md.

Closes #13559

Summary

- Ensure Libre/OpenOffice citations get a space after the inserted citation by default and make this behaviour configurable.

What I changed

- Added a new preference (ooAddSpaceAfter) to store whether a space should be added after inserted citations (default: true). (JabRefCliPreferences, OpenOfficePreferences)
- Exposed the preference in the Libre/OpenOffice panel as a new "Add space after citation" checkbox in the settings context menu. (OpenOfficePanel)
- Passed the preference into the citation insertion code so markManager.insertReferenceIntoOO will add a space according to the user setting. (CSLCitationOOAdapter)
- Persisted the property using EasyBind so changes are saved and restored. (JabRefCliPreferences)
- Added the new localization string for the checkbox and updated the CHANGELOG. (JabLib resources, CHANGELOG.md)

Why

Previously the behaviour around adding spaces after inserted citations was inconsistent and caused reference extension issues when users manually added spaces. This change makes a sensible default (add a space) while allowing users to disable it if desired.

Notes

- Default is true to preserve a natural writing flow.
- No functional breaking changes.
- Manual testing required for the Libre/OpenOffice integration UI and citation insertion. If further adjustments are needed for edge cases, they can be addressed in follow-up PRs.

Summary

- Implement robust URL download and MIME detection logic and improve linked-file download handling.

What changed

1. URLDownload
- Reworked URLDownload to use Unirest for HTTP requests, set a default User-Agent and enable cookie management.
- MIME detection improved: attempt HEAD (with manual redirect handling), then GET, and finally fallback to URLConnection for local URIs.
- Added canBeReached() which uses a HEAD request and throws UnirestException on failure.
- Response handling: asInputStream() now checks HTTP response codes and throws FetcherClientException/FetcherServerException for 4xx/5xx responses.
- toTemporaryFile() creates a sensible temporary filename based on the source URL (keeps name when available and uses .tmp fallback).
- Exposed setSSLVerification to allow resetting the default SSLSocketFactory and HostnameVerifier.
- Added connect timeout support and enforced a non-null default timeout.
- Improved redirect handling and error logging; added MAX_RETRIES constant for redirect handling in mime detection.

2. DownloadLinkedFileAction
- Uses URLDownload to download files and binds download progress to a BackgroundTask for UI progress reporting.
- Infers file type first from reported MIME type, then from URL extension if needed, to pick the appropriate ExternalFileType.
- Builds a unique suggested filename and folder using existing LinkedFileHandler and FileNameUniqueness utilities.
- Handles HTML downloads specially: can either keep the original URL (no file change) or remove the URL/link and delete the downloaded HTML based on the keepHtmlLink flag.
- Preserves source URL in the new linked file according to filePreferences.shouldKeepDownloadUrl().
- Ensures duplicate files are detected and avoided (FileNameUniqueness), and cleaned up appropriately.
- Proper SSL handshake detection that prompts user confirmation in case of SSLHandshakeException.
- File copying is performed in FileDownloadTask using ProgressInputStream and EasyBind to report progress.

3. Tests
- Added/updated tests covering URLDownload and DownloadLinkedFileAction behavior using WireMock:
  - URLDownloadTest: verifies string and file downloads, mime detection, temporary file naming, connect timeout behavior, exception mapping for 429/503, and redirect handling.
  - DownloadLinkedFileActionTest: verifies replacing linked files after download, preserving source URL on re-download, keeping or removing HTML links depending on the flag, using a WireMock HTML endpoint.

Motivation and impact

- More reliable MIME/type detection avoids misclassifying resources (e.g. arXiv redirects giving HTML), leading to better file type inference and correct handling of HTML vs PDF downloads.
- Centralizing HTTP behavior in URLDownload (with Unirest, cookie handling and explicit error mapping) improves robustness and makes error reporting clearer.
- Improved UX: progress reporting for downloads, user confirmation on SSL issues, and correct handling of duplicates and HTML links.

Notes

- The changes rely on Unirest and WireMock in tests; ensure those dependencies are available in the build environment.
- Behavior for HTML downloads can be controlled through the keepHtmlLink flag and the FilePreferences.shouldKeepDownloadUrl setting.

Summary

Fix selection and context-menu behavior in GroupTreeView and update changelog.

What I changed

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/groups/GroupTreeView.java
  - Ensure the tree selection is updated when the user right-clicks a group so context-menu actions apply to the clicked node.
  - Preserve the currently selected node(s) when the tree model is refreshed/updated, avoiding unexpected selection loss during small updates (expand/collapse, reloads, or model changes).
  - Improve focus and input handling after mouse interactions so keyboard navigation and shortcuts continue to work predictably.
  - Simplify/optimize tree update logic to limit unnecessary rebuilds of the whole tree (only refresh affected nodes) which improves responsiveness.

- CHANGELOG.md
  - Add an entry describing the bug fixes and UX improvements for group tree interactions.

Why this change

Users reported that right-clicking a group did not reliably select the clicked node, causing context-menu commands to target the wrong group. The tree could also lose the selected node unexpectedly after refreshes/updates, leading to confusing UX. The changes make group selection and context-menu behavior predictable and reduce unnecessary work when updating the view.

How to test

1. Right-click a group entry — the clicked group should become selected and the context menu should operate on it.
2. Perform operations that refresh or update the group tree (expand/collapse groups, apply small model changes) — the selection should be preserved unless the selection node was removed.
3. After interacting with the tree using the mouse, use keyboard navigation and shortcuts — focus and keyboard handling should continue to work.

Files modified

- CHANGELOG.md
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/groups/GroupTreeView.java

Notes

This is a user-facing bugfix/UX improvement and changelog entry has been added accordingly.

text:
Summary
- Implements session restoration for shared databases: JabRef will attempt to reopen the last shared database connection on startup (related to #1703).

What I changed
- Restore flow on startup: JabRefGUI now checks preference flags and attempts to restore the last shared database tab using SharedDatabaseUIManager. If restoration fails (SQLException or DatabaseNotSupportedException) the OpenSharedDatabaseDialog is shown to let the user re-connect.
- SharedDatabaseUIManager: added API to open a new shared database tab and to open the last shared database from stored shared preferences. It now creates a BibDatabaseContext, opens the DBMSSynchronizer, registers itself as a listener and selects the new tab.
- OpenSharedDatabaseDialog: switched to using SharedDatabaseUIManager to open new shared database tabs (removes direct manipulation of BibDatabaseContext here).
- DBMSConnectionProperties: added a constructor that reads connection data from SharedDatabasePreferences and decrypts the stored password (handles decryption errors). Ensures password is non-null when some DBMS expect an empty string.
- JabRefFrame: records two new preference flags on quit/tear-down: sharedDatabaseLastEdited and sharedDatabaseLastFocused. These are used to decide whether to restore a shared DB on next startup. Converts shared DB context to local on quit (retains logic) and sets the appropriate flags.
- JabRefPreferences: added keys and defaults for sharedDatabaseLastEdited and sharedDatabaseLastFocused.
- CHANGELOG.md: added entry documenting the new session restoring functionality for shared databases.

Notes and error handling
- Restoration is attempted only when preferences indicate a shared database was edited and possibly focused in the last session.
- Errors during automatic restore (SQL or unsupported DB) are caught; JabRef logs a message and shows the connection dialog.

Testing and QA
- Manually tested in running JabRef.
- Internal QA done; CHANGELOG updated. See issue #1703 for background.

- Updated documentation and export-related comments to explain the precedence rules (inventor field takes precedence; fallback to author).

- Pay attention to template rendering and metadata writing to ensure no duplication of fields.

- Suppress acceptance dialog when a `.sav` file is found without changes.

- Merged "Append contents from a BibTeX library" into the "Import into database" flow.

- Prevented full-text search downloads from overwriting files with the same name.

- Numerous additional bug fixes improving stability and UX.

Removed
- Removed obsolete External programs / Open PDF preferences section.
- Always enable `.bib.bak` file generation on save (option removed).
- Removed built-in list of IEEE journal abbreviations (now provided separately at https://abbrv.jabref.org).

text:
Implement LinkedFileViewModel to manage linked file operations in the UI: open/open-folder, rename (including suggested rename and prompting), move to default directory (and move+rename), delete (with confirmation to remove link or delete from disk), edit metadata, write XMP metadata to PDF, and download online links into the project file directory. Key features:

- Download handling: prepares a download task that infers file type from MIME type or URL suffix, suggests filename and destination (applies file-dir pattern and ensures uniqueness), runs FileDownloadTask in BackgroundTask and binds download progress and ongoing state to the view.
- File type inference: attempts to infer a file type from URLDownload MIME type and, if missing, falls back to an extension/suffix-based inference.
- XMP metadata support: writeXMPMetadata runs in background and writes XMP to PDFs when applicable.
- Validation: fileExistsValidator validates existence of local linked files and produces a warning when missing.
- Properties exposed for binding: downloadProgress, downloadOngoing, isAutomaticallyFound, canWriteXMPMetadata, plus observables for updates.
- Robust user interaction: uses DialogService to prompt for confirmations and show errors, handles overwrite checks and I/O exceptions gracefully, and prevents renaming/moving of online links.
- Entry update after download: replaces or inserts the downloaded linked file into the entry file list.

Also contains utility methods to compute truncated display strings and to compare generated filenames/paths with originals.

Summary

This PR updates the Java Keyring dependency to the latest release which includes our upstream fix (javakeyring/java-keyring#90). This is a follow-up to #10224 and addresses the problem tracked in #8055 by using the upstream-corrected implementation instead of our temporary workaround.

What changed

- Bumped Java Keyring dependency to the release that integrates javakeyring/java-keyring#90.
- Removed the temporary workaround applied in #10224 (the fix is now provided upstream).

Why

The upstream project merged our fix, so we can rely on the official release instead of maintaining a local workaround. This should resolve the credential/keyring issues described in #8055.

Testing notes / How to verify

Please perform the following manual checks on supported platforms (Windows, macOS, Linux):
- Start JabRef and use features that store/retrieve credentials (e.g., synchronization, remote database authentication, or other features that use the keyring).
- Verify credentials are stored and retrieved without exceptions or errors.
- Verify behavior across application restart.

If you have platform-specific setups (Windows Credential Manager, macOS Keychain, libsecret on Linux), please test those to ensure the integration works across OSes.

- Upstream fix: https://github.com/javakeyring/java-keyring/pull/90
- Follow-up to: https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/pull/10224

Introduce persistent preferences for the Unlinked Files dialog and expose them through the main GUI preferences.

What I changed
- Added UnlinkedFilesDialogPreferences to encapsulate settings for the Unlinked Files dialog (e.g. dialog size/position and dialog-specific options).
- Updated JabRefGuiPreferences to create and provide access to the new UnlinkedFilesDialogPreferences so the rest of the UI can read/write those settings.

Why
- Persisting Unlinked Files dialog state improves the user experience by remembering user choices and dialog layout across restarts.
- Centralizing the dialog preferences under JabRefGuiPreferences keeps GUI-related settings organized and accessible.

Compatibility
- This is a non-breaking change: it only adds a new preferences container and an accessor in the existing GUI preferences class.

Notes
- No behavior changes to the dialog itself were included here; this change only provides the persistence layer and integration point for the dialog to use.

Improve OpenOffice integration and UI stability

Summary
- Fixes and refactors OpenOffice integration code to improve stability and connection handling.
- Updates the OpenOffice control panel UI to provide clearer status feedback and more robust enable/disable behavior.
- Adds/updates localized English strings used by the OpenOffice UI.
- Records the change in the top-level CHANGELOG.

Details
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/openoffice/OOBibBase.java
  - Add null checks and more robust lifecycle handling for the OpenOffice/LibreOffice connection to prevent runtime exceptions.
  - Ensure resources are cleaned up properly on disconnect and during error conditions.
  - Improve reconnection/error reporting logic.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/openoffice/OpenOfficePanel.java
  - Refactor UI logic to give better visual feedback about connection state (connected, disconnected, error).
  - Disable/enable controls appropriately to avoid invalid actions when not connected.
  - Improve threading/EDT usage so status updates happen safely in the UI thread.

- src/main/resources/l10n/JabRef_en.properties
  - Add and update English localization keys/values for the OpenOffice UI and status/error messages.

- CHANGELOG.md
  - Add entry describing the OpenOffice integration improvements and fixes.

Notes
- Behavior and UX for the OpenOffice panel should be more reliable after these changes; users who experienced crashes or unclear state indications when using the OpenOffice/LibreOffice connector should see improvements.
- No public API changes outside the GUI integration are expected.

Add comprehensive guide 'Set up a local workspace' under docs/getting-into-the-code.

This PR introduces a detailed developer onboarding document that covers:
- Prerequisites: GitHub account, git installation, recommended IDEs (IntelliJ IDEA, Eclipse) and JDK 20
- Getting the code: forking, cloning recommendations (including shallow clone example) and remote setup
- Generating sources (gradlew assemble) and when it's required
- Step-by-step IntelliJ setup: open build.gradle, trust project, configure JDK 20, Gradle JVM, compiler parameters (add-exports), enable annotation processors, reload Gradle, run via Gradle task and create run configuration
- Use IntelliJ internal build system for tests with guidance when to run Gradle to regenerate sources
- Code style and CheckStyle integration: import IntelliJ code style XML, install CheckStyle-IDEA plugin, configure checkstyle.xml and scan scope
- Editor preferences: JavaDoc wrapping, auto import, code folding settings
- Eclipse setup: gradle tasks, run/debug configurations, required VM arguments, optional e(fx)clipse plugin and localization test VM args
- Troubleshooting and common issues: Java installation errors, generated sources, buildSrc, module not found, OpenJFX local repo problems, JournalAbbreviationLoader NPE, IntelliJ version hints and cache invalidation steps

Notes for reviewers:
- Verify correctness of commands and VM/Gradle options
- Check screenshots and external links
- Confirm guidance for JDK 20 and IntelliJ/Eclipse workflows is accurate and up to date

This document should make it significantly easier for new contributors to get a working local development environment and avoid common setup pitfalls.

Summary:
Fixes launcher startup and robustness issues so the application no longer silently fails in certain environments and provides clearer errors when configuration or permissions are incorrect.

What this change does:
- Corrects launcher path resolution and ensures the correct executable is used when launching the process.
- Propagates required environment variables to the launched process reliably.
- Adds explicit checks for configuration file existence and executable permissions with clear, actionable error messages.
- Improves logging around startup failure modes to make diagnosis easier.
- Adds tests to cover the common failure scenarios (missing config, wrong permissions, env propagation).

Why this is needed:
Users were encountering launcher failures that were either silent or produced unhelpful errors. This change makes startup behavior deterministic and failures visible so they can be fixed quickly.

How to verify:
1. Start the application normally and confirm it launches as before.
2. Start with the config file missing and confirm the launcher emits a clear error message and exits with a non-zero status.
3. Start with the binary lacking execute permissions and confirm a clear error is produced.
4. Verify that required environment variables are present in the launched process.
5. Check logs for improved, actionable messages during startup.

Compatibility:
No breaking changes for normal startup paths; changes only affect error handling and edge cases to improve reliability.

Fix bug where wanted special characters placed between pattern parts (for example '-' or ':') were removed from generated citation keys.

Problem

cleanKey was previously called on the entire generated key. This removed separators that the user had placed in the key pattern (e.g. [author]-[year] produced Kilian2019 instead of Kilian-2019). See issue #4767.

Solution

Move the cleaning of illegal characters into the per-field label generation so that each label is cleaned individually, but non-field pattern characters (separators like '-' or ':') are preserved. The final key string is no longer globally cleaned.

What changed

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/bibtexkeypattern/BibtexKeyGenerator.java: apply cleanKey to label parts and stop cleaning the whole key at the end
- src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/bibtexkeypattern/BibtexKeyGeneratorTest.java: add test generateKeyWithMinusInCitationStyleOutsideAField asserting that [auth]-[year] produces "Newton-2019"
- CHANGELOG.md: add entry referencing issue #4767

Tests & verification

- Added unit test covering the case with a separator outside a field
- Manually tested key generation in a running JabRef instance

Issue

Fixes #4767

- Improved null-safety around column lookups/initialization to avoid potential NPEs and made initialization of derived values more explicit.
- Minor formatting and code-style improvements to match project conventions.

Why this change
- Makes it easier to add or modify main table columns in the future and reduces the chance of subtle bugs by centralizing column-related logic.

Compatibility
- No public API changes outside the GUI's internal table-format handling. Behavior should remain the same; changes are internal refactors.

Notes for reviewers
- Focus review on the extracted helper methods and any logic that determines column visibility/ordering to ensure behavior is preserved.

Summary

This PR improves the main toolbar layout and icons to match the prototypes (see screenshots). It groups related toolbar actions with separators, reorders some buttons, and adds a dedicated "Generate BibTeX keys" toolbar button. It also updates a couple of icon mappings and adjusts the toolbar separator spacing.

What I changed

- Grouped and reordered toolbar icons and added vertical separators to improve visual grouping and spacing (JabRefFrame.java).
- Added a new toolbar button for generating citation keys (Generate BibTeX keys) and placed it in the grouped section.
- Swapped/updated icon mappings:
  - COPY now uses MaterialDesignIcon.CONTENT_COPY instead of the previous material mapping (IconTheme.java).
  - OPEN folder comment adjusted (icon mapping clarified) (IconTheme.java).
- Ensured the "New library (BibTeX/BibLaTeX)" actions have an icon (StandardActions.java).
- Increased toolbar separator insets for better spacing (Base.css).
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to mention the toolbar grouping and icon changes.

Files modified

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/JabRefFrame.java (toolbar layout, inserted Separator nodes, reordered items)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/icon/IconTheme.java (COPY / OPEN icon changes)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/actions/StandardActions.java (added icons for New library BibTeX/BibLaTeX)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/Base.css (separator insets)
- CHANGELOG.md (note about grouped toolbar icons & icon changes)

Motivation

Make the toolbar visually clearer and more consistent with the proposed UI prototypes (by MartinKarim). Grouping related actions and adding separators helps users find and recognize functionality faster. Adding the Generate BibTeX keys button gives quick access to a frequently used action.

Issue

Fixes #4584

Testing & notes

- Manually tested UI changes in a running JabRef instance.
- Screenshots of the new layout are included in the original issue/PR description.
- No automated tests were added for this UI-only change.

Closes https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/13404

### Summary
This PR implements a new **Wiley TDM Fetcher** to enable full-text retrieval from Wiley journals using their official Text and Data Mining (TDM) REST API.

### Changes made
- Added `WileyFetcher.java` under `fetcher/fulltext/`
- Integrated it into `FulltextFetcher.java`
- Verified DOI-based PDF downloads work through the Wiley API
- Ensured compatibility with existing fulltext fetchers (e.g., Springer, IEEE)

### Notes
Wiley full-text PDFs require a valid **TDM API token**, which the fetcher can handle via standard API headers.

### Testing
- Tested with DOI: `10.1002/we.2952` (Wind Energy Journal)
- Fetcher correctly identifies and downloads the associated PDF.

Summary

Adjust the RFC fetcher so it correctly handles RFC IDs that refer to IETF drafts. Previously the fetcher blindly prefixed IDs with "RFC", which produced invalid identifiers for drafts (e.g. "RFC draft-ietf-...") and caused lookups to fail.

What I changed

- Detect identifiers that start with "draft" (case-insensitive, allowing a following '-' or space) and do not add the "RFC" prefix for those IDs.
- Added unit tests covering draft IDs (including the example draft-ietf-sidrops-aspa-verification) to prevent regressions.
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to describe the user-visible fix.
- Manually tested the change in a running JabRef instance and verified RFC fetcher now resolves draft IDs correctly.
- Verified relevant documentation and created/checked documentation issues where applicable.

Testing & screenshots

- Test case: draft-ietf-sidrops-aspa-verification (added automated test)
- Manual verification screenshots show the fetcher failing before this change and succeeding after. The images were included in the original issue to demonstrate the fix.

Fixes

This PR improves the Key Bindings preference UI and backing view model, fixes related bugs, and adds/adjusts unit tests. The change also updates the changelog.

- Manual verification of the key bindings tab: searching, editing a binding, detecting conflicts, and resetting to defaults.

Notes

- This is primarily an internal bugfix/refactor for the preferences UI; no migration steps are required for users.
- If you see any further issues with specific bindings or platform-specific shortcut behavior, please report them with steps to reproduce.

Summary

- Change default keyboard shortcuts for navigating between entries when the Entry Editor is active to Alt+Up / Alt+Down. (Changelog updated)
- Persist window state on close and restore it on start. (Changelog punctuation fixed)

Behavior & bugfixes

- Improve robustness of application startup by wrapping JabRefMain.start(...) initialization in a try/catch and logging unexpected exceptions instead of letting them crash the JVM.

Entry-table selection/navigation

- Simplified selection logic in BasePanel: selectPreviousEntry/selectNextEntry now use clearAndSelect(...) with arithmetic on the current selected index instead of separate clear/select calls. Removed a deprecated clearAndSelect(int) helper and other now-unused selection helpers.

Entry editor navigation & focus

- Added new key bindings in EntryEditor for ENTRY_EDITOR_NEXT_ENTRY and ENTRY_EDITOR_PREVIOUS_ENTRY which call panel.selectNextEntry()/selectPreviousEntry() so the editor can move to the next/previous entry using the new Alt+Up/Alt+Down shortcuts.
- Updated KeyBinding defaults for ENTRY_EDITOR_NEXT_ENTRY and ENTRY_EDITOR_PREVIOUS_ENTRY to use "alt+DOWN" and "alt+UP" respectively.

Focus handling & threading simplifications

- Removed many uses of DefaultTaskExecutor.runInJavaFXThread and simplified bind/notification flows in EntryEditor and EntryEditorTab to call bindToEntry/notifyAboutFocus directly on the JavaFX thread.
- EntryEditor: factored out getSelectedTab() helper and simplified notification path.
- EntryEditorTab: no longer uses DefaultTaskExecutor; bindToEntry is invoked directly.

Field editors: focus preservation

- FieldEditorFX: replaced requestFocus() with focus() which focuses the first child node (if present). Added childIsFocused() to detect whether any child control currently has focus.
- ControlHelper: added childIsFocused(Parent) helper used by FieldEditorFX to check focus recursively.
- FieldsEditorTab: when rebinding to a new entry, the previously focused field (if any) is remembered and focus is restored with Platform.runLater(...) after rebuilding the editor UI. Also switched to the new FieldEditorFX.focus() API.

Formatting / cleanup

- Minor import cleanup and small refactorings across EntryEditorTab, EntryEditor, FieldsEditorTab, FieldEditorFX, ControlHelper and BasePanel.
- Changelog adjusted to reflect the keyboard shortcut change and window state behavior.

text:
Add comprehensive BasePanel implementation for JabRef UI

This change provides the full BasePanel class which coordinates a database view and editor within the JabRef desktop application. Key responsibilities and features included:

- UI composition
  - Manages main split pane with top main table and bottom component that can be an entry editor (EntryEditor) or preview (PreviewPanel) embedded via JFXPanel.
  - Creates and configures MainTable, MainTableDataModel and MainTableFormat and wires selection, keyboard and focus listeners.
  - Persists and restores splitter/divider locations and supports preview/entry-editor height preferences.

- Actions and command dispatch
  - Registers a large set of actions (save, save as, copy/paste/cut, delete, edit/present entry, open URL/file, merge, replace, generate keys, cleanup, abbreviate/unabbreviate, export, send email, write XMP, mark/unmark entries, group operations, file operations, back/forward history etc.).
  - Implements runCommand to dispatch BaseAction or AbstractWorker actions and provides proper error handling and frame unblock on failure.

- Clipboard and copy/paste support
  - Implements ClipboardOwner and supports copying TransferableBibtexEntry objects and pasting parsed BibEntries from clipboard.
  - Provides copy utilities for titles, cite keys, key+title and citation formatting using CitationStyleToClipboardWorker.

- Persistence and saving
  - saveDatabase method handles saving entire or partial database, character encoding handling (reporting unencodable characters and retrying with another encoding), and commit/cancel session logic.
  - registerUndoableChanges to add undo edits for changes made during save operations.
  - autoGenerateKeysBeforeSaving option to generate keys pre-save when enabled.

- Undo/Redo
  - Integrates CountingUndoManager with Undo/Redo actions and stores compound edits for insert/delete/type/key/field changes.
  - Handles non-undoable changes and marks base-changed state accordingly.

- Entry lifecycle and navigation
  - Insert/new entry creation, automatic field updates, key collision handling, selection and optional auto-open of entry editor.
  - Entry highlighting, selecting next/previous/first/last, ensuring correct focus and avoiding selection loss.
  - Maintains back/forward history of shown entries and enables/disables frame actions accordingly.

- Search and autocompletion
  - Instantiates PersonNameSuggestionProvider and SuggestionProviders for auto-completion and indexing existing entries.
  - Registers AutoCompleteUpdater to keep suggestion providers in sync with database changes.
  - Integrates with GlobalSearchBar to update and react to entry additions/changes/removals.

- Collaboration and external changes
  - Hooks DatabaseChangeMonitor for databases backed by files to detect external modifications and expose temp file.
  - Offers resetChangeMonitor/markExternalChangesAsResolved/updateTimeStamp utilities.

- Miscellaneous
  - File search and automatic opening of associated files using FileFinder/FileFinders with ExternalFileType resolution.
  - Special field actions for relevance, quality, printed, priority, ranking, read status.
  - Preview style cycling and preview activation toggling across all panels.
  - Proper cleanup to unregister change monitors and hide related side panels.

Threading and integration notes:
- Mixes Swing EDT code and JavaFX usage via JFXPanel and DefaultTaskExecutor.runInJavaFXThread.
- Uses SwingUtilities.invokeLater/invokeAndWait for thread-safe UI updates.

Overall, BasePanel centralizes the GUI logic, user actions, interaction with BibDatabaseContext, undo/redo bookkeeping and UI history management. This provides the core interactive behavior for a JabRef database tab.

text:
Implement Abbreviation model with fuzzy matching and repository + tests

Summary:
- Add Abbreviation class that represents a journal name and its abbreviations, including:
  - Normalization of fields and generation of a dotless form (abbreviation without dots and extra spaces).
  - Support for an explicit shortest unique abbreviation.
  - Fuzzy similarity check using Levenshtein distance (isSimilar) for tolerant comparisons.
  - getNext rotation logic to cycle between full name, abbreviation, dotless and shortest-unique forms.
  - Proper equals and hashCode that compare normalized fields; implements Comparable with fuzzy matching to treat similar entries as equal.
  - Serializable with some transient fields and string interning for memory efficiency.

- Update JournalAbbreviationRepository to:
  - Load abbreviation data from an H2 MVStore file into Abbreviation objects and populate lookup maps (full, abbreviation, dotless, shortest-unique).
  - Provide a demo constructor when no MV file is available.
  - Support custom abbreviations via a TreeSet with deduplication based on Abbreviation.compareTo/equals.
  - Expose lookup utilities: isKnownName, isAbbreviatedName, get, getNextAbbreviation, getDefaultAbbreviation, getDotless, getShortestUniqueAbbreviation, getFullNames, getAllLoaded.
  - Handle ampersand unescaping and ignore inputs containing question marks.

- Add comprehensive unit tests (AbbreviationTest) covering:
  - Trimming/space normalization behavior and dotless generation.
  - Semicolon-containing abbreviation strings.
  - getNext behavior including shortest unique abbreviation cases.
  - Equality, compareTo and fuzzy similarity checks (punctuation, missing letters, case differences).

Other:
- Add VSCode recommendations and LTEX dictionary entries used by the project.
- Workspace Java/Checkstyle settings for consistent formatting and Checkstyle version.

These changes introduce robust abbreviation handling and tolerant comparisons used by the journal abbreviation repository, and are verified by unit tests.

- CHANGELOG.md was updated.

Summary

Centralize and improve backup/autosave handling by moving responsibilities into BackupManager and ensuring backups are created reliably using database-specific context. Update UI frame integration and database context to work with the revised backup flow. Update CHANGELOG accordingly.

What changed

- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/logic/autosaveandbackup/BackupManager.java
  - Centralized logic for creating and cleaning up backup files.
  - Ensure backups are created using the active BibDatabaseContext so database-specific settings (paths, file names) are respected.
  - Improved error handling around backup creation and deletion to avoid crashes during shutdown or when IO errors occur.

- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/model/database/BibDatabaseContext.java
  - Expose or adapt API to provide the information BackupManager needs (e.g. base file name/path and database-specific settings) so backups are stored in the correct location and with correct naming.
  - Small resilience improvements to avoid null pointer scenarios when no file is associated yet.

- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/gui/JabRefFrame.java
  - Integrate with the updated BackupManager: use the new API for triggering backups on save/auto-save and during shutdown.
  - Ensure UI shutdown sequence waits for backup tasks to complete or handles failures gracefully to avoid data loss or exceptions.

- CHANGELOG.md
  - Document the behavior change and bug fixes related to backups and autosave.

Why this change

- Previously backup handling was scattered and sometimes failed to produce backups for specific databases or during shutdown, which could result in lost data or uncaught exceptions.
- Centralizing backup logic in BackupManager and providing the necessary database context allows for consistent, reliable backups per database and improves error handling.

Testing performed

- Manual testing of save, autosave and application shutdown to validate backup files are created in expected locations and with expected names.
- Verified behavior when database has no associated file yet (new database) and when file IO errors are simulated.
- Confirmed UI shutdown sequence no longer crashes when backup creation fails; warnings are logged instead.

Notes for reviewers

- Pay attention to the API changes in BibDatabaseContext used by BackupManager; this may affect other callers that previously accessed path/name directly.
- BackupManager contains improved error handling — consider whether logging detail and user-visible notifications are sufficient or should be expanded.

Backward compatibility / Migration

- Existing user settings are preserved; backup files will continue to be created but the location/naming is now tied more closely to the database context.
- If other modules accessed database file paths directly, they may need minor updates to align with the new BibDatabaseContext API.

- Update and add unit tests for the new behavior and MIME parsing. Tests cover: notification when an HTML page is downloaded, correct filetype (.html) for downloaded HTML pages, that PDF URLs are still detected as PDF, and that MIME types with parameters are handled.

- src/main/resources/l10n/JabRef_en.properties: add notification message.
- src/test/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/LinkedFileViewModelTest.java: add tests and test setup/teardown for cookie handling; add tests for HTML notification, HTML/PDF download handling, and MIME parameter parsing.
- CHANGELOG.md: add entry describing the fix.

Enhance entry-merge UI and duplicate resolution flow

This change introduces several improvements to the merge entries UI and integrates merging more robustly into duplicate/ import workflows:

- Add DefaultRadioButtonSelectionMode to MergeEntries and constructors that allow selecting which side (LEFT or RIGHT) should be preselected by default. This enables callers to control initial radio-button selection when presenting merge UI.
- Add select-all buttons and corresponding API methods (selectAllLeftRadioButtons, selectAllRightRadioButtons) to MergeEntries. The header now contains buttons to quickly choose all left or all right values.
- Add a DiffMode combobox in MergeEntries to choose how differences are displayed (plain, word/character diff, symmetric diffs). The chosen diff mode is persisted to GUI preferences.
- Improve MergeEntries layout with headings/icons and support for custom left/right header text via setLeftHeaderText/setRightHeaderText.
- Ensure merged entry is computed and kept consistent with radio-button selections (getMergedEntry and updateMergedEntry behavior).

- Add MergeEntriesDialog: a simple dialog wrapper around MergeEntries that returns the merged BibEntry when accepted.

- Update DuplicateResolverDialog to use MergeEntries for presenting merge UI in duplicate resolution and to expose getMergedEntry() for callers.
  - The dialog also preserves/updates its window state via StateManager when closing.

- Update EntryChangeViewModel to initialize a MergeEntries instance for the change description and to toggle radio-button selections depending on acceptance state (select all right when accepted, select all left when not). Also ensure description is initialized before applying changes to avoid NPEs.

Restores recognition of Material Design icons that stopped working after commit 2b760cddf53cceae54fd149774226461f5290daa. This fixes #6078 (related to #5245).

Problem
A recent change made only icons contained inside JabRefIcons available, so references to icons from the MaterialDesignIcon enum were no longer resolved and those icons were not shown in the UI.

What this PR does
- Reintroduces the lookup for MaterialDesignIcon entries so icon codes referencing material-design icons are recognized again.
- Fixes #6078 by restoring the ability to use MaterialDesignIcon values (see the original lookup approach below):
  return Enums.getIfPresent(MaterialDesignIcon.class, iconCode.toUpperCase(Locale.ENGLISH))
              .toJavaUtil()
              .map(icon -> new InternalMaterialDesignIcon(getColor(), icon));

Notes & risks
- The change that caused this regression is commit 2b760cddf53cceae54fd149774226461f5290daa. Reverting or restoring the lookup may reintroduce the problem reported in #5245 if that underlying cause is not addressed. Reviewers should verify that reintroducing MaterialDesignIcon resolution does not bring the original issue back.
- Exposing all Material Design icons in practice makes most sense when there is a UI element (e.g. a dropdown in the new/edit group dialog) that allows users to pick from available icons. Without such a control, free-text icon codes may lead to confusion.

Testing
- Create / edit a group and use an icon code that corresponds to a MaterialDesignIcon name (case-insensitive).
- Verify the icon is displayed as expected in the group list and dialogs.

Related
- Fixes #6078
- Related: #5245
- Cause: commit 2b760cddf53cceae54fd149774226461f5290daa

Request for reviewers
Please verify there is no regression of the issue discussed in #5245 after restoring MaterialDesignIcon lookup. Consider whether we should add a dropdown or selector for available icons in the new/edit group dialog to improve discoverability and avoid free-text errors.

Summary

This PR extends the RIS importer to better handle a larger set of RIS fields and multi-valued fields. It adapts mappings where possible (based on the lists linked by @dsifford) and introduces custom fields for RIS tags that don't have a direct BibTeX/JabRef equivalent. This work addresses import-related gaps described in #3634 and #2607.

What changed

- Expanded the RIS-to-BibTeX field mapping to cover many additional RIS tags.
- Support for multiple occurrences of the same RIS tag (multi-valued fields) so repeated fields are preserved on import.
- Unknown or unmapped RIS tags are now saved as custom fields instead of being dropped.
- Mapping updates were implemented following the external lists referenced in the issue discussion.
- CHANGELOG entry updated to reflect these importer improvements.

What I changed
- Updated src/main/java/org/jabref/model/strings/LatexToUnicodeAdapter.java
  - Refactored the adapter implementation to make the conversion logic more robust and maintainable.
  - Improved handling of LaTeX diacritics and composed characters so sequences such as \"{o}, \^e, and similar constructs are converted consistently to their Unicode equivalents.
  - Better handling of braces and nested commands to avoid accidental removal or misinterpretation of grouped content.
  - Fixed a number of edge-case conversion bugs (e.g. special ligatures and multi-character macros).
- Updated/added unit tests in src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/layout/format/LatexToUnicodeFormatterTest.java
  - Added comprehensive tests that cover plain commands, composed diacritics, braces, nested constructs and regression cases to prevent future breakage.
  - Ensures the adapter yields the expected Unicode output for a variety of representative inputs.

Why this matters
- Provides more accurate and predictable conversion from LaTeX-encoded names and strings to Unicode for display and export.
- Reduces user-visible errors caused by malformed conversions and prevents regressions via added tests.

Notes
- No public API changes were intended beyond corrected conversion behavior; callers should see improved output for previously failing cases.
- All added/updated tests are included to validate the new behavior.

Summary:
This PR adds a simple mechanism to restore backward compatibility for users who want to return to JabRef 4.3.1 after having run JabRef 5.0 on Windows. It provides a Windows registry patch (JabRef-downgrade-regpatch.reg) that restores the registry entries expected by JabRef 4.3.1 so the old version can run again without needing a fresh system state.

What this PR contains:
- JabRef-downgrade-regpatch.reg: a Windows registry patch that reverts registry changes introduced by newer JabRef versions and restores associations/entries required by 4.3.1.
- Tests: unit tests added where applicable (see checklist).
- Manual verification: the changed features were manually tested in a running JabRef build.

How to use (Windows):
1. Close JabRef 5.x.
2. Double-click JabRef-downgrade-regpatch.reg and allow it to update the registry (or import it using regedit).
3. Install or re-run JabRef 4.3.1 — it should now find the registry settings it expects.

Notes / open questions:
1. Installer inclusion: I need guidance on how to include JabRef-downgrade-regpatch.reg in the Windows installer package (or whether we should ship it in a separate downgrade bundle). Any suggestions on installer integration are welcome.
2. Testing: I don’t have Java 8 and JabRef 4.3.1 available locally to perform an end-to-end downgrade test. Volunteers who can test the full downgrade flow (Windows, Java 8, JabRef 4.3.1) would be appreciated.

Related issues:
fixes https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/5933
fixes https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/6234
refs https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/4579

text:
Summary

This PR fixes a bug in RegExpBasedFileFinder that caused duplicate results when searching recursively and also caused non-recursive patterns to unexpectedly match files in subdirectories.

What was happening

- Files.find was called with Integer.MAX_VALUE as maxDepth which allowed the same file to be discovered multiple times: once when searching from a parent directory and again when searching from its own directory.  
- Non-recursive patterns (without "**") could still return files from subdirectories because of the deep Files.find invocation.

What I changed

- Limit the search depth used with Files.find to 1 so that Files.find only inspects the target directory and its immediate children. This avoids discovering the same file multiple times when directory traversal is performed elsewhere in the code. (src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/util/io/RegExpBasedFileFinder.java)
- Added tests to cover both behaviors: a recursive pattern that finds a file in a subdirectory, and a non-recursive pattern that must not find files in subdirectories. (src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/util/io/RegExpBasedFileFinderTests.java)
- Updated the CHANGELOG to record the bug fix. (CHANGELOG.md)
- Included the test resource PDF used by the new tests. (src/test/resources/.../pdfInSubdirectory.pdf)

Tests & verification

- Added tests: testFindFileInSubdirectory (ensures recursive pattern finds a file in a subdirectory) and testFindFileNonRecursive (ensures non-recursive pattern does not find files in subdirectories).  
- Ran the tests and manually verified the behavior in a running JabRef build.

Notes

- This change addresses the duplicate-result behavior and aligns the finder with expected semantics: recursive behavior should be expressed by the pattern (e.g. using "**"), and non-recursive patterns must not traverse into subdirectories.
- Related: may be connected to issue #2274.

Checklist

- [x] CHANGELOG updated
- [x] Tests added
- [x] Manually tested in running JabRef
- [ ] Documentation/screenshots (not applicable)

Summary

This PR introduces an application theme system and exposes theme selection in Preferences -> General. It adds a ThemeManager to control and apply themes, persists the chosen theme in preferences, and updates the UI and resources to allow users to pick Light, Dark, or System default themes.

What changed

- Added ThemeManager to manage and apply themes at runtime.
- Exposed theme selection in the General preferences UI (GeneralTab.fxml, GeneralTab.java, GeneralTabViewModel.java).
- Added preference keys and handling in JabRefPreferences and WorkspacePreferences to store the user's theme choice.
- Updated localization (JabRef_en.properties) with strings for the new theme options.
- Updated module-info.java and build files (build.gradle, external-libraries.md) for required modules/dependencies.
- Documented the change in CHANGELOG.md.

Behavior

- Users can select Light, Dark, or System Default theme from Preferences -> General.
- The chosen theme is applied immediately and stored so it persists across restarts.
- System Default defers to the operating system theme when available.

Migration & Compatibility

- Existing preferences remain compatible; this only adds new preference keys for theme selection with sensible defaults.

Testing notes

1. Open Preferences -> General.
2. Change the Theme setting to Light, Dark, or System Default.
3. Verify the UI updates immediately to reflect the selected theme.
4. Restart the application and confirm the chosen theme persists.

Summary

- Add a small shell launcher and integrate it into snap packaging so the JabRef snap invokes the bundled Java runtime correctly.

What I changed

1. Added snap/local/JabRef-launcher
   - A POSIX shell wrapper that calls the snap-provided Java runtime at $SNAP/lib/runtime/bin/java with module path -p "$DIR/../app" and module main org.jabref/org.jabref.JabRefLauncher. It forwards all arguments to the Java process.

2. Updated snap/snapcraft.yaml
   - Added a new part jabref-launcher that sources the local launcher and organizes it as bin/JabRef inside the snap.
   - Keeps the main jabref part (downloads the portable distribution, sets the snap version from JabRef.cfg, patches native messaging host JSON files to point at the snap browser-proxy, removes the original bin/JabRef so the new launcher replaces it).
   - Existing apps entries remain: jabref -> bin/JabRef, browser-proxy -> lib/jabrefHost.py.
   - Environment _JAVA_OPTIONS continues to set user.home to $SNAP_USER_DATA.

Why

- The launch script ensures JabRef is started with the Java runtime bundled inside the snap and uses the modular invocation expected by the application (module path + module main). This is necessary for strict-confinement snaps to reliably find and use the embedded runtime and for replacing the upstream portable Linux launcher removed during packaging.
- The packaging change wires the local launcher into the final snap (bin/JabRef) and ensures native messaging host files are rewritten to call the snap's browser-proxy.

Notes / testing

- Build the snap (snapcraft) and install or run with snap try to verify the launcher starts JabRef.
- Verify native messaging hosts were patched to point at /snap/bin/jabref.browser-proxy and that browser integration behaves as expected.
- Ensure the launcher file preserves the executable bit in the final snap (the part uses dump/plugin and organize to bin/JabRef).

Add AbbreviateAction to handle journal name abbreviation/unabbreviation from the UI. This command integrates with StandardActions (ABBREVIATE_DEFAULT, ABBREVIATE_DOTLESS, ABBREVIATE_SHORTEST_UNIQUE and UNABBREVIATE), binds its executability to whether entries are selected, and executes work in the background via TaskExecutor/BackgroundTask.

Key behaviors:
- Supports multiple abbreviation types and reads preferences for whether to use the fjournal field.
- For abbreviation: builds a set of Callables (one per selected entry) which check all journal name fields and invoke an UndoableAbbreviator inside the JavaFX thread (via UiTaskExecutor.runInJavaFXThread).
- Executes callables concurrently using HeadlessExecutorService.executeAll, collects results, counts modified entries, and returns a localized summary message.
- For unabbreviate: executes in-stream, counts changes, and returns a localized summary message.
- Creates a NamedCompound for each operation and registers it with the UndoManager to enable undo, and marks the library tab as changed.
- Notifies the user when operations start and when finished, and logs unexpected actions or errors.

This class centralizes the journal abbreviation workflow, ensuring background execution, concurrency, undo support and proper UI-thread handling for per-entry modifications.

text:
Implement main application window (JabRefFrame)

Summary
- Adds the primary JavaFX BorderPane implementation for the main JabRef window. This class composes menus, toolbar, tabbed libraries, side pane and orchestrates application lifecycle behaviors (open/close/quit).

Key features
- Menu and toolbar construction: builds File/Edit/Library/Quality/Lookup/View/Tools/Options/Help menus and the main toolbar with grouped action buttons (new/open/save, undo/redo, new-entry, search bar, social links, task indicator, etc.).
- Tabbed library management: manages LibraryTab lifecycle (add/remove/close), context menus for tabs, and helpers to open/import parser results into tabs.
- Drag & drop support: adds visual DnD indicator tab and handles dropping .bib files to open them (initDragAndDrop).
- Key bindings: central handling of keyboard shortcuts (initKeyBindings) wired to application actions (focus table, library navigation, new entries, paste workaround on macOS, search, etc.).
- Background task indicator & pop-over: toolbar progress indicator bound to stateManager task progress and background tasks list displayed in a PopOver with task-specific icons.
- Import-by-ID popover: creates a popover dialog to generate new entries from identifiers (DOI/ArXiv/etc.) using GenerateEntryFromIdDialog.
- Telemetry prompt: shows a delayed notification (initShowTrackingNotification) asking user to opt-in to anonymous telemetry; stores preference accordingly.
- Autosave & backup integration: starts/stops AutosaveManager and BackupManager for databases when opening/closing tabs; determines readiness for autosave.
- Save/close/quit flows: robust confirmation dialogs for unsaved changes and empty entries, waiting for background tasks before quitting, and tear-down logic that persists recent file history and preferences.
- State bindings: uses EasyBind to connect tab selection, active database, open databases list and active search to StateManager; keeps UI and global state in sync.
- Undo/redo wiring: registers per-tab UndoRedoEvent listeners to keep UI updated on undo/redo events.
- Misc: file-history menu integration, open-folder selection, window title binding, and telemetry event tracking when opening new database.

Notes
- The class depends heavily on many application services (Globals, stateManager, prefs, dialogService, taskExecutor, themeManager, etc.) and composes numerous actions.
- Contains platform-specific workarounds (macOS paste handling) and careful JavaFX thread handling (Platform.runLater and DefaultTaskExecutor usage).

This change centralizes and organizes the main UI wiring and application lifecycle handling for JabRef.
