Summary

This PR adds a new option to let JabRef follow the OS light/dark preference. When enabled, JabRef will automatically switch between the light and dark themes according to the current system appearance and will react to live changes from the OS.

What changed

- Added a new "Use System Preference" checkbox to Preferences -> General -> Appearance. When enabled, the Visual theme combobox and custom-theme input are disabled.
- Added a persistent workspace preference (themeSyncOs) (default: false) so the choice is saved and restored.
- Integrated jSystemThemeDetector to detect OS theme and listen for changes; ThemeManager now uses this detector to switch themes when themeSyncOs is enabled.
- Hooked up the new preference into the UI view model and preferences storage.
- Added the new dependency to build.gradle and module-info, and documented it in external-libraries.md.
- Added an English translation entry for the new checkbox label.

Files changed (high level)

- UI: GeneralTab.fxml, GeneralTab.java, GeneralTabViewModel.java
- Theme handling: ThemeManager.java
- Preferences: JabRefPreferences.java, WorkspacePreferences.java
- Build & modules: build.gradle, module-info.java
- Docs & metadata: CHANGELOG.md, external-libraries.md, l10n/JabRef_en.properties

Behavior details

- If the new preference is enabled, ThemeManager will choose Theme.light() or Theme.dark() based on OsThemeDetector.isDark() and will update the UI when the OS preference changes.
- If the preference is disabled, the explicit theme selection (Light / Dark / Custom) behaves as before.
- The choice persists across restarts via the workspace preferences (defaults to false).

Notes

- Adds dependency: com.github.Dansoftowner:jSystemThemeDetector:3.6 (Apache-2.0).
- Based on work in #9263.

Closes #8729

Closes #14414

Summary

This PR restores the ability to reset the entry table column configuration when preferences are cleared. Previously, clearing preferences did not restore main table/column preferences to their built-in defaults. The change adds default constructors and helper methods to provide and apply default Column/MainTable preferences and hooks them into the preference clearing and importing flows.

What changed

- ColumnPreferences
  - Added a private default constructor that initializes the built-in default column set (types, field names and widths).
  - Added static ColumnPreferences.getDefault() to obtain the default column configuration.
  - Added setAll(ColumnPreferences) to replace current settings with another ColumnPreferences instance.

- MainTablePreferences
  - Added a private default constructor and static getDefault() to create default main table preferences.
  - Added setAll(MainTablePreferences) to copy all values from another MainTablePreferences instance.

- JabRefGuiPreferences
  - When clearing preferences (clear()) the main table and column preferences are now reset to defaults by calling setAll(...) with MainTablePreferences.getDefault() and ColumnPreferences.getDefault().
  - importPreferences(...) now also restores main table/column preferences from the imported backing-store values when present; otherwise defaults are used.
  - Replaced direct construction of main table/column preferences with new helper methods getMainTablePreferencesFromBackingStore(...) and getMainTableColumnPreferencesFromBackingStore(...) that return defaults if no stored values are present (ensuring a proper reset behavior and backward compatibility).

Behavioral notes

- Clearing preferences will now restore the entry table columns to the original built-in configuration.
- When importing preferences, stored main table and column settings are respected when present; otherwise defaults are used.
- Existing stored preferences are still read and used as before; the new code simply provides a proper fallback to defaults when no stored configuration exists.

Testing

- Changes were manually tested in a running JabRef instance to verify that clearing preferences restores the table columns to the default layout.

Other

- This change focuses on reset behavior and does not alter the persisted format. No user-visible changes occur unless preferences are cleared/imported.

- [x] Manually tested in JabRef.
- [/] JUnit tests added (n/a).
- [/] Screenshots/CHANGELOG/docs updated if needed.

Summary:
- Update tests to reflect two upstream changes: the Ads fetcher now returns a `url` field, and DBLP no longer supports negative operators in queries.

What changed:
- Ads fetcher tests:
  - Updated assertions to expect the returned `url` attribute instead of the previous field.
  - Updated fixtures/mocks to include the `url` value returned by the fetcher.
- DBLP tests:
  - Removed or replaced tests that relied on negative operators (e.g. queries with `-term`).
  - Converted those cases to equivalent positive-query tests or marked them as skipped with an explanatory comment where behavior cannot be reproduced.
  - Updated DBLP-related fixtures/mocks to match the current DBLP behavior.
- Minor test refactors and added comments explaining the rationale for test changes.

Why:
- The external Ads fetcher contract changed to provide a `url` field; tests must assert the new structure.
- DBLP no longer honors negative operators, so tests that expected filtering via negative operators were failing and must be adapted to current semantics.

Impact & follow-ups:
- Only test code and fixtures were modified; no production logic changes are included.
- CI should pass once tests are aligned with the new external behavior.
- If DBLP restores negative-operator support in the future, we can reintroduce the original tests or add compatibility handling in the codebase.

Summary

This PR implements a workaround for issue #796: undoing deletion or cutting of multiple entries only undoing the first entry. The root cause is that when the first entry is re-inserted, that insertion creates and inserts a NamedCompound into the UndoManager which closes/kills the main compound that represents the multi-entry undo. That leaves only the first entry undone.

What I changed

- Each deleted/cut entry is now wrapped in its own NamedCompound when building the undo operation. This prevents a single nested insertion from killing the entire multi-entry NamedCompound.
- Adjusted undo construction logic so that each entry gets its own NamedCompound and is added separately to the UndoManager.

Why this change

- This is a pragmatic workaround to avoid the multi-entry undo being interrupted by nested insertion operations that register their own undo compounds.

Behavioral trade-offs / Known limitations

- User-visible behavior: undoing a multi-entry delete/cut now requires multiple Undo actions (Ctrl+Z) — one per entry — instead of a single Undo that restores all entries at once.
- This is not the ideal UX, but it prevents loss of undo steps. A proper fix would allow nested operations to avoid inserting a NamedCompound that interferes with an outer compound, or to temporarily suspend insertion of new compounds during an outer compound.

- CHANGELOG.md: updated
- Pull request description: included

- This is marked WIP because it’s a workaround; I plan to follow up with a cleaner fix that preserves multi-entry undo as a single action, or otherwise prevents inner operations from closing the outer NamedCompound.
- See issue #796 for discussion and reproduction steps.

- Undo building logic where Deleted/Cut entries are collected and NamedCompounds are created (see commits for exact files).

Next steps

- Add automated tests that reproduce the original bug and validate the final desired behavior.
- Investigate alternatives to support a single multi-entry undo without nested compounds interfering.

text:
Summary

Add fuzzy matching to journal abbreviation lookup to improve matching for variations, punctuation differences, common typos, and alternate abbreviation styles.

What this change does

- Introduces a normalization step that strips punctuation, collapses whitespace, and lowercases input for more robust comparisons.
- Adds a fuzzy match layer (token- and edit-distance-based) that runs when exact matches fail and returns the best candidate above a configurable similarity threshold.
- Keeps existing exact-match behavior as the primary path to avoid regressions.

Implementation notes

- The lookup function now attempts: exact match -> normalized exact match -> fuzzy match.
- Fuzzy matching uses a combination of token similarity and Levenshtein distance (configurable threshold) to prefer semantically close candidates and avoid false positives.
- Caching and an early-rejection threshold are used to limit the performance impact on large abbreviation sets.

Tests and docs

- Adds unit tests covering punctuation differences, case differences, common typos, and ambiguous abbreviations.
- Updates documentation to describe the new behavior and configuration options (similarity threshold and normalization toggles).

Backward compatibility

- Exact matches remain unchanged. Fuzzy matching is only applied after exact and normalized exact checks, and its sensitivity can be tuned or disabled via configuration.

Notes

- This improves matching quality for inputs like “JAMA”, “J. Am. Med. Assoc.”, “J Am Med Assoc”, and minor misspellings such as “J Am Med Assocn.” while avoiding broad overmatching by using conservative defaults.

Summary

Keep the group pane width/height when the application window is resized so that the user's adjusted pane size is preserved instead of being reset to the default.

Problem

When resizing the main window, the group pane (side/secondary pane) would revert to its default size or behave inconsistently, losing the user's manual resize. This created a jarring UX when users had customized the pane size.

Solution

- Preserve the group pane size during window resize events by storing and re-applying the current pane size (via flex-basis / stored pixel value) rather than resetting to defaults.
- Add resize handling logic to the layout manager / group pane component so the pane maintains its size while respecting min/max constraints and collapse/expand state.
- Ensure behavior is consistent across toggling visibility and across different window aspect changes.

Files/areas touched

- Group pane component (resize logic)
- Layout manager / window resize handler
- Related CSS to ensure flex sizing and constraints are applied correctly
- Unit/integration tests for resize behavior

Testing / QA steps

1. Open the app with the group pane visible. Manually resize the group pane to a custom width.
2. Resize the main application window (make it wider and narrower). Verify the group pane keeps the custom size rather than snapping back to default.
3. Collapse/expand the group pane and repeat the resize to ensure size is preserved when re-expanded.
4. Confirm min/max constraints still apply and no layout regressions occur in different viewport sizes.

Notes

- No breaking API changes.
- Fixes #6180.

Refactor BibTeX string editor UI and validation

Summary
- Rework the BibTeX String Editor dialog to a two-column layout with an inline editable table and a compact icon toolbar. Improve UX for adding, editing and removing strings.
- Centralize and improve invalid-state styling and table/list cell validation visuals.
- Remove dependency on ControlsFxVisualizer for cell validation visualization and replace it with in-house tooltip + pseudo-class handling.

Key changes
- UI (FXML & icons)
  - Replaced the old dialog layout with a new HBox/VBox layout containing:
    - a TableView with three columns: label, content, and an actions column with a delete icon
    - a vertical icon button toolbar containing help and add buttons (JabRefIconView glyphs and tooltips)
  - Updated IDs and sizes for components (stringsList, labelColumn, contentColumn, actionsColumn, addStringButton).

- View (BibtexStringEditorDialogView.java)
  - Wiring for new table columns and actions column using ValueTableCellFactory to show a delete icon with tooltip and click handler.
  - Inline editing support for label and content columns, including commit handlers.
  - Duplicate-label prevention: if a label already exists, show an error dialog and revert to the old value.
  - After adding a new string, start editing the new label cell automatically.
  - Removed ControlsFxVisualizer usage and related visualizer code.
  - Adjusted method signatures (addString(), openHelp(), removeString(item)).

- ViewModel (BibtexStringEditorDialogViewModel.java)
  - Replaced old view-model type with a ListProperty of BibtexStringEditorItemModel.
  - addNewString now creates a unique placeholder label ('NewString', 'NewString1', ...) and adds it to the list.
  - removeString accepts the item to remove.
  - save() now persists the current listProperty to the database.
  - Added labelAlreadyExists(String) helper and exposed stringsListProperty() and validProperty().

- Item model (BibtexStringEditorItemModel.java)
  - Renamed from BibtexStringViewModel to BibtexStringEditorItemModel and adjusted validators to reference the new class.

- Cell factories and helpers
  - ViewModelTextFieldTableCellVisualizationFactory: rewritten to remove ControlsFxVisualizer, add proper tooltip handling, manage pseudo-class subscriptions, and focus/select the TextField when editing starts (also handles graphic+TextField HBox case).
  - ViewModelListCellFactory: ensure pseudo-class state is reset on empty and manage subscriptions consistently.

- CSS
  - Moved invalid background styling into Base.css for .table-cell:invalid and .list-cell:invalid to centralize the look-and-feel and removed the duplicate rule from EntryEditor.css.

- i18n
  - Adjusted localization keys: changed "Remove selected strings" → "Remove string %0" and removed duplicate keys. Note: translators may need to update translations for the new key and the parameterized message.

Why
- Provide a more compact and modern editor layout with streamlined actions (icon buttons).
- Improve inline validation UX by showing tooltips and visually marking invalid cells consistently via CSS pseudo-classes.
- Simplify and decouple visualization logic by removing the external ControlsFxVisualizer dependency and implementing lightweight in-place visualization and pseudo-class handling.

Migration notes / potential impacts
- The view-model class was renamed from BibtexStringViewModel to BibtexStringEditorItemModel; any external references to the old class will need updating.
- The i18n key for removing strings changed; update translations if necessary.
- removeString now takes an item parameter; callers of the old no-arg removeString must be updated.
- Validation visualization no longer uses ControlsFxVisualizer; if custom visualizer behavior was expected elsewhere, review cell factories.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/metadata: BibtexStringEditorDialog.fxml, BibtexStringEditorDialogView.java, BibtexStringEditorDialogViewModel.java, BibtexStringEditorItemModel.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/util: ViewModelTextFieldTableCellVisualizationFactory.java, ViewModelListCellFactory.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui: Base.css, EntryEditor.css
- src/main/resources/l10n/JabRef_en.properties

Tests and follow-ups
- Ensure translations are updated for the new i18n key.
- Consider adding unit/UI tests for duplicate-label prevention and for the add-new-entry auto-editing behavior.

Summary

This PR ensures exceptions thrown while generating an entry from an identifier are properly logged, fixes a couple of minor typos in user-facing messages, and updates the changelog.

What I changed

- Log the exception and its stacktrace in GenerateEntryFromIdAction using SLF4J (LOGGER.info(..., exception)). This makes debugging fetcher failures easier for developers and contributors.
- Reworked the error handling flow in GenerateEntryFromIdAction: build the localized message first, log the exception, then show the confirmation dialog to optionally add an entry manually.
- Fixed a typo in the server-side error message ("agan" -> "again") in two places:
  - EntryTypeViewModel.java (user dialog text)
  - JabRef_en.properties (localization key/value)
- Updated CHANGELOG.md with a short, user-friendly note about the exception logging fix.

Files modified

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/importer/GenerateEntryFromIdAction.java
  - Added SLF4J Logger and logging call
  - Simplified flow to collect msg, log exception, and then show confirmation dialog
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/EntryTypeViewModel.java
  - Fixed typo in server-side error dialog
- src/main/resources/l10n/JabRef_en.properties
  - Fixed typo in localized server-side error message
- CHANGELOG.md
  - Added an entry describing the exception logging fix

Motivation

Previously exceptions occurring during fetching by identifier were not logged properly, making it harder to investigate issues reported by users. Logging the exception (including stacktrace) improves observability and helps maintainers track down causes.

Tests and verification

- Changes that affect behavior were manually tested in a running JabRef instance.
- Localization strings were updated to correct the typo.
- CHANGELOG entry added to be understandable for the average user.

Related issue

Fixes: https://github.com/koppor/jabref/issues/627

text:
Update CHANGELOG.md with Unreleased section summarizing new features, improvements and fixes

Highlights:
- Added new settings and features: citation relations TTL (default 30 days), distribution of Linux arm64 images, warning when adding entries that already exist in an active library, and addition of `monthfiled` to default fields for BibTeX string resolution.
- New integrations and fetchers: ID-based EuropePMC fetcher, LOBID as an alternative ISBN fetcher, and an initial Cite-As-You-Write (CAYW) endpoint.
- New tooling and CLI improvements: introduction of the `jabkit` application (with a new `pseudonymize` command) and movement of several CLI verbs to the toolkit.
- LibreOffice/OpenOffice integration: more CSL bibliography header/body formats, ability to choose CSL body formats (hanging indent, first-line, etc.), improved performance and UI for the Select Style dialog, and other UX improvements.
- AI and PDF features: AI chat and summarization improvements, markdown rendering for AI responses, and document viewer enhancements (text selection, search/highlight, page rotation).
- Usability and workflow improvements: new “Add JabRef suggested groups” option, merged Create New Entry tool (merge of New Entry / Import by ID / New Entry from Plain Text), automatic detection of identifier types from clipboard, ‘Copy to’ success dialog, toggle for absolute/relative paths in library properties, auto-selection/pre-fill of identifier tab from clipboard, and improved file/path handling and multi-file imports.
- Background tasks and consistency checks: progress dialogs for consistency checks and CLI exit code behavior (non-zero on issues) to support CI usage.

Fixes and reliability:
- Numerous bug fixes across file linking, tooltips, entry editor behavior, importers/exporters, LibreOffice integration, citation/key generation, document viewer exceptions, and more to improve stability and reduce false positives in consistency checks.

Removals and breaking changes:
- Removed ability to change internal preference values, dropped support for MySQL/MariaDB and Oracle, and removed library migrations (users must use JabRef 6.0-alpha.1 to migrate).

Notes:
- This changelog entry aggregates many smaller UI, importer/exporter, and performance improvements; please review individual sections in CHANGELOG.md for a full list of changes and links to issues/PRs.

- CHANGELOG.md — added changelog entry for this fix

  - Introduces properties to represent the groups tree and selection: rootGroup, selectedGroups.

  - Subscribes to StateManager.activeDatabase to react to database switches and rebuild the groups root accordingly.
  - Propagates group selection changes back to StateManager so the main table updates with selected group(s).
  - Implements group CRUD operations and helpers:
    - addNewGroupToRoot / addNewSubgroup: open dialogs and add new groups, notify user and persist changes to MetaData

    - removeSubgroups / removeGroupKeepSubgroups / removeGroupAndSubgroups: remove groups/subgroups with confirmation and cleanup of explicit assignments when appropriate
    - addSelectedEntries / removeSelectedEntries: add/remove currently selected entries to/from a group
    - removeGroupsAndSubGroupsFromEntries: recursively remove explicit-group assignments from entries when groups are removed
    - sortAlphabeticallyRecursive: sort subtree alphabetically using a case-insensitive comparator
  - Ensures group changes are written back to the database MetaData (writeGroupChangesToMetaData) and notifies the user via DialogService
  - Notes/TODOs remain for undo support and better propagation/update mechanisms where applicable

  - Adds/ensures English messages used by the groups UI and GroupTreeViewModel are available (confirmation dialogs, notifications, error messages, filter/group labels, etc.)

  - Unreleased section contains recent notable changes (new fetcher entries and other items) — ensures these changes are tracked in the project changelog

- Centralize and encapsulate the group tree behaviour and its interaction with StateManager and the UI.
- Provide filtering support for the groups pane and ensure all group operations persist to the library metadata and notify users.

- Several TODOs in the view model point out missing undo support and the lack of a finer-grained update mechanism; these are left for a follow-up where undo/redo and more efficient updates will be added.

Summary:
Fixes a NullPointerException that occurred when using the middle mouse button (mouse wheel click) on Windows.

Problem:
On Windows, middle-click events could trigger a code path that assumed a non-null field/state and resulted in a NPE. This manifested whenever the user pressed the middle mouse button, causing the application to crash or behave unpredictably.

Root cause:
The event handling code did not properly account for the middle-button case on Windows. A missing null-check / improper branching allowed a null reference to be dereferenced when processing those events.

What I changed:
- Added a defensive null-check and explicit handling for middle-button (BUTTON2) mouse events.
- Normalized mouse button handling so Windows behaves the same as other platforms.
- Added unit/integration tests that reproduce the previously failing middle-click scenario and assert no exception is thrown.
- Updated a brief comment explaining the Windows-specific behavior and why the check is required.

Testing:
- Reproduced the original crash locally on Windows and verified it no longer occurs.
- Ran existing test suite and new tests; all pass.
- Manual smoke-tested mouse interactions on Windows and macOS to confirm consistent behavior.

Impact:
- Fixes a crash bug for Windows users when using the middle mouse button.
- No public API changes; backwards-compatible.

Notes:
If you still see issues with other mouse-related input after this change, please include platform and input-device details in the issue.

Summary: Remove support for Markdown strikethrough (~~text~~) and task list (- [ ] / - [x]) syntaxes from the Markdown parser and renderer.

What changed:
- The Markdown parsing rules that recognized and rendered strikethrough and task list syntaxes have been removed.
- Renderer behavior and tests/snapshots were updated to reflect the removal.
- Documentation and the changelog have been updated to call out the breaking change.

Why:
- Keep the Markdown implementation aligned with a stricter subset of the spec and reduce ambiguity and implementation complexity.
- Avoid inconsistent rendering behavior across consumers and reduce surface area for edge cases.

Impact and migration notes:
- Existing content that relied on "~~text~~" or "- [ ] / - [x]" will now display the raw Markdown characters instead of rendered strike or task list elements. This is a breaking change for authors who used those syntaxes.
- Recommended migrations:
  - Replace strikethrough with HTML tags such as <del> or <s> where appropriate.
  - Replace task lists with native UI task widgets if the platform provides them, or convert to plain lists with explicit indicators (e.g., ✓ / ☐ or emoji), or transform content via a one-time automated search-and-replace.
- Update any content-generation scripts, templates, or importers that produced these Markdown constructs.

Testing and release:
- Unit and integration tests updated to remove expectations for these renderings.
- Add a prominent note in the release notes and docs, and notify users/teams so they can update content before upgrading.

Summary

- Adds UI and background support for copying linked files of selected entries to a user-chosen folder.
- Enhances paste-from-clipboard between libraries to also copy associated PDF files from the source library into the current library's file directory when possible.

What I changed

1) New copy-files feature
- Introduced CopyFilesAction (command) that: prompts for an export directory, creates and runs a CopyFilesTask, and shows a results dialog on completion.
- Added CopyFilesTask (background Task) that copies all linked files for the provided entries to the chosen directory, writes a timestamped log file (copyFileslog_yyyy-MM-dd-HH-mm-ss.log) to the export folder, updates each LinkedFile link to the new location on success, and returns result view models for the UI.
- Added CopyFilesDialogView to display results (file, status icon and message) after the background task finishes. Success and errors are shown using green/red icons and localized messages.
- The CopyFilesAction shows a progress dialog while the CopyFilesTask runs and notifies the user if no linked files were found.

2) Paste entries: copy PDFs from source library
- Extended LibraryTab.pasteEntry() so that when entries are pasted from another library (copied via copyEntry), JabRef attempts to find PDF files referenced by those entries in the source library's default file directory and copy them into the target library's default file directory.
- For each pasted entry, the code iterates its LinkedFile list and for files of type "pdf" will try to locate the file in the source library folder. If found, it copies the file (REPLACE_EXISTING) into the current library's default file directory.
- Logs warnings when the source PDF cannot be found and logs errors if copy fails.
- After (attempted) file copies, entries are imported into the current library using importHandler.importEntriesWithDuplicateCheck(...).

3) Utilities and behaviour
- Reuses FileUtil.copyFile and FileUtil.find utilities for file operations and path resolution.
- The implementation prefers the default file directory metadata from BibDatabaseContext for source/target resolving.
- Progress, success and failure messages are localized.

Notes and considerations

- CopyFilesTask writes a per-operation log into the export directory documenting copied or failed files.
- The paste behavior only attempts to copy files of type "pdf" and only if the clipboard originated from another library (copiedBibDatabaseContext is set by copyEntry).
- Error conditions (missing source path, IO errors) are logged and surfaced where appropriate via dialogService notifications.

- Modified: src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/LibraryTab.java (pasteEntry and copyEntry integration)
- Reuses existing FileUtil (src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/util/io/FileUtil.java)

This change makes it easy to export linked files for a selection of entries and to reliably copy associated PDFs when moving entries between libraries via copy/paste.

Add ImportHandler to manage importing of external files, pasted strings, and BibTeX data into a BibDatabaseContext.

Key features:
- importFilesInBackground(List<Path>) runs imports in a BackgroundTask, reports progress/messages to the UI, and integrates with Undo via UndoableInsertEntries.
- Supports importing PDFs (extracts metadata via ExternalFilesContentImporter and links the original file), .bib files (parses entries), and other files (creates an empty entry with a file link).
- Relativizes file paths against database file directories using file preferences.
- importEntries/importCleanedEntries: performs ImportCleanup, inserts entries into the database, generates citation keys (configurable), applies automatic fields, and adds entries to currently selected groups.
- Duplicate handling: import entries with duplicate checks using DuplicateCheck and DuplicateResolverDialog, with support for user decision persistence (apply-to-all option). Exposes cleanUpEntry as @VisibleForTesting.
- Clipboard/string import: handleStringData recognizes DOI, arXiv, and ISBN identifiers and uses respective fetchers (DoiFetcher, ArXivFetcher, IsbnFetcher); falls back to ImportFormatReader for unknown formats.
- handleBibTeXData: parses raw BibTeX text into entries and imports string constants with collision checks and user warnings.
- downloadLinkedFiles: optionally downloads online linked files after import based on file preferences.

Notes and implementation details:
- Uses ExternalFilesEntryLinker to attach files to entries.
- Uses preferences services throughout for import, file, citation key, owner/timestamp and merge dialog configuration.
- Error handling logs exceptions and notifies the user for import errors and warnings.
- addToGroups currently applies group entry changes but contains a TODO to add undo support for group modifications.

This addition centralizes import logic (file, string, and BibTeX) and ties it into UI feedback, preferences, duplicate resolution, and undo support.

Closes #3590

Summary

This PR changes the Recent Files feature so that file paths stored for entries inside the current project are saved as project-relative paths instead of absolute paths. This makes the Recent Files list resilient to moving the project folder or sharing the project across machines, since entries will be resolved relative to the current project location.

What changed

- When adding a file from a project to the Recent Files list, the path is converted to a relative path with respect to the project root (if the file is inside the project). Files outside the project remain stored as absolute paths.
- When opening a recent entry, relative paths are resolved against the current project folder so the file can be found after the project is moved.

Why

Absolute paths break if a project folder is moved or opened on another machine. Converting to project-relative paths improves portability and consistency for users working across different environments.

How to test

1. Open JabRef.
2. Open any .bib file that is located inside a project folder.
3. Close JabRef and reopen it.
4. Move the entire project folder to a different location (or open it on another machine with a different absolute path).
5. Open JabRef again and check the Recent files list — the .bib file should resolve and open correctly using the relative path.

- I manually tested the change in a running JabRef instance.

Summary: Fixes a bug where the 'Open Terminal' action on Linux did not honor the requested working directory for two of the three supported terminal implementations. Users previously saw terminals open in the home directory instead of the target folder.

Root cause: Two terminal launch implementations were building their argument lists incorrectly (wrong flag/argument placement and insufficient quoting), so the working-directory/path argument was ignored by the terminal process.

What I changed:
- Corrected the argument construction for the two affected Linux terminal launchers so the working-directory/path is passed using the terminal's supported flags/options (and properly quoted).
- Consolidated and clarified the launcher logic so all three supported terminals share the same path-sanitization and fallback behavior.
- Added unit tests and manual verification steps to ensure the terminal opens in the expected folder across tested terminals.

Testing: Unit tests added to cover argument construction; manual verification performed on the three common terminal types (GNOME Terminal, Konsole, XTerm) to ensure the terminal now opens in the selected folder.

Notes: No user-facing API changes. This should resolve reported issues where terminals opened in the home directory instead of the project/folder path.

Summary

This PR adds a new integrity check that detects unescaped ampersands (&) in BibTeX/BibLaTeX entry fields and reports them in the Integrity Check view. It implements counting of ampersands preceded by an even number of backslashes (i.e. not properly escaped), and reports the number found per field.

What changed

- Added AmpersandChecker (src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/integrity/AmpersandChecker.java) implementing EntryChecker. It matches ampersands and treats those preceded by an even number of backslashes as unescaped.
- Registered the new checker in the IntegrityCheck list (src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/integrity/IntegrityCheck.java).
- Added localization entries for the integrity message in English and German (src/main/resources/l10n/JabRef_en.properties, JabRef_de.properties).
- Added unit tests for the checker covering accepted and rejected inputs and several backslash/ampersand combinations (src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/integrity/AmpersandCheckerTest.java).
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to mention the new integrity check.

Behavior notes

- The message shown is: "Found %0 unescaped '&'" (localized), where %0 is the count of unescaped ampersands found in a field. Tests rely on this message text, so change it consistently if needed.

Issues fixed

- Fixes #8948
- Fixes https://github.com/koppor/jabref/issues/585

Tests

- Unit tests added to validate correct detection of escaped and unescaped ampersands, including complex combinations of multiple backslashes.

Developer notes

- The checker iterates over all fields in an entry and adds an IntegrityMessage per field if unescaped ampersands are found.
- The detection logic counts backslashes directly preceding an ampersand and treats an ampersand as unescaped when that count is even.

Fixes #8747 — Prevent uncaught exception when editing the "date" field in biblatex library mode

Short summary
- Fixes a NullPointerException that occurred when editing an entry's date field with invalid input and then clicking away (library mode: biblatex).
- Adds validation and more tolerant parsing so invalid input no longer throws and the UI shows the validation state (warning icon) instead of crashing.

What was wrong
- Invalid date input triggered code paths that assumed a non-null TemporalAccessor and caused an uncaught NPE when focus was lost.
- Parsing fallback only caught DateTimeParseException in some places and did not always handle blank input or other parse errors.

What I changed
- DateEditor
  - Inject PreferencesService and wire an EditorValidator to show validation feedback for the date editor instead of letting an exception propagate.
- FieldEditors
  - Pass PreferencesService when creating DateEditor instances so the validator can be configured.
- DateEditorViewModel
  - Broadened the catch in fromString to catch all Exceptions so the Date.parse(...) fallback is used more reliably.
- TemporalAccessorPicker
  - Handle null TemporalAccessor in getLocalDate() to avoid NPE.
  - Make the string converter tolerant: blank input returns null; parse exceptions fall back to Date.parse(...).
  - Keep original editor text when the value is invalid (prevents clearing the text when clicking away).
- CHANGELOG.md
  - Added a changelog entry describing the bug fix for users.

Files changed
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/DateEditor.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/DateEditorViewModel.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/FieldEditors.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/util/component/TemporalAccessorPicker.java
- CHANGELOG.md

Testing / verification
- Manually tested UI behavior: typing invalid dates now shows the validation icon and does not throw on focus loss; pressing Enter still commits/clears as before. Screenshots/GIFs demonstrating before/after behavior were included in the issue description.

Notes
- This is a behavioral/robustness fix; no public API changes. The changes make parsing more tolerant and add validation feedback to avoid silent crashes.

Summary

- Improved GroupTreeView UX and behavior for drag & drop, searching and rendering of group hit counts.

What changed

- Drag & Drop
  - Implemented smooth auto-scrolling while dragging (periodic scroll timer) so long drag operations near the top/bottom scroll the tree automatically.
  - Added drag-to-expand behavior with a delay (1s) so hovering on a node while dragging expands/collapses it reliably (DragExpansionHandler).
  - Improved drag visual feedback and dropping handling, including support for moving group nodes and dropping BibEntries from the local dragboard.

- Search / Filter
  - Debounced filter execution (400 ms) for the groups search field to avoid running expensive searches on each keystroke.
  - Added a clear button to the search field using ControlsFX’ TextFields.setupClearButtonField via reflective access (with fallback logging).

- Group hit counts & layout
  - Display hit counts with compact formatting (e.g. 1.2k, 2.3m) and show exact value in a tooltip.
  - Adaptive font-size for the hit-count text to avoid layout issues on large font sizes (fix for issue that cut off group counts).
  - Added pseudo-class handling for selected/partially-selected group count styling.

- Selection and tree behavior
  - Bidirectional binding between the TreeTableView selection and the ViewModel selection with helpers for keeping both sides in sync.
  - Selecting a group from the ViewModel optionally expands parents so the selected node becomes visible.
  - Removed default disclosure node to use a dedicated expansion column (custom arrow cell) and prevent default disclosure behaviour interfering with custom UI.

- Context menu
  - Context menu construction improved and menu item icons removed for a cleaner appearance.

Other

- Minor refactors and helper additions (e.g. getFormattedNumber, setupClearButtonField reflective helper, drag handlers).
- Added logging for search execution and for failure to setup the clear button.

Why

These changes make group management smoother and more responsive, especially when working with large or deeply nested group trees and during drag-and-drop operations. The debounced search reduces UI lag, the auto-scrolling and drag-to-expand behaviors improve drag usability, and the hit-count formatting and adaptive sizing improve the visual stability of the groups panel.

This PR introduces JUnit 5 tests for several formatter classes in jablib:

- RemoveHyphenatedNewlinesFormatterTest
  - Verifies removal of hyphens that precede various newline sequences (\n, \r\n, \r).
  - Checks handling of platform-specific newline insertion.
  - Ensures strings without hyphenation remain unchanged.

- TrimWhitespaceFormatterTest
  - Parameterized tests that ensure trimming of a wide range of blank characters: horizontal tabs, line feeds, form feeds, carriage returns, spaces, and combinations thereof.

- UnicodeConverterTest (UnicodeToLatexFormatter)
  - Tests conversion of combining accents and plain Unicode characters to LaTeX equivalents.
  - Includes combined-accent cases and standalone characters (e.g. umlauted letters and Greek letters).

- UnitsToLatexFormatterTest
  - Verifies unit formatting rules (non-breaking space/grouping and proper handling of minus signs in unit strings).
  - Checks example input is formatted as expected.

All tests use parameterized cases where appropriate to cover multiple inputs succinctly.

Summary: Throw a specific BibEntryNotFound exception when a requested bibliography entry is no longer present.

What I changed:
- Replace previous behavior (silently returning null / throwing a generic exception) with a dedicated BibEntryNotFound exception when code attempts to access an entry that does not exist anymore.
- Ensure the exception is thrown at the point of retrieval/lookup so callers can handle the missing-entry case explicitly.

Why:
- Makes error handling clearer and more reliable for callers that need to react to removed or missing bibliography entries.
- Improves debugging by providing a clear, typed signal that the failure is due to a missing BibEntry rather than some other error.

Tests:
- Added unit tests to verify the BibEntryNotFound exception is thrown when attempting to retrieve a non-existent entry.

Notes:
- This is a behavior change for callers that previously relied on null or generic errors. Callers should catch BibEntryNotFound where appropriate or adjust logic to account for the explicit exception.
- No other functional changes to entry retrieval logic were made.

Fix Linux terminal working directory argument handling

This change fixes a bug where the working-directory argument passed to Linux terminal emulators was malformed (including an extra '=' as a separate argument) and therefore ignored, causing the terminal to open in the wrong directory. Adjustments made:

- gnome-terminal: use "--working-directory" as a separate argument with the path following it.
- xfce4-terminal: pass "--working-directory=<directory>" as a single argument (xfce4 requires the "=" form).
- konsole: use "--workdir" as a separate argument with the path following it.
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to include the bugfix entry.

Files changed: src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/desktop/os/Linux.java, CHANGELOG.md

Fixes: #9953 (https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/9953).

- Adds a new scheduled workflow (.github/workflows/check-links.yaml) that runs markdown-link-check on the documentation once a month (cron: "0 9 1 * *"). The job prepares docs by copying CHANGELOG.md and README.md to docs/ROOT before running.
- Removes the markdown-link-check steps from the main tests workflow (.github/workflows/tests.yml) to avoid running external link checks on every CI run.
- Adds an ADR (docs/adr/0011-test-external-links-in-documentation.md) documenting the decision to check external links monthly, the alternatives considered, and the rationale.

Why:
To reduce CI noise and avoid failing PRs because of flaky external sites while still providing automatic notification of broken documentation links. This implements the decision discussed in issue #6677.

Notes:
- The check uses mlc_config.json and runs against the docs/ folder.
- Some external sites (e.g. github.com) may need to be disabled or filtered due to 403/forbidden responses; this limitation is documented in the ADR.

text:
Fixes Issue #12585 — Remove duplicate associations when merging groups or keywords.

Summary:
- Previously, merging two groups or keywords could create duplicate join/association records if both source and target shared the same related entities (e.g., users, items, tags). This PR ensures duplicates are removed and associations are consolidated during merges.

What I changed:
- Updated merge logic for Group and Keyword models (Group#merge_with, Keyword#merge_with):
  - Reassigns all associations from the source to the target using a deduplicated set/SQL distinct operation before creating join records.
  - Deletes the source record after reassigning associations.
  - Removes any duplicate join records that may exist (safe-guard for pre-existing duplicates).
  - Wraps the operation in a transaction to ensure atomicity.
- Updated counter caches/metadata updates so counts are consistent after merge.
- Added reindexing hooks where applicable so search/index state remains correct after merges.

Tests:
- Added unit tests covering:
  - Merging two groups/keywords with overlapping associations results in no duplicate associations on the target.
  - Counts and caches are correct after merge.
  - Behavior when source has unique associations, or when source has none.
- Added integration test demonstrating a real-world merge scenario and verifying related records are deduplicated.

Backward compatibility / migration:
- No DB schema changes or migrations required. Behavior is an internal fix to merge operations and is backward compatible.

Manual testing steps:
1. Create two groups/keywords A and B that share some related entities.
2. Trigger A.merge_with(B) (or the inverse depending on API) or use the merge endpoint.
3. Verify the target contains all unique associated entities and there are no duplicate join records.
4. Verify counts/caches and search/index state are updated.

Notes:
- The merge remains destructive to the source (source is deleted) — this is unchanged behavior.
- If there are any custom association types, confirm they are covered by the same deduplication logic; extend tests if needed.

Fixes: #12585

Summary:
Adds a new Wiley TDM fetcher and updates the fulltext fetching pipeline to better support TDM-enabled Wiley content and improve overall reliability of fulltext retrieval.

What this change does:
- Introduces a new fetcher module for Wiley TDM (wiley_tdm_fetcher) that implements the Wiley Text and Data Mining API flow for authorized fulltext access.
- Updates the central fulltext fetching logic to: use a unified interface for provider-specific fetchers, perform better content negotiation (PDF/HTML), handle HTTP retries and exponential backoff, and provide clearer error classification (transient vs permanent).
- Adds support for configurable Wiley credentials/API key (environment/config variable WILEY_TDM_KEY) and optional tenant/config values required by the Wiley TDM API.
- Improves logging and metrics around fetch attempts, failures, and content-type detection to aid debugging and monitoring.

Compatibility & Migration:
- Backwards compatible: existing fetchers continue to work. To enable Wiley TDM fetching, set the new WILEY_TDM_KEY (or the configured credential name) in your environment/config.
- No database migrations required.

Tests & Docs:
- Unit tests and mocked integration tests added for the new Wiley fetcher and the updated fulltext fetching flow.
- Documentation updated with configuration instructions and an example of enabling Wiley TDM access.

Notes:
- Future follow-ups may include rate-limiting per-tenant controls and richer handling for mixed HTML/PDF deliveries by Wiley.

Summary:
Fixes a bug that prevented new entries from being inserted. The PR corrects the insertion flow so that newly created records are saved reliably and consistently.

Problem:
- New entries submitted through the create flow were not being persisted. This was caused by an incorrect control flow and timing issue around the create vs update path (the code was treating new items as existing and skipping the insert).

What I changed:
- Reworked the create/insert logic so the code clearly distinguishes between creating a new entry and updating an existing one.
- Fixed the condition that detects whether an entry is new (now uses presence/absence of id and/or explicit create flag rather than a brittle truthy check).
- Ensured the database insert call is awaited and any transactions/commits complete before returning success.
- Added validation earlier in the flow and moved side-effects (like emitting events) after persistence to avoid inconsistent state on failures.

Tests and verification:
- Added unit/integration tests covering: successful creation, failure on invalid data, and duplicate-id protection.
- Manual test steps included: create a new entry from the UI, verify it appears in the list and in the DB; create with invalid data to confirm validation prevents insertion.

Backward compatibility / migration:
- No data migrations required. Existing update flows remain unchanged.

Notes:
- This should resolve reported failures when creating new entries. If you see related edge cases (concurrent creates with client-generated ids), we may want to add server-side id generation or stronger uniqueness handling in a follow-up.

Closes: fixes insertion failures reported in the create flow.

Add "Regenerate" functionality to AI chat

This PR introduces a "Regenerate" button to the AI chat prompt and wires up the logic to re-run the last user prompt so the language model can produce an alternative response.

Key changes
- UI: Added a Regenerate button to the chat prompt FXML (ChatPromptComponent.fxml).
- Chat prompt: Exposed a regenerate callback and hook in ChatPromptComponent (regenerate button and onRegenerateMessage handler).
- Chat logic: Implemented regenerate behavior in AiChatComponent. When invoked the component:
  - finds the last user message in the chat history,
  - removes assistant messages generated after that prompt (so the history contains the last user prompt as the most recent user message),
  - re-sends the last user prompt (onSendMessage) and restores the prompt state.
- Minor UI/UX: loading state is set during regeneration; error/retry/cancel handling is preserved.
- Changelog: documented the new "Regenerate" button under Unreleased -> Added.

Behavior notes
- Regenerate uses the last user message from the chat history; if none exist, nothing happens.
- The chat history is trimmed (assistant responses after the last user prompt are removed) before re-sending to ensure the model reformulates the response to the same prompt.
- Existing retry/cancel flows remain unchanged.

- Added unit and integration tests to cover saving, loading, and common failure modes.

Impact
- Personal journal list updates now persist as expected across reloads and device restarts.
- No database migrations are required.

- Focus on the storage adapter changes and the save invocation in the journal-list component.
- Tests demonstrating the previous failing behavior are included to validate the fix.

Add FileFilterConverter utility and update resources

- Introduces org.jabref.gui.util.FileFilterConverter
  - Provides conversions between JabRef FileType / FileChooser.ExtensionFilter and Java file filters (java.io.FileFilter and DirectoryStream.Filter<Path>).
  - Adds ANY_FILE constant for a generic file filter.
  - Methods include: toExtensionFilter(FileType), toExtensionFilter(description, FileType), importer/exporter <-> ExtensionFilter helpers, forAllImporters(), importerToExtensionFilter(), exporterToExtensionFilter(), toFileFilter(List<String>) and toDirFilter(List<String>). 
  - Cleans and normalizes extension strings, handles empty extension lists (accept all files), and catches IOExceptions when evaluating java.io.FileFilter to avoid bubbling errors.
  - Enables mapping ExtensionFilter descriptions back to Importer/Exporter instances.

- Updates resources
  - Includes changes to English localization (src/main/resources/l10n/JabRef_en.properties).
  - Updates CHANGELOG.md (Unreleased) to reflect recent additions/changes.

Why

These utilities centralize and standardize creation and conversion of file filters across the UI and backend, improve robustness when dealing with extension lists and file-system checks, and make it easier to present consistent Open/Save/Import dialog filters that map cleanly to JabRef importers/exporters.

text:
Fixes #8390

Summary

This PR fixes a bug where attempting to remove several selected groups only deleted one group. The removal routine now properly iterates over all selected groups, prompts a single confirmation dialog for the full selection (or for a single group when only one is selected), and deletes all confirmed groups.

What I changed

- When removeGroupAndSubgroups() is called, iterate through all selected groups instead of only the group that triggered the event handler.
- Show a confirmation dialog that adapts to single-group or multiple-group deletion.
- Copy the selectedGroups (ListProperty<GroupNodeViewModel>) into a new array before iterating to avoid the known issue where forEach skips elements when previous elements are removed.

Behavioral notes

- Single group deletion: shows the regular single-group confirmation and deletes that group.
- Multiple groups deletion: shows a single confirmation mentioning multiple groups and deletes all selected groups when confirmed.

Testing

- Manually tested the changed features in a running JabRef instance.
- Screenshots demonstrating single- and multiple-group deletion flows are included in the PR description.

Files and checklist

- No automated tests added.
- CHANGELOG/documentation not updated in this PR.
- Manual testing and screenshots included.

text:
Add GroupNodeViewModel: a view-model representing a group node in the groups tree UI. This class encapsulates presentation and behavior for a GroupTreeNode, including:

- Construction from a GroupTreeNode or AbstractGroup, and a factory method for the "All entries" group.
- Display name conversion using LatexToUnicodeFormatter and handling of AutomaticGroup: automatically creates and sorts subgroup view models when appropriate.
- Children management via an ObservableList and hasChildren binding; retains reference to the database entries list to avoid weak-listener GC issues.
- Expansion state binding that persists back to the underlying group model.
- Hit-count calculation performed asynchronously via BackgroundTask and TaskExecutor, and change throttling using a DelayTaskThrottler to limit recalculation frequency when the database changes.
- Bindings to reflect whether any or all selected entries match the group (using EasyBind and BindingsHelper).
- Icon handling: parsing material design icon names (case-insensitive) and falling back to a default colored group icon based on group color or theme default.
- Drag-and-drop support via acceptableDrop(), draggedOn(), moveTo() and helpers for dropping entries or groups; checks for GroupEntryChanger when accepting entry drops.
- Group modification helpers: addEntriesToGroup(), addSubgroup(), moveTo(), getChildByPath(), getParent(), toggleExpansion(), matches-for-search.
- Proper equals(), hashCode(), and toString() implementations based on the underlying GroupTreeNode.

Other details and safeguards included:
- Comments indicating TODOs for undo/notifications and warning about assignment side effects.
- Use of JavaFX properties (SimpleIntegerProperty, SimpleBooleanProperty, BooleanBinding) to support UI bindings.

This change centralizes group node UI logic into a single view-model class, enabling asynchronous hit counting, reactive UI updates on selection/database changes, and drag-and-drop group manipulation.

  - Improved handling of entry change state and lifecycle in the collaboration UI. Fixed potential null-pointer scenarios and made the view model more robust when entries are added/removed/updated.

  - Refactored dialog behavior and UI logic for resolving duplicates. Improved user interaction flow and stabilized state updates when resolving or skipping duplicate entries.

These changes increase the stability and user-friendliness of workflows that involve collaboration edits, importing external files, deduplication and entry merging, and automatic citation key creation. text:
Add support for creating a new SLR study and ensure the study definition is committed correctly, plus several GitHandler enhancements.

What this change does:
- StartNewStudyAction: implement starting a new study by showing the metadata dialog, writing the study YAML into the repository, initializing the Git repository if needed, and amending the initial commit so the created YAML is included in the initial commit.
- GitHandler: broadened git utility capabilities and robustness:
  - initIfNeeded now initializes a repository with initial branch main, creates .gitignore, and falls back to creating an empty initial commit when needed.
  - createCommitOnCurrentBranch supports amending the last commit and handles non-clean and merging repository states.
  - Added credential resolution (environment fallback and explicit setter), push/pull/fetch helpers, and checks for remote configuration.
  - Added repository discovery helpers findRepositoryRoot and fromAnyPath.
  - Added semantic merge utilities: beginOursMergeNoCommit, fastForwardTo, abortSemanticMerge, and a MergeGuard RAII helper to safely finalize or rollback a pre-commit merge state for targeted file operations.

Why:
- Ensure that when users create a new study through the UI, the generated study definition file is reliably part of the repository history (amended into the initial commit).
- Provide safer and more flexible git operations required by the SLR workflow, including support for credentialed remotes, fetching/pushing, and guarded semantic merges to avoid leaving repositories in an inconsistent state.

Notes:
- The GitHandler credential resolution currently supports environment variables as a fallback and an explicit setCredentials method; this is intended to be replaced by a preferences-backed approach later.
- Error handling logs failures and surfaces credential errors when required by remote operations.

text:
Add PDF fulltext indexing and search infrastructure

Summary
- Implement PdfIndexer: uses Apache Lucene (NIOFSDirectory) and an English stem analyzer to create, update and flush a fulltext index for PDF files linked to BibTeX entries. It resolves linked files, skips online/non-PDF links, checks file modification time against indexed documents, and writes PDF text/metadata into the index via DocumentReader.
- Add IndexingTaskManager: a BackgroundTask-based queue that executes indexing operations in the background via a TaskExecutor. It enqueues create/add/remove operations, manages task execution state, and updates user-facing progress and title properties.
- Add RebuildFulltextSearchIndexAction: UI action that asks the user for confirmation, notifies the user, and triggers index creation and population for the current library using the IndexingTaskManager on a background executor.
- Add/extend localization keys (JabRef_en.properties) for user-visible messages related to rebuilding/rebuilding progress and error notifications.
- Provide comprehensive unit tests:
  - PdfIndexerTest: verifies indexing behavior (indexing PDFs, skipping non-PDFs and online links, indexing with/without citation keys, metadata handling and flush behavior).
  - PdfSearcherTest: verifies search functionality and edge cases (search results for words, stop words, empty/null queries, and invalid limits).

Error handling & logging
- Index and IO operations are guarded with try/catch blocks; failures are logged and the user is notified via DialogService notifications when rebuild fails.

Why
- Enables reliably indexing and searching the full text of linked PDF files in the background, improving search capabilities and user experience without blocking the UI.

Notes
- PdfIndexer uses the database context to obtain the index path and file resolution; IndexingTaskManager ensures indexing work runs off the JavaFX thread and reports progress to the UI.

text:
Add clipboard and selection support to preview viewer

This PR enhances the PreviewViewer by adding clipboard operations and improving link handling and error reporting:

- Implemented methods to copy the generated preview to the clipboard in multiple formats:
  - copyPreviewHtmlToClipBoard(): copies the generated HTML preview (pasteable as rich text/HTML).
  - copyPreviewPlainTextToClipBoard(): copies the plain-text representation of the preview (uses document.body.innerText).
  - copySelectionToClipBoard(): copies the current text selection from the preview in both plain text and HTML formats (uses JS to get the selection text and HTML snippet).
  - getSelectionHtmlContent(): exposes execution of a JS helper for extracting the selected HTML fragment.
- Added a JS snippet (JS_GET_SELECTION_HTML_SCRIPT) to reliably extract selected HTML from the WebView.
- Ensured all clipboard interactions use ClipBoardManager and ClipboardContent to put the appropriate payloads on the system clipboard.
- Improved anchor handling inside the WebView so that clicks open externally via NativeDesktop.openBrowser, with robust error logging for malformed or failing URLs.
- Strengthened printing error handling: when no PrinterJob is available a localized error dialog is shown; printing is performed as a BackgroundTask and errors are displayed via the DialogService.
- Preserved UI responsiveness and threading safety by using BackgroundTask and UiTaskExecutor where appropriate.

Why

These changes allow users to copy preview content (full preview or selections) conveniently in both rich (HTML) and plain formats, improving interoperability with external editors and workflows. External links in the preview are now opened using the native browser instead of inside the embedded WebView.

Notes for reviewers

- ClipboardContentGenerator.processHtml(...) is used to produce HTML clipboard payloads; ensure the HTML/clipboard integration works across platforms.
- The implementation relies on WebView JavaScript execution; verify selection copying behaves correctly for complex previews and across different styles/themes.
- The new behavior for anchor click handling prevents default navigation in the WebView and delegates opening to the OS.

Tests performed

- Manual testing of copying full preview (HTML and plain text) to clipboard and pasting into rich-text and plain-text targets.
- Manual testing of copying a selection (text + HTML) from the preview.
- Manual testing of opening links from the preview and handling invalid URLs.
- Manual testing of printing with and without available printers; error dialogs and logging verified.

  - Validates ISBN, downloads the /bibtex page using Jsoup with the configured USER_AGENT, extracts the textarea content and uses BibtexParser.singleFromString to convert it into a BibEntry.
  - Handles IO and parse exceptions by wrapping them in FetcherException.
  - getURLForID returns null (not used because the identifier is posted/constructed differently).

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/IsbnFetcher.java
  - Updated to include OttoBib as the last fallback when ebook.de and chimbori do not return an entry.

- Tests
  - Added/updated tests under src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/* for IsbnViaOttoBibFetcher, IsbnViaChimboriFetcher, and IsbnViaEbookDeFetcher to assert expected behavior for short/long ISBNs, author formatting, and cases where one provider lacks an ISBN but others may have it.
  - WebFetchersTest updated to exclude the internal ISBN fetchers from the list of id-based fetchers exposed to the user.

Motivation
- Provide an additional ISBN lookup source (ottobib) to improve coverage when ebook.de and chimbori do not return a result.

Testing
- Unit tests exercise retrieval and parsing for each provider and validate that missing-but-valid ISBNs are handled gracefully (return Optional.empty()) when appropriate. Manual and CI test runs should confirm no regressions in existing fetchers.

Fix exception when abbreviating journals for multiple entries (#12634) and small changelog cleanup

What changed
- Fix: AbbreviateAction no longer uses a HeadlessExecutorService and Futures to run per-entry abbreviation callables concurrently. Instead, abbreviation is processed sequentially and the successful abbreviation count is computed directly. This avoids ExecutionException/InterruptedException handling and fixes the exception observed when running "Abbreviate journals" for multiple entries. (See issue #12634)
- Changelog: Added the new bugfix entry for the abbreviation exception and fixed punctuation for the deletion-cancellation message. (See issue #12645)
- Cleanup: Removed several unused imports related to concurrency and simplified the stateManager.ifPresent lambda usage.

Why
- The previous implementation collected Callables, executed them via HeadlessExecutorService and then inspected Future results, which led to error-prone exception handling and a reported crash when abbreviating multiple entries. The new approach is simpler, synchronous, and more robust while still executing inside the existing BackgroundTask/taskExecutor flow.

Notes
- BackgroundTask/taskExecutor usage is unchanged, so the UI remains responsive while the operation runs in the background.

Add External File Types preferences UI and view models

This change implements a complete UI for managing external file types in the preferences, including an editable table and a dialog for adding/editing entries.

Key additions and behavior:
- ExternalFileTypesTab.fxml: FXML layout for the preferences tab, showing a TableView with columns for icon, name, extension, MIME type, application and action columns (edit/delete). Also includes buttons to add a new file type and reset to defaults.
- ExternalFileTypesTab.java: Controller that wires up the table using ValueTableCellFactory to display icons/text and clickable edit/delete icons. It initializes the ExternalFileTypesTabViewModel and connects UI actions (add, reset) to view model methods.
- ExternalFileTypesTabViewModel.java: ViewModel for the tab that loads/saves external file types from FilePreferences, supports add, edit (shows dialog), remove, reset-to-defaults and sorts entries by name. Persists settings into FilePreferences using ExternalFileType conversions.
- ExternalFileTypeItemViewModel.java: Item view model wrapping ExternalFileType data (icon/name/extension/mime/application) and converting back to a CustomExternalFileType for persistence. Includes default constructor for creating a new entry.
- EditExternalFileTypeEntryDialog.fxml / EditExternalFileTypeEntryDialog.java / EditExternalFileTypeViewModel.java: A dialog and view model for editing an external file type. Fields include icon preview, name, extension, MIME type, and application selection with radio buttons (Default vs Custom) and a Browse button to pick an application. The view model:
  - Initializes fields from the item view model.
  - Handles trimming/removal of a leading dot from extensions when storing.
  - Stores application as empty when Default is selected or the application string is empty (representing using the system default).
  - Provides getIcon() for the dialog preview.
- Uses DialogService to show file chooser and custom dialog. Uses JabRefDesktop/NativeDesktop to set initial directory for the file chooser.

Other details:
- UI binds controls bidirectionally to ViewModel properties and disables the application text & browse button when Default is selected.
- Table uses constrained resize policy and sorting by name.

This implements the full UI/workflow for listing, adding, editing, deleting and persisting external file types in preferences, including input sanitization and default/custom application handling.

  - Adjusted the javax.websocket module mapping to use "javax.websocket.api" as the module name.

  - Replaced implementation("com.github.eclipse:lsp4j") with implementation("org.eclipse.lsp4j:org.eclipse.lsp4j") and added implementation("org.eclipse.lsp4j:org.eclipse.lsp4j.websocket").

  - Updated opens and requires to reference the module names "org.eclipse.lsp4j", "org.eclipse.lsp4j.jsonrpc" and "org.eclipse.lsp4j.websocket".

  - Replaced implementation("com.github.eclipse:lsp4j") with implementation("org.eclipse.lsp4j:org.eclipse.lsp4j").

text:
Summary

- Fixes a bug where arXiv imports sometimes downloaded an HTML page instead of the actual fulltext PDF (see CHANGELOG entry referencing #4913).

What changed

- URLDownload
  - Robust MIME detection: getMimeType() now returns Optional<String> and tries HEAD first, follows redirects manually for HEAD requests (to correctly detect content-type after redirects such as arXiv), falls back to GET and local URLConnection, and retries redirects up to MAX_RETRIES.
  - Unirest now configured once in a static initializer: followRedirects(true), enableCookieManagement(true), and a default User-Agent header.
  - Improved error handling in openConnection(): disconnects before following redirects by creating a new URLDownload, and simplifies throwing FetcherClientException vs FetcherServerException based on status code.
  - Utility methods refactored to use Optional where appropriate (inferFileTypeFromMimeType, isMimeType).
  - Small fixes and cleanups (typos, imports, logging messages).

- Tests
  - Added WireMock (wiremock-standalone) as a test dependency and updated tests to use a local WireMockServer for deterministic responses.
  - DownloadLinkedFileActionTest
    - Uses WireMock to stub HEAD/GET responses for HTML content to validate behavior when keeping or removing HTML links.
    - Cleaned up temp dir usage and file deletion (uses Path and Files.delete).
  - URLDownloadTest
    - Adjusted assertions to the new Optional getMimeType() API.
    - Added a redirectWorks test that verifies following redirects and downloading the final PDF using WireMock.

- Build / Changelog
  - build.gradle: added testImplementation 'org.wiremock:wiremock-standalone:3.3.1' (recommended workaround for WireMock issues).
  - CHANGELOG.md: added entry describing the arXiv HTML vs PDF fix.

Why

- The changes ensure we detect the real content type even when intermediate URLs redirect (arXiv commonly redirects to actual PDF locations), preventing HTML pages from being saved instead of PDFs.
- Tests were made deterministic and more robust by using WireMock, and the API change to Optional encourages explicit handling of missing MIME types.

Notes for reviewers

- getMimeType() signature changed to Optional<String> across URLDownload; callers have been updated in this PR but please check for any other usages in the codebase.
- The retry/redirect logic for HEAD is implemented manually because Unirest.followRedirects(true) doesn't work for HEAD in the used Unirest version.
- WireMock standalone was added to the test classpath to avoid runtime issues seen with other WireMock artifacts.

text:
Improve PdfContentImporter robustness and add unit tests

Summary:
- Harden PdfContentImporter against malformed or minimal PDF files and unexpected IO conditions.
- Add comprehensive unit tests in PdfContentImporterTest to verify behavior on normal PDFs, PDFs without metadata, and error conditions.

What changed:
- PdfContentImporter.java:
  - Added null and empty checks to avoid NullPointerExceptions when PDF metadata (e.g., Title, Author, XMP) is absent.
  - Improved exception handling to ensure InputStreams/resources are closed reliably and IO errors are handled gracefully.
  - Refactored parsing logic slightly for readability and to make behavior explicit when no content can be extracted.

- PdfContentImporterTest.java:
  - New/updated tests covering successful content extraction, PDFs without metadata, and handling of IO problems.
  - Ensures the importer returns expected Optional/empty results and does not throw on edge cases.

Why this change:
- Previously, importing certain PDFs could cause uncaught exceptions or leak resources. These changes make PDF import more reliable in real-world scenarios where PDF files may lack metadata or be partially malformed.

Notes:
- No public API changes; behavior is tightened and made safer.
- Tests added to prevent regressions and document expected behavior for edge cases.

text:
Fix issue #2811 — make BibTeX key generator use crossref information

Summary
- When generating BibTeX keys, missing/empty required fields are now resolved from crossreferenced parent entries (crossref) when available.

What changed
- BracketedPattern: all field lookups in label/bracket expansion now use resolved field access (respecting crossref and string resolution) by calling getResolvedFieldOrAlias and resolving via the database when provided. This ensures patterns like author, title, keywords, year, pages, etc. consider crossreferenced parent entries.
- BibEntry: added getResolvedKeywords(database) which parses keywords from a resolved keywords field; refactored getKeywords to reuse KeywordList.parse(Optional, delimiter).
- KeywordList: added parse(Optional<String>, Character) to parse Optional keyword strings conveniently.
- EntryEditor: avoid overwriting the cite key field when no cite key was generated (only update the entry field and undo stack if the entry actually has a cite key). This prevents inserting empty keys.
- Tests: expanded unit tests to cover crossref resolution in bibtex key generation and bracket expansion (many new tests in BibtexKeyPatternUtilTest, BracketedPatternTest, BibEntryTest, KeywordListTest).
- CHANGELOG updated to mention the fix.

Notes for reviewers
- The bibtexkey field itself is not inherited from the crossref parent (behavior unchanged) — only individual fields used for key pattern generation are resolved from the referenced entry.
- New methods are small and additive; behavior of existing APIs is preserved for callers that do not use the database-resolving label expansion.

Tests
- Added tests verifying author, shorttitle, keywords, university/department/school/institute handling for entries that only reference a parent via crossref.
- Added tests for KeywordList.parse(Optional) and for BibEntry getResolvedKeywords.

This implements the requested behavior so the key generator can produce meaningful keys for child entries that rely on parent entries for data.

- Add/adjust tests (DatabaseSearcherTest, DatabaseSearcherWithBibFilesTest) to reflect the new indexing flow and verify search behavior with the refactored indexers.

- Provides a clear, extensible contract for adding new indexers in the future.
- Separates concerns: index building logic is encapsulated in indexer implementations while LuceneManager handles Lucene resources and orchestration.
- Enables read-only linked-files indexing through a dedicated ReadOnlyLinkedFilesIndexer implementation.

Behavioral notes
- No intended UI changes. This is an internal refactor to improve maintainability and extensibility.

Summary

This PR introduces a database migration and accompanying code changes to replace the existing ambiguous/boolean button_review field with a meaningful, enumerated review state. The goal is to make the intent of stored button-review data explicit (instead of a single boolean or unclear values), backfill existing records with sensible values, and prepare the app to use the new enum going forward.

What changed

- DB migration: adds a new column (button_review_state) with an enumerated/string type representing meaningful states (e.g. "approved", "changes_requested", "no_response" / or similar values as defined in code).
- Data backfill: a safe data migration that maps legacy button_review values and related audit/activity fields to the new states. Backfill is deterministic and documented in the migration file.
- Application code: updates models, validations, serializers, and API responses to use the new button_review_state field instead of the old field.
- Tests: adds/updates unit and integration tests to cover the new field, the mapping/backfill logic, and API contract changes.
- Cleanup plan: keeps the legacy column untouched for now to make deployment safe; includes a follow-up migration to drop the old column once we confirm production data is healthy.

Backfill rules (high-level)

- If legacy indicators show a positive review action -> set state to "approved".
- If legacy indicators show a negative review action -> set state to "changes_requested".
- If there is no record of a review action -> set state to "no_response".

These rules are implemented in the migration script; specifics are documented in the migration header comments.

Deployment and rollback

- The migration is safe to run online: it adds a new column and performs a backfill without removing the legacy column.
- App code is backward-compatible for the duration of the migration window: reads will prefer the new field when present, and fall back to legacy values if needed.
- Rollback is possible by reverting this PR and running the reverse migration; the migration is marked reversible and the old column remains until the follow-up cleanup.

Notes

- Please review the migration mapping rules in the migration file for edge cases.
- Follow-up PR will remove the legacy column after we verify production migration results and metrics.
- Related ticket: Meaningful button review field migration (reference in repo tracker).

- Updated the UI update flow to correctly insert the new entry into the filtered result set and maintain a sensible selection state.

Tests and verification
- Added tests that cover adding an entry while a filter/search is active and assert the item appears in the visible list.
- Manual QA steps: enable a filter or search, create a new entry that matches the filter, confirm it appears without changing the filter.

Notes
- No breaking API changes. This improves UX by preventing newly created items from being hidden by active filters.

Summary

Adds a dedicated "Clear content" tab to the Automatic Field Editor with a viewmodel and undo/redo support.

What this PR does

- Adds a new "Clear content" tab that contains a dropdown to select which field to clear and a "Clear field content" button.
- Adds a "Show only set fields" checkbox to filter the dropdown to only fields that are set in the currently selected entries.
- Removes the old "Clear field content" button from the "Edit content" tab (function moved to the new tab).
- Implements clearing with Undo/Redo using NamedCompound + UndoableFieldChange so clears can be reverted via Ctrl+Z.
- Adds i18n keys for all new UI text.

Why

The new tab groups clearing functionality into a focused, discoverable place and improves UX by letting the user scope the dropdown to fields that are actually set in the selected entries. Adding undo support ensures changes are reversible.

How to test

1. Open or create a library with a few entries (fill fields like author, journal).
2. Select one or more entries.
3. Open Edit → Automatic field editor.
4. Switch to the "Clear content" tab.
5. Toggle the "Show only set fields" checkbox: the dropdown should shrink to only fields currently filled in the selected entries.
6. Select a field (e.g., author) and click "Clear field content": the field value should be removed from all selected entries.
