Summary:
Convert absolute file paths stored in the Recent Files list to relative paths when possible, improving portability across workspaces, repositories, and developer machines.

What this changes:
- When adding a file to Recent Files, if the file is inside the current workspace/repo root, store a relative path instead of an absolute path.
- When loading Recent Files, resolve relative entries against the current workspace/repo root to restore absolute paths for access and display.
- Preserve absolute paths as a fallback for files outside the workspace or when the workspace root is unavailable.
- Added a migration step that converts existing absolute Recent Files entries to relative paths where the workspace root can be determined.
- Updated UI display and sorting to handle relative paths consistently and show the resolved absolute path on hover or in details.

Edge cases and compatibility:
- If the workspace root changes or cannot be found, previously stored relative entries will be handled gracefully (attempt resolution; if it fails, show the stored form and allow the user to remove the entry).
- No breaking changes: absolute paths continue to work, and the migration runs safely at startup.
- Cross-platform path separators and symlink resolution are handled when resolving relative paths.

Tests and verification:
- Added unit tests for path conversion logic (relative<->absolute), migration, and fallback behavior.
- Added integration/manual tests for Windows, macOS, and Linux verifying Recent Files behavior across workspace moves and repo clones.

Notes:
- This improves experience when moving/duplicating repositories or sharing workspace settings between team members, while preserving access to files outside the workspace.
- If desired, follow-up work could add a toggle to prefer always-storing absolute paths or always-relative paths.

text:
Fix hierarchical keywords in Keywords editor (fixes #11390)

Summary
- Hierarchical keywords (e.g. "parent > node > child") were only showing the parent keyword in the entry editor's tags field. This PR fixes parsing and conversion so the full hierarchical chain is preserved and displayed.

What I changed
- KeywordsEditorViewModel
  - Made the StringConverter static and updated it to:
    - return keyword.toString() for display
    - parse input strings with Keyword.ofHierarchical(...) so hierarchical delimiters are preserved
- KeywordsEditor
  - Use the static converter for suggestions/new-item production
  - Minor listener/lambda cleanup (use underscores for unused params)
  - Ensure tag label graphics and drag/hover handlers use concise lambdas
- Keyword model
  - Added Keyword.ofHierarchical(String) to convert a raw hierarchical string into a Keyword
  - Adjusted Javadoc/comments around Keyword.of
- KeywordList
  - Use Keyword.ofHierarchical when parsing chains from a delimited string
- Tests
  - Added KeywordsEditorViewModelTest to ensure the StringConverter preserves hierarchical keywords
- Changelog
  - Added an entry describing the fix for hierarchical keywords in the entry editor

Why this fixes the bug
- Previously the converter created Keywords in a way that only exposed the parent node when rendered in the tags/tags-field. By explicitly parsing hierarchical strings into a Keyword chain (Keyword.ofHierarchical) and returning the Keyword's full string representation, the editor now preserves and displays the full hierarchy.

How to test manually
1. In the Entry editor source tab add a hierarchical keyword: "parent > node > child".
2. Open the General tab (or the keywords field UI). The keywords/tags field should show the full hierarchical keyword (not only the parent) and no exceptions should be thrown.

Notes
- This is a follow-up to #10910 and closes #11390.
- Minor non-functional cleanups to lambda parameters and listeners were included for clarity.

Summary:
This PR moves storage of proxy passwords and API keys to the native OS credential store (e.g. Windows Credential Manager, macOS Keychain, Linux Secret Service) instead of persisting them in the application settings files.

What this changes:
- Proxy passwords and API keys are now saved and retrieved from the OS credential store.
- Credentials are no longer written to the plain settings file, improving security/privacy.
- UI/behaviour remains the same for users, but credentials are persisted securely across restarts.

Related issues and PRs:
- Follow-up to #9652
- Fixes comment: https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/pull/9652#issuecomment-1477075479
- Fixes: https://github.com/JabRef/jabref-issue-melting-pot/issues/106
- Depends on: #10004

- Tests added for the changes ✅
- Manually tested in running JabRef ✅
- Screenshots included in the PR description ✅
- Developer/user documentation checks: not fully completed (see PR notes)

How to test manually:
1. Open Preferences → Network / API keys (or relevant settings page).
2. Enter a proxy password or API key and save.
3. Restart JabRef and verify the credential is still available and works.
4. Inspect that the credential is not stored in the plain settings file but is present in the OS credential store.

Notes:
- This PR focuses on secure storage only; it does not change how credentials are used at runtime.
- Merge of #10004 is required for this PR to work as intended.

Summary
- Improve autosave and save behavior across local and shared (DBMS) databases; prevent autosave for remote/shared databases and make save actions more robust.

What changed
- Disable or adjust autosave where inappropriate (AutosaveUIManager, SharedDatabaseUIManager, DBMSSynchronizer).
- Ensure SaveDatabaseAction and NewDatabaseAction / OpenDatabaseAction correctly initialize and persist autosave-related settings and backups.
- Fix lifecycle and synchronization issues in DBMSSynchronizer to avoid unwanted autosave and to handle connection state changes cleanly.
- Update UI behavior in JabRefFrame, BasePanel and MainTable to better reflect save/connection state and to avoid data-loss scenarios (prompts/notifications when required).
- Make FromAuxDialog work correctly with shared databases and improve related import workflows.
- Update localization (JabRef_en.properties) and add changelog entry (CHANGELOG.md).

Why
- Autosave is not appropriate for remote/shared DBMS databases and could cause conflicts or unexpected writes; these changes prevent autosave where it could be harmful and tighten up save/synchronization logic.
- Improve stability and UX when opening, creating, saving and synchronizing databases, especially in shared setups.

Notes for reviewers
- Pay attention to DBMSSynchronizer lifecycle changes and interactions with SharedDatabaseUIManager.
- Verify autosave UI state transitions when opening/creating local vs. shared databases.
- Check updated localization keys in JabRef_en.properties and the CHANGELOG entry.

Tests
- Manual testing recommended for: opening/creating local DB, opening shared DB, enabling/disabling autosave, saving local DB, and synchronization behavior for shared DBs.

Introduce synchronous indexer shutdown and update tests to avoid races

- Add LuceneIndexer.closeAndWait() to the interface and implement it in the indexers (BibFieldsIndexer, DefaultLinkedFilesIndexer, ReadOnlyLinkedFilesIndexer). These implementations use HeadlessExecutorService.executeAndWait(...) to close indexes synchronously.
- Add LuceneManager.closeAndWait(), which synchronously closes the bib fields and linked files indexers, removes the linked-files preference listener, and posts IndexClosedEvent.
- Use closeAndWait() in DatabaseSearcher to ensure indexers are fully closed both when a query is invalid and after a search completes (replacing asynchronous close() calls). This prevents race conditions and flakiness in tests that rely on indexes being closed.
- Update unit tests to provide a temporary index directory and spy the BibDatabaseContext so getFulltextIndexPath() returns the TempDir. Add necessary imports and annotations (@TempDir, spy) to make tests deterministic.

This change makes index shutdown deterministic and stabilizes tests that previously experienced intermittent failures due to asynchronous indexer shutdown.

## Previous discussion about removing several selected groups only delete one of them #8390 
> You are prompted to confirm the deletion of one group. After accepting, this group is deleted, but you are not prompted to delete the other groups.
So, while it seems that several can be removed at the same time, groups can be removed only one by one.

## Proposed solution
Fixes #8390 

- When `removeGroupAndSubgroups()` is called, iterate through all selected groups instead of the group that triggers the event handler.
- Popup a confirmation dialog and confirm if user decides to delete:
    - single group
    - multiple groups (if multiple groups selection)
- assign selectedGroups (which is `ListProperty<GroupNodeViewModel>`) to new array to prevent [forEach skips an element when a previous element is deleted](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/17852412/foreach-skips-an-element-when-a-previous-element-is-deleted)

Summary
- Add SSL / keystore and server timezone support to the Shared Database login dialog.

What this PR does
- Introduces fields and bindings for keystore path, keystore password, useSSL toggle and serverTimezone in SharedDatabaseLoginDialogViewModel.
- Adds a file chooser for selecting a Java keystore file (showOpenKeystoreFileDialog) and a validator that ensures the keystore file exists.
- Persists keystore file, useSSL and serverTimezone to SharedDatabasePreferences and restores them when the dialog is opened.
- Applies the selected keystore to the JVM trust store (System properties javax.net.ssl.trustStore and javax.net.ssl.trustStorePassword) and enables basic SSL debugging (javax.net.debug = ssl) before opening the connection.
- Extends DBMSConnectionProperties building to include useSSL, keyStore and serverTimezone as well as explicitly allowing public key retrieval (helpful for some MySQL authentication methods).
- Keeps existing behavior for autosave/overwrite prompts, connection opening, migration help dialog, and preference saving (including encrypted password storage when "remember password" is enabled).
- Keeps UI convenience behavior: selected DBMS type updates the default port.

Why
- Users need to connect to secured/shared databases that require a trust store or specific server timezone. Persisting these settings and applying them before connecting makes it easier to use SSL-protected DB servers from the shared database UI.

Testing notes
1. Open Shared Database dialog.
2. Select DB type and verify port updates automatically.
3. Toggle "Use SSL", select a keystore via the keystore file chooser and enter keystore password.
4. Enter connection details and open the database. Confirm the connection proceeds and that system properties javax.net.ssl.trustStore and javax.net.ssl.trustStorePassword are set while connecting (SSL debug logging enabled).
5. If "Remember password" is selected, ensure the password is stored encrypted and restored on reopen; ensure keystore, useSSL and serverTimezone are restored from preferences.
6. Verify autosave behavior and overwrite confirmation still work as before.

Notes / Caveats
- The patch sets system properties for the running JVM to use the chosen trust store; this affects all SSL connections in the JVM. Ensure this behavior is acceptable for your environment.

text:
This PR contains a set of fixes and improvements across the entry source editor, import pipeline, database opening flow and the BibTeX parser. Key changes include:

- SourceTab (entry editor)
  - Add a robust source editor (CodeArea) setup with input method workarounds (InputMethodRequestsObject) and improved input handling.
  - Persist source edits when the editor loses focus or when save-related keybindings are triggered.
  - Validate parsed source and show a user-facing warning dialog if parsing fails, instead of silently failing.
  - Add context menu and keyboard handling (cut/copy/paste/select all) and integrate custom key bindings.
  - Implement search-term highlighting inside the source view.

- ImportAction / Import pipeline
  - Improve automated import flow and background task handling (wrap import in BackgroundTask and handle results/errors appropriately).
  - Ensure Grobid-related opt-in/reset logic is considered before importing PDFs (resets import formats if user opt-in flows are needed).
  - Collect import errors and surface appropriate messages for empty import results or import exceptions.
  - Use the shared task executor for running background tasks to improve testability and consistency.

- ImportFormatReader
  - Make import format registration configurable: add/reset import formats in a single place and only enable Grobid importer if configured.
  - Add helper variants for importing unknown formats (from file or string) and make matching more robust when trying multiple importers.

- OpenDatabaseAction
  - Move file-opening to background tasks and create LibraryTab with a background task for loading the DB to avoid UI blocking.
  - Add telemetry tracking for newly opened databases (number of entries) and warn/show parser warnings when the opened file has syntax issues.
  - Handle shared-database opening errors and fall back to not opening the original file in case of DB connection problems.

- BibtexParser
  - Improve newline detection to preserve original newline separator when parsing (detect CR/LF/LF within the first lookahead window).
  - Improve resilience: better parsing routines for entries, strings, preamble and JabRef metadata comments; more helpful warnings are produced on parse errors.
  - Strengthen handling for bracketed/quoted field parsing, key recovery and EOF detection to make parsing of malformed input more robust.

- Localization
  - Add/update English localization strings used by the above components (error/warning messages, UI labels and prompts).

Overall this PR focuses on making the source editor more reliable and user-friendly, improves the robustness and user-feedback during import/open operations (particularly for PDF/Grobid scenarios), and hardens the BibTeX parsing logic so malformed input is handled more gracefully.

Optimize saving by improving date parsing performance and reducing exception churn.

What changed
- Replaced the previous loop of DateTimeFormatter attempts (which relied on many try/catch paths) with a single combined DateTimeFormatter (SIMPLE_DATE_FORMATS) built via DateTimeFormatterBuilder using optional patterns. This avoids repeatedly throwing and catching DateTimeParseException for each format.
- Introduced NORMALIZED_DATE_FORMATTER constant and use it in getNormalized().
- Added an early check for empty date strings in Date.parse(...).
- Kept the same set of supported input formats (month/day/year variants, textual month names, dots, slashes, etc.) and use Locale.US for parsing month names.
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to mention the fix for saving large .bib files (#7265).

Why
- Parsing many date strings with the old approach generated a lot of exceptions, which was costly when saving large bibliographies. The new approach significantly reduces the exception overhead and improves save performance.

Other notes
- The change addresses issue #7265.
- Tests were added and manual testing was performed as noted in the issue checklist.

Introduce a dedicated date field editor with flexible parsing/formatting and improved handling of incomplete dates, and integrate it into the field editor factory.

What this PR does
- Adds DateEditor and DateEditorViewModel to provide a field editor tailored for date-like fields. The editor uses a TemporalAccessor-based converter and binds the text to the view model with validation.
- Adds TemporalAccessorPicker, a DatePicker-derived control that stores a TemporalAccessor (supports LocalDate, LocalDateTime, YearMonth, Year, etc.), uses a configurable StringConverter, preserves original text for invalid input, and supports incomplete dates/time. It also wires the editor context menu and keeps synchronization between underlying LocalDate and the TemporalAccessor value.
- Updates FieldEditors to return DateEditor for the configured timestamp field (uses the user-configured timestamp format from preferences) and for fields that carry FieldProperty.DATE (uses a default pattern of "[uuuu][-MM][-dd]").
- Date parsing/formatting: the editor first tries the provided DateTimeFormatter, and falls back to the model parser (Date.parse(...)) so a wide range of date formats is accepted.

Why
- Provide robust and user-friendly editing for dates and incomplete dates/times in entry fields (including biblatex date handling).
- Fixes issues related to editing the "date" field (uncaught exceptions and poor parsing) by using a converter that can handle a variety of formats and incomplete dates.

Notes for reviewers
- The DateEditor is wired to use the timestamp format from PreferencesService for the timestamp field; non-timestamp date fields use a conservative default pattern.
- The TemporalAccessorPicker exposes a stringConverterProperty so callers (like DateEditor) can supply custom converters.
- Validation is set up via EditorValidator using the view model's field validator.

Files added/changed (high level)
- Added: src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/DateEditor.java
- Added: src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/DateEditorViewModel.java
- Added: src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/util/component/TemporalAccessorPicker.java
- Updated: src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/FieldEditors.java (integrated DateEditor selection)

Impact
- Improves date input UX and robustness across different date formats and incomplete dates.
- Should fix crashes when editing date fields in certain library modes by providing resilient parsing and validation.

Improve autosave/backup behavior and reduce unnecessary UI-triggered saves

What this PR does
- Introduces DelayTaskThrottler, a small utility to schedule work with a configurable delay and to consolidate rapid successive requests into a single execution.
- Integrates DelayTaskThrottler into AutosaveManager and BackupManager so autosave and backup operations are throttled/debounced when many changes occur in quick succession. This reduces disk churn and avoids excessive save/backup runs while the user is actively editing.
- Adjusts GroupNodeViewModel to avoid triggering unnecessary persistence actions from rapid UI updates (prevents extraneous autosave requests originating from group node view changes).
- Updates CHANGELOG.md with a note about the improvement.

Why this change
- Previously, frequent quick changes (typing, bulk edits, UI updates) could trigger many autosave/backup runs, causing performance issues and excessive IO. Throttling these operations makes the app more responsive and reduces wear on storage.
- Preventing group view updates from firing redundant saves reduces unnecessary work and aligns UI behavior with expected persistence semantics.

Summary
This change fixes a bug where the customImporterTabViewModel was duplicated when exporting Preferences. Exporting preferences could previously lead to the same custom importer view model being added more than once, resulting in duplicate tabs or duplicated entries after import/restore.

Root cause
The export/import flow included transient UI view-model state (or re-registered the same view model) without checking for existing registrations. As a result the customImporterTabViewModel was appended multiple times on export/import operations.

What I changed
- Prevent duplicate registration of customImporterTabViewModel during preferences export/import by adding a guard that checks for existing entries before adding.
- Ensure the exporter persists exporter data (model) instead of transient view-model registration state where appropriate.
- Add id-based deduplication to the preferences restore logic so imports do not create duplicates.
- Add unit tests covering export/import round-trip to assert no duplication occurs and include manual verification steps.

Testing / Verification
- Unit tests added for preferences export/import ensure the custom importer is present only once after export/import.
- Manual steps: export preferences, import them back and confirm the custom importer tab appears only once; open Preferences UI and confirm no duplicate tabs/entries.

Compatibility
This is a backwards-compatible bugfix. No breaking API changes. The fix only changes how preferences are exported/imported to avoid duplicating UI registration state.

- Add a duplicate checker for Citation Relations items in the Entry Editor’s Citation Relations tab.
- When a fetched relation matches an entry already present in the local database, the item is marked visually and the “add” control is replaced by a link button that jumps to the existing local entry.

- Added DuplicateCheck usage to CitationRelationsTab to detect local duplicates when search results are processed.
  - The duplicate check is executed in onSearchForRelationsSucceed(...) when the fetched list of relations is mapped to view items.
  - If a duplicate is found, we create a CitationRelationItem holding a reference to the local entry and mark it as local.
- Modified CitationRelationItem to hold an optional localEntry reference and added a convenience constructor for the old shape.
- Updated the UI for fetched items: if an item is identified as local/duplicate, the item’s container gets the CSS class duplicate-entry and the action button becomes a link button that jumps to the existing entry in the library.
- Added a small style in Base.css (duplicate-entry) to visually highlight duplicate items.
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to mention the new feature.

Files touched
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/entryeditor/citationrelationtab/CitationRelationsTab.java
  - Introduced DuplicateCheck and BibEntryTypesManager/BibDatabaseModeDetection imports.
  - Integrated duplicate detection into the mapping of fetched relations to view items.
  - Adjusted the jump action to navigate to the found local entry when present.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/entryeditor/citationrelationtab/CitationRelationItem.java
  - Added localEntry field and a constructor overload for compatibility.

Summary

This PR brings together multiple user-facing improvements, preference updates and bug fixes as documented in the Unreleased section of CHANGELOG.md.

Highlights

- UI / functionality
  - Show "editor" (as alternative to author) and "booktitle" (as alternative to journal) in the main table by default (#470).
  - Add ability to format / cleanup the date field.
  - Move BibTeX / BibLaTeX mode switcher to the File menu and display the active edit mode (BibTeX or BibLaTeX) in the window title.
  - Make the search field clear when pressing the clear button or ESC (when the search field has focus) (#444).

- Preferences / networking
  - Add support for proxy authentication via VM arguments and GUI settings (implements Feature Request #388). New preference keys are present for proxy hostname, port, username, password and a flag to enable proxy authentication.
  - Default encoding set to UTF-8 and other preference defaults updated.
  - Improvements around preferences handling: export/import of preferences (jabref.xml) is used for memory-stick mode; better handling of default/legacy user file dir names; updated external file type registration and serialization.

- Fixes
  - Reenable preference changes (fix #420).
  - Rework BibLaTeX entry types with correct required and optional fields (fix #414).
  - Fix help links in released jar (fix #413).
  - Preserve capital letters for BibLaTeX (fix #412) — integrity check lowercasing no longer required.
  - Toolbar wrapping after search field fixed for small windows (fix #437).
  - Cut/Copy/Paste translations in menus fixed (fix #438).

- Removed
  - Removed file history size preference (was not available in the UI).

Notes about code changes

- JabRefPreferences contains updated defaults and new preference keys for proxy support (USE_PROXY, PROXY_HOSTNAME, PROXY_PORT, USE_PROXY_AUTHENTICATION, PROXY_USERNAME, PROXY_PASSWORD) and other defaults (e.g. DEFAULT_ENCODING = UTF-8). It includes logic to import/export preferences (jabref.xml) on startup / memory-stick mode, management of external file types, key bindings restoration, and helper methods for color, arrays and custom entry types.

Testing

- Preference import/export and memory-stick behavior should be tested (export to jabref.xml and re-import).
- Proxy authentication should be tested both via VM args and the GUI settings.
- Verify editor/booktitle are visible by default in the main table, and the search clear behaviour (button and ESC) works as expected.

Add ottobib fetcher with fallbacks to ebook.de and chimbori.com

Summary:
- Implemented a new fetcher that uses ottobib as the primary source for bibliographic metadata.
- If ottobib returns no results or an error, the fetcher falls back to ebook.de and then chimbori.com.

What I changed:
- Added ottobib request/response handling and parsing.
- Implemented fallback logic (ottobib -> ebook.de -> chimbori.com).
- Added basic error handling and retry behavior for transient failures.
- Added unit/integration tests covering ottobib success, ottobib failure with fallback, and parsing edge cases.
- Updated documentation to describe the new fetcher and its fallback order.

Why this change:
- Provides a more reliable metadata lookup by leveraging ottobib first and using other sources when necessary.

Related issue: #2581

This PR fixes UI behavior when an invalid BibTeX key is entered and updates the changelog. Changes:

- Fix: EntryEditor no longer always pops up an error dialog when an invalid BibTeX key is detected. The code now sets the field to an invalid background and returns immediately; the JOptionPane is only shown when the current thread is not the Swing Event Dispatch Thread (and requestFocus() is invoked in that case). This prevents the previous problematic dialog behavior that could lead to crashes or UI issues when handling invalid keys.

- Docs: CHANGELOG.md updated — link formatting corrected for existing fixes and a new entry added for #1882 ("Crash after saving illegal bibtexkey in entry editor").

Summary

This PR contains a set of refactorings, bug fixes and reliability improvements across importers, formatting utilities, citation key generation, URL downloading, the AI summarization task and a set of JBang helper launchers used for development workflows.

What changed

- JBang tooling
  - Updated jbang helper classes (CheckoutPR, CloneJabRef, JabKitLauncher, JabLsLauncher, JabSrvLauncher) to improve UX and robustness when launching development utilities and scripts.

- AI / summarization
  - Touched GenerateSummaryTask to improve stability and error handling when generating summaries (better handling of invalid inputs and downstream failures).

- BibTeX / importers
  - Improved BibtexParser resilience for malformed input and edge cases during import.
  - PdfContentImporter: enhanced extraction logic to better handle PDF metadata/content and avoid crashes on unexpected PDF content.
  - INSPIREBibtexFilterReader: improved handling of INSPIRE-specific BibTeX filters to avoid data loss and incorrect parsing results.

- Bibliography logic and formatting
  - BstFunctions: refined BST-related functions (corner-case handling and null-safety improvements).
  - CitationKeyGenerator: improved generation logic to produce more stable keys and handle unusual metadata.
  - NameFormatter: adjusted name formatting behavior to correctly format complex names and edge cases.
  - UnprotectTermsFormatter: improved case-changing logic to respect protected terms and avoid unwanted transformations.

- External files and downloads
  - LinkedFileHandler: fixed path handling and improved robustness when linking and resolving external files.
  - URLDownload: made download code more reliable (better timeout/redirect handling and improved error reporting) and safer against network edge cases.

Miscellaneous

- General code quality improvements (null checks, logging clarity and small refactors) across several modules to make behavior more predictable and easier to maintain.

Testing & Migration

- Existing unit and integration tests should continue to pass; changes focused on robustness and bug fixes rather than API breaks.
- No user-facing configuration changes are expected. If you rely on edge-case parser behavior, please verify imports with a representative sample of your data.

Notes for reviewers

- Reviewers may want to focus on the importer/parser changes and the URLDownload updates, as those affect critical IO paths and parsing logic.
- JBang scripts are development tooling — please validate launch flows on your platform if you use these helpers.

text:
Improve PdfMergeMetadataImporter

What changed
- Implement more robust metadata extraction for merged PDF files in PdfMergeMetadataImporter.
- Prefer XMP metadata when available and fall back to PDF document info fields when XMP is absent.
- Parse common metadata fields (title, author, subject, keywords, creation/modification dates) and normalize/trim values before returning.
- Add null-safety and stronger error handling to avoid NPEs when metadata sections are missing.
- Use try-with-resources to ensure PDF resources are closed reliably and reduce resource leaks.
- Add logging for parsing failures and unexpected metadata formats to aid debugging.

Why
- Previously metadata extraction could miss XMP data or throw exceptions when fields were absent, leading to incomplete or broken import results for merged PDFs. These changes make metadata import more reliable and resilient.

Compatibility and impact
- Behavior is backward-compatible: when XMP is not present, the importer continues to use standard PDF info fields.
- More robust handling reduces risk of crashes during import and improves metadata quality for merged PDFs.

Notes
- No public API changes outside of the importer behavior. Logging additions may increase diagnostic output when parsing problematic PDFs.

Summary

This PR adds support for the biblatex `langid` field as an optional/important field in the entry editor and integrates it into the model, GUI, and tests. It implements parsing and formatting for langid values and provides a language dropdown editor for biblatex libraries. Closes #10868.

What I changed

- Model
  - Added new enum org.jabref.model.entry.Langid with valid BibLaTeX language identifiers, parsing helpers (parse, getByLangid) and getJabRefFormat() for storage.
  - Added BibEntry.setLangid(Langid) to set the LANGUAGEID field.
  - Marked StandardField.LANGUAGEID as a non-text field in FieldFactory.

- GUI / Editor
  - Added LanguageEditorViewModel (org.jabref.gui.fieldeditors.optioneditors.LanguageEditorViewModel) that provides items, conversion and display text for Langid values.
  - Hooked the LANGUAGE FieldProperty into FieldEditors so the OptionEditor uses LanguageEditorViewModel for language fields.

- Entry type definitions
  - Integrated StandardField.LANGUAGEID into BiblatexEntryTypeDefinitions (added to important/detail fields where applicable) so langid appears in the editor for relevant biblatex entry types.

- Tests
  - Added tests for the Langid model (LangidTest.java).
  - Added tests for the LanguageEditorViewModel (LanguageEditorViewModelTest.java).
  - Updated BibEntryTypesManagerTest to assert usage of StandardField.LANGUAGEID instead of an UnknownField("langid").

- Misc
  - Small cleanup in MonthEditorViewModel to mark databaseMode as final.
  - Updated CHANGELOG to mention added support for langid.

Why this change

- Support for biblatex langid allows users to set an entry's language identifier in a structured way, improves editor UX by giving a dropdown of valid language IDs, and enables correct formatting/processing for biblatex libraries.

Notes

- The Langid enum contains the language names and canonical langid strings based on the biblatex manual.
- LanguageEditorViewModel currently uses the Langid enum values as items and converts to/from strings for display and storage.
- Manual testing and unit tests were added/updated to cover the new functionality.

Summary

Fixes a concurrency bug in the abbreviate action that could produce incorrect results or data races when the action ran concurrently.

Problem

The abbreviate action relied on shared mutable state (e.g. re-used buffers/formatters or non-thread-safe caches) which allowed concurrent requests to interfere with each other, occasionally producing corrupted or incorrect abbreviations.

What I changed

- Removed/avoided shared mutable state in the abbreviate action by moving mutable objects to method-local scope.
- Replaced non-thread-safe caches/containers with thread-safe alternatives (ConcurrentHashMap) or made caches immutable when appropriate.
- Eliminated re-use of mutable builders/formatters across threads; where reuse was required, used ThreadLocal or synchronized access with minimal scope.
- Added unit and concurrency tests that reproduce the race and verify the fix.

Impact

- Corrects intermittent incorrect outputs and potential race conditions under concurrent load.
- Behavior is unchanged for single-threaded use; concurrency behavior is now deterministic and safe.
- Performance: negligible overhead from thread-safe changes; removed data corruption risk.

Notes

- Added tests to prevent regression. Recommend monitoring the first release after merge for any edge cases in production.

Summary
Improve the user-facing handling of parsing errors caused by missing commas in .bib files when importing or opening a library. Instead of showing a generic error dialog (or silently showing an empty library), show a clear warning with the parser's message so users know their .bib file is malformed.

Problem
- Importing a .bib file with missing commas produced a stack trace ("Could not find a suitable import format") and the import failed with an unhelpful exception.
- Opening such a file via the normal file-open flow produced an empty library with no message, leaving users unaware of the underlying parsing problem.

Solution
- Use the parser result's error message to create an ImportException: throw new ImportException(parserResult.getErrorMessage());
- In the import/open error handling, when the thrown error is an instance of ImportException, show a warning dialog (instead of a generic error dialog) with the localized import error message. Example call used:
  DefaultTaskExecutor.runAndWaitInJavaFXThread(() -> dialogService.showWarningDialogAndWait(Localization.lang("Import error"), importError.getLocalizedMessage()));
- Apply the same handling to both importing and opening .bib files so users consistently receive a meaningful warning when the file cannot be parsed due to formatting issues.

Fixes
- Fixes #8011

Testing and notes
- Manually tested in running JabRef.
- Screenshot showing the warning dialog included in the PR description.

- Manually tested: done

This pull request introduces a variety of enhancements and bug fixes for JabRef, improving the user experience and ensuring smoother operations. Key changes include:

- **New Features**:
  - Added a query parser and mapping layer to enable conversion of queries formulated in simplified Lucene syntax by the user into API queries.
  - Introduced basic functionality to customize the look of JabRef by importing a CSS theme file.
  - Added a connection check function in network preference settings.

- **UI Improvements**:
  - Restructured the 'File' tab and extracted some parts into the 'Linked files' tab.
  - Improved the responsiveness of the general fields specification dialog window.
  - Moved the group search bar and the 'New group' button to a more prominent top position.
  - Enhanced the layout for buttons in the Open Office side panel to ensure the button text is always visible, especially when resizing.

- **Bug Fixes**:
  - Fixed an issue where the `.sav` file was not deleted upon exiting JabRef.
  - Resolved a linked identifier icon inconsistency.
  - Ensured that font size changes are reflected in dialogs.
  - Fixed the issue where the entry preview tab had no name in the drop-down list.
  - Addressed an issue where long directory names created from patterns could cause exceptions.

- **Other Changes**:
  - Synchronization of SpecialFields to keywords is now disabled by default.
  - JabRef no longer opens the entry editor with the first entry on startup.
  - Removed the 'enforce legal key' option and the 'External programs / Open PDF' section in the preferences, as they are now obsolete.

These changes aim to enhance the usability and stability of JabRef, making it a more robust tool for managing bibliographic references.

text:
Fixes #13868 — Export AI conversations & summaries to Markdown/JSON

Summary
- Adds the ability to export AI conversations and their summaries in two formats: Markdown (.md) and JSON (.json).
- Users can export whole conversations or just the generated summaries.

What I changed
- Backend
  - New export service and serializers to produce canonical JSON and human-readable Markdown outputs, including metadata (conversation id, title, participants, timestamps, models, and summary data).
  - New API endpoint: GET /api/ai/conversations/:id/export?format={json|md}&type={conversation|summary}
  - Authorization checks added to ensure only users with access to the conversation can export it.
  - Streamed responses for large conversations to avoid high memory usage.
- Frontend
  - Export button added to conversation UI with a modal/dropdown to choose format (Markdown or JSON) and scope (conversation or summary).
  - File naming pattern: ai_conversation_<id>_<type>.<ext> (e.g. ai_conversation_123_summary.md).
  - Progress and error feedback for long-running exports.
- Tests & docs
  - Unit and integration tests for export service, API endpoint, and frontend export flow.
  - Added documentation snippet explaining export formats and sample schema for JSON.

Behavior / Notes
- Markdown export includes front-matter metadata and readable conversation content with speaker labels and timestamps, followed by summaries when requested.
- JSON export provides a structured payload suitable for programmatic consumption, including messages array, metadata, and summary objects.
- Large conversations are streamed; the client will receive a downloadable file without loading entire content into server memory.
- Backwards-compatible: no existing APIs changed, only added endpoints and UI elements.

How to test
1. Create or open an AI conversation and ensure you have view access.
2. Generate or confirm a summary exists (if exporting summary).
3. Click the new Export button, select format and type, and download.
4. Verify:
   - File extension matches chosen format.
   - Markdown file contains front-matter metadata and readable conversation text.
   - JSON file follows the documented schema (metadata, messages, summary) and parses successfully.
   - Unauthorized users cannot access the export endpoint.

Related
- Fixes: #13868

Notes
- If additional export formats are desired, the export service is designed to be extensible to add more serializers in the future.

Summary

This PR lazily initializes context menus for editor fields to eliminate the memory and performance overhead of instantiating them for every visible field. Previously the context menus were created eagerly for each visible text field (profiling showed ~40% of allocated object size and ~8% of CPU time when browsing 50 entries). By moving construction into a Supplier and creating the menu only when the user actually requests it (right-click), the memory and performance impact while simply browsing entries is removed.

What I changed

- Use Supplier-based late initialization for context menus so they are instantiated on first use (right-click) instead of on field creation.
- Bumped checkstyle version in Gradle so javadoc comments can use {@link ...} to classes that are otherwise unused.

Why

- Eager creation of many small context menus accumulates a significant memory footprint and measurable CPU cost while the user is just scrolling/browsing entries. Lazy initialization defers that cost until the menu is actually needed.

Results

- Profiling before/after included in the original issue shows a large reduction in memory objects and the performance impact disappearing when simply scrolling through entries (screenshots attached in issue: mem1/perf1 before, mem2/perf2 after).

Testing

- Manually tested in a running JabRef instance. Context menus appear and behave correctly when right-clicking.

Fix TAB navigation in EntryEditor (closes #11937)

Summary
- Pressing TAB on the last field of a tab now moves focus to the first field of the next tab inside the EntryEditor.
- Navigation is restricted to fields inside the EntryEditor and will not jump to unrelated UI components outside the editor.

What I changed
- Added static helper methods in EditorTextField to centralize and manage TAB navigation logic.
- Ensured all TextField instances in SimpleEditor, CitationKeyEditor, PersonsEditor, and MarkdownEditor have their id set correctly so the code can identify the last field in a tab.

Summary

- Remove XMP declaration wrapper (<?xpacket ...?>) from generated .xmp files so they can be used with the xmpincl LaTeX package. This addresses koppor#338.
- Fix DublinCore date/month extraction and improve handling of bibtex/* relationships stored in Dublin Core relations (bibtex/ key/value pairs). Add a workaround for corrupted month/date values produced by some XMP writers.

What I changed

- XmpExporter: now writes XMP content generated without the leading/trailing <?xpacket ...?> tags (uses new helper in XmpUtilWriter).
- XmpUtilWriter:
  - Added generateXmpStringWithoutXmpDeclaration(...) which returns the Dublin Core XMP metadata string without the <?xpacket ...?> begin/end lines.
  - Renamed the previous generator to generateXmpStringWithXmpDeclaration(...) and used it as the basis for the new method.
  - Utility to strip ?xpacket begin/end tags introduced (used to support xmpincl usage).
- DublinCoreExtractor:
  - Adjusted year/month extraction so that an all-default date of YYYY-01-01 (calendar defaulting to January 1) is not treated as containing a month; only a real month is written.
  - Parse dc:relations entries that start with "bibtex/" using a functional style (Predicate + Consumer) and properly split into key/value even when value contains slashes.
  - Normalize and override month fields when a bibtex/month relation is present (parse and set short month name).
  - Documented reasoning: PDFBox XMP date defaulting to January can yield false months. Workaround added; see PDFBOX-4196 for the underlying library issue.
- Tests and resources:
  - Updated XmpExporterTest expectations to reflect the removed xpacket lines (line counts and line indices changed).
  - Updated test resource article_dublinCore.bib to use "mar" for month to match new month parsing/normalization behavior.

Files changed (high level)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/exporter/XmpExporter.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/xmp/XmpUtilWriter.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/xmp/DublinCoreExtractor.java
- src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/exporter/XmpExporterTest.java
- src/test/resources/org/jabref/logic/xmp/article_dublinCore.bib

Notes

- Removing the <?xpacket ...?> wrapper lets users include JabRef-exported .xmp files via LaTeX packages such as xmpincl.
- The month/date change is conservative: it avoids interpreting an implicit default 1st January as a real month. If JabRef wrote explicit month=jan, it will still be preserved.
- The month/date workaround is defensive until the underlying PDFBox XMP handling issue (PDFBOX-4196) is resolved.

Tests

- Existing tests adjusted to match changed output format; CI should validate behavior across single/multiple entry exports.

Related issues

- Fixes: koppor#338
- Related PDFBox issue: https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/PDFBOX-4196

Add UI and persistence for save actions and save-order configuration in Library Properties

What changed
- Introduced a new FieldFormatterCleanupsPanel that allows users to manage "save actions" (field formatters applied when saving a library). The panel supports:
  - enabling/disabling save actions
  - selecting a field and a formatter (editable field list + built-in formatters)
  - adding/removing actions and clearing all actions
  - resetting to recommended BibTeX/BibLaTeX actions
  - showing formatter descriptions and preventing duplicate actions
  - ProtectTermsFormatter is included in the available formatters
  - helper methods for persistence and change detection: getFormatterCleanups(), storeSettings(metaData), hasChanged(), isDefaultSaveActions()
- Integrated save-order UI into the Library Properties dialog using SaveOrderConfigDisplayView and added the corresponding FXML (SaveOrderConfigDisplay.fxml). The display was adjusted to present the save-order options (original order / table order / specified order) and to enable/disable sort criterion controls accordingly.
- Updated LibraryPropertiesDialogView to include the new components in the dialog:
  - loads the stored SaveOrderConfig from the library metadata (or falls back to preferences)
  - adds the SaveOrderConfigDisplayView and the FieldFormatterCleanupsPanel into the dialog content
  - on OK persists encoding, database mode, directories, protection flag, save order config and save actions to MetaData
  - clears metadata entries when the default configuration is used to avoid leaving redundant metadata
  - marks the base as changed when relevant properties changed so the UI updates appropriately
- FieldFormatterCleanupsPanel is built programmatically (no separate FXML) and uses ViewModelListCellFactory and EasyBind for UI bindings and tooltips.

Why this is useful
- Users can now configure per-library save actions and save-order settings from the Library Properties dialog, making it easier to manage formatting/sanitization rules and export/save order on a per-library basis.

Implementation notes
- Save actions are persisted in MetaData and cleaned up (removed) when the user restores defaults or removes all actions.
- SaveOrderConfig is compared against the stored/old config; if it equals the default save order it is cleared from metadata to avoid unnecessary metadata entries.
- The new UI respects BibTeX vs BibLaTeX recommended actions when resetting to recommended settings.

Files added/changed
- Added/updated: SaveOrderConfigDisplay.fxml
- Added: src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/cleanup/FieldFormatterCleanupsPanel.java
- Updated: src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/libraryproperties/LibraryPropertiesDialogView.java
- Updated: src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/libraryproperties/LibraryPropertiesDialog.fxml

No user-visible breaking changes: this is an additive feature that centralizes save action and save-order configuration in the Library Properties dialog.

text:
Implements the LinkedFileViewModel which encapsulates UI logic and actions for a LinkedFile attached to a BibEntry.

Key responsibilities and features:
- Exposes properties and bindings for the linked file (link, description), file icon, download progress, download state, automatic-find and offline-PDF flags.
- Validates existence of local files via a FunctionBasedValidator (shows a warning if file cannot be found), while allowing online links to pass validation.
- Provides operations for opening files, opening containing folder, editing link metadata, renaming (including user prompt and overwrite conflict handling), moving to the library's default directory, and combined move+rename.
- Ensures remote/online links cannot be renamed or moved locally.
- Deletion confirmation UI: lets user remove link from entry or delete the file from disk, with error handling for permission issues.
- Downloading of online links:
  - Validates target directory exists, checks SSL handshake (with user confirmation on SSL certificate issues), infers file type from MIME or URL, picks a non-conflicting filename and downloads using a BackgroundTask/FileDownloadTask.
  - Binds download progress to UI, shows messages, handles failures and notifies user on success (including a specific notification for HTML downloads).
- File-type inference helpers: infer from MIME type or URL suffix using ExternalFileTypes and preferences.
- Integrates with LinkedFileHandler for suggested filenames, renames, moves and detection of existing files; also uses FileNameUniqueness to avoid overwriting.
- Supports parsing PDF metadata sources (verbatim, embedded bib, Grobid, XMP, content) and launching a MultiMergeEntriesView to merge metadata into the database.
- Misc: utility methods for truncated display strings, generated-name/path comparisons, and wrapping Importer executions into Suppliers for background import/merge dialogs.

Error handling: logs errors and displays user-friendly dialogs for IO, download and SSL issues. Uses DialogService, TaskExecutor, PreferencesService and BibDatabaseContext for integration with the rest of the application.

Add library selector to AUX import dialog and refactor parsing into a view model

What changed
- A ComboBox was added to the FromAuxDialog UI so users can select the reference library used when importing .aux files (src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/auximport/FromAuxDialog.fxml).

- LibraryTabContainer interface now exposes an addTab(BibDatabaseContext, boolean) overload (src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/LibraryTabContainer.java) which is used to add the generated database as a new tab.
- New localization key for the library selector label was added (src/main/resources/l10n/JabRef_en.properties).
- CHANGELOG updated to mention the new dropdown.

Why
- Users may have multiple open libraries; selecting the reference library when importing an AUX file makes parsing more accurate and improves the user experience.
- Moving logic into a ViewModel improves separation of concerns and testability.

Notes for integrators
- Implementations of LibraryTabContainer need to provide the new addTab(BibDatabaseContext, boolean) method.
- The ViewModel depends on StateManager to list open databases and on DialogService/Preferences for file selection.

I believe I could bring down the performance impact of the context menus to a bare minimum. I reported this in https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/3335 and @tobiasdiez provided me with the hint how this could work. Against his suggestion to not overshoot, I decided to prove my point that even those small context menus have a significant impact because things will sum up in the end and those menus are newly instantiated for every visible field in the editor.

The starting point was the current master-branch and profiling it by going through only 50 bib-entries. This means that the context menus are instantiated for the visible text fields. This has an impact on performance and memory and, unfortunately, it is not only a tiny fraction. 

## Memory

Notable are the columns "Objects", which are all objects that are created by this method and underlying sub calls and the overall "Size".

![mem1](http://i.imgur.com/pjBJSlF.png)

With almost 40% of the overall memory size, it's definitely something to look into.

## Performance

The performance is with 8% not so large but still noticeable. 

![perf1](http://i.imgur.com/STSGgNj.png)

## Fixing it

By using the `Supplier` interface, we can move the instantiation to the point where the user actually right-clicks into the field. I debugged this, and it seems to work nice. The outcome was as expected. Since no one actually triggers the context menu by just browsing through the list, it vanished altogether. Here is the used memory with this PR created by exactly scrolling through the 50 entries. First the memory footprint

![mem2](http://i.imgur.com/dRrKaxs.png)

and here the performance impact

![perf2](http://i.imgur.com/HgJNhLl.png)

In conclusion, this means as long as the user doesn't need a context menu, we have no memory or performance impact at all.

## Note

I updated the `checkstyle` version in the Gradle built. I like to write comments, and now it doesn't prevent me any longer from using `{@link ...}` in doc-comments to classes that are otherwise not used.

Summary:
Improves the user experience around files that are automatically linked by the system. Makes automatic linking clearer, less error-prone, and easier to manage from the UI.

What changed:
- Clearer labeling and metadata for automatically linked files so users can distinguish them from manually added files.
- Added explicit visual indicator (icon/tooltip) and a short explanation for why a file was auto-linked.
- Improved naming and conflict resolution: auto-linked files now receive a readable suggested name and prompt the user only when there is a naming conflict.
- New quick actions: users can now easily unlink an automatically linked file, rename it, or mark it as trusted from the file list.
- Preview and details pane now show the source and linking rule that caused the file to be linked.
- Batch operations: allow unlinking or marking multiple auto-linked files at once.
- Accessibility improvements for the new UI elements (aria labels, keyboard navigation).
- Minor performance optimizations when loading large lists of linked files.

Why:
- Users were confused about which files were auto-linked and why, which led to accidental edits and frustration. These changes make the behavior transparent and give users quick control over auto-linked files.

Migration / Backwards compatibility:
- No breaking changes to existing file storage or APIs. UI-only changes; existing links remain intact.
- If your workflow relies on implicit naming of auto-linked files, be aware that suggested names may change to a clearer format. Users can rename files as before.

Testing:
- Added unit and integration tests for the new conflict-resolution logic and batch actions.
- Manual QA performed on linking/unlinking, rename flow, and accessibility keyboard navigation.

Notes:
- If you have suggestions for wording of the auto-link explanation or additional quick actions, please add them to the PR comments.

Add Automatic Field Editor UI and view-models with unit tests

This PR introduces the Automatic Field Editor feature (tabs for Edit content, Copy/Move content, Clear content and Rename field) including UI views, view-model logic and tests:

- New view-model: AutomaticFieldEditorViewModel — aggregates tabs and wires undo support via NamedCompoundEdit and an UndoManager.
- Clear content tab: ClearContentTabView + ClearContentViewModel — lets users clear a chosen field across selected entries, with a "Show only set fields" option and focus handling. The view-model records the number of affected entries and the composed undo edit.
- Edit content tab: EditFieldContentTabView + EditFieldContentViewModel — supports setting or appending values to a selected field across multiple selected entries, input validation (field name) and bindings to enable/disable Set/Append controls according to validation and overwrite settings. Uses ControlsFxVisualizer for validation feedback.
- Rename and Copy/Move tabs: scaffolding views are included and integrated into the tab list.
- FXML layouts for Edit and Clear tabs and localization keys for new UI labels.
- Unit tests: EditFieldContentTabViewModelTest and ClearContentViewModelTest verify behavior for overwrite vs. non-overwrite flows, append behavior, clearing fields, and basic view-model invariants (available fields, default selection).

Implementation notes:
- Field combo boxes use the shared FIELD_STRING_CONVERTER and are populated from available fields / selected entries.
- Actions produce NamedCompoundEdit instances recorded via stateManager.setLastAutomaticFieldEditorEdit so the UI can present and undo the last automatic edit.
- Care has been taken to bind button enabled states to validation properties and selection state to provide immediate UI feedback.

Files added/modified (high level):
- jabgui: AutomaticFieldEditorViewModel, ClearContentTabView/ViewModel, EditFieldContentTabView/ViewModel, RenameFieldTabView and related FXML
- test: EditFieldContentTabViewModelTest, ClearContentViewModelTest
- resources: localization entries

This brings batch field-editing capabilities to the application with undo support and test coverage for core behaviors.

- Implement and consolidate database save operations in SaveDatabaseAction.

Key changes
- Added support for saving only selected entries as plain BibTeX via saveSelectedAsPlain().
- Centralized save logic with overloaded save/saveAs methods to handle explicit Path, user-prompted path and mode (SILENT/NORMAL).

Summary

Enhance the DOI parser to robustly handle special characters and varied DOI formats that previously caused parsing failures.

Problem

DOIs containing parentheses, semicolons, plus signs, percent-encoding, HTML-encoded entities, or surrounding whitespace were not consistently parsed. The parser also failed to accept common prefixes in different casing and formats.

What I changed

- Broadened and tightened the DOI detection pattern to allow common ASCII punctuation and percent-encoded sequences while preventing accidental over-capture.
- Added normalization steps: trim surrounding whitespace, strip common prefixes (case-insensitive), decode HTML entities, and preserve percent-encoded segments.
- Improved Unicode handling by normalizing input to NFC where appropriate.
- Added unit tests covering multiple edge cases: parentheses, semicolons, plus signs, percent-encoded DOIs, HTML-encoded DOIs, leading/trailing whitespace, and mixed-case prefixes.
- Updated parser documentation and examples.

Backward compatibility

This change is fully backward compatible: valid DOIs that parsed before will continue to parse the same way; the parser is just more permissive for valid-but-uncommon formats.

Testing

- New unit tests added for each special-character scenario.
- Existing tests retained and run to ensure no regressions.

Notes

If you have additional DOI examples that still fail, please add them to the test suite so we can extend coverage.

Improve URL handling and validation in URLUtil and update tests

This PR refactors and hardens URL utilities and updates tests to match the new behaviour:

- Add and expose a URL regex (URL_PATTERN) to better detect protocol-based URLs.
- Strengthen isURL(...) to use the URL_PATTERN and to attempt creation via create(...); rejects null/blank, embedded or protocol-less strings (e.g. "www.example.com" or "dblp..., http://...").
- Introduce create(String) which validates and converts a string to a java.net.URL with stricter checks:
  - Rejects null or empty strings (throws IllegalArgumentException).
  - Trims input and automatically prefixes "https://" for strings starting with "www.".
  - Parses via URI and enforces that the URI is absolute and contains both scheme and host; throws MalformedURLException with informative messages for invalid inputs.
- Improve createUri(String) to percent-encode pipe characters ("|") by replacing them with "%7C" before creating the URI to work around JDK URI differences.
- Improve getFileNameFromUrl(String): extracts filename, falls back to "downloaded.pdf" for empty names, and sanitises via FileUtil.getValidFileName.
- Update and add unit tests to cover the new behaviour (isURL, create with www-prefix, createUri handling of pipe, null/empty inputs, various malformed cases) and adjust FileFieldParser tests to use the new create(...) semantics.

These changes fix multiple corner cases when parsing and normalising URLs (including Google search result cleanup, missing schemes, pipe characters and invalid URIs) and make error reporting more explicit in failing cases.

- Builds installers, portable archives and JabKit for Linux (x86_64 & arm64), Windows and macOS (Intel & Apple Silicon) using a matrix strategy.

- Conditions job determines whether to run builds/uploads/notarization based on event type, labels, repository owner and provided secrets. It exposes outputs: upload-to-builds-jabref-org, secretspresent, tagbuild, should-build and should-notarize.
- Build job (per-OS matrix) performs:
  - Full checkout with submodules and GitVersion calculation

text:
Summary

- Improve the Linked Files editor UI and behavior, add supporting CSS and new icons, and update the changelog.

What I changed

- LinkedFilesEditor
  - Reworked file list cell layout so automatically found files show an "accept" button on the far left (uses the link+ icon) and a tooltip asking whether to link the file to the entry.
  - File name text is rendered with a reduced opacity pseudo-class while a file is automatically found, and switches back once accepted (uses a :opacity pseudo-class).
  - Added a progress bar bound to the file download progress and a conditional button to write XMP metadata to PDFs.
  - Icon click opens the file; double-clicking the item opens the edit dialog.
  - Drag-and-drop support for reordering linked files (uses a serializable LinkedFile on the dragboard), and keyboard handling (DELETE removes selected file).
  - Context menu items wired to commands and dynamically enabled/disabled via bindings (open, open folder, download, rename/move to pattern, delete, copy, remove link, ...).

- Base.css
  - Added/updated styles to support the new visual treatment for file rows (.file-row-text and .file-row-text:opacity) and other theme tweaks to ensure consistent appearance of the new buttons/indicators.

- IconTheme
  - Added/registered more icons and support for application icons (TeX editors and other external applications used by flatpak integration), and adjusted some color constants used by the UI.
  - Centralized icon-property reading and image helpers remain in place; new icons make the new linked-file and external-app UI look consistent.

- CHANGELOG.md
  - Updated the Unreleased section to document the new 'automatically found PDF' UX (link button and opacity), flatpak extension / external application support (Texshow, Texmaker, LyX), and related improvements.

Why

- Make automatically detected files more discoverable and easier to link from the entry editor by surfacing a dedicated accept action and clearer visual cues (reduced opacity until linked).
- Provide better UX when downloading/writing metadata and when interacting with linked files (drag reorder, context actions, keyboard delete).
- Add icons for external applications (required for the flatpak extension/external app support) so the new features have consistent visuals.

Notes

- The new opacity state is implemented as a CSS pseudo-class (":opacity") toggled from the view model, and the corresponding styles are added to Base.css.
- Context menu item availability depends on file state (online vs local, whether a file is already in the file directory, generated name/path matches original, etc.).

Related

- UX for automatically found PDFs: #3607
- Flatpak extension / external app support (Texshow, Texmaker, LyX): #7248

text:
Summary

- Introduces a set of classes and metadata support to manage and apply field formatter save-actions and content selectors.

What changed

- Added FieldFormatterCleanup (CleanupJob) that runs a Formatter on a specific field of a BibEntry and returns FieldChange events. Handles removal of fields when the formatter returns an empty string.
- Added FieldFormatterCleanups which:
  - Defines default and recommended formatter lists for BibTeX and BibLaTeX workflows.
  - Serializes/deserializes formatter configurations to/from metadata strings (getMetaDataString / parse).
  - Provides enable/disable state and utilities to apply configured formatters to an entry (applySaveActions).
  - Integrates with existing Formatter/Formatters registry and falls back to IdentityFormatter when unknown.

- Added ContentSelector model class to represent a selector for a field with a list of values (immutable access, equals/hashCode/toString implemented).

- Extended MetaData to store and manage both save actions and content selectors:
  - New constants: SELECTOR_META_PREFIX and SAVE_ACTIONS.
  - New fields and methods: saveActions (Optional<FieldFormatterCleanups>), getSaveActions(), setSaveActions(), clearSaveActions().
  - New content selector APIs: getContentSelectors(), getContentSelectorList(), addContentSelector(ContentSelector), clearContentSelectors(Field), getContentSelectorValuesForField(Field).
  - ContentSelectors and saveActions are included in equals/hashCode/toString checks and modifications trigger MetaDataChangedEvent via postChange().

Why

- This change formalizes save-action (field formatter) configuration, serialization and runtime application so that formatters can be stored in library metadata and consistently applied on save.
- Content selectors provide a lightweight metadata model to store per-field selection values used by UI or import/filtering features.

Compatibility & notes

- Existing metadata without save actions falls back to DEFAULT_SAVE_ACTIONS via parse() overload.
- Unknown formatter keys are handled by using IdentityFormatter as a safe no-op fallback.
- All metadata changes post MetaDataChangedEvent to keep the rest of the application in sync.

Files touched (high level)

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/cleanup/FieldFormatterCleanup.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/cleanup/FieldFormatterCleanups.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/model/metadata/ContentSelector.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/model/metadata/MetaData.java

Testing

- The implementation returns FieldChange objects for downstream consumers and avoids applying changes when no modification occurred. Serialization/parsing of save action metadata is implemented and will need to be exercised through metadata read/write tests and UI integration.

Summary

This PR fixes issue #12000 by adding support for extracting arXiv identifiers from the first page of PDFs when importing into JabRef. When an arXiv id is found it is stored in the entry (StandardField.EPRINT) and used to derive the year prefix from the arXiv id where applicable.

What I changed

- Added import of ArXivIdentifier and implemented a new helper method getArxivId(...) in PdfContentImporter.java. The method scans the current parsed string for occurrences of "arxiv"/"arXiv" and uses ArXivIdentifier.parse(...) to extract a canonical arXiv id when present.
- Integrated arXiv extraction into getEntryFromPDFContent(...) so that arXiv ids are collected alongside DOI and other metadata while parsing the first page content.
- If an arXiv id is present, it is set on the created BibEntry using StandardField.EPRINT. The code also derives a year prefix from the arXiv id ("20" + first two digits) where the logic applies.
- Added a unit test extractArxivIdFromPage1 in PdfContentImporterTest to ensure an arXiv id like "arXiv:2408.06224v1" is detected and the EPRINT field is populated accordingly.

Files changed

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fileformat/PdfContentImporter.java
- src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fileformat/PdfContentImporterTest.java

Why

PDF first pages commonly include arXiv identifiers. Previously these were not parsed or stored by the PDF content importer, which caused loss of useful metadata when importing. This change improves metadata extraction and preserves arXiv ids in imported entries.

Tests

- Added extractArxivIdFromPage1 unit test verifying parsing and population of the EPRINT field.

Closes

Update MainTableColumn to properly resolve and format displayed values in the main table

Summary
- Add database-aware field resolution and LaTeX->Unicode formatting for column values.
- Improve detection and formatting of person-name columns.
- Provide constructors for regular columns, database-backed columns and icon columns.
- Implement robust logic to detect if a displayed value is resolved (e.g. from crossrefs, strings or alias fields) while excluding special headers (type/key).

Details
- Store an Optional<BibDatabase in the column so getColumnValue can call BibDatabase.getResolvedField(...) to obtain resolved values (this handles crossrefs, strings and alias fields).
- Use MainTableNameFormatter for fields that contain PERSON_NAMES to display names consistently.
- Convert LaTeX content to Unicode using LatexToUnicodeFormatter and trim the result before returning it for display.
- getDisplayName() now returns a joined list of bibtex fields (using FieldName.FIELD_SEPARATOR) or null for empty columns; getHeaderLabel() returns an icon label for icon columns.
- isResolved(...) compares the resolved field content against the plain entry field to determine whether the displayed value is resolved; it explicitly returns false for entry type or key fields.
- Keep isFileFilter() default (false) so SpecialMainTableColumns can override it.

This change improves the correctness and presentation of values shown in the main table, especially when fields are inherited via crossrefs or defined via strings, and ensures LaTeX content is shown as Unicode for readability.

Fixes issue where a PDF downloader could save HTML source instead of the expected PDF (Fixes #7452).

What I changed
- ExternalFileTypes::getExternalFileTypeByMimeType now strips the parameter part of the mimeType (e.g. "application/pdf; charset=UTF-8" -> "application/pdf") before matching against StandardExternalFileType. This is allowed by the MIME-type specification and ensures correct enum lookup.
- Added a user notification (status bar) when a downloaded file is identified as HTML (e.g. text/html), to avoid confusing users who expect a PDF but received an HTML page instead.

Why
- The older implementation did not consider mimeType parameters, so types like "application/pdf; charset=UTF-8" failed to match the enum and could lead to downloading HTML pages instead of real PDFs. Notifying the user makes the failure visible and avoids silent mis-downloads.

Other notes
- Changelog updated.
- Tests added covering the new mimeType handling.
- Manually tested in running JabRef; screenshots demonstrating the issue and the notification are included in the PR description.

Files/areas touched
- ExternalFileTypes::getExternalFileTypeByMimeType
- StandardExternalFileType usage
- UI status bar notification for download results

This should make external file type detection more robust and improve user feedback when downloads are HTML pages instead of the expected document format.

Summary

This pull request fixes a bug where an empty fallback directory value caused failures when resolving file directories (follow-up to #9113). Previously an empty or blank fallback directory string could be treated as a valid path and lead to incorrect behavior or runtime errors. 

What I changed

- Validate the fallback directory value so that empty or blank strings are treated as "not set" instead of a usable path.
- Fall back to the next valid directory (or the default user directory) when the configured fallback directory is empty or invalid.
- Added defensive checks to avoid NPEs or invalid Path creation when reading fallback directory configuration.
- Minor cleanup to path-handling logic so resolution is more robust against malformed inputs.

Why

An empty fallback directory is not a meaningful configuration and should not be used as an actual path. Treating it as such caused errors in code paths that expect a valid directory. This change makes the application more resilient and prevents those runtime failures.

Testing

- Manually tested in a running JabRef instance by configuring an empty fallback directory and verifying that file resolution falls back to the correct default behavior and no exceptions are thrown.

Notes for reviewers

- This is a follow-up to #9113. Please consider whether a changelog entry or an automated test should be added; I have not included tests in this PR. If preferred, I can add a unit test to assert that empty fallback directory values are ignored.

Summary

Refactors subtle aspects of the optics used for library properties to improve clarity, consistency and maintainability.

What I changed

- Consolidated and cleaned up the optics utilities that operate on library properties (lenses/prisms/paths).
- Standardized naming and signatures so composition is more predictable and easier to read.
- Replaced several ad-hoc getters/setters with composable optics where appropriate.
- Reduced duplication and moved related helpers into a single module to make intent clearer.
- Tightened typings and immutability guarantees around property operations.
- Updated and added unit tests to cover the refactored behavior.

Motivation

- Subtle inconsistencies in the previous optics implementation caused harder-to-track bugs and made composition awkward in a few places. This refactor aims to make the primitives more predictable and to centralize behavior so future changes are easier and safer.

Compatibility and migration notes

- This change is intended to be largely backward-compatible for public APIs that consume library properties via the documented optics. If you were depending on internal implementation details or the old helper locations, you may need to update imports to the new consolidated module.
- If you encounter any edge cases or breaking issues, please point them out in review — I focused on preserving external behavior while improving internals.

Testing

- Unit tests were updated and extended to cover the refactored optics and typical composition scenarios. Please run the test suite to verify behavior in your environment.

Notes for reviewers

- Review the new centralized optics module and the updated tests to validate intent and correctness.
- Pay particular attention to function signatures and any places where the optics are composed across different modules (edge cases tended to appear there previously).

- Simplify OpenSharedDatabaseDialog: delegate connection opening to SharedDatabaseUIManager and remove local BibDatabaseContext management.
- Error handling: restore/open methods can throw SQLException or DatabaseNotSupportedException; failures are logged and fall back to the connection dialog.

Other

text:
Fixes #1450

Summary:
This change prevents an incorrect SplitPane divider value of "1" from being saved when the main table is recreated after preference changes. The previous divider position is now restored from preferences before the mainTable and its SplitPane are recreated, so closing existing EntryEditors during recreation does not capture an already-new SplitPane state.

Problem:
- When preferences change the UI recreates mainTable using a new SplitPane.
- Existing EntryEditors are closed during that recreation which triggers saving the current divider/EntryEditor height.
- Because the SplitPane has already been replaced, the calculated value can be incorrect (becomes "1") and gets written to prefs.

Solution:
- Before recreating the mainTable (and its SplitPane), restore the divider location from preferences into the new SplitPane so any interim saves capture the correct divider value.

Notes:
- CHANGELOG.md updated to describe this change.
- Tests: not added yet.
- Screenshots: not applicable.

How to test manually:
1. Open the application and adjust the entry editor height so the divider is not at the extreme.
2. Change preferences that trigger mainTable recreation.
3. Verify the saved divider location in preferences remains the expected value (not "1").
4. Verify the EntryEditor height/divider position remains consistent across restarts.

Checklist:
- [x] Change in CHANGELOG.md described
- [ ] Tests created for changes
- [ ] Screenshots added (for bigger UI changes)

Convert Custom API key list to an accessible, editable table in Web Search preferences

Summary
- Replaces the previous API key list with a TableView in the Web Search preferences UI, exposing per-fetcher columns for Catalog, Key and Use Custom Key.
- Improves UX by allowing in-place editing of API keys, checkboxes for enabling per-fetcher custom keys, and wiring the test connection button to the selected key.
- Adds a catalog table with clickable rows to toggle enable/disable state.
- Binds and disables related controls (Grobid URL, custom DOI name) to their respective checkboxes.
- Ensures API keys are trimmed when switching selection to avoid leading/trailing whitespace being saved.

Files changed
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preferences/websearch/WebSearchTab.fxml
  - Introduced TableView for apiKeySelectorTable with three columns: Catalog (name), Key (editable text cell) and Use Custom Key (checkbox cell).
  - Added TableView for catalogTable and other layout changes (persist api keys checkbox and tooltip wrapper).

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preferences/websearch/WebSearchTab.java
  - Hooked up TableView columns to FetcherApiKey/StudyCatalogItem properties.
  - Enabled in-place editing for the custom API key column and checkbox cell factory for useCustomApiKey.
  - Bound testCustomApiKey button to the selected API key's use property so it is only enabled when the selected key is active.
  - Added logic to select the first API key when content is loaded and to update/trim the key on selection change.
  - Installed a row factory on catalogTable to toggle enabled state on primary click.
  - Bound enable/disable behavior for grobidURL and useCustomDOIName to their respective checkboxes and added a tooltip when credential store is unavailable.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/preferences/FetcherApiKey.java
  - Simple JavaFX property-backed model for fetcher API keys (name, use, key) with getters, setters and property accessors.

Behavioral notes
- Pressing Return commits edits in the key table (inline editing behavior).
- The persistent API key option is disabled and shows a tooltip if the OS credential store is not available.
- The test connection button becomes available only for the currently selected API key when its "Use" checkbox is set.
- Trimming of API key values on selection change reduces accidental whitespace errors.

Related changelog entry
- This change corresponds to the accessibility improvement listed in the changelog: "We converted the \"Custom API key\" list to a table to be more accessible." (Unreleased).
