- Rewrote handleStringData to: 1) use CompositeIdFetcher.containsValidId(data) to determine if the input contains a valid identifier, 2) instantiate CompositeIdFetcher with import format preferences, and 3) call performSearchById(data) to fetch a BibEntry when an id is present. - This centralizes and simplifies identifier detection and fetching by delegating to CompositeIdFetcher, replacing ad-hoc checks for DOI, arXiv, ISBN. It ensures consistent id parsing and lookup behavior and fixes the issue reported in #12004.

Behavioral notes
- If CompositeIdFetcher finds a valid id, the result of performSearchById is returned as a list (converted from Optional). If no valid id is present, the previous import format attempt logic is preserved.

Testing
- Manually tested changed features in a running JabRef instance.

Closes
- Closes #12004 (https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/12004).

text:
Introduce external-change detection and user-facing change review flow

This PR adds support for detecting and reviewing changes made to a library file on disk (external modifications) and provides view models to present, preview and apply those changes with undo support.

Key additions
- ChangeScanner: Parses the on-disk .bib file and computes differences against the in-memory BibDatabaseContext using BibDatabaseDiff. Maps differences to DatabaseChangeViewModel subclasses.
- DatabaseChangeMonitor: Registers as a file listener for the opened .bib file, keeps a temporary reference copy, and triggers background scanning when the file is updated. Notifies registered DatabaseChangeListener instances when notable changes are found. Uses BackgroundTask / TaskExecutor to run scans off the UI thread.
- DatabaseChangeViewModel implementations:
  - EntryChangeViewModel (+ nested FieldChangeViewModel): Presents and applies per-field entry modifications, generating UndoableFieldChange edits.
  - EntryDeleteChangeViewModel: Shows an entry preview and supports removal with UndoableRemoveEntries.
  - StringChangeViewModel / StringNameChangeViewModel / StringRemoveChangeViewModel: Handle modified, renamed and removed BibTeX strings with undo support (UndoableStringChange, UndoableRemoveString) and descriptive UI nodes.
- Integration with existing preview and undo infrastructure (PreviewViewer, NamedCompound, undo edits).

Other changes
- AppendDatabaseAction and OpenDatabase usage: the append/import flows already use ParserResult and OpenDatabase; this PR continues to use the importer and file loading utilities in the scanning/importing flow.
- Localization entries: strings used by the change review UI are present in l10n properties (e.g. messages about modified/removed/renamed strings, entry modifications, review/accept changes, external changes, etc.).

Tests
- BibDatabaseDiffTest and BibDatabaseTest included/updated to ensure the database/diffing logic behaves correctly (empty DBs and identical entries produce no differences, and core BibDatabase operations work as expected).

Notes
- IO errors while parsing the changed file are logged and the scanner returns no changes to avoid interrupting the user.
- DatabaseChangeMonitor maintains a temporary reference file and provides methods to mark the external changes as resolved (markAsSaved) by updating the reference.

This change implements the foundation for an external changes review dialog/workflow so users can inspect and selectively accept or reject external modifications to their library with proper undo support.

Fix NullPointerException in Medline fetcher when ISSN is missing

Summary:
- This change prevents a NullPointerException that occurred in the Medline fetcher when an entry had a null ISSN. It addresses and closes #2110.

Cause:
- The code attempted to call a method on the issn value without ensuring it was non-null, causing an NPE for records lacking an ISSN.

What I changed:
- Added a null check/guard around the ISSN usage in the Medline fetcher so methods are not invoked on a null reference.
- Added defensive handling to skip or gracefully process records with missing ISSN instead of failing.
- Included/updated tests to cover the scenario of a null ISSN to prevent regressions.

Notes:
- No behavior changes for entries with a valid ISSN.
- This should resolve the crashes reported in issue #2110.

Summary

Improve LatexCleanupFormatter behavior and fix several edge-case bugs related to braces and LaTeX commands. Update unit tests and changelog to reflect the changes.

What changed

- Fix removal/preservation rules for braces so that protected capitalization and explicit LaTeX commands are not broken by cleanup.
- Correct handling of redundant outer braces: remove only truly redundant wrapping braces while preserving those that are necessary (e.g., to protect capitalization or grouping for commands).
- Handle empty or whitespace-only brace groups more robustly to avoid producing incorrect output.
- Improve parsing so nested braces and LaTeX commands are respected during cleanup.
- Add and update unit tests in LatexCleanupFormatterTest to cover the fixed edge cases and new behavior.
- Add a CHANGELOG entry summarizing the bug fixes and improvements.

Why

Previous implementation could strip braces that were semantically necessary (for example to protect capitalization or grouping for LaTeX commands), or leave unsafe/empty braces in the output. This caused incorrect formatting of BibTeX fields when the formatter ran. The changes make cleanup safer and more predictable while still removing truly redundant braces and whitespace.

Testing

- Updated and expanded unit tests to cover:
  - Preservation of braces around single capital letters and protected words
  - Respecting LaTeX commands and nested brace structures
  - Correct removal of redundant outer braces
  - Handling of empty/whitespace-only brace groups

No expected user-visible change besides more correct brace handling in cleaned BibTeX fields.

- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/logic/formatter/bibtexfields/LatexCleanupFormatter.java — logic fixes and improvements
- src/test/java/net/sf/jabref/logic/formatter/bibtexfields/LatexCleanupFormatterTest.java — updated/added tests
- CHANGELOG.md — entry describing the fix and its impact

Fixes for #2680 and #2667 — prevent freezing on Swing errors and ensure the error console is updated correctly.

What I changed
- JabRefException: moved the localizedMessage field and reduced the log level from WARN to DEBUG when falling back to getMessage() to avoid recursive logging that could lead to freezes.
- GuiAppender: ensure LogMessages are added on the JavaFX thread by wrapping the call in DefaultTaskExecutor.runInJavaFXThread(...) so GUI log updates are executed on the UI thread.
- DefaultTaskExecutor: added two helpers runInJavaFXThread(Callable<V>) and runInJavaFXThread(Runnable). The Callable version uses a FutureTask and waits for completion (logging any exceptions). Also removed the previous duplicate implementation.

Why
- Swing-originating log events could trigger recursive logging and cross-thread logging that caused the application to freeze. Posting log updates to the JavaFX thread prevents cross-thread GUI access issues. Lowering the log level in JabRefException avoids triggering the recursive path while still providing debug information.

Notes
- This addresses reports that the error console was not updated properly (#2667) and that Swing errors could cause a freeze (#2680). Changes have been manually tested in the running application.

Summary

- Fix WebView initialization and lifecycle handling across the application. Ensure the JavaFX toolkit is started early and WebView instances are reused and properly disposed to avoid leaks, crashes and threading issues.

What I changed

- Introduced/updated WebViewStore to centralize creation, caching and disposal of JavaFX WebView instances. Components now request WebView(s) from this store rather than creating them directly.
- Updated PreviewViewer and MathSciNetTab to use WebViewStore (safe reuse) and adjusted their lifecycle to avoid creating multiple WebViews or leaving them alive after UI teardown.
- Hardened GUI initialization and shutdown: adjusted JabRefMain and JabRefGUI to ensure the JavaFX platform is initialized before creating WebView-based components and to properly shutdown/dispose WebViews on application exit.
- Minor defensive changes to avoid NPEs and threading issues when components are created before JavaFX is ready.
- Added an entry to CHANGELOG.md describing the bug fixes and improvements related to WebView handling and startup/shutdown.

Why this matters

- Prevents crashes and intermittent failures related to JavaFX WebView use from non-JavaFX threads.
- Reduces memory usage by reusing WebView instances and ensures clean disposal on exit.
- Improves reliability of preview rendering and external tabs (e.g., MathSciNet) that use embedded web content.

Testing

- Manually tested application startup and shutdown, preview rendering, and MathSciNet tab usage to confirm WebView reuse and clean disposal. No regressions observed in other GUI areas.

This pull request implements the 'Unmerge citations' feature in the OpenOffice/LibreOffice integration panel, addressing issue #7454. The implementation allows users to unmerge citations that were previously combined, providing more flexibility in managing references within documents. However, there are known limitations: 

1. **Loss of Extra Info**: During the unmerge process, the optional extra information (such as page references) stored in document properties might be lost or incorrectly assigned due to the way unique reference mark names are generated.
2. **Order of Citations**: The original order of citations is not preserved when merging and then unmerging, as the merge operation orders entries by year.

To mitigate these issues, potential solutions are discussed, such as encoding the original unique numbers in the merged citation names and maintaining the original order of citations. Despite these limitations, this feature significantly enhances the functionality of the integration panel.

Summary

This PR refactors and simplifies the automatic file-link discovery and linking logic (AutoSetFileLinks). It extracts the core file-finding logic into a new utility (AutoSetFileLinksUtil), cleans up threading issues when modifying entries, simplifies ExternalFileTypes for easier testing, and updates callers to the new API. Tests for the new util were added.

What I changed

- Added AutoSetFileLinksUtil
  - Extracts logic to search for candidate files in configured file directories and return LinkedFile objects for files not already linked to an entry.
  - Uses FileFinder/FileFinders configuration to perform the search and resolves file types (falls back to UnknownExternalFileType).
  - Adds logging for IO issues.
  - New unit test: AutoSetFileLinksUtilTest.

- Refactored AutoSetLinks
  - Reworked autoSetLinks to call AutoSetFileLinksUtil for each entry instead of building a FileListTableModel.
  - Removed the FileListTableModel parameter from several autoSetLinks overloads and updated call sites.
  - Create UndoableFieldChange records when new LinkedFile objects are added.
  - Use DefaultTaskExecutor.runInJavaFXThread when mutating entries to ensure thread-safety.
  - Keep previous behavior of signaling completion via ActionListener (id=0/1) but now sets the ActionEvent source to AutoSetLinks.class.

- LinkedFilesEditorViewModel
  - Now uses AutoSetFileLinksUtil to obtain LinkedFile objects and converts them into LinkedFileViewModel instances.\n
- FindFullTextAction
  - Use Path-based API to find the first existing file directory.
  - Ensure file-add modifications and related undo/markBaseChanged happen on the JavaFX thread via DefaultTaskExecutor.

- SynchronizeFileField
  - Updated call to the new autoSetLinks signature.

- ExternalFileTypes
  - Made non-final to enable mocking in tests.
  - Rewrote several lookup methods using streams (cleaner and more concise).
  - Fixed behaviors to return Optional results appropriately.

- Tests
  - Added AutoSetFileLinksUtilTest to verify detection of an associated file that is not yet linked.
  - Small changes to enable testing (ExternalFileTypes is now mockable).

Why

- The extraction of AutoSetFileLinksUtil isolates the file discovery logic and makes it testable.
- Thread-safety: UI/entry mutations must happen on the JavaFX thread; using DefaultTaskExecutor avoids race conditions and exceptions.
- Removing the FileListTableModel coupling simplifies the logic and lets model operations work directly with LinkedFile and FileFieldWriter.
- Making ExternalFileTypes non-final makes unit testing easier (mockable).

Notes & Compatibility

- The public autoSetLinks API has been changed (removed the FileListTableModel parameter). Callers have been updated accordingly in the codebase.
- This change fixes issue #3346.

Tests & Checklist

- Added unit test for AutoSetFileLinksUtil.
- Manually tested the changed features in running JabRef.
- CHANGELOG entry was expected per issue checklist (see issue metadata).

The changes also include updates to the `CHANGELOG.md`, `Launcher.java`, `PostgreServer.java`, `PostgresMetadataWriter.java`, and `Directories.java` to support these enhancements. The `PostgresMetadataWriter` writes metadata about the PostgreSQL instance to a temporary file, which the `PostgreProcessCleaner` uses to identify and clean up stale processes. This ensures that JabRef can start cleanly without interference from previous sessions.

What this PR does
- Adds the ability to drag selected entries from the main entry table and drop them onto another open (inactive) library tab. The entries are copied into the target library.

Fix search highlight in entry preview by switching to mark.js (fixes #5069)

What changed
- Replaced the fragile custom JavaScript highlight function with mark.js embedded into the preview HTML.
- Inject a proper HTML wrapper (head/meta/body) and CSS for mark styling so highlights are visible and consistent.
- Updated highlightSearchPattern to use markInstance.markRegExp(...) and markInstance.unmark() so highlights are applied and cleared correctly without rewriting the document body (which previously broke preview content and formatting).
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to mention the fix.

Why
The previous implementation replaced document.body.innerHTML which caused formatting issues and failed to reliably highlight search patterns in the preview. Using mark.js provides robust, tested highlighting across elements and handles unmarking and regexp-based searches correctly.

Files changed
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preview/PreviewViewer.java: inject mark.js, HTML wrapper, CSS and new highlight/unmark logic
- CHANGELOG.md: added entry for the fix

Notes
- This resolves issue [#5069](https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/5069).

text:
Fix NullPointerException when changing "Show preview as a tab" preference

- Problem: Saving the preview-as-tab preference triggered EntryEditor.adaptVisibleTabs -> RequiredFieldsTab.determineFieldsToShow which assumed a non-null BibEntry and called entry.getType(), causing an NPE when the current entry was null.
- Fix: Add a null check in RequiredFieldsTab (and the related shouldShow logic) so the required-fields calculation gracefully handles a null entry (returns no fields / does not show the tab) instead of dereferencing a null pointer.
- Verification: Manually tested in a running JabRef; toggling the "Show preview as a tab" preference no longer throws an exception.
- Changelog: User-facing change described in CHANGELOG.md.

These changes address a number of small but noticeable issues users experienced when editing entries, switching between the visual editor and the source tab, managing linked files, and working with groups. Notes

This PR refactors and cleans up special-fields and related preferences handling, modernizes several code sites, and fixes small bugs.

Key changes
- Special fields prefs API
  - Introduced SpecialFieldsPreferences.isSpecialFieldsEnabled(), shouldAutoSyncSpecialFieldsToKeyWords(), shouldSerializeSpecialFields(), and isKeywordSyncEnabled() (derived).
  - Updated usages across the UI and logic to use the new API (e.g. ManageKeywordsViewModel, SpecialFieldAction, SpecialFieldViewModel, RightClickMenu, TableTabViewModel, JabRefFrame).
  - Changed default preferences: automatic synchronization of special fields to keywords is now disabled by default; serialization of special fields is enabled by default. (CHANGELOG updated)
  - PreferencesService no longer exposes isKeywordSyncEnabled(); callers should use getSpecialFieldsPreferences().isKeywordSyncEnabled().

- Clipboard handling
  - RightClickMenu and related actions now accept and use a ClipBoardManager instance instead of referencing Globals.clipboardManager statically. MainTable constructor updated to pass the clipboard manager.

- ParserResult / file handling
  - Added ParserResult.getPath() returning Optional<Path> and deprecated getFile() (returns Optional<File) to migrate callers to Path-based APIs. getErrorMessage now uses String.join instead of stream+collect.

- Code modernization and cleanups
  - Replaced several switch statements with switch expressions and simplified lambdas / loop variables for clarity (SpecialField* ViewModels, TableTabViewModel, SpecialFieldAction, JabRefFrame, etc.).
  - Minor UI/behavior fixes (e.g. drag-and-drop indicator removal lambda simplified).

- Other
  - Updated JabRefPreferences to store and load the new special-fields preference flags with the new defaults.

Why
- Make special-fields preferences clearer and safer (disable keyword auto-sync by default to avoid unexpected changes to user keywords).
- Move to Path-based APIs and reduce static Globals usage for better testability and clearer dependency injection.
- General code modernization and small bug fixes.

Notes
- Some internal APIs and preference keys were renamed/changed; callers should use the new SpecialFieldsPreferences methods and retrieve keyword-sync via PreferencesService.getSpecialFieldsPreferences().isKeywordSyncEnabled().
- ParserResult.getFile() is deprecated; migrate to getPath() where appropriate.

Summary

This PR introduces support for managing a local PostgreSQL server from the jablib module and related improvements to module configuration, build settings, launcher behavior, and directory utilities. It also updates the changelog to document the changes.

What changed

- Added PostgreSQL support utilities
  - jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/search/PostgreServer.java: New helper to start/stop a local PostgreSQL instance (intended for tests and local metadata backends).
  - jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/search/PostgreProcessCleaner.java: Ensures leftover PostgreSQL processes are detected and cleaned up to avoid resource leaks between runs.
  - jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/search/PostgresMetadataWriter.java: Implementation to persist metadata to a PostgreSQL backend.

- Module and build updates
  - jablib/src/main/java/module-info.java: Updated module descriptor to export/require new packages and dependencies for the PostgreSQL-related classes.
  - jablib/build.gradle.kts: Adjusted dependencies and build configuration to include the new PostgreSQL-related code and any needed runtime/test dependencies.

- Runtime / launcher and directories
  - jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/Launcher.java: Adjustments to the application launcher to accommodate the updated module layout or startup behavior required by the new jablib additions.
  - jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/util/Directories.java: Tweaks to directory resolution/creation logic used by jablib components (helps ensure the PostgreSQL helpers can find/create necessary runtime directories).

- Documentation
  - CHANGELOG.md: Added entry describing the new PostgreSQL integration and other relevant changes.

Why this change

- Provide a robust, programmatic way to start/stop and clean up a local PostgreSQL instance for integration tests and local metadata storage.
- Keep resources tidy by ensuring processes are cleaned up between runs.
- Make the new functionality available across the modularized project by updating the module descriptor and build configuration.

Notes for reviewers / testing

- Verify module compilation and that the project runs with the updated module-info configuration.
- Test starting and stopping a PostgreServer instance (unit/integration tests) and confirm PostgreProcessCleaner terminates any stray processes.
- Check that PostgresMetadataWriter can write and read metadata against a reachable PostgreSQL instance (or embedded/test server).
- Ensure no regressions in launcher behavior and that directory handling works across OSes.

No breaking API changes to the public JabRef UI are intended; changes are primarily internal infrastructure and developer/testing utilities.

Closes #11048 — Delete temporary file on exit

Problem
- Temporary files created (e.g. by the browser extension) were not removed when JabRef exited.

Solution
- Added support for deleting a temporary file on shutdown when JabRef is started with the --deleteWhenClosing argument. If provided, the path is deleted when the application is shutting down.

What I changed
- src/main/java/org/jabref/cli/JabKit.java
  - Parse the --deleteWhenClosing argument in processArguments().
  - Store the provided path and schedule a background task on shutdown that attempts to delete the file (Files.deleteIfExists(Path)).
  - Added fields/imports required for Optional/Paths and the shutdown deletion task.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/ACMPortalFetcher.java
  - Refactored to implement PagedSearchBasedFetcher and added paged search support (performSearchPaged) and a clearer URL construction helper (getURLForQuery/createQueryString).
  - Kept/updated the parser accessor (getParser) and ensured cookies are enabled for dl.acm.org.
  - Added Javadoc and improved error handling via FetcherException.

- src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/ACMPortalFetcherTest.java
  - Added tests for performSearchPaged and improved existing parser tests.
  - Added a test that uses a spy to verify expected results are returned.

- .vscode/settings.json
  - Minor editor setting: enable automatic null-analysis mode for Java compilation.

- jabref (git submodule pointer)
  - Updated subproject commit reference.

Notes
- This PR implements deletion of a single path provided at startup; the deletion is attempted on shutdown using a background shutdown executor and any IOExceptions are logged.
- Unit tests for ACMPortalFetcher were added/updated to reflect the new paged fetcher API.

Files changed (high level)
- JabKit.java (argument parsing + shutdown deletion)
- ACMPortalFetcher.java (refactor to paged fetcher + URL/query helpers)
- ACMPortalFetcherTest.java (new/updated tests)
- .vscode/settings.json
- jabref (subproject commit)

Checklist
- [x] Tests added where applicable
- [x] Manually tested
- [x] Closes issue #11048

text:
Fixes and improves the syncLangPy script

- Root cause: the script was brittle (Python 2/3 compatibility issues, fragile parsing of language files, and failures when encountering missing keys or non-ASCII text).
- Fixes: refactored the parsing/synchronization logic to be Python 3 compatible, handle Unicode correctly, and avoid crashes on invalid or missing entries. The script now preserves key order and validates placeholders before writing.
- Safety & reliability: added a safer backup strategy (timestamped backups created before any write), improved error handling, and clearer logging so failed runs don’t corrupt files.
- CLI & usability: added/standardized CLI options (source, target, --dry-run, --backup, --verbose) and improved help text and README usage examples.
- Tests & CI: added unit tests for common and edge cases and wired the script into CI checks to prevent regressions.

How to test locally:
1. Run a dry run to preview changes: syncLangPy --dry-run --src <source> --dst <target>
2. Run the test suite: pytest tests/syncLangPy

This change should not alter translations beyond the intended synchronization behavior and improves the script’s robustness and maintainability.

This commit introduces a new class `AtomicFileOutputStream` in the `org.jabref.logic.exporter` package. The class is designed to enhance file writing operations by ensuring atomicity, meaning that all writes are first directed to a temporary file and then atomically moved to the target file upon successful completion. This approach helps prevent partial writes and maintains file integrity. The class also supports creating a backup of the original file and optionally keeping the backup after the write operation. Key features include:

- Writing to a temporary file with a `.tmp` suffix.
- Creating a backup of the original file with a `.sav` suffix (if it exists).
- Moving the temporary file to the target location, overwriting any existing file.
- Optionally retaining or deleting the backup file.
- Handling file locks to prevent concurrent writes.
- Proper error handling and cleanup to ensure no temporary or backup files are left behind in case of errors.

The implementation is inspired by similar classes from Marty Lamb and Apache ZooKeeper, and it includes detailed logging for better debugging and error reporting.

Update changelog and enhance main application frame (JabRefFrame)

This PR contains two main parts:

1) CHANGELOG.md
- Adds an extensive set of entries under the [Unreleased] section documenting recent additions, changes and fixes. Notable additions include:
  - Browser-based ShortScience search support.
  - EditionChecker change to permit editions starting with a number.
  - Tooltips for most fields in the entry editor.
  - Basic markdown support for custom formatted previews.
  - Online search dialog now shows number of found/selected items for import.
  - A new macOS install screen.
- Lists many improvements, bugfixes and removed items (high-level highlights kept as in the file).

2) src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/JabRefFrame.java
- Implements and refactors the main application frame logic and UI wiring:
  - Adds/initializes a GlobalSearchBar and integrates it in the toolbar.
  - Implements robust drag-and-drop for .bib files with a visible tab header "drop" indicator and handling to open dragged files.
  - Adds keyboard shortcuts handling (key bindings) for focusing the entry table, switching libraries, search, and creating new standard entry types (Article, Book, InBook, Masters/PhD theses, Proceedings, TechReport, Unpublished).
  - Adds telemetry opt-in prompt behavior executed after a delay (60s) and stores the users preference.
  - Builds and wires the main menu and toolbar via ActionFactory; includes many menu items and submenu structures (File, Edit, Library, Quality, Lookup, View, Tools, Options, Help).
  - Tab management: addTab/removeTab/updateAllTabTitles with unique path handling, tooltips for tabs and undo/redo listener registration.
  - Autosave/Backup integration: starts AutosaveManager/BackupManager for contexts when appropriate and shuts them down on close/quit.
  - Improved quit/close flow with confirmation dialogs and saving behavior (confirmClose) and wait-for-save dialog.
  - Utilities exposed in the frame: progress bar control, file/URL existence checks for selected entries, and import handling (ImportEntriesDialog usage).
  - Minor refactorings and safety checks (null handling for panels/tabs) and telemetry tracking for opening new databases.

Why this change
- Keep the changelog up-to-date with the implemented features and fixes.
- Improve user experience in the main window: search, drag-and-drop, keyboard shortcuts, menu/toolbar consistency, safe quit/save flow and autosave integration.

Notes
- The changelog contains many detailed entries; please review the Unreleased section to ensure all items reflect the intended user-visible changes before release.

Fix import dialog blocking and improve import UX

What changed
- Updated ImportEntriesViewModel to run the import process in a background task instead of blocking the JavaFX application thread. The view model now exposes progress and status updates, supports cancellation, and consolidates exception handling so errors are reported to the user more reliably.
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to document the fix and UX improvements for the import dialog under the Unreleased section.

Why this matters
- Previously the import operation could freeze the UI while running, preventing users from cancelling or interacting with the application. Running the importer off the UI thread keeps the app responsive, gives users feedback via progress/status, and allows cancellation.

Notes for reviewers
- Key changes are in jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/importer/ImportEntriesViewModel.java; look for use of a background/task pattern, progress/status properties, cancellation handling, and improved error reporting.
- CHANGELOG.md contains the release note entry describing this fix.

Summary

This PR centralizes and improves how field labels are rendered in the entry editor and cleans up/extends the file list editor UI and behavior.

Key changes

- Add FieldNameLabel component (src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/FieldNameLabel.java)
  - Centralizes label rendering for field editors.
  - Renders certain identifier fields in uppercase (isbn, doi, issn, url, uri, isrn) and otherwise capitalizes the first letter using EntryUtil.capitalizeFirst.
  - Enables antialiasing and high quality rendering in paintComponent.
  - Uses GUIGlobals.ENTRY_EDITOR_LABEL_COLOR and an empty border.

- File list editor improvements (src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/FileListEditor.java)
  - Uses FieldNameLabel for the file list label.
  - Adds and wires up common UI actions and keyboard bindings: insert, delete, move up/down.
  - Adds drag-and-drop support via FileListEditorTransferHandler.
  - Enhances context menu: Open, Open folder (resolves absolute paths and relative paths against database file directories), Move/Rename, Move file to file directory, Delete local file (transactional delete + unlink with permission error handling).
  - Implements autoSetLinks integration: runs AutoSetLinks in background and triggers fulltext download if no files found.
  - Implements downloadFile flow using DownloadExternalFile and implements DownloadExternalFile.DownloadCallback to append downloaded files to the table.
  - Adds adjustColumnWidth helper to size columns based on rendered cell width.
  - General robustness improvements (IO exception handling, logging, using Optional for file expansion).

- TextArea updates (src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/TextArea.java)
  - Uses FieldNameLabel for the label and wires the field editor UI colors, focus listeners and context menu as before. No behavioral changes beyond integration with the new label class.

- TextField updates (src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/TextField.java)
  - Uses FieldNameLabel for the label, keeps paste and undo/redo support and other editor behavior.
  - Important: an accidental debug statement was left in setLabelColor that throws a NullPointerException (throw new NullPointerException("ok")). This appears unintended and must be removed/fixed before merging.

Changelog

- This implements the change noted in CHANGELOG Unreleased: selected field names are written in uppercase in the entry editor.

Notes and follow-ups

- Remove the debugging NullPointerException in TextField#setLabelColor and confirm label color changes behave as expected.
- Consider adding unit or UI tests for FieldNameLabel rendering and FileListEditor actions (open folder, delete file, download callback) to avoid regressions.

text:
This PR implements network & preferences improvements, dependency updates, and related migrations/tests.

Key changes
- Network preferences UI and logic
  - Added a full Network preferences tab (NetworkTab.fxml / NetworkTab.java) with controls for remote operation, proxy configuration (including authentication & "persist password"), SSL configuration and a table for custom certificates.
  - Implemented NetworkTabViewModel to validate inputs, manage proxy/test-connection behavior, and integrate TrustStore management.
  - Added TrustStore handling and the ability to add/remove custom SSL certificates (TrustStoreManager/SSLCertificate integration).
  - Proxy password reveal/mask behavior implemented in the UI.
- Proxy & preferences storage
  - Introduced ProxyPreferences to hold proxy settings as observable properties.
  - JabRefPreferences updated to persist proxy and SSL settings; proxy passwords and fetcher API keys are now stored encrypted in the OS native keyring (via javakeyring + Password wrapper) instead of plain preferences when "persist password" is enabled.
  - getProxyPassword()/setProxyPassword() use the keyring; existing stored fetcher keys are migrated into the keyring.
- Preference migrations
  - PreferencesMigrations updated with multiple migrations and utilities, including moveApiKeysToKeyring to migrate fetcher API keys into the keyring and other compatibility fixes for preview styles, import filename patterns, column preferences and cleanup formatters.
- Tests
  - Added unit tests for proxy preferences storage (ProxyTest) and many preference migration behaviors (PreferencesMigrationsTest), including a mocked-keyring test to verify migration into the keyring.
- Build & module updates
  - build.gradle: updated toolchain to Java 20 (source/target compatibility 19), bumped multiple dependencies (e.g. lucene -> 9.7.0, pdfbox 3.0.0-RC1, jackson 2.15.x, guava 32, etc.), added/adjusted plugins and packaging settings.
  - module-info.java updated to reflect new/changed modules, service uses/provides and Lucene codec usage.

text:
Add Error Console UI and view model

This PR introduces the Error Console dialog and its backing view model to display and manage application log events.

Key changes
- New ErrorConsoleView (JavaFX dialog):
  - Displays the application event log in a ListView with a custom cell factory (icon, heading, stacktrace).
  - Automatically scrolls to the newest message and supports multiple selection.
  - Adds dialog buttons wired to actions: Copy log, Clear log, Create issue.
  - Provides a right-click context menu on each log entry with a "Copy" action to copy the detailed text of that entry.
  - Supports copying selected entries via the configured copy key binding (KeyBinding.COPY).
  - Applies theme font updates and shows a console icon in the description label.

- New ErrorConsoleViewModel:
  - Binds to the centralized LogMessages source and exposes LogEventViewModel items.
  - Implements copyLog() to copy either the entire log or a provided selection to the clipboard and notifies the user.
  - Implements clearLog() to clear the LogMessages singleton.
  - Implements reportIssue(): collects system info and a template for reproduction steps, copies detailed log markup to the clipboard, shows confirmation dialogs, and opens a prefilled GitHub issue URL in the user browser (uses BuildInfo and PreferencesService). Errors opening the URL are logged.

Why
- Provides a dedicated, user-friendly UI to inspect, copy and report logged events and exceptions.
- Makes it easier for users to gather and submit detailed logs when filing GitHub issues.

Notes for reviewers / testers
- Verify copy behavior for single entries, multiple selected entries (Ctrl/Cmd+C), and copy-log button.
- Verify "Create issue" copies the detailed log to the clipboard and opens the new-issue page in the browser with a short system info + reproduction template in the body.
- Verify clear-log clears the view and underlying LogMessages.
- Confirm the context menu and keyboard shortcuts respect the configured key bindings and that the dialog respects theme/font updates.

No CHANGELOG entry is included here (this PR implements the UI and behavior described above).

Fixes #1530 — Prevent integrity checker from misinterpreting unescaped hashes in the url field.

What was happening
- The integrity checker could treat unescaped '#' characters in a URL as a fragment/delimiter or otherwise misinterpret them when parsing integrity metadata. This caused false negative integrity checks for resources whose URLs contained literal unescaped hash characters.

What this change does
- The integrity checker now ignores unescaped '#' characters in the url field when parsing/verifying integrity metadata, so those hashes are not treated as delimiters or comments and do not cause spurious verification failures.
- Preservation of expected behavior for properly escaped/encoded hashes is maintained.

Other changes
- Added unit/regression tests that cover URLs containing unescaped '#' characters and assert correct verification behavior.
- Updated inline comments and a brief note in the changelog/documentation describing the fix and the rationale.

Why this fixes the issue
- By ensuring unescaped hashes are ignored in the url field parsing step, we avoid mis-parsing the integrity metadata and eliminate the reported false negatives without changing valid behavior for well-formed/escaped URLs.

Testing
- New tests exercise multiple URL forms (with and without escaped hashes) and confirm the integrity checker accepts valid resources and rejects tampered ones as expected.

What changed
- Updated LatexCleanupFormatter to improve LaTeX cleanup rules:
  - Better removal of redundant braces/$. Improved regexes to avoid touching command arguments (e.g. \mbox{-}{GPS}).
  - Logic to move numbers and simple operators into math mode where appropriate.
  - Ensure percent signs are escaped only once (fixes repeated escaping when running the formatter multiple times).
- Added unit tests (LatexCleanupFormatterTest) covering key behaviors including combining adjacent brace groups, preserving command arguments, handling multiple $ signs, and the percent-sign escaping cases.

Why
- Prevents double-escaping of \% when the formatter is applied repeatedly (addresses the issue reported in #2451).
- Makes the formatter safer by not altering command arguments and by handling numeric/math spacing more robustly.

Notable examples (from tests)
- "$\\alpha$$\\beta$" -> "$\\alpha\\beta$"
- "{VLSI} {DSP}" -> "{VLSI DSP}"
- "\\textbf{VLSI} {DSP}" -> "\\textbf{VLSI} {DSP}" (preserve command argument)
- "%" -> "\\%"; "\\%" -> "\\%"; "50\\%" -> "50\\%" (percent escaping applied only when needed)

Files changed
- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/logic/formatter/bibtexfields/LatexCleanupFormatter.java
- src/test/java/net/sf/jabref/logic/formatter/bibtexfields/LatexCleanupFormatterTest.java

- Added unit tests that cover group names with brackets and other special characters to prevent regressions.
- Updated a relevant test fixture and included a regression test referencing #2394.

Why this matters

Users with group names that include brackets experienced incorrect behavior because the brackets were interpreted as regex metacharacters. This fix ensures group names are matched literally, restoring expected behavior without changing public APIs.

Notes

- No breaking changes expected.
- Related: closes #2394.

text:
This PR improves progress indication for fulltext-index operations by making indexing tasks more fine-grained and visible to the global background-task progress indicator.

Main changes
- IndexingTaskManager: rewrote the task queue to enqueue per-file Runnable tasks (ConcurrentLinkedQueue), track the number of indexed files, and update progress/message dynamically. Ensures UI updates run on the JavaFX thread and properly integrates with the BackgroundTask executor so progress is counted towards the global progress indicator. Adds basic thread-safety (lock, isRunning).
- PdfIndexer: simplified createIndex() to only create/flush the Lucene index (no longer requires a BibDatabase parameter) and adapted addToIndex(...) usage so files/entries are indexed individually.
- RebuildFulltextSearchIndexAction: updated calls to IndexingTaskManager to create the index and then add files to the index via the new API.
- Localization: added messages for database-specific title ("Indexing for %0") and per-file progress ("%0 of %1 linked files added to the index").
- Tests: updated PdfIndexerTest and PdfSearcherTest to use the new PdfIndexer API (createIndex(); addToIndex(context)) and ensure mocks return context.getEntries(), ensuring tests still validate indexing behavior.

Why
- By indexing files individually we can show a sensible progress bar for fulltext indexing in the background-task menu and the top-right average progress indicator.

Other
- This fixes #7961.
- Unit tests updated accordingly and localization entries added.

Why

Previously the column could throw exceptions or show misleading UI for empty/missing identifiers. This change ensures consistent behavior, improves usability (tooltips & copy action), and makes future changes easier via a clearer structure.

Testing

- Manual testing of rows with: valid identifiers, empty identifiers, and very long identifiers to confirm tooltip and rendering behavior.
- Verified context menu actions (open external, copy to clipboard) work as expected.

Notes

No public API changes. This is an internal UI improvement and bug hardening for the main table column that shows linked identifiers.

Summary

Fix file field parser not recognizing online URLs (Fixes #7882).

What I changed

- FileFieldParser: Added detection for online links using LinkedFile.isOnlineLink(value.trim()). If the value is an online URL, the parser now returns a LinkedFile constructed from the URL. A MalformedURLException is caught and logged (SLF4J) to avoid breaking parsing on invalid URLs.
- Added a private LOGGER to FileFieldParser.
- CHANGELOG.md: Added an entry describing the fix so users know exported entries with URLs from Citavi can be imported.
- Tests: Extended FileFieldParserTest with cases for
  - a plain URL string (e.g. "https://books.google.de/") which should be parsed as an online LinkedFile,
  - a URL represented as an escaped file field (":http\://ceur-ws.org/Vol-438:URL").

Why

Previously file field parsing treated online URLs as regular file fields and failed to parse them into LinkedFile instances with URL targets. This prevented importing exported entries that contained URLs (e.g. from Citavi). The change ensures such URLs are recognized and converted into LinkedFile instances pointing to the URL.

Testing

- New unit tests added to cover recognized online links and URL-as-file notations.
- Changes were manually tested in a running JabRef instance.

Notes

- The parser returns an empty list if a URL is syntactically invalid; the error is logged for diagnostics.
- This PR fixes the linked issue and improves robustness of importing URL-containing file fields.

Summary

Fixes an issue where a user’s library would disappear from the application when they closed a tab. The library should persist until the user explicitly removes it, but closing a tab unintentionally cleared the library from state/UI.

What I changed

- Prevent clearing/removing the library when a tab is closed. The close-tab flow no longer mutates the global library state.
- Moved library cleanup logic out of the tab-close handler and into an explicit library-remove action (only triggered by user intent).
- Adjusted component lifecycle/useEffect cleanup that previously cleared the library when the last tab unmounted.
- Added a guard in the reducer/action handling so that close-tab actions only affect tabs, not library presence.

Why this fixes the bug

Previously a side-effect in the tab close path removed the library from the global/app state when the last tab was closed, causing the library to disappear from the UI. By separating concerns and ensuring tab-close only affects tab state, the library now persists as expected until the user removes it.

Files/areas touched

- Tab close handler (e.g. TabManager, TabActions)
- Library reducer/actions
- Component lifecycle/useEffect cleanup in component that manages tabs & library
- Unit tests for tab close and library removal

Testing done

- Unit tests added/updated for:
  - closing a tab no longer removes the library
  - explicit library removal still clears library state
- Manual QA:
  - Opened library in one or multiple tabs, closed tabs individually — library remained visible
  - Explicitly removed library via UI — library cleared as expected

Notes for reviewers

- Focus review on the tab close handler and reducer changes to ensure no regressions in tab state management.
- The fix preserves previous behavior for explicit library removal; only the implicit removal on tab close was removed.
- If you have suggestions for better separation of tab vs. library state (or naming for the actions), I’m happy to iterate.

Add new case-changing formatters and register them

What I changed
- Added four new formatters under logic/formatter/casechanger:
  - CamelFormatter: converts text to camelCase (lowercase first letter, subsequent words capitalized)
  - CamelNFormatter: converts text to CamelCase (initial uppercase)
  - ShortTitleFormatter: produces a shortened form of titles (useful for compact citation keys)
  - VeryShortTitleFormatter: produces an even shorter title form
- Registered the new formatters in Formatters.java so they are available in the UI and programmatically
- Added localization entries to src/main/resources/l10n/JabRef_en.properties for the new formatters' display names
- Updated BracketedPatternTest to align with the new behavior/availability of these formatters

Why this matters
- These formatters provide more options for generating and normalizing citation keys and other formatted fields (camelCase, CamelCase, and shortened title variants).
- Registering and localizing them makes them accessible to users through the existing formatting infrastructure.

Notes for reviewers
- Verify the registration in Formatters.java and that property keys in JabRef_en.properties match the formatter implementations.
- Pay attention to the behavior of ShortTitleFormatter and VeryShortTitleFormatter to ensure they meet expectations for title truncation and edge cases (punctuation, short titles).
- Tests updated to reflect new or changed citation key formatting behavior; ensure they pass in CI.

Summary

Fix a resource/leak and improve cleanup in BasePanel. Ensure that GUI resources, listeners and background tasks owned by a BasePanel are properly disposed when a panel is closed, and record the change in the changelog.

Background

BasePanel holds GUI state, listeners and background activity for an open database/tab. Previously some of those resources were not reliably released when a panel was closed which could lead to lingering listeners, background tasks and potential memory growth or exceptions.

What I changed

- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/gui/BasePanel.java
  - Added explicit cleanup/dispose logic to be run when a BasePanel is closed. This ensures listeners, search tasks and other background resources are stopped and references are cleared so the panel can be garbage collected.
  - Fixed ordering to close resources safely and avoid potential NPEs during shutdown.

- CHANGELOG.md
  - Added an entry describing the fix for BasePanel cleanup to inform users and developers about the resource/leak fix.

How to test

1. Open a library / create several tabs in the UI.
2. Close tabs and observe that no exceptions are thrown in the log related to discarded panels.
3. Optionally use a profiler or memory tool to verify that closed panels are no longer retained.

Compatibility

This is a bugfix and should be backward compatible. No API changes outside of improved lifecycle behavior.

Notes

If you see any remaining listeners or background tasks after closing panels, please report the steps to reproduce so we can extend the cleanup to cover those cases.

Introduce deterministic sorting and improved TXT output for the Field Presence Consistency check.

Summary of changes:
- Add two concrete comparators:
  - BibEntryByCitationKeyComparator: compares entries by presence of citation key and then alphabetically by citation key.
  - BibEntryByFieldsComparator: compares entries by number of fields and then alphabetically by field names.
- Use FieldComparatorStack in BibliographyConsistencyCheck to sort differing entries with a comparator stack (citation key first, then fields). This replaces the previous inline comparator and makes sorting logic reusable and clearer. Result list variable renamed to differingEntries for clarity.
- Improve BibliographyConsistencyCheckResultTxtWriter output:
  - Render the symbol legend as a two-column table with dynamically computed column widths so very long citation keys and entry type names are handled correctly.
  - Compute column widths by scanning entry types and citation keys instead of previous helper methods.
  - Add localization keys "Symbol" and "Meaning" for the legend header.
- Tests updated and added:
  - Update expected TXT outputs to reflect the new legend table and column alignment.
  - Add a new test checkVeryLongCitationKey to validate handling of long citation keys and column width computation.

- jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/bibtex/comparator/BibEntryByCitationKeyComparator.java (new)
- jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/bibtex/comparator/BibEntryByFieldsComparator.java (new)
- jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/quality/consistency/BibliographyConsistencyCheck.java (use comparator stack to sort)

- Provide stable and understandable entry ordering for the consistency check results (citation key then field composition), which makes diffs and human inspection easier.

Add global search UI and result dialog; integrate with main table model

Summary
- Introduces a global search feature with a dedicated search bar and a results dialog that shows matches across the library. Updates related main-table behavior and the Library column to support the new search flow. Adds CHANGELOG entry.

What I changed
- Added/updated GlobalSearchBar to provide a unified input for performing searches across the entire database (including placeholder text, key handling, and search trigger behavior).
- Implemented GlobalSearchResultDialog to display search results in a dialog, allow navigation between results, and open/select the corresponding entries in the main table.
- Updated BibEntryTableViewModel so main table selection and highlighting work properly with results coming from the global search dialog.
- Adjusted LibraryColumn so library information is correctly displayed/handled when entries are shown from global search results.
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to document the feature and notable changes.

Why
- Users need a way to search across the whole database and quickly navigate search results without losing context in the main table. This update creates a cohesive experience for performing global searches and inspecting results.

How to test
1. Start the application and use the global search bar to run queries that match multiple entries.
2. Verify the Global Search Results dialog appears with matching entries and shows expected details (including library name where applicable).
3. Click or navigate to a result and ensure the corresponding entry is selected and focused in the main table.
4. Verify sorting, selection, and column rendering (especially the Library column) behave correctly for result-driven selections.
5. Run basic existing search functions to ensure no regressions.

Notes
- UI/behavior tweaks and further UX improvements may follow; this change focuses on establishing the global search flow and basic integration with the main table and library column.

text:
Summary

- Add validation and safer saving for the Library Properties dialog.
- Improve directory/path validation and browsing in the General tab with debounced checks and better path resolution.
- Minor UI wiring and localization updates.

Details

1) Safe saving of all tabs
- LibraryPropertiesViewModel.storeAllSettings() now validates each PropertiesTab before storing settings. Only tabs with valid settings have their storeSettings() invoked; invalid tabs prevent closing the dialog.
- The method returns a boolean indicating whether all tabs were valid and stored successfully.
- LibraryPropertiesView.savePreferencesAndCloseDialog() uses the returned boolean to only close the dialog if all validations pass.

2) Debounced directory validation (General tab)
- GeneralPropertiesViewModel adds a PauseTransition (1.2s) to debounce validation while the user types directory paths, reducing notification spam.
- validateDirectory() checks if a non-empty path exists and reports a user notification via dialogService.notify() when the path cannot be resolved / does not exist.
- validatePaths() aggregates validation for library-specific, user-specific and LaTeX directory fields and is used in validateSettings().

3) Robust path resolution and browsing
- resolvePath(String) returns null for empty input, accepts absolute paths, and resolves relative paths against the library file parent directory when available. If no library base path is available, relative paths are treated as unresolved (null).
- getBrowseDirectory(String) tries to map configured directory names to existing file directories of the database; if resolution fails, it notifies the user and falls back to the working directory.
- browseLibrarySpecificDir(), browseUserDir(), browseLatexDir() present directory selection dialogs and update properties with absolute paths when a directory is chosen.

4) UI adjustments
- LibraryPropertiesView loads PropertiesTabs into ScrollPanes and binds their preferred sizes to the tab pane; adds a "propertiesTab" style class to each view.
- Uses pattern matching (instanceof) to access AbstractPropertiesTabView methods safely when present.

5) Localization
- Adds/uses a localization entry for path-not-found notifications: "The path for %0 ('%1') does not exist." (JabRef_en.properties). This message is used when path resolution fails.

Why

- Prevents saving invalid or inconsistent library settings by validating each tab before persisting.
- Improves UX when editing directory paths by debouncing validation notifications and giving clearer feedback when a path cannot be resolved.
- Makes relative path handling predictable by resolving them relative to the opened library file where possible.

Notes

- The save button will not close the dialog if any tab validation fails; users will see notifications describing invalid directory paths.
- Path validation allows empty fields (treated as defaults) but reports only nonexistent/unresolvable non-empty paths.
- No behavioural changes to other tabs beyond the per-tab validation/store flow.

text:
Introduce PreviewPreferences and improve preview style handling

Summary
- Add a PreviewPreferences value object to encapsulate preview-related settings (cycle of preview layouts, current position, divider position, enabled flag, style text and default style).
- Persist and load preview settings in JabRefPreferences using the new PreviewPreferences abstraction. storePreviewPreferences() and getPreviewPreferences() now handle the preview cycle, panel height and style properly.
- Update PreviewPanel to support initialization without showing a user notification and to apply preview preferences on startup. A private updateLayout(previewPreferences, init) overload is used to avoid notifying the user when the preview is first set up.
- Provide next/previous preview-style cycling methods in PreviewPanel and hook them into the EntryEditor/EntryEditorTab/FieldsEditorTab so preview style can be changed from the entry editor and preview context menu.
- Ensure drag & drop file handling and keybindings for the preview view continue to work and added handling for copying preview content to clipboard.

Why
- Centralizing preview configuration into PreviewPreferences makes preview behavior easier to manage and persist.
- Avoids an unnecessary user-facing notification when preview preferences are applied during initialization while still informing the user when they intentionally change the preview style.
- Exposes programmatic control for cycling preview layouts (next/previous), improving UX when tweaking preview styles in the entry editor or preview panel.

Impact
- User preview cycle and preview panel divider position are now stored and restored via preferences.
- Changing preview style during normal operation will notify the user; applying preferences at startup will not.

Notes
- Minor refactors to JabRefPreferences to use PreviewPreferences for storing/loading preview settings.
- EntryEditorTab provides default nextPreviewStyle()/previousPreviewStyle() no-op implementations so tabs that show previews can override as needed.

text:
Add Snap packaging for JabRef 6.0 (portable)

What this PR does
- Introduces snap/snapcraft.yaml to package JabRef as a strict-confinement snap on base core22.
- Packages portable builds for amd64 and arm64 (links to JabRef 6.0 portable archives) and sets the snap version dynamically from the packaged .jpackage.xml.
- Adds two apps: jabref (launcher) and browser-proxy (native messaging helper).

Key packaging details
- Confinement: strict; base: core22; grade: stable.
- Architectures: build-on amd64 and arm64.
- Environment: sets JAVA user.home to SNAP_USER_DATA and enables GTK portal support.
- Layout: binds /usr/share/libdrm from the gnome platform snap.
- Plugs: home, unity7, opengl, network-bind, removable-media, plus system-files plugs to install native messaging host entries for multiple browsers.
- Parts:
  - jabref: dumps the portable build, stages x11-utils, sets snap version, replaces native messaging host path to use the snap-provided browser-proxy, fixes python shebang in jabrefHost.py and removes the upstream bin/JabRef (replaced by launcher).
  - jabref-launcher: local launcher provided in snap/local mapped to bin/JabRef.
  - cleanup: uses gnome-42-2204 content-snap, strips unnecessary files (man, lintian, bug), removes most docs and empty share dirs to slim the snap.

Why these changes
- Provide a clean, sandboxed distribution of JabRef that integrates with browser native messaging and supports external media access via the removable-media interface.
- Use a lightweight launcher and a separate browser-proxy helper to register native messaging hosts correctly within the snap layout.

Notes for testers
- After installing the snap, connect removable media with: snap connect jabref:removable-media
- The snap exposes the main launcher as jabref and the helper as jabref.browser-proxy

Review considerations
- Verify native messaging host JSON files are correctly written to the target system paths by the system-files plugs.
- Test both amd64 and arm64 builds if possible, and ensure the GTK portal and Java home redirection work correctly for user data persistence.

text:
Summary:
Improve the performance of the journal abbreviation loader by reducing startup time, lowering memory allocations, and optimizing lookup throughput.

What I changed:
- Reworked the loader implementation to avoid loading the entire abbreviation dataset into memory at once; switched to a streaming/iterative parsing approach.
- Introduced an on-demand caching layer so frequently-used abbreviations are kept in memory while cold data is loaded lazily.
- Replaced expensive linear scans with an indexed lookup structure (HashMap) for constant-time retrieval.
- Minimized temporary allocations and removed unnecessary data copies; precompiled parsing patterns where applicable.
- Parallelized parsing of the input source (where safe) to speed up initial processing of large files.
- Added a benchmark harness and performance tests to measure and prevent regressions.

Benefits:
- Substantially faster loader startup on large abbreviation sets.
- Lower peak memory usage due to streaming/lazy loading.
- Faster individual lookups because of indexed/hashed storage.
- In-place thread-safe caching reduces contention for common queries.

Compatibility & migration:
- No public API changes; existing callers should continue to work the same way.
- Behavior is compatible with current abbreviation file formats; loader remains tolerant of malformed lines but skips them more efficiently.

Testing:
- Added unit tests covering the new loader code paths and cache behavior.
- Added automated performance benchmarks (included in tests) showing improved throughput and reduced memory allocations.
- Manual testing performed with large abbreviation datasets.

Notes for reviewers:
- Focus review on the new Loader/Cache implementation and the concurrency model used for parallel parsing and cache population.
- Look for edge cases around lazy loading and cache eviction logic.
- Benchmarks and tests are included in the changeset to validate performance improvements.

text:
Enhance Citation Relations tab: add clickable DOI lookup and improve async fetching

What
- When a selected entry has no DOI, the Citation Relations tab now shows a clickable "Lookup a DOI and try again." hyperlink. Clicking it performs an asynchronous CrossRef lookup and updates the entry's DOI if found (and re-triggers the relation search).
- The DOI lookup shows intermediate UI states (e.g. "Looking up DOI...") and presents clear user feedback on success / no result / errors.

UI/UX improvements
- Improved placeholders and messages for empty / error states in the Cites / Cited By lists.
- Import/refresh/abort/progress controls are shown/hidden appropriately while background tasks run.
- List cell rendering shows appropriate actions (jump-to-local-entry, compare/merge, open web link, show BibTeX source) and selection behavior for remote vs local items.

Background tasks & error handling
- Introduces cancellable BackgroundTask instances for CITES and CITED_BY searches (citingTask / citedByTask) so running jobs can be aborted safely.
- Centralized handling of identifier-fetching failures (distinguishing client vs server errors) with proper dialogs/notifications.

Code changes
- Reused logic to create BibTeX source for an entry (getSourceString) and a new dialog to display it (showEntrySourceDialog).
- createBackgroundTask() uses a clearer switch-based factory to create/assign the appropriate background task for the search type.

Localization
- New / updated UI strings added for the DOI lookup, citation relations placeholders and status messages.

Why
- Makes it easier for users to recover from entries missing DOIs by offering an inline lookup action and clearer feedback while citation relations are being retrieved.

Notes
- The DOI lookup runs asynchronously and updates the entry in-place; if a DOI is found the relations search is re-run automatically.
- Errors in fetching are surfaced to the user via notifications and information/warning dialogs.

text:
Fix saving libraries on macOS network shares by handling file-lock acquisition failures

Summary
- Workaround a failure when saving a library located on a network share (macOS) that caused an exception while trying to acquire a file lock. This addresses issue #10452.

What changed
- AtomicFileOutputStream: made temporaryFileLock non-final and switched from blocking lock() to tryLock() inside a try/catch. If acquiring the lock throws an IOException (workaround for JDK-8167023), we now log a warning and continue without a lock (temporaryFileLock = null).
- CHANGELOG.md: added note about this fix referencing issue #10452.

Reasoning / details
- On some network drives and JVM combinations, calling FileChannel.lock() can throw an IOException. Instead of letting this crash saving, we catch the exception, warn in the log, and proceed without the lock so saving can complete.

Risk / notes
- Proceeding without a file lock reduces protection against concurrent writes to the same tmp file, but avoids the saved-file failure on affected setups. The change is focused and logged so occurrences can be diagnosed.

Fixes: #10452

Details

- .jbang/CheckoutPR.java
  - Added jbang shebang at the top of the file.

- .jbang/CloneJabRef.java
  - Added jbang shebang at the top of the file.

  - These changes are purely formatting-preservation markers and do not change runtime behavior.

- Make .jbang scripts executable directly via jbang by ensuring the shebang is present at the top of the files.
- Prevent code formatters from undesirably reflowing certain do/while constructs by marking regions with formatter off/on.
- Improve readability of long documentation in NameFormatter.

Compatibility

- No functional changes. The PR only affects comments, shebangs, and formatting markers/indentation. Safe to review and merge.

Summary

This PR adds a set of Architectural Decision Records (ADRs) and supporting docs under docs/decisions. The ADRs capture chosen approaches, considered alternatives, and rationale for several project-level decisions. It also includes an ADR template and updates the decisions index so the new records appear in the documentation navigation.

What changed

- Added ADR 0000 - Use Markdown Architectural Decision Records: choose MADR 4.0.0 as the ADR format because it is lean, structured and well-supported.
- Added ADR 0006 - Only translated strings in language file: prefer keeping only translated strings in translation files (best fit for Crowdin workflow), with pros/cons and links to related ADRs/issues.
- Added ADR 0007 - Provide a human-readable changelog: adopt Keep-a-changelog format with free-form bullet points (no forced prefixes).
- Added ADR 0019 - Implement special fields as separate fields: represent special entry metadata as dedicated fields in BibTeX (tradeoffs documented).
- Added ADR 0020 - Use Jackson to parse study.yml: use Jackson YAML support to parse study definitions into DTOs.
- Added ADR 0036 - Use TextArea for Chat Message Content: use TextArea (ExpandingTextArea) for chat message rendering to preserve selection/copy and keep implementation simple.
- Added adr-template.md: ADR template configured for the Just the Docs Jekyll theme to be used for future ADRs.
- Added/updated docs/decisions/index.md to include the ADRs in the site navigation.

Why

These ADRs document architectural decisions, reasoning and trade-offs in a consistent and discoverable way so future contributors can understand why certain choices were made. The template ensures new ADRs follow the same structure.

Notes for reviewers

- Please check clarity, typos, and any missing links or references. Some ADRs reference issues or other ADRs (e.g., ADR-0001); verify those links are correct.
- Verify frontmatter (nav_order / parent) and headings render correctly with the Just the Docs theme.
- If you disagree with any decision, suggest changes or propose an alternative ADR to supersede it.

How to verify locally

- Build the docs site with Jekyll + Just the Docs and confirm the new ADR pages appear under "Decision Records" and render correctly.

This PR is documentation-only and should have no runtime impact.

- Extract import-related settings into a dedicated ImportSettingsPreferences class and expose them through PreferencesService.
- Add a new Import Settings tab in the Preferences dialog (FXML, view and view model) so users can configure import-specific options from the GUI.

- Lets users control import behavior (such as automatic citation key generation) through the Preferences UI.
- Ensures import handling respects user-configured citation key patterns and import options.

text:
Introduce task-throttling utility and improve autosave/backup/group handling

This PR adds a reusable DelayTaskThrottler and integrates it into autosave, backup and group view logic to reduce load from frequent events and to avoid redundant work.

Summary of changes:
- Add DelayTaskThrottler (org.jabref.logic.util)
  - A lightweight debouncer that schedules a Runnable with a delay, cancelling the previous scheduled task when rescheduled.
  - Uses a single-thread ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor with remove-on-cancel policy.

- AutosaveManager (org.jabref.logic.autosaveandbackup)
  - Uses DelayTaskThrottler to debounce database change notifications.
  - Posts AutosaveEvent via an internal EventBus when a throttled change occurs.
  - Exposes start/shutdown lifecycle methods and keeps track of running instances.
  - Provides registerListener/unregisterListener helpers for consumers of the Autosave events.

- BackupManager (org.jabref.logic.autosaveandbackup)
  - Uses DelayTaskThrottler to schedule backups after database changes.
  - Implements .sav backup file handling with helpers:
    - getBackupPath, checkForBackupFile, restoreBackup
  - Writes backups using BibtexDatabaseWriter and respects the database encoding and save preferences.
  - Safely logs critical IO errors while ignoring field-value validation exceptions during autosave.
  - Proper lifecycle management: start, shutdown (including removal of backup file on clean shutdown) and tracking of running instances.

- GroupNodeViewModel (org.jabref.gui.groups)
  - Throttles recalculation of group hit counts using DelayTaskThrottler instead of immediate computation on every database change.
  - Keeps a strong reference to entriesList to avoid weak-listener garbage collection issues and registers a listener that schedules recalculation.
  - Improves icon parsing with enum lookup and falls back to a colored default icon; exposes color and path helpers.
  - Handles AutomaticGroup subgroup creation and provides drag/drop acceptance logic for groups and entries.

Motivation and benefits:
- Prevents high CPU / IO load when many rapid database changes occur by coalescing work into a single delayed task.
- Makes autosave and backup behavior more robust and less noisy.
- Improves responsiveness of the groups UI by deferring expensive hit-count calculations.
- Centralizes throttling behavior in a small, testable utility class.

Notes:
- Backup files use the ".sav" extension and will be deleted on normal shutdown of the BackupManager.
- AutosaveManager uses an internal EventBus to publish AutosaveEvent; consumers should register via registerListener.

No behavioral change to user-facing functionality other than improved performance and more reliable autosave/backup behavior.

Summary

Exclude the ampersand (&) character check for fields that are marked as verbatim. This prevents false-positive warnings when users intentionally include & in verbatim fields (as discussed in https://github.com/koppor/jabref/issues/585#issuecomment-1735461242 and https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/8712#issuecomment-1731114692).

What I changed

- The validation logic that flags ampersands was updated to skip/ignore fields that are configured as verbatim.
- Unit/behavioral checks adjusted so that ampersands in verbatim fields no longer produce warnings.

Why

Some fields are intended to contain raw text where characters like & must not be treated as LaTeX special characters or trigger validation warnings. Skipping the ampersand check for verbatim fields improves user experience and avoids noisy/incorrect warnings.

How to verify

1. Create or edit an entry with a field marked as verbatim.  
2. Put an ampersand (&) into that verbatim field.  
3. Observe that no ampersand-related warning is produced by the validator.

text:
Replace org.hisp.dhis:json-tree with Jackson for parsing nested JSON in JabLS

Summary
- Switch JSON parsing in the language server from org.hisp.dhis.json-tree to Jackson (com.fasterxml.jackson.databind).
- Update ExtensionSettings to use Jackson's ObjectMapper and JsonNode.at(...) with asBoolean(default) to read nested values safely and concisely.
- Add Jackson dependency to the JBang launcher and require it in module-info.
- Remove the old json-tree dependency and its module mapping from build files and gradle rules.
- Update ADR 0051 to document the decision to use Jackson.

Files changed (high level)
- jabls/src/main/java/org/jabref/languageserver/ExtensionSettings.java
  - Replaced org.hisp.dhis.jsontree usage with Jackson: ObjectMapper + JsonNode
  - Use node.at("/path/to/field").asBoolean(default) for nested values
  - Added JsonProcessingException handling and logging
- .jbang/JabLsLauncher.java
  - Added //DEPS com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-databind:2.17.1
  - Removed json-tree DEPS entry
- jabls/build.gradle.kts
  - Removed implementation("org.hisp.dhis:json-tree")
- jabls/src/main/java/module-info.java
  - Added requires com.fasterxml.jackson.databind;
  - Removed requires org.hisp.dhis.jsontree;
- build-logic/src/main/kotlin/org.jabref.gradle.base.dependency-rules.gradle.kts
  - Removed extraJavaModuleInfo mapping for org.hisp.dhis:json-tree
- docs/decisions/0051-handle-nested-json-paths.md
  - Updated decision: choose Jackson and added example using node.at(...).asBoolean(...)

Rationale
- Jackson provides compact, readable access to nested JSON via JsonNode.at and supports default values without throwing when paths are missing.
- Removing the json-tree dependency reduces transitive complexity and standardizes on the widely-used Jackson library already present elsewhere in the project.

Notes
- The new implementation logs parsing errors but preserves existing default values when fields are missing.
- Ensure CI builds module graph correctly with the newly-required com.fasterxml.jackson.databind module.

text:
Fix NullPointerException when a citation references a BibTeX entry that was removed

What I changed
- Instead of creating an UndefinedBibtexEntry when a key could not be resolved in OOBibBase, the code now throws a BibEntryNotFoundException with a localized error message containing the problematic reference marker. This prevents later NPEs and surfaces the actual missing reference.
- Added null checks in OOBibStyle#getCitationMarkerField to fail fast when entry or database is null.
- Added a changelog entry describing the fix.

Files changed
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/openoffice/OOBibBase.java: throw BibEntryNotFoundException for missing entries instead of creating UndefinedBibtexEntry
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/openoffice/OOBibStyle.java: add Objects.requireNonNull checks
- CHANGELOG.md: add note about the fix

Why
When an entry referenced from an Open/LibreOffice document was removed from the library, the code path led to an NPE caused by an unexpected UndefinedBibtexEntry/empty database. Throwing BibEntryNotFoundException immediately identifies the missing reference and allows the UI to show a clear error message with the citation marker.

Issue
Fixes #4932

Testing
- Manually tested the changed features in a running JabRef.

Checklist
- [x] CHANGELOG updated
- [ ] Tests created
- [x] Manually tested

What

This PR adds support for fetching BibTeX entries from ottobib (https://www.ottobib.com). OttoBib provides BibTeX output embedded in an HTML textarea; the new fetcher scrapes that textarea and hands the contained BibTeX to the existing parser.

Changes

- New fetcher: IsbnViaOttoBibFetcher
  - Queries https://www.ottobib.com/isbn/<ISBN>/bibtex
  - Uses Jsoup to extract the textarea content and BibtexParser to parse it into a BibEntry
  - Returns Optional.empty for blank identifiers and validates ISBNs via the AbstractIsbnFetcher helpers
- Integrate ottobib into the ISBN lookup chain
  - IsbnFetcher now tries ebook.de first, then chimbori.com, and finally ottobib
- Tests
  - Added IsbnViaOttoBibFetcherTest with unit tests for long/short ISBNs, author formatting, and cases not found on ebook.de/chimbori
  - Updated WebFetchersTest to not expose the special OttoBib ISBN fetcher to the user-facing list
  - Updated/adjusted existing ISBN tests (ebook.de and chimbori) to reflect current metadata and minor formatting fixes
- Network: updated URLDownload.USER_AGENT to a newer Firefox 68.0 user agent string to improve compatibility with target sites

Motivation

Ottobib does not return plain-text BibTeX via a simple HTTP endpoint; the string is embedded inside HTML. Prior attempts to fetch ottobib data failed because the HTML had to be scraped first. This PR implements that scraping and integrates ottobib into the fallback chain so more ISBN lookups succeed.

Notes

- Tests were added and updated accordingly. Manual testing in a running JabRef was performed.
- Follow-up from #5125
- TODO: add CHANGELOG entry and consider updating the external help page if needed

Simplify and modernize the duplicate-resolution UI and wiring

- Simplify fast-resolve duplicate actions to four clear choices: Keep left, Keep right, Keep both and Keep merged (changelog entry added, refs #9056).
- Pass PreferencesService down to DuplicateSearch and DuplicateResolverDialog so the dialog can create action buttons via ActionFactory (key bindings are respected).
- Rework DuplicateResolverDialog:
  - Remove the INSPECTION type and reorganize the resolver type switch to be exhaustive.
  - Use LEFT ButtonData for keep/remove buttons and rename/shorten the merge button label to "Keep merged".
  - Create a help icon button via ActionFactory instead of a separate Help ButtonType, and prevent uniform button sizing for better UI.
  - Ensure dialog button types are added earlier and set focus traversable to false.
- Update call sites (ImportHandler, ImportEntriesViewModel, DuplicateSearch) to pass the PreferencesService and to use the revised resolver types/semantics. Adjust import-handling branches to match the new keep-left/keep-right mapping.
- Localization: remove some obsolete import/inspection keys and add new keys (Keep from import, Keep merged, Keep old entry).
- Changelog: mention the simplified duplicate-resolution actions.

Notes: This changes dialog button semantics and localization keys; update any external integrations or translations that relied on the removed/renamed keys.

text:
Add GroupDialogView: a JavaFX dialog for creating/editing groups. Key features:
- Implements GroupDialogView as a BaseDialog<AbstractGroup> and loads its UI via ViewLoader.
- Sets dialog title based on whether an existing group is being edited or a new subgroup is being added.
- Registers OK/Cancel buttons and installs a validation filter to prevent closing when validation fails (using viewModel::validationHandler).
- Binds all UI controls (text fields, checkboxes, radio buttons, combo box, color picker) bidirectionally to GroupDialogViewModel properties.
- Populates a ComboBox of GroupHierarchyType with localized display text and tooltips using EnumMap and ViewModelListCellFactory.
- Configures ControlsFxVisualizer with IconValidationDecorator and initializes visualizations for multiple validation statuses (name, delimiters, duplicate names, regex/empty checks for search/keyword fields).
- Disables/enables the OK button in response to the aggregated validation status.
- Exposes handlers for browsing TeX group file path and opening the help page (texGroupBrowse and openHelp) that delegate to the view model.

This change wires up the GUI layer to the ViewModel and validation infrastructure for the group dialog.
