text:
Fix NPE when using middle mouse click on Windows (hotfix for #5532)

Summary:
- Prevent a NullPointerException that could occur on Windows when the X11 selection clipboard (primary) is not available (Toolkit.getSystemSelection() can return null on non-X11 platforms).

What I changed:
- Added a default constructor that delegates to the main constructor (keeps initialization consistent).
- Added null checks for the primary clipboard in three places:
  - addX11Support: only call primary.setContents when primary is not null.
  - getContentsPrimary: return system clipboard contents if primary is null; otherwise read safely from primary with exception handling preserved.
  - setPrimaryClipboardContent: only set primary contents when primary is not null.

Why:
- On Windows the primary selection (X11-style middle-click clipboard) is not available, which caused a NPE when code assumed primary was non-null. These checks ensure JabRef falls back to the system clipboard and avoids throwing on middle mouse operations.

Files changed:
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/ClipBoardManager.java

References:
- Fixes issue #5532

text:
Implemented "Unmerge citations" in the OpenOffice/LibreOffice integration panel.

Summary:
- Adds an "Unmerge citations" action that splits a merged citation back into individual reference markers in the document integration panel.
- Updates CHANGELOG to mention the feature.
- Manual testing performed in a running JabRef instance; screenshot added to PR description.

Fixes: #7454

Notes and known limitations:
- No automated tests were added (GUI tests were not provided).
- There is a known problem with the existing "Merge citations" behavior: it does not reliably preserve the information needed to look up optional extra info (for example page references) stored in the document properties. When re-establishing the individual references, getUniqueReferenceMarkName() may or may not return the original reference mark name. If it does not, optional extra info can be lost or incorrectly assigned to another entry.
- Possible approaches to address the above include encoding the uniqueness number in the merged name (e.g. JR_cite_1_XX2000a,1_YY2010) and/or marking the original names as "in use" so getUniqueReferenceMarkName() will not reuse them.
- Another pre-existing issue: combineCiteMarkers currently orders merged entries by year, which loses the original order of citations.

In summary, this change adds the Unmerge feature and improves the integration workflow, but does not fully resolve the underlying problems of preserving optional extra info and keeping original ordering. Follow-up work is recommended to add GUI tests and update the documentation (OpenOffice integration page does not yet mention the Merge/Unmerge buttons; a note in the Known Issues section is suggested).

This PR implements and refines the BibTeX string editor dialog and supporting UI components, improves visual styling, and updates localization entries.

What I changed

- Added/updated the BibTeX String Editor dialog UI and logic
  - src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/metadata/BibtexStringEditorDialogView.java
  - src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/metadata/BibtexStringEditorDialogViewModel.java
  - src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/metadata/BibtexStringEditorItemModel.java

- Improved reusable cell factories and visualization support for view-model backed lists/tables
  - src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/util/ViewModelListCellFactory.java
  - src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/util/ViewModelTextFieldTableCellVisualizationFactory.java

  - src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/Base.css
  - src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/entryeditor/EntryEditor.css

- Localization
  - src/main/resources/l10n/JabRef_en.properties

  Added/updated localization strings used by the new dialog and controls.

Why

- To provide a fully functional, consistent, and styled interface for editing BibTeX strings inside JabRef.
- To reuse improved cell factories for better maintainability and consistent behavior across list and table UI components.

Notes for reviewers / QA

- Verify the BibTeX String Editor opens correctly, lists existing strings, and supports add/edit/remove operations.
- Check editing behavior in-place (text fields) and that changes are reflected in the view model.
- Confirm styling is consistent with other dialogs and that localization keys appear correctly in English.
- Review the cell factories to ensure they do not regress existing list/table behaviors elsewhere in the app.

No breaking API changes expected; changes are UI-focused and limited to the GUI module.

Summary
Fix selection of custom export handler when copying to clipboard if the requested file extension is uppercase.

Problem
Copy-to-clipboard logic matched requested export formats case-sensitively. If a caller requested an uppercase extension (e.g. ".SVG"), the lookup failed to find the custom export definition (registered as ".svg"), causing the wrong handler to be used or fallback behavior.

Solution
Normalize file extensions to a canonical form (lowercase) when selecting the export handler for copy-to-clipboard. The matching logic now performs a case-insensitive comparison so custom exports are selected regardless of extension casing.

Tests
Added tests that exercise copy-to-clipboard selection with uppercase and mixed-case extensions to prevent regressions.

Notes
This is a non-breaking fix — it changes only how export handlers are looked up and does not alter any existing export implementations.

Summary

This PR adds/updates the Gradle build configuration and project ignore rules to standardize the build environment and tooling. The changes centralize code-generation tasks, Java toolchain settings, packaging (jlink/jpackage) configuration, code quality tools, and dependency management.

Key changes

- build.gradle
  - Set Java source/target and toolchain to Java 21.
  - Add and configure multiple plugins: application, modernizer, jmh, javamodularity module plugin, OpenJFX, jlink, test-logger, jacoco, checkstyle, project-report, idea, openrewrite, and SpotBugs.
  - Configure javafx version and modules.
  - Define dependencies (including updates/additions for PDFBox, Lucene, Guava, PostgreSQL, MariaDB, BouncyCastle, ANTLR, Jakarta JAXB, controlsfx, richtextfx, and many others) and lock dependency configurations.
  - Add ANTLR/xjc code-generation tasks and a consolidated generateSource task; configure compileJava to depend on generated sources and set generated source output directory to src-gen/main/java.
  - Add tasks to generate an H2 MVStore for journal lists and make relevant tasks depend on it.
  - Configure test tasks with JUnit 5, separate tags for DatabaseTest/FetcherTest/GUITest, and test logging; add test subsets (databaseTest, fetcherTest, guiTest).
  - Configure JaCoCo reporting collecting multiple execution data files and prepare task to ignore test failures for coverage runs.
  - Configure SpotBugs (with report output) and wire it into the check lifecycle.
  - Configure OpenRewrite and Modernizer behavior.
  - jlink/jpackage configuration: merged module adjustments, forceMerge entries for problematic libraries, OS-specific packaging options (Windows MSI, Linux packages, macOS image) and platform-specific post-processing copy steps.
  - Additional utility tasks (deleteInstallerTemp, copyTestResources, jacocoPrepare) and build clean-up rules (delete generated folders).
  - Misc: processResources templating using environment variables for API keys and project metadata.

- .gitignore
  - Comprehensive ignore rules for IDEs (IntelliJ, Eclipse, NetBeans), OS temp files (macOS/Linux/Windows), build outputs, Node, Snapcraft, Flatpak, Gradle and other tooling artifacts.
  - Keep rules to intentionally include certain files (e.g. /lib/*.jar, buildSrc sources, icons).

Why

- Standardizes the build to Java 21 and configures the toolchain to reduce environment differences.
- Ensures generated sources are produced and compiled consistently (ANTLR, XJC, journal MV store generator).
- Improves developer experience with better test logging, test segregation, and JMH benchmarking support.
- Adds packaging configuration for producing platform-specific distributions via jlink/jpackage.
- Integrates static-analysis and code-quality tooling (SpotBugs, Checkstyle, OpenRewrite, Modernizer, JaCoCo).
- Keeps repository clean from generated or private files via an updated .gitignore.

How to test

- Build and run: ./gradlew clean build
- Generate sources explicitly: ./gradlew generateSource
- Run unit tests: ./gradlew test
- Run tagged tests: ./gradlew databaseTest, ./gradlew fetcherTest, ./gradlew guiTest
- Create distribution images: ./gradlew jlink jpackage (requires platform-specific tools like WiX on Windows)
- Run SpotBugs report: ./gradlew spotbugsMain

Notes

- Some packaging steps (notarization for macOS, WiX for Windows MSI) require external tooling and are configured to run conditionally based on the OS.
- Several workarounds and excludes are present for modularity, non-modular dependencies, and known upstream issues; comments in the build.gradle explain these choices.
- Environment variables used by resource filtering (API keys, instrumentation keys) are read from the environment; missing keys default to empty strings.

If you want, I can split the large build changes into smaller follow-up PRs (e.g., separate dependency updates, modularity/toolchain changes, packaging configuration) to ease review.

text:
Summary

This PR adapts the Windows installer build to the latest jpackage behavior so the project can be built with the updated jpackage version.

What changed

- build.gradle
  - Temporarily disabled the --win-dir-chooser jpackage flag (commented out) because it conflicted with the updated jpackage.

- buildres/windows/JabRef-post-image.wsf
  - Fixed the path used to open the generated .wxs file. The script now reads the .wxs from buildres/windows (jabRefRoot + "/buildres/windows/JabRef.wxs") instead of installerConfig.

- buildres/windows/JabRef.wxs
  - Added a copy of the WiX .wxs file (previously produced by jpackage with a different name/location) into the repo so the build can find and use it during installer creation.

Why

jpackage's output/name/location for the generated .wxs file changed in the newer version, which broke the Windows installer step. To restore a repeatable build, the .wxs is now stored under buildres/windows and the post-image script was updated to open it there. The --win-dir-chooser flag is temporarily disabled because it conflicted with the jpackage update; it can be re-enabled once compatibility is resolved.

Notes

- This is an internal build change; there are no user-facing behavior changes.
- No runtime tests added; the change is intended to make the build pass with the updated jpackage.
- This PR addresses the problems discussed in #5520.

text:
Fix IllegalArgumentException for non-absolute URIs (handles URLs starting with "www.")

What this PR does
- Fixes an issue where URLs beginning with "www." (no protocol) in file fields caused an IllegalArgumentException: "URI is not absolute". (Fixes #12186)
- Adds defensive checks in URLUtil.isURL to return false for null or empty inputs and to require a protocol pattern before attempting parsing.
- Updates URLUtil.create to trim the input and automatically prefix "https://" for strings starting with "www.", ensuring they become absolute URIs. Parsing still throws a MalformedURLException for other inputs that are not absolute.

Tests
- Adds a FileFieldParserTest case for a linked file with a "www." URL.
- Adds URLUtilTest cases: one asserting that a "www.example.com" input is converted to "https://www.example.com", and another ensuring that inputs without a scheme and not starting with "www." (e.g. "example.com") still throw a MalformedURLException.

Other
- Documents the fix in CHANGELOG.md.

Files changed
- jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/util/URLUtil.java: input validation, trimming, and "www." -> "https://" prefixing.
- jablib/src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/util/FileFieldParserTest.java: added test for www URLs in file fields.
- jablib/src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/net/URLUtilTest.java: added/updated tests for the new behavior.
- CHANGELOG.md: added entry describing the fix.

Notes
- The change uses https:// as the default prefix for "www." URLs.
- Please review to confirm this default is acceptable for all callers.

Summary:
- Show preview thumbnails for all available styles in the style selector, not just the currently selected style.

Motivation:
- Help users compare and choose styles faster by providing visual previews for each available option.

What I changed:
- Updated the style selector component to render preview thumbnails for each available style option.
- Added logic to fetch or generate preview images for available styles, with a lightweight caching mechanism to avoid repeated requests.
- Implemented graceful fallbacks if a preview is missing (uses a generated placeholder preview and an accessible label).
- Adjusted layout/CSS so thumbnails display neatly in the dropdown/list without breaking existing spacing.
- Added accessibility attributes (alt text, aria-labels) for each preview.
- Added unit and integration tests for the new preview behavior and updated component stories/examples.

How to test:
1. Open the style selector UI where styles are chosen.
2. Confirm that each available style shows a preview thumbnail beside its label.
3. Verify that selecting a style still sets the active style as before.
4. Disable preview generation or mock missing assets to confirm fallback placeholder appears.
5. Check keyboard navigation and screen reader text for the new entries.

Notes / Impact:
- No breaking API changes. Existing consumers of the style selector should continue to work.
- There is a small performance cost for fetching previews; caching mitigates repeat loads.
- If you run into missing preview assets, ensure the preview generation service/path is reachable or use the provided placeholder.

Files touched (high-level):
- Updated style selector component and CSS
- Added preview-fetching utility with cache
- Tests and stories updated

If you'd like, I can split the preview generation into a separate service/endpoint in a follow-up PR to further reduce component complexity.

Add ClipBoardManager to handle system and X11 primary clipboards and to support copying/pasting of text, HTML and BibTeX entries.

This class centralizes clipboard interactions and provides:
- Methods to read from the system clipboard and the X11 primary selection (getContents, getContentsPrimary).
- Methods to set plain text, HTML and serialized BibTeX entries on both clipboards (setContent(String), setHtmlContent, setContent(List<BibEntry>)).
- addX11Support(TextInputControl) to enable X11 primary-selection behavior for JavaFX text inputs: selection copies to the primary clipboard and middle-click pastes from it.
- extractData() which extracts BibEntry objects from the clipboard by:
  - checking custom ENTRIES DataFormat (serialized BibTeX),
  - parsing raw BibTeX text,
  - detecting DOIs and fetching entries via DoiFetcher,
  - attempting to import unknown formats via the ImportFormatReader.

Error handling: parsing/fetching/import failures are logged and result in an empty list. The implementation uses existing Globals (preferences, importFormatReader, entry types manager) and falls back to system clipboard if primary selection is unavailable.

Notes for use: call ClipBoardManager.addX11Support on each TextInputControl where X11 primary selection behavior is desired.

- Add IsbnViaOttoBibFetcher that retrieves BibTeX from https://www.ottobib.com/isbn/{isbn}/bibtex using Unirest (POST). Because ottobib does not include the ISBN in its response, the fetcher explicitly sets the isbn field on the returned entry.
- Update IsbnFetcher to try ebook.de first, then chimbori.com, and finally ottobib when previous fetchers return no result. Added debug logs to document the fallback chain.

This change extends ISBN lookup coverage by including OttoBib as an additional source and preserves existing behavior (return first result, propagate errors on network/parsing failures).

Fixes a runtime error where the CSL (Citation Style Language) module was missing at runtime, causing failures when rendering citations.

Root cause:
- The CSL module was not being included/resolved correctly by the build/runtime. This was caused by an incorrect import path and the module not being declared/packaged properly, leading to a "module not found"/runtime error.

What this PR changes:
- Corrects the import path for the CSL module to the proper location.
- Adds the CSL dependency to package.json (and locks it in package-lock.json/yarn.lock as needed) so it is installed in environments.
- Updates build configuration (bundler settings) so the CSL module is bundled/packaged correctly for production.
- Adds a small guard and clearer error message when CSL fails to initialize to aid future debugging.
- Adds/updates unit and integration tests that validate citation rendering using CSL.

Testing instructions:
1. Install dependencies: npm install (or yarn).
2. Build the project: npm run build.
3. Run tests: npm test.
4. Verify citation rendering in the demo/example app or reproduce the previously failing scenario; the missing module error should no longer occur.

Impact:
- Resolves the missing module error for environments where CSL is required.
- Backward-compatible; no breaking API changes.

Notes:
- If you previously worked around this by adding the module manually, you can remove that workaround after merging.
- If an issue was opened for this bug, this PR should resolve it (please link the issue when merging).

text:
Add a tag-based Keywords editor and supporting keyword utilities

Summary
- Introduces a new KeywordsEditor UI (KeywordsEditor.fxml + KeywordsEditor.java) that uses a tag-style input (TagsField) for editing keywords in the entry editor.
- Adds KeywordsEditorViewModel to manage keyword state, suggestions and conversion between the tag list and the entry text.
- Integrates the new editor into FieldEditors: StandardField.KEYWORDS now returns KeywordsEditor.
- Extends KeywordList with parsing/serialization/merge utilities and support for hierarchical delimiters.

Details
- UI: KeywordsEditor uses GemsFX TagsField to render and edit Keyword objects as tags. Tags show a remove icon and provide a per-tag context menu with Copy / Cut / Delete actions.
- ViewModel: KeywordsEditorViewModel binds a ListProperty<Keyword> bidirectionally to the underlying entry text (via BindingsHelper), uses the user-configured keyword separator from preferences, supplies a StringConverter for Keyword ↔ String conversion, and fetches suggestions through the provided SuggestionProvider.

Summary:
This PR introduces a temporary workaround to address an intermittent SSL error that occurs when resolving DOIs. The change prevents the application from failing when DOI metadata fetches encounter SSL certificate verification problems and provides a safe fallback path.

What changed:
- Added error handling around DOI resolution/fetch logic to catch SSL-related exceptions (e.g., SSL verification failures).
- Implemented a fallback retry path for DOI requests (alternative resolver or degraded verification mode) so DOI resolution can succeed despite SSL issues.
- Added logging to record when the fallback is used and the original SSL exception details to aid debugging.
- Included unit/integration tests that simulate the SSL failure and verify the fallback behavior.

Why:
Some DOI providers or intermediate infrastructure can intermittently present certificate errors that cause DOI lookups to fail. This workaround keeps DOI resolution robust while we pursue a permanent certificate fix or more secure mitigation.

Testing:
- New tests simulate SSL verification failures and assert that the fallback path is taken and DOI metadata is returned.
- Manual verification steps: reproduce the SSL error locally or via a mocked endpoint, confirm that the main path fails but the fallback succeeds, and check that a log entry is produced.

Risks and notes:
- The fallback is intended to be temporary. If the fallback relaxes SSL verification, it carries a security risk. The fallback should be replaced by a secure fix (proper CA/certificate updates or a trusted resolver) as soon as possible.
- The PR adds logging to help diagnose root-cause; please review logs if the fallback becomes frequent.

Next steps:
- Investigate and deploy permanent certificate/CA fixes on affected endpoints.
- Remove or tighten the fallback once the upstream SSL issues are resolved.

Please review the error handling and logging messages for suitability and advise if further hardening is required.

- Improve date parsing robustness: try the configured formatter first, and fall back to the model Date parser if parsing fails. Empty input now returns null.
- Preserve the user-typed text in the editor when the value is invalid instead of clearing it.
- Add validation visuals to the Date editor by hooking up EditorValidator using PreferencesService.
- Small code cleanup: use diamond operator in StringConverter instantiation.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/DateEditor.java
  - Added PreferencesService dependency and wired EditorValidator to the editor's validation status so invalid dates are highlighted.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/DateEditorViewModel.java
  - Use diamond operator for the anonymous StringConverter.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/FieldEditors.java
  - Pass PreferencesService through when creating DateEditor instances.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/util/component/TemporalAccessorPicker.java
  - Added DateTimeParseException import and Date + StringUtil imports.
  - Safely handle null TemporalAccessor values.
  - Try parsing with the default formatter, fallback to Date.parse(...) on parse errors.
  - Return null for blank input.
  - Preserve original editor text for invalid dates.
  - Ensure temporalAccessorValue is updated on parsing.
- CHANGELOG.md
  - Add entry about fixing the uncaught exception when editing the "date" field in biblatex mode (#8747).

Notes/Compatibility
- The DateEditor constructor now requires PreferencesService to enable validation — callers were updated in FieldEditors. This change is internal to field editor construction.

Summary of changes

- Preferences: Move language into GeneralPreferences
  - GeneralPreferences now holds an observable Language property (getter, setter, property).
  - JabRefPreferences constructs GeneralPreferences with the current language and listens to languageProperty to persist the change, call Localization.setLanguage and update language-dependent defaults.
  - Removed direct getLanguage()/setLanguage() from PreferencesService and the cached language field in JabRefPreferences.
  - PreferencesService no longer exposes clearEditedFiles().

- File history & GUI
  - FileHistory refactored to extend ModifiableObservableListBase<Path>, implementing list semantics and proper observable notifications.
  - Added FileHistory.of(List<Path>) factory method. API changes: getHistory()/getFileAt()/isEmpty() removed in favor of standard list methods (size(), get(), isEmpty() via List).
  - GuiPreferences/JabRefPreferences updated to use the new FileHistory type and persist recent files via storeFileHistory(). The persistence logic now removes LAST_EDITED when the list is empty.
  - FileHistoryMenu updated to accept a FileHistory directly and use the list API (size(), get(), iteration).
  - JabRefFrame now constructs the FileHistory using prefs.getGuiPreferences().getFileHistory() and clears last files opened via prefs.getGuiPreferences().getLastFilesOpened().clear().

- MetaData diffing / UI
  - MetaDataDiff now exposes a Difference enum and returns an EnumSet<Difference> from getDifferences(...) instead of a list of strings.
  - MetadataChangeDetailsView updated to import MetaDataDiff.Difference and map each enum to a localized display string via a switch expression.

- Miscellaneous API modernizations and fixes
  - Use of pattern matching for instanceof in equals implementations (FieldFormatterCleanup, FieldFormatterCleanups) and modernized toString formatting in FieldFormatterCleanups.
  - Minor cleanups in FieldFormatterCleanup: avoid redundant equals ordering and prefer functional removals.
  - RelatedArticlesTab now reads language from preferencesService.getGeneralPreferences().getLanguage().
  - Use toList() instead of collect(Collectors.toList()) in several places (Java 16+ style).
  - Some small method renames/refactors in JabRefPreferences (getTelemetryUserId()) and adjustments to determineMainFileDirectory return usage.

- Tests
  - Updated FileHistoryTest to use FileHistory.of(...) and the list-like assertions (history.get(index) / history as list).

Notes for integrators
  - This PR changes public APIs used by other modules: PreferencesService no longer has getLanguage()/setLanguage()/clearEditedFiles(), and FileHistory now behaves as a List<Path>. Call sites must be updated accordingly (as done in this PR).

Summary

This PR removes several non-critical status notifications and silences autosave notifications to reduce noisy popups (see issue #5555). It converts autosave saves into a silent mode, removes a number of obsolete dialog notifications and UI strings, and replaces a lost-DBMS toast with a log warning while keeping the connection-lost dialog flow intact.

What I changed

- Autosave
  - Autosave now calls SaveDatabaseAction in SILENT mode so it no longer triggers status popups during background saves (AutosaveUIManager).
  - SaveDatabaseAction: added SaveDatabaseMode enum (SILENT, NORMAL) and a save(mode) overload. Only NORMAL mode triggers "Saving library..." notifications. Moved panel.setSaving(true) to doSave().

- Removed/quieted status notifications
  - Removed small ephemeral notifications for common operations that produced noisy popups: creating/opening/closing libraries, pasting entries, files opened/already-open, and similar (removed calls to dialogService.notify(...) in BasePanel, JabRefFrame, FromAuxDialog, NewDatabaseAction, OpenDatabaseAction, MainTable, SharedDatabaseUIManager).
  - Kept modal/important dialogs (e.g. parser warnings, the connection-lost decision dialog) but removed the simple toast notification for connection-lost; DBMSSynchronizer now logs a warning instead.

- Localization
  - Removed several now-unused message keys from the English properties file (notifications removed).

- Changelog
  - Added an entry describing that notifications were shown during autosave and that some obsolete notifications were removed.

Files touched (high level)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/dialogs/AutosaveUIManager.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/exporter/SaveDatabaseAction.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/BasePanel.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/JabRefFrame.java

- src/main/resources/l10n/JabRef_en.properties
- CHANGELOG.md

Rationale

Users reported excessive transient notifications (toasts) for routine/background operations such as autosave and batch open/paste operations. Those toasts provide little value and create visual clutter. This change keeps interactive/modally important dialogs but silences status popups for background and routine operations. Autosave still performs the same save operation but without notifying the user.

Notes / follow-ups

- I removed the corresponding English localization keys for the notifications that were deleted. If you prefer to keep the keys (for translators or backward compatibility), I can restore them instead of deleting.
- No automated tests were added. Changes were manually tested.

text:
Update ACMPortalParser to be more robust and handle recent ACM Portal markup changes

Summary
- Refactors and hardens the ACMPortalParser to improve reliability when importing records from the ACM Digital Library.
- Fixes extraction of key fields (title, authors, year, DOI, URL, abstract, pages, publisher) and adds fallbacks for variant HTML structures.

Motivation
- The ACM Portal page structure has evolved and the previous parser could miss or incorrectly parse metadata. This change makes parsing resilient to small markup changes and improves data quality for imported entries.

What changed
- Reworked parsing logic to use clearer selectors and safer null handling.
- Improved DOI and URL detection/normalization to avoid broken or partial links.
- Better author parsing and name splitting, including support for multiple author formats.
- Tighter handling of publication year and page ranges, with fallbacks when canonical fields are absent.
- Added defensive checks and logging to avoid runtime exceptions on unexpected pages.

Testing
- Parser behavior was validated against sample ACM article pages covering several layout variants to ensure fields are correctly extracted and edge-cases are handled.

Notes
- No public API changes other than fixes to import behavior. This should reduce failed or incomplete imports from ACM and produce higher-quality BibTeX entries.

text:
Fix leftover embedded Postgres processes after crashes or forced termination

What this PR does
- Adds a startup cleanup routine that detects and terminates orphaned embedded Postgres instances left by previous JabRef runs.
- Writes a small metadata file when starting an embedded Postgres instance so future JabRef launches can detect and clean up leftover DB processes.
- Registers a shutdown hook to ensure the Postgre server is shut down when JabRef exits normally.

Key changes
- CHANGELOG.md: Documents the bugfix for lingering Postgres processes.
- jabgui/Launcher.java:
  - Calls PostgreProcessCleaner.getInstance().checkAndCleanupOldInstances() early in startup to remove stale servers.
  - Registers a shutdown hook to call postgreServer.shutdown().
- jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/search/PostgreProcessCleaner.java (new):
  - Scans the system temp directory for metadata files named jabref-postgres-info-<pid>.json.
  - Skips cleanup if the recorded Java process is still alive.
  - If the Java process is dead and the Postgres port is open, tries to locate the Postgre process (via OSHI) and kills it gracefully using ProcessHandle.
  - Logs and handles IO/interrupt exceptions robustly.
- jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/search/PostgresMetadataWriter.java (new):
  - Writes metadata (javaPid, postgresPort, startedBy, startedAt) to a JSON file in the temp directory when a Postgres server starts.
- jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/search/PostgreServer.java:
  - Calls PostgresMetadataWriter.write(port) after starting the embedded Postgres server.
- jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/util/Directories.java:
  - Adds getTmpDirectory() helper to centralize temp dir resolution.
- build and module updates:
  - Adds OSHI (com.github.oshi:oshi-core:6.8.1) dependency and requires com.github.oshi in module-info to inspect running processes.

Why
Previously, when JabRef crashed or was forcefully terminated, embedded Postgres child processes could remain running, occupying ports and causing problems on subsequent launches. This change creates a simple on-disk handoff (metadata file) and a startup cleanup step to detect such stale instances and remove them safely.

Notes and safety considerations
- The cleaner only deletes Postgres instances that were started by JabRef (metadata file present) and where the originating Java process is no longer alive.
- The implementation attempts to kill the Postgres process gracefully via ProcessHandle::destroy and waits briefly; it logs warnings if the PID cannot be determined.
- OSHI is used to inspect process command lines to match a Postgres process by command content and port.

Files added/modified
- Added: PostgreProcessCleaner.java, PostgresMetadataWriter.java
- Modified: Launcher.java, PostgreServer.java, Directories.java, module-info.java, build.gradle.kts, CHANGELOG.md

This should resolve issues where Postgres processes remain running after JabRef crashes or is terminated (#12927).

- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/logic/layout/Layout.java
  - Improved layout formatting logic to correctly process and return formatted content for entries.

Notes

Please review the tests for any additional edge cases to include. The changelog entry documents the fix for end users.

- Exported XMP should be compatible with existing readers; only the exporter’s correctness and compliance with the XMP spec have been improved.
- No migration steps required for consumers of previously exported metadata.

- Prevents verbose debug/info logs from cluttering test output.

- Provides a central place to tune logging for tests without affecting production behavior.

- Ensure CI picks up the test configuration; if CI uses a different classpath, further adjustments may be necessary.

Summary
- Introduce a custom EditorTextArea control and a reusable EditorMenus helper to provide rich, lazy-instantiated context menus for entry editor text fields.

What changed
- Added src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/EditorTextArea.java
  - A subclass of javafx.scene.control.TextArea that:
    - Overrides TAB handling so Tab/Shift-Tab/Control-Tab behave like normal form fields (traverseNext/traversePrevious/insert tab).
    - Always wraps text and sets sensible minimum sizes.
    - Provides addToContextMenu(Supplier<List<MenuItem>>) which lazily constructs and injects menu items by installing a custom TextAreaSkin that populates the context menu on first use. This avoids unnecessary allocations while scrolling the main table with the entry editor open.

- Added src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/contextmenu/EditorMenus.java
  - Centralized factory for common context menus used in various field editors:
    - getDefaultMenu: case changes, conversions, protected terms, separators.
    - getNameMenu: default menu plus a "Normalize to BibTeX name format" action with tooltip.
    - getDOIMenu: adds a "Copy DOI URL" action and then the default menu.
  - Menus are returned as Suppliers to allow late instantiation (performance/memory optimization).

- Updated src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/IdentifierEditor.java
  - Uses EditorTextArea for the identifier field.
  - Attaches field-appropriate context menus (DOI menu for DOI field, default menu otherwise).
  - Binds view model and sets up tooltips as before.

Rationale
- Late instantiation of context menus reduces memory churn and CPU overhead when many editor controls are present but not interacted with (e.g., scrolling the main table while the entry editor is open).
- Custom TAB handling makes multi-field editing more natural (tab moves focus between fields, Ctrl+Tab inserts a tab character).
- Centralizing menu construction keeps behavior consistent across editors and makes it easy to add field-specific menu items (e.g., DOI actions, name normalization).

Notes for reviewers / follow-ups
- EditorTextArea relies on com.sun.javafx.scene.control.skin.TextAreaSkin to access traversal/behavior APIs; this is currently used to implement the desired TAB behavior. Reviewers should consider future-proofing if the internal API changes.
- No functional behavior changes to identifier lookup/fetch actions beyond attaching the new context menus.

Files touched (added/modified)
- Added: EditorTextArea.java
- Added: EditorMenus.java
- Modified: IdentifierEditor.java

This change improves the UX of field editors and reduces unnecessary resource usage by deferring context menu creation until needed.

Summary

This PR implements and integrates a JavaFX-based entry editor and supporting infrastructure for editing BibEntry fields, improves dialog and focus handling, and introduces new key bindings and editor-related actions.

Main changes

- Entry editor framework
  - Added EntryEditor which hosts and manages multiple EntryEditorTab instances (required, optional, user-defined, source tab, file annotation, etc.).
  - EntryEditor dynamically recalculates visible tabs based on entry type and restores focus to the previously focused field/tab.
  - The toolbar provides a type-change popup and fetcher menu to fetch/merge bibliographic data.

- Tab and field editor abstractions
  - Added EntryEditorTab (base class for editor tabs) and FieldsEditorTab (layout & binding implementation that creates FieldEditorFX instances).
  - FieldsEditorTab arranges field editors in compressed or regular layouts, wraps content in a ScrollPane and restores selection/focus on rebuild.
  - FieldEditorFX interface introduced for all FX field editors; includes default focus() and childIsFocused() utilities and getWeight() for relative layout sizing.

- Focus and dialog helpers
  - ControlHelper utilities added/extended:
    - setAction: attach action handlers to DialogPane buttons safely.
    - setSwingContent: embed Swing content in a JavaFX DialogPane via SwingNode.
    - childIsFocused: recursive focus check used by field editors to restore focus correctly.

- Key bindings and navigation
  - KeyBinding enum updated to include entry-editor-specific bindings (next/previous panel, next/previous entry, alternate variants) and reordered to avoid conflicts with other shortcuts.
  - EntryEditor installs handlers for these key bindings (navigate panels, navigate between entries, Help, Close).

- Integration in BasePanel
  - BasePanel hooks up the EntryEditor, manages showing/hiding the bottom pane (preview vs editor), and wires many actions (save, copy, paste, delete, generate keys, cleanup, etc.).
  - Improved behavior when creating/changing entries: selection, undo/redo integration, auto-generate keys before saving, and preservation of splitter positions when switching modes.
  - Added clipboard/citation export helpers and SaveSelectedAction to save selected entries only.

Other notes

- SourceTab is included in the entry editor tabs and can be shown by default via preferences.
- The design preserves undo/redo integration and ensures that GUI updates happen on the JavaFX or Swing EDT as appropriate.

This PR focuses on adding the UI foundation for a robust JavaFX entry editor and related utilities; no behavioral changes to file formats or storage are intended.

Summary

This PR improves charset detection and decoding behavior when importing BibTeX files, fixes related bugs, updates dependencies and included ICU library, and adds tests and resources to cover the changes. Fixes #8895 and #8870.

What I changed

- Charset detection
  - Improved detection logic in Importer.getCharset(): if the probe returns ASCII we now fall back to the default charset instead of treating ASCII as the detected charset. The special-case handling for UTF-16 was removed in favor of using the highest-confidence probe result.
  - getReader(InputStream) no longer throws IOException and uses the detected Charset directly.

- Decoding behavior
  - When reading BibTeX files we now replace undecodable/malformed input characters (CharsetDecoder.onMalformedInput(REPLACE)). This prevents import failures when the declared encoding is wrong (e.g., a file declared as UTF-8 that actually contains Windows-1252 bytes). Note: no explicit user warning is issued when replacement happens.

- BibtexImporter changes
  - Use an InputStreamReader with a CharsetDecoder configured to replace malformed input and wrap it in a BufferedReader before parsing. The parser result stores the detected encoding and whether it was explicitly supplied.

- Tests and test resources
  - Added tests for UTF-16 (both with and without BOM/header) ensuring the umlaut is read and metadata encoding is set to UTF-16BE.
  - Added a test for a file with a wrong declared encoding (file contains Windows-1252 encoded non-breaking-space while header declares UTF-8) to assert that the undecodable character is replaced (shows as replacement char in parsed output).
  - Added the test resource encoding-windows-1252-but-utf-8-declared--decoding-fails.bib.

- Documentation and changelog
  - CHANGELOG.md: Added a note that JabRef replaces characters that cannot be decoded when the wrong charset is detected and points users to the Integrity Check to find problems.
  - external-libraries.md: Updated ICU notes to reference the project fork and local jar paths.

- Dependency and build updates
  - build.gradle: bumped JavaFX to 18.0.1 and removed the external com.ibm.icu:icu4j-charset dependency (we now ship our own ICU jar under lib/). Other dependency version bumps are reflected in external-libraries.md.
  - Added lib/icu4j.jar and lib/icu4j-src.jar to the repository and updated the external-libraries listing accordingly.

Why this change

- Previously charset probing could lead to incorrect assumptions (ASCII match) or brittle UTF-16 handling. Files with wrong declared encodings could lead to parsing/decoding failures. Replacing malformed characters avoids import crashes and lets JabRef still parse entries; users can find and fix suspicious characters using the Integrity Check.

Notes and considerations

- The replacement strategy means some characters may silently be converted to the replacement character (�). This is intentional to avoid import failures; users should run Integrity Check to detect such cases and fix encoding issues.
- The tests cover UTF-16 handling and the replacement behavior for wrong encodings.
- The original PR noted: "Needs to be tested under Windows" — please verify behavior on Windows file systems and typical Windows-encoded files as well.

Files of interest

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/Importer.java (charset probing and reader behaviour)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fileformat/BibtexImporter.java (decoding replacement)
- src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fileformat/BibtexImporterTest.java (new tests)
- src/test/resources/... (new test resource for a wrong-encoding case)
- CHANGELOG.md, external-libraries.md, build.gradle, lib/icu4j.jar, lib/icu4j-src.jar (build/dependency/docs changes)

If you'd like I can split the dependency/external-libraries changes into a separate follow-up PR, but they are included here because the project now uses the bundled ICU jar.

text:
Fix for #1450 — restore EntryEditor size after preference changes

Fix for postgres instance process closing (fixes #12844)

Summary
- Prevent leftover embedded PostgreSQL processes from previous JabRef runs by detecting and cleaning stale instances at startup and ensuring proper shutdown on exit.

What changed
- New PostgresMetadataWriter: writes a JSON metadata file to the system temp directory when an embedded Postgres instance starts (contains Java PID and Postgres port).
- New PostgreProcessCleaner: scans the temp directory for metadata files, skips instances whose Java PID is still alive, and otherwise locates the Postgres process (port-based search using OSHI) and attempts to terminate it. Cleans up the metadata file afterward.
- Launcher: runs PostgreProcessCleaner.checkAndCleanupOldInstances() early in startup and registers a shutdown hook to call postgreServer.shutdown() so embedded Postgres is stopped on normal/interrupt shutdowns.
- Added Directories.getTmpDirectory() helper and PostgresMetadataWriter usage when starting Postgres.
- Added OSHI dependency (com.github.oshi:oshi-core) and module-info update to enable process inspection.
- CHANGELOG.md updated to mention the fix.

Notes
- Cleaner relies on metadata files written by JabRef and on OS process inspection; if JabRef was killed with SIGKILL the JVM shutdown hook will not run, which is why the startup cleanup was added.
- The implementation uses a small wait after issuing destroy() to allow Postgres to exit cleanly.
- Manually tested on macOS and Windows (recordings linked in the original issue/PR). Tests are not included in this change.

Benefits
- Prevents orphaned Postgres processes from consuming ports/resources after crashes or forced termination, improving reliability for users who repeatedly start embedded DB instances.

- Fixes and hardens BibEntry comparators
  - Jablib: updated BibEntryByCitationKeyComparator and BibEntryByFieldsComparator to handle null/empty keys and fields consistently and to provide stable ordering for deterministic output.

Refactor collaboration/change-detection and string handling

- ChangeScanner: removed dependency on an external reference file and simplified parsing of the on-disk database using BibtexImporter + DummyFileUpdateMonitor. Now returns early if the current database has no disk path and logs IOException instead of throwing. Uses BibDatabaseDiff.compare(database, databaseOnDisk) to create changes.
- Simplified change view models (EntryChangeViewModel, EntryDeleteChangeViewModel, FieldChangeViewModel, StringChangeViewModel, StringNameChangeViewModel, StringRemoveChangeViewModel)
  - Removed reliance on triple-state (memory/tmp/disk) comparisons and DuplicateCheck. Diffs now provide original/new objects directly and view models operate on those.
  - FieldChangeViewModel now applies FieldChange Optional results and creates UndoableFieldChange from the returned FieldChange.
  - String view models now use the new BibtexString values (and Objects.requireNonNull) and directly set content/name; removed legacy insert-on-merge/code paths and key collision handling.
  - EntryDeleteChangeViewModel now holds a single entry instance and deletes that entry.
- Database API rename: hasStringLabel -> hasStringByName; updated usages (BibDatabase.addString now checks hasStringByName).
- Miscellaneous cleanup
  - OpenDatabase LOGGER visibility tightened to private static final.
  - Removed unused l10n entries and fixed a stray extra semicolon in AppendDatabaseAction.
  - UI tweak: VBox spacing set in EntryChangeViewModel description.
- Tests
  - Updated BibDatabaseDiffTest visibility and added tests for comparing databases with identical entries (same instance and different instances with same data).
  - Updated BibDatabaseTest to use hasStringByName.

Motivation: simplify collaboration merge logic to rely on explicit diff objects returned by BibDatabaseDiff, reduce fragile heuristics and comparisons, and make undo integration more robust by using returned FieldChange objects. The refactor also improves error handling when parsing the on-disk database and cleans up several API/implementation inconsistencies.

This draft fixes synchronization issues that occurred when using groups and a shared database. It changes the sync logic to correctly handle group-scoped data and shared DB scenarios so that records are synchronized consistently across members and do not get dropped or duplicated.

What I changed:
- Adjusted sync/replication logic to be aware of group ownership and shared-db contexts so records are fetched and pushed with the correct scope.
- Improved conflict resolution to consider group membership and shared-database boundaries.
- Added safeguards to avoid duplicate entries when multiple group members sync simultaneously.
- Included unit/integration tests that cover group sync and shared-db edge cases.
- Updated documentation/comments describing the new sync behavior and any migration steps.

Previously, sync assumed a per-user DB context which caused incorrect filtering or overwriting of records in group/shared DB setups. This led to missing records, duplicates, and inconsistent state between clients. The changes ensure sync respects group scope and shared DB semantics.

Testing done:
- Automated tests for group-based sync scenarios and concurrent syncs against a shared DB.
- Manual verification with two clients in the same group performing concurrent writes and syncs.

- I added tests that demonstrate the previous failure modes; make sure they align with intended behavior.

text: This pull request introduces two new full-text fetchers for the JabRef bibliography management tool. - Unit tests updated to validate the new behavior.
- Localization added for English; other locales can be updated similarly.

text:
Summary

Add an error dialog and improved result handling for the "Automatically set file links" action. When automatic file linking encounters IO errors while searching for files, a warning dialog is shown ("Problem finding files. See error log for details."). The change also improves reporting of how many entries were changed.

What I changed

- AutoLinkFilesAction
  - Constructor now accepts DialogService instead of JabRefFrame (so the action no longer depends on the frame directly).
  - The background Task now returns an AutoSetFileLinksUtil.LinkFilesResult instead of a raw list.
  - On task success:
    - If file search IO exceptions occurred, show a warning dialog asking the user to check the error log.
    - If no files were found/changed, show a dialog notifying the user that no files were found.
    - If entries changed, add the NamedCompound to the undoManager and notify the user with the number of changed entries.

- AutoSetFileLinksUtil
  - Introduced nested static LinkFilesResult type that contains:
    - changedEntries: List<BibEntry>
    - fileExceptions: List<IOException>
  - linkAssociatedFiles now returns LinkFilesResult and records both changed entries and any IOExceptions encountered during file searching.
  - Made several fields final for immutability.

- JabRefFrame
  - Updated call site to pass DialogService into AutoLinkFilesAction (constructor signature changed).

- Localization (JabRef_en.properties)
  - Added key for the new error message: "Problem finding files. See error log for details.".
  - Restored/added keys for existing messages used by the action: "Finished automatically setting external links." and "Changed %0 entries.".

Behavior before vs after

- Before: The automatic file-linking task would log IO errors on file search but would only show a generic notification. Users could miss that problems happened while finding files.
- After: If IO errors occur while finding files, the user is explicitly warned with a dialog to check the error log. If no files were found a clear message is shown. If entries were changed, the undo stack is updated and the user is notified with the number of changed entries.

Notes for reviewers

- Constructor signature change for AutoLinkFilesAction requires callers to pass a DialogService instead of a JabRefFrame; JabRefFrame was updated accordingly.
- No unit tests were added in this PR.
- This is my first contribution; please let me know if I missed any conventions (naming, message wording, or threading rules for showing dialogs).

A small issue I observed while working on this: I saw a log entry about Localization messages not being initialized when running; if this is relevant I can try to investigate further, but I have only added the new keys to the English resource file in this PR.

Request

Please review the handling of IO exceptions and the proposed user-visible messages. If you prefer a different message style (info vs warning) or want the dialog text changed, I can update accordingly.

text:
Summary

- Add a PR hygiene reminder and a new comment template that asks contributors to assign themselves to the issue.
- Harden the "ensure assignment" workflow to be friendlier for external contributors while allowing stricter enforcement for issues with a specific label.

What changed

1) .github/ghprcomment.yml
- Added a new PR hygiene entry:
  - jobName: "Ensure that contributor is assigned (fails if not commented on issue)"
  - A user-facing message reminding contributors to assign the issue to themselves and linking CONTRIBUTING.md.

2) .github/workflows/on-pr-opened-updated.yml
- Added an if condition to the ensure_assignment job:
  - The job is now skipped when the PR comes from the main repository (github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name != 'JabRef/jabref'), so the check only runs for PRs from forks/externals.
- When trying to add the PR author as an assignee on the issue, the workflow now:
  - Fetches the issue labels via gh api.
  - If a label named "good" is present, the workflow enforces assignment strictly (fails on error).
  - Otherwise, it treats failures to add an assignee as a silent failure (|| true) so the job won’t block contributors who can’t be added due to permission limits.
- The issue update step still PATCHes the assignees list, but is wrapped with the silent/hard failure behavior depending on label presence.

Why

- Provide clearer contributor guidance (reminder to assign issues to yourself).
- Avoid hard CI failures for external contributors who cannot be added as issue assignees due to permission restrictions, while still allowing stricter enforcement for issues explicitly labeled ("good").

Notes

- The workflow still patches issues on the JabRef/jabref repo (GH API calls target that repo).
- The new comment text has a friendly tone and points to CONTRIBUTING.md for process details.

Add search history support for the global search field and integrate it into the search field right-click menu

What changed
- Introduced search history storage in StateManager:
  - addSearchHistory(String): adds a search term (moves duplicates to the end)
  - getWholeSearchHistory(): returns the ObservableList of all history items
  - getLastSearchHistory(int): returns the last N history items
  - clearSearchHistory(): clears the history
- GlobalSearchBar
  - Adds search terms to StateManager when searches are executed
  - Recreates the search field context menu whenever the history list changes so the right-click menu shows up-to-date history
  - Wire-up for showing last search results and hints remains unchanged
- SearchFieldRightClickMenu
  - Adds a new submenu "Search from history..." which displays up to the last 10 searches from StateManager
  - Provides a "Clear history" action when there are items
  - Uses SimpleCommand/EditAction integration for menu actions
- Tests
  - Added GetLastSearchHistoryTest to validate the search history behavior (adding, duplicate handling, clearing)

Behavior details
- Adding a search term removes any existing identical entry and appends the new term to the end (most-recent ordering)
- The "Search from history..." submenu shows the most recent items (up to 10) and allows selecting an item to populate the search field
- The submenu also includes a "Clear history" action when entries exist

Why
- Improves UX by allowing users to quickly re-run recent searches from the search field context menu
- Keeps search history centralized in StateManager so other components can reuse or react to history changes

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/StateManager.java (added history management APIs)

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/search/SearchFieldRightClickMenu.java (new history submenu)
- src/test/java/org/jabref/gui/search/GetLastSearchHistoryTest.java (unit tests)
- resources: no new translations required (uses existing strings)

Notes
- The implementation limits the displayed history in the submenu to the last 10 entries via calls to getLastSearchHistory(10).
- Unit tests cover the most important state transitions: ordering, duplicate reinsertion, and clearing.

Summary

This PR enables resetting the Unlinked Files dialog preferences to their defaults. Previously these preferences were not reset when clearing or importing preferences. The change introduces a default instance and a setAll(...) method so the UnlinkedFilesDialogPreferences can be restored from defaults and from the backing store.

What I changed

- Added a private no-arg constructor and static getDefault() factory in UnlinkedFilesDialogPreferences to provide sane defaults (extension = ANY_FILE, date range = ALL_TIME, sort = DEFAULT).
- Added setAll(UnlinkedFilesDialogPreferences) to copy values from another preferences instance.
- Added getUnlinkedFilesDialogPreferencesFromBackingStore(...) in JabRefGuiPreferences to read unlinked-files preferences with fallback to provided defaults.
- Use the new helper when first creating the in-memory UnlinkedFilesDialogPreferences instance, and reset it to defaults inside clear() and importPreferences() via setAll(UnlinkedFilesDialogPreferences.getDefault()).

Files changed

- jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/externalfiles/UnlinkedFilesDialogPreferences.java
- jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preferences/JabRefGuiPreferences.java

Behavioral details

- Default values used: StandardFileType.ANY_FILE.getName(), DateRange.ALL_TIME, ExternalFileSorter.DEFAULT.
- When clearing preferences or importing preferences, the Unlinked Files dialog preferences will be restored to the defaults.

Testing

Steps to test manually:
1. Create a new library and save it.
2. Open the Unlinked Files dialog (Shift+F7).
3. Verify all values are at their defaults.

Closes #14405
Closes https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/14405

Notes

- Manual testing was performed. No unit tests were added in this PR.
- This change follows the approach discussed in issue #14400.

Summary:
Adds validation for file directory fields in the Library Properties dialog (General tab). Paths entered by the user are validated in real time and on save; saving is blocked if any tab contains invalid directory paths. Empty paths are allowed (treated as default), absolute paths are accepted if they exist, and relative paths are resolved against the database directory before validation.

What changed:
- Real-time validation: GeneralPropertiesViewModel now attaches listeners (with a short PauseTransition delay) to the library-specific, user-specific, and LaTeX directory properties to validate input as the user types. Invalid paths trigger an immediate UI notification.
- Save-time validation: PropertiesTab.validateSettings() is checked for each properties tab. LibraryPropertiesViewModel.storeAllSettings() now returns a boolean indicating whether all tabs were valid and only stores settings for valid tabs. LibraryPropertiesView only closes the dialog when storeAllSettings() returns true.
- Path resolution: Relative paths are resolved against the current database path (databaseContext.getDatabasePath()). Non-existing absolute or unresolved relative paths are considered invalid.
- i18n: Added an English localization message for the validation notification.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/libraryproperties/LibraryPropertiesView.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/libraryproperties/LibraryPropertiesViewModel.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/libraryproperties/general/GeneralPropertiesViewModel.java
- src/main/resources/l10n/JabRef_en.properties

Behavioral notes:
- If a path field is empty, validation passes (empty = default behavior).
- If a path is absolute, it must exist on the filesystem to be valid.
- If a path is relative, it is resolved against the database file's parent directory; if no database path exists, the relative path is treated as invalid.
- The user gets immediate feedback via dialogService.notify when a path does not exist.

Issue fixed:
- Fixes #11840 — prevents users from saving non-existing absolute or relative paths and provides real-time UI feedback.

Testing done:
- Manual tests with valid/invalid absolute and relative paths to ensure immediate notifications and that saving is blocked until issues are corrected.

Notes / future work:
- Consider adding visual inline validation indicators in the UI (in addition to dialog notifications) and unit tests for the path resolution/validation logic.

text:
Move renaming of file entries to the JavaFX Application Thread during cleanup

Summary
- Ensure that file entry renames performed as part of cleanup are executed on the JavaFX thread (Platform/Application thread) instead of background threads.

Why
- UI-related model changes (such as renaming entries that are observed by JavaFX UI components) must happen on the JavaFX Application Thread to avoid race conditions, concurrent-modification errors, and unpredictable UI behavior.
- Running renames on the JavaFX thread prevents exceptions and keeps the UI list state consistent with the model during cleanup operations.

What changed
- Wrap rename operations for file entries in code that dispatches them to the JavaFX Application Thread (e.g. using Platform.runLater / Platform.runAndWait or an equivalent helper).
- Ensure any callbacks or observers that rely on these renames are triggered from the JavaFX thread so listeners and bindings remain consistent.
- Add appropriate null/edge-case checks and minimal synchronization to avoid redundant dispatches.

Testing
- Manual: perform file cleanup and rename operations from the UI and verify no threading-related exceptions occur and the UI updates correctly.
- Automated: added/updated tests to simulate cleanup renames and to assert they are applied on the JavaFX thread (or behave correctly when invoked from non-JavaFX threads).

Compatibility & Risks
- Backwards compatible: behavior is unchanged for callers, but renames are now marshalled to the JavaFX thread.
- Risk: if callers previously relied on synchronous completion on the calling thread, consider using a runAndWait helper or adding callbacks to be notified after rename completion.

Notes
- This change improves stability and consistency of UI updates during cleanup operations that rename file entries.

Summary

Refactor and stabilize the Groups tree UI by moving logic out of the view and into a dedicated view model. This change clarifies responsibilities, improves maintainability, and fixes several issues related to selection and tree updates.

What I changed

- Added/updated GroupTreeViewModel to encapsulate the state and behavior previously handled directly in GroupTreeView.

- Minor performance improvements by centralizing tree update logic in the model.
- Updated CHANGELOG.md with an entry describing the change.

Separating model logic from the view makes the codebase easier to reason about and reduces bugs where UI state and business logic were mixed. The fixes address user-visible issues such as lost selection after group changes and unstable behavior when manipulating groups.

Testing

- Manual verification of common group interactions: creation, renaming, deletion, drag-and-drop, and selection persistence after refreshes.
- Verified keyboard navigation and focus behavior in the groups tree.

Notes for reviewers

- Review primarily focuses on the split of responsibilities between GroupTreeView and GroupTreeViewModel and the correctness of selection/update behavior.
- No public API changes outside the GUI internals.

text:
Summary

- Fix GUI logging to always run on the JavaFX Application Thread and make it resilient to threading issues.
- Improve JabRefException to better preserve cause and message information.
- Harden DefaultTaskExecutor with a utility method for scheduling tasks on the JavaFX thread and safer task execution.

Changes

1) src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/logging/GuiAppender.java
- Ensure all UI-related append operations are executed on the JavaFX Application Thread using DefaultTaskExecutor.
- Surround append code with try/catch to avoid logging failures from propagating and affecting application stability.
- Simplify thread dispatch logic and centralize JavaFX scheduling to DefaultTaskExecutor.

2) src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/util/DefaultTaskExecutor.java
- Add a dedicated API to schedule work on the JavaFX Application Thread (runInJavaFXThread / runInJavaFXThreadAsync semantics).
- Use Platform.isFxApplicationThread to avoid unnecessary scheduling when already on the FX thread.
- Improve exception handling for submitted tasks to prevent silent failures and to log uncaught exceptions.
- Minor thread-safety and shutdown reliability improvements.

3) src/main/java/org/jabref/JabRefException.java
- Add constructors that accept a cause (Throwable) and message+cause to preserve original exception information.
- Ensure the cause is stored and that message formatting is consistent.
- Add serialVersionUID and minor API cleanups to make the exception easier to work with in catch/throw scenarios.

Rationale

- Logging from non-JavaFX threads to UI components can cause IllegalStateExceptions and visual glitches. Ensuring append operations run on the FX thread avoids these problems.
- Richer JabRefException constructors make it easier to wrap lower-level exceptions without losing the original stack trace or cause.
- Centralizing FX scheduling in DefaultTaskExecutor reduces duplicate code and makes behavior consistent across the app.

Compatibility & Migration

- No public API breaking changes expected beyond the added convenience constructors in JabRefException and new scheduling helpers in DefaultTaskExecutor.
- Callers that previously handled FX scheduling around GuiAppender no longer need to, as GuiAppender now ensures correct threading internally.

Testing

- Manual testing performed by exercising logging while interacting with the UI and by throwing/wrapping exceptions to verify cause propagation and logging stability.

Notes

- If your code directly scheduled GUI logging on the FX thread prior to this change, it will continue to work. If you relied on logging to run synchronously, be aware that GuiAppender may schedule work on the FX thread (when necessary). If synchronous behavior is required, consider using DefaultTaskExecutor APIs explicitly.

Summary:
- Introduce builder-style APIs and small API cleanups, replace direct LinkedFile constructors with factory methods, add null-safety checks, and update some submodule pointers and IDE profile.

Notable changes:

1) AutoCompletionTextInputBinding (jabgui)
- Added Objects import and improved Javadoc.
- Introduced a Builder<T> inner class to configure and create AutoCompletionTextInputBinding instances (withConverter, withInputAnalyzer, withShowOnFocus, build).
- Updated existing convenience static autoComplete(...) methods to use the new Builder and to expose additional configuration options.
- Default behavior preserved but creation is now more flexible and readable.

2) LinkedFile usage (jabgui)
- Replaced direct LinkedFile constructor calls with factory methods: LinkedFile.of(...) and LinkedFile.fromUrl(...).
- Files updated: AutoSetFileLinksUtil, DownloadFullTextAction, ExternalFilesEntryLinker.
- This aligns callers with the new LinkedFile factory API.

3) BibDatabaseContext (jablib)
- Reworded and tightened Javadoc; added guidance to use the new Builder for custom instances.
- Replaced @NonNull-based parameters with explicit Objects.requireNonNull checks in constructors/setters where appropriate.
- Marked the 3-arg constructor as @Deprecated and made the 4-arg constructor private (internal use) to encourage using the Builder.
- Added a static Builder class with fluent withDatabase, withMetaData, withDatabasePath, withLocation and build() methods.
- Minor formatting and annotation adjustments (getFulltextIndexPath signature formatting).

4) Misc
- Added IDE inspection profile (.idea/inspectionProfiles/Project_Default.xml) turning off some inspections by default.
- Updated submodule commit pointers for jablib resources (csl-locales, csl-styles, and abbrv repo reference).

Why:
- Builder patterns improve clarity and extensibility when constructing complex objects.
- Factory methods for LinkedFile centralize instantiation logic and make code resilient to internal LinkedFile changes.
- Explicit null checks improve robustness and make contracts clearer.
- Submodule updates and IDE config are housekeeping changes.

Compatibility / Migration notes:
- Call sites that previously invoked new LinkedFile(...) must now use LinkedFile.of(...) or LinkedFile.fromUrl(...).
- Code that constructed BibDatabaseContext with certain constructors should migrate to BibDatabaseContext.Builder for new code; the old 3-arg constructor is deprecated.

Solution proposal for #4854 

In `FindFullTextAction`, `Task` is now used instead of `BackgroundTask` to be able to show a progress dialog which shows the progress for searching files online.

![lookupDialog](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/24212145/55612578-cabc0800-5788-11e9-92b4-ec4081977b7d.PNG)

Furthermore, the functionality for downloading a file in `LinkedFileViewModel` is split into `download` and `prepareDownloadTask` to be able to define a custom onSucess-action for the background task. The functionality provided by `LinkedFileViewModel.dowload` remains as it is, so it does not affect the download of a single file via the EntryEditor.

- This is a draft / WIP: more CLI options from CitationKeyPatternPreferences will be added incrementally.

Add support for sending entries via external email and Kindle, and provide a new External Applications preference UI to configure related settings.

What changed
- Introduced SendAsEMailAction, SendAsStandardEmailAction, and SendAsKindleEmailAction to handle sending selected entries through email (including Kindle addresses).
- Integrated the new send-as-email actions into the UI: wired them into the main frame (JabRefFrame), the main table right-click menu (RightClickMenu), and standard action registry (StandardActions).
- Added a new External tab in Preferences (ExternalTab.fxml, ExternalTab, ExternalTabViewModel) to let users configure external application settings such as email/Kindle addresses and commands.
- Added ExternalApplicationsPreferences and extended JabRefPreferences to persist external app related preferences.
- Updated localization strings (JabRef_en.properties) and documented the change in CHANGELOG.md.

Why this matters
- Users can now send bibliographic entries directly via email or to a Kindle address from within JabRef and can configure how external applications (including a Kindle email) are invoked.
- The new preferences UI makes it simpler to manage external application settings and improves integration with system email capabilities.

Notes
- UI elements and actions are connected so the functionality is accessible from the main menu and context (right-click) menus.

- Set search.setDefaultButton(false) so the search button is no longer the default button and no longer intercepts Enter presses from other controls.

Summary

Refactor and polish various field editor components: FieldNameLabel, FileListEditor, TextArea and TextField. These changes unify common behavior across editors (focus, keyboard handling, selection), fix a number of UX issues, and add small quality-of-life improvements for file handling. The CHANGELOG is updated to reflect the changes.

What I changed

- General
  - Extracted and unified common behaviors across field editor components (focus handling, select-on-focus behavior, keyboard/focus traversal). This reduces duplicated code and ensures consistent UX across text fields and areas.
  - Improved keyboard handling and caret/selection behavior to avoid surprising cursor jumps when focusing or pasting text.

- FieldNameLabel (src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/FieldNameLabel.java)
  - Improved focus and keyboard accessibility so labels behave consistently with other field editors.
  - Small refactor to simplify label interaction code and make mnemonic/tooltip behavior predictable.

- FileListEditor (src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/FileListEditor.java)
  - Improved file entry handling and editing flow (double-click and keyboard navigation feel more natural).
  - Better handling of file link clicks and context menu actions; fixed issues with selection/activation while editing entries.
  - Minor robustness improvements around drag-and-drop and path resolution.

- TextArea & TextField (src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/TextArea.java, src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/TextField.java)
  - Ensure consistent select-on-focus behavior and caret positioning across single-line and multi-line editors.
  - Fixed issues with undo/redo and multi-line paste that resulted in incorrect caret placement or lost selection.
  - Small refactors to simplify input validation and reduce duplicated logic.

- CHANGELOG.md
  - Added entries summarizing these UX and refactor improvements.

Why this change

These changes make field editors behave consistently and predictably across the app, reduce duplicated code, and address several small but noticeable bugs related to focus, selection, and file-list interactions. This improves overall usability for editing entries and files.

Notes for reviewers

- Mostly refactors and behavioral fixes. No public API changes intended; however, reviewers should check editor interactions (select-on-focus, paste behavior, double-click file open, keyboard navigation) to confirm parity with previous behavior and that no regressions were introduced.
- If anything in the UI feels different than expected, please highlight specific steps to reproduce so we can adjust behavior accordingly.

Fixes #12215

Problem: When multiple files were attached, the tooltip and context menu in the "Linked File" tab removed the first underscore (_) from file names. Internally the file paths were correct and files opened correctly, but JavaFX treats underscore as a mnemonic indicator, causing the first underscore to be hidden in displayed text.

Solution: Update ControlHelper.truncateString() to escape single underscores by replacing "_" with "__" before rendering text in the UI. This preserves visible underscores in tooltips and context menu entries while leaving internal paths unchanged.

Testing: Manually verified that the first underscore is now shown correctly in tooltips and context menus. Screenshot attached showing the fix.

Notes: This change only affects displayed labels; no file handling logic was modified.

Improve AbbreviateAction behavior and robustness

What changed
- AbbreviateAction was refactored to be more robust and user friendly.
- Long-running abbreviation work is executed off the JavaFX UI thread to avoid freezing the interface.
- Additional null/selection checks were added so the action safely handles empty selections or entries without a journal field.
- Progress and completion are reported to the user (via existing UI notification mechanisms) and operations that have no effect are skipped with a clear message.
- Improved logging and error handling so failures during abbreviation are reported without crashing the UI.

Why
- Previously, abbreviating many entries could freeze the UI and could produce unexpected exceptions when no suitable field/entry was available. Running the work in the background and adding defensive checks improves stability and user experience.

Testing
- Manually tested with single and multiple entry selections, empty selections, and entries missing the journal field to verify no UI freeze and correct notifications on completion or when there is nothing to do.

Compatibility
- No public API changes; behavior is compatible with existing workflows but more resilient to edge cases.

Notes for reviewers
- Focus review on threading (background task usage), null checks, and user notification flows. Ensure logging and error messages match application conventions.

text:
Fix behavior when importing entries from the browser extension while JabRef is not running (fixes #10450)

Summary
- Previously, when the browser extension sent an import request and JabRef was closed, JabRef would create a temporary database and import the entry without letting the user choose where to store it. This change prevents creation of an anonymous temporary database and instead opens the application and prompts the user to choose an existing library or create a new one before importing.

What I changed
- Modified the startup/import request handling so that incoming import requests are queued until the main window and database selection UI are available.
- Removed the automatic creation of a temporary database for external imports when no library is open.
- When no database is open, JabRef now presents a prompt to the user to select an existing library, create a new one, or cancel the import. Only after the user selects a target does the import proceed and the Import dialog is shown.
- Updated the browser-extension import handler to forward the import payload to the main application on startup rather than performing an immediate import.
- Added unit/integration tests covering the new startup + import flow and user selection behavior.

Why this fixes #10450
- The reported problem occurred because external import requests were handled immediately even if JabRef had no open library, resulting in a temporary DB the user could not control. By deferring the import until the user selects where to import, imports are now deterministic and visible to the user.

How to test manually
1. Close JabRef.
2. Trigger an import via the browser extension (or simulate the same import request).
3. Verify JabRef starts, shows a prompt to select or create a database, and does not silently import into a temporary DB.
4. Choose a database and confirm the imported entry appears in the selected library.

Notes
- This change is backward compatible for users who already have a library open: in that case the import still proceeds directly into the open library.
- Addresses the usability issue described in #10450 and adds tests to prevent regression.
