Summary

This PR improves the handling and parsing of journal abbreviation files and ensures reliable repository reloads when abbreviation files change. It also ports bug fixes and edge-case handling into the unit tests.

What changed

- src/main/java/org/jabref/collab/FileUpdateMonitor.java
  - Fixed race conditions and improved detection of external file updates so that listeners are reliably notified when abbreviation files change.
  - Improved resource management for the underlying watcher to avoid missed events and potential leaks.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/journals/AbbreviationParser.java
  - Hardened the parser against malformed lines: now skips empty lines and comments, trims tokens, and tolerates missing fields instead of failing.
  - Improved handling of entries containing commas or unusual separators so abbreviations and full names are parsed correctly.
  - Normalizes parsed keys (e.g. lower-casing and trimming) to make lookups stable.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/journals/JournalAbbreviationRepository.java
  - Ensures consistent caching and reload behavior: repository now reloads when the monitored file changes and avoids returning stale data.
  - Improved error handling during load, and ensures the internal map does not contain duplicate or malformed entries.
  - Exposed clearer APIs for requesting a reload and for querying whether the repository is currently up-to-date.

- Tests
  - src/test/java/org/jabref/gui/journals/ManageJournalAbbreviationsViewModelTest.java
    - Updated and extended tests to reflect parser robustness and to validate UI model behavior when abbreviations are reloaded.

  - src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/journals/JournalAbbreviationRepositoryTest.java
    - Added tests for reload-on-change, ignored malformed lines, normalization of keys, and duplicate handling.
    - Fixed unstable timing-related assertions by making the file-monitoring behavior deterministic in tests.

Why this change

- Users reported that updated journal abbreviation files were not always picked up by JabRef and that some abbreviation files with unusual formatting caused exceptions or incorrect mappings. These changes make parsing more tolerant and make repository updates reliable.

Impact

- More robust loading and parsing of journal abbreviation files.
- Fewer crashes or mis-parsed abbreviations caused by malformed files.
- UI and other consumers of the repository will see up-to-date abbreviations when files are externally modified.

Notes

- Behavior for legacy or custom abbreviation file formats remains supported where possible; malformed entries are now skipped with logging instead of causing a load failure.
- Tests were updated to be deterministic and to cover the new edge cases.

text:
Summary

Fixes a bug where attempting to remove multiple groups would only delete one group. The delete action and state update now correctly remove all selected groups.

Problem

When the user selected several groups and clicked delete, only a single group was removed from the backend and the UI. This happened because the delete handler only processed one id and the client-side state update removed only that one id.

Root cause

- The deletion flow used a single id (or resolved only the first id) instead of iterating over the full selection/bulk payload.
- The store/component state update filtered out only one id, leaving other selected groups intact in the UI and backend.

What I changed

- Updated the delete handler to process all selected group ids. The handler now either calls the bulk delete endpoint (if available) or iterates through the selection and issues deletes for each id.
- Fixed the state mutation so all deleted ids are removed from the local store/state in one operation.
- Cleared the selection after successful deletion and ensured the group list refreshes to reflect backend state.
- Added error handling for partial failures: if some deletions fail, the UI shows an error and refreshes to reflect the actual server state.

Tests

- Added unit tests to verify multiple ids are sent to the delete flow and that the store removes all deleted ids.
- Added an integration/e2e test that selects multiple groups, deletes them, and asserts they no longer appear in the list.

Manual verification steps

1. Create or select multiple groups in the UI.
2. Click delete and confirm.
3. Verify all selected groups are removed from the list and selection is cleared.
4. Verify no leftover group entries or errors occur.

Notes

This change is backwards compatible. If a bulk delete API is available the code will use it; otherwise it falls back to iterating individual deletes while aggregating results. Error handling ensures the UI remains consistent with server state.

text:
Add robust file-field parsing and LinkedFile handling, plus unit tests.

What I changed:
- Implement FileFieldParser.parse to decode JabRef file-field strings into LinkedFile objects. The parser handles escaped characters (backslash), XML special character constructs (e.g. ,), separators (colon for fields, semicolon for multiple files), online links (URLs) and malformed URLs, missing fields, and entries with varying numbers of separators. It normalizes and collects entries into LinkedFile instances.
- Enhance LinkedFile behavior: properties are transient for serialization, with custom writeObject/readObject methods. link normalization replaces backslashes with forward slashes for local paths, and there are helper methods isOnlineLink and findIn to locate files in provided directories. A NULL_OBJECT is used for empty checks.
- Add comprehensive tests in FileFieldWriterTest covering: empty input, parsing normal and online inputs (including malformed URLs), handling missing descriptions, escaped characters and XML constructs, escaped file paths, subsets of fields (description-only, file-only, type-only), extra separators, and string encoding/quoting behavior used for writing file fields.

Notes and considerations:
- MalformedURLException during URL construction is silently ignored and parsing falls back to creating a local Path-based LinkedFile.
- Path.of is used for local file links; invalid path input is handled defensively in findIn.
- Unit tests assert expected parsing and encoding behavior to prevent regressions.

Make font size in entry editor and group panel customizable

Summary
- Add support for using the "Menu and label font size" preference for various JavaFX UI parts (entry editor, source editor, linked files context menu, and groups tree).
- Update CHANGELOG to mention the new behavior. (Fixes #3034)

What I changed
- ENTRY EDITOR (EntryEditor.java): apply font-size style to the tabbed pane created for the entry editor using Globals.prefs.getFontSizeFX().
- SOURCE TAB (SourceTab.java):
  - Reorganized getSourceString (removed duplicate) and applied the font-size style to the code area’s styled-text-area so the source view respects the preference.
- LINKED FILES (LinkedFilesEditor.java): set the context menu font size style so file context menus match the configured font size.
- GROUPS TREE (GroupTreeController.java): import Globals and set the group tree style to use the configured font size.
- PREFERENCES (JabRefPreferences.java): added getFontSizeFX() which converts the existing "Menu and label font size" preference into a JavaFX-friendly font size (subtract 3 because JavaFX default is 9 vs Swing 12).
- CHANGELOG.md: added an Unreleased entry describing this change and referenced issue #3034.

Implementation notes
- Styling is applied via inline -fx-font-size CSS on the relevant JavaFX nodes, using Globals.prefs.getFontSizeFX() to obtain the adjusted size.
- The preference conversion is intentionally offset to account for the different default font sizes between Swing and JavaFX so the visual size matches user expectations.

No behavioral changes to data handling were introduced; this only affects presentation/font sizes.

  - Refactored Abbreviation model to be clearer and more robust (src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/journals/Abbreviation.java).

- Adds tests to prevent regressions and ensure future changes preserve expected behavior.
- Keeps the project IDE configuration consistent for contributors.

- No user-facing UI changes; this is an internal logic and tooling improvement.

Add ImportHandler to manage importing external files and bibliographic data into a library.

This class centralizes import logic and user interactions for different input types (PDF, .bib files, pasted BibTeX or identifier strings). Key behaviors and features:
- Background import task for multiple files with progress and messages (uses BackgroundTask, UiTaskExecutor and TaskExecutor).
- Detects PDF, BibTeX (.bib) and other files; extracts BibTeX entries from PDFs or .bib files via ExternalFilesContentImporter, and creates an empty entry with a linked file when no BibTeX data is found.
- Adds imported entries to the database on the JavaFX thread, registers undo edits (UndoableInsertEntries + UndoManager) and records per-file import results.
- Cleans up entries (ImportCleanup), imports cleaned entries, generates citation keys (CitationKeyGenerator) according to preferences, sets automatic fields, and adds entries to selected groups.
- Duplicate detection and resolution flow: findDuplicate, handleDuplicates, getDuplicateDecision using DuplicateResolverDialog; supports applying the same merge decision to all entries via preferences.
- Methods to import string constants with duplicate checks and to import data by identifier (DOI, arXiv, ISBN) or by attempting generic import formats (ImportFormatReader).
- Downloads online linked files after import when enabled in preferences (LinkedFileViewModel.download).
- Exposed helper methods (e.g., cleanUpEntry annotated @VisibleForTesting) and comprehensive logging and user dialogs for errors and warnings.

This consolidates file/content import handling, duplicate resolution and post-import processing and integrates with UI threading, undo, preferences and the dialog service.

This PR fixes a logical bug in the syncLang script (the merging/merging-duplicates logic) and refactors the script to be easier to use and maintain. It addresses #3573.

- Fix: Corrected merging logic when synchronizing properties files (resolves the bug reported in #3573).

- Logging: Reworked the extended logging flag to be explicit (extended_logging) and wired it into the new CLI (-e/--extended).
- Markdown: status_create_markdown now accepts a filename argument; markdown subcommand added.
- Safety/compatibility: argparse usage is safe for Python 2.7 (Jython) per code comment.
- Small behavior change: code that automatically inserted main translations for missing keys has been commented with a note (missing keys are not auto-filled anymore by default).

Other improvements

- Consolidated file read/write helpers and ensured UTF-8 handling via codecs.
- Better separation of concerns and more modular functions to ease future maintenance and testing.

- The change was tested manually (see issue comment). Automated tests and documentation updates were not added in this PR.
- This closes #3573.

text:
Closes #11937

Summary

This PR fixes TAB navigation inside the Entry Editor: pressing TAB on the last field of a tab now moves focus to the first field of the next tab (instead of stopping or moving focus outside the editor).

What changed

- Implemented tab-navigation logic in EditorTextField with static setupTabNavigation(...) so EditorTextField instances can detect when TAB was pressed on the last field and request selecting the next tab.
- Added an isLastFieldInCurrentTab(TextField) helper in EntryEditor to determine whether a given TextField is the last field shown in the currently selected tab. EntryEditor registers this checker together with a next-tab selector when it is constructed.
- Ensured field controls have stable ids so the last-field check works:
  - SimpleEditor.createTextInputControl(...) now accepts Field and sets the control id
  - PersonsEditor, CitationKeyEditor and SimpleEditor now set ids on their TextField/TextInputControl instances
  - MarkdownEditor adjusted createTextInputControl signature to pass the Field
- CHANGELOG.md updated to mention the bugfix.

Files modified (high level)

- EntryEditor.java: added isLastFieldInCurrentTab(...) and registered EditorTextField.setupTabNavigation(...)
- EditorTextField.java: added tab-key event handling and setupTabNavigation static API
- SimpleEditor.java / MarkdownEditor.java / PersonsEditor.java / CitationKeyEditor.java: set control ids and adjusted factory signatures where needed
- CHANGELOG.md: added entry for this bugfix

Behavior notes

- Navigation is scoped to the Entry Editor: TAB presses that reach the last field of a tab will move to the first field of the next tab in the Entry Editor. The change does not affect focus navigation outside the Entry Editor.
- Works for both single-line (EditorTextField) and multi-line editors (EditorTextArea) used by SimpleEditor, PersonsEditor and MarkdownEditor.

Testing steps

1. Open JabRef and load an entry in the Entry Editor.
2. Use TAB to move through fields inside a tab.
3. When focus is on the last field of a tab, press TAB again.
4. Verify focus moves to the first field in the next tab of the Entry Editor.
5. Repeat across multiple tabs and verify focus does not jump to unrelated UI elements outside the Entry Editor.
6. Test with single-line and multi-line fields (SimpleEditor, PersonsEditor, MarkdownEditor).

Other

- Co-Contributor: Noah-Martin1
- All changes are referenced in CHANGELOG.md

text:
Fixes #4688 — Merge optional / optional2 / other fields tabs and simplify layout

Summary
- Merge the various "optional" tabs into a single "Optional fields" tab and remove the now-redundant OptionalFields2Tab and OtherFieldsTab classes.
- Simplify the entry editor layout by removing the compressed two-column layout for optional/other fields; fields are now rendered in a single column to avoid layout issues.
- Update OptionalFieldsTabBase to determine which fields to show based on the entry's actual fields (fields that are not part of the entry type's known fields) and to exclude deprecated fields.
- Remove instantiation of the removed tabs from EntryEditor and update the UI resources slightly (additional imports in the FXML).
- Add a changelog entry describing the change.

Files changed (high level)
- Deleted: src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/entryeditor/OptionalFields2Tab.java
- Deleted: src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/entryeditor/OtherFieldsTab.java
- Updated: src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/entryeditor/OptionalFieldsTabBase.java (new logic for fields to show)
- Updated: src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/entryeditor/FieldsEditorTab.java (removed compressed two-column layout code)
- Updated: src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/entryeditor/EntryEditor.java (stop creating removed tabs)
- Updated: src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/customentrytypes/CustomizeEntryTypeDialog.fxml (minor import additions)
- Updated: CHANGELOG.md (note about fixing #4688)

Behavioral details
- The GUI now shows a single "Optional fields" tab that contains what used to be spread across Optional fields, Optional fields 2 and Other fields.
- The logic in OptionalFieldsTabBase now collects fields present on an entry that are not part of the entry type’s known fields and removes deprecated fields. This merges the previously-separated sets into a single tab.
- The compressed two-column rendering (which previously attempted to split fields into two columns) has been removed. All fields are displayed in a single, regular row layout to avoid misaligned/ugly field editors.

Why
- This PR addresses issue #4688 by consolidating redundant tabs and simplifying presentation, fixing layout problems and reducing UI complexity.

How to test / verify manually
1. Create a new library.
2. Add a new entry (e.g. via "New entry") and set a type / DOI etc.
3. Open the entry editor (double-click an entry) and inspect the tab area: there should be a single "Optional fields" tab (in addition to other existing tabs). Fields that previously appeared in Optional fields 2 / Other fields should now be available there.

Notes
- UI screenshots showing before/after were included in the original issue/PR description to demonstrate the layout problem and the result.
- This change removes two classes/files from the codebase; if any external code relied on those classes directly, it will need to be adjusted.

Changelog
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to mention the fix for #4688 (merging optional, optional2 and otherFields).

Checklist
- CHANGELOG entry updated
- Manual testing performed
- Tests added where applicable

text: This pull request introduces a new feature that allows users to select a reference library during AUX file import. This is achieved by adding a dropdown menu in the `FromAuxDialog` which lists all currently open databases. The user can choose the library against which the AUX file should be parsed. The selected library is used as the reference for identifying and resolving BibTeX keys. If the generated database contains no entries, the 'Generate' button remains disabled. text:
Improve UX for file rename conflicts by adding a dialog with clearer options and button tooltips

What this PR does
- Adds a new DialogService API: showCustomButtonDialogWithTooltipsAndWait(...) to allow attaching tooltips to dialog buttons.
- Implements the new API in JabRefDialogService, attaching Tooltip objects to dialog buttons (using Platform.runLater).
- Updates LinkedFileViewModel.rename flow to detect existing files and present a clearer conflict dialog with the options: Replace, Keep both, Provide alternative file name, and Cancel. The "Keep both" option includes a tooltip that shows a suggested non-conflicting filename (computed via FileNameUniqueness).
- Adds relevant localization strings for the new dialog texts and tooltips.
- Updates CHANGELOG.md with a short note about the improved file-exists warning dialog.

Why
- Renaming linked files could unintentionally overwrite an existing file. Before this change the user was presented with a single overwrite confirmation. Now the UI offers clear alternatives (keep both, replace, provide alternative) and shows a suggested non-conflicting filename, reducing accidental data loss and improving clarity.

Implementation notes
- New DialogService method signature uses a Map<ButtonType,String> to provide per-button tooltip text.
- JabRefDialogService attaches tooltips by looking up buttons from the dialog pane and calling setTooltip on each Button.
- LinkedFileViewModel now builds the dialog with explicit ButtonType instances, a tooltip for the "Keep both" option and handles each result accordingly (replace => overwrite, keep both => use suggested name, provide alternative => prompt user, cancel => abort).
- IOException during rename still displays an error dialog.

Files changed (high level)
- jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/DialogService.java: add new API method
- jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/JabRefDialogService.java: implement new API
- jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/LinkedFileViewModel.java: use new dialog to handle existing-file conflicts and suggest non-conflicting file names
- jablib/src/main/resources/l10n/JabRef_en.properties: add strings for new dialog
- CHANGELOG.md: add note about improved file exists warning dialog

Backward compatibility
- DialogService interface extended; implementation added in JabRefDialogService to keep runtime compatibility. Review other custom implementations of DialogService (if any) when backporting this change to alternative builds.

- Reworked build logic to rely on explicit JaCoCo report/merge tasks where needed.
- Updated comments/documentation that referenced the property.

The append flag caused exec data to be merged across test runs, producing misleading coverage results. Relying on the plugin defaults and explicit merge tasks yields clearer and more predictable coverage artifacts.

Testing:
- Local and CI builds completed successfully.
- Unit/integration tests pass.
- Verified JaCoCo reports are generated and reflect expected (non-aggregated) coverage numbers.

Impact & notes for reviewers:
- No runtime or production behavior changes expected.
- Coverage reports may differ from previous aggregated results; re-run coverage reports to see updated numbers.
- If you relied on implicit appending, consider adding an explicit jacocoMerge task to recreate that behavior. Please check CI artifacts and build files for any remaining references to "append".

Summary

Add a scheduled GitHub Actions workflow that checks external links in repository Markdown files once a month.

Why

The repository contains many Markdown documentation files with external links. Running link checks on every PR is noisy and interferes with normal development. A monthly scheduled check notifies maintainers about broken links while avoiding disruption of PR workflows (see issue #6677).

What I changed

- Added a new GitHub Actions workflow (.github/workflows/check-external-links.yml) that runs monthly.
- The workflow installs Node.js and runs markdown-link-check (the same tool used previously) against repository .md files.
- A small allow/ignore list is used to skip known problematic hosts (e.g. GitHub.com endpoints that return 403), see .markdown-link-check.json (or the config section in the workflow).

Known limitations

- Some hosts (notably github.com) return 403 and must be explicitly disabled/ignored. See discussion in PR #6542 and the upstream issue about status filtering: https://github.com/tcort/markdown-link-check/issues/94#issuecomment-634947466.
- The tool can produce false positives for transient network problems and rate limits. The monthly schedule aims to reduce noise but occasional manual follow-up may be required.

How to run locally

- Install Node.js and run: npm install -g markdown-link-check
- Run the check against a file: markdown-link-check README.md -c .markdown-link-check.json

Follow-up / future work

- Improve filtering rules for specific HTTP status codes if/when the tool supports it.
- Consider additional scheduling or integrations (e.g. Slack/email) for link failure notifications if desired.

Related issues/PRs

- Issue: #6677
- Related PR: #6542

Checklist

- [x] Add scheduled workflow
- [ ] Update config to fine-tune ignored hosts (future)

This change implements the chosen option from the decision process: "Check external links once a month" to reduce noise in PRs while still detecting broken documentation links.

Summary
Optimize saving logic to reduce redundant work and improve save throughput and latency.

What changed
- Introduced a centralized SaveManager that batches/coalesces save requests for the same entity to avoid duplicate writes.
- Replaced many per-item synchronous DB writes with bulk operations where appropriate (bulk upsert/delete) to cut round-trips.
- Added a delta check to skip serialization and DB writes when an object has not changed.
- Moved heavy serialization work off the hot path (lazy serialization / serialize on background worker) for operations that can be deferred.
- Ensured save operations use transactions for consistency when batching multiple related updates.
- Minor refactor of serializer and DB adapter to expose bulk methods and make intent clearer.

Why
- Reduce the number of database calls and expensive serializations when a large number of rapid updates occur.
- Improve responsiveness for user-facing actions by offloading expensive work to background tasks and batching.
- Maintain data consistency while improving throughput.

Testing
- Added unit tests covering batching, skipping unchanged objects, and transactional behavior.
- Added integration tests for bulk upserts and background save flow.
- Basic benchmarks included demonstrating reduced DB calls and improved end-to-end save latency (see benchmark files).

Migration / Backwards compatibility
- No API changes for external callers. All changes are internal and should be transparent to existing code.

Testing

- Manual testing performed on multiple Linux environments to verify that files and URLs open correctly using the available system openers.
- Verified fallback behavior when Desktop.getDesktop() is unavailable and when common openers are not present.

Notes for reviewers

- Focus review on the detection logic and process invocation in Linux.java to ensure it is conservative and does not introduce platform-specific regressions.
- CHANGELOG.md update is small and reflects the user-visible fix.

Compatibility

No migration steps required for users. This is a bugfix to improve behavior on Linux.

text:
Fix DOI extraction to avoid including trailing punctuation and add tests.

Summary:
- Update DOI regex in org.jabref.model.entry.identifier.DOI to avoid capturing trailing punctuation (spaces, commas, semicolons) and to ensure the suffix does not end with a period/comma/semicolon. This prevents punctuation from being included in detected DOIs.
- Add unit tests in DOITest to cover DOIs followed by ",", ";" and ".", as well as ensuring legitimate DOI suffixes containing dots are still captured (e.g. 10.1007/s10549-018-4743-9.1234). Also add tests for short DOI occurrences followed by punctuation.

Details:
- Regex change: previously the suffix was matched with "(?:[^\\s]+)" which could consume trailing punctuation. The new pattern "(?:[^\\s,;]+[^,;(\\.\\s)])" disallows commas/semicolons within the end of the matched suffix and prevents the match from ending on ".", "," or ";".
- Tests added/expanded in DOITest to validate extraction in various surrounding text scenarios (commas, semicolons, periods, and embedded dots in the DOI suffix).

This resolves cases where extracted DOIs contained trailing separators, improving DOI detection robustness.

Summary

Fixes an issue where keyboard shortcuts in Preferences → Keyboard shortcuts could not be edited. The KeyEvent was being consumed by global application shortcuts before it reached the shortcut editor in KeyBindingsTab, so pressing keys did not update the selected shortcut and changes were not persisted.

What I changed

- Added a key event filter in KeyBindingsTab so the TreeTableView receives key presses.
- Forward key events to the ViewModel via setNewBindingForCurrent to update the selected binding.
- Ensure edited shortcuts are persisted by syncing the repository into GuiPreferences.
- Added/updated a JUnit test to verify binding update behavior.
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to document the fix.

Behavioral notes

UI remains unchanged; the fix ensures that when a user selects an entry in the keyboard shortcuts list and types a new key combination, the selection is updated, Save persists the new binding, and the shortcut works after restart.

How to test

1. Open JabRef → Preferences → Keyboard shortcuts.
2. Select any shortcut entry (e.g., “Close library”).
3. Press a new key combination (e.g., Ctrl+Shift+L).
4. Click Save.
5. Restart JabRef.
6. Verify that:

This PR addresses a missing module error caused by the absence of Apache Commons Text on the module path. It ensures the commons-text module is available at compile/runtime and in the jlink image.

- Similar change: https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/pull/10689

- Manual testing / rebuilding the jlink image is recommended to confirm the error is resolved.

- Consolidated duplicated equals(...) logic into a single, shared implementation (utility/base) so related classes behave consistently.
- Fixed bugs around null handling and subclass comparisons that broke symmetry and transitivity.
- Ensured equals and hashCode implementations are consistent with the contract (if two objects are equal, their hashCode is equal).

- Replaced per-class duplicated equals code with calls to the unified helper or shared base implementation.
- Updated or removed custom equals overrides that were redundant or incorrect.
- Added/updated unit tests to cover equality semantics (nulls, cross-class comparisons, hashCode consistency).

Impact:
- No public API changes; behaviour is more predictable and correct.
- Potential risk: classes that relied on the previous (incorrect) behavior may need to be reviewed, but tests exercise expected equality semantics.

Testing:
- Ran full test suite and added unit tests verifying reflexivity, symmetry, transitivity, null handling, and hashCode consistency.

Fixes #6621 — Disable automatic synchronization of special fields to keywords by default and consolidate special fields preference usage

Summary
- Change the default to NOT synchronize special fields to keywords (Autosync disabled by default).
- Centralize and modernize access to special-fields preferences, replacing scattered JabRefPreferences boolean checks with SpecialFieldsPreferences methods.
- Small API/behavioral cleanups and refactorings such as passing a ClipBoardManager where needed, replacing deprecated getFile usage with getPath(), and minor code style improvements (switch expressions, Optional handling, String.join).

What changed
- Default behavior
  - JabRefPreferences: AUTOSYNCSPECIALFIELDSTOKEYWORDS now defaults to false and SERIALIZESPECIALFIELDS defaults to true. CHANGELOG updated accordingly.

- Special fields preferences
  - SpecialFieldsPreferences: renamed getters to clearer names (isSpecialFieldsEnabled, shouldAutoSyncSpecialFieldsToKeyWords, shouldSerializeSpecialFields) and added isKeywordSyncEnabled() which returns (specialFieldsEnabled && autoSyncSpecialFieldsToKeyWords).
  - Preferences are now read via PreferencesService.getSpecialFieldsPreferences() / Globals.prefs.getSpecialFieldsPreferences() in multiple places.
  - PreferencesService interface: removed isKeywordSyncEnabled() (always use getSpecialFieldsPreferences().isKeywordSyncEnabled()).
  - JabRefPreferences stores/reads SpecialFieldsPreferences using the new method names.

- Behavior changes in code paths
  - Special field updates and actions now consult SpecialFieldsPreferences.isKeywordSyncEnabled() when deciding to synchronize keywords (SpecialFieldAction, SpecialFieldViewModel, ManageKeywordsViewModel, etc.).
  - ParserResult: introduced getPath() returning Optional<Path> and kept getFile() as deprecated. Parsing-related equality and tab-open checks switched to use Path-based methods.
  - MainTable/RightClickMenu: ClipBoardManager is injected where previously Globals.clipboardManager was used; updated constructors and menu creation accordingly.

- Miscellaneous cleanups
  - Replaced several switch statements with Java switch expressions in view models (SpecialFieldValueViewModel, SpecialFieldViewModel, TableTabViewModel).
  - Use String.join for joining warnings in ParserResult.getErrorMessage().
  - Small UI code tidy-ups (lambda formatting, path filename handling improvements, etc.).

Files touched (high level)
- CHANGELOG.md
- Preferences: JabRefPreferences.java, PreferencesService.java, SpecialFieldsPreferences.java
- GUI: JabRefFrame.java, MainTable.java, RightClickMenu.java, TableTabViewModel.java, SpecialFieldAction.java, SpecialFieldViewModel.java, SpecialFieldValueViewModel.java, ManageKeywordsViewModel.java
- Logic: ParserResult.java

Notes
- This change intentionally switches off auto-sync by default to address surprising data modification behavior (see #6621). Users can re-enable synchronization in preferences.
- getFile() on ParserResult is kept as deprecated for compatibility; new code paths use getPath().
- The PR includes a small proof-of-concept refactor to reduce direct calls to JabRefPreferences.get()/put() by using typed preference objects. Further refactoring is possible to continue reducing scattered preference access.

Testing
- Manually tested in a running JabRef instance. No automated tests added in this PR.

Checklist
- CHANGELOG updated
- Manually tested

Summary

This PR enables command-line customization of citation key generation in JabKit. It introduces a new "citationkeys" command group with a "generate" subcommand and adds multiple CLI options that allow overriding CitationKeyPatternPreferences for the current run without changing GUI settings. Also updates the CHANGELOG and removes the old standalone `generate-citation-keys` command in favor of `citationkeys generate`.

What changed

- Added a new command group: `citationkeys` (jabkit/src/main/java/org/jabref/toolkit/commands/CitationKeys.java).
- Renamed the previous CLI command to the new subcommand: `citationkeys generate` (GenerateCitationKeys class):
  - Command name changed from `generate-citation-keys` to `generate` and moved under `citationkeys`.
  - New CLI options added to override citation key generation preferences at runtime:
    - --pattern (override default citation key pattern)
    - --transliterate
    - --warn-before-overwrite
    - --suffix (KeySuffix enum)
    - --regex
    - --regex-replacement
    - --unwanted
    - --keyword-delimiter
    - --avoid-overwrite
    - --generate-before-saving
  - The command now builds a CitationKeyPatternPreferences instance using provided CLI options (falling back to existing CLI preferences when options are not set) and uses it to create the CitationKeyGenerator for the run.
- Registered the new `citationkeys` command in JabKit's subcommands (jabkit/src/main/java/org/jabref/toolkit/commands/JabKit.java).
- CHANGELOG updated to mention the new CLI parameter support and the removal of the standalone command (CHANGELOG.md).

Behavior and compatibility notes

- CLI overrides only affect the current invocation; GUI preferences are not modified.
- The old standalone `generate-citation-keys` command has been removed; use `jabkit citationkeys generate` instead.

Example usage

:jabkit:run --args="citationkeys generate --input=C:\\git-repositories\\jabref\\jablib\\src\\main\\resources\\Chocolate.bib --pattern='[auth][year]'"

Notes / TODO

- This is a work in progress. More options from CitationKeyPatternPreferences will be added step-by-step as needed.
- Unit tests have not been added yet.
- Documentation and user docs updates are still TODO.

text:
Closes #14505

Summary

This PR fixes proxy preference reset behavior by introducing explicit defaults for ProxyPreferences and ensuring they are restored when preferences are cleared or when importing incomplete/corrupt preferences. It implements factory and helper methods to obtain and apply default proxy settings and centralizes reading proxy values from the backing store with fallbacks to defaults.

What changed

- jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/net/ProxyPreferences.java
  - Added a private no-arg constructor that creates a ProxyPreferences instance populated with sensible defaults (useProxy=false, hostname="", port="80", useAuthentication=false, empty credentials, persistPassword=false).
  - Added public static ProxyPreferences.getDefault() to obtain a default instance.
  - Added setAll(ProxyPreferences) to overwrite an instance's properties from another ProxyPreferences object.

- jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/preferences/JabRefCliPreferences.java
  - Removed hard-coded proxy defaults from the CLI defaults map and instead read proxy values from the backing store with fallbacks.
  - Added getProxyPreferencesFromBackingStore(ProxyPreferences defaults) to build ProxyPreferences using values from the backing store, falling back to provided defaults.
  - Updated getProxyPreferences() to use getProxyPreferencesFromBackingStore(ProxyPreferences.getDefault()).
  - When clearing preferences (clear()), proxy preferences are reset to defaults via setAll(ProxyPreferences.getDefault()).
  - When importing preferences, fall back to default proxy preferences in case of incomplete/corrupt XML.

Why

Previously proxy preferences were not reliably reset to their defaults when clearing preferences or when imports failed/are incomplete. By centralizing default values and using them when reading from the backing store, we ensure proxy settings are restored consistently and avoid stale/partial proxy configuration.

Behavioral notes / testing

- Clearing preferences now resets proxy settings to the new default ProxyPreferences.
- Importing preferences will fall back to default proxy settings if the import is incomplete or corrupt.
- The new API provides getDefault() and setAll(...) to support applying/resetting preferences.

Checklist

- [x] I manually tested changes in running JabRef.
- [x] Closes #14505
- [ ] Added unit tests (if applicable)
- [ ] Updated CHANGELOG / user documentation where applicable

Fix keyboard shortcuts editing in Preferences

Summary:
This PR fixes a bug that prevented users from editing keyboard shortcuts in Preferences. Selecting a shortcut would not enter edit mode or capture keystrokes, leaving bindings effectively read-only.

Root cause:
A regression in the shortcut editor's activation logic caused the component to remain in a non-editable state so keyboard events were never captured or applied.

What this changes:
- Ensure the shortcut editor toggles into edit mode on activation and receives keyboard input
- Capture and validate key combinations correctly and update the displayed binding
- Persist updated shortcut bindings via the settings API
- Add tests to cover activation, key capture, and persistence

QA / Testing steps:
1. Open Preferences → Keyboard Shortcuts
2. Click a shortcut to edit it; the field should enter edit mode
3. Press a new key combination; it should be captured and displayed
4. Save/close Preferences and verify the new shortcut takes effect
5. Restart the app and confirm the binding persists

Closes #14237

Summary
- Introduces centralized LayoutFormatterPreferences and enables export filters to provide bundled name formatters.

Key changes
- New LayoutFormatterPreferences class
  - Encapsulates NameFormatterPreferences, JournalAbbreviationPreferences, FileLinkPreferences and a JournalAbbreviationLoader.
  - Stores custom export name formatters (put/get/clear) so formatters provided with an export filter can be registered and looked up during export.

- ExportFormat
  - Reads an optional formatter file named <lfFileName>.formatters (readFormatterFile) before exporting and registers any custom name formatters with the supplied layoutPreferences.
  - Clears custom export name formatters after the export to avoid leaking state across exports.
  - Uses LayoutFormatterPreferences when creating LayoutHelper for the begin/layout/end templates so layout formatters have access to preferences and custom formatters.
  - Adds finalizeSaveSession that flushes/closes the writer, logs encoding issues and commits the save session.
  - Minor robustness: skip export when entries list is empty, fallback handling for encoding and save session creation.

- LayoutEntry
  - Improved formatter resolution and mapping in getLayoutFormatterByName (many formatter classes supported, backward compatibility name cases maintained).
  - getOptionalLayout now consults LayoutFormatterPreferences for custom export name formatters and falls back to user-defined name formatters.
  - Option field handling updated: when option text starts with a backslash it resolves the referenced field instead of treating it solely as literal text (allowing both resolved fields and raw text to be used).
  - Begin/end layout support extended: encoding token returns encoding.displayName(), filename/filepath tokens return database file name/path.
  - Keeps track of invalid formatters and logs them when applicable.
  - Contains parsing utilities (parseMethodsCalls) used to parse formatter method calls and parameters.

Behavioral impact
- Export filters can now ship a .formatters file alongside their layout templates to define custom name formatters local to that filter.
- Begin/end layouts can use encoding, filename and filepath tokens.
- Custom name formatters are scoped to the export and cleaned up afterward.
- Missing/invalid formatters are collected and logged to help troubleshooting.

Notes for integrators
- ExportFormat constructors already support passing LayoutFormatterPreferences and SavePreferences; ensure exporters provide proper LayoutFormatterPreferences (use LayoutFormatterPreferences.fromPreferences(...) to create one from JabRef preferences).
- This change keeps backward compatibility for many formatter names and also adds support for additional formatters.

Summary

Adds a new "Jstor Fetcher" component to fetch metadata and full-text (when available) from JSTOR for ingestion into our pipeline.

What I changed

- New module: jstor_fetcher/ - core logic to call JSTOR endpoints, handle pagination, retries, rate limiting, and basic normalization to our internal record schema.
- CLI: bin/jstor-fetch - simple command-line tool to run one-off fetches or backfills.
- Config: reads JSTOR_API_KEY, JSTOR_BASE_URL (optional), FETCH_BATCH_SIZE, and RATE_LIMIT from environment variables.
- Tests: unit tests for request/response parsing and retry logic; integration tests using mocked HTTP responses.
- Documentation: README section describing configuration, usage, and examples.

Why

We need an automated, reliable way to ingest JSTOR content into our system. This implemention centralizes JSTOR-related fetching code, enforces consistent rate limiting/retries, and returns normalized records ready for indexing.

How to use

1. Set environment variables (example):
   - JSTOR_API_KEY=your_api_key_here
   - FETCH_BATCH_SIZE=50
   - RATE_LIMIT=5

2. Run a one-time fetch (example):
   - ./bin/jstor-fetch --query "topic:education" --limit 200

3. Use the module programmatically:
   - from jstor_fetcher.client import JstorClient
   - client = JstorClient(api_key=os.environ['JSTOR_API_KEY'])
   - records = client.fetch(query, limit=100)

Testing

- Run unit tests: pytest tests/unit
- Run integration tests (mocked): pytest tests/integration

Backward compatibility and notes

- Non-breaking: the feature is opt-in and requires an API key; nothing changes unless the new CLI or module is invoked.
- Implemented robust error handling: exponential backoff, idempotent retries, and basic caching for repeated fetches.
- Known limitations / TODOs: support for additional export formats (e.g. RIS), richer metadata mappings, and an optional persistent cache layer.

Files of interest

- jstor_fetcher/client.py
- jstor_fetcher/utils.py
- bin/jstor-fetch
- tests/unit/test_client.py
- tests/integration/test_endpoints.py
- docs/JSTOR_FETCHER.md

If you want, I can split the client into smaller components or add a scheduler integration in a follow-up PR.

text:
Add BackupManager for automatic backup handling and comprehensive unit tests

- Introduces BackupManager: manages scheduled autosave backups for a BibDatabaseContext.
  - Schedules periodic backup attempts using a ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor.
  - Maintains a queue of backup files (max 10) and deletes the oldest when exceeding the limit.
  - Creates backups atomically (AtomicFileWriter) to avoid corrupted files on partial writes.
  - Determines backup file locations via BackupFileUtil and supports restoring the latest backup.
  - Uses a CoarseChangeFilter to mark when a backup is needed and avoids redundant backups.
  - Implements backupFileDiffers(Path) to determine whether the latest backup differs from the original file; compares modification timestamps and uses Files.mismatch, returning conservative results on I/O errors.
  - Suppresses logging of InvalidFieldValueException (field value errors) during autosave to avoid noisy logs.

- Adds BackupManagerTest with tests validating:
  - Backup file name/path generation in the app data directory.
  - backupFileDiffers behavior when no backup exists, when backup equals original, and when backup differs.
  - Correct choice of the most recent backup file among multiple .bak files with different timestamps.
  - Timestamp handling: newer backup leads to detection of differences; older backup is ignored.

This change provides a robust autosave backup mechanism and verifies its behavior across multiple edge cases via unit tests.

- Add screenshots demonstrating the preference and results for the UI change.
- Update documentation / help pages if needed and run localization update when localization changes are made.

Introduce CLI customization for citation key generation in JabKit

- Add a new parent command citationkeys and make the previous generate-citation-keys command a subcommand: jabkit citationkeys generate. The old standalone command generate-citation-keys has been removed. (See CHANGELOG entries for #14361 and #14500.)

- Expose runtime overrides for citation key preferences via new CLI options on the generate subcommand, allowing users to customize generation without changing GUI preferences. New options include:
  --pattern, --transliterate, --warn-before-overwrite, --suffix, --regex, --regex-replacement, --unwanted, --keyword-delimiter, --avoid-overwrite, --generate-before-saving

- Implement getCitationKeyGenerator(...) to construct a CitationKeyPatternPreferences instance that merges provided CLI overrides with existing CLI preferences, and use it when generating keys.

- Wire parent/child commands correctly so the generate command reads preferences and managers from the command hierarchy and uses them for importing, saving and output.

Why this change
- Enables non-GUI workflows and scripting by letting users control citation key generation behavior from the command line.

Compatibility notes
- The standalone command generate-citation-keys was removed; use jabkit citationkeys generate instead. Default behavior remains unchanged when no override options are provided (existing preferences are used).

Add JSTOR fetcher and tests

What I changed
- Added a new fetcher: org.jabref.logic.importer.fetcher.JstorFetcher
  - Implements SearchBasedParserFetcher and FulltextFetcher.
  - Builds search URLs against https://www.jstor.org/open/search and query-to-parameter mapping for complex queries (authors -> au:, titles -> ti:, journal -> pt:, year -> sd/ed).
  - Parser scrapes "cite-this-item" elements, requests the citation text endpoint (https://www.jstor.org/citation/text...), concatenates the returned BibTeX and uses BibtexParser to produce entries.
  - findFullText reads the entry URL page, looks for an element with a data-doi attribute, and returns the linked PDF URL. Returns empty when URL field is missing or the page does not contain exactly one matching element.
  - Returns TrustLevel.META_SEARCH.
- Registered the new JstorFetcher in WebFetchers.getSearchBasedFetchers(...) and WebFetchers.getFullTextFetchers(...).
- Added unit tests: src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/JstorFetcherTest.java
  - Tests searchByTitle and fetchPDF behavior using a sample BibEntry.
  - Some year-based tests are disabled because JSTOR does not support search-only-by-year.
- Documentation/metadata
  - CHANGELOG.md updated: added a note about the new JSTOR fetcher.
  - AUTHORS updated: added "Johannes Theiner".

Notes & limitations
- The parser relies on HTML structure and the citation/text endpoint; changes on JSTOR may break extraction.
- findFullText requires the entry to contain a URL and expects exactly one element with a data-doi attribute to locate the fulltext link.
- Tests use mocked ImportFormatPreferences and are annotated as Fetcher tests.

Files added/modified (high level)
- Added: src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/JstorFetcher.java
- Added: src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/JstorFetcherTest.java
- Modified: src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/WebFetchers.java (registered fetcher)
- Modified: CHANGELOG.md (added entry)
- Modified: AUTHORS (added contributor)

This change introduces JSTOR search and fulltext resolution support into JabRef as a meta-search fetcher.

- Added comprehensive tests to cover normal moves, moved-and-renamed cases, missing targets, and permission/edge-case scenarios.

Why: This fixes issues where moving a file would break links or leave stale references. The new behavior makes the system more resilient to user file moves.

Testing:
- Run the test suite to execute the new unit tests.
- Manual test: move a tracked file to a new path (or rename it) and verify the system updates references and continues to operate with the new path.

Compatibility: No breaking API changes. The relink method is internal and should be safe to deploy; it only activates when the file move is detected.

Add ScholarArchive fetcher and query transformer

What I changed
- Introduce ScholarArchiveFetcher: a PagedSearchBasedParserFetcher implementation that queries https://scholar.archive.org/search?format=json, sets Accept: application/json, handles pagination (from, size), and parses the JSON response into BibEntry objects. The parser maps fields including title, authors (from contrib_names), journal/container_name, doi, issue, language, publisher, year, volume, abstract, url (from fulltext.access_url), date, issn and sets an appropriate entry type (InCollection by default, Book or Article when inferred).
- Add ScholarArchiveQueryTransformer: transforms Lucene queries into the Scholar Archive query format (contrib_names for author, container_name for journal, publication.startDate for year and year ranges, and logical operators).
- Register the new fetcher in WebFetchers so it is available with the other search-based fetchers.
- Add unit tests: ScholarArchiveFetcherTest to validate getName and basic search behavior. Update ManageStudyDefinitionViewModelTest to include ScholarArchive in the catalog list and refactor a helper to avoid duplicated setup.
- Update CHANGELOG to announce the new fetcher (issue #10498).

Why
- Provide an additional source for metadata retrieval via scholar.archive.org to improve coverage for searches and imports.

Notes and implementation details
- The fetcher uses URIBuilder to build the request URL with q, from, size and format parameters.
- The JSON parsing is defensive: ParseException is thrown if the expected JSON structure changes.
- Year handling in the transformer supports exact years and ranges, mapping them to publication.startDate queries.
- Tests were added/updated to include the new source in the UI test expectations and to exercise the fetcher code.

Summary
- Removed the PreferencesService field and constructor parameter from ClipBoardManager.
- ClipBoardManager now has a no-arg constructor and a constructor that accepts only Clipboard, primary Clipboard and ImportFormatReader.
- All internal uses of preferencesService were replaced with Globals.prefs (e.g. getFieldWriterPreferences(), getImportFormatPreferences()).
- Globals now constructs the ClipBoardManager with the no-arg constructor and includes a small javadoc note indicating the manager can be injected (@Inject) if desired.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/ClipBoardManager.java
  - Deleted the preferencesService field and removed it from constructors.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/Globals.java
  - Instantiate clipboardManager using the new no-arg constructor and added a comment about DI/injection.

Rationale
- Decouples ClipBoardManager from directly holding a PreferencesService instance and centralizes preference access through Globals.prefs.
- Makes ClipBoardManager easier to construct without passing PreferencesService everywhere and signals that it can be injected by DI frameworks.

Potential impacts / notes
- Globals.prefs must be initialized before using ClipBoardManager since the class now relies on Globals.prefs at runtime.
- Behaviour should remain the same provided Globals.prefs is available; no functional changes to clipboard parsing/writing are intended.
- If any code constructed ClipBoardManager by passing a PreferencesService previously, it should be updated to the new constructors or rely on injection.

No changes to public API beyond constructor signatures of ClipBoardManager and the Globals clipboardManager instantiation.

Summary
- Implement fuzzy matching for journal abbreviations using Levenshtein distance and normalize inputs for comparisons.

What changed
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/journals/Abbreviation.java
  - Added Levenshtein-based fuzzy matching (LEVENSHTEIN) and an isSimilar(String) helper that normalizes strings (lowercase, strip non-alphanumeric except spaces) and returns true when distance <= 2.
  - Added normalize(...) helper and updated equals(...) to compare normalized name, abbreviation, and shortestUniqueAbbreviation via Objects.equals.
  - Updated compareTo(...) to treat names/abbreviations as equal when they are similar (fuzzy match) before falling back to lexical comparison.
  - Added @Serial annotation and serialVersionUID; included necessary imports.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/journals/JournalAbbreviationRepository.java
  - Trim input in getNextAbbreviation(text) to avoid whitespace affecting lookup.

- src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/journals/AbbreviationTest.java
  - Added multiple unit tests covering fuzzy matching behavior (slight differences, missing letters, punctuation, case differences) and compareTo behavior with fuzzy matching.
  - Added necessary assertTrue import.

- Removed editor configuration files under .vscode
  - Deleted .vscode/extensions.json, .vscode/ltex.dictionary.en-US.txt, and .vscode/settings.json (cleanup of workspace-specific settings).

Rationale
- Fuzzy matching improves robustness when abbreviations or journal names contain small typos, punctuation differences, or case variations, allowing better equality and ordering behavior across slightly different inputs.
- Normalization ensures comparisons ignore irrelevant differences (punctuation/casing).
- Trimming lookup input prevents lookup failures caused by surrounding whitespace.
- New tests ensure the fuzzy matching and comparison logic behave as expected.

Notes
- The fuzzy threshold is currently set to Levenshtein distance <= 2. This can be tuned later if required.
- Ensure the Apache Commons Text dependency (for LevenshteinDistance) is available in the project classpath.

Fixes #3389 — Skip invalid prolog content when loading CitationStyles

Summary
- When a citation style file contained invalid characters or garbage before the XML prolog (for example a BOM or stray text), parsing threw an exception and prevented the preferences dialog from opening. This PR strips any invalid leading content up to the first '<' before parsing the style XML, preventing that exception.

What I changed
- Added a private helper method stripInvalidProlog(String) in CitationStyle that finds the first '<' and returns the substring from there (or the original string if none found).
- Use stripInvalidProlog(source) when creating the InputSource for XML parsing in createCitationStyleFromSource(...).
- Small reordering of the null/empty checks in createCitationStyleFromSource (no behavioral change beyond readability).
- Added a brief note to CHANGELOG.md mentioning the bugfix.

Behavior
- If the style source contains leading invalid characters before the XML root, these are skipped and parsing continues normally.
- If there is no '<' in the source, the original source is returned (parsing will proceed and fail as before if the XML is invalid).

Testing
- Manually tested in a running JabRef instance. The preferences dialog no longer fails to open when encountering styles with invalid prolog content.
- No automated tests added in this PR — recommended to add unit tests for stripInvalidProlog and for parsing edge cases in a follow-up.

Notes
- This is intended as a defensive measure to tolerate minor corruption or stray bytes before the XML prolog in citation style files. It does not attempt to repair otherwise invalid XML beyond skipping leading noise.

Fixes #8108

Summary
- Allow showing a preview for styles listed in the "Available" list in Preferences -> Preview (previously preview was shown only for the chosen/selected styles).
- Add a search/filter box for the Available styles so users can quickly find a style by name.

What I changed
- UI (PreviewTab.fxml): added a CustomTextField search box with padding and prompt text.
- Controller (PreviewTab.java): wired the search box, added a search icon, bound available list view to the view model's filtered list, and updated visibility bindings so the preview viewer and the source editor are shown when either an available or a chosen style is selected. - ViewModel (PreviewTabViewModel.java): introduced a FilteredList wrapping the available previews, exposed getFilteredPreviews() and a setFilterPredicate(searchTerm) method to update filtering, and simplified some initialization. Made restartWarning immutable.

- Preview preferences (PreviewPreferences.java): tightened getCurrentPreviewStyle to avoid out-of-bounds when there are no previewCycle entries and fixed creation of the TextBasedPreviewLayout to use the stored previewStyle.
- CHANGELOG.md: documented the new behavior and the search option in the preferences.

Behavioral notes
- Selecting an item in the Available list now triggers the preview viewer and shows the source text editor (same behavior as selecting items in Chosen).
- The search box filters Available styles case-insensitively by display name.

Testing and other notes
- Manually tested in a running JabRef instance. Screenshot included in the PR description.
- No automated tests added in this change.

text: This PR significantly improves the performance and memory usage of the journal abbreviation loader/repository/parser (partial fix for #2966). Loading and parsing that previously took nearly 10 seconds is now almost instantaneous. Update build configuration and tooling for the project

This PR standardizes and improves the Gradle build script (build.gradle) by configuring plugins, toolchains, dependencies, code generation tasks, testing, packaging and quality tooling. Key changes and highlights:

- Plugins and Java toolchain
  - Apply application, modernizer, JMH, Java modularity, JavaFX, jlink, test logger, jacoco, checkstyle, rewrite and other helper plugins.
  - Use Java source/target compatibility 19 and a toolchain language version of 20.
  - Disable modularity inferModulePath workaround and JavaFX effective arguments adjustment as noted.

- Source sets and code generation
  - Add generated sources folder src-gen/main/java alongside src/main/java.
  - Add XJC and ANTLR code generation tasks: generateBstGrammarSource, generateSearchGrammarSource, generateCitaviSource, generateJournalAbbreviationList and aggregate generateSource task.
  - Compile task depends on generateSource and writes generated sources to the configured directory.

- Dependencies and repositories
  - Configure mavenLocal, mavenCentral, Sonatype, jitpack and custom repo.
  - Lock dependencies via dependencyLocking.lockAllConfigurations().
  - Add and pin numerous dependencies: PDFBox, Lucene, Commons CSV/Lang, H2 MVStore, BouncyCastle, ANTLR, JGit, Jackson, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, Oracle JDBC, Guava (with jsr305 excluded), Jakarta APIs, JavaFX related libs, mvvmfx, controlsfx, jsoup, unirest, tinylog, SLF4J bridge, citeproc, jaxb, latex2unicode, application insights, flexmark, appdirs, jool, Jersey and related HTTP/JSON libs, test deps (JUnit 5, Mockito, TestFX, ArchUnit, ClassGraph), and plugin-specific dependencies for xjc.

- Module options and runtime access
  - Configure addExports and addOpens for JavaFX and ControlsFX to support required internal access (temporary workarounds noted with TODOs).
  - Adjust run and javadoc module options similarly.

- Testing and code coverage
  - Configure test task to use JUnit Platform, exclude GUI/Database/Fetcher tags by default and collect Jacoco reports across multiple test tasks.
  - Add specialized Test tasks: databaseTest, fetcherTest and guiTest with isolated tag inclusion and logging settings.
  - Add jacocoPrepare task to allow ignoring test failures when preparing coverage.

- Packaging and native images
  - Configure jlink with stripping/compression, forceMerge for known problematic modules and a mergedModule stanza to fix module info issues.
  - Configure jpackage for Windows, Linux and macOS with platform-specific installer options, icons, file associations and resource copying. Skip macOS installers on local builds to support pipeline notarization.

- Code quality and rewrite
  - Configure rewrite plugin with active recipes and exclusions, and set failOnDryRunResults = true.
  - Configure modernizer with tests included and one exclusion.
  - Checkstyle configured (only runs explicitly).

- Convenience tasks
  - downloadDependencies task to pre-resolve most dependencies.
  - Clean task extended to remove generated folders.

Notes
- Several workarounds and TODO comments remain where upstream fixes are expected, e.g., module exports/opens, forceMerge entries, and dependency exclusions.
- Environment variables are used to populate build.properties during processResources for API keys and instrumentation keys.

text:
Refactor layout formatting: introduce and use LayoutFormatterPreferences

This PR refactors the way layout formatting options are handled across the exporter/layout code by encapsulating formatter settings in a dedicated LayoutFormatterPreferences class and wiring it into the layout pipeline.

Summary of changes
- Add LayoutFormatterPreferences to encapsulate formatting preferences used by layout formatters.
- Update LayoutEntry to accept and use LayoutFormatterPreferences instead of relying on implicit/global configuration. This simplifies LayoutEntry responsibilities and improves testability.
- Update ExportFormat to provide the LayoutFormatterPreferences when constructing/using layout entries during export.

Why
- Centralizes layout formatter configuration in a single, typed object.
- Decouples formatting behavior from LayoutEntry, making the code easier to test and to change formatting behavior at runtime.
- Prepares the codebase for future additions of configurable formatting options without spreading preference access throughout the code.

Compatibility / Migration
- Functionality should remain unchanged for end users; this is a refactor to improve code structure and configurability.
- Call sites that previously constructed LayoutEntry directly may need to supply a LayoutFormatterPreferences instance (or use existing factories that do so).

No behavioral changes to formatting are intended by this PR; it is focused on refactoring and improving separation of concerns.

- New unit tests cover verbatim fields containing ampersands.
- All existing validator tests were run and adjustments made only where tests incorrectly assumed ampersands should be rejected inside verbatim fields.

Summary

Store sensitive credentials (proxy password and API keys) in the native OS credential store instead of plaintext configuration files.

What this PR does

- Saves proxy passwords and API keys to the platform-native credential store: Windows Credential Manager, macOS Keychain, and Linux Secret Service / libsecret where available.
- Removes persistent storage of these secrets in plain config files; when credentials are migrated the file-stored secrets are removed/cleared.
- Adds a migration path that moves existing secrets from config files into the OS store on first run (with user confirmation where applicable).
- Keeps existing environment variable and CLI flag overrides functioning (these still take precedence but are ephemeral and not persisted).
- Provides a fallback behavior: if no supported credential store is available, the app falls back to the previous behavior but logs a clear security warning and prompts the user to opt into a local encrypted store or provide credentials each session.
- Adds configuration options to opt out of using the OS credential store or to force migration.

Why this change

- Improve security by leveraging OS-managed, encrypted credential stores rather than storing secrets in configuration files.
- Reduce risk of accidental secret leakage from source control, backups, or misconfigured file permissions.

User-visible changes

- On first run after upgrade, users who previously had saved proxy passwords or API keys will be prompted (or automatically migrated per settings) to move those secrets into the OS credential store.
- Documentation updated with instructions for supported platforms, how to opt out, and how to remove credentials from the OS store.

Implementation notes

- Introduces a thin abstraction layer over credential stores to keep code portable and testable.
- Adds unit and integration tests for the credential-store behavior and migration logic.
- Adds logging for migration steps and for the fallback path when no store is available.

Security considerations

- No secrets are transmitted off-device during migration; all moves are local to the user's machine.
- The app no longer leaves long-lived secrets in configuration files after migration.

Files changed / highlights

- credential_store/* (new) – implementation of OS-specific stores and common interface
- config/migration.go – migration logic for moving file-stored secrets into the credential store
- cli/flags.go – new flags for opting out/forcing usage of the OS store
- docs/security.md – documentation describing new behavior and platform support
- tests/* – tests for storage and migration behavior

Please review:
- Platform-specific credential handling (Windows/macOS/Linux)
- Migration UX and prompts
- Logging and error messages for fallback scenarios

Summary

- Implemented relinking logic so that files are automatically relinked to entries when a user moves the file (first implementation of the behavior described in issue #9798).
- Added unit tests (6) covering move and copy scenarios.
- Updated CHANGELOG to reflect the improvement.

What I changed

1) src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/externalfiles/AutoSetFileLinksUtil.java
- Added a new private method relinkFileIfMoved(List<LinkedFile> newLinkedFiles, BibEntry entry).
- The method detects the common case where an entry previously had two file references (old and new) and only one new linked file is discovered. If the old referenced path no longer exists in the configured file directories, the method replaces the entry's FILE field with the new path.
- Invokes relinkFileIfMoved during linkAssociatedFiles processing.
- Added a few imports required by the implementation.

2) src/test/java/org/jabref/gui/externalfiles/AutoSetFileLinksUtilTest.java
- Added 6 new tests that exercise relinking vs. copying behavior:
  - relinkMoveFileFromRootFolderToSubfolder
  - relinkMoveFileFromSubfolderToRootFolder
  - relinkMoveFileFromSubfolderToSubfolder
  - noRelinkCopyFileFromRootFolderToSubfolder
  - noRelinkCopyFileFromSubfolderToRootFolder
  - noRelinkCopyFileFromSubfolderToSubfolder
- The tests set up temporary directories, create/move/copy files and assert that the entry file links are updated or preserved as expected.

3) CHANGELOG.md
- Added an entry under "Added" describing the improvement to automatically set file links so files moved by the user are relinked. (Refs #9798)

Motivation and behavior

This implements the "Automatically set file links" improvement so that when a file previously linked to an entry is moved within the project directories, JabRef will relink the entry to the file at its new location (instead of keeping a broken link or creating duplicate links). The code implements the first, straightforward approach described in the original issue and covers move vs copy semantics via unit tests.

Notes

- Tests cover both move (relink) and copy (do not relink; both links should exist) scenarios.
- This PR implements the first approach and is ready for review; feedback and suggestions are welcome.

Fixes: #9798

- Added unit tests for sample inputs including: arXiv:2101.01234v2, 2101.01234, hep-th/9901001, and filename-based ids like 2101.01234.pdf.
- Updated integration tests to exercise import paths and confirm external_id/arXiv fields are set as expected.

Migration/Compatibility: No database migrations required. Behavior is backward compatible; existing records are unchanged.

Implements a full “Reset to defaults” flow for MainTablePreferences so users can restore column, sort, filter and paging preferences back to the application defaults.

What I changed:
- Added a reset() method to MainTablePreferences that clears persisted preferences and re-applies the default configuration.
- Wired up a Reset control in the MainTable preferences UI (with confirmation) that calls the new reset() flow.
- Ensured the main table listens for preference changes and re-renders immediately after a reset.
- Persisted state is updated so resetting updates storage (and subsequent app reloads will use defaults).
- Added unit tests and an integration test to cover the reset behavior and the persistence interactions.

Why:
Users needed a safe and reliable way to revert any table customizations back to the original defaults. This change centralizes the logic in MainTablePreferences and ensures UI and persisted state remain consistent.

How to test:
1. Open the main table preferences and change columns, sort order, filters or page size.
2. Click the Reset button and confirm in the dialog.
3. Verify the table immediately shows the default columns/order/sort/filters/page size.
4. Refresh the page/app and verify defaults are still in effect (persisted storage was updated).
5. Run unit/integration tests: verify new tests pass.

Backward compatibility / notes:
- Existing stored preferences will be cleared/overwritten by the reset action; this is expected behavior.
- No public API breaking changes introduced; reset() is additive and safe for callers to use.

Files changed (high level):
- MainTablePreferences (logic): added reset() and storage handling
- Preferences UI: added Reset button + confirmation
- MainTable component: update listener to respond to preference resets
- Tests: unit + integration coverage for reset flow

If you want a different confirmation text or analytics tracking for resets, I can add that in a follow-up.

Introduce ColumnPreferences and MainTablePreferences to encapsulate main table column configuration and integrate them into the GUI preferences system.

Summary of changes:
- Add ColumnPreferences to hold ObservableLists of MainTableColumnModel for columns and columnSortOrder, with default column layout and width constants (DEFAULT_COLUMN_WIDTH, ICON_COLUMN_WIDTH).
- Add MainTablePreferences to wrap ColumnPreferences plus BooleanProperties for auto-resize and extra file columns, with defaults and property accessors.
- Integrate main table and search-dialog column persistence into JabRefGuiPreferences:
  - Load/restore ColumnPreferences and MainTablePreferences from the backing store with sensible defaults and fallbacks.
  - Store changes reactively: listeners on columns and sort order write COLUMN_NAMES, COLUMN_WIDTHS, COLUMN_SORT_TYPES and COLUMN_SORT_ORDER (and equivalents for the search dialog) to preferences.
  - Provide parsing utilities getColumns(...) and getColumnSortOrder(...) to reconstruct MainTableColumnModel lists from stored string lists, with robust parsing of widths and sort types and logging on parse errors.
  - Provide conversion helpers to serialize ColumnPreferences to lists of strings (names, widths, sort types, sort order).
- Ensure clear() and importPreferences(...) correctly reset and restore main table preferences and column preferences.
- Use main table column sort order when building a SelfContainedSaveOrder for export configuration.

Other notes:
- Various default and migration-related preference keys are used to preserve backwards compatibility.
- Error handling/logging added for malformed stored column widths and invalid side pane positions when restoring preferences.

text:
Fix handling of UTF BOM at start of file

What changed:
- Strip leading UTF-8 BOM (and other common BOM sequences) from the beginning of input before performing line.startsWith checks and other parsing logic.

Why:
- Lines starting with '%' (and similar checks) failed when files contained a BOM because the BOM placed additional invisible characters ahead of the first visible character, making the '%' appear at index 1 instead of 0. Java reads the BOM into the string, so explicit removal is required before parsing.

Impact:
- Ensures files beginning with a BOM are parsed correctly; prevents missed metadata/comments detection due to BOMs.

Notes:
- Fixes #9926.

Notes

Summary:

Summary:
Enable passing parameters to the CLI so commands can accept and forward named and positional parameters. This change adds support for parameter parsing, validation, and wiring into existing CLI commands.

What changed:
- Added CLI parameter parsing and validation logic.
- Introduced new flags/options for commands to accept parameters (named and positional).
- Updated command dispatch to forward parameters to underlying handlers.
- Added unit and integration tests covering parameter parsing and command execution with parameters.
- Updated CLI help text and documentation to show usage examples for parameters.

Why:
Some workflows require dynamic input to the CLI commands. Enabling parameters makes the CLI more flexible and scriptable, allowing callers to pass configuration and runtime values without modifying code.

Usage examples:
- Named parameter: mycli run --param "key=value" or mycli run --param key=value
- Positional parameter: mycli run value1 value2
- Multiple params: mycli run --param a=1 --param b=2

Compatibility:
- Default behavior remains unchanged if no parameters are provided.
- Existing commands continue to work; new parameter options are additive.

Testing:
- Unit tests added for the parameter parser and validation.
- Integration tests added to verify end-to-end command execution with parameters.
- Manual QA: verify help output, single/multiple params, invalid param formats, and backward compatibility.

Notes for reviewers:
- Pay attention to the parser behavior for edge cases (empty values, repeated keys).
- Look at help text changes to ensure clarity and consistency.
- Confirm validation rules are sensible for our use cases; adjust error messages if needed.

This PR implements feature/14361: enable parameters for CLI.

text:
Improve SourceTab editor and add CodeArea key bindings

This PR enhances the BibTeX/source editor experience in the entry editor by adding explicit key-binding handling, search highlighting, IME support, parsing/validation on focus loss and save, and undoable updates to entries.

Key changes
- Add CodeAreaKeyBindings: centralized handling of editor-related key bindings (navigation, deletion, word operations, case transformations, kill-line/word, etc.). These bindings are mapped using the existing KeyBindingRepository and operate on the RichTextFX CodeArea.
- Wire key bindings into SourceTab: SourceTab now installs the CodeAreaKeyBindings handler and maps save-related key bindings to persist the edited source.
- Persist and validate source on focus-loss and save: when leaving the source editor (or invoking a save binding) the editor content is parsed and applied to the current BibEntry. Changes are applied as an undoable NamedCompound (field changes + type change + citation key) and invalid inputs/warnings are surfaced to the user via validation/dialog.
- Input method workaround: add InputMethodRequestsObject and input-method handling to improve IME behavior with RichTextFX CodeArea (workaround for known RichTextFX issue).
- Search highlighting: SourceTab listens to the StateManager active search query and highlights occurrences in the source editor.
- Various editor setup improvements: wrap text, context menu (cut/copy/paste/select all) keyed to KeyBindingRepository, and validator wiring.

Files changed
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/entryeditor/SourceTab.java: integrate CodeArea key bindings, IME workaround, focus/save handling, parsing & validation, search highlight hookup.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/keyboard/CodeAreaKeyBindings.java: new helper for mapping KeyBindingRepository bindings to CodeArea operations.
- CHANGELOG.md: documented under Unreleased (summary of user-facing changes).

Why this change
- Makes the source tab behave more like a normal text editor with familiar keybindings and IME support
- Ensures that manual edits to BibTeX source are validated and applied safely with undo support
- Improves discoverability/consistency by using the shared KeyBindingRepository

Notes
- Parsing errors and warnings are shown to the user; invalid edits are not silently lost.
- The implementation reuses existing import/parse logic (BibtexParser) and FieldWriter validation to ensure field values are legal before applying changes.

text:
Fix for #8788 — JabRef not showing contents of shared database library

Summary:
This PR fixes a bug where opening a shared database/library could result in an empty view even though entries existed in the remote/shared source. The root cause was that the shared library contents were not being loaded into the local model and the UI table was not refreshed after the shared connection synchronized.

What I changed:
- Ensure shared database contents are loaded into the local BibDatabase when a shared library is opened or synchronized.
- Trigger the model and table view refresh after synchronization completes so entries become visible immediately.
- Add defensive checks around the shared-library load path to avoid NPEs and race conditions when synchronization happens on a background thread.
- Small refactor of the shared-database sync flow to make the update/refresh sequence explicit and testable.
- Added unit/integration tests that verify entries from a shared library are present in the local model and visible in the UI after opening/sync.

How to test:
1. Create or use an existing shared database and ensure it contains at least one entry.
2. Open the shared database in JabRef.
3. Verify that the entries are displayed in the main table immediately after the library opens and after a sync.
4. Add/remove an entry on one client and verify changes propagate and the view updates on the other client.

Notes:
- This change closes #8788.
- Backwards compatible: users' existing libraries and workflows are unaffected; this simply ensures shared library contents are loaded and shown reliably.

Problem
The resolver assumed incoming URIs were absolute and attempted operations that only work on absolute URIs, causing IllegalArgumentException for relative or file paths.

What I changed
- Added defensive handling for non-absolute URIs: if a base URI is provided, relative URIs are resolved against it; otherwise relative paths are converted to absolute file: URIs before further processing.
- Added validation so an IllegalArgumentException is only thrown for truly invalid inputs, with a clearer error message.
- Added unit tests covering relative URIs, file paths, and invalid input cases.

Impact
- Fixes crashes when callers pass relative URIs or file paths. Behavior is backwards-compatible for existing absolute URIs; relative URIs are now resolved instead of causing exceptions.
- No public API changes. CI tests updated and passing.
