Closes #12810

Summary

This PR fixes a bug in KeywordList where delimiter characters (commas, pipes, etc.) inside a keyword were always treated as separators, even when they were escaped with a backslash. As a result strings like "AI\, ML" were previously split into two keywords instead of remaining a single keyword.

What I changed

- Implemented escaping-aware tokenization in KeywordList.parse by adding getKeywordsAsStrings. The parser now treats a backslash as an escape character so that the next character (including the delimiter or a backslash) is taken literally.
- Updated KeywordList.serialize to escape backslashes and delimiter characters when producing a keyword string (so serialization round-trips correctly).
- Added a unit test (parseKeywordListContainingSingleBackslashBeforeComma_ShouldTreatBackslashLiterally) verifying that an escaped comma inside a keyword yields a single Keyword with a comma in its value.
- Updated CHANGELOG.md with an entry explaining the fix.

Files modified

- src/main/java/org/jabref/model/entry/KeywordList.java — add escape-aware parsing and safer serialization
- src/test/java/org/jabref/model/entry/KeywordListTest.java — add tests for escaped delimiters
- CHANGELOG.md — user-facing note about the fix

Behavior notes

- Backslash (\) is used as the escape character. Example: "AI\\, ML" (in source) will be parsed as a single keyword with the value "AI, ML".
- Existing behavior is preserved for unescaped delimiters (they still separate keywords).
- Serialization now ensures backslashes and delimiter chars inside keywords are escaped so that parsing the serialized output returns the original keywords.

Tests

- Added unit test covering an escaped comma case and kept existing tests intact.

This change ensures keywords containing delimiter characters can be represented and round-tripped safely.

text:
Add automatic file-linking feature

This PR implements an "Autolink files" feature that searches the library file directories for files associated with selected entries and automatically adds LinkedFile references to those entries. The main changes are:

- New AutoSetFileLinksUtil class
  - Encapsulates the logic to find files matching entries using FileFinders and configured external file types.
  - Builds a LinkFilesResult containing changed entries and any IO exceptions encountered.
  - Creates LinkedFile objects with relative paths and guessed file types (falls back to UnknownExternalFileType).
  - Applies entry modifications on the JavaFX thread and records UndoableFieldChange edits in a NamedCompound for undo support.
  - Provides a public findAssociatedNotLinkedFiles(...) method to locate files without linking them.

- New AutoLinkFilesAction class
  - UI action bound to the presence of an open database and selected entries.
  - Constructs AutoSetFileLinksUtil with preferences and executes linking in a background Task.
  - Shows a progress dialog while searching and updates the UI when finished.
  - Handles results: notifies user of completion, records undo edits when there are changes, and shows warnings when no files found or when file exceptions occurred.
  - Uses the TaskExecutor to run the task and DialogService for progress/dialogs.

- Localization updates (JabRef_en.properties)
  - Add strings used by the new feature (e.g. "Automatically set file links", "Finished automatically setting external links.", "Problem finding files. See error log for details.", "No files found.").

Integration details
- The action is registered in the Quality menu (already wired in the frame) and will only be enabled when a database is open and entries are selected.
- The auto-linking respects configured AutoLinkPreferences, FilePreferences (directories), and the currently configured ExternalFileTypes.
- All filesystem comparisons use Files.isSameFile to avoid duplicate linking and paths are relativized against the library directories.

Error handling & robustness
- IOExceptions encountered while searching are collected and reported via the DialogService.
- Type detection gracefully falls back to UnknownExternalFileType if the extension is not recognized.
- Updates to entries are executed on the JavaFX thread to remain UI-safe.

This change provides a user-friendly, undoable, and background-executed way to automatically attach external files (PDFs, etc.) to entries based on filename heuristics and preferences.

Summary:
- Add a new "Send to Kindle" feature that lets users send articles/books from the app directly to their Kindle device via the user’s Kindle email address.

What this PR does:
- UI: Adds a "Send to Kindle" button to the reader toolbar and a new input on the Account/Settings page for users to save their Kindle email address.
- Validation: Validates Kindle email format on the client and server, and provides helpful error messages in the UI.
- Conversion: Converts article content to a Kindle-compatible format (PDF/ePub/MOBI as appropriate) before sending.
- Delivery: Implements a backend delivery flow that composes the email with the converted attachment and sends it to the user’s Kindle address.
- Reliability: Uses a background job queue with retry logic and logs delivery attempts/failures.
- Configuration: Supports configurable email transport via environment variables (SMTP or SES config) and a configurable sender address.
- Tests & Docs: Adds unit tests for validation and conversion, integration tests for the delivery flow (mocked), and updates user-facing docs explaining how to enable and use the feature.

How to test locally:
1. Set a valid Kindle address in Account -> Settings.
2. Configure email transport env vars (SMTP_HOST/SMTP_PORT/SMTP_USER/SMTP_PASS or equivalent SES settings) and a sender address.
3. Open any article in the reader, click "Send to Kindle."
4. Verify the background job is queued and the delivery log shows success or failure. Check the Kindle inbox to confirm receipt.

Notes & considerations:
- Privacy: only the user’s Kindle address is stored; attachments are generated per request and not permanently archived.
- Rate limiting: the background job includes basic rate limiting to avoid sending large volumes in short timeframes.
- No breaking changes to existing APIs or UX.

Files/areas touched (high level):
- frontend: reader toolbar component, settings page, client-side validation
- backend: API endpoint /jobs/send-to-kindle, conversion service, email service, background worker, logs
- tests: unit and integration tests for validation, conversion, and delivery
- docs: user guide on adding Kindle address and troubleshooting delivery

Extend RIS import with additional tag mappings and custom fields

Summary
- Broaden RIS import support by mapping many additional RIS tags to JabRef/BibTeX fields and by storing several previously-unmapped tags into custom fields when no direct mapping exists.
- Add a missing FieldName constant for SHORTTITLE and small code cleanup in RisImporter (rename local BibEntry variable and consistently set month).
- Update tests and test resources to reflect the extended import behavior.
- Add changelog entry referencing the related issues.

Details
- Improved tag handling in RisImporter:
  - Journal/title tags: treat T2, J2, JA as fallback journal title and JO, J1, JF as definitive journal title.
  - Author/editor tags: accept multiple author tags (AU, A1, A2, A3, A4) and map ED to editor.
  - Page/number/address/url/year handling extended with additional RIS tags: IS, AN, C7, M1 -> number; AD, CY, PP -> address; UR, L2, LK -> url; include Y2 alongside Y1/PY/DA for year parsing.
  - DOI and related: M3 and DO are used to add DOI.
  - Additional mappings: C3 -> eventtitle; N1 and RN -> note; ST -> shorttitle; C2 -> eprint + eprinttype=pubmed; TA -> translator.
  - Several tags with no direct BibTeX mapping are stored as custom fields (string keys): archive_location (AV), call-number (CN/VO), archive (DB), number-of-volumes (NV), original-title (OP), reviewed-title (RI), status (RP), section (SE), refid (ID).
- Minor refactor: rename local variable b -> entry for clarity and use entry when adding to results.
- Added FieldName.SHORTTITLE constant.

Tests & resources
- Updated RisImporterTestFiles parameter list to include RisImporterTest7.
- Updated several expected .bib test resources to match the new import mappings (authors, booktitle, editor, month, number fields, etc.).
- Added new test RIS/expected pairs RisImporterTest7.ris / RisImporterTest7.bib and adjusted RisImporterTestDoiAndJournalTitle.ris to use ED tag for editor.

Changelog
- Added entry: "We fixed and extended the RIS import functionality to cover more fields." (references #3634 and #2607).

Notes
- This change expands RIS coverage and keeps previously unmapped information by storing it under custom keys when necessary. Manual testing and unit tests were updated accordingly.

Add integrated preview panel and robust layout handling to entry editor fields tab

Summary
- Integrates a PreviewPanel into the FieldsEditorTab and arranges the field editors and preview in a SplitPane alongside a ScrollPane.
- Lazily initializes the grid/preview container in initPanel to avoid unnecessary work in tests and reduce startup overhead.
- Implements regular and compressed grid layouts, using FieldEditorFX weights to compute row constraints for proportional space allocation.
- Adds a safety check to skip setup when Globals.prefs is not initialized (useful for unit tests).

Details
- previewPanel is now created in initPanel and setEntry(...) is called when binding an entry so the preview always reflects the active entry.
- The content is wrapped in a ScrollPane (no horizontal scrollbar, vertical as needed) and combined with the preview using a SplitPane.
- setRegularRowLayout computes percent heights for rows based on editor weights so larger editors get more vertical space.
- setCompressedRowLayout distributes rows evenly in compressed mode and supports two-column compressed layout with labels/editors arranged accordingly.
- Request focus and preview style navigation (next/previous) are delegated to the corresponding editor/preview components.

Why
- Improves the user experience by showing a live preview next to the field editors in the entry editor.
- Makes the layout more flexible and visually consistent by respecting editor weights and supporting compact two-column rendering.
- Avoids failing tests or NPEs by ensuring setup is skipped when application preferences are not available.

Testing
- Open an entry in the entry editor: fields should render and the preview should appear on the right.
- Toggle compressed/regular layouts and verify labels/editors align in one or two-column modes.
- Use preview style switching to ensure nextPreviewStyle() and previousPreviewStyle() change the preview style.
- Run unit tests to ensure behavior when Globals.prefs is null is handled gracefully.

text:
Summary

This PR implements comprehensive drag & drop support and related UI/UX improvements across the JabRef GUI. It introduces typed local dragboard utilities, data format constants, file-detection helpers, drag & drop logic for groups and entries, import/linking behavior for dropped files, visual feedback via CSS pseudo-classes, and unit tests for group DnD behavior.

Main changes

- Add Drag & Drop data formats and helpers
  - Introduced DragAndDropDataFormats with constants for GROUP, LINKED_FILE, ENTRIES and PREVIEWLAYOUTS (and a typed PREVIEWLAYOUT_LIST_CLASS).
  - Added DragAndDropHelper#getBibFiles and hasBibFiles for file detection during drag operations.

- Implement a typed in-memory dragboard
  - Added CustomLocalDragboard: a type-safe local dragboard for moving complex objects (List<BibEntry>, PreviewLayout lists, etc.) without serialization.
  - Integrated GUIGlobals.localDragboard usage across tables and group views.

- Main table drag & drop and clipboard support
  - MainTable now starts drag operations for selected entries and accepts file drops; behavior depends on drop location (top/bottom => import as new entries; center => add/link/copy/move files to the target entry depending on TransferMode).
  - Implemented clipboard copy/paste/cut handling for BibEntry objects (copy uses Globals.clipboardManager, paste inserts entries and generates keys, undo support via UndoableInsertEntry).

- File import/linking logic
  - Added ImportHandler to import files as new entries (PDF/XMP/Bib files or create empty entry with link), generate keys, populate fields and add to groups; integrates with ExternalFilesEntryLinker, ExternalFilesContentImporter and undo support.

- Groups drag & drop and view updates
  - GroupNodeViewModel: handles group view model logic, calculating hits asynchronously, handling acceptable drops and moving/adding groups/entries.
  - GroupTreeView: integrates drag detection/over/dropped behavior to move groups and to add entries to groups via the local dragboard; includes a drag-expansion handler for hover-to-expand behavior.

- UI helpers and visual feedback
  - ControlHelper: added methods to compute dropping mouse location and manage drag pseudo-classes (dragOver-top/center/bottom) for visual drop cues.
  - CSS additions: MainTable.css, GroupTree.css and updates to Base.css to style dropping states, group hits, toolbar and general theme variables.
  - JabRefFrame: added a visual tab header DnD indicator and logic to open/append dropped .bib files onto tabs. Uses DragAndDropHelper to detect .bib files.

- Utilities and plumbing
  - ViewModelTableRowFactory and ViewModelTreeTableCellFactory used/extended to wire DnD event callbacks and context menus consistently.
  - CustomLocalDragboard and DragAndDropDataFormats used where needed to avoid serialization and to pass complex objects efficiently.

- Tests
  - Added GroupNodeViewModelTest with multiple cases verifying group tree generation for automatic keyword groups, drag ordering semantics (top/bottom/center behavior), display name conversion (LaTeX to Unicode) and adding entries to explicit groups.

Why this change

These changes provide a robust, type-safe, and user-friendly drag & drop experience for both file imports and internal data movement (entries/groups). The behavior covers expected workflows: dragging PDFs/BIB files into the table or tab header, linking/moving/copying files to entries, and reordering/moving groups by drag & drop. Visual feedback and CSS ensure a more intuitive user experience.

Notes / Considerations

- Importing PDFs tries XMP, then PDF-extraction, and finally creates an empty entry linking the file.
- Undo support is provided for inserted entries; some group operations mention TODOs for undo support to be added later.
- The new CustomLocalDragboard avoids serializing Java objects to the system clipboard and is intended for in-app DnD only.

Files touched (high level)

- Added/modified GUI classes: DragAndDropDataFormats, DragAndDropHelper, CustomLocalDragboard, ControlHelper, MainTable, GroupTreeView, GroupNodeViewModel, JabRefFrame, ViewModelTableRowFactory, ImportHandler
- CSS: Base.css, GroupTree.css, MainTable.css
- Tests: GroupNodeViewModelTest
- Resources: l10n/JabRef_en.properties (unchanged strings large file bundled)

This PR lays the groundwork for intuitive DnD in JabRef and should make importing/organizing entries much smoother for users.

Summary

Implements an "Unmerge citations" (labelled "Separate citations") action in the OpenOffice/LibreOffice integration panel that splits combined/merged citation reference marks back into individual reference marks.

What I changed

- Added OOBibBase.unCombineCiteMarkers(...) which reverses combineCiteMarkers by parsing combined reference-mark names, removing the combined bookmark and inserting one bookmark per original key (inserting a space between them). The method also checks and applies the citation character style if requested and refreshes cite markers when modifications were made.
- Added a new button to the OpenOfficePanel UI:
  - Button label: "Separate citations" (Localization keys added)
  - Tooltip: "Separate merged citations"
  - Wiring: calls ooBase.unCombineCiteMarkers(...) and handles expected exceptions; is enabled/disabled with the other citation actions.
- Updated localization (JabRef_en.properties) with two new strings: "Separate merged citations" and "Separate citations".
- Added a changelog entry noting that "Merge citations" now has an opposite/undo action. (Fixes #7454)

Files changed

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/openoffice/OOBibBase.java — new unCombineCiteMarkers implementation
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/openoffice/OpenOfficePanel.java — new button, tooltip, handler and enable/disable logic
- src/main/resources/l10n/JabRef_en.properties — new localization keys
- CHANGELOG.md — user-visible changelog entry

Why

Users who previously merged multiple citations in Writer had no built-in way to split them back into individual reference marks. This change provides a UI action to do that from the OpenOffice/LibreOffice panel, improving the round-trip editing workflow.

Notes and known limitations

- This implementation improves the situation but does not fully resolve all edge cases described in the original issue:
  - When citations are merged, the code that creates unique reference-mark names may not preserve the original unique suffix numbers. If getUniqueReferenceMarkName() returns a different name than the original, any extra per-reference data stored in document properties (e.g. page numbers attached to a specific reference mark) may be lost or (rarely) taken from another entry.
  - combineCiteMarkers orders merged entries (by year), so the original order of entries in the document may not be restored when unmerging.

These limitations are documented in the related issue (#7454). A robust fix would require preserving per-reference unique identifiers in the merged name (or otherwise storing/reusing them) and preserving original ordering when combining.

Testing

- Manually tested in a running JabRef/Writer instance; UI screenshot was added to the PR description.
- No automated tests were added (GUI-related change). See issue notes for more context on testability and edge cases.

Fixes

- Fixes #7454

text:
Fix citation key table and improve consistency check output

This PR fixes the citation key column layout and improves the readability of the Field Presence Consistency Check TXT output (fixes #13013).

What changed

- Added explicit comparators for sorting entries:
  - BibEntryByCitationKeyComparator: sorts entries by presence of citation key and then alphabetically by citation key.
  - BibEntryByFieldsComparator: sorts entries by number of fields and then by field names.
  These are combined with FieldComparatorStack and used when building the differing entries list in BibliographyConsistencyCheck.

- Refactored BibliographyConsistencyCheck:
  - Replaced the previous inline comparator with the new comparator stack for clearer sorting behavior.
  - Now collects differing entries using the comparator stack.

- Improved TXT writer formatting (BibliographyConsistencyCheckResultTxtWriter):
  - The legend for the meaning of symbols is now emitted as a Markdown table with a header row (Symbol | Meaning) and a dynamic column width based on content.
  - Column width calculation for the entry type and citation key columns has been fixed and now accounts for actual citation key lengths (prevents truncated/uneven columns for long keys).
  - The symbol legend is localized; added two new localization keys: "Meaning" and "Symbol".

- Tests updated and expanded:
  - Updated expectations in several tests to match the new Markdown table legend and adjusted column spacing.
  - Added checkVeryLongCitationKey test to ensure very long citation keys are handled and column widths adapt correctly.

Other notes

- Localization: added JabRef_en.properties entries for "Meaning" and "Symbol".
- No CHANGELOG entry included (feature not yet released).
- This PR includes unit tests covering the formatting and sorting changes.

References

- Fixes: https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/13013

Summary:
Fixes the working-directory arguments used when opening a terminal on Linux for two terminal types (gnome-terminal and konsole). This resolves issue #9953 where those terminals opened in a default directory (typically the user home) because their ProcessBuilder arguments were malformed.

What I changed:
- Corrected how the working-directory argument is constructed for gnome-terminal and konsole so the intended directory is actually passed to the launched terminal.
- Left the third Linux terminal command unchanged (it was already correct).

Reason & background:
The bug was caused by a slight misuse of ProcessBuilder which produced badly formed argument lists for gnome-terminal and konsole. As a result, the terminal sessions opened in the default directory instead of the directory requested by the user.

Tests:
- I did not add unit tests for the low-level OS command invocation because verifying a running terminal’s working directory from unit tests is complex and would require significant refactoring (and might still be unreliable). Fix several bugs in import flow, MSBib mapping and entry type dialog initialization

This PR fixes multiple issues discovered in the GUI/import code paths:

- EntryTypeView: Fix initialization order to avoid NullPointerExceptions
  - The dialog previously referenced the viewModel in the constructor (bindings and button actions) before viewModel was created in initialize(). The bindings and generate-button setup are now performed after viewModel is created (in initialize()), preventing NPEs when opening the entry type dialog.

- ImportHandler.importEntryWithDuplicateCheck: Use the final entry object when adding to groups and downloading files
  - After duplicate resolution the code may replace the imported entry (entryToInsert). The old implementation incorrectly passed the original local variable entry to addToGroups and used it when downloading linked files. These operations now use entryToInsert so that merges/keeps are reflected correctly in group assignment and file downloads.

- MSBibMapping.getLanguage: Correct LCID→language lookup
  - The previous implementation incorrectly used the wrong map and default values, causing incorrect behavior and a compile-time/type mismatch. getLanguage(int LCID) now correctly looks up the language string for the provided LCID and returns "english" as the default when no mapping is found.

- Misc
  - Fixed a few related inconsistencies (small refactors and safer null/default handling) to make the fixes robust.

Validation
- Project builds and existing unit tests (ImportHandlerTest.handleBibTeXData) were run to verify no regressions in the import parsing path.

Benefits
- Prevents runtime crashes when opening the Entry Type dialog.
- Ensures entries resulting from duplicate resolution/merging are correctly added to groups and have their linked files downloaded when requested.
- Correct mapping of LCIDs to language names for MSBib import/export.

Add RenamePdfCleanup cleanup job

- Introduces RenamePdfCleanup which implements CleanupJob and renames linked files (e.g. PDFs) for a BibEntry to their suggested names.
- Behavior:
  - Iterates over all LinkedFile objects on an entry.
  - If onlyRelativePaths is true, skips files with absolute paths.
  - Uses LinkedFileHandler.renameToSuggestedName() to perform renaming and logs any IOExceptions.
  - If any file was renamed, updates the entry's file list on the JavaFX thread (via DefaultTaskExecutor.runInJavaFXThread) and returns the resulting FieldChange(s); otherwise returns an empty list.
- Constructor takes: onlyRelativePaths, BibDatabaseContext, and FilePreferences.

This change centralizes PDF renaming logic into a cleanup job usable by the cleanup framework and ensures UI-thread-safe updates of entry data.

- Added a Table of Contents for easier navigation.

The goal is to lower the barrier to contribution by making the expectations and steps for submitting PRs explicit, to reduce repetitive reviewer feedback, and to provide concrete references for common tasks (dependency additions, localization, keyboard shortcuts, ADRs). Documentation-only change — no code changes or tests required.

Summary

- Change the handling of duplicate fields in custom BibEntryType definitions: instead of throwing IllegalArgumentException during parsing/building, duplicate fields are now logged as warnings and the builder records that it has warnings.
- MetaDataParser now skips (returns empty) for custom entry type definitions that produced warnings and logs a warning with the offending comment. This prevents failing to open libraries that contain custom entry types with duplicate fields (#11127).

What changed

- src/main/java/org/jabref/model/entry/BibEntryTypeBuilder.java
  - Added an SLF4J logger and a hasWarnings flag.
  - Duplicate-field checks now log a warning and set hasWarnings instead of throwing IllegalArgumentException.
  - Minor refactor of field/collection initializations and added hasWarnings() accessor.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/util/MetaDataParser.java
  - After building the entry type, MetaDataParser checks entryTypeBuilder.hasWarnings() and logs a warning and returns Optional.empty() when warnings are present. This avoids loading malformed custom types.

- src/test/java/org/jabref/model/entry/BibEntryTypeBuilderTest.java
  - Disabled tests that expected IllegalArgumentException for duplicate fields, since the behavior changed to logging warnings instead of throwing.

- CHANGELOG.md
  - Added a note to the changelog describing the fix for libraries with custom entry types containing duplicate fields (refs GitHub issue #11127).

Motivation

Previously, parsing custom entry types that contained duplicate fields caused exceptions and prevented opening existing libraries. To make JabRef more robust and tolerant of malformed custom entry type definitions, such cases are now logged and the problematic custom type is skipped instead of failing the entire import/open operation.

Notes

- The behavior change is intentionally non-breaking: malformed custom types are not loaded but do not prevent the application from opening the library.
- Tests that asserted exceptions for duplicate fields were disabled because the builder no longer throws; consider updating tests to assert logged warnings or the hasWarnings behavior in future work.

Summary
- Remove noisy and obsolete UI notifications and make autosave silent.
- Introduce a SaveDatabaseMode to distinguish between NORMAL (user-initiated) and SILENT (background/autosave) saves.
- Adjust saving flow to set the panel into a saving state and avoid showing notifications for silent saves.
- Remove several localization strings that are no longer used and update the changelog accordingly.
- Log a warning when a shared DBMS connection is lost.

What changed
- Added SaveDatabaseMode enum to SaveDatabaseAction and added an overloaded save(SaveDatabaseMode) method. The default save() delegates to NORMAL.
- Autosave now calls save(SaveDatabaseMode.SILENT) in AutosaveUIManager to prevent notifications during autosave.
- doSave() now sets panel.setSaving(true) earlier in the save process.
- Removed many dialogService.notify / panel.output calls that produced user notifications for operations that should be silent or are redundant (new database creation, opening/closing libraries, pasting entries, autosave, connection lost dialogs, etc.).
- Deleted corresponding unused localization keys from JabRef_en.properties and added a changelog entry noting that notifications shown during autosave were fixed and obsolete notifications were removed.
- DBMSSynchronizer now logs a warning (LOGGER.warn) when an SQL connection is lost before posting ConnectionLostEvent.

Rationale
- Background operations such as autosave (and certain internal events) should not produce distracting user notifications. This makes the UI less noisy while preserving notifications for explicit user actions.
- Adding an explicit mode for save operations keeps the behavior explicit and extensible.
- Logging connection loss aids debugging without immediately notifying the user when the app can handle reconnection flows.

Summary:
This PR reduces UI and CPU load by throttling reactions to frequent BibDatabase change events. Instead of running expensive actions immediately on every event, they are now scheduled with a short delay and deduplicated if more events arrive within that delay. This makes editing entry fields feel smoother and reduces spikes when opening large libraries.

What changed:
- Added a new utility DelayTaskThrottler to schedule a Runnable after a configurable delay and cancel/reschedule if new requests arrive.
- Replaced ad-hoc executor/future logic in autosave and backup management with DelayTaskThrottler.
- Throttled group recalculation in GroupNodeViewModel.
- Updated CHANGELOG to mention the performance improvement.

Configured delays (defaults used in this PR):
- Group match recalculation: 1000 ms (1 s)
- Autosave trigger: 2000 ms (2 s)
- Backup trigger: 15000 ms (15 s)

Files touched:
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/util/DelayTaskThrottler.java (new)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/groups/GroupNodeViewModel.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/autosaveandbackup/AutosaveManager.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/autosaveandbackup/BackupManager.java
- CHANGELOG.md

Implementation notes for reviewers:
- DelayTaskThrottler uses a single-thread ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor with setRemoveOnCancelPolicy(true) and keeps a reference to the currently scheduled Future to cancel/reschedule.
- AutosaveManager and BackupManager no longer manage their own executor queues/futures; they delegate scheduling and shutdown to the throttler.
- GroupNodeViewModel now schedules calculateNumberOfMatches via the throttler to avoid frequent recalculation when many entry fields change quickly.
- shutdown() methods now call throttler.shutdown() to clean up executors.

Motivation / Fixes:
- This change targets high CPU/memory spikes seen when opening or editing very large bib files (see discussion and report in #5734). By throttling frequent change events, CPU and memory usage remain much lower and the editor interaction is smoother.

Testing / TODO:
- Manual testing has been considered in the PR description, but unit tests were not added.
- Ensure no regression in autosave/backup behavior and that throttled delays are acceptable for users. Adjust delays if needed.

Related issue:
- Should help with and is related to: #5734

Fix file field parser not recognizing online URLs

What I changed
- Fixed the file-field parser so that it recognizes and correctly parses online URLs (e.g. http://..., https://..., ftp://..., and common www-based links) stored in the `file` BibTeX field.
- Updated the URL detection logic/regex in the file-field parser to treat matching values as online links instead of treating them as invalid or local file paths.
- Added unit tests covering multiple URL formats and edge cases to prevent regressions.
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to mention the fix.

Why
- Previously some online URLs in the `file` field were not recognized and therefore could not be opened from JabRef or were parsed incorrectly. This change ensures URLs are handled consistently and can be opened as external links.

Testing
- New automated tests added for http/https/ftp and www-style URLs, plus a few edge cases.
- Manually tested in a running JabRef instance: adding entries with URL values in the `file` field, opening links from the entry, and importing/exporting entries with URL file fields.

Fixes: #7882

Summary

Fixes a bug where the PDF Downloader would save HTML source (for example a login page or an error page) to disk when the server refused access or returned a non-PDF response. Instead of producing a clear error, the downloader treated any response body as a PDF and wrote it to file.

Reproduction

1. Attempt to download a PDF from a URL that requires authentication or returns an error page (e.g. 401/403/404) or returns HTML content.
2. The downloader creates a .pdf file containing the HTML source instead of failing with a meaningful error.

Root cause

The downloader assumed that a successful HTTP response body was always a PDF and did not validate the response status code or Content-Type header before saving.

What this change does

- Validates the HTTP response before saving:
  - Checks for a 2xx status code.
  - Verifies the Content-Type header contains 'application/pdf'.
- If validation fails, the downloader:
  - Does not write the response to disk.
  - Raises/returns a clear, descriptive error indicating the status code and/or unexpected Content-Type.
- Adds unit/integration tests to cover:
  - Successful PDF download (application/pdf, 200).
  - 401/403/404 responses (should error, no file created).
  - 200 responses with Content-Type 'text/html' (should error, no file created).
- Improves logging/user-facing error messages to help diagnose permission and authentication issues.

Notes and compatibility

- This is a non-breaking change for normal successful downloads; only invalid responses will now surface an error instead of producing an invalid PDF file on disk.
- If callers relied on the previous behavior of saving whatever came back, they should now handle the new error conditions.

Testing done

- Added automated tests for the new validation logic.
- Manual testing against a protected endpoint and a mock HTML error page to confirm errors are raised and no files are created.

Reviewer guidance

- Focus on the response validation logic (status code and Content-Type checks).
- Check error messages for clarity and that they include enough info (status code, Content-Type) without leaking sensitive content.

This PR implements several UX improvements and small refactors around the global search dialog, updates the table model API used by the Library column, and refreshes the CHANGELOG entries.

- Global search UX

  - Adds getBibDatabaseContext() to access the full BibDatabaseContext where needed.

  - Updates CHANGELOG.md: adds entries for the separated search bar, double-click behavior, and moves/cleans up some previously listed items; fixes a small typo for the Keywords field line.

Fix keyword parsing and serialization (fixes #12810)

What changed
- Replaced the old StringTokenizer-based parsing with a custom parser that correctly handles escaped delimiters. Delimiters preceded by a backslash are now treated as part of the keyword instead of splitting the list.
- Added getKeywordsAsStrings(...) helper to implement the new parsing logic and removed the unused StringTokenizer import.
- Updated serialize(...) to escape backslashes and the configured delimiter when producing a string representation of keywords.
- Added a unit test to cover parsing of a comma that is escaped with a backslash (Machine\, Learning).
- Minor formatting/refactor changes in tests and a changelog entry noting the fix.

Why
- Previously delimiters inside keywords (e.g., commas in keyword values) were incorrectly split, causing keywords to be parsed incorrectly. The new code properly supports escaping and preserves intended keywords when delimiters are escaped.

Notes
- Serialization now escapes delimiters and backslashes so that round-tripping keywords containing delimiters will work correctly.
- CHANGELOG.md updated to reference the bugfix.

Summary
- Add client-side validation for library directory path fields in the General tab and prevent closing the Library Properties dialog if any properties are invalid.

What changed
- LibraryPropertiesView: savePreferencesAndCloseDialog() now closes the dialog only when viewModel.storeAllSettings() returns true.
- LibraryPropertiesViewModel: storeAllSettings() now returns a boolean and runs validation for each PropertiesTab via validateSettings(). It stores settings for a tab only if validation passes, and returns true only if all tabs are valid.
- GeneralPropertiesViewModel:
  - Introduced debounced validation using a PauseTransition (1.2s) for the three directory path properties (Library Specific, User Specific, LaTeX). Listeners trigger validation after the delay.
  - Implemented validateSettings(), validatePaths(), validateDirectory(...) and resolvePath(...) helpers.
  - Validation allows empty paths (treated as default) but checks that non-empty paths exist. Relative paths are resolved against the database file parent directory when possible; absolute paths are used as-is. If a path is invalid, an error notification is shown via DialogService.
- l10n: added an English localization key for the new validation error message: "The path for %0 ('%1') does not exist.".

Rationale
- Prevents the properties dialog from closing when the user enters non-existent directory paths so users can correct errors before saving.
- Debounced validation reduces noise by avoiding immediate validation on every keystroke while still giving quick feedback.

Behavioral notes
- If any tab's validateSettings() returns false, storeAllSettings() returns false and the dialog remains open.
- Empty directory fields are allowed and treated as defaults.
- Relative paths are resolved against the library's database file location when available; if no base path exists, a relative path is treated as invalid.

Fix file type detection and improve linked-file handling + tests

This PR makes several fixes and improvements to how external file types are detected and handled for linked files and downloads, and adds/updates unit tests to cover these behaviors.

Key changes

- ExternalFileTypes
  - getExternalFileTypeByMimeType now strips MIME parameters (e.g. "; charset=UTF-8") before lookup.
  - For the MIME type "text/html" a URL/HTML fallback file type is always returned (StandardExternalFileType.URL).

- LinkedFileViewModel
  - Uses the injected ExternalFileTypes instance for icon lookup and MIME/extension inference instead of relying on a global lookup in some places.
  - File type inference for downloads first tries the MIME type (via ExternalFileTypes) and then falls back to deriving from the URL suffix.
  - prepareDownloadTask ensures the suggested file type/extension is preserved and avoids overwriting file type information incorrectly.
  - Downloading an HTML page now notifies the user that a website was downloaded as HTML rather than PDF.

Summary

Improve toolbar icons and their layout for better consistency, accessibility and responsiveness.

What changed

- Replaced previous toolbar icons with updated SVG assets for improved clarity and visual consistency.
- Standardized icon dimensions and spacing by introducing CSS variables (icon-size, icon-gap) and applying them to the toolbar and icon-button components.
- Reworked toolbar layout to use a flex-based structure that supports proper alignment, spacing and responsive wrapping.
- Improved interactive states (hover, focus, active) and added visible focus outlines for keyboard users.
- Added/ensured ARIA labels on icon buttons so screen readers announce their purpose reliably.
- Refactored duplicated styles into a single icon-button component used across the toolbar.
- Updated unit snapshots and visual tests to reflect the new icons and layout.

Why

- Prior icons were inconsistent in size and weight which caused a cluttered UI.
- The old layout did not adapt well to small viewports and had accessibility gaps (missing focus outlines and ARIA labels).
- Standardizing styles and assets makes the toolbar easier to maintain and extends more reliably to new buttons.

Notes for reviewers

- No public API changes; existing toolbar usages should continue to work.
- Please verify the toolbar at multiple breakpoints and in both light/dark themes.
- Confirm keyboard navigation (Tab/Shift+Tab) highlights controls correctly and screen readers announce labels.
- Run the test suite and review updated visual snapshots to confirm there are no unintended regressions.

How to test

1. yarn install && yarn test
2. yarn storybook and inspect the toolbar stories across widths and themes
3. Manually test keyboard focus and screen reader output for icon buttons

Files touched

- Updated SVG icon assets
- toolbar styles / layout files
- icon-button component (styles + accessibility fixes)
- Storybook stories and visual snapshots

This change improves the toolbar's visual consistency, responsiveness, and accessibility while consolidating icon/button styling for easier future changes.

text:
Summary

- Add a Library column to the main table and expose the database path on the table view model.
- Add a dedicated Global Search window with its own search bar and result dialog; allow double-clicking a global-search result to switch to the corresponding library and select the entry.

Details

1) Main table / model
- BibEntryTableViewModel
  - Store a BibDatabaseContext for each entry and expose bibDatabasePathProperty() (read-only string) so the UI can display the library the entry belongs to.
  - Adjusted matched-groups binding to use the database metadata groups binding inside a UiThreadBinding.
- LibraryColumn
  - New MainTable column that displays the base name of the library file using bibDatabasePathProperty(). It integrates with the main table column model and uses the existing ValueTableCellFactory.

2) Global search UI
- GlobalSearchBar
  - Generalized the search bar to support NORMAL_SEARCH and GLOBAL_SEARCH modes (uses different searchQuery properties from the StateManager depending on mode).
  - Keeps the same set of modifier buttons (regex, case sensitive, fulltext, keep search string), with visibility logic and validation for regex input.
  - Uses a delayed update (reactfx Timer) to debounce user input before updating the search query in StateManager.
  - Adds auto-complete support and uses reflection to access the ControlsFX auto-completion popup so it can be skinned and used reliably.
  - Displays results count/hint text and builds a richer tooltip with advanced hints when enabled in preferences.

- GlobalSearchResultDialog
  - New dialog that hosts a dedicated GlobalSearchBar and shows search results from all open libraries using a SearchResultsTable and a PreviewViewer.
  - Removes special-field columns from the results table and wires the selection to update the preview.
  - Double-click on a result finds the corresponding library tab, shows it, clears the search, selects the entry in the main table and closes the dialog.
  - Adds a keep-on-top toggle and persists window size in preferences.

Behavioral notes
- The new Library column allows users to identify which library an entry comes from when multiple libraries are open.
- The separated Global Search window (with its own search bar) enables searching across open libraries and provides an improved workflow to navigate directly to entries from the result list.

No user-facing behavior was removed. The changes introduce UI functionality and wiring required for the new global search window and the library column.

Fixes #10414

This PR adds a duplicate checker for Citation Relations entities. The implemented check compares the names of entries to detect possible duplicates and shows a warning when a potential duplicate is found.

Details

- Implements duplicate detection for Citation Relations by comparing entry names.
- Integrates the duplicate check into the UI flow where entries are added/linked. Note: there is existing logic that replaces the “add” button with a “link” button for local entries, and the duplicate check is invoked accordingly when using that button.

Notes / Limitations

- The current duplicate heuristic is a simple name comparison; I am not sure this is the best approach and it may need refinement for more robust duplicate detection.
- No automated tests were added in this PR.

Checks and artifacts

- Screenshots of the UI change included in the PR description

Next steps

- Improve the duplicate detection algorithm (e.g., fuzzy matching or additional field comparisons).
- Add unit/integration tests to cover duplicate-checking behavior and edge cases.

Fix incorrect styling of error console log entries when scrolling

Problem
- When scrolling the error console, different log messages could pick up the wrong style classes. This was caused by never resetting style classes on list cells when reusing/adding them.

What I changed
- Ensure style classes are reset on cells when they are created/added so messages cannot inherit previous state.
- Introduce a generic ListFactory class (pattern borrowed from #1917) to centralize list cell creation and reuse, preventing the same class-resetting bug from recurring.

Why
- Properly resetting classes fixes the visual glitches seen while scrolling the console and makes cell lifecycle handling explicit and robust.

Notes
- This addresses the behavior described in #2210.
- Manual testing: scrolled through many different log types (info/warn/error) and confirmed styles remain correct; no regressions observed.

Fixes #8446 

### Problem
After a fresh start; selecting an entry for the first time causes a small freeze of ~3-4 seconds. In short, the freeze occurs when creating a new WebView instance for the preview panel.

### Solution
My solution is to preload a number of WebView instances at startup *(4 instances for now)*. To ensure the preload has no effect on startup performance, I wrapped the web view construction code in `Platform.runLater()`.
Instances are added dynamically when the number of available instances goes under a certain threshold.

### Alternative Solution
I tried a Proxy design pattern; I used a proxy class for `PreviewViewer`; the proxy builds a `PreviewViewer` instance using a combination of `CompletableFuture<PreviewViewer>` and `Platform.runLater()`, then it redirects method calls to `PreviewViewer` by registering callbacks. However, this solution was complex and hard to implement without altering app behavior. 


https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/21198231/160512108-7e79c206-6d7e-439c-9198-71cacff3da5e.mp4

Summary: Fixes a bug where metadata changes on external groups were not being merged into the canonical group record.

What was happening: When an external group’s metadata was updated, those changes were ignored during the merge path. The merge logic treated external groups differently and skipped applying incoming metadata updates, causing stale or missing metadata to persist.

This change: • Updates the merge logic to include metadata changes for external groups so incoming metadata is applied correctly. • Ensures metadata maps are deep-merged (preserving existing keys unless overwritten) to avoid unintentionally discarding nested entries. • Adds unit tests covering merging behavior for external and non-external groups, including nested metadata cases.

Impact: Metadata updates for external groups will now be reflected properly after merges. No breaking API changes. Tests added to prevent regressions.

- Ensure the shared database is fully loaded and the UI is refreshed when a shared library is opened. This includes initializing the view/state for shared databases and triggering the same entry population path used for local databases.

This PR adds/updates developer-facing documentation and a small launcher script to make building, packaging and debugging JabRef easier.

What changed

- docs/code-howtos/jpackage.md
  - New how-to describing how to build jpackage application images and installers (uses Badass JLink Gradle plugin). Includes Windows prerequisites (WiX Toolset) and exact Gradle commands for jpackageImage and jpackage.
  - Adds a step-by-step guide for remote debugging installed jpackage builds (how to keep debug symbols, modify the generated Jabref.bat to enable JDWP on port 8000, and connect an IDE).

- docs/getting-into-the-code/guidelines-for-setting-up-a-local-workspace.md
  - Clarifications and expanded guidance for setting up a local development environment (JDK 18 requirement, git, IDE configuration for IntelliJ and Eclipse, enabling annotation processors, Gradle vs IntelliJ build, code style and CheckStyle setup).
  - Adds troubleshooting tips and common issues encountered during setup (generated sources, buildSrc, openjfx artifacts, journal abbreviation loader, etc.).

- snap/local/JabRef-launcher
  - Adds a small POSIX shell launcher used by the snap packaging to start the modular runtime (invokes java with module path and the org.jabref.cli.Launcher module).

Why

- To provide clear, reproducible instructions for building platform installers and for debugging issues that only appear in installed, modularized builds.
- To help new contributors set up their IDE and local workspace reliably and to surface frequent pitfalls and fixes.
- To provide a simple snap-compatible launcher for running the modular image.

Testing / How to use

- Build from source: ./gradlew assemble (or ./gradlew run)
- Create jpackage image: ./gradlew -PprojVersion=... jpackageImage
- Create installer: ./gradlew -PprojVersion=... jpackage
- For debugging installed Windows builds: remove --strip-debug from jlink options, build jpackageImage, edit the generated Jabref.bat as documented to enable remote debugging, start the app and attach your IDE to localhost:8000.
- Snap environments can use snap/local/JabRef-launcher to run the modular image.

No functional code changes to core logic; mainly documentation and packaging/launcher support.

Summary

Fix handling of legacy linked-file entries that incorrectly included the file directory as a separate element in the stored filename. This caused broken or duplicated paths for attachments imported from older JabRef exports and prevented some linked files from being opened.

What I changed

- Detect the legacy format during parsing of the file-links field and normalize entries where the directory was stored as an extra element of the filename. The parser now reconstructs the intended relative/absolute path and drops the spurious directory element. 
- Add a lightweight migration step applied on library load to convert existing legacy entries in .bib files to the corrected format, preserving link targets where possible. 
- Ensure serialization no longer writes the directory as a separate filename element so new exports are correct.
- Added unit tests covering several legacy variants and round-trip serialization to prevent regressions.

Compatibility and notes

- Migration is applied automatically on load; it modifies only malformed linked-file entries and aims to avoid data loss. Users are still advised to keep a backup of their library before upgrading large or important databases. 
- No UI changes. Performance impact is negligible (one-time normalization on load).

Summary

- Add an explicit "Copy citation" / "Export to clipboard" flow and integrate it into the UI (main table context menu and preview). This makes it easy to copy formatted citations directly from the entry list or the preview pane.

What changed

- GUI
  - src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/maintable/RightClickMenu.java: Added menu item(s) to export/copy citations to the clipboard from the main table context menu.
  - src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preview/CopyCitationAction.java: New/updated action to copy the currently previewed citation to the system clipboard.
  - src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/exporter/ExportToClipboardAction.java: Implemented the exporter action that writes exported citation strings to the clipboard.
  - src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/JabRefFrame.java: Hooked up the new action(s) to menus/shortcuts and ensured correct lifecycle/registration.

- Logic
  - src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/exporter/TemplateExporter.java: Improved handling of exported content (template-based exporters) so they can be routed to the clipboard consistently.
  - src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/util/StandardFileType.java and src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/util/UnknownFileType.java: Improve file-type handling for exporters; ensure exporters expose/return sensible file type information even when no standard extension is present.

- Documentation
  - CHANGELOG.md: Documented the feature addition and relevant fixes.

Notes

- The new clipboard export action reuses existing exporter templates and file-type metadata so copying a citation yields the formatted result users expect.
- File-type changes add robustness for exporters that previously returned no/unknown types; this avoids failures when exporting to non-file targets such as the clipboard.
- No breaking API changes expected for existing external code, but exporters should provide a file type when possible to improve integration.

Testing

- Tested manually by right-clicking entries in the main table and selecting the new "Copy citation"/"Export to clipboard" action, and by using the preview pane action. The clipboard contains the exported citation in the selected format.

This PR groups UX wiring, action implementation, and small exporter/file-type improvements to provide a smooth "copy citation to clipboard" experience.

Summary

This PR fixes the behavior of the file-link deletion dialog shown when removing a linked file from a bibliography entry.

What I changed

- Default dialog action now only removes the file link from the entry ("Remove link from entry"), instead of deleting the linked file from disk.
- Clicking "Cancel" no longer removes the file from the list. The return value of the delete() method has been corrected to reflect the cancel action.

Why

- Previously the dialog's first (default) option performed a destructive delete-from-disk, which was surprising and unsafe for users. The safer default is to only remove the link.
- Canceling the dialog had the side-effect of removing the file entry; this is now fixed so Cancel is non-destructive.

Fixes

- Fixes #3679

Improve metadata synchronization for remote databases (fixes #3235)

What I changed
- CHANGELOG.md: Added a note about improved metadata updates in remote databases.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/shared/DBMSProcessor.java: Reworked setSharedMetaData(...) to stop truncating the METADATA table and instead perform an UPDATE-then-INSERT for each metadata entry.

Why
- Previously the code TRUNCATED the METADATA table and then inserted entries, which was destructive and could interfere with concurrent clients or lose keys not present in the provided map. The new approach updates existing keys and inserts missing ones, preserving other metadata rows.

Details
- Build an UPDATE prepared statement and an INSERT prepared statement.
- For each metadata entry: try UPDATE; if no rows were affected, perform INSERT.
- SQL exceptions are logged.

Impact
- Non-destructive metadata updates; safer for remote/shared databases and multi-client scenarios.

Related issue: #3235

text:
Add scheduled workflow to check external links in documentation and record ADR

What this PR does:
- Adds a new GitHub Actions workflow (.github/workflows/check-links.yaml) that runs markdown-link-check on the docs/ folder on a monthly schedule (cron: "0 9 1 * *" — first of each month at 09:00).
  - The job prepares a docs/ROOT folder and copies CHANGELOG.md and README.md there so they are included in the check.
  - Uses gaurav-nelson/github-action-markdown-link-check@v1 with mlc_config.json and quiet mode enabled.
- Removes the duplicated markdown-link-check steps from the existing tests workflow (.github/workflows/tests.yml) so link checking no longer runs as part of the regular test/checkstyle flow.
- Adds an ADR describing the decision to check external documentation links monthly (docs/adr/0011-test-external-links-in-documentation.md).

Why:
- Running external link checks in a separate, scheduled workflow prevents external site flakiness from breaking or slowing down normal CI and PR checks.
- A monthly run provides automated notification of broken links without interfering with day-to-day development.

Notes / future work:
- Some external sites (e.g. github.com) may return forbidden and need to be ignored/filtered; the ADR and tool issue links note this limitation and that filtering is future work.

Change default behavior when removing linked files and add tests

- Change: When removing a linked file from an entry the default dialog option now removes the link from the entry instead of deleting the file from disk. This is documented in CHANGELOG (refs #3679).

    - delete() returns true and deletes the file when "Delete from disk" is chosen,
    - delete() returns false and shows an error when attempting to delete a missing file,
    - delete() returns false and preserves the file when the dialog is cancelled.

This PR implements the safer default removal behavior, fixes the cancelation bug, and adds unit tests to prevent regressions.

This PR implements several improvements and features for the main application frame (JabRefFrame) and documents them in the changelog: 

- Welcome tab management
  - Adds support for a WelcomeTab and a showWelcomeTab() method which reuses an existing Welcome tab if present or creates and selects a new one. Ensures correct selection behavior when opening/closing libraries.

- Dynamic side pane integration and persistence
  - Integrates SidePane into the main SplitPane and adds logic to add/remove the SidePane when it has/no children. 
  - Persists side pane width via preferences and updates divider positions when the stage is visible. 

- File history menu and keyboard quick-open
  - Adds FileHistoryMenu wired to recent files preferences with keyboard handling to open history items by typed key. The menu is automatically disabled when empty.

- Key bindings and new entry shortcuts
  - Centralizes key binding handling for frame-level shortcuts (focus entry table, focus groups, next/previous library, search, global search dialog). 
  - Adds shortcuts to create common new entries (Article, Book, InBook, Master/PhD thesis, Proceedings, TechReport, Unpublished, InProceedings) using NewEntryAction.

- Tab management and behavior
  - Provides APIs to list/get current LibraryTab, show library tabs and add tabs by context or by BibDatabaseContext. 
  - Hides the tab bar automatically when workspace preference requests hiding and at most one library is open.
  - Keeps application title bound to the active library tab title and updates stateManager when switching tabs. 

- Tab context menu and close actions
  - Adds per-tab context menu items: Library properties, Open database folder, Open console, Close library, Close other libraries, Close all libraries.
  - Implements CloseAction, CloseDatabaseAction, CloseOthersDatabaseAction and CloseAllDatabaseAction with appropriate state checks and safe close flows (requestClose and Tab.CLOSED_EVENT firing).

- Drag-and-drop and frame DnD handling
  - Initializes frame-level drag-and-drop support via FrameDndHandler to enable opening databases by dropping files onto the frame.

- Open database folder helper
  - Adds OpenDatabaseFolder command to open the folder of a saved database and select the file in the OS file manager (uses NativeDesktop and handles IO exceptions).

- State and binding improvements
  - Binds the list of open databases to the tabs and maps active search queries and focus owner to the correct library. 
  - Ensures selected entries and global search autocompleter are updated when the user switches tabs. 
  - Adds refresh() that resets field formatters for open library table models and openLastEditedDatabases() to reopen the last used files from preferences. 

- ViewModel and UI command handling
  - Instantiates JabRefFrameViewModel and delegates UI commands handling to it. Also exposes viewModel.close() usage for window close.

Other notes:
- Defensive programming and logging are added for cases such as trying to close when no library is open or failing to open the database folder.

Overall this change centralizes frame-level UI responsibilities: welcome screen handling, tab & side pane lifecycle, keyboard shortcuts, file history, DnD and tab context actions, and improved state synchronization with StateManager.

Add FieldFormatterCleanupsPanel UI and improve internal field handling + integrity tests

- Introduce FieldFormatterCleanupsPanel: a Swing panel to configure field formatter cleanups. The panel provides:
  - a checkbox to enable/disable cleanups,
  - a list of configured cleanup actions with add/remove/reset/recommend controls,
  - selectors for target field and formatter (including tooltips and descriptions),
  - ability to store/load settings from MetaData.
- Populate the field selector from InternalBibtexFields.getAllPublicAndInternalFieldNames() and include the BibEntry key field to allow formatting the entry key.
- InternalBibtexFields: expose helpers to query and retrieve field properties, weights and lists used throughout the UI and validation logic (getAllPublicFieldNames, getAllPublicAndInternalFieldNames, getPersonNameFields, getJournalNameFields, getBookNameFields, etc.). These utilities centralize knowledge about which fields are public/internal and their special properties.

text:
Fix selecting custom export for Copy -> Export to Clipboard when the custom export used an uppercase file extension (Fixes #6285).

What I changed
- Fixed the exporter selection logic so custom exporters with uppercase or mixed-case extensions are recognized for the "Export to Clipboard" action.
- Introduced FileType.fromExtensions and a new UnknownFileType which normalizes extensions to lowercase and implements proper equality/hashCode based on normalized extensions.
- Updated StandardFileType: documented extensions are lowercase, added htm as HTML extension, and replaced the previous helper with fromExtensions.
- TemplateExporter now uses StandardFileType.fromExtensions to construct the file type for template-based exporters.
- Reworked ExportToClipboardAction to use the ExporterFactory for obtaining exporters and to compare FileType objects against a supported Set<FileType> (instead of string extension comparisons). Also:
  - Injects ExporterFactory, ClipBoardManager and TaskExecutor instead of relying on Globals, and uses the injected ClipBoardManager when setting clipboard content.
  - Improves error reporting and uses the injected TaskExecutor for background execution.
- Updated JabRefFrame and RightClickMenu call sites to pass the new constructor parameters.
- Added @Override to CopyCitationAction.execute (small cleanup).
- Added CHANGELOG entry.

Why
Previously exporter selection for copying to clipboard matched extensions via raw strings, which caused mismatches when custom exporters defined extensions with uppercase letters. By normalizing and comparing FileType objects we ensure case-insensitive matching and correct handling of unknown/custom extensions.

Notes
- No new automated tests were added; change was manually tested.
- This PR fixes the user-reported issue #6285.

2. In the app, select a citation (or multiple citations) and choose "Push to Texmaker".

Summary
- Restore intelligent title selection when merging candidates by adding best-title picking logic to mergeCandidates.

- Updated mergeCandidates so it still merges all candidate fields but then selects and overrides the merged title with the best-scoring title candidate instead of relying on last-wins behavior.

- This addresses a regression where multiple title candidates were resolved in a last-wins manner, sometimes choosing suboptimal titles. The new logic chooses the most suitable title according to the heuristics.

- Screenshots demonstrating the fix are included in the PR description.

Fixes #8907 — Remember Sidepane width after restart

Summary
- Previously the SplitPane divider position was stored as a proportion of the window width. If the divider was adjusted while the window was maximized, restarting the app could reset the visible sidepane width because the proportion was applied to a minimized window width and then preserved when the window was later maximized.

What I changed
- Persist the sidepane width in a way that restores the same visible width after restart, avoiding the incorrect shrink/expand behavior when the app starts minimized and is later maximized.

Why
- Users expect the side pane to keep the same pixel width they set, even after restarting the application in a different window state (minimized/maximized).

Manual testing / verification
1. Maximize JabRef.
2. Move the SplitPane divider to roughly half the window (or any desired width).
3. Restart the app.
4. Confirm the sidepane width after restart matches the width before restart, even if the app starts minimized and is later maximized.

Other notes
- CHANGELOG.md updated with a user-facing note about this fix.
- Manually tested in a running JabRef build.
- Developer documentation and user documentation were checked and are up to date; an issue was opened/submitted to docs if required.
- No automated tests were added for this change.

Summary

Fixes an issue where LibreOffice reference filenames lost or incorrectly modified their file extension after users added spaces to the name.

Problem

When a reference filename contained additional spaces (for example "document .odt" or trailing spaces around the extension), the extension-parsing/sanitization logic could treat the extension as part of the base name or otherwise corrupt the extension. This caused LibreOffice references to be invalid or not recognized.

What I changed

- Normalize and sanitize filenames so spaces around the extension are trimmed before parsing the extension.
- Ensure the file extension is preserved and handled consistently when creating/updating LibreOffice references.
- Added unit tests covering cases with leading/trailing spaces, spaces before the dot, multiple spaces, and filenames without extensions.

Testing

- New unit tests added to cover all edge cases with spaces and extensions.
- Manual verification: created and opened references in LibreOffice with names containing spaces; extensions are preserved and files open as expected.

Notes

- This is a non-breaking fix; existing references remain unchanged.
- If desired, we can add a migration step later to normalize any existing filenames that currently have incorrect extensions.

Summary

This PR applies creational design patterns and small API improvements to enhance code readability, configurability and intent clarity:

- Introduces Builder patterns for constructing complex objects with optional parameters.
- Replaces direct LinkedFile constructors with descriptive static factory methods to clarify intent (of, fromUrl).
- Adds minor API hardening (Objects.requireNonNull) and improves javadoc/comments for clarity.
- Keeps backward compatibility where reasonable and marks the older multi-arg BibDatabaseContext constructor as @Deprecated.

Key changes

- AutoCompletionTextInputBinding (jabgui/src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/autocompleter/AutoCompletionTextInputBinding.java)
  - Added a fluent Builder<T> to configure and create AutoCompletionTextInputBinding instances (converter, input analyzer, showOnFocus).
  - Updated convenience autoComplete(...) methods to delegate to the Builder, improving readability and extensibility.
  - Added Objects import and improved javadoc for class and methods.

- BibDatabaseContext (jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/model/database/BibDatabaseContext.java)
  - Added a Builder to create BibDatabaseContext instances with optional database, metadata, path and location.
  - Replaced some @NonNull parameter annotations with explicit Objects.requireNonNull checks for clearer runtime errors.
  - Marked the 3-arg constructor (database, metadata, path) as @Deprecated and made the 4-arg constructor private to direct construction through the Builder.
  - Minor javadoc formatting and method signature cleanups.

- LinkedFile usage updates
  - Replaced direct LinkedFile constructor invocations with descriptive static factory methods:
    - LinkedFile.of(...) used in AutoSetFileLinksUtil and ExternalFilesEntryLinker.
    - LinkedFile.fromUrl(...) used in DownloadFullTextAction.
  - These changes make the creation site intent clearer and improve API usability.

- Misc
  - Added a small IntelliJ inspection profile (.idea/inspectionProfiles/Project_Default.xml).
  - Updated submodule pointers under jablib resources (csl-locales, csl-styles, abbrv).

Why

- Builder pattern: simplifies construction when multiple optional parameters or sensible defaults exist; improves readability and makes future extension easier.
- Static factory methods for LinkedFile: improve expressiveness and hide constructor details.
- Non-null checks: fail-fast behavior for incorrect usage.

Testing

1. Build the project: ./gradlew build
2. Run unit tests: ./gradlew test
3. Generate javadoc to verify there are no warnings for modified files: ./gradlew javadoc
4. Verify LinkedFile instances are created via LinkedFile.of(...) / LinkedFile.fromUrl(...).

The new tests validate parsing and storage behavior of Abbreviation/JournalAbbreviationRepository and exercise the view model logic to ensure correct UI-model interactions and file IO behavior. No production code changes are included in this PR; it focuses on increasing test coverage for the journals feature.

Summary

This PR fixes broken middle-button paste behavior when running under X (X11). Middle-click paste should now correctly insert the PRIMARY selection into the focused window/application.

Problem

Users reported that middle-button paste did not work or pasted incorrect/empty contents in X sessions. The root cause was incorrect handling of the X selection transfer and event timing, which could result in missed or stale selection data.

What this change does

- Properly requests and converts the PRIMARY selection from the X server when a middle-button paste is triggered.
- Ensures the paste is performed after the selection data is received (avoids race conditions where the paste ran before data was available).
- Handles selection ownership and fallbacks more robustly so that the expected clipboard contents are inserted.
- Keeps behavior unchanged for non-X backends (no regressions for Wayland).

Testing

- Manually tested on X11 with common X clients (terminal, text editors, web browsers) to verify that middle-click now pastes the PRIMARY selection reliably.
- Verified that other mouse-click behaviors and clipboard interactions are unaffected.

Notes

- This is a targeted fix for X11 environments. If you see any edge cases with specific applications or complex clipboard managers, please open an issue with reproduction steps and logs.

Fixes: Middle-button paste not working in X (PRIMARY selection handling and timing).

text:
Motivation

Quick workaround for issue #8126: some users intermittently failed to fetch resources (DOI/IEEE) due to SSL certificate validation errors. To reduce these failures we apply a global bypass for SSL verification early during application startup.

What changed

- Call URLDownload.bypassSSLVerification() once at startup in JabRefMain.start().
- Removed scattered calls to URLDownload.bypassSSLVerification() from multiple places where they were previously invoked (IEEE, MrDLibFetcher, ZbMATH, Version and other fetchers).
- Removed an automatic bypass in LinkedFileViewModel that would have been triggered after user confirmation; the confirmation dialog still appears but no longer toggles global bypass there.
- Cleaned up unnecessary imports related to URLDownload in the modified files.

Files modified (high level)

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/JabRefMain.java: add global URLDownload.bypassSSLVerification() on startup.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/LinkedFileViewModel.java: stop enabling global bypass after user confirmation.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/IEEE.java: removed local bypass call.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/MrDLibFetcher.java: removed local bypass call.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/ZbMATH.java: removed local bypass calls and unused import.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/util/Version.java: removed local bypass call and unused import.

Notes & implications

- This is an application-wide, global workaround that disables SSL verification for URLDownload. It reduces failures fetching from DOI/IEEE/ZbMATH and when checking for new versions, but it weakens SSL security globally. This is intended as a short-term measure to improve reliability while a proper fix is developed.
- A better long-term solution should handle certificate validation per-connection, allow trusting specific certificates/hosts, or fix the underlying certificate/path issues on affected servers.

Testing

- Manual testing performed for the main fetch/use cases described in the issue (DOI/IEEE fetches and version check).

Follow-up

- Track issue #8126 for a secure, long-term solution.
- Consider documenting this temporary behavior in the changelog and user documentation so users are aware of the trade-off.

Checklist

- [ ] CHANGELOG update (if applicable)
- [ ] Add tests (if applicable)
- [x] Manually tested changed features in running JabRef
- [ ] Update documentation (if applicable)

Improve ArXiv fetcher title handling and add tests

- Apply normalization to titles when building queries and when matching results: remove braces around capitalized words (handles nested braces like {{Word}} -> Word). This increases matching robustness for titles that use LaTeX-style curly braces.
- Added new utility methods in StringUtil:
  - removeAllBraces(String): remove all curly braces from a string.
  - removeBracesAroundCapitalizedWords(String): iteratively strip pairs of braces around capitalized words.
  - removeSingleBracesAroundCapitalizedWords(String): helper used by the above, and a regex pattern to find braced capitalized words.
- Updated ArXiv fetcher to map title through StringUtil.removeBracesAroundCapitalizedWords when constructing the search query and when comparing fetched arXiv titles against the entry title.
- Added tests in ArXivTest: two tests verifying findFullText works for titles without curly braces and for titles with curly braces around capitalized words. Also simplified JUnit imports to a wildcard import.

- src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/ArXivTest.java: added tests and import cleanup.

Notes:
- The change improves matching for common bibtex/title bracing usage. A debug println(query) was introduced in ArXiv.java (may be removed later).

text:
Fix arXiv HTML download redirect and improve MIME type detection

What changed
- Properly handle HTTP redirects when determining MIME type so arXiv (and similar services) no longer report HTML for the original URL and cause downloading the HTML page instead of the PDF.
- URLDownload.getMimeType() now returns Optional<String> and performs a HEAD request following Location headers manually (with a retry limit) because Unirest only follows redirects for GET. It also falls back to GET and to URLConnection content type when needed.
- Configure Unirest once (followRedirects, cookie management, default User-Agent) and add a MAX_RETRIES constant for redirect handling.
- Improve related methods to use Optional (isMimeType, inferFileTypeFromMimeType) and small bugfixes in openConnection() to properly disconnect and handle redirects/errors.
- Update error classification in openConnection() so client vs server exceptions are thrown correctly.

Tests & dependencies
- Add wiremock-standalone as a test dependency and introduce WireMock-based tests to cover redirects and content-type behavior (URLDownloadTest.redirectWorks and updated DownloadLinkedFileActionTest). Tests start/stop WireMock servers and stub HEAD/GET responses for HTML/pdf/redirect scenarios.

Other
- Updated CHANGELOG with a note referencing the fixed issue.
- Small refactor: inferFileTypeFromMimeType simplified to use Optional chaining, and a typo fix in a comment.

Why
- Previously a 301/302 redirect from an arXiv link caused the initial HEAD/GET to return HTML content-type for the original URL, leading JabRef to download HTML pages instead of the intended PDF. By following Location headers for HEAD (and falling back to GET/URLConnection) we reliably determine the final resource MIME type and avoid downloading HTML when a PDF is available.

Closes #4913

Closes #10560

Summary
- Replace the plain text Keywords editor with a GemsFX TagsField UI so keywords are displayed and edited as tags.
- Adds a dedicated KeywordsEditor view and a KeywordsEditorViewModel to handle binding, suggestions and serialization.

What I changed
- UI & view:
  - Added KeywordsEditor.fxml which contains a TagsField for keywords.
  - Implemented KeywordsEditor (JavaFX control) that loads the FXML, configures the TagsField (cell factory, tag view, suggestions, converter, matcher, comparator) and binds tags bidirectionally to the view model.
  - Tags show a remove icon and provide a context menu with Copy, Cut and Delete actions.
- View model & logic:
  - Added KeywordsEditorViewModel to manage the Keyword list property, convert between Keyword and String, provide suggestions, and serialize/parse the field text.
  - Added KeywordList.serialize(List<Keyword>, Character) to support converting the tag list back into the keyword string using the configured separator.
- Integration:
  - FieldEditors now constructs the new KeywordsEditor (updated constructor signature).
- Changelog:
  - Noted that keywords are now displayed as tags in CHANGELOG.md.

Files touched
- Added/modified:
  - src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/KeywordsEditor.java (new JavaFX control)
  - src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/KeywordsEditorViewModel.java (new view model)
  - src/main/java/org/jabref/model/entry/KeywordList.java (added serialize)
  - src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/FieldEditors.java (updated KeywordsEditor instantiation)
  - src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/KeywordsEditor.fxml (new FXML)
  - CHANGELOG.md (user-facing note)

Behavioral notes
- Suggestions are provided from the existing SuggestionProvider and displayed in the TagsField; the currently typed value is included as the first suggestion if missing.
- Tags are ordered using a comparator and the TagsField is configured to create new Keyword instances from free text.
- The tag context menu supports Copy, Cut (copy + remove) and Delete; copy/cut send text to the clipboard and show a short notification.

- Manual testing performed and screenshot added to the PR description.
- Unit tests were not included in this change; adding tests can be considered in a follow-up.
- Documentation updates (developer/user docs) were not included; please update docs if necessary for contributors or plugin integrators.

This change improves usability of the Keywords field by making keywords visible and easily manageable as tags.
