text:
Add CI deployment workflow and packaging resources

This PR introduces a complete build and deployment setup for producing native installers and portable distributions for Linux, Windows and macOS via GitHub Actions and Gradle packaging tasks. Main highlights:

- GitHub Actions workflow (.github/workflows/deployment.yml)
  - Matrix build for ubuntu-latest, windows-latest and macOS-latest
  - Uses GitVersion to derive version info and sets up Java 15 for builds
  - Builds runtime image (jlinkZip) and native installers (jpackage)
  - macOS specific steps: codesign, notarization, dmg/pkg creation and stapling
  - Produces portable archives and uploads artifacts per-platform
  - Optional deployment to builds.jabref.org via rsync when secrets are present

- Gradle build configuration (build.gradle)
  - Application and packaging configuration with jlink/jpackage
  - Per-OS installer options (msi for Windows, rpm/deb-like options for Linux, dmg/pkg handling for macOS)
  - Tasks to generate ANTLR/XJC sources, bundle LibreOffice jars, pre-download dependencies and run JMH
  - Dependency management and dependencyUpdates checks with rules to exclude unstable versions
  - Jacoco merge/reporting and test task configuration
  - Various module exports/opens and merged module customizations to support modular runtime image

- macOS resources (buildres/mac)
  - Entitlements for app signing (myapp.entitlements and myapp.entitlements duplicate at repo root)
  - DMG layout script (JabRef-dmg-setup.scpt) and other helper files
  - ICNS placeholders and background images

- Windows resources (buildres/windows)
  - post-image WiX script (JabRef-post-image.wsf) to set up installer registry entries and banner

- Icon tooling script (src/main/resources/icons/svg2icns.sh)
  - Script to generate .icns from SVG sources (uses svg2png + iconutil)

Notes / things to review
- macOS signing identities and notarization rely on repository secrets (OSX_SIGNING_CERT, OSX_NOTARIZATION_APP_USERNAME/PWD)
- The workflow and Gradle configuration use Java 15 (EA builds) — confirm JDK availability and compatibility
- Some resource files are placeholders (binary icns/png content in repository listed as binary blobs)
- There are two entitlements files (buildres/mac/myapp.entitlements and myapp.entitlements) containing the same content; consider deduplicating

This PR lays the foundation for automated cross-platform packaging and release artifact deployment. Please review signing/notarization steps and secret handling before enabling automatic deploys.

text:
Summary

Fix recognition and handling of icons from Material Design Icons (MDI). Previously, icons using MDI names (for example, "mdi-home" or other "mdi-" prefixed names and some recent variant names) were not detected by the icon parser and therefore failed to render or fell back incorrectly.

What I changed

- Updated the icon recognition logic to accept MDI naming patterns (including common prefixes/suffixes and alias variants).
- Added an alias/mapping layer to normalize MDI names to the internal icon identifiers used by our renderer.
- Implemented a fallback loader that will use @mdi/font or @mdi/js SVG paths when available, so MDI icons render even if the standard icon set isn’t present.
- Added unit tests and integration tests covering common MDI names, aliases, and edge cases to prevent regressions.
- Updated documentation to mention support for MDI icons and how to enable the @mdi packages if desired.
- Bumped/added optional dependencies for MDI packages where appropriate (documented as opt-in in README).

Why this fixes the issue

The previous name-parsing regex and mapping only covered our original icon set. MDI names use slightly different conventions (prefixes, multi-word tokens, and some newer variant names). Normalizing these names and supporting the MDI asset loaders ensures those icons are recognized and rendered correctly.

Testing

- Unit tests: added tests for recognition and normalization of MDI names.
- Integration: verified rendering with both @mdi/font (webfont) and @mdi/js (SVG path) in a sample page.
- Manual verification: checked common icons (mdi-home, mdi-account, mdi-account-outline, etc.) render as expected.

Migration / Compatibility notes

- No breaking changes to existing icon names or behavior for current users.
- If you rely on MDI icons, you may need to install/enable @mdi/font or @mdi/js as documented (these are optional). If not installed, the system will attempt the best available fallback.

Files changed (high level)

- icon-parser.* — updated recognition/normalization logic
- mdi-mapping.* — new mapping/alias helpers
- loaders/mdi-loader.* — optional loader for @mdi/font and @mdi/js
- tests/mdi-*.spec.* — tests for the new behavior
- docs/icons.md — documentation for MDI support

If you want, I can split the mapping and loader into a separate optional package to keep core bundle size smaller.

text:
Add FieldMerger implementations for GROUPS and KEYWORDS used by the new merge dialog

- GroupMerger
  - Merges values for StandardField.GROUPS.
  - Handles empty/blank inputs (returns the other or empty string appropriately).
  - Trims both inputs, splits on common separators (semicolon or comma + optional whitespace) using a regex, trims each token, removes duplicates and joins the result with a canonical ", " separator.

- KeywordMerger
  - Merges values for StandardField.KEYWORDS using BibEntryPreferences and KeywordList.
  - Attempts to detect a single non-alphanumeric/non-whitespace character used as keyword separator in each input.
  - Validates that at most one separator type is used across the inputs; if multiple different separators are found an IllegalArgumentException is thrown.
  - Updates bibEntryPreferences with the detected separator and delegates merging to KeywordList.merge, returning the merged keywords as a string using the chosen delimiter.
  - detectSeparator reports detailed IllegalArgumentException messages when multiple separators are present in a single input or when no valid separator is found.

These additions centralize and standardize merging logic for groups and keywords in the merge dialog, including normalization (trimming/deduplication) and separator handling/validation for keywords.

Summary:
This PR ensures that PDFs (and other files) referenced by entries in a source .bib are properly copied into the destination when entries are copied or moved between .bib files. It fixes cases where the entry's 'file' field pointed to an asset that was not transferred or where the path was left invalid after the move.

What changed:
- Copy files referenced in the BibTeX 'file' field when copying/moving entries between .bib files.
- Resolve both absolute and relative paths from the source .bib location, and copy files into the target .bib's directory (or configured files directory).
- Update the entry's 'file' field to point to the new relative path in the destination .bib.
- Avoid overwriting existing files in the destination directory by adding a numeric suffix to colliding filenames (e.g. 'paper.pdf' -> 'paper (1).pdf').
- Properly handle multiple files listed in a single 'file' field (copy each and update the field accordingly).
- Skip copying for non-local URIs (http/doi) and log/notify missing files instead of failing.
- Added a CLI/command option to control this behavior (can be disabled if desired).

Tests and validation:
- Unit tests added for path resolution, file copying, collision handling, and updating of the 'file' field.
- Integration tests that copy entries between test .bib files and verify files exist and paths were updated.

Compatibility & notes:
- Default behavior preserves previous functionality but now includes associated files when enabled. The copy-files option can be turned off to maintain older behavior.
- Requires write permission in the destination directory; missing source files are reported but do not abort the operation.

This change should make moving or sharing entries much safer by keeping their associated PDFs intact and ensuring .bib entries remain consistent.

Summary

Fixes issue #5555 where status popups could show incorrect content, remain visible when they should dismiss, or be mis-positioned in certain edge cases.

What I changed

- Fixed popup lifecycle so status updates always propagate to visible popups and stale content is not displayed.
- Corrected event handling for open/close commands to prevent popups from getting stuck.
- Adjusted positioning logic and CSS z-index so popups render in the correct place and above other UI layers.
- Added debounce/throttle to rapid status updates to avoid flicker and duplicate popups.
- Added unit/integration tests covering the lifecycle, update, and dismissal scenarios.

Why this is needed

Users were seeing confusing or persistent status popups under certain timing conditions. This patch makes popup behavior deterministic and consistent across platforms.

How to test

1. Reproduce the original issue steps from #5555 (rapid status updates / opening and closing popups). Verify the popup content is correct and updates as expected.
2. Test opening and closing popups rapidly; they should not get stuck or duplicate.
3. Verify positioning across different screen sizes and stacking contexts.
4. Run the test suite; new tests should pass.

Notes

- No API changes.
- Closes #5555.

Summary:
Extend RIS import functionality to support mapping and importing of multiple fields for a single target field. This change enables importing repeated or related RIS tags into compound or multi-value fields in the application.

What this PR does:
- Enhances the RIS parser to recognize and aggregate multiple occurrences of the same RIS tag or related tags.
- Adds support for mapping multiple incoming fields to a single target field (e.g., multiple author roles, multiple keywords, or combined institution/address fields).
- Updates the import mapping configuration and UI (if applicable) to allow selecting multiple source tags for a field mapping.
- Adds validation and normalization to correctly handle duplicates, ordering, and empty values.
- Includes unit/integration tests covering common scenarios: multiple authors, multiple keywords, repeated tags, and mixed single/multi-value targets.

Motivation:
RIS files commonly contain repeated tags or several tags that should be combined into one multi-value field in our system. Previously we only supported a one-to-one mapping which caused loss of data or required manual post-processing. This change preserves all relevant metadata during import and improves fidelity of imported records.

Compatibility and migration:
- Existing import mappings remain valid. If a mapping targets a single source tag, behavior is unchanged.
- New mappings may specify multiple source tags; these will be concatenated or stored as multi-value depending on the target field type.
- No database schema changes are required (unless the target field is being migrated from single- to multi-value; that would be a separate migration and is not included here).

Testing notes:
- Added tests for RIS files with repeated TY/AU/KW tags and for cases where different tags should map to the same target field.
- Manual testing performed with representative RIS exports to ensure ordering and deduplication behave as expected.

Notes / Future work:
- Consider exposing more advanced mapping rules (e.g., separators, deduplication toggles, per-mapping normalization) in the UI.
- Evaluate performance on very large RIS files and optimize aggregation logic if necessary.

Summary

Fixes a bug where several library-related actions remained enabled even when no libraries were open, which could lead to errors or confusing UI state. Actions that require an open library are now disabled when there is no active library.

What I changed

- Updated the enablement logic for library-dependent actions (menu items, toolbar buttons, and command handlers) to check for an active/open library before enabling.
- Added a defensive early-return in handlers for actions that require a library to avoid runtime errors if invoked unexpectedly.
- Ensured keyboard shortcuts reflect the updated enablement state.
- Added/updated unit and/or integration tests to cover the disabled state when no libraries are open.

Actions affected (examples)

- Save / Save As
- Close Library
- Export / Import within a library
- Add / Remove items that operate on current library
- Search-scoped-to-library

Behavioral changes

- When no library is open, the above actions are disabled in menus and toolbars and will not run if triggered programmatically.
- When a library is opened, the actions are re-enabled immediately.

Testing

- Automated tests added to assert actions are disabled with zero libraries and enabled after opening a library.
- Manual test steps:
  1. Start the app with no libraries open.
  2. Verify library-dependent menu items and toolbar buttons are disabled.
  3. Try keyboard shortcuts for those actions — they should be inactive.
  4. Open a library and verify the actions become enabled and function normally.

Notes

- This change improves UX and prevents null/invalid-state errors when users operate the app without any libraries open.
- If there are any other actions you want covered by the same enablement check, mention them and I can extend the list/tests.

text:
Add option to sync app theme with OS system preference (Light/Dark)

Summary
- Implements a new preference allowing JabRef to follow the operating system's light/dark theme preference.
- When enabled, JabRef will automatically switch between the built-in Light and Dark themes and keep them in sync with the OS. The setting supports live updates while the app runs.

What changed
- UI: Added checkbox and related controls to General preferences (GeneralTab.fxml) and a "Get more themes..." link.
- Preferences & model: Persisted new setting in WorkspacePreferences and JabRefPreferences (THEME_SYNC_OS), with bindings in GeneralTabViewModel and GeneralTab.
- Theme handling: ThemeManager now integrates OsThemeDetector to listen for OS theme changes and updates scenes/web engines; added live reloading/watch support for additional stylesheets.
- Wiring: GeneralTab/GeneralTabViewModel validation, import/browse helpers and bindings updated to handle custom and synchronized themes.
- Build: Added runtime dependency for OS theme detection (jSystemThemeDetector) and hooked theme-related resources into the build.

Files of interest
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preferences/general/GeneralTab.fxml
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preferences/general/GeneralTab.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preferences/general/GeneralTabViewModel.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/theme/ThemeManager.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/preferences/JabRefPreferences.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/preferences/WorkspacePreferences.java
- build.gradle (dependency + javafx/version wiring)

User notes
- Default behaviour remains unchanged (theme sync disabled). Enable "Use System Preference" in Preferences → General to opt in.
- Theme changes are applied live; some dialogs may need to be reopened to pick up font-size changes.

Closes: #8729

Summary

This PR changes the behavior of the file-link deletion dialog and fixes a bug where files were accidentally deleted when the user cancelled the dialog. It also makes the LinkedFileViewModel more testable by allowing a DialogService to be injected and adds unit tests covering the different dialog outcomes.

What I changed

- Change default dialog action: The default (first) dialog option when removing a file link is now "Remove from entry" instead of deleting the file from disk. This avoids accidentally deleting users' files. (LinkedFileViewModel.java)
- Fix cancel behavior and return semantics: The delete() method now returns false when the file is not found or when the dialog was cancelled; previously it always returned true, which led to linked files being removed despite a cancel. (LinkedFileViewModel.java)
- Make DialogService injectable: Added a protected constructor overload to LinkedFileViewModel that accepts a DialogService, and the public constructor delegates to it. This enables mocking/stubbing the dialog in unit tests. (LinkedFileViewModel.java)
- Tests: Added LinkedFileViewModelTest with cases for missing file, choosing "Remove from entry", choosing "Delete from disk", deleting when file missing, and cancelling. The tests verify both return values and file-system effects. (LinkedFileViewModelTest.java)
- CHANGELOG: Documented the behavior change and the bug fix. (CHANGELOG.md)

Files modified

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/LinkedFileViewModel.java
- src/test/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/LinkedFileViewModelTest.java (new)
- CHANGELOG.md

Issue fixed

- Fixes #3679: default dialog option changed to "Remove from entry" (no longer defaults to deleting file from disk).
- Fixed bug where clicking Cancel still removed file links from entries.

Notes

- The tests use a mocked DialogService to simulate the different button choices. The added constructor makes this possible.
- Behavior: when the user explicitly chooses to delete the file from disk, the file is deleted and delete() returns true. When the user chooses remove-from-entry, the link is removed and delete() returns true. If the dialog is cancelled or the file is missing, delete() returns false and appropriate dialogs or logs are shown.

This pull request addresses a NullPointerException (NPE) that occurs during search tests in JabRef. The issue arises because multiple tests share the same index path, and the index is closed in a background thread, leading to potential race conditions. To resolve this, the following changes have been made:

1. Added `@TempDir` annotation to provide a unique temporary directory for each test, ensuring that tests do not interfere with each other's indices.
2. Introduced a `closeAndWait` method in the `LuceneManager` and related classes to ensure that the index is fully closed before the next test starts. This method waits for the background task to complete, preventing race conditions.

These changes should prevent the NPE and ensure that tests run reliably without interfering with each other's indices.

text:
Add automatic detection and display of unlinked files in the Entry Editor

Summary
- Introduces a new preference and UI toggle to automatically search for and show unlinked files when an entry is opened in the entry editor.
- Implements background lookup of candidate files and shows them in the linked-files editor without immediately serializing them to the entry (they are marked as "automatically found").

Behavior
- When the new preference "Automatically search and show unlinked files in the entry editor" is enabled, opening the entry editor triggers a background search for likely associated but not-yet-linked files for that entry.
- Found files are added to the linked-files list and marked as automatically found. These automatically found files are not included when serializing the entry's file field (so they are only suggestions until the user keeps them).
- The lookup runs asynchronously via BackgroundTask/TaskExecutor to avoid blocking the UI. File-system errors are shown via the dialog service.

Persistence & UI
- A new checkbox was added to the Entry Editor preferences UI (EntryEditorTab.fxml) and bound through EntryEditorTab/EntryEditorTabViewModel.
- The setting is persisted via Preferences (JabRefPreferences) under the existing key autoLinkFilesEnabled and defaults are wired correctly.

Files changed (key highlights)
- Added/updated EntryEditorPreferences (Java): new property and getters/setters for autoLink files.
- LinkedFilesEditorViewModel: added logic to kick off a background search when binding to an entry, convert found files into LinkedFileViewModel instances, mark them as automatically found, and ensure only non-automatic files are serialized.
- EntryEditorTab.fxml / EntryEditorTab.java / EntryEditorTabViewModel.java: added the preferences control, wiring and store/set logic.
- JabRefPreferences: ensures the preference is read/written and wired to EntryEditorPreferences.
- l10n JabRef_en.properties: added UI text for the new checkbox.

Rationale
- Improves usability by surfacing likely local files (e.g. PDF) related to the opened entry without forcing immediate linking. Users can more easily review and accept suggested links.

Notes / Implementation details
- The automatic search respects existing FilePreferences, database file directories and the existing AutoSetFileLinksUtil logic to find candidate files.
- Found files are marked as automatically found (LinkedFileViewModel.markAsAutomaticallyFound) so they are shown but not serialized until user action.
- Errors reading the file system are handled and reported via the dialog service.

Refactor and centralize shared-database UI and preferences

This PR refactors how JabRef handles shared (DBMS-backed) databases by introducing a dedicated SharedDatabaseUIManager and related preference and model updates. - Add SharedDatabaseUIManager to centralize UI-related behavior for shared database operations and dialogs.
- Update OpenSharedDatabaseDialog to use the new manager and to read/write connection settings consistently.
- Move DBMS connection storage/handling into DBMSConnectionProperties and expose access via JabRefPreferences. This makes connection properties a first-class model and simplifies persistence.
- Update JabRefGUI and JabRefFrame to obtain shared-database UI functionality through the new manager instead of scattered code paths.
- Update JabRefPreferences to include getters/setters for DBMSConnectionProperties and any new preference keys used by the manager/dialog.
- Update CHANGELOG.md with a short entry describing the refactor.

Why
- Centralizing shared-database UI logic reduces duplication and makes intent clearer.
- Introducing DBMSConnectionProperties as a model simplifies handling and persistence of connection info.
- These changes pave the way for future features (multiple saved connections, improved validation, enhanced UI flows) with minimal disruption.

Notes for reviewers
- No functional change to shared-database workflows is intended; behavior should remain the same from an end-user perspective.
- Verify that existing saved connection preferences are still read correctly and that opening a shared database functions as before.
- The refactor concentrates UI responsibility in SharedDatabaseUIManager — please check dialog wiring and lifecycle interactions in JabRefFrame/JabRefGUI.

Fix: show found entries when dropping a PDF that contains XMP metadata

What this PR does
- Ensures that when a user drags-and-drops a PDF file containing XMP metadata, the application parses the XMP and displays the discovered entries in the UI.
- Previously, PDFs with embedded XMP metadata were not producing visible results on drop; this change makes those entries visible and selectable.

Implementation notes
- Added XMP extraction/parsing on file-drop handling pipeline and integrated the parsed entries into the existing result rendering flow.
- Updated the UI component to render found entries immediately after parsing, including handling of multiple entries and missing fields.
- Added unit/integration tests to cover PDF drop behavior, XMP parsing, and UI rendering of found entries.
- Added defensive handling and a clear fallback when no XMP metadata is present or it cannot be parsed.

How to test
1. Drag-and-drop a PDF that contains XMP metadata into the application.
2. Confirm that the parsed entries are displayed in the results list.
3. Try PDFs without XMP metadata to verify the fallback behavior remains unchanged.

Notes
- This change is limited to the file-drop/XMP parsing path and does not affect existing importers for other formats.
- Error logging was added for malformed XMP but errors are surfaced non-blockingly so the UI remains responsive.

text:
Fix #2336 — Ensure BackupManager shutdown works reliably

Summary
- Fixes an issue where JabRef would not always close properly via the Quit menu (issue #2336). The BackupManager is now always registered correctly and shutdown behaves as expected.

What I changed
- BackupManager now registers itself as a listener in its constructor, ensuring it is always registered with the BibDatabaseContext event bus.
- JabRefFrame: always starts a BackupManager for a BibDatabaseContext (removed the earlier readyForBackup check). This avoids cases where a manager was not created/registered and therefore not shut down.
- Backup lifecycle: BackupManager now determines the backup path on demand (using a new getDatabasePath() method on BibDatabaseContext) and performs/delete backup files via helper methods. This removes former reliance on stored File fields and makes shutdown/delete behavior robust.
- Shutdown logic: static shutdown(...) now calls the instance shutdown method for matching instances and removes them from runningInstances. The instance shutdown unregisters listeners, shuts down the executor, and deletes the backup file if present.

text:
Closes #10926

Summary

This PR converts the existing "Custom API key" UI from a ComboBox + TextField + CheckBox to a editable TableView with three columns: Catalog (name), Key, and Use Custom Key. The change improves accessibility and makes the list of API keys easier to scan and edit.

What I changed

- Replaced the ComboBox/TextField/CheckBox UI with a TableView in the web search preferences FXML (WebSearchTab.fxml).
- Updated WebSearchTab.java to work with a TableView and TableColumns instead of a ComboBox and separate controls:
  - Added TableView and TableColumn bindings for name, key and use properties.
  - Installed a ViewModelTableRowFactory for row behavior and selection handling.
  - Wired up editable cells: name (read-only), key (editable text cell), use (editable checkbox cell).
  - Bound the "Check connection" button to the selected fetcher key's use property (disabled when not using custom key).
  - Selection now updates the viewModel.selectedApiKeyProperty.
  - Persisted the existing logic to select the first item when the list changes.
- Exposed nameProperty() in FetcherApiKey so the TableColumn can bind to it.
- Added a short note to CHANGELOG.md describing the UI change.

Files touched

- CHANGELOG.md — added entry about converting the custom API key list to a table.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preferences/websearch/WebSearchTab.fxml — replaced HBox controls with a TableView and configured columns.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preferences/websearch/WebSearchTab.java — switched controller logic to TableView/columns; cell factories; property bindings; selection handling.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/preferences/FetcherApiKey.java — added nameProperty() accessor.

Behavioral notes / current limitation

- The TableView makes the Key column editable even when the "Use Custom Key" checkbox for a row is unchecked. Previously the key TextField was disabled when "Use Custom Key" was false. I did not find an efficient way to disable editing of a specific cell based on the corresponding row's use property while keeping the table editable (row-level/column-level editing in JavaFX is global). I left the Key editable at all times so users can prepare keys in advance; the Check connection button remains disabled unless "Use Custom Key" is checked for the selected row. I'm open to feedback or suggestions on a better approach to conditionally disable editing per-row.

Testing notes

- Manually tested in a running JabRef instance.
- Steps to verify:
  1. Preferences -> Web search -> Custom API key section should show a table with Catalog, Key and Use Custom Key columns.
  2. Selecting a row binds selection to the view model; the "Check connection" button is enabled only when "Use Custom Key" is checked for the selected item.
  3. Edit the Key cell and press Return to commit the change (the FXML label reminds users to press Return to commit changes).
  4. Ensure persist API keys toggle and catalog list behavior still work as before.

Notes

- No automated tests were added for the UI change.
- Screenshot included in the issue/PR description to show the new layout.

If you'd like, I can follow up with an attempt to prevent editing of the Key cell when "Use Custom Key" is false (for example, by adding a custom cell factory that checks the row's useProperty and prevents edits), but I wanted to open the PR to gather feedback on the current approach first.

Testing
- Manually tested the affected dialogs and preferences panels in a running JabRef instance; lists now display alphabetically and behavior is unchanged apart from ordering.

No user-facing API changes; purely UI ordering improvements.

text:
Add Field Presence Consistency Check feature and TXT report writer

This PR introduces a new BibliographyConsistencyCheck that analyzes a list of BibEntry objects grouped by entry type and reports fields that are not present in all entries of the same type. For each entry type it computes: (a) the set of fields present in any entry, (b) the set of fields present in all entries, and (c) the entries that differ from the common field set. Results are returned via BibliographyConsistencyCheck.Result and EntryTypeResult records.

A plain-text report writer (BibliographyConsistencyCheckResultTxtWriter) formats and writes the findings as aligned tables with configurable column widths and a legend of symbols. The writer supports a porcelain mode that suppresses human-readable headers/legend for machine consumption. Column widths are computed to correctly display long citation keys and to keep the table aligned. The writer reuses a FieldComparatorStack (using BibEntryByCitationKeyComparator and BibEntryByFieldsComparator) to produce stable, predictable ordering of differing entries.

Also included are comparator implementations (BibEntryByCitationKeyComparator, BibEntryByFieldsComparator) and comprehensive unit tests (BibliographyConsistencyCheckResultTxtWriterTest) covering multiple scenarios: simple/different/complex libraries, very long citation keys, porcelain vs non-porcelain output, and a disabled manual test for local report generation. Localization keys for the check and legend are present in JabRef_en.properties.

The change is focused, well-tested, and adds no-op close() in the TXT writer for resource compatibility. This prepares the codebase for exporting field-presence consistency reports (TXT and CSV writers can be used together) and for integration with CLI or UI consistency-check flows.

- Follow-up to: #8361
- Related: #8406

text:
Summary

Enable downloading of linked files reported by identifier (ID) fetchers. When an ID fetcher (e.g. DOI/PMID-based importer) returns links to files, JabRef now downloads those files into the library file directory and attaches them to the fetched entry as linked files.

Fixes

- Fixes #9756
- Fixes https://github.com/JabRef/jabref-issue-melting-pot/issues/127

What changed

- The import flow for ID fetchers was extended to process linked-file information returned by the source and to download these files automatically (respecting JabRef file preferences).
- Downloaded files are saved into the configured file directory and corresponding LinkedFile entries are added to the BibEntry.
- The download process reports progress and handles failures gracefully (failed downloads are reported but do not block importing the entry).

Why

Some ID-based metadata sources provide direct links to PDFs or supplementary material. Previously these links were ignored; this change improves user experience by retrieving and attaching available files automatically during ID fetch.

Manual testing & artifacts

- Manually tested in running JabRef (screenshot included in PR description).

Notes for reviewers

- Please focus review on the fetcher import pipeline and the file-download/attachment logic to ensure it respects user file preferences and performs appropriate error handling.
- A changelog entry and additional automated tests should be added before release (not included in this PR).

Summary

This PR fixes several issues in the entry editor: re-enables the keyboard shortcuts for moving between entries when the entry editor is active and preserves/restores focus of text fields when switching between entries. Additionally it contains a few related cleanups (selection handling, focus helpers) and a safer startup catch in JabRefMain. This addresses the behaviour reported in #4104.

What I changed

- Re-enabled next/previous entry shortcuts inside the entry editor
  - Added handling for ENTRY_EDITOR_NEXT_ENTRY and ENTRY_EDITOR_PREVIOUS_ENTRY in EntryEditor to call panel.selectNextEntry()/selectPreviousEntry().
  - Updated default key bindings to use Alt+Down / Alt+Up for Entry editor next/previous entry (KeyBinding).
  - Updated CHANGELOG to document the new default shortcuts.

- Preserve focus of field editors when switching entries
  - FieldsEditorTab now detects which field child was focused before rebuilding the editor panel and restores focus after the new panel is set (using Platform.runLater).
  - FieldEditorFX: replaced requestFocus() with focus() which focuses the first meaningful child node, and added childIsFocused() to query whether any child is focused.
  - ControlHelper: added recursive childIsFocused(Parent) helper used by field editors.

- Fix selection logic when moving between entries
  - BasePanel.selectPreviousEntry() and selectNextEntry() now use clearAndSelect(currentIndex +/- 1) to ensure the selection is updated properly and that selection/focus behaviour remains consistent.

- Simplified/synchronized binding behavior in entry editor tabs
  - EntryEditorTab.notifyAboutFocus() and EntryEditor.setEntry(...) removed unnecessary DefaultTaskExecutor runnables so binding/notification happens directly on the FX thread, and added a small helper getSelectedTab(). This avoids some ordering/focus issues.

- Minor startup hardening
  - JabRefMain.start() wrapped in a try/catch that logs unexpected exceptions to avoid uncaught exceptions during startup.

Files changed (high level)
- CHANGELOG.md: documented the new default shortcuts and tidy up.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/JabRefMain.java: added top-level try/catch around startup flow.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/BasePanel.java: improved selectNext/Previous implementation.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/entryeditor/EntryEditor.java: added key handling for next/previous entry, removed deferred runnables, helper for selected tab.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/entryeditor/EntryEditorTab.java: removed DefaultTaskExecutor usage in notifyAboutFocus.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/entryeditor/FieldsEditorTab.java: remember and restore focused field across rebinds.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/FieldEditorFX.java: introduced focus() and childIsFocused() methods.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/keyboard/KeyBinding.java: changed default shortcuts for entry editor navigation to alt+up/down.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/util/ControlHelper.java: added childIsFocused(Parent) utility.

Why

- Shortcuts: users expect to be able to navigate entries using keyboard shortcuts while editing an entry. These had been effectively disabled in the editor; they are reactivated and given intuitive defaults (Alt+Up/Alt+Down).
- Focus preservation: when switching between entries in the editor, users expect the same text field to keep focus (or to be restored) so they can continue uninterrupted typing. Previously focus was lost when the tabs were rebuilt.
- Selection: clearer selection semantics (clearAndSelect) ensure selection changes behave consistently and trigger any selection listeners.
- Simpler threading: removing redundant runnables reduces the chance of ordering bugs and makes focus/notification deterministic.

Notes

- This PR fixes: #4104 (reactivate next/previous entry shortcuts in entry editor and preserve focus across entry switches).
- Manually tested in a running JabRef instance.

Please merge and do not squash the commits.

Fix crash when editing date fields in biblatex library mode (#8747)

Summary
- Fixes an uncaught exception that occurred when editing an entry's "date" field in biblatex library mode. See issue: #8747.

What I changed
- CHANGELOG.md: Added entry describing the fix.
- DateEditor.java: Wire up field validation for the date editor by creating an EditorValidator from PreferencesService. Constructor signature updated to accept PreferencesService.
- FieldEditors.java: Pass PreferencesService into DateEditor where it is created.
- DateEditorViewModel.java: Broadened the parse exception handling to fall back to the model Date parser if the formatter parsing fails.
- TemporalAccessorPicker.java:
  - Improved parsing robustness: try the configured DateTimeFormatter first, fall back to Date.parse(...). If input is blank, return null.
  - Preserve the editor text when the entered date is invalid instead of clearing it.
  - Guard getLocalDate against null TemporalAccessor.

Why
- The previous parsing/validation flow allowed an uncaught exception to propagate for certain inputs/formats in biblatex mode. Additionally, invalid inputs were being cleared from the editor which was confusing for users. This change ensures parsing falls back to the flexible Date parser, validation UI is configured, and invalid input is preserved so the user can correct it.

Behavioral notes / migration
- DateEditor constructor signature changed: callers must pass a PreferencesService instance (updated in FieldEditors in this PR).
- Users will see validation feedback in the date editor and will no longer experience a crash when entering dates in unsupported formats; invalid text will remain in the editor so it can be fixed.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/DateEditor.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/DateEditorViewModel.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/FieldEditors.java

Summary

- Add new Customize Entry Types dialog FXML (CustomizeEntryTypeDialog.fxml) to provide the UI for creating and editing custom entry types/fields.
- Refactor entry editor tabs and field-handling code:
  - Introduce abstract FieldsEditorTab that centralizes layout and preview integration for tabs that show field editors.
  - Implement OptionalFieldsTabBase (shared implementation) and add a new OptionalFields2Tab which extends it (label: "Optional fields 2").
  - Add OtherFieldsTab to show remaining/unknown fields not covered by known/optional/deprecated/custom tabs.
  - Improve determination of which fields are shown per tab and expose getShownFields()/requestFocus APIs to focus a specific field programmatically.
- EntryEditor changes:
  - Reworked tab creation and management: createTabs() builds the list of tabs and recalculateVisibleTabs() adds/removes tabs while avoiding UI animation glitches when changing visibility.
  - Added better subscription handling for entry type changes to update the visible tabs and update the type label.
  - Drag & drop handling improved to handle COPY/MOVE/LINK transfer modes (now using switch expressions) and to perform the appropriate file-link actions (copy/move/add) via ExternalFilesEntryLinker.
  - Fetcher menu wiring updated: builds menu from available entry-based fetchers and special-cases PDF-merge/Grobid fetcher to show opt-in dialog before running.
  - New helper methods and small UX improvements: setFocusToField(), navigation between preview styles, and safer behavior when preferences are not initialized (tests).

Why

- Reduce duplication across the different field tabs and centralize layout/preview logic.
- Provide an additional optional-fields tab to support more complex field layouts / preferences.
- Provide a dedicated "Other fields" tab to surface fields that are not part of the canonical entry type definition or configured custom tabs.
- Improve UX and robustness in the entry editor (drag & drop file handling, fetcher handling, dynamic tab visibility) and add the missing FXML for customizing entry types.

Notes

- The refactor keeps backwards compatibility for existing tabs but consolidates behavior into the new base classes.
- The code guards against uninitialized preferences (useful for headless/tests).
- Grobid opt-in flow is preserved for the PDF metadata fetcher wrapper.

Summary

This PR adds a timestamp validation step to Backupmanager for .bak files. Backupmanager will now detect and validate a timestamp present in the .bak filename (using the configured timestamp format). Files that do not contain a valid timestamp will be ignored and a warning will be logged.

What changed

- Added filename timestamp check when scanning .bak files.
- Timestamp format is configurable (falls back to the existing default format). Invalid or missing timestamps cause the file to be skipped, preventing incorrect ordering or accidental processing of non-backup files.
- Improved logging to report which files were ignored due to missing/invalid timestamps and why.
- Unit tests added/updated to cover valid and invalid timestamp cases.

Why this change

Previously .bak files without a clear timestamp could be picked up or ordered incorrectly. Verifying timestamps ensures backups are correctly identified and processed in the right order, reducing the chance of restoring the wrong state.

Compatibility and notes

- Default behavior remains unchanged for environments that already include timestamps in .bak filenames.
- The timestamp format can be configured; make sure to update configuration if your naming differs from the default.
- No breaking API changes; only alters file selection/validation logic.

Files/areas touched

- Backup scanning/validation logic
- Configuration for timestamp format
- Logging messages
- Unit tests

Follow-ups

- Consider adding an option to attempt to infer timestamp from file metadata as a fallback (not implemented in this PR).

Introduce MainTable UI component and update build wrapper

This PR introduces the MainTable class which implements the main entries table used in the UI and wires up selection, keyboard shortcuts, clipboard and drag-and-drop behaviour. It also includes the Gradle wrapper update to 6.3.

Key changes in MainTable.java:
- Implements a TableView for BibEntryTableViewModel with column creation from MainTableColumnFactory and persisted visual state via PersistenceVisualStateTable.
- Integrates with MainTableDataModel to display filtered/sorted entries and binds the table comparator to the model's comparator.
- Adds selection helpers: clearAndSelect, clearAndSelectFirst/Last, getEntryAt, getSelectedEntries and findEntry.
- Keyboard handling: ENTER to open/edit entry; support for mapped KeyBinding actions (SELECT_FIRST_ENTRY, SELECT_LAST_ENTRY, PASTE, COPY, CUT).
- Clipboard operations: copy, cut, paste using Globals.clipboardManager and panel insert/delete operations.
- Drag-and-drop support using ViewModelTableRowFactory handlers:
  - Drag detection stores entries in localDragboard and starts dragboard handshake.
  - Drag over/entered/exited visuals using ControlHelper pseudo-classes.
  - Drop handling supports importing files as new entries (drop top/bottom) or linking/moving/copying files to an entry (drop center). Uses ImportHandler and its linker for file operations.
- Listens for EntriesAddedEvent via EventBus to clear selection and select new entry on JavaFX thread.
- Context menu wired via RightClickMenu and supports double-click to edit.
- Uses styles from MainTable.css and supports multi-selection + column resize policy from preferences.

Other changes:
- gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties updated to use Gradle 6.3 distribution.

Notes for reviewers:
- Drag-and-drop logic distinguishes TOP/BOTTOM vs CENTER drop locations; verify UX for different platforms and modifier keys (MOVE/COPY/LINK semantics).
- Clipboard-related operations depend on Globals.clipboardManager and may need integration tests.

Summary

Ensure the group display is refreshed whenever the grouping configuration changes.

Problem

When a user changed the grouping criteria (for example group-by field or sort direction), the UI sometimes continued to show the old grouping layout until a separate refresh or navigation occurred. This caused stale group headers, incorrect item placement and confusing UX.

What I changed

- Detect changes to the grouping configuration and trigger a group display update/recompute when the grouping key or grouping options change.
- Add a single, targeted update path so that only group rendering/data aggregation is recomputed rather than forcing a full page reload or unrelated components to rerender.
- Added unit/integration tests to cover grouping changes and verify the UI updates correctly.

Files/areas touched

- Grouping logic/service/store: added change detection and emit update events.
- Group display component: subscribe to grouping change events and call the recompute/refresh routine.
- Tests: new tests that simulate grouping changes and assert the displayed groups update.

Why this fix

This makes grouping changes immediate and consistent for the user without heavy-handed rerenders. It fixes reported issues where groups remained stale after configuration changes.

Testing instructions

1. Open list view that supports grouping.
2. Change group-by field (and/or grouping options like direction).
3. Observe that group headers and member items refresh immediately to reflect the new grouping.
4. Run the test suite to confirm the newly added tests pass.

Notes

- The update is scoped to grouping-related data, minimizing performance impact.
- If you see any edge cases where groups are not updated, please include repro steps and sample data in the issue.

Summary
Fix saving files on network drives under macOS by changing the save strategy and adding a robust fallback for volumes that do not support atomic replace operations.

Problem
Saving files to network-mounted volumes (SMB/AFP/NFS) on macOS could fail or cause data loss. The root cause was the use of an atomic replace/write strategy that depended on behaviors (local temporary files and POSIX rename semantics) not guaranteed on network volumes. On some network mounts this resulted in errors or failed saves.

What this change does
- Writes temporary files next to the target file on the same volume to ensure rename/replace occurs on the same filesystem when possible.
- Falls back to a safe non-atomic write (overwrite in place) when the filesystem does not support atomic replace/rename semantics.
- Adds macOS-specific checks to detect remote/network volumes and choose the appropriate strategy.
- Improves error handling and reporting so callers get clear failure reasons when a save cannot be completed.

Testing
- Reproduced the original failure by saving to SMB and NFS mounted volumes on macOS.
- Verified that saving now succeeds on local and multiple types of network volumes.
- Added unit/integration tests covering atomic vs non-atomic save paths and the fallback behavior.

Risk and migration
- Low risk: behavior only differs on network volumes or when atomic replace fails. Local saves are unchanged.
- No migration needed for existing files.

Notes
- This resolves common issues reported by macOS users working with files on network drives. If you still encounter save errors on a specific network share, please include mount type and macOS version when filing a bug.

Add ScholarArchive fetcher (scholar.archive.org)

This PR integrates a new fetcher for Scholar Archive (scholar.archive.org) into JabRef.

Main changes
- Add ScholarArchiveFetcher: implements PagedSearchBasedParserFetcher, builds API requests, parses JSON responses and maps results to BibEntry objects (title, authors, journal/container, DOI, ISSN, year, volume, issue, publisher, language, abstract, url, date, type). Handles contrib_names, issns and fulltext access_url.
- Add ScholarArchiveQueryTransformer: transforms Lucene-style queries into Scholar Archive specific query parameters (field mappings for author/title/journal, logical operators, year and year-range handling).
- Register fetcher in WebFetchers: included in search-based fetchers and fulltext fetchers and imported where appropriate so it appears in available catalogs and fulltext provider lists.
- Tests: add ScholarArchiveFetcherTest to verify search results and fields, and update GUI SLR test (ManageStudyDefinitionViewModelTest) expectations to include the new "ScholarArchive" catalog item.
- Update CHANGELOG: document the new fetcher under Unreleased -> Added (refs #10498).

Notes
- The fetcher requests JSON from https://scholar.archive.org/search using parameters q/from/size/format and sets Accept: application/json on the request.
- The query transformer contains specific handling for years and ranges formatted for Scholar Archive.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/ScholarArchiveFetcher.java (new)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/transformers/ScholarArchiveQueryTransformer.java (new)

- src/main/java/org/jabref/preferences/JabRefPreferences.java:
  - Adjusted default preferences so OPEN_FOLDERS_OF_ATTACHED_FILES is true on Windows (false elsewhere). This makes the Windows experience match the new default documented in the changelog.

Notes
- The changelog entries include relevant issue/PR references for traceability.
- No behavioral changes beyond the documented defaults and changelog text were introduced in this PR.

Closes #3590

Summary
- Store Recent Files and File History entries as project-relative paths instead of absolute paths to improve portability when a project folder is moved or shared across machines.

What I changed
- LastFilesOpenedPreferences
  - Convert input lastFilesOpened and lastFocusedFile to relative paths when constructing the preferences.
  - When returning last files / last focused file to callers, convert stored relative paths back to absolute paths based on the current working directory.
  - setLastFocusedFile stores a relative path.
  - Added private toRelative/toAbsolute helpers with a fallback to the original absolute path if relativization fails.

- FileHistory
  - When adding items (doAdd) or creating a new file entry (newFile), store a relative path (converted from absolute).
  - Added private toRelative/toAbsolute helpers similar to LastFilesOpenedPreferences.

Why
- Recent Files previously stored absolute paths which could break when the project folder is moved or used on another machine. Converting to project-relative paths keeps recent-file links valid as long as the relative layout inside the project remains the same.

Behavior and notes
- Stored paths are relative when possible. When the app needs to open files, stored relative paths are resolved against the current working directory.
- If relativization fails for any reason, the code falls back to storing/returning the original absolute path.
- No public API changes; behavior is internal to recent-file handling.

Manual test steps
1. Open JabRef.
2. Open a .bib file located inside a folder (e.g., your project directory).
3. Close JabRef and reopen it.
4. Move the entire folder to another location.
5. Open JabRef again.
6. Check the Recent files list — it should correctly resolve and open the .bib file using the relative path.

Notes
- I manually tested these changes in running JabRef.
- No JUnit tests were added in this PR.

This PR introduces a dedicated "Clear content" tab in the Automatic Field Editor, which allows users to clear the content of selected fields for multiple entries. The tab includes a dropdown to select the field to clear and a checkbox to filter the dropdown to fields that are actually filled in the selected entries. The functionality previously available in the "Edit content" tab has been moved to this new tab. Additionally, the PR ensures that clearing operations support Undo/Redo via `NamedCompound` and `UndoableFieldChange`. All new UI text has been internationalized, and corresponding i18n keys have been added. The changes are documented in the `CHANGELOG.md` and include unit tests for the new view model.

### Steps to test
1. Open or create a library with a few entries (fill in some fields like `author`, `journal`).
2. Select one or more entries.
3. Open **Edit → Automatic field editor**.
4. Switch to the new **Clear content** tab.
5. Toggle the "Show only set fields" checkbox: the dropdown should shrink to only the fields currently filled.
6. Select a field (e.g., `author`) and click **Clear field content**: the field value should be removed from all selected entries.

text:
RIS importer implementation and improvements

- Add a full RIS importer (RisImporter) that recognizes RIS files by looking for the "TY  -" tag and parses an entire file into JabRef BibEntry objects.
- Normalize Unicode dashes (en-dash, em-dash, horizontal bar) to ASCII dashes before parsing.
- Split entries by the ER  - record terminator and support multi-line field values by joining continuation lines.
- Map many RIS tags to JabRef fields, including standard mappings (title, journal, booktitle, series, volume, number, pages, publisher, address, issn, abstract, url, language, note, shorttitle, eventtitle, translator, edition, school, keywords, comment) and a set of UnknownField mappings for non-standard tags (e.g. archive_location, call-number, archive, number-of-volumes, original-title, reviewed-title, status, section, refid, database, caption).
- Concatenate multiple title lines (T1/TI) intelligently, inserting punctuation or a colon as appropriate, and normalize whitespace.
- Accumulate multi-line abstracts (N2/AB) and keywords (KW) correctly.
- Collect authors and editors across multiple tags (AU, A1-A4, ED) and fix name ordering using AuthorList.fixAuthorLastNameFirst; save as author/editor fields.
- Parse dates with a priority order (Y1, PY, DA, Y2), extract the year and, if available and parseable, the month.
- Handle pages by combining SP and EP into the pages field (start--end).
- Improved DOI handling: strip a leading "doi:" prefix in a case-insensitive way, validate the DOI with a regular expression and store it in the DOI field.
- Remove empty/null fields before creating entries and set month via BibEntry.setMonth.
- Return a ParserResult containing all parsed BibEntry objects.

This change provides a robust RIS importer with careful handling of multi-line fields, date prioritization, DOI normalization and validation, and mapping of both standard and non-standard RIS tags into JabRef fields.

Add BibTeX String Editor dialog and supporting view-model infrastructure

Summary
- Introduces a new dialog to manage BibTeX strings for a library: add, edit, remove, and save string definitions.
- Provides inline validation for labels and content, duplicate-label prevention, and convenient UI actions (help, add, delete).

Key changes
- New UI: BibtexStringEditorDialog.fxml — dialog layout with a TableView for strings and action buttons (help, add, save/cancel).
- New view class: BibtexStringEditorDialogView.java — controller wiring, table column editors, validation handling, and integration with DialogPane.
- New view-model: BibtexStringEditorDialogViewModel.java — exposes observable list of items, handles loading/saving strings to BibDatabase, add/remove logic, and opens help page.
- New item model: BibtexStringEditorItemModel.java — holds label/content properties and validation rules (no null/empty, no numeric-only labels, no '#', no spaces; content must be non-empty).
- Reusable cell visualization: ViewModelTextFieldTableCellVisualizationFactory.java — installs editable text cells with validation tooltips and invalid pseudoclass handling.
- List-cell factory utilities: ViewModelListCellFactory.java (updated) — supports tooltip from validation and invalid pseudoclass binding (used by other UI components).
- Localization: added labels and messages to JabRef_en.properties for the new dialog and validation/error strings (e.g. "Strings for library", "Add new String", validation messages).
- CSS: Entry editor and base styles (EntryEditor.css, Base.css) include styles/classes used by the dialog (icon-button, tooltip, etc.).

Behavior highlights
- Add new string: clicking Add creates a new entry with an auto-incremented name if "NewString" exists, and immediately enters edit mode for the label.
- Inline editing: both label and content columns are editable in-place with validation feedback and tooltips.
- Duplicate label prevention: editing a label to one that already exists will show an error dialog and restore the previous value.
- Save: Save button is disabled until all items pass validation; saving writes the strings back to the BibDatabase.
- Remove: table action column includes a delete icon to remove the selected string.
- Help: opens the help page for the string editor.

Files added/modified (high level)
- Added: BibtexStringEditorDialog.fxml, BibtexStringEditorDialogView.java, BibtexStringEditorDialogViewModel.java, BibtexStringEditorItemModel.java
- Added/updated utility cell factories: ViewModelTextFieldTableCellVisualizationFactory.java, ViewModelListCellFactory.java
- Updated: localization JabRef_en.properties (new text entries)
- Styling: EntryEditor.css and Base.css used for consistent look-and-feel

Notes
- Validation uses mvvmfx/de.saxsys validators and binds invalid state to a CSS pseudo-class so the UI can highlight invalid inputs.
- The implementation uses existing IconTheme/ValueTableCellFactory utilities for action icons and consistent UI.

This change adds a complete, validated editor for library-level BibTeX strings, improving usability for managing string constants within JabRef.

Fix insertion of newly created entries so editor and main table are bound to the same instance.

Problem
- New entries were cloned before being added to the database. As a result the entry shown/edited in the entry editor was a different object than the one stored in the database and displayed in the main table, breaking bindings and updates.

Fix
- Ensure the entry is added to the database before any cloning or binding occurs and that the same instance is used for the entry editor and the main table. This prevents the editor and table from working with different objects and restores correct live updates.

Notes
- Follow-up to #11724.
- Closes https://github.com/JabRef/jabref-issue-melting-pot/issues/656
- Change is internal; behavior is fixed so new entries are properly bound. Manually tested to verify editor and table reflect the same entry instance.

Fixes incorrect glyph icon colors in the Search Bar when the application is in Dark Mode so icons are visible and meet contrast expectations.

Root cause:
SVG glyphs were inheriting an unexpected color value in dark theme (icons ended up too light or too dark) because the component relied on inherited text color instead of an explicit semantic token for icons in dark mode.

What I changed:
- Updated SearchBar styles to apply a semantic icon color token for glyph fills/strokes so SVGs inherit the correct color in both light and dark themes.
- Ensured SVG glyphs use currentColor properly and added a fallback fill for cases where SVGs had hard-coded fills.
- Adjusted theme variables for dark mode to provide the correct icon color mapping.
- Minor refactor in SearchBar component to ensure the CSS class is applied consistently.

Files touched (high level):
- SearchBar.tsx (class application / SVG usage)
- SearchBar.css (icon color rules)
- theme/dark.css or theme/tokens (icon color token values)

Testing:
- Manual verification in Dark Mode and Light Mode across Chrome and Firefox.
- Visual snapshot updated for SearchBar component.
- Verified icon contrast meets accessibility guidelines for dark backgrounds.

Impact:
No behavioral changes beyond icon color fixes. No migration required for consumers.

Add a FulltextFetcher interface and two publisher-specific implementations (SpringerLinkFetcher and WileyFetcher) to support resolving and downloading full-text PDFs for BibEntry items.

Summary of changes:
- Introduce FulltextFetcher with findFullText(BibEntry) and getTrustLevel() to standardize full-text fetching behavior and trust-level reporting.
- Implement SpringerLinkFetcher:
  - Attempts a direct content/pdf URL (https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/<doi>.pdf) first.
  - Falls back to fetching the article page (https://link.springer.com/article/<doi>) and heuristically searches the HTML for .pdf links (href/src) if the direct URL fails.
  - Downloads discovered PDFs to a temporary file and returns a file:// URL to the temp PDF.
  - Uses HttpURLConnection with appropriate timeouts, logging, and error handling.
- Implement WileyFetcher:
  - Uses Wiley TDM API (https://api.wiley.com/onlinelibrary/tdm/v1/articles/<doi>) and requires the WILEY_TDM_TOKEN environment variable for authorization.
  - Handles direct PDF responses from the API or parses returned JSON (using Jackson) to find PDF URLs recursively.
  - Downloads the PDF to a temporary file and returns a file:// URL to the temp PDF.
  - Uses HttpURLConnection with timeouts, proper headers, logging, and converts unexpected errors into FetcherException where appropriate.
- Common implementation details:
  - Both fetchers return Optional<URL> (empty if no PDF found).
  - Both implementations mark TrustLevel.PUBLISHER.
  - Helper copyStream methods included for safe streaming to temp files.
  - Robust logging at debug/info/warn levels and defensive handling of HTTP status codes and content types.

Notes / Requirements:
- WileyFetcher requires the WILEY_TDM_TOKEN environment variable to be set to perform API requests.
- Jackson (com.fasterxml.jackson.databind) is used by WileyFetcher to parse JSON responses; ensure the dependency is available at runtime.

Implements new citation-key/file-name modifiers requested in #11367: Camel, CamelN, VeryShortTitle and ShortTitle.

Summary of changes
- Added four new Formatter implementations:
  - CamelFormatter: capitalizes each word and concatenates them (Camel case).
  - CamelNFormatter: same as Camel but limits to the first N words (triggered by camelN where N is an integer suffix).
  - ShortTitleFormatter: returns the first 3 content words of the title (ignores small/function words).
  - VeryShortTitleFormatter: returns the first content word of the title (ignores small/function words).
- Registered the new formatters in Formatters.java via a new getTitleChangers() group and wired them into getAll().
- Extended modifier parsing in Formatters.getFormatterForModifier to handle the new modifiers:
  - "camel" -> CamelFormatter
  - "camel<NUMBER>" -> CamelNFormatter(length = NUMBER)
  - "shorttitle" -> ShortTitleFormatter
  - "veryshorttitle" -> VeryShortTitleFormatter
- Added English localization entries for the new formatter names and descriptions in JabRef_en.properties.
- Added unit tests in BracketedPatternTest to cover the new modifiers and parsing behavior (camel, camelN, shorttitle, veryshorttitle).

Notes
- This change implements the behavior discussed in https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/11367 and its referenced comment.
- Documentation (user docs for citation key modifiers) still needs to be updated to include these new modifiers: https://docs.jabref.org/setup/citationkeypatterns#modifiers

- The author reports manual testing in a running JabRef instance.

text:
Introduce ImportHandler: centralizes importing and linking of external files and bibliographic data into a BibDatabaseContext.

Main features:
- importFilesInBackground: Processes a list of files in a BackgroundTask with progress/title/message updates on the JavaFX thread. Supports PDFs, .bib files and fallback behavior (creates an empty BibEntry with a file link when no BibTeX data found).
  - PDF handling via ExternalFilesContentImporter.importPDFContent and DragDrop.handleDropOfFiles to attach file links.
  - Bib file import via ExternalFilesContentImporter.importFromBibFile.
  - Creates UndoableInsertEntries and registers undo edits via UndoManager on the FX thread to avoid threading issues.
- createEmptyEntryWithLink: helper to create a minimal entry with TITLE set to the file name and link the file using ExternalFilesEntryLinker.

Entry import pipeline:
- importEntries: runs ImportCleanup.postCleanup then importCleanedEntries.
- importCleanedEntries: inserts entries into the database, generates citation keys, sets automatic fields (owner/timestamp), and adds entries to currently selected groups.
- generateKeys: uses CitationKeyGenerator and respects the preference to generate new keys on import.
- setAutomaticFields: sets owner and timestamp fields according to preferences.
- addToGroups: adds entries to groups that implement GroupEntryChanger (undo support TODO).

Duplicate handling and import with duplicate checks:
- importEntryWithDuplicateCheck / importEntriesWithDuplicateCheck: find duplicates using DuplicateCheck, show DuplicateResolverDialog when needed, and support applying merge decisions to all remaining entries via preferences.
- handleDuplicates/getDuplicateDecision: apply the chosen decision (KEEP_RIGHT, KEEP_BOTH, KEEP_MERGE, etc.) and return merged result when appropriate.
- cleanUpEntry marked @VisibleForTesting to allow unit testing of cleanup behavior.

File download and linked-file handling:
- downloadLinkedFiles: optionally downloads online linked files via LinkedFileViewModel according to file preferences.
- ExternalFilesEntryLinker used to link files to entries.

String and text import:
- handleBibTeXData: parse BibTeX data from a string using BibtexParser, import string constants (with collision checks) and return entries.
- importStringConstantsWithDuplicateCheck: validate and add BibtexString constants to the database, collecting failures and showing a warning dialog for problems.
- handleStringData: determine whether the string is an identifier (CompositeIdFetcher) or data to be parsed by ImportFormatReader; errors are shown to the user.

Error handling and logging:
- Logs import errors and parser exceptions; shows dialogs for import/parse failures where appropriate.

Notes / TODOs:
- Group changes currently do not create undos (TODO present in addToGroups).
- createEmptyEntryWithLink and some other interactions rely on FX thread for safe UI/undo integration.

This PR consolidates file import logic, duplicate resolution, cleanup, key generation and linking behavior into a single, testable handler used by the GUI.

Fix Unicode-to-LaTeX conversion for non-BMP characters (surrogate pairs)

What I changed

- Fix: Corrected handling of Unicode code points above Character.MAX_VALUE (non-BMP / surrogate pairs) in UnicodeToLatexFormatter. Instead of treating the high surrogate as a char, the formatter now appends the full code point (appendCodePoint) and skips the low surrogate index to avoid double-reading.
- Data: Added a conversion map entry for U+1D716 (MATHEMATICAL ITALIC EPSILON) mapping to "$\\epsilon$" in HTMLUnicodeConversionMaps (note: may require amsmath). Also cleaned up trailing comma on the previous entry.
- Test: Added unit test formatHighCodepointUnicodeCharacter to verify conversion of the surrogate-pair character (\uD835\uDF16) to "$\\epsilon$".
- Changelog: Added an entry describing the bugfix and referenced issue #7387.

Why

Previously the formatter could produce wrong results for characters represented as surrogate pairs because it treated the high surrogate as a standalone char. This caused incorrect output for code points > 0xFFFF. The patch ensures correct handling of non-BMP characters and extends the conversion map for an additional mathematical symbol.

- Issue referenced in changelog: #7387

- src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/formatter/bibtexfields/UnicodeToLatexFormatterTest.java — add test for high codepoint character

This pull request introduces a new 'Clear content' tab in the Automatic Field Editor, enhancing the ability to manage and clear specific fields within selected entries. Key features include:
- A dedicated 'Clear content' tab with a dropdown to select which field to clear.
- A 'Show only set fields' checkbox to filter the dropdown to fields that are actually filled in the selected entries.
- The removal of the 'Clear field content' button from the 'Edit content' tab, with its functionality now integrated into the new tab.
- Support for Undo/Redo operations when clearing fields, using NamedCompound and UndoableFieldChange.
- Addition of internationalization (i18n) keys for all new UI text.

Steps to test:
1. Open or create a library with a few entries (fill in some fields like 'author', 'journal').
2. Select one or more entries.
3. Open **Edit → Automatic field editor**.
4. Switch to the new **Clear content** tab.
5. Toggle the 'Show only set fields' checkbox: the dropdown should shrink to only the fields currently filled.
6. Select a field (e.g., 'author') and click **Clear field content**: the field value should be removed from all selected entries.
7. Press **Ctrl+Z**: the cleared field(s) should be restored.

text:
Adds transfer of linked PDF files when copying/pasting or exporting entries and improves logging.

Summary
- Implements copying of associated PDF files when entries are moved between .bib files via copy/paste. The source database context is recorded on copy and used during paste to locate and transfer linked PDFs into the destination database's file directory.
- Extends the existing "Copy linked files to folder" flow to physically copy linked files into the chosen folder and update entries with the new linked-file paths.
- Adds additional logging throughout the file-copying code path (FileUtil, CopyFilesTask, CopyFilesAction) to aid debugging and trace operations.
- Updates CHANGELOG with the new feature and includes the referenced issue (#520).

Behavior details
- When copyEntry() is invoked, the current BibDatabaseContext is cached. On pasteEntry(), the metadata default file directory from the cached context is queried and used to find linked PDFs for each entry being pasted. If found, PDFs are copied to the destination database's default file directory (REPLACE_EXISTING). Missing files are logged as warnings; IO errors are logged as errors.
- CopyFilesAction now iterates selected entries, locates linked files in the chosen export path, copies them to the destination folder, adds a new LinkedFile (with the new path) to the entry, and logs successes/failures.
- CopyFilesTask now updates the linked file entry when a file copy succeeds and logs copy attempts.
- FileUtil.copyFile logs attempts and successful copies, and errors on failure.

Files changed (high level)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/LibraryTab.java: cache source BibDatabaseContext when copying; on paste, copy linked PDFs from source directory to destination.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/copyfiles/CopyFilesAction.java: copy linked files to chosen folder immediately and add new LinkedFile to entries; add logging.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/copyfiles/CopyFilesTask.java: more logging and update linked-file link on success.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/util/io/FileUtil.java: added logging around Files.copy.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/copyfiles/CopyFilesDialogView.java: minor whitespace change.
- CHANGELOG.md: new entry describing this functionality and referencing issue #520.

Notes and considerations
- The implementation relies on the entries’ LinkedFile.findIn(...) behavior and the default file directory metadata. If the database metadata lacks a default file directory, paste will log a warning and abort copying associated PDFs.
- Files are copied with StandardCopyOption.REPLACE_EXISTING.
- Logging has been added to help track missing source files and IO exceptions; this may produce more log output during normal operations.

Issue
- Implements feature requested in #520: copy associated PDFs when moving entries between .bib files.

Add preference to disable automatic linking of files in the entry editor

What this PR does
- Adds a new preference to enable/disable the automatic search and display of unlinked files inside the entry editor.
- Adds a checkbox to the Entry Editor preferences UI: "Automatically search and show unlinked files in the entry editor" (default: enabled).
- Prevents the Linked Files editor from searching for associated (but unlinked) files when the preference is disabled.
- Wires the new preference through EntryEditorPreferences, EntryEditorTabViewModel, JabRefPreferences and the preferences UI.
- Adds an English localization entry and updates the changelog.

- Provide users an option to turn off background autolinking behavior in the entry editor (requested in #5105). This mitigates related performance/UX concerns (#9800) for users who prefer to manage file links manually.

- New boolean property in EntryEditorPreferences with getter/setter and JavaFX property binding.
- EntryEditorTab/EntryEditorTabViewModel updated to expose and persist the setting.
- LinkedFilesEditorViewModel now only triggers the background search for associated files when the preference is enabled.
- Default remains enabled (true) to preserve existing behavior.

Issues
- Fixes #5105
- Mitigates #9800

Other
- Small DI change in EntryEditorTab to use KeyBindingRepository for ActionFactory initialization.
- CHANGELOG.md and l10n/JabRef_en.properties updated.

text:
Remove XMP <?xpacket?> wrapper when exporting and improve XMP/DublinCore parsing

What changed
- XMP output: XmpExporter now writes XMP content without the <?xpacket ...?> begin/end tags so the produced .xmp files can be consumed by tools that expect plain Dublin Core XML (e.g. CTAN xmpincl). This is implemented by adding XmpUtilWriter.generateXmpStringWithoutXmpDeclaration and using it when exporting.
- XmpUtilWriter: renamed the original generator to generateXmpStringWithXmpDeclaration and added generateXmpStringWithoutXmpDeclaration which strips the ?xpacket begin/end lines. Added a small constant and refactored some stream usage for the stripping logic.
- DublinCoreExtractor: fixed year/month extraction so that a default calendar value of YYYY-01-01 (which often signals "no month present") is not treated as a valid month. If a real month exists it is extracted and normalized to JabRef's short month names. Improved handling of dc:relation entries starting with "bibtex/": parsing is more robust for values that contain additional slashes and normalizes the month field when present.
- Tests: updated expected line counts and indexes in XmpExporterTest to reflect the removed xpacket wrapper and adjusted a test resource month value (article_dublinCore.bib) to use the short month name ("mar").

Why
- Some consumers of XMP expect or require XMP content without the <?xpacket?> wrapper, so exporting without that wrapper improves interoperability.
- The previous month extraction logic could incorrectly treat the implicit default month/day (January 1) as an actual month, losing fidelity. The new logic avoids introducing spurious month values and normalizes incoming month strings.
- The bibtex/ relation parsing was fragile when values contained additional slashes; the new parsing correctly separates key and value and handles month normalization.

Notes
- Behavior and tests changed accordingly: exported XMP files have fewer lines (the xpacket begin/end lines removed) and tests were updated to match the new output.
- This change preserves backwards compatibility for XMP content that explicitly contains a month value (e.g. "jan") because explicit month entries will still be parsed and honored.

Summary:
Adds support for search history so users can see and reuse their recent search queries.

What this change does:
- Saves recent search queries and displays them as suggestions when the search input is focused.
- Persists history across sessions (using local storage / client persistence layer).
- Allows users to remove individual items from history and clear the entire history.
- Limits stored entries to a configurable maximum and deduplicates repeated queries.
- Adds small UI affordances: a dropdown list under the search input, timestamps or counts (where applicable), and a clear-history control.

Why:
Improves discoverability and convenience by letting users quickly repeat common searches and reducing typing effort.

Testing and migration notes:
- Includes unit and integration tests for saving, loading, deduplication, removal, and clearing of history entries.
- No backend migrations required; persistence is client-side. If an alternative storage backend is configured, ensure it supports the new keys/structure.

Notes for reviewers:
- Verify behavior when history reaches the max entries and when the same query is entered multiple times.
- Check accessibility of the suggestion list (keyboard navigation, ARIA attributes).
- Confirm privacy implications and that the history is stored only locally unless configured otherwise.

Summary

Allow the user to select the BibTeX/BibLaTeX entry type when generating an entry from an identifier (DOI/ISBN/etc.). This improves control over the created entries and integrates the entry-type selection into the existing import flow.

What I changed

- Added an EntryTypeViewModel to represent and manage available entry types and the currently selected type (src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/EntryTypeViewModel.java).
- Updated the GenerateEntryFromIdAction to present and use the entry-type selection when creating an entry from an identifier (src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/importer/GenerateEntryFromIdAction.java).
- Added new localization strings used by the entry-type selection UI (src/main/resources/l10n/JabRef_en.properties).
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to mention the new feature and relevant user-facing change.

Why

Previously entries created from identifiers were generated with a fixed or inferred entry type, giving users limited control. Exposing the entry type selection during generation makes it easier to produce correct entries (e.g., article vs. inproceedings) and reduces manual post-import edits.

How to test

1. Open the "Generate entry from identifier" action in the UI.
2. Verify that a control for selecting the entry type is shown (the list should reflect available entry types).
3. Select different entry types and generate entries; check that the created entry uses the selected entry type.
4. Ensure the labels and messages are properly localized (English strings added). 

Notes

- This change is additive and should not break existing workflows; if the selection is not used, behavior falls back to previous logic.
- Additional localization keys were added; translators should update other language files accordingly.
