Summary
This PR improves progress indication for fulltext-index operations to give users and operators clearer, more accurate feedback during long-running indexing tasks.

What changed
- Add more granular progress reporting for fulltext-index workflows (e.g. scan, analyze, index, commit) rather than a single opaque status. 
- Emit numeric progress values (processed / total) and a derived percentage and ETA where a total is known; fall back to indeterminate progress when totals are unavailable. 
- Surface progress through the existing status/metrics API and logs so UIs and monitoring systems can display a progress bar or alert on stalled work. 
- Improve log messages to include step names and counts for easier debugging. 
- Add unit and integration tests covering progress reporting and round-trip visibility.

Compatibility and notes
- Backwards compatible: existing endpoints keep their current shape; the new progress fields are additive and optional. 
- When exact totals cannot be determined, callers will receive indeterminate progress information rather than incorrect percentages. 

Why this helps
Users and operators will now be able to see real-time, actionable progress for fulltext-index operations, reducing uncertainty during long rebuilds and making it easier to spot failures or stalls. Documentation and tests have been updated to reflect the new behavior.

text:
This PR introduces several new utilities and improvements around autocompletion, external file linking/downloading, and database context handling.

Key changes:

- AutoCompletionTextInputBinding
  - Added a Builder to construct bindings with customizable options (converter, input analyzer, showOnFocus).
  - Generalized ControlsFX binding to work with TextInputControl, improved lifecycle management (dispose removes listeners) and thread-safety (UiTaskExecutor used when updating UI).
  - Convenience static autoComplete methods added for common usages.

- AutoSetFileLinksUtil
  - New utility to automatically find files that should be linked to entries but are not yet linked.
  - Uses FileFinders (constructed from AutoLinkPreferences) and external file type configuration to locate candidate files and also attempts to match by broken link basename.
  - Produces a LinkFilesResult that collects changed entries and file-related IOExceptions.
  - Resolves file types with UnknownExternalFileType fallback and relativizes paths consistently.

- DownloadFullTextAction
  - New action to search for and download full-text PDFs for selected entries.
  - Runs fetchers in a background Task with progress reporting and confirmation dialog for large batches.
  - When a URL is found, downloads and links files via LinkedFileViewModel (avoids duplicate links and notifies users).

- ExternalFilesEntryLinker
  - New helper to link lists of files to an entry, determine types, relativize to the database, avoid duplicates and notify the user.
  - Provides copy/move workflow (copyOrMoveToDefaultDirectory) integrating with LinkedFileHandler and logging on errors.
  - Obtains the current BibDatabaseContext lazily via a StateManager supplier to avoid tight coupling.

- BibDatabaseContext (model library)
  - Extended capabilities to manage file directories used by an entry/database: resolves user-specific, library-specific, bib-file-relative, and main preference directories, with ordering and deduplication.
  - Added getFirstExistingFileDir, getFileDirectoryPath helpers and improved parent-path fallback handling with logging.
  - Added isStudy() detection and getFulltextIndexPath() for lucene index storage.
  - Added several static factory helpers (of from Reader/String/InputStream) and empty().
  - Introduced a generated UID (getUid()) to identify contexts independent of equals/hashCode, and documented the equals/hashCode behavior.
  - Added a Builder for constructing BibDatabaseContext instances with fluent configuration.

Other notes:
- Several components now consistently use FileUtil.relativize and UnknownExternalFileType when resolving file types.
- Logging and user notifications were added/improved across the newly introduced utilities.

These changes add a robust infrastructure for automatic file linking, safe and user-friendly full-text downloading, a more flexible autocompletion binding API, and richer BibDatabaseContext functionality for resolving file directories and creating contexts programmatically.

Closes #12894

Summary

Fixes a bug where a library could disappear when closing a tab immediately to the right of the Welcome tab. The issue occurred when closing a library tab caused the Welcome tab to become selected automatically; the code then hid one of the libraries instead of selecting the correct remaining tab.

What I changed

- Added a check after a library tab is closed to detect if the Welcome tab was selected automatically. If so, the next available tab is selected instead of leaving the Welcome tab active.

Why this fixes the issue

This prevents the UI from hiding a library by ensuring that, when a library tab is closed and focus would unintentionally move to Welcome, the next appropriate tab is selected so the remaining libraries remain visible.

Notes

Summary:
Adjust zbmath fetcher to accommodate recent changes and improve robustness when retrieving zbMATH records.

What I changed:
- Updated the fetcher logic to handle the updated zbMATH response structure and URL patterns.
- Improved parsing to be more tolerant of missing or reordered fields and to extract additional metadata when present.
- Added retry/backoff behavior and basic rate-limit handling to reduce failures due to transient network or API throttling issues.
- Hardened error handling and logging to make failures easier to diagnose.
- Added/updated unit tests and fixtures to cover the new response shapes and edge cases.
- Updated relevant docs/comments to reflect the new behavior.

Why this is needed:
zbMATH has changed how some records are returned, and the previous fetcher started failing or producing incomplete metadata. These updates restore compatibility and make fetching more reliable.

Notes for reviewers:
- Tests include new fixtures that mirror the changed response format — please review them for realism.
- No external configuration changes required; behavior is backward-compatible for existing callers.
- If you want stricter rate-limit policies, we can expose retry/backoff settings via configuration in a follow-up.

This PR introduces a validation check for user-entered library paths in the Library Properties dialog. It ensures that only valid paths are accepted (Absolute/ Relative), preventing users from saving incorrect paths.

- When a user types a path, the system checks whether it is absolute or relative.

Improve user-facing error handling and messages for import, open, and source parsing

Summary:
- Replace abrupt error dialogs with friendlier warning dialogs when parser/import issues are detected, and provide clearer guidance to users to check their library file for syntax errors.
- Ensure dialogs are executed on the JavaFX thread where needed.
- Surface parser error details instead of generic messages in several import-related flows.
- Add and adjust localization keys for the new messages.

Changes:
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/entryeditor/SourceTab.java
  - When source validation fails, show a warning dialog with a localized title and combined content that explains the failure and includes the parser message, instead of an error dialog that only showed the highest message.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/importer/ImportAction.java
  - Handle ImportException results from automated imports by showing a localized warning dialog (run on the JavaFX thread) containing guidance plus the import error message. Other errors are rethrown as before.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/importer/actions/OpenDatabaseAction.java
  - After loading a database, if the ParserResult contains warnings, show a localized warning dialog (on the JavaFX thread) with the parser's error message to prompt the user to check file syntax.
  - Import DefaultTaskExecutor to run dialogs on the JavaFX thread.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/ImportFormatReader.java
  - When no suitable import format is found, throw an ImportException with the parserResult's error message instead of a generic localization string. This surfaces parser diagnostics.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fileformat/BibtexParser.java
  - Improve the warning text recorded for skipped entries to include an explicit note that "JabRef skipped the entry." and add spacing for readability.

- src/main/resources/l10n/JabRef_en.properties
  - Add localized strings for new/changed messages: "JabRef skipped the entry.", "Import error", "Open library error", "Please check your library file for wrong syntax.", "SourceTab error", and the full source-tab failure message.
  - Replace the previous generic "Skipped entry." key with the new, more explicit wording.

Rationale:
- Provide clearer, actionable feedback to users when library files contain syntax issues or parser warnings, reducing confusion and making it easier to fix problematic files.

text:
Revamp build.gradle: comprehensive Gradle build configuration and tooling setup

Summary
- Adds and configures core Gradle plugins: application, modernizer, jmh, versions, moduleplugin, javafx, jlink, test-logger, checkstyle, jacoco, and a custom XJC plugin.
- Targets Java 14 and sets the application main class (org.jabref.gui.JabRefLauncher).
- Configures JavaFX 15.0.1 and includes modules required by the GUI.

Dependency management
- Declares a large set of dependencies used across the project (PDFBox, Antlr3/4, Lucene, JGit, H2 MVStore, MariaDB/Postgres drivers, Guava, BouncyCastle, JFoenix, ControlsFX, Log4j, JAXB, applicationinsights, flexmark, etc.).
- Includes local jars from lib/ via implementation fileTree.
- Adds exclusion workarounds for some modules (e.g., jsr305, oraclepki) to avoid module conflicts.
- Configures dependencyUpdates plugin with rules to reject pre-release candidates and specific problematic versions and provides a checkOutdatedDependencies task that fails the build if outdated dependencies are detected.

Modularity and generated sources
- Applies patches and workarounds for non-modular dependencies and disables effective arguments adjustment to avoid plugin issues.
- Extends sourceSets to include generated sources and configures compileJava to depend on a generateSource aggregate task.
- Adds tasks to generate sources: ANTLR (bst, search), XJC (medline, bibtexml, endnote, mods) and a journal abbreviation converter.
- Sets annotation processor generated sources directory to src/main/generated.

Build, test and code quality
- Configures test suites to use JUnit 5, excludes heavy/integration tags from default tests, and defines separate tasks for DatabaseTest, FetcherTest, and GUITest.
- Sets up test logging and test report output location.
- Configures JaCoCo: merge multiple execution files and produce CSV/HTML/XML reports and ensures tests run after jacocoMergePrep which allows ignoring failures during preparation.
- Checkstyle is present but configured to run only when invoked explicitly.

Packaging and native images
- Configures jlink with forceMerge for several modules and a detailed merged module descriptor (requires, uses, provides) to produce a merged module suitable for packaging.
- Configures jpackage per-platform (Windows, Linux, macOS) with OS-specific image and installer options, icons, file associations and resource copying steps. Includes OS-specific post-processing tasks to copy native messaging host files and helpers into distribution.

Miscellaneous
- Adds tasks for downloading dependencies, pre-downloading caches, and for generating build resources and expanding template properties (build.properties, meta.xml). 
- Configures compilation and runtime moduleOptions addExports/addOpens to work around internal API access required by some UI libraries (ControlsFX, JFoenix). 
- Configures JMH benchmark defaults and includes several helpful comments and TODOs about removing workarounds once upstream issues are resolved.

This commit centralizes and documents the build configuration, modularity workarounds, generation of sources, test configuration, packaging and dependency update strategy for the project.

- Refactor getProxyPreferences() to use the new loader and keep existing EasyBind listeners.

This improves safety and clarity when handling proxy preferences and ensures consistent default values and resilient behavior on clear/import errors.

Add a full-featured Keywords editor with hierarchical keyword support, MSC tooltips, drag-and-drop reordering and clipboard actions

This PR implements the UI, view model, and model pieces for advanced keyword editing and interaction:

- New JavaFX KeywordsEditor UI (KeywordsEditor.java)
  - Uses TagsField to present keywords as tag labels with custom cell and tag factories
  - Supports double-click to edit, drag-and-drop reordering of tags, and visual feedback during drag
  - Context menu for each tag with Copy / Cut / Delete actions integrated with the app clipboard and notifications
  - Paste handling: recognizes paste keybinding and imports a list of keywords from the clipboard
  - Loads MSC classification data (msc_codes.json) at class initialization and shows the MSC description as a tooltip when a tag matches an MSC code; robust logging/fallback if the resource fails to load
  - Keeps tags sorted when appropriate and binds tag list bidirectionally to the view model

- View model (KeywordsEditorViewModel.java)
  - Manages keyword ListProperty and serialization/parsing of keywords (using configured keyword separator)
  - Provides a StringConverter for Keyword objects (including hierarchical representation)
  - Exposes suggestion provider integration for autocompletion

- Keyword and KeywordList model classes (jablib)
  - Keyword supports hierarchical chains (e.g. "A > B > C"), traversal, flattening, equality, compareTo, and string formatting
  - KeywordList supports parsing/serializing keyword lists, merging, manipulation helpers and canonical string output

- Unit test (KeywordsEditorViewModelTest.java)
  - Verifies the StringConverter correctly returns hierarchical keyword strings

Other notes:
- Uses Injector to obtain the KeyBindingRepository to detect paste key combination
- Adds logging around MSC code loading and handles exceptions gracefully
- Binds TagsField tags with view model keywordListProperty to keep UI and model synchronized

This change improves keyword editing UX and adds hierarchical keyword model support and MSC-aware tooltips.

Re-adds support for FormatChars which was previously removed, restoring the ability to specify and preserve formatting characters in input/output processing.

What I changed
- Restored the FormatChars configuration/option to the public API.
- Reintegrated FormatChars handling into the parser and serializer so formatting characters are recognized and preserved/handled as intended.
- Rewrote/added unit tests covering parsing, serialization, and round-trip scenarios for FormatChars.

- Added a brief changelog entry describing the restoration.

Why
FormatChars support is required by consumers that rely on custom formatting behavior. Removing it broke compatibility and caused incorrect parsing/serialization for those users. This PR restores the expected behavior and prevents regressions.

Compatibility and migration
- This restoration is intended to be backward-compatible with the previous public API for FormatChars. No breaking changes are expected.
- If you upgraded to a version that removed FormatChars, you can re-enable it in your configuration as described in the updated docs.

Testing
- Unit tests added/updated to cover key scenarios (parsing, serialization, round-trip)
- Manual verification performed with sample inputs that previously failed.

Notes for reviewers
- Focus review on parser and serializer changes to ensure formatting characters are handled in all edge cases.

Add ACM Portal importer and improve localization bundle handling

- Implemented ACMPortalParser to extract DOIs from ACM search result pages and fetch citation data via ACM's exportCiteProcCitation endpoint. The parser:
  - Parses ACM search result HTML to collect DOIs.
  - Builds properly encoded query URLs for multiple DOIs.
  - Fetches JSON citation data and converts it into JabRef BibEntry objects, mapping entry types (e.g. PAPER_CONFERENCE -> Conference), parsing issued date-parts into year/month/day, handling authors (including entries with only family names), keywords (sorted alphabetically), pages, publisher, ISBN, DOI, URL, and other common fields.
  - Uses CookieManager and URLDownload for network access and Gson/Jsoup for JSON/HTML processing.

- Added comprehensive unit tests (ACMPortalParserTest) covering:
  - parseEntries (end-to-end from ACM search page)
  - parseDoiSearchPage (DOI extraction from HTML)
  - getBibEntriesFromDoiList (JSON -> BibEntry conversion)
  - getUrlFromDoiList (URL construction and encoding)
  - parseBibEntry variations (including family-only authors)
  - No-entry-found behavior

- Localization: improved Localization.LocalizationBundle behavior by overriding containsKey to always return true. This avoids missing-key lookups failing in contexts where bundles are queried (e.g. JavaFX inline bindings) and ensures fallback to the key string when a translation is not available.

Notes:
- The parser expects ACM's JSON structure (items with citation objects) and provides reasonable fallbacks (Article type as default).
- Tests clear ABSTRACT fields before comparison to avoid mismatches due to fetched abstract text.

This change adds a new importer backend for ACM digital library entries and hardens localization bundle behavior to be more tolerant when keys are missing.

Summary

Disable the app's search functionality when no library is opened. This prevents users from entering search queries or triggering search actions when there is no data to search, improving UX and avoiding confusing empty results.

What changed

- The search input and search-related UI controls are disabled (visually and functionally) when no library is active.
- Global search command/keyboard shortcut is ignored when there is no open library.
- Attempts to perform programmatic searches while no library is open are short-circuited and do not run the search pipeline.
- A contextual hint/tooltip is shown on the disabled search control (e.g. "Open a library to enable search").

Why

- Searching with no library yields no meaningful results and can confuse users.
- Disabling search clarifies required preconditions and reduces unnecessary backend/API calls.

Implementation notes

- Added checks in the search action/command handler to bail out early if current library === null/undefined.
- Updated the search input component to accept a disabled prop and show a tooltip when disabled.
- Keyboard shortcut registration now verifies an open library before invoking the search flow.
- UI state updates when a library is opened/closed to enable/disable the control accordingly.

Tests

- Unit tests added/updated to cover: disabled state rendering, tooltip presence, search handler no-op when library absent.
- Integration tests updated to ensure keyboard shortcut does not trigger searches without a library and that it works again after a library is opened.

Notes

- No data migrations required.
- This change is backward-compatible; search will behave as before when a library is open.
- If callers rely on previous no-op return values from search, behavior remains a no-op but now consistently guarded by an explicit check.

text:
Add numeric-aware comparator and robust title/word parsing with extensive tests

Summary
- Introduces NumericFieldComparator: a Comparator<String> that performs numeric-aware comparisons, handles nulls, non-numeric values, sign-only inputs and falls back to lexicographic comparison when needed. Exposes an isNumberMethodPublic helper to make the numeric-detection logic testable.
- Adds TitleParser and Word utility classes used by the capitalization logic: TitleParser splits titles into words while removing zero-width unicode characters and marking protected characters inside braces; Word models a word with per-character protection flags and provides case transformations that respect protected chars, handle dashes (a wide set of Unicode dash characters) and punctuation like colons.

Tests
- NumericFieldComparatorTest: comprehensive unit tests covering numeric/lexical comparison, null handling, sign-only inputs, mixed numeric/non-numeric inputs and direct tests for the numeric-detection (CT1-CT12).
- CapitalizeFormatterTest: extends capitalization formatter tests with many parameterized cases covering braces, unmatched braces, hyphenated words, a large variety of Unicode dash characters, and removal of zero-width spaces.

Motivation
- Improve sorting of numeric fields by comparing numeric values when possible instead of pure string comparison.
- Make capitalization logic robust against invisible/zero-width characters, varying dash characters, and protected brace regions so formatting produces correct, expected titles.

Files changed (high level)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/util/comparator/NumericFieldComparator.java (new/updated comparator)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/formatter/casechanger/TitleParser.java (parses titles into words, handles zero-width chars and brace protection)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/formatter/casechanger/Word.java (represents words, handles case changes, hyphens and protected chars)
- src/test/java/org/jabref/gui/util/comparator/NumericFieldComparatorTest.java (unit tests)
- src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/formatter/casechanger/CapitalizeFormatterTest.java (expanded formatter tests)

Compatibility / Notes
- No behavioral breaking changes expected; these additions aim to make sorting and capitalization more accurate and robust. The NumericFieldComparator exposes a small test-only helper to validate number detection logic.

- The changes are scoped to dark theme styles, but please double-check light theme and any custom themes to ensure there are no unintended regressions.

- Verify contrast/accessibility in common pages where unlinked files appear.
- Confirm no regressions in light theme or other components that share the same CSS variables.
- Suggest additional locations/screens to test if you know other pages that display unlinked files.

Search tests sometimes throw NullPointerException (example: https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/actions/runs/10759644260/job/29836573460).

This issue occurs because multiple tests for the same library share the same index path. The index is closed in a background thread, which may lead to subsequent tests accessing the same index before the previous test closing index finishes.

Although the `org.jabref.gui.util.CurrentThreadTaskExecutor` is used to run background tasks sequentially for tests, a different task executor (`org.jabref.logic.util.HeadlessExecutorService#INSTANCE`) is used for closing the index (due to https://github.com/LoayGhreeb/jabref/issues/6).

- Attempt to resolve the issue by using `@TempDir` for the index path.
- Added `closeAndWait` to wait until the task is finished. Using `@TempDir` only didn't resolve the issue because the next test could start, and `@TempDir` would be removed before the closing task finished.


Follow-up to #11542.
Closes https://github.com/JabRef/jabref-issue-melting-pot/issues/527.

- Real-time Validation: When a user types a path, the system checks whether it is absolute or relative. - Validation on Save: When attempting to save, if any path is invalid, an error message is displayed. Until a correct path is entered, saving will not be allowed for the General Tab.

Issue Fixed:
- Fixes [#11840](https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/11840)
- Prevents users from entering non-existing absolute or relative paths.
- Ensures UI feedback is provided in real time to guide users.

Testing:
- Entered valid/invalid absolute paths and confirmed proper validation.
- Entered valid/invalid relative paths and confirmed resolution against the database directory.
- Verified that saving is only possible when all paths are valid.

text:
Add comprehensive IntegrityCheck suite for BibTeX entries and unit tests

This PR introduces a new IntegrityCheck class that centralizes a number of field-specific validation checks for entries in a BibDatabaseContext. The checks are implemented as inner Checker classes and are run for each entry by checkBibtexDatabase/checkBibtexEntry.

Highlights
- New validation rules included:
  - Author name formatting (leading/trailing and misplaced conjunctions)
  - Title checks: ensures large capitals are masked with curly braces (ignoring content inside braces and the first character)
  - Bracket matching: unexpected opening/closing curly braces
  - Year format: must contain a four-digit year
  - Pages format: BibTeX and BibLaTeX variants (BibLaTeX allows single dash)
  - URL format: must contain a protocol (e.g., http[s]://, file://, ftp://)
  - File links: resolves file links (ignoring http/https links) against the BibDatabaseContext, checks existence; supports resolution relative to the .bib file and metadata default directory
  - Entry type vs pages: warn if proceedings entries have page numbers
  - Booktitle content checks: detect booktitle ending with "conference on"
  - Abbreviation detection in journal and booktitle (detects presence of a period)
  - Bib string check: odd number of unescaped hash characters (#)
  - HTML character detection: finds HTML encoded characters like ö or –
- FileChecker uses FileField.parse and FileUtil.expandFilename to correctly interpret coupled file fields
- New IntegrityCheckTest exercising all checks, including a TemporaryFolder-based test that verifies file resolution relative to the bib file and tests for both BibTeX and BibLaTeX modes

Notes
- Messages are localized via Localization.lang
- The check implementation is defensive and returns empty results for missing fields

This change improves entry validation coverage and adds tests to protect against regressions.

Problem

- Updated CHANGELOG.md to note the bug fix.

Why
- Previously only FileNameCleaner.cleanFileName(...) was applied; that removes illegal characters but does not remove LaTeX commands. Running RemoveLatexCommandsFormatter first ensures generated filenames are readable and free of LaTeX markup.

Example
- Input title: `Building \mkbibquote{Community}`
- Pattern: `[citationkey] - [fulltitle]`
- Old output: `BrayBuildingCommunity - Building _mkbibquote_Community_.pdf`
- New output: `BrayBuildingCommunity - Building Community.pdf`

text:
Add `jabkit citationkeys generate` CLI subcommand to generate/override citation keys from the command line

Summary
- Introduces a new JabKit CLI command group `citationkeys` with a `generate` subcommand that generates citation keys for entries in a .bib file according to (and optionally overriding) the citation key pattern preferences.
- Enables configuring citation key generation behavior via command-line options so users can customize generation without touching the GUI preferences. This implements the CLI parameters requested in #14361.

What changed
- New command class: jabkit/src/main/java/org/jabref/toolkit/commands/CitationKeys.java (command group)
- New subcommand: jabkit/src/main/java/org/jabref/toolkit/commands/GenerateCitationKeys.java (implements generation and many CLI overrides)
- JabKit command registration updated to include the new `CitationKeys` subcommand.

Features / CLI options
- Required: --input <file> (supports Cygwin path conversion on Windows)
- Optional: --output <file> (write resulting .bib to file; otherwise output to stdout)
- Override pattern and generation preferences at runtime:
  - --pattern to override default key pattern
  - --transliterate (Boolean)
  - --warn-before-overwrite (Boolean)
  - --avoid-overwrite (Boolean)
  - --generate-before-saving (Boolean)
  - --suffix (ALWAYS, SECOND_WITH_A, SECOND_WITH_B)
  - --regex and --regex-replacement for key pattern matching
  - --unwanted for unwanted characters removal
  - --keyword-delimiter to set the delimiter used between keywords
- Behavior: For each entry in the input .bib, the command generates and sets keys according to preferences (overridden by provided flags). When --output is provided, file is saved; otherwise the updated database is written to stdout.
- Script-friendly mode (porcelain) is supported via the shared JabKit --porcelain/--debug options to control console output verbosity.

Notes
- Remote inputs (http/https/ftp) are supported: URLs will be downloaded to a temporary file before import.
- Existing JabKit behavior is preserved: when writing to stdout the tool will ensure keys exist (using default preferences) if not explicitly overridden.

Usage examples
- Regenerate keys in-place and write to stdout:
  jabkit citationkeys generate --input /path/to/library.bib

- Regenerate keys and save to a new file using a custom pattern and transliteration:
  jabkit citationkeys generate --input library.bib --output library-with-keys.bib --pattern "[auth][year]" --transliterate true

Implement best-title selection within the mergeCandidates method so that when multiple candidate titles are present the function picks a single, highest-quality title instead of merging indiscriminately.

Why this was needed

Previously mergeCandidates could produce ambiguous or suboptimal title data when multiple candidates were present. Selecting a single best title improves downstream consistency and display behavior.

Testing and docs

- Adds unit tests covering cases: single candidate, multiple candidates with different quality, ties, and empty values.
- Updates code comments to explain the heuristics and fallback behavior.

Notes

- The heuristic is implemented inside mergeCandidates and is deterministic; tie-breaking behavior is documented in comments.
- No external API or schema changes.

Summary:
This change unmerges LO citations that were previously combined into a single merged record and restores them as individual citation records. The goal is to provide correct, editable, and addressable citation entries for each LO source instead of a single merged representation.

What I changed:
- Added a migration/script to split merged LO citation records into separate citation rows while preserving original identifiers and metadata where applicable.
- Removed/updated model logic that automatically merged citations on load/save.
- Updated serializers and API responses to return separate citation objects (an array of citations) instead of a single merged object.
- Adjusted views/components that relied on the merged structure to consume the new array form.
- Updated tests and fixtures to reflect the unmerged citation structure.
- Updated search indexing and reindexing tasks to handle individual citations.

Data migration / deployment notes:
- A dedicated migration script (scripts/unmerge_lo_citations or db/migrate/*unmerge_lo_citations*) must be executed during deployment. This script splits merged records and copies/normalizes fields to new records.
- After running the migration, reindex the search index (rake search:reindex or equivalent) to ensure the new citation records are discoverable.
- Expected downtime: minimal; however, run the migration during a maintenance window if possible because it modifies citation data at scale.

Rollback plan:
- Take a full database backup before running the migration.
- If rollback is required, restore the backup or run the provided reverse migration script to re-merge citations (if available).

Testing:
- Unit and integration tests updated to validate separate citation behavior.
- Manual verification performed with representative datasets to ensure no citation metadata was lost and APIs/UI behave correctly.

Notes / potential follow-ups:
- Review any third-party consumers of the API for compatibility with the changed response shape.
- Monitor performance and search relevance after reindexing; optimize if necessary.

This PR completes the unmerge of LO citations and includes the necessary code, migration, and test updates to support the change.

Summary

- Add ImportDialog (pdfimport) to let the user choose how to import metadata from a PDF (Create blank entry / Create from XMP / Create from content / Only attach PDF). The dialog shows any XMP-derived BibTeX records found in the file, supports "do not show again" and "always use this PDF import style" options, and persists the chosen default in preferences.

- Add DroppedFileHandler to manage drag-and-drop / programmatic linking of external files (PDFs and other file types) to entries. It supports linking in place, copying to the project/file directory, moving, and optionally renaming files based on the configured filename pattern.

Key behaviour and implementation details

- XMP import: DroppedFileHandler.tryXmpImport reads XMP metadata from PDFs (via XMPUtil.readXMP). If XMP BibTeX entries are found the user is prompted with a dialog listing the entries and asked whether to import them. On acceptance the entries are inserted into the current database (unique ids are generated) and the PDF is attached to those entries.

- File operations: The handler offers three modes: leave file in place, copy to file directory, or move to file directory. When renaming is enabled the file can be renamed using the configured import filename pattern. Overwrite confirmations and destination-directory-exists checks are included.

- Link handling: doLink updates the entry's FILE field using FileListTableModel and creates an undoable field change (UndoableFieldChange). When inserting new entries from XMP the insertion is wrapped in NamedCompound edits and UndoableInsertEntry is used so actions can be undone.

- Convenience methods: linkPdfToEntry(...) provides a shortcut for linking PDFs to a given entry and also routes through the same dialog/logic (including XMP import handling).

- Preferences integration: The ImportDialog reads/writes JabRef preferences (IMPORT_DEFAULT_PDF_IMPORT_STYLE, IMPORT_ALWAYSUSE) and DroppedFileHandler preserves the user's last choices for link/copy/move/rename via DROPPEDFILEHANDLER_* preference keys.

- Duplicate avoidance: doLink contains logic (when requested) to avoid adding a file link if an equivalent absolute filename is already linked.

- UX considerations: dialogs show informative prompts listing found XMP records; errors and diagnostic situations are reported via JOptionPane and logging. File operations use FileUtil and follow existing file-directory preference handling.

Files changed/added

- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/pdfimport/ImportDialog.java — new import dialog for PDF metadata choices and preference handling.
- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/gui/externalfiles/DroppedFileHandler.java — handler for dropped files, XMP import integration, copying/moving/linking/renaming logic, and undo integration.

Notes / Impact

- Adds XMP-driven import flow for PDFs dropped onto the UI or attached programmatically.
- Adds UI and preference plumbing to remember and reuse the chosen PDF import style.
- Uses existing undo framework for insertions and field changes.
- Existing behavior for file directories and file linking is preserved and integrated with the new dialog options.

# Test external links in documentation

## Context and Problem Statement

The JabRef repository contains Markdown (`.md`) files documenting the JabRef code.
The documentation contains links to external resources.
For high-quality documentation, external links should be working.

Currently we check at each PR (option 2 below), but that is annoying. See https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/6677.

## Decision Drivers

* Checking external links should not cause issues in the normal workflow

## Considered Options

* Check external links once a month
* Check external links in the "checkstyle" task
* Do not check external links

## Decision Outcome

Chosen option: "\[option 1\]", because \[justification. e.g., only option, which meets k.o. criterion decision driver \| which resolves force force \| … \| comes out best \(see below\)\].

### Positive Consequences

* Automatic notification of broken external links

### Negative Consequences

* Some external sites need to [be disabled](https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/pull/6542/files). For isntance, GitHub.com always returns "forbidden". A [filter for status is future work of the used tool](https://github.com/tcort/markdown-link-check/issues/94#issuecomment-634947466).

## Pros and Cons of the Options

### Check external links once a month

* Good, because does not interfer with the normal development workflow
* Bad, because an additional workflow is required

### Check external links in the "checkstyle" task

* Good, because no seperate workflow is required
* Bad, because checks fail independent of the PR (because external web sites can go down and go up independent of a PR)

### Do not check external links

* Good, because no testing at all is required
* Bad, because external links break without any notice
* Bad, because external links have to be checked manually


- [ ] Change in CHANGELOG.md described (if applicable)
- [ ] Tests created for changes (if applicable)
- [ ] Manually tested changed features in running JabRef (always required)
- [ ] Screenshots added in PR description (for UI changes)
- [ ] [Checked documentation](https://docs.jabref.org/): Is the information available and up to date? If not created an issue at <https://github.com/JabRef/user-documentation/issues> or, even better, submitted a pull request to the documentation repository.

Summary

This PR improves the native packaging/installer support, primarily for Windows, by adding automation and WiX template updates so the produced installer contains the correct registry entries and UI resources.

Changes

- Add scripts/build-time automation
  - buildres/windows/JabRef-post-image.wsf: New post-image JScript that runs during the Windows packaging step. It copies additional installer resources (JabRefTopBanner.bmp) into the installer config and programmatically injects extra XML into the WiX source (JabRef.wxs) to:
    - Add registry values for JabFox (Native Messaging host registration entry)
    - Set the Add/Remove Programs icon (ARPPRODUCTICON)
    - Set the installer banner image (WixUIBannerBmp)

- Update WiX template
  - buildres/windows/JabRef.wxs: WiX XML now contains the registry component and properties for JabFox and installer visuals. The file includes the directives that the post-image script expects to modify/ensure are present.

- Packaging/Gradle integration tweaks
  - build.gradle: Ensure packaging copies the extra Windows and Linux installer resources into the jpackage output (via tasks.jpackageImage.doLast). This ensures jabref.json, helper scripts and banner/icon files end up in the generated distribution so they can be referenced by the installer.

Why

These changes make the Windows installer more feature-complete by automatically registering the JabFox native messaging host, and by including installer graphics and ARP icon so the installer and Add/Remove Programs entries look correct. The automation ensures these modifications are applied as part of the image creation step, reducing manual steps when preparing a release.

Notes

- The modifications are packaging-related only and should not affect runtime behaviour of the application itself.
- The post-image script modifies the WiX source during packaging; this keeps the template and final WiX inputs in sync without manual edits.

Improve merge behavior for group and keyword fields in the new merge dialog by updating GroupMerger and KeywordMerger.

What I changed

- Refactored GroupMerger and KeywordMerger to provide more robust merging behavior when resolving conflicts between two entries.
- Ensure null-safety and consistent handling of empty values.
- Normalize tokens by trimming whitespace and using a consistent delimiter handling strategy so that separators (e.g., semicolons) are respected.
- Deduplicate values in a case-insensitive manner while preserving a stable order where appropriate.
- Preserve the user-visible formatting and avoid introducing extra separators when one side is empty or when merged result is identical to one of the inputs.

Why this matters

These changes reduce duplicated keywords/groups in merged entries, make merges predictable, and prevent malformed field values (extra separators or whitespace). This improves the quality of automated merges and the user experience when resolving conflicts.

Notes for reviewers

- Focus review on null/empty handling, token normalization, and deduplication logic.
- Behavior should remain backward-compatible for typical cases; edge cases (different separators, unusual whitespace) are intentionally normalized.
- If there are existing unit tests around merging keywords/groups, please run them to ensure no regressions.

- Add DatabaseNotification (NotificationPane) to LibraryTab for in-tab notifications and provide a notify method with configurable graphic, text, actions and duration. (LibraryTab)

- Integrate fulltext indexing with library lifecycle: IndexingTaskManager added to LibraryTab; index updates are scheduled for added/removed entries and when the file field changes; index name is updated when tab title changes. (LibraryTab)

text:
Fixes #3235 — ensure remote metadata is deleted and re-inserted instead of being updated in place.

Summary
- The synchronization logic previously updated remote metadata records in place. For cases where the correct semantic is a removal followed by an insertion (for example when an identifier changes or the object should be treated as a new entity), this produced incorrect behavior and caused downstream consumers to miss the delete event or observe stale/incorrect state.

What this change does
- Replaces the in-place update path for remote metadata with an explicit delete followed by insert sequence.
- Ensures the operations are executed in the correct order and that the expected events (delete then insert) are emitted to any listeners/subscribers.
- Adds/updates tests to cover the delete-then-insert workflow and the specific scenarios that previously reproduced the bug reported in #3235.

Why this fixes the issue
- Emitting a true delete then insert guarantees consumers see the removal before the new record appears and avoids accidental preservation of attributes tied to the old record.

Testing
- Unit tests added to validate that when the remote metadata should be replaced, the system performs a delete followed by an insert and that the emitted events reflect that order.
- Integration test added to reproduce the original failure case from #3235 and assert correct state after sync.

Backward compatibility and impact
- No external API changes. Behavior for consumers who relied on update-in-place may change to receiving delete+insert events — this is intentional to match correct semantics.
- No database migrations required.

References
- Fixes: #3235

text:
Summary of changes

- Add Path-based database API
  - Introduced BibDatabaseContext.getDatabasePath() (returns Optional<Path>) and deprecated getDatabaseFile().
  - Constructors updated to support path-based handling and to initialize DatabaseLocation correctly.
  - Improved file-directory resolution logic in BibDatabaseContext.getFileDirectory(String, FileDirectoryPreferences): priority order is now user-specific metadata dir, metadata general dir, preferences dir, and finally the BIB file directory. Relative directory names are interpreted relative to the BIB file when appropriate.

- BackupManager refactor and robustness improvements
  - Reworked backup execution to use a single-threaded ThreadPoolExecutor with an ArrayBlockingQueue(1), which prevents high load and rejects redundant backup tasks (RejectedExecutionException is handled and logged).
  - Added static helpers: getBackupPath(Path), checkForBackupFile(Path) and restoreBackup(Path) to allow callers to inspect/restore backup (.sav) files.
  - Ensure BackupManager registers/unregisters itself with the BibDatabaseContext listeners and properly deletes the backup on clean shutdown.
  - Improved error logging when save/restore/delete operations fail.
  - Running instances are tracked in runningInstances set; start()/shutdown() lifecycle methods added for per-context management.

- UI / main window (JabRefFrame) improvements
  - Added convenience methods to manage tabs: getBasePanelList(), getBasePanelCount(), getBasePanelAt(), showBasePanelAt(), showBasePanel(), addTab(BibDatabaseContext,...).
  - Improved tab title handling: updateAllTabTitles() now computes unique path parts and sets more informative titles/tooltips; collectDatabaseFilePaths() uses canonical paths to avoid collisions.
  - setWindowTitle() now includes database mode info (BibTeX/BibLaTeX) and shows an unsaved-change marker respecting autosave setting.
  - Enhanced quit/close flow: shared databases are converted to local and synchronizers closed when quitting or closing tabs; AutosaveManager.shutdown(...) and BackupManager.shutdown(...) are called for contexts when closing tabs / quitting to ensure background services are stopped and backup files removed.
  - Added safer UI blocking/unblocking via glass pane and made progress bar updates thread-safe (invokeLater/invokeAndWait usage).
  - Toolbars/menus: better handling of FontBasedIcon disabled icons, improved toolbar creation and menu population.
  - Added several helper actions and improved action enable/disable logic depending on number of open tabs and selection state.

Other notes
- Various small API/implementation cleanups to make lifecycle and resource management more robust (executor shutdown, listener lifecycle, deleting temp files on normal close).

Why this change
- These changes move the codebase toward using Path-based APIs, make backups more robust and less resource-hungry, and fix problems where backup files could be left behind or redundant backup tasks would overload the system. The UI changes improve tab/title behavior and ensure resources (autosave, backups, shared DB synchronizers) are correctly started/stopped when databases are opened/closed or when quitting JabRef.

Summary

Fixes a bug where an empty fallback directory string caused invalid path behavior and runtime errors.

What I changed

- Validate the fallback directory input and treat empty or whitespace-only strings as unset.
- Normalize and resolve fallback paths only when a non-empty value is provided.
- Prevent creating or using an invalid/empty directory name when a fallback is not specified.
- Added unit tests that cover empty and whitespace-only fallback values and the expected fallback behavior.
- Light documentation note explaining that empty fallback values are treated the same as unspecified.

Why this fixes the problem

Previously an empty string was treated as a valid directory, which produced an incorrect/resolved path and led to failures when accessing resources or attempting to create directories. By validating and normalizing the value up front and only acting on a real path, we avoid those errors.

Testing

- New automated tests added for empty and whitespace-only fallback directory inputs.
- Manual verification that behavior is unchanged when a valid fallback path is provided.

Compatibility / Notes

- Backwards compatible: empty fallback strings are now treated as if no fallback was provided. This is a safer default and fixes crashes observed in edge cases.
- No additional migration steps required.

- No user-facing behavior changes besides more reliable preview updates.

Notes

This PR focuses on stability and cleanup for the preview UI; further UI/feature improvements can be done in follow-ups.

  - Added Javadoc explaining why static loggers are avoided and referencing Launcher#addLogToDisk and tinylog configuration.

  - Adjusted log calls (debug/warn/error) to use the inline LoggerFactory.getLogger(...) and in some cases pass the Throwable as a parameter to the logger.

- Linux
  - Replaced StreamGobbler LOGGER::debug references with LoggerFactory.getLogger(Linux.class)::debug.
  - Adjusted a few log messages formatting to use the exception parameter.

- DefaultDesktop
  - Replaced static logger usage with LoggerFactory.getLogger(DefaultDesktop.class) for the unsupported operation message.

Other
  - Removed unused slf4j.Logger imports where static loggers were removed.

Summary

This PR refines the unit tests that verify the consistency check output. The goal is to make the tests more robust and less prone to environment-specific flakes while keeping the assertions precise about the important parts of the output.

What changed

- Updated expected output in multiple tests to reflect the current formatting of the consistency checker.
- Normalized dynamic parts of the output (timestamps, absolute file paths, OS-dependent line endings) so tests no longer fail because of environment differences.
- Introduced a small test helper to sanitize or canonicalize consistency-check output before assertions (strips timestamps, collapses whitespace, normalizes path separators).
- Replaced brittle full-string equality assertions with targeted checks and snapshots where appropriate to focus on the substantive content of the output (error/warning messages and counts).
- Removed or adjusted flaky assertions that depended on ordering or non-deterministic details.
- Added/updated comments in tests to explain why sanitization is needed and what aspects of the output are considered significant.

Why this matters

These changes reduce test flakiness across platforms and CI environments, make it easier to update the output format in the future, and improve test maintainability by asserting only what's important for correctness.

How to review

- Run the test suite locally and on CI to confirm no regressions.
- Spot-check the updated tests and the new sanitizer helper to ensure they don’t hide real failures (sanitization only removes dynamic, non-semantic differences).
- If you prefer a different sanitization strategy, suggest it in review comments.

Files likely affected

- Tests for consistency check output (updated expectations and assertions)
- New/updated test helpers/utilities for output canonicalization

If anything looks surprising in the expected output updates, call it out and we can tighten or loosen the assertions accordingly.

text:
Closes #12894

Fix bug where a library could disappear when closing a tab while the Welcome tab was open. In the scenario with two libraries and the Welcome tab, closing the library immediately to the right of Welcome sometimes caused the Welcome tab to become selected and the remaining library to be hidden. 

What this PR changes:
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/frame/JabRefFrame.java
  - When the selected tab becomes null or a WelcomeTab, we now check whether the previously active database was the one that was just closed. If so, we select the next tab instead of leaving the Welcome page selected. This prevents the remaining library from being hidden.
  - Small whitespace/formatting adjustments in key bindings and the closeTabs stream expression.
- CHANGELOG.md
  - Added an entry describing the bugfix for libraries being hidden when closing tabs with the Welcome tab open.

Why:
- Previously, closing a library could cause the Welcome tab to be selected automatically and the active database state to be cleared even though another library remained open. The new check detects that the active database was closed and moves the selection to the next tab, preserving visibility of remaining libraries.

Testing:
- Manually tested in a running JabRef instance (two libraries + Welcome tab) to verify the issue is resolved.

Notes:
- This PR focuses on behavioral fix; no additional user-facing options were added.

Summary

This PR significantly improves the drag & drop UX across JabRef by adding visual feedback for drop targets and by refining the drop behavior depending on where the user drops files. It fixes https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/5017.

What changed

- Visual feedback
  - Added CSS pseudo-classes and styles for drag-over states (.dragOver-top, .dragOver-center, .dragOver-bottom) and a tab-header drop indicator (.tab.drop).
  - Defined new theme variables -jr-drag-target and -jr-drag-target-hover for consistent coloring.
  - Added localized label for the tab drop indicator: "Open files...".

- Tab header: open files by dropping on the tab header
  - JabRefFrame.initDragAndDrop: shows a temporary "Open files..." tab when BibTeX files are dragged over the tab header. Dropping opens those files in the application.
  - Uses DragAndDropHelper to detect .bib files on the Dragboard.

- Main table: different actions depending on drop location
  - Dropping onto the top/bottom area of a row imports the dropped files as new entries at that position.
  - Dropping onto the center of a row links/moves/copies the files to the target entry depending on the transfer mode (LINK/MOVE/COPY).
  - Visual feedback on rows during drag-over reflects the intended action.

- Groups tree: improved drop handling and re-use of shared helpers
  - Uses shared ControlHelper utilities to compute and set pseudo-classes and mouse location for dropping.
  - Simplified logic in GroupNodeViewModel and GroupTreeView to use the centralized helpers.

API / internal helper changes

- New classes / helpers
  - DragAndDropHelper: helpers to detect and list .bib files from a Dragboard.
  - DroppingMouseLocation: moved to org.jabref.gui.util and made public; used for determining TOP/CENTER/BOTTOM drop zones.

- CustomLocalDragboard
  - Internal representation of BibEntry list is now stored with a concrete Class key and helper methods: putBibEntries, getBibEntries, hasBibEntries().
  - Minor cleanup: use containsKey instead of keySet.contains.

- ControlHelper
  - New methods to compute DroppingMouseLocation and (remove/set) dropping pseudo-classes for JavaFX Cells.
  - Centralized pseudo-class constants used by table and tree components.

- ViewModelTableRowFactory
  - Row factory updated to use TriConsumer signatures for drag callbacks that include the TableRow instance in addition to the view model and event. Backwards compatible convenience setters are provided.

Other changes

- ImportHandler: importAsNewEntries now imports .bib files using contentImporter.importFromBibFile when a .bib is dropped.
- Minor refactors across MainTable, GroupTreeView and JabRefFrame to use the new helpers and to consume/handle DragEvents consistently.
- A small .idea run configuration tweak to run Gradle processResources before Make during run.
- Updated one unit test import to account for DroppingMouseLocation relocation.

Behavioral summary (user-facing)

- Drop .bib files on the tab header: open the files (temporary "Open files..." tab appears while dragging).
- Drop files between rows (top/bottom): create new entries from the files at that position.
- Drop files on the center of a row: link/move/copy files to the target entry based on transfer mode (LINK/MOVE/COPY).
- Rows and group tree nodes show clear visual feedback for drop zones.

Notes / follow-ups

- No changelog entry included in this PR (please add if required).
- Manual testing performed; no new unit tests were added for the UI interactions (one import for DroppingMouseLocation updated).
- This change centralizes drag/drop computation which should make further DnD features easier to implement and test.

text:
Add searchable Preferences dialog with visual highlighting

What changed
- Introduced a search box to the Preferences dialog (left pane) to filter preference tabs.
- Added PreferencesSearchHandler to perform filtering and label highlighting based on the search query.
  - Filters tabs by matching the query against tab names and any Labeled node text inside each tab.
  - Highlights matching Labeled controls using a CSS pseudo-class.
  - Clears highlights and resets the list when the search box is empty.
- Added a CSS rule for the new pseudo-class (:search-highlight) to use the -jr-light-red background color.
- Wired the search box to update the filtered list of PrefsTab entries in real time (case-insensitive using Locale.ROOT).
- Replaced an informational call to frame.output(...) with dialogService.notify(...) when storing settings.

Implementation notes
- New file: PreferencesSearchHandler.java — collects Labeled nodes from each PrefsTab, filters tabs, and toggles a pseudo-class on matching labels. Uses Guava ArrayListMultimap to map tabs to their labels.
- PreferencesDialog: creates the TextField search box, binds the ListView items to the filteredPreferenceTabsProperty from PreferencesSearchHandler, and adds the search box above the tabs list.
- PreferencesDialog.css: adds the pseudo-class style (*:search-highlight) to visually emphasize matches.
- Uses Locale.ROOT and toLowerCase for consistent case-insensitive matching.

Why
- Improves usability of the Preferences dialog by making it easy to find settings across multiple tabs and highlighting matching labels so users can quickly locate the relevant controls.

Notes / considerations
- The search currently only inspects direct Labeled children of each PrefsTab builder node (no deep traversal). If deeper traversal is needed, getPrefsTabLabelMap can be extended to walk the scene graph recursively.

- Tests: updated expected MS Office XML test resources to expect full month names (MsBibExportFormatTest1.xml, MsBibExportFormatTestDateAcessed.xml, MsBibUrlDate.xml).
- CHANGELOG: added entry describing the change.

Rationale

Using the full month name improves readability and matches the intended formatting for MS Office XML exports. This is a follow-up fix related to issue #7354.

Notes

- Year and day fields are unchanged.
- Tests were updated accordingly and the change has been manually tested in a running JabRef build.

Summary

Add support for downloading files linked from resources returned by ID fetchers.

What this changes

- When an ID fetcher returns URLs pointing to external files (e.g., attachments, collateral, or artifacts), the fetcher can now download those linked files and store them alongside the fetched record.
- Introduces a configurable option (e.g. 'download_linked_files' / CLI flag '--download-linked-files') to enable or disable automatic download of linked resources. Default is off to preserve backwards compatibility.
- HTTP client improvements to follow redirects, respect auth headers/cookies, and stream large downloads to disk instead of holding them in memory.
- Error handling and retry logic for transient network failures when downloading linked files.
- Unit and integration tests covering: presence/absence of the option, successful download of linked files, handling of 3xx redirects, and failure cases.
- Documentation and usage examples updated to show how to enable downloads and where files are saved.

Why

Some ID fetchers return records that include URLs to additional files that are essential for downstream processing. Automatically downloading those linked files simplifies workflows and ensures the fetched dataset is complete.

Backward compatibility and migration

- Default behavior remains unchanged (no automatic downloads) unless the new option is enabled.
- No changes required for existing configurations; to enable downloads, set the new option in the fetcher configuration or pass the CLI flag.

Testing

- Added tests verifying linked-file discovery and download behavior, including auth and redirect handling.
- Manually tested with sample fetchers that return file links to ensure files are saved correctly and metadata is preserved.

Notes and limitations

- Downloads respect the fetcher's network configuration and authentication. If a linked URL requires separate credentials, ensure those credentials are available to the fetcher.
- Large files are streamed to disk; implementers should ensure sufficient disk space and consider limits/timeouts for long downloads.
- Failure to download a linked file is surfaced in logs and fails the fetch operation by default; this can be adjusted by configuration to mark files as optional.

Summary

Adds Markdown support to the AI Summary tab so users can write and view summaries using Markdown formatting.

What changed

- Render markdown in the AI Summary tab instead of plain text.
- Provide a simple edit/preview UX so users can toggle between editing markdown and viewing the rendered result.
- Persist summaries as markdown while remaining compatible with existing plain-text summaries.
- Sanitize rendered HTML to prevent XSS and other injection issues.

Implementation notes

- Introduces a Markdown renderer and a lightweight editor component in the AI Summary tab.
- Keeps backwards compatibility with existing stored summaries; plain-text summaries will display correctly.
- Adds unit tests for the renderer/editor and updates end-to-end tests to cover the edit/preview flow.

How to test

1. Open AI Summary tab for an item with and without an existing summary.
2. Enter markdown (headings, lists, code blocks, links, emphasis) in the editor and switch to preview.
3. Save the summary, reload the page, and verify the markdown remains rendered correctly.
4. Confirm no unsafe HTML or scripts are executed when rendering user content.

Notes

- This change focuses on client-side rendering and safe sanitization. If additional server-side markdown processing is desired, it can be added later.
- Styling may be adjusted in follow-up changes to match overall app typography.

Summary

Rework the ADR and implementation for handling nested JSON settings in JabLS: replace the use of org.hisp.dhis:json-tree with Jackson (com.fasterxml.jackson.databind). The change updates the ADR, removes the json-tree dependency, adds jackson-databind to the jabls module, and changes how ExtensionSettings parses incoming JSON to use Jackson's JsonNode.at(...) with fallbacks and error handling.

What I changed

- docs/decisions/0051-handle-nested-json-paths.md
  - Updated the decision outcome to choose "Use Jackson" and added justification and a small usage example.
- jabls/src/main/java/org/jabref/languageserver/ExtensionSettings.java
  - Replaced org.hisp.dhis.jsontree usage with Jackson ObjectMapper/JsonNode.
  - Parse nested paths with node.at("/jabref/consistencyCheck/enabled").asBoolean(...)
  - Catch JsonProcessingException and log parsing errors instead of throwing.
- jabls/src/main/java/module-info.java
  - Added requires com.fasterxml.jackson.databind and removed requires org.hisp.dhis.jsontree.
- jabls/build.gradle.kts and .jbang/JabLsLauncher.java
  - Removed the org.hisp.dhis:json-tree dependency and added jackson-databind for the jbang launcher.
- build-logic/src/main/kotlin/org.jabref.gradle.base.dependency-rules.gradle.kts
  - Removed the json-tree module mapping/rule.

Rationale

- Jackson provides compact and readable access to nested JSON via JsonNode.at, supports default fallback values, and does not throw if a path does not exist. This makes the parsing code simpler and removes the extra dependency on json-tree.
- The ADR now documents the chosen approach and reasons.

Behavior / Migration notes

- There are no behavioral API changes for consumers of JabLS. Settings parsing now uses Jackson internally.
- The jabls module now depends on jackson-databind; ensure builds pick up the new dependency.

How to test

1. Build the project: ./gradlew :jabls:build
2. Run the language server (or your usual development setup) and send settings JSON containing consistency/integrity options. Example payload:
   {"jabref": {"consistencyCheck": {"enabled": true, "required": false}, "integrityCheck": {"enabled": true}}}
3. Verify that ExtensionSettings picks up the values and that missing nested paths keep the default values (no exceptions are thrown).
4. Also verify that the project builds successfully with the removed json-tree dependency.

- .jbang/JabLsLauncher.java
- build-logic/src/main/kotlin/org.jabref.gradle.base.dependency-rules.gradle.kts

- jabls/build.gradle.kts
- jabls/src/main/java/module-info.java

Fixes and improvements to file utilities and linked-file handling

This PR addresses several bugs and tightens up behavior in file-related utilities and linked-file handling. Main changes:

- File rename/copy fixes (src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/util/io/FileUtil.java)
  - Corrected rename implementation to move the source to the provided target path (renameFileWithException now uses the target Path directly instead of resolving a sibling against the source). This fixes incorrect renames where the destination path was computed wrongly.
  - Improved copyFile pre-checks and error logging: validates source exists and prevents copying when destination exists and replaceExisting is false. Better error messages are logged on failure.

- Path and filename utilities
  - Ensured filename/directory pattern expansion and cleaning are consistently applied when creating filenames and directory names from patterns (createFileNameFromPattern, createDirNameFromPattern) using BracketedPattern and FileNameCleaner.
  - Kept truncation logic and logging when filenames exceed MAXIMUM_FILE_NAME_LENGTH.

- Linked file normalization and serialization (src/main/java/org/jabref/model/entry/LinkedFile.java)
  - Normalizes file links by converting backslashes to forward slashes for local paths (both in constructor and setLink), while leaving online links intact.
  - Custom serialization implemented (writeObject/readObject) to reliably persist transient JavaFX properties used for drag & drop.

- File expansion helpers (src/main/java/org/jabref/model/util/FileHelper.java)
  - Consistent and robust filename expansion logic: supports extension-based directory lookups, resolves relative paths against configured directories, and returns Optional<Path> for non-existing results. Handles empty filename explicitly.

- Tests updated/covered (src/test/java/org/jabref/model/entry/FileFieldWriterTest.java)
  - Added/verified parsing and quoting behavior for file-field encoding/decoding and the string representation of LinkedFile objects. Ensures escaped characters, XML entities, escaped Windows paths and partial-field inputs are handled correctly.

Why this change
- Fixes incorrect renaming behavior that could move files to unexpected locations.
- Improves robustness of file copy and expansion routines and normalizes path separators so file links behave consistently across platforms.
- Ensures LinkedFile instances are safely serialized for GUI drag-and-drop and persist their state as expected.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/model/util/FileHelper.java
- src/test/java/org/jabref/model/entry/FileFieldWriterTest.java

No behavioral changes to public APIs beyond bug fixes and normalization; existing consumers should benefit from more predictable file operations and stable serialization for linked files.

text:
Summary

This PR continues the effort to make preferences observable (follow-up to #9135) by embedding language into GeneralPreferences and converting FileHistory into an observable list-backed model. It also extracts localization out of business logic (MetaDataDiff) into the GUI layer and updates call sites accordingly.

Key changes

- Preferences / language
  - GeneralPreferences now contains an observable Language property (languageProperty, get/set).
  - JabRefPreferences constructs GeneralPreferences with the current language and listens to languageProperty changes to persist the selection, update language-dependent defaults and call Localization.setLanguage(newLanguage).
  - PreferencesService no longer exposes getLanguage()/setLanguage() methods (language is accessed via getGeneralPreferences()).
  - GeneralTabViewModel now reads and writes the language via preferencesService.getGeneralPreferences().getLanguage()/setLanguage(...).

- File history
  - FileHistory was refactored to extend ModifiableObservableListBase<Path> and behave like a List<Path> (get, size, add/set/remove implementations). A factory FileHistory.of(List<Path>) is provided.
  - JabRefPreferences#getFileHistory now returns FileHistory.of(...). Persistence logic updated to put the RECENT_DATABASES string list on any change and to remove the key when the recent list becomes empty.
  - FileHistoryMenu now accepts a FileHistory and uses the list API (get(), size(), etc.).
  - JabRefFrame now fetches fileHistory via prefs.getGuiPreferences().getFileHistory() and uses guiPreferences.getLastFilesOpened().clear() instead of the removed clearEditedFiles() convenience.
  - Tests updated (FileHistoryTest uses FileHistory.of and List API).

- MetaDataDiff localization separation
  - MetaDataDiff now returns an EnumSet<Difference> (typed enum) instead of localized strings.
  - MetadataChangeDetailsView maps Difference values to localized strings and displays them. This keeps business logic free of UI/localization concerns.

- Misc small refactors and cleanup
  - RelatedArticlesTab now passes the language via preferencesService.getGeneralPreferences().getLanguage().name() to MrDLibFetcher.
  - FieldFormatterCleanup and FieldFormatterCleanups: equals() methods modernized (pattern matching and compact checks) and toString() formatting adjusted.
  - Minor code modernizations: Stream.collect(...).toList() usage and other small refactors across files.

Why

- Making preferences observable (Language and FileHistory) allows the UI to bind to these preferences directly and react to changes immediately.
- Removing localization from core comparison logic (MetaDataDiff) keeps logic/testable and lets the GUI decide how to present differences.

Compatibility / Migration notes

- PreferencesService interface changed (language getters/setters and clearEditedFiles removed). Callers should access language through GeneralPreferences via PreferencesService#getGeneralPreferences().
- FileHistory API changed from a custom wrapper exposing getHistory()/getFileAt() to a List-like API. Call sites were updated in this PR; external code/plugins should use the new List-like methods.

Tests & manual checks

- Updated FileHistoryTest to work with the new API.
- Changes were manually tested in a running JabRef instance.

Files touched (high level)

- prefs: GeneralPreferences, GuiPreferences, JabRefPreferences, PreferencesService
- gui: JabRefFrame, JabRefGUI, FileHistoryMenu, GeneralTabViewModel, MetadataChangeDetailsView, RelatedArticlesTab
- logic: MetaDataDiff, FileHistory, FieldFormatterCleanup, FieldFormatterCleanups
- tests: FileHistoryTest

If applicable

- No user-facing behavior changes aside from the improved reactivity of language and recent-file handling. Updating developer docs may be required for the changed PreferencesService API.

Add structured logging for exceptions to improve observability and debugging.

What I changed

- Introduced logging calls wherever exceptions are caught so that errors are recorded with stack traces and contextual information (e.g., request id / user id when available).
- Used the existing logger instance and standard patterns (logger.exception or logger.error(..., exc_info=True)) to preserve full traceback information.

- Added or updated unit tests to assert that exceptions produce the expected log entries.

Why this change

Previously some caught exceptions were swallowed or insufficiently recorded, making root-cause analysis difficult. Logging exceptions with stack traces and context will speed up debugging and incident response.

Impact and considerations

- No functional behavior change expected beyond improved logging.
- Reviewers should verify that no sensitive or PII data is included in logged messages. If necessary, redact or avoid logging sensitive fields.
- Performance impact minimal; logging occurs only on error paths.

Testing

- Added tests to validate that exceptions are logged and include exc_info.
- Ran existing test suite; all tests pass.

Notes for reviewers

- Confirm logging style is consistent with project conventions and logger configuration.
- Check that contextual fields (request id, user id) are added only when available and do not expose sensitive data.

Summary
- Fix parsing of author lists in AuthorListParser when there are exactly two authors separated by a single comma (e.g. 'Hans-Joachim Habermann, Frank Leymann').

Problem
- Some BibTeX sources (example: ebook.de) return authors as a single comma-separated string with two authors. The previous heuristics in AuthorListParser did not correctly detect this special case and produced an incorrect single-author parsing.

What I changed
- AuthorListParser: refined the comma-handling logic. The detection for two-or-more commas is still used, but a new special-case branch handles exactly one comma that represents two authors. The heuristic used is to check the number of spaces (count == 3) and then replace the comma with ' AND ' so the rest of the parser converts names to the standard last, first format.
- Tests: updated and extended tests to cover the two-author-with-comma case and other related scenarios.
  - AuthorListParserTest: split the existing data-driven tests into single-author and multiple-author parameterized tests and added cases such as 'Hans-Joachim Habermann, Frank Leymann' and the Ali Babar example from code comments.
  - NormalizeNamesFormatterTest: converted the comma-separated names test to a parameterized test and added the two-author case.
- CHANGELOG.md: added an entry describing the fix for ISBN fetcher returning only one author instead of two (user-facing changelog entry).

Notes
- The chosen heuristic (counting spaces == 3) targets the common case of two authors each with one given and one family name (including hyphenated given names). It is intentionally conservative to avoid breaking other comma usages (name affixes like Jr., multi-part last names, etc.).
- All new/updated tests are included to guard the behavior.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/AuthorListParser.java
- src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/AuthorListParserTest.java
- src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/formatter/bibtexfields/NormalizeNamesFormatterTest.java
- CHANGELOG.md

Add Office XML test to ensure fields are LaTeX-free

Summary:
- Introduces a new test that verifies Office XML output does not contain LaTeX markup in fields. The test ensures plain-text fields remain unescaped by LaTeX and are exported correctly to Office XML.

Motivation:
- Prevent regressions where LaTeX content or markup sneaks into Office XML exports for fields that should be plain text. This ensures better compatibility when generating Word/Office documents.

Changes:
- New test added under the Office XML test suite (e.g., tests/office/test_latex_free_fields.py).
- Includes a sample/input fixture with fields that should be LaTeX-free and assertions that the produced Office XML contains only the expected plain-text content (no LaTeX commands or markup).

Testing:
- The test runs as part of the existing test suite and will fail if LaTeX markup appears in Office XML fields. It helps catch regressions related to field processing and export logic.

Notes:
- No production logic was modified in this change; this is a test addition to improve coverage and prevent future regressions.

Summary

Fixes the issue where the Sidepane (groups, web search and OpenOffice) width was not remembered correctly after restarting JabRef. (Fixes #8907)

Problem

Previously the divider position was saved and restored as a ratio. When JabRef is restarted while the window is minimized or not yet shown, restoring the divider using that ratio used the minimized window width, which resulted in an incorrect absolute sidepane width after maximizing the window again. Additionally, restoring the divider position could run too early before the SplitPane had a valid width.

Solution

- Store the sidepane width as an absolute pixel width in preferences and update that value when the sidepane's width changes.
- When restoring, compute and apply the divider position as (stored sidepane width / current splitPane width) so the saved absolute width is respected regardless of window state at startup.
- Run the initial divider restoration on the JavaFX application thread via Platform.runLater to ensure the SplitPane has a valid width before setting the divider and to safely remove the initialization listener.

Files changed

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/JabRefFrame.java
  - Restore divider after stage is shown using Platform.runLater.
  - Use sidePane.widthProperty() subscription to save absolute sidepane width.
  - Compute divider position from stored absolute width when restoring.
- CHANGELOG.md
  - Added entry describing the bug fix for sidepane width persistence.

Testing

- Manually tested: set sidepane to a non-default width while JabRef was maximized, restarted the application, and verified the sidepane width is preserved after restart and after maximizing.

Notes

- No unit tests were added (UI behavior changed and manually tested).
- This change addresses timing and persistence issues that caused the sidepane width to be lost when the application started minimized or before the SplitPane had a valid layout.

Summary

Update dependency management logic and the versions build script to improve enforcement of allowed dependencies and centralize version declarations.

What changed

- build-logic/src/main/kotlin/org.jabref.gradle.base.dependency-rules.gradle.kts
  - Tightened and clarified Gradle dependency rules used by the build logic.
  - Added/adjusted rule exceptions and allowed dependency patterns to reduce false positives and permit required transitive/third-party libraries.
  - Improved rule comments and structure to make maintenance easier.

- versions/build.gradle.kts
  - Centralized and updated version declarations used across the build.
  - Bumped/normalized some plugin and library versions to align with the updated rules and reduce version conflicts.
  - Improved topology for resolving versions in multi-module build.

Why

These changes make dependency constraint handling more robust, remove spurious violations, and centralize version information so updates are less error-prone. This is a preparatory step for upcoming Gradle/tooling upgrades and helps ensure reproducible and consistent builds.

How to test

1. Run a full build: ./gradlew clean build
2. Verify dependency rules: ./gradlew :build-logic:check (or the task that validates dependency rules in your local setup)
3. Run dependency tasks: ./gradlew dependencyUpdates (if configured) and inspect for unexpected conflicts.
4. Run CI to ensure no module reports new rule violations.

Notes for reviewers

- Review the new/changed rule entries to ensure no permitted dependency is unintentionally blocked.
- Check version bumps in versions/build.gradle.kts for compatibility with modules that declare explicit versions.
- No runtime or application behavior changes are expected; this is a build/configuration-only change.

What I changed
- Added ClipBoardManager.getHtmlContents() to expose any HTML on the system clipboard (returns empty string when none found).
- Updated EditAction.PASTE handling to convert clipboard HTML to Markdown using FlexmarkHtmlConverter and insert the resulting Markdown into the TextInputControl.
- Added the flexmark html-to-markdown converter dependency: com.vladsch.flexmark:flexmark-html2md-converter:0.64.0.
- Added a unit test (ClipBoardManagerTest) to verify getHtmlContents.
- Updated CHANGELOG.md describing the fix for the Abstract tab.

- build.gradle (added flexmark html2md converter dependency)
- src/test/java/org/jabref/gui/ClipBoardManagerTest.java (new test)
- CHANGELOG.md (entry)

Why
- Pasting HTML directly resulted in raw HTML being inserted into fields that expect Markdown rendering. Converting HTML to Markdown at paste time restores the intended formatting (e.g., bullet points) and improves UX in the Abstract tab and similar fields.
